thank you, madam president. commissioner, it's always a pleasure to have you here with us. i would also like to welcome the rapporteur, mr gabriel mato. it has done important work and it has sent parliament a series of decisions which, as you very well point out, belong to us. i would like to support the amendment tabled by the socialists and democrats, which stresses the importance of combating monopolies in fisheries. although the internal allocation of quotas is a matter for the member states, it is up to the european union to make a positive contribution to small-scale fisheries such as those in regions such as the azores and madeira. if we continue to support the large-scale initiatives, we will be strangling the pole-and-line fisheries, such as those in the outermost regions of the atlantic. i repeat the need to respect scientific recommendations and to use the precautionary principle without sparing. too many fish aggregating devices are still being used in tuna fishing without a serious environmental impact study being carried out.
madam president, the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna has allowed the stocks to develop positively. the biomass of this species has been showing a positive trend since 2008. in 2014, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas decided to increase the tac by 20% for the subsequent 3 years from 2015 to 2017. we, for our part, support criticism of a system of fishing quotas which penalizes the more sustainable small-scale fisheries to the benefit of the large shipowners of the main european fishing powers. the role of the artisanal frames used in the south of portugal, in the algarve, their potential and selectivity should be recognised. it is also important to recognize that island fishermen who use the jumping rod technique and who today spend their time fishing for bluefin tuna without being able to do so, it is important that these sinners should have their right to fish for this species recognised, especially now that catch limits are being adjusted to improve the resource, which, for example in the case of fishermen in the azores, would only partially compensate for the damage caused by the sharp declines in the stocks of another species.
member of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank the members very much for their views and opinions again. i fully respect and understand all of their concerns. let me come back to the most important questions. first, let me underline again that the commission did not ignore any signals before: neither in 2006 when we worked on a proposal for euro 5/6 in order to bring emissions down – although this was for laboratory testing, and that has to be stressed – nor in 2011 and 2012 when it was the jrc, not anybody else, who indicated for the first time that there is a problem with the real driving emissions. we now have to finish this process with a positive vote. we cannot make any new proposals on conformity factors, firstly because member states will not change their views, and secondly because it would extremely delay the whole process. to make things very clear: if we do not have rules in place by 2017, we will maintain this situation with 4-5 times higher emissions in real driving – in real life – and have 4-5 times more pollution. rejection implies that we will not have rules in 2017, and we will have to explain to our citizens why we now have 500 mg/km of nox emissions and have not done anything to reduce it to 168 mg/km. i feel, of course, that a consensus can emerge. let me outline a possible way forward without new proposals on conformity factors: the commission is ready to make a declaration for the plenary vote next month, outlining the solution that we discussed today, so i can honestly commit to activating the annual revision clause for the second conformity factor as soon as possible next year. this is more or less the same as reducing the second conformity factor. you can take this as my personal commitment too, and the second one is that we will adopt the reinforced type approval system on real driving emissions. i can commit to these two things before you now without making new proposals for conformity factors. i hope that this will allow you – or at least some of you – to cast a positive vote on the proposals on real driving emissions in the next 2 or 3 weeks’ time.
many european countries today face serious air quality problems, particularly in urban centres where there is a high population density and traffic. the european commission has been working for several years to develop a more reliable process for measuring nitric oxide emissions to reflect those under real driving conditions. this process was based on proper technical and scientific analysis, which is now being called into question under political pressure from member states and industry. this proposal for a delegated act is shameful because it is not based on objective technical criteria and because it was taken without any transparency, subverting the democratically approved political objectives in the basic legislative document. it is particularly shameful, following the volkswagen scandal, that it gives companies that do not comply with, or that falsify, european emission standards, a competitive advantage over those that already comply. i express my support for the position taken by the envi commission i consider this to be in the public interest; i'm taking your side!
in writing. if there are powerful lobbies within the eu institutions, and particularly within the one with the power of legislative initiative the european commission , influencing legislative proposals and leaving their indelible mark on them, one of these lobbies is the automotive industry. the developments surrounding the volkswagen emissions-manipulation scandal only confirm this fact. a technical committee of the european commission proposes to allow euro 6 diesel cars to emit more than twice the previously established limits between 2017 and 2019, allowing a 110% discrepancy between laboratory tests (which the industry manipulates more or less widely) and tests under real conditions. from 2020, this discrepancy could be as high as 50%, i.e. emissions 50% above the previously set limits. all this without any scientific backing. the commission's stated environmental ambition is thus at the doorstep of the vast interests of the multinational car companies. it is essential that measurements under real conditions are made as quickly as possible. but it is essential that they move forward in ways that ensure adequate protection of the environment and public health, and not the protection of the interests of multinationals against the people and the environment.

in writing. ‒ last august, the prosecutor-general of the republic of poland forwarded to the president of the european parliament a request from the polish road traffic inspectorate, requesting authorisation to take action against member czesław adam siekierski for a traffic offence. as the polish constitution provides that no criminal action may be brought against members of parliament or senate without the prior authorisation of the parliament or senate of which they are members, a decision of the european parliament is necessary to determine whether criminal action may be brought against mr siekierski. in this case, the request for waiver of the member's immunity was made as a result of an alleged infringement consisting of exceeding the speed limit applicable to urban agglomerations. it is apparent from the file that mr siekierski admitted that he was driving the vehicle at the time of the infringement, although he did not indicate on the relevant form whether or not he accepted the fine. the facts are not related to your activity as a member of the european parliament, agreeing to the waiver of parliamentary immunity.
in writing. ‒ this report deals with the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr czesław adam siekierski. here are the facts: the polish road traffic inspectorate claims that on 10 january 2015, when driving a vehicle, the member of parliament did not respect the speed limit applicable to urban agglomerations which is 50 km/h when driving the vehicle at a speed of 77 km/h. the inspectorate-general also states that in response to a notification sent to mr siekierski on 19 january 2015, he submitted a statement admitting that he was driving the vehicle at the time of the infringement. the facts of which he is accused constitute a violation of article 92 (a) of the polish code of criminal procedure, in conjunction with article 20 (1) of the law on road traffic of 20 june 1997. the alleged infringement has no direct and obvious connection with the performance of the duties of czesław adam siekierski as a member of the european parliament, and parliament has also found no substantiated evidence that the request is aimed at harming the member's political activity. that is why we voted to lift the immunity.
‒ i have voted in favour of the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr czeslaw adam siekierski. the immunity shall be waived where the case falls within the scope of article 9 of protocol no 7, provided that there is no serious and well-founded suspicion that the criminal action is being brought with the intention of causing political damage to the member concerned.
‒ i am voting in favour of this report because all the legal procedures have been completed and because the offence in question is not in any way connected with the performance of the duties of a member and because there is no evidence or suspicion that the criminal offence was committed with the intention of causing political damage to the member concerned.
‒ on 13 august 2015, the prosecutor general of poland requested the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr czesław adam siekierski in a criminal case initiated by the polish road traffic inspectorate, in which the member of the european parliament is accused of a traffic offence related to the breach of the speed limit applicable to urban agglomerations. in accordance with article 9 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament shall enjoy in their own state the immunities accorded to members of their national parliament. in this context, and taking into account the provisions of the constitution of the republic of poland, a decision of the european parliament is necessary to determine whether criminal proceedings may be brought against mr czesław adam siekierski. according to the report of the committee on legal affairs, it can be concluded, in the light of the circumstances of the case, that the alleged infringement is not related to the activity of mr czesław adam siekierski as a member of parliament, and there is no evidence of fumus persecutionis. in these terms, and in the light of the report, i voted in favour of this decision to waive the immunity of czesław adam siekierski.

in the light of the recent developments in the fisheries sector, the commission has decided to extend the current fishing season to the year 2000. it is up to the european commission to draw up proposals which respect the recommendations of iccat (international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas). we are taking the necessary measures to collaborate on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna, which ends in 2022. after several years of declining maximum allowable catches, there seems to be some growth, as there is scientific data proving that stocks have healthy levels of abundance. i agree with the rapporteur when he emphasises the objective of ensuring a level playing field for all operators involved in tuna fishing, including operators from third countries. otherwise, if other rules are applied to foreign fleets, all the efforts and restrictions applied to eu fishermen will have been in vain. i also appreciated the reference to artisanal frames, such as traditional frames (almadrabas), in the conservation of stock units. the european union should pay particular attention to these traditional frames, which contribute to the recovery of tuna stocks, as they are extremely selective. in addition, they have very little impact on marine ecosystems, thanks to their low level of energy consumption and bycatch.
‒ the european union is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), which has adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, which expires in 2022. to allow the stock to be rebuilt, the plan provides for a gradual reduction in the level of total allowable catches between 2007 and 2011, fishing restrictions in certain zones and periods, a new minimum size, measures related to sport and recreational fishing activities and fishing and farming capacities, and strengthens the iccat joint international inspection programme. the current tac in 2015 is 15 821 tonnes, of which 9 372,9 tonnes are for the eu. the proposal contains technical measures, such as those relating to live transfer and caging operations for bluefin tuna, including also measures on the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate bluefin tuna quantities and releases, catch reporting requirements and the implementation of the iccat regional observation programme, with which i agree.
‒ after the species had reached a critical state, the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna, adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) in 2006, allowed a positive evolution of the stocks. the biomass of this species has been showing a positive trend since 2008. in 2014, iccat decided to increase the tac by 20% for the three subsequent years (2015 to 2017). we generally follow the rapporteur's positions. we also support the criticism of a system of fishing quotas which penalizes small-scale fishing, which is more sustainable, for the benefit of the large shipowners of the main european fishing powers, and we therefore voted in favour of the amendment. portugal does not currently have an extractive fishery for bluefin tuna. in the azores, only by-catches of other tuna shall be authorised. the portuguese annual quota for atum-rabilho, 332 tonnes in 2016, is almost entirely exhausted by the existing algarve frames. this situation was to be changed, taking account of the more favourable context for the conservation of the species, by increasing the national quota and by granting azorean fishermen, who fish by jumping and using rods, the right to exploit this resource, which is now more abundant in the waters of the archipelago.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean, repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009. the eu, which is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), adopted a multiannual plan for this tuna in 2006, which only ends in 2022. bluefin tuna is the most important species regulated by iccat. every effort should be made to ensure that bluefin tuna continue to increase their stocks
‒ this proposal aims to ensure a uniform and effective application throughout the european union of all recovery plan measures adopted between 2012 and 2014 by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas. i agree with the rapporteur that uniform application should in principle ensure a level playing field for all tuna fishermen, including, in particular, those from third countries. the rapporteur warns that if other rules are applied to foreign fleets, all the effort and restrictions applied to eu fishermen will have been in vain. european union operators should not be penalised with more severe measures than those agreed. i also agree with the rapporteur's position on the specificities of the different tuna fishing gear. the role of artisanal farming, such as traditional farming, in the conservation of stocks and that, in the implementation of the recovery plan, the european union should pay particular attention to these traditional farming systems, which contribute to the recovery of tuna stocks, given that they are highly selective.
in writing. this proposal for a regulation aims to transpose into union law the measures of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) at its annual meetings between 2012 and 2014. iccat is the regional fisheries management organisation (rfm) responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas and has the authority to adopt binding recommendations which are subsequently to be transposed into union law. the proposal in question contains technical measures, relating, for example, to the transfer and caging of live bluefin tuna, the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate bluefin tuna quantities and releases, catch reporting requirements and the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme. the rapporteur generally considers that the proposal is a good transposition of the iccat recommendations. however, amendments were made to ensure that the recommendations are applied uniformly and that their transposition remains a joint competence of parliament and the council. i voted in favour.
‒ bluefin tuna is the most important species regulated by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas, which in 2006 adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan ending in 2022. i voted in favour of this report, which currently sets the total allowable catch at 15 821 tonnes, with the eu's share at 9 372.9 tonnes, given its importance for the fishermen of my region, the azores. fishermen have made considerable efforts to adjust their catches to the strict conditions set out in the plan. for this reason, and with a view to ensuring uniform and effective application throughout the european union, the proposal contains technical measures, including also measures on the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate the quantities of bluefin tuna and releases.
‒ according to the rapporteur, the recovery observed in recent years in the bluefin tuna stocks justifies the decision to bring forward to 2016 the tac (total allowable catch) for 2017 (23155 tonnes), which will still be well below the tac in force before the recovery plan enters into force. the s&d group has nevertheless succeeded in getting an amendment adopted to protect small fishermen against any form of monopoly, because it is a bit punitive for small fishermen.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur, gabriel mato, has done an important job and he refers to parliament a set of decisions which, as he points out, belong to parliament. this, combined with the importance of the protection of bluefin tuna and its protection plan, led me to vote in favour. i would like to stress that the amendment proposed by the socialists and democrats, which i also voted in favour of, stresses the importance of combating monopolies in fisheries. although the internal allocation of fishing quotas is a prerogative of the states, it is also the responsibility of the european union to make efforts to favour small-scale fisheries, such as those in regions such as the azores and madeira. if we continue to give aid to the large enterprises, we will strangle the pole-and-line fisheries, such as those in the outermost regions of the atlantic. i repeat the need to respect scientific recommendations and to use the precautionary principle without sparing. in the tuna fishery, too many fish aggregating devices are still being used without a serious environmental impact study.
‒ bluefin tuna stocks have been showing a positive trend since 2008. in 2014, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas decided to increase the tac by 20% for the following three years (2015 to 2017). we, for our part, support the criticism of a system of fishing quotas which penalizes small-scale, more sustainable fishing, to the benefit of the large shipowners of the main european fishing powers. it is important to recognize the role of the artisanal frames used in the south of portugal, in the algarve, and their potential and selectivity, and it is also important that the island fishermen who use the art of the pole and hop, who today see the bluefin tuna pass without being able to fish, see their right to fish this species recognized.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009, as i consider that the european commission proposal correctly transposes the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat). in 2006, iccat adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan which provided for a gradual reduction in the level of total allowable catches between 2007 and 2011. this proposal aims to integrate into a single regulation all the measures adopted between 2012 and 2014 by iccat, based on the proven increase in bluefin tuna since 2008, which was reflected in the gradual increase of the total allowable catch at international level. however, it is important that the quota system for bluefin tuna be revised under the new proposal and that the iccat recommendations be transposed into community law and applied uniformly throughout the eu, ensuring a level playing field for all operators involved in bluefin tuna fishing, in particular for small-scale fishermen.
‒ we generally follow the rapporteur's positions. we also support the criticism of a system of fishing quotas which penalizes small-scale fishing, which is more sustainable, for the benefit of the large shipowners of the main european fishing powers, and we therefore voted in favour of the amendment. portugal does not currently have an extractive fishery for bluefin tuna. in the azores, only by-catches of other tuna shall be authorised. the portuguese annual quota for atum rabilho, 332 tonnes in 2016, is almost fully exhausted by the existing algarve stockpiles. this situation was to be changed, taking account of the more favourable context for the conservation of the species, by increasing the national quota and by granting azorean fishermen, who fish by jumping and using rods, the right to exploit this resource, which is now more abundant in the waters of the archipelago.
‒ competition policy has always been an instrument for a healthy economy, with benefits for consumers, and not an instrument in itself. however, as the report points out, competition policy must be seen as a cross-cutting instrument with social impacts, in the consolidation of the internal market, in the creation of a digital single market or in the soundness of the banking system. the 2014 annual report also assesses competition policy in the light of the commitments made by president juncker and commissioner vestager. the report points out that, in the first year, the commission acted in all the areas it had promised. in particular, in the digital field, as regards the abusive practices of large multinationals, or at the level of state aid at the expense of taxpayers. however, the commission's performance has not been without faults and there is ample room for improvement. i would stress the transparency of the procedures and the need to genuinely involve parliament in the development of regulatory instruments which, in some cases, are genuine legislative measures and therefore go beyond the implementing powers of the european commission.
‒ the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) provides for binding rules on competition in the internal market, based on an open economy with free competition, prohibiting agreements and concerted practices between undertakings which affect trade between member states and give rise to the abuse of a dominant position. state aid to certain undertakings or products distorting competition in the internal market is generally prohibited, with a few exceptions, but may be authorised by the commission under certain conditions. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the aid is compatible with the internal market. the billions of euro in fines imposed as a result of price-fixing agreements should in future be effectively complemented by sanctions on company directors and managers to prevent this type of behaviour more effectively.
‒ eu competition policy does not prevent the concentration of economic and financial power in the hands of a few. on the contrary, this is the dynamic of the whole process of integration, given its capitalist nature. subjecting most public services and strategic sectors of the economy to the eu's competition policy and its single market has served the objectives of the large private economic groups who want to appropriate these services and sectors, subordinating them to the logic of the relentless search for maximum profit and minimum cost. under the false pretext of unfair competition or distortions of competition, this policy has resulted in legislation aimed at preventing public and democratic control of strategic sectors of the economy and the promotion of universal, free and quality public services. we support the call to stop social dumping, but the whole of eu policy is against it. the deepening of the single market and the elimination of so-called market restrictions serve the objectives of monopolistic concentration and deepen the divisions within the eu. we call for every effort to be made to cooperate among the member states and for a genuine commitment to combat tax havens and tax evasion and avoidance.
‒ competition regulation is essential for the smooth functioning of markets. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the market is not distorted by the introduction of new technologies, and that the market is not distorted by the introduction of new technologies. the annual report on eu competition policy is a key tool for analysing the state and evolution of a policy central to the definition of well-functioning markets and economic prosperity.
‒ the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) provides, in articles 101 to 109, for binding rules on competition in the common internal market, based on an open economy with free competition. i am voting in favour of this report, arguing that there should be free competition between companies and that the member states should only be in the role of regulators and monitor whether there is a dominant position. the european union must also give stronger support to all those entrepreneurs who want to start new businesses, especially those associated with the digital economy, because they have ample opportunities for job creation and wealth creation. finally, it is extremely important that social aid for the transport of residents of peripheral regions has been taken into account in the general block exemption regulation (gber), which now recognises the problem of connectivity. connectivity of peripheral island regions is also essential to maintain and develop acceptable levels of economic and social initiative through the maintenance of essential business links.

‒ mainstream economic theory points to the scarcity (or reduced enforcement) of financial regulation and supervision, lack of transparency and reporting as the main, and virtually the only, explanation for the financial crisis of 2007/08. for this reason, we have seen a high production of legislation in the eu in the area of regulation and supervision, which, its advocates claim, will prevent the emergence of new financial crises. it was a hoax. the most important changes are still to come: the separation of commercial and investment banking and the public control of banking. only such measures can protect the workers and peoples of the member states from paying for new 'adventures' of high finance. the european commission has also proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by smes. its main objective, however, is to increase profits in the financial sector. its promoters say that improvements in legislation will prevent a crisis like the one in 2007/2008. another con. we voted against it.

‒ although entrepreneurship has been identified as a political priority since the start of the lisbon treaty, the truth is that the european union is still somewhat behind in this area. entrepreneurship is fundamental to employment, economic growth, innovation, development and poverty reduction in general. indeed, it is widely recognised that in order to restore growth and create new jobs, the european union needs more entrepreneurs and its strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth (europe 2020) explicitly states that more concrete policy initiatives are needed to develop european entrepreneurship. in this context, female entrepreneurship deserves particular attention, as equality in terms of economic independence remains uncertain in the european union and the employment rate for women, which stood at 59,6% in 2014 at eu-28 level, is neither in line with the europe 2020 employment target of 75% nor with the male employment rate of 70,1%. this report deals with the issue of female entrepreneurship, identifying the obstacles to it and proposing ways of overcoming them. i voted in favour.

‒ differences between men and women are still noticeable in entrepreneurial careers. in 2012, of all eu-28 citizens who were self-employed, only 31% were women. when women set up businesses, they are more likely to do so in sectors related to human health, social action or education, while male entrepreneurs are more present in areas of the construction, transport and ict sectors. it's no wonder that the net income of female entrepreneurs was 6% lower than that of men in 2012. in addition, women's enterprises remain smaller, with only 23% of female entrepreneurs being employers, compared with 30% of men. the work-life balance that entrepreneurship can offer women represents a first obstacle to their success, as it can lead them into a vicious circle where they create fewer opportunities to gain management experience to run their businesses, consolidate their credit history and gain the trust of investors. we're still working to reverse this.

in writing. the report reflects on the unemployment figures that have been plaguing the european union, focusing mainly on youth unemployment. the unemployment rate in the eu in 2014 was on average 9.9% (in portugal it was around 20%), youth unemployment was 21.4% and in the most affected countries, such as portugal, it was above 30%. the report proposes measures to combat youth unemployment. there are positive aspects, such as the defence of the increase in qualifications, criticism of the increase in the costs of attending the various levels of education, the valorisation of local economies and traditional know-how, the affirmation of a holistic education (against the tendency to specialise), the reference to the exploitation of trainees, the defence of the fight against some forms of discrimination. however, there are also negative aspects, most notably the advocacy of adapting curricula, programmes and education/training provision to the needs of the 'labour market'; the overvaluation of 'entrepreneurship', with the advocacy of its inclusion in school curricula and the affirmation of mobility as a response to the problems of youth unemployment. the solution to youth unemployment is to break with the policies that have been imposed on us and break with those who impose them. the present and future of young people depend on it.

in writing. ‒ there are currently 4.5 million unemployed young people aged 15-24 in the european union and more than 7 million young europeans in the same age group are not working, studying or training. the union-wide unemployment rate stood at 9,9% at the end of 2014 and the youth unemployment rate was more than double that at 21,4%. this situation seriously threatens the social cohesion and economic development of the eu. the solution will require a new approach to factors such as globalisation, demographic change, the economic crisis, new technologies and changes in the organisation of work. an approach that puts people back at the centre of the economy, not the other way around.

madam high representative, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, 2016 could be the most decisive year in colombia's recent history, with the signing of the peace agreement with the farc guerrillas, scheduled for march, putting an end to a conflict that, in half a century, has killed more than 220 000 people and left a lasting mark on colombian society. the european union, which has always encouraged the establishment of peace negotiations, will have to offer its full support to the government of juan manuel santos at this decisive moment in the implementation of this final peace agreement, as well as in the complex post-conflict challenges, plans which will require enormous resources: support for the strengthening of the economy, the reintegration of guerrillas, the transformation of guerrillas into political parties and compensation for victims, in the name of a lasting and lasting peace in colombia. i also believe, ladies and gentlemen, that the solution to consolidating the peace process in colombia will inevitably be national reconciliation, as mrs mogherini has rightly said, in the name of lasting peace in colombia. i conclude, mr president, by hoping and wishing that this parliament will take a different approach to colombia than it unfortunately took to venezuela in its recent democratic transition process, where it was absent.

mr president, the dutch presidency will be confronted with the daunting challenge of responding to the refugee crisis and protecting the schengen area. but you can be sure that if you want european citizens to be united in this great undertaking, you also need to ensure much stronger recovery. much stronger recovery means, to start with, an ambitious strategy for growth and jobs, updating europe 2020 and making the best use of the energy transition and the digital revolution. this is definitely needed. but let me say that the single market is important but it is not enough. you need to ensure that the investment plan will be implemented much more swiftly. you also need to tackle the difficult problems of tax avoidance and tax evasion in europe. we can no longer go on with the unfair competition between multinationals and smes, between member states. we need to support the commission action plan on tax policy and make sure that we have full transparency, we have country-by-country reporting and we ensure that taxes are paid where profits are made. but then we also have another problem, namely the euro area. the euro-area crisis is still there. we cannot be mistaken about this. it is still there which means that the problem is not only stability, but bringing convergence upwards – upward social and economic convergence. to do this you need to make sure that all members of the euro area have similar investment conditions. this will depend on completing the banking union and on providing a proper fiscal capacity for the euro area. this is also an important roadmap for the dutch presidency to push for.
mr president, the deepening of the single market is presented as the panacea for all ills - unemployment, poverty or the absence of growth. it is true that this deepening, in addition to fuelling the attack on the rights, public services and social functions of the state, is one of the driving forces behind the growing inequalities between the member states. moreover, like the common policies, the euro and economic and monetary union, it is a ruthless machine of divergence. the instrument which could mitigate this divergence or, preferably, counteract it - the budget of the european union - has been reduced to poverty, is the lowest ever. there is no indication that the situation will change during the dutch presidency, although it would be imperative to make an interim review, which would substantially increase this budget, especially when it is already clear who will benefit from the juncker plan - mainly the great powers and their economic groups. in a euro zone still mired in crisis, the problem of peripheral debts, which are among the largest in the world and have long demonstrated their unsustainability, continues to be ignored. as far as refugees are concerned, the european union continues to show one of its most inhuman faces.
mr president, i would first of all like to congratulate the dutch presidency on its programme. it is a very ambitious programme and it is essentially on the right track. i would just like to stress two aspects. the first concerns the refugee question and therefore the problem of migration, and here i would sincerely like to see a greater commitment from the dutch presidency to the creation of a border guard and a coast guard, because i think this is the essential pillar, on the one hand, to defend our borders, but also to create what will be the embryo of a security policy and even a defence policy of the european union. if we have this force, which is part military, part police force, working - and unfortunately the results of the december council were disappointing - i think we can make a great step forward in protecting our borders and in defending the status of refugees, and even in migration policy for the union. the second aspect is a more negative one and has to do with the question of international trade. i have noticed that the priorities of the dutch presidency do not include mercosur. mercosur made its offer to the european union last year. how can the dutch presidency leave behind countries like brazil, argentina, uruguay and paraguay? how can there be a bet here, as we see in the case of, for example, mexico, in renegotiation, and if it is creating the most important trade space in latin america, and the eu is completely paralysed? this is strange, especially coming from the dutch presidency, which has historical relations with brazil and which has the suriname and the netherlands antilles space right on this front. it is strange that a country with this tradition has forgotten mercosur.
mr president, i welcome the ambitious programme of the dutch presidency of the european union and the capacity for choice it shows. these are four priorities, but they are four priorities which, if they are to be dealt with with with results, imply the mobilisation of all the resources and agendas of the european union. responding to the challenges of migration and security threats is a priority closely linked to the confidence of a successful innovation and job creation drive. at the same time, innovation and job creation will benefit from the leadership taken in delivering the paris climate agenda and from the commitment to the energy tradition and the digital revolution. but i would also like to point out, mr prime minister, a shortcoming in the priority of your presidency: trade agreements. the netherlands has a strong tradition of trade agreements. the progress made in the transatlantic partnership and mercosur was very important. i call for mercosur to be a priority of the dutch presidency.

‒ this report aims at the launch in latvia of the automated exchange of vehicle registration data (vrd) in the context of the deepening of crossborder cooperation prüm decision (2008/615/jha) in the fight against terrorism and crime. the provision of personal data provided for under that decision may not take place until the general provisions on data protection have been transposed into national law in the territory of the member states participating in that transmission. the prüm convention, signed in may 2005 in prüm, germany, between seven member states austria, belgium, france, germany, luxembourg, spain and the netherlands aims to intensify and accelerate the exchange of information between authorities. we know that under the pretext of fighting terrorism and crime, the eu has been setting up a surveillance system which reduces the freedoms and guarantees of citizens and which calls into question the sovereignty of states in the control and safeguarding of data and information. the aim is to create a supranational structure which will progressively impose on the member states strategies and actions outside national and democratic control. we therefore voted against.

‒ the commission has presented the final package procedural rights containing three proposals for a directive, following the adoption of the first three instruments of the european union's roadmap for strengthening procedural rights. these three directives will complete the european legal framework on the rights of defence of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings throughout the european union. the proposal strengthens certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at trial in criminal proceedings. i voted in favour.
‒ this report is based on the presentation of the final package procedural rights, which contains three proposals for a directive that are part of the eu roadmap for strengthening procedural rights. these directives aim to complete the european legal framework on the rights of defence of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings throughout the eu. it is worth noting that a process of reducing the rights and safeguards of suspects and accused persons is under way in certain member states. the presumption of innocence is an essential principle to prevent arbitrariness and any abuse in criminal proceedings, and is a principle underlying the protection of the right to a fair trial, in accordance with article 11 (1) of the universal declaration of human rights, which states that 'everyone accused of a criminal offence shall be presumed innocent until proven guilty in a public trial in which all necessary guarantees of defence have been provided'. in the light of the content of the proposal, it is worth noting that portuguese law already provides these guarantees in essence. the commission's proposal is not a new one, but it is a new one, and it is a new one.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on the strengthening of certain aspects of the rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, namely the presumption of innocence until proven guilty by a final decision and the right to appear at trial. the presumption of innocence and the right to be tried in criminal proceedings are fundamental values for a state to be considered to be a state governed by the rule of law, a value enshrined in article 6 of the echr, article 48 of the cfreu, the iccpr and the udhr.
in writing. - i vote in favour of this report because it deals substantially with the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at trial in criminal proceedings. the principle of the presumption of innocence, or of non-guilt, is a fundamental principle of criminal procedure and establishes the status of innocence as a rule with regard to the accused of committing a criminal offence. this proposal aims to ensure that the principle of the presumption of innocence is applied at all stages of criminal proceedings. in this connection, i believe it is essential to extend the scope of application of a fundamental principle of the rule of law, the 'presumption of innocence of the accused', which is also enshrined in the declaration of the rights of man and of the citizen, the universal declaration of human rights and the european convention on human rights.
‒ this proposal for a directive is part of a broader package to strengthen the rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, in order to ensure full respect for their rights of defence and a fair trial throughout the european union. to that end, it lays down minimum standards concerning certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at the trial itself. on 4 november 2015, the council and parliament agreed on this proposal, and parliament succeeded in achieving some objectives, in particular with regard to: clarifying the temporal scope of the directive (the directive applies at all stages of the procedure from the time a person is considered a suspect or accused person until the final conclusion of the procedure); prohibiting any statement by public authorities presuming the guilt of the accused or suspect; and enshrining the principle that the burden of proof is on the prosecution and the right to remain silent. this is a particularly important initiative, as the presumption of innocence is an essential dimension of the right to a fair trial. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ the presumption of innocence is a fundamental right and an essential principle to avoid arbitrariness and any abuse in criminal proceedings. the proposal for a directive which i voted for is particularly important, since in many of the member states of the european union there is a reduction in the rights of suspects and accused persons, as well as an erosion of the principle of the presumption of innocence. the commission initially adopted a minimalist approach and may 'level down' national provisions. the proposal is therefore to clarify the scope of the directive, both at the personal, temporal and material level. the right to remain silent, the right not to incriminate oneself, the right not to cooperate and the right to be present at one's own trial are also fundamental elements. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour of this report. it is essential to protect suspects or accused persons from premature convictions and it is important that member states ensure appropriate legislation to prevent the usual violations of the presumption of innocence by the media.
‒ the adoption of rules guaranteeing the presumption of innocence is an important step towards balancing repressive measures and the right of individuals to a fair trial. the court of human rights believes that there are some minimum requirements for the presumption of innocence that must be generally respected: the right not to be publicly declared guilty by the authorities before trial; the burden of proof that must be on the prosecution; the right of the accused to be informed of the charges against him; the right to be present in court; the right not to cooperate and to remain silent (and to be informed of this right). these are requirements that all eu member states must comply with. only then can we have the necessary legitimacy to demand them from third countries.

‒ this proposal for a regulation on personal protective equipment updates directive 89/686/eec in line with the new legislative framework, harmonising and clarifying the regulatory requirements in this area. although the directive has successfully achieved its objectives of creating a single market and ensuring a high level of protection for users of personal protective equipment, some problems have been encountered in its implementation. ppe is any means or device intended to be used by a person against possible risks to his health or safety while performing a certain activity. i support the ford report because i believe that this new proposal amends and clarifies a number of provisions of the existing directive, bringing it into line with the provisions of decision no 768/2008/ec establishing a common framework for the marketing of products.
‒ the placing of personal protective equipment (ppe) on the eu market has been fully harmonised by council directive 89/686/eec. over the 25 years since then, this directive has enabled the single market to function smoothly. however, the current legislation on ppe needs to be updated. this regulation clarifies the role of economic operators, enhances cooperation between actors and introduces common definitions. the proposal essentially concerns the modernisation and simplification of a system which is already working well and does not require substantial changes to its objectives. the amendments are therefore intended to clarify certain aspects, on the basis of reservations made by member states and by the security industry federations. the report also proposes to eliminate the maximum five-year period of validity of the eu type-examination certificate, taking into account reservations made by economic operators. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ it is proposed that directive 89/686/eec be replaced by a regulation, given the lack of flexibility in its transposition. the purpose of this directive was to harmonise health and safety requirements for personal protective equipment (ppe) in all member states and to remove barriers to trade in such equipment. this regulation lays down requirements for the design and manufacture of ppe intended to be placed on the market in order to ensure the protection of the health and safety of users and to lay down rules on the free movement of ppe within the eu. it is essential that ppe does not endanger the health or safety of persons, domestic animals or property. it is therefore imperative that health and safety rules are well defined and therefore respected. it is also essential that smes in the member states active in this sector, in particular manufacturers, can receive the necessary support (technical and financial) to respond correctly and in a timely manner to the changes introduced by the regulation, since such legal changes should not constitute a blanket way of favouring the largest companies in the sector and therefore increasing the concentration of market power.

the european union's deliberate strategy in the fight against terrorism is to curb democratic freedom and individual freedoms. insisting on the pilgrim thesis of the false freedom/security dichotomy, supporting a militaristic vision of the alleged fight against terrorism which, instead of weakening, strengthens the logic of hatred and war. the repeated imposition of increased measures that undermine fundamental rights and freedoms, which is always accompanied by the escalation of the militarization of international relations, war and interference and destabilization of sovereign states, feeds the growth of racist, xenophobic and fascist forces and their terrorist action. horrible crimes, such as those committed in paris or those which have been perpetrated for years in various places around the world, call for a policy of peace in international relations and respect for international law, which puts an end to interference and aggression against sovereign states, particularly in the middle east region, which have led to the resurgence of terrorist groups.
we have not been able to protect our citizens against the threat of terrorism and related organised crime, which does not take us by surprise and requires us to work in a coordinated way at european level, because no country can overcome it alone. we are paying the price for the lack of coordination in syria, iraq, libya and the palestinian question. we need to work for peace and security in the neighbourhood and to tackle the sources of funding for terrorism, such as the trafficking of human beings, arms, oil and drugs, including by governments that claim to be our allies, such as saudi arabia, turkey and qatar. we need to coordinate our support for the resistance forces on the ground, such as the peshmerga, and provide more effective aid to displaced people and refugees to reoccupy and rebuild liberated areas, such as sinjar, because it is not with walls and the end of schengen, the closure of borders, that we will stop those who flee barbarism from coming. internally we suffer from disunity and distrust; we resist sharing information against terrorism and taking action against organized crime. we have failed to create an effective european pnr, to counteract recruitment advertising; and with the neoliberal policies that create more unemployment and ghettos, we have actually facilitated the radicalization campaign of europe's own young people who are joining the ranks of the so-called islamic state, within our borders and even within our prisons. in addition to the dismay we display, we have helped terrorists with the wave of xenophobia, which now miserably attacks the refugees fleeing terrorism and war and whom we have an obligation to welcome. we do not need to invent anything; we need political will and a sense of strategic interest in a world governed by the rule of law and human rights. the solutions lie in an intelligent and coherent articulation of our internal and external security policies. what we need is for our governments to work together. this is a european problem and the main weapon we need is unity, european union. blue-card answer.– well, my country has actually volunteered to accept up to 5 000 refugees in these coming months, but they are not coming because the system is not working. but those who have come are, actually, indeed properly supported to be socially integrated. having access to work, for instance, is very important apart from other aspects – to actually work according to the rules in our society. social inclusion is the most important thing, and all the economically liberal policies that have only been fostering social exclusion and discrimination, in particular in communities of migrants, is actually what has been helping the terrorists recruit young people within our borders and to fight both abroad and against us.
mr president, the fight against terrorism begins with the fight against racism, xenophobia and fanaticism, and continues with a ceaseless struggle for democracy, the rule of law and individual freedoms, especially the freedom of movement of all european citizens. the europe in which i believe and for which i grieve is, as georg steiner teaches, a europe which is the daughter of athens and the enlightenment, but also the daughter of jerusalem and the three revealed religions, that is, a europe culturally constructed from the three religions of jerusalem: christianity, judaism and islam. for centuries europe has persecuted and even tried to exterminate many of its citizens, the jews, and now, under the pretext of fighting terrorism, it is preparing to segregate, persecute and expel muslims. mr president, commissioner, minister, the fight against the radicalisation so in vogue must begin with the fight against the intolerance that is dangerously developing within europe.
mr president, the recent terrorist attacks in turkey and burkina faso, following those in 2015, reinforce the evidence not only of the increase in the terrorist threat, but also of its transnational character and its universalist pretensions, which require a global and holistic response in order to prevent and combat it. in the fight against terrorism, the european union must not only strengthen cooperation in the military and security components, but also in the prevention of radicalisation, in the sources of funding, as well as in logistical support and in medical and hospital care for combatants who on the war fronts defend with their own lives our values and our model of civilisation. it is therefore a shame to hear from the mouth of a peshmerga soldier that wounded combatants in need of medical care in europe have to pay out of their own pockets for the treatment they need here in europe, because they do not have sufficient help from the european union. mr president, i once again call on the european union to ensure that the fight against terrorism does not involve the sacrifice of human rights and that refugees are not allowed to become the collateral victims of the terrorists who are actually the ones who are at the forefront of the atrocities being committed.
‒ the stabilisation and association agreement between the eu and kosovo (saa) was negotiated between october 2013 and may 2014 and initialled in july 2014. the eea establishes contractual relations which provide for enhanced political dialogue, greater trade integration and new forms of cooperation. it covers a number of areas, including respect for and strengthening of democratic principles and human rights, and the establishment of a framework for cooperation in areas such as education, energy, the environment, justice and home affairs. it also includes provisions to promote european standards in areas such as competition, public procurement, intellectual property and consumer protection, and aims to create a free trade area. i agree that the saa is a very important first formal step in the eu accession process and the council should adopt the decision to sign and conclude the framework agreement on kosovo's participation in eu programmes, which will strengthen cooperation between kosovo and the eu in different sectors.

‒ the developments surrounding the volkswagen scandal, concerning the manipulation of data on light vehicle emissions, once again show that we are facing a european commission gripped by lobbies, in this case the automobile industry lobby, one of the most powerful in the eu institutions, influencing legislative proposals and leaving their indelible mark on them. following a warning from the us environmental protection agency (epa) and the california air resources board (carb) that the volkswagen group had violated pollution standards and recent data showing a large discrepancy between nitrous oxide emissions measured under laboratory conditions and under normal driving conditions, the european parliament approved the establishment of a committee of inquiry to investigate alleged breaches and maladministration in the application of eu law in this area, without prejudice to the jurisdiction of national courts. the purpose of this committee will be to investigate and collect data on alleged failures of the european commission and member states to comply with the obligations imposed by regulation (ec) no 715/2007. we will follow your work closely and will not fail to intervene so that light can be shed on this case.
in writing. - i have given my approval to the composition of the members of the committee of inquiry into the measurement of emissions in the automotive sector. the commission of inquiry will be tasked with examining alleged infringements of european rules on emission measurements in the automotive sector.
‒ the ongoing infringement proceedings against directive 2008/50/ec, directive 2007/46/ec and regulation (ec) no 125/2007 of the european parliament and of the council have led to a request for the establishment of a temporary committee of inquiry to examine alleged breaches of union law and maladministration in the application of community provisions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. under this regulation, the committee of inquiry is to investigate the alleged failure of the commission to comply with the obligation to review the test cycles used to measure emissions and the alleged failure of the commission and the member states authorities to provide for measures to control and prohibit tampering devices, to introduce tests that reflect real driving conditions and to lay down provisions on applicable penalties, ensuring that applicable penalties are enforced. i voted in favour.

‒ following the terrorist attacks in paris, the president of the french republic declared that france is at war. this allocation of 16 november 2015 was followed by the invocation of the mutual defence clause provided for in article 42 (7) of the treaty on european union, which triggers aid and assistance to the requesting country by all means available to the member states. this unprecedented request was met with ad hoc measures, ad hoc management and ad hoc cooperation, which exposed the absence of practical arrangements and guidelines indispensable to give an effective response to the invocation of the clause. the rapporteur considers that basic and fundamental structures are lacking in the solidarity effort to help france. without them, cooperation and coordination between member states will not be possible. in this context, the report recommends the creation of a permanent civilian-military headquarters for strategic and operational planning in collective defence. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls on the council and the member states to make progress in establishing a political framework to guide the implementation of the above-mentioned article.

in writing. ‒ in the 2015-2017 biennium, portugal is a member of the united nations human rights council. this resolution is therefore of particular importance to us portuguese and presents a set of guidelines on the major challenges in 2016, as well as some ways forward and criticisms. i cannot fail to highlight the challenges facing the right of asylum, the fight against the death penalty and women's rights. i should also like to point out the recommendation that the union itself should defend and promote human rights in a coordinated manner across all its policies. finally, i would remind you that portugal is among the countries which respect and promote fundamental rights on their territory. unfortunately, not all members of this un council do. as the resolution points out, i do not think that is reasonable.
‒ the promotion of respect for human rights, irrespective of race, origin, religion, class, caste, gender, sexual orientation or colour, is an obligation of all states, which have the obligation to respect the fundamental rights of their populations and the duty to take concrete measures to facilitate respect for these rights at national level, as well as to cooperate at international level with a view to eliminating obstacles to the realization of human rights in all areas. i therefore believe that the members of the unhrc should be elected from among states which uphold respect for human rights, the rule of law and democracy, based on criteria of human rights performance.
‒ the european union is facing numerous challenges today, ranging from the humanitarian crisis of the wave of asylum applications, to climate change, to the fight against terrorism, which require concerted action and enhanced cooperation from the union. at the unhrc sessions, the european union should lead the process with one voice to address internal and external challenges.
‒ i agree that respect for, and the promotion and safeguarding of, the universality of human rights are part of the legal and ethical acquis of the european union. they are fundamental principles of european unity and integrity and ensure internal and external coherence in the field of human rights in external relations. i would like to stress my dismay at the continuing violations of women's rights, the emergence of violent extremist groups such as boko haram in west africa and is in syria and iraq, and the violence against the most vulnerable. i would also like to stress the plight of refugees and migrants, one of the greatest humanitarian scourges of recent times, created by the exponential increase in the number of people forced to leave their countries because of armed conflict and widespread violence. all countries should safeguard the rights of migrants and refugees in migration policies, with particular attention to marginalized and disadvantaged groups such as women and children.
‒ the united nations human rights council (unhrc) is a part of the supporting body to the united nations general assembly, established to assess the human rights situation in all member states of the organisation. in order to achieve a full understanding of the human rights situation in all member states, the unhrc has a universal periodic review mechanism. the review assesses the situation of the parties, advising the general assembly on the promotion and safeguarding of human rights on the one hand, and formulating specific recommendations to member states, which are intended to effect real change on the ground, on the other. despite the recommendations contained in the universal periodic review, some members of the human rights council are among the most serious human rights offenders. in this regard, and in order to be able to follow up on the unhrc recommendations, the rapporteur urges the european union and its member states to explore ways and means of implementing the unhrc recommendations. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this resolution of the european parliament, which reaffirms the universality of human rights and, therefore, the obligation to enforce them.
‒ this report expresses deep concern about human rights and democratic values (such as freedom of expression, thought, conscience and religion), as well as the fact that the public space for civil society is shrinking and that an increasing number of human rights defenders are being attacked worldwide. the report was voted in favour, as it calls on the eu and the member states to redouble their efforts to put human rights and democratic values at the heart of their relations with the rest of the world, and reiterates the importance of ensuring greater coherence between the eu's internal and external policies.
‒ the members of the united nations human rights council (unhrc) should be elected from among states which uphold respect for human rights, the rule of law and democracy. un member states should promote human rights performance-based criteria as a condition for a state to be elected as a member of the unhrc. we are concerned about human rights violations in some of the newly elected unhrc member states. hence the importance of the universality of the universal periodic review (upr) in order to achieve a full understanding of the human rights situation in all un member states. it is also necessary to ensure the participation of a wide range of stakeholders, including civil society, in this review.

‒ the annual report of the united nations high commissioner for human rights contains very positive aspects such as the points on the economic crisis and its consequences on the peoples, especially those in the 2015 report: increasing inequalities and the political, economic and social exclusion of marginalised groups undermine the dignity and rights of peoples in many states and are largely responsible for the emergence of the above problems and conflicts. economic, social and cultural rights, as well as the right to development, have suffered from austerity policies which, together with corruption, have disproportionately affected the poor and the marginalised. it is therefore time to look at the european union itself, where the arrogant practice of trying to teach the world lessons prevails when, within it, the rights of the people are not respected and democracy is repeatedly disrespected.
‒ the committee on petitions does essential work in the relationship between citizens and the eu institutions. the eu treaties give all european citizens the right to address the european parliament to report on various types of problems they face in their daily lives, provided that the issues raised are within the framework of the european union's activities. i support this annual report, which i consider to be of great importance, as it provides a precise and complete picture of the work of the committee on petitions, enabling us to know the number of petitions received, closed or dealt with by the committee, or the countries or issues concerned, and is an important quantitative tool in evaluating the work of the committee. this tool allows members and european bodies to be closer to citizens and to any misapplication of european law by member states.
‒ according to statistics, in 2014 the european parliament received 2 714 petitions, a decrease of 6% compared to 2 891 in 2013. this annual report aims to provide a precise and complete picture of the work of the committee on petitions by presenting statistics on the number of petitions received, closed or dealt with by the committee, or on the countries or issues concerned, which constitute an important quantitative tool in evaluating the work of the committee. the annual statistics show that the majority of citizens turn to parliament for help on issues relating to justice, the environment, the internal market and fundamental rights. other petitioners seek to make their proposals for the implementation of union policies heard and others still address the european parliament to challenge decisions taken by national authorities and to appeal against judgments of national courts. others also point to shortcomings in the application of european legislation, either due to faulty transposition of legislation, non-application of community rules or violation of them.
‒ the right to petition is intended, together with the european ombudsman, to deal with cases of maladministration by the eu institutions, or national institutions, in the context of the application of eu law. it often coincides with the simultaneous filing of a complaint with the european commission, which may lead to the initiation of a non-compliance procedure or an action for failure to act. in 2014, 1 887 petitions were closed, of which 1 070 were declared inadmissible. these figures correspond to an increase of around 10% compared to 2013. the most pressing issues addressed in the petitions concern environmental legislation (water and waste management, oil and gas exploration and extraction, and major infrastructure and development projects); fundamental rights (in particular children's rights and the rights of persons with disabilities); the free movement of persons, discrimination, immigration, the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) negotiations; animal welfare, the administration of justice and the social inclusion of persons with disabilities. despite the indisputable correctness of most of the causes underlying many of the petitions, we do not follow up on several of the observations and recommendations contained in the report, nor on some aspects of the philosophy of this instrument.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on the activities of the committee on petitions in 2014. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon confirmed the right to petition the european parliament as one of the pillars of european citizenship and as a fundamental right under article 227 of the treaty. it is important to know and to be aware of citizens' concerns about different eu policies and legislation.
‒ the right to petition the european parliament, already provided for in article 227 of the maastricht treaty, was confirmed as a pillar of european citizenship and as a fundamental right by the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. it is a tool which provides a simple means for citizens to approach the institutions of the union and to submit a complaint or request on any matter relating to their fields of activity. the 2014 annual report aims to summarise and present the work of the committee on petitions by compiling statistical data on the number of petitions received, closed or dealt with by the committee, or on the countries or issues concerned. in the light of the foregoing, i supported the rapporteur's conclusions in my vote, considering them to be an indispensable descriptive and quantitative tool in the evaluation of parliamentary work.
‒ any citizen of the european union or resident in a member state may, individually or in association with others, submit a petition to the european parliament on matters falling within the scope of the activities of the european union and which affect him or her directly. this was a huge opportunity as a result of the lisbon treaty. the annual report on the committee on petitions aims to provide a precise and complete picture of the work of the committee by presenting statistics on the number of petitions received, closed or dealt with by the committee, or on the countries or issues concerned, which are an important quantitative tool in evaluating the work of the committee. according to statistics, in 2014 the european parliament received 2714 petitions, which represents a decrease of 6% compared to the declarations submitted in 2013. in relation to 2013, there were several changes in the list of countries of origin of the petitions in 2014, with spain remaining in the first place. justice was the main subject of the petitions filed during the two years. i voted in favour of this report because of the commitment and quality of the work presented.
‒ the number of petitions received in 2014 amounted to 2714, representing a decrease of around 6% compared to 2013, when parliament received 2885 petitions. 790 petitions were considered admissible and acted upon, 1070 were considered inadmissible, 817 were declared admissible and closed and 37 had their recommendation challenged. the purpose of this annual report on the activities of the committee on petitions is to present an analysis of the petitions received in 2014 and to discuss possible improvements to the procedures and relations with the other institutions.
‒ with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the right to petition the european parliament has emerged as one of the pillars of european citizenship and as a fundamental right enabling citizens of the union to petition the european parliament, either individually or in association with other citizens. this right, which now allows any matter falling within the union's fields of activity and directly affecting it to be reported to this institution, is a key instrument for citizens to express their concerns about the effects of different eu policies and legislation on their daily lives, as well as acting as a proactive mechanism for european citizens' initiative. this report calls on the european commission to respond to the requests for inquiry contained in the petitions within three months, together with the peti commission. it also urges the member states' authorities to participate more actively in their meetings, not only by generating public debate and scrutiny, but also by highlighting the importance of the european citizens' initiative as a new tool for participatory democracy at eu level, with a view to publicly exposing any anomalous, irregular or illegal situations. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of this report.

madam president, the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work must be a shared effort, for the european union and the member states. undocumented work harms the union economy, jeopardises the financial sustainability of social protection systems, generates unfair competition by distorting market laws, leads to a lack of social and labour protection for workers and often has a cross-border dimension. a large proportion of undeclared workers are particularly vulnerable, including women, migrants and domestic workers. a particularly worrying area in this area is the use of young trainees to replace temporarily absent professionals. under the guise of vocational training, some companies are actually using these young people for non-specialised professional tasks, paying them no pay or much less than the work they have done.
madam president, undeclared work is a social and economic scourge with very deep and complex roots, which seriously harms workers in their social and labour rights, has serious budgetary implications and leads to a reduction in tax revenue and social security contributions. i therefore welcome the commission's initiative to create a european platform to strengthen cooperation in the fight against undeclared work, for which the involvement of the social partners is indispensable. but beyond sharing good practices on how member states articulate the prevention and punishment of such abusive situations, it is essential to promote duly reported work and also to combat abuses against workers. i am referring not only to paid activities which become illegal because they are not properly declared to the competent authorities, but also to false selfemployment situations. however, we can only effectively prevent undeclared work situations if we create real incentives for workers and employers to realise that they only have advantages in declaring work done. i would therefore draw the commission's attention to the need to reduce overall taxes on labour and to increase benefits for workers and their families in the form of social assistance. i call on the commission to encourage member states to move towards other forms of tax revenue and to invest in health care, pensions and unemployment support, which will limit the temptation to evade tax through the unregulated employment relationship that has been undeclared work.

‒ this regulation, commonly referred to as the 'schengen borders code', was adopted in 2006 and consolidates and develops the legislative policy component of integrated border management in the european union. over the years it has undergone six alterations. among the most important is the establishment of common rules on the temporary reintroduction of internal border control in exceptional circumstances, under the so-called 'schengen governance package'. the amendments which i support now merely consolidate the text which has resulted from the amendments to the original regulation, so as to allow it to be better applied and interpreted.
