‒ the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission concluded in its opinion that the proposal in question is simply a codification of the existing texts without any substantive changes. i am voting in favour of this report, which stresses that the setting of rules for the crossing of borders cannot be done sufficiently by the member states and can be better achieved at union level. to this end, the union shall take the necessary measures in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union. in accordance with the principle of proportionality, as set out in that article, that regulation and its successive amendments do not go beyond what is necessary in order to achieve that objective.
in writing. the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it by merely codifying the existing texts without any substantive changes. the amendments focus mainly on clarifying the definition, the entry conditions for third-country nationals and the duration of validity of certain travel documents. the amendments also extend the exemption from stamping of travel documents for train and bus crews on international routes, as is already the case for airline crews. this includes measures to train border guards to detect situations of unaccompanied minors and victims of trafficking. regardless of the assessment of these minor amendments, we do not change our previous thinking on schengen. we are not keeping pace with the increasing harmonisation of immigration and border policies, which oblige member states to report on the bilateral agreements they establish under the schengen borders code. nor is there any obligation for member states to inform when 'legal' third-country nationals enter another member state.
‒ this regulation lays down the rules for the control of persons crossing the external borders of the member states of the union. this report, which i voted for, was drawn up in such a way as to ensure full respect for human dignity and to ensure that border control is not only in the interest of the member state at whose external borders it is carried out, but in the interest of all the member states which have abolished control at their internal borders. those measures should continue to contribute to the fight against illegal immigration and trafficking in human beings, as well as to the prevention of any threat to the internal security, public order and health, and the international relations of the member states.
‒ this report concerns a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the compilation of a set of scattered legislation on the rules governing the movement of persons across borders with a view to establishing a community code (schengen borders code). in view of the growing terrorist threat in europe and the international measures taken to combat this escalation of violence, this proposal for a regulation codifies the existing rules on the passage of persons at border controls by means of a preliminary analysis of the risks to internal security and of the threats that may affect the security of the external borders. in an area without internal border controls such as the eu, there is a need for a common response to situations that could seriously affect public policy or internal security, thus allowing for the temporary introduction of internal border control in exceptional circumstances, without jeopardising the principle of free movement of persons. in view of the exceptional nature of this measure (which is of a very technical nature), i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 562/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 15 march 2006 establishes the community code on the rules governing the movement of persons across borders (schengen borders code), which has been amended several times. the new regulation voted on today will replace the various acts incorporated in it, merely codifying the existing texts without any substantive changes.
in writing. - i support the report by mr la via on the strengthening of the fight against heavy metal pollution. the 1998 aarhus protocol on heavy metals aims to reduce and control man-made emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury into the atmosphere. it aims to reduce annual emissions of the three metals to levels below those recorded in 1990. as the rapporteur points out, the protocol aims to reduce emissions from industrial sources (iron and steel, non-ferrous metals), combustion processes (industry, electricity generation, road transport) and waste incineration. it is within this framework that it is intended to phase out leaded petrol, reduce mercury concentration levels in alkaline batteries and include other mercury-containing products such as measuring devices. the amended protocol sets stricter limit values for dust emissions which need to be transposed by a new directive. i agree with the rapporteur that ratification of the amendment will be an important step towards better protection of human health and the environment against transboundary air pollution, especially as regards heavy metals.
‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect the human environment from air pollution. the convention, signed in 1979 and in force since 1983, was the first legally binding international instrument in this field. to date, the scope of the convention has been extended by eight protocols identifying specific measures to be taken by parties to reduce their emissions of air pollutants. in december 2012, the protocol was amended by decisions 2012/5, 2012/6 and 2012/7, the latter two concerning bat, and was subject to ratification by the parties. the amended protocol sets, inter alia, stricter limit values for dust emissions from certain large fixed sources, as well as flexible transitional provisions that should benefit future parties to the amended protocol before the end of 2019, including countries in eastern and south-eastern europe. the ratification of the amendment will be an important step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment against transboundary air pollution. i therefore welcome the draft council decision.
‒ the 1998 aarhus protocol on heavy metals aims to reduce and control anthropogenic emissions of lead (pb), cadmium (cd) and mercury (hg) into the atmosphere. it requires parties to reduce their total annual emissions of the three metals indicated to levels below those recorded in 1990 or in an alternate year between 1985 and 1995. the protocol aims to reduce emissions from industrial sources (iron and steel, non-ferrous metals), combustion processes (industry, electricity generation, road transport) and waste incineration. the protocol also suggests the inclusion of management measures for other mercury-containing products, including measuring devices. the amended protocol sets, inter alia, stricter limit values for dust emissions from certain large fixed sources, as well as flexible transitional provisions that should benefit future parties to the amended protocol before the end of 2019, including countries in eastern and south-eastern europe. the amendment to the protocol is already covered by eu legislation, but it still needs to be transposed through a new directive that will update national emission limit values for certain air pollutants and provide for national inventories of annual emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury, among others. we voted in favour.

‒ the prosecutor-general of the republic of poland has forwarded to the president of the european parliament a request from the polish road traffic inspectorate to waive the immunity of mr robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz, member of the european parliament, in connection with a traffic offence, on the grounds that he did not respect the speed limit applicable to urban agglomerations. it follows from the circumstances of the present case that the alleged offence and the subsequent criminal proceedings clearly have nothing to do with mr iwaszkiewicz's office as a member of the european parliament and i therefore agree with the rapporteur's request for the waiver of immunity.
in writing. ‒ this report deals with the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr robert jaroslaw iwaszkiewicz. here are the facts: the polish road traffic inspectorate claims that on 7 september 2014, when driving a vehicle, mr iwaszkiewicz did not respect the speed limit for urban agglomerations of 50 km/h when driving the vehicle at a speed of 79 km/h. the inspectorate-general also states that, in response to a notification sent to the owner of the vehicle, mrs m. iwaszkiewicz, she confirmed that the member was the driver of the vehicle on the date in question. the facts of which he is accused constitute an infringement of article 92 (a) of the polish code of civil procedure, in conjunction with article 20 (1) of the law on road traffic of 20 june 1997. apart from other considerations that may be made, the alleged infringement has no direct and obvious connection with the performance of the duties of robert jaroslaw iwaszkiewicz as a member of the european parliament, and parliament has also found no substantiated evidence that the request is aimed at harming the political activity of the member. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the request for waiver of the immunity of robert jaroslaw iwaszkiewicz. the request fulfils the requirements for the application of article 9 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union: the member's immunity shall be waived where the offence is not related to the performance of the duties of a member and where there is no suspicion of fumus persecutionis, that is to say, a serious and well-founded suspicion that the criminal offence was committed with the intention of causing political damage to the member.
‒ i am voting in favour of this report because all the necessary legal procedures have been completed and because the offence in question is not in any way connected with the performance of the duties of a member and because there is no evidence or suspicion that the criminal offence was committed with the intention of causing political damage to the member concerned.
in writing. ‒ this report deals with the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr robert jaroslaw iwaszkiewicz. the alleged breach on which the request for the waiver of parliamentary immunity is based has no direct and obvious connection with the performance of the duties of robert jaroslaw iwaszkiewicz as a member of the european parliament, and parliament has also found no substantiated evidence that the request is aimed at prejudicing the political activity of the member. we voted for the waiver of parliamentary immunity by express vote.
in writing. ‒ on 13 august 2015, the prosecutor-general of the republic of poland forwarded to the president of the european parliament a request from the polish road traffic inspectorate to waive the immunity of the member of the european parliament, mr robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz, in relation to a traffic offence. the polish road traffic inspectorate claims that at 23.46 on 21 august 2014 in the town of rawicz, mr iwaszkiewicz was recorded by a traffic control camera while travelling at a speed of 94 km/h in a zone with a speed limit of 60 km/h. this report approves the decision to waive the immunity of mr robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz and instructs its president to forward this decision, together with the report of its committee responsible, to the relevant authorities of the republic of poland and mr robert jaroslaw iwaszkiewicz without delay.
‒ this report concerns the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr robert jaroslaw iwaszkiewicz. this is a request made by the prosecutor general of the republic of poland, which relates to a case related to a traffic offence where, allegedly on 7 september 2014, the member of parliament did not respect the speed limit applicable to urban agglomerations which is 50 km/h by driving the vehicle at a speed of 79 km/h. it is therefore an offence concerning conduct allegedly committed outside your mandate as an mep. in the absence of any reason to doubt the legitimate intention underlying this legal action, and in view of the fulfilment of the conditions set out in article 9 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union, i consider the request for the waiver of parliamentary immunity to be appropriate and, in that regard, i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ in this case, the request for waiver of mr iwaszkiewicz's immunity was made on the basis of an alleged infringement consisting in exceeding the speed limit applicable to urban agglomerations, since the vehicle he was driving was recorded by a traffic control camera when travelling at a speed of 94 km/h in an area with a speed limit of 60 km/h. it follows from the circumstances of the present case that the alleged offence and the subsequent criminal proceedings clearly have nothing to do with mr iwaszkiewicz's office as a member of the european parliament and i therefore agree with the rapporteur's request for the waiver of immunity.

in writing. - mr florian philippot is accused by the government of a third country, namely qatar, of having defamed that country during a radio broadcast by insinuating that qatar was financing terrorism. for a member of the european parliament, immunity covers not only the views expressed by the member in official meetings of the parliament but also the expression of his views elsewhere, for example in the media. however, the public expression of opinions on the foreign policy of the european union and of third countries is part of the duties of a member of the european parliament, and i agree that the conditions for the waiver of mr philippot's immunity are not met.
‒ this report deals with the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of florian philippot, a member of the national front. here are the facts: the mp is accused by the government of qatar of having defamed that country by suggesting, in a radio show and a television show (both in january 2015), that qatar finances terrorism. the french authorities have requested the waiver of immunity following the criminal proceedings brought by a third country. in accordance with article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union and article 26 of the constitution of the french republic, it is prohibited to bring any civil or criminal proceedings against a member of parliament for opinions expressed in the performance of his duties. article 8 of protocol no 7 provides that 'members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties'. it is clear that this principle also applies in the case of criminal proceedings for defamation against a member of parliament by a third country. it is understood that the intention underlying the criminal action is to harm the political activity of this member. we voted in favour of the report rejecting the request for waiver of immunity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the request for waiver of the immunity of florian philippot, which decides not to waive the immunity. the application does not meet the requirements for the application of article 9 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union: the facts are related to the performance of the duties of a member, since there is a link between the statements made and parliamentary duties.
‒ having regard to the provisions of article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union and article 26 of the french constitution, which prohibit any civil or criminal action against a member for opinions expressed in the exercise of his duties, and considering that the immunity of a member of the european parliament covers not only the opinions expressed by the member in official meetings of parliament but also the manifestation of his views anywhere else for example in the media, where there is 'a link between the opinion expressed and parliamentary duties' and that the rapporteur considers that the conditions for the waiver of the immunity of mr philippot are not met, this report deserves my vote in favour.
‒ this report deals with the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr florian philippot. the member of parliament is accused by the government of qatar of having defamed that country by suggesting, in a radio programme broadcast on 9 january 2015 and in a television programme broadcast on 19 january 2015, that qatar finances terrorism. the french authorities have requested the waiver of immunity following the criminal proceedings brought by a third country. in accordance with article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union and article 26 of the constitution of the french republic, it is prohibited to bring any civil or criminal proceedings against a member of parliament for opinions expressed in the performance of his duties. in general terms, the purpose of parliamentary immunity is to allow the legislature to exercise its constitutional functions without undue external interference, especially from the executive. in the light of the foregoing, the request for waiver of parliamentary immunity should not be granted.

‒ the french ministry of justice requested a request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr florian philippot on 2 september 2015 in the context of a defamation case pending before the court of first instance of nanterre. the request follows a criminal action brought by a third state qatar , which accuses the member of parliament of having defamed that country during a radio broadcast on 9 january 2015, by referring to that country as financing terrorism. however, the french constitution states that "no member of parliament may be prosecuted, investigated, arrested, detained or judged for opinions or votes he or she has given in the performance of his or her duties". and article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union prohibits any civil or criminal action against a member for opinions expressed in the performance of his duties. in view of the above, the conditions are met for mr florian philippot's parliamentary immunity to be maintained, which is why i voted in favour.

‒ undeclared work is a phenomenon that seriously harms working conditions, fair competition and public budgets in the member states. the commission has proposed to establish a european platform which should improve cooperation on the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work at eu level by bringing together a number of national law enforcement bodies involved in the fight against undeclared work. although the main responsibility for tackling this problem lies with the member states, there are cases where cooperation between the different entities at national level is not sufficiently structured or does not prove to be effective, and this new platform should be an added value not only to prevent and deter undeclared work but also to regulate it. i support the pirinski report, as i believe that action at eu level can help member states to combat undeclared work more effectively, while also contributing to tackling the challenges associated with professional mobility in a positive and constructive way at eu level, while preserving the free movement of workers as one of the fundamental freedoms of the eu.
‒ undeclared work is a serious problem in europe. by 2012, it will have accounted for 18.4% of eu gdp and the negative effects are felt by workers, businesses and governments. undeclared work is legal work that is not properly declared to the competent authorities. from unfair competition to lost tax revenues and social security contributions, there are many negative consequences of undeclared work, and workers are left with their basic social and labour rights reduced. so i agree that the platform is an opportunity to analyse data and share good practices, especially in a cross-border undeclared work context.
in writing. ‒ this report focuses on the creation of an eu-wide platform to combat undeclared work, as any paid activity that is lawful but not declared to public authorities. this platform aims at enhanced cooperation between member states of their structures and authorities for labour inspection, health and safety conditions, financial taxation, services for foreigners, etc. , by sharing information and best practices, developing a database and common principles and methodologies, as well as training actions. undeclared work (together with fake self-employment and other forms of precarious employment) has repercussions on the financial and ethical structure of states, accounting on average for 18% of gdp in the eu. workers involved in these schemes are more vulnerable in their rights such as protection against accidents, unemployment or pension guarantee , so the establishment of strategies to combat the phenomenon is essential and is understood as positive. however, there are aspects of the architecture of this platform that merit our disagreement, including the use of data and that may jeopardize the freedoms of individuals. the relevance of a formal structure to these objectives is also questioned, despite the importance of cooperation in this and other contexts.
‒ undeclared work or false selfemployment has so far been dealt with sporadically and in an uncoordinated manner. in this regard, the creation of a european platform will provide the necessary means for enhanced and more effective cooperation between states in combating labour law offences, tax evasion and breaches of social security requirements. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
‒ i support the creation of the european platform to strengthen cooperation in the fight against undeclared work, given that it is harmful to the union's economy, creates unfair competition, undermines the financial sustainability of the union's social models and results in a growing lack of social and labour protection for workers. the platform, in addition to tackling undeclared work, will also address falsely declared work, including false self-employment. i agree that undeclared work has serious implications for the workers affected, who are forced to accept precarious and dangerous working conditions, very low wages, serious violations of their labour rights and considerably reduced protection under labour law and social protection, which deprives them of adequate social benefits, pension rights and access to health care, as well as opportunities for skills development and lifelong learning. i believe that the 'platform' will provide better working conditions, promote integration into the labour market and foster social inclusion. close and effective cooperation between member states is essential to implement the fight against undeclared work.
‒ undeclared work has repercussions on the financial and ethical structure of states and workers involved in these schemes are more vulnerable in their rights. the establishment of strategies to combat this phenomenon is essential and positive. the report overlooks that it is right-wing policies, implemented at national level under the guidance of eu policies, which have contributed to the deregulation of labour legislation, the attack on collective bargaining and the deepening of mechanisms for devaluing and precariousness of work. it omits that austerity policies have contributed to the increase in totally or partially undeclared work, false service provision, false paid internships or false volunteering situations. the architecture of this platform has a tendency towards the standardisation of methodologies and legislation, which suggests that decision-making will be more prevalent at the supranational level, thus compromising national sovereignty. the fight against precariousness and undeclared work can only be achieved, within the framework of the sovereignty of the member states, through links that guarantee security and stability, the promotion of collective agreements, wages and work with rights, in other words, the opposite of what the european union has been imposing. for the reasons stated, we abstained.
‒ this report concerns the decision of the european parliament and the council on the creation of a european platform to strengthen cooperation in the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work. undeclared work is one of the most worrying and complex problems facing the eu today and urgent action is needed to mitigate the extremely negative consequences of this and the serious losses to member states' budgets and social security systems. this platform aims to improve cooperation between member states' authorities to prevent and deter undeclared work and to alert citizens, through the exchange of best practices, analyses and opinions. i considered that joint action by the member states and the social partners, together with other stakeholders (including at regional level), in interaction with the eu institutions and capacities, was essential and indispensable, and therefore i voted in favour of this report, as only through a joint and concerted position can a whole complex set of challenges facing the eu in this field be successfully overcome.
in writing. ‒ this platform aims at enhanced cooperation between member states of their structures and authorities for labour inspection, health and safety conditions, financial taxation, services for foreigners, etc. , by sharing information and best practices, developing a common database, principles and methodologies, and training actions. this platform shall be coordinated by the commission. it also provides for the participation of partners, including employers' and workers' representatives. however, there is a tendency in the architecture of this platform to standardize methodologies and legislation, to use data that may jeopardize the freedoms of individuals, or to override the importance of supranational decision-making over national sovereignty. we also question the relevance of a formal structure to these objectives, despite the importance of cooperation in this and other contexts.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council establishing a european platform to strengthen cooperation in preventing and deterring undeclared work, also considering this phenomenon, accentuated by the current crisis, particularly harmful, as austerity measures lead to the resurgence of parallel economies, and also believing that a coordinated approach at eu level to understand the causes and combat informal work could contribute to strengthening workers' rights and protection, increasing social security funding and strengthening labour standards. on the other hand, given that underemployment continues to characterize the situation of women in european labour markets, any proposal which aims to contribute to achieving the great objective of 75% employment by 2020 and, even more so, the goal of full employment naturally has my support. although the eu platform is aimed at law enforcement authorities, i believe that the needs and consequences for the undeclared worker himself, whether male or female, cannot be ignored, and authorities must devote special attention to their working conditions and employment inclusion for all.
‒ the european target of halting biodiversity loss was not met in 2010. the eu responded by drawing up a new strategy in 2011, with heads of state and government setting the central objective of ending biodiversity loss and the deterioration of ecosystem services, restoring them, as far as possible, by 2020 and stepping up eu efforts to prevent the degradation of global biodiversity. according to 2015 figures, we are far from achieving the proposed targets, and political will is needed to put biodiversity at the top of the agenda. i support the demesmaeker report, because i believe that more measures are needed to protect biodiversity, to build a smart, sustainable and environmentally conscious europe, and that member states should be more effective in implementing european environmental legislation.
in writing. ‒ biodiversity is under enormous pressure, globally and in europe. species are going extinct at a mind-boggling rate because of human activity. habitat changes, pollution, over-exploitation, invasive alien species and climate change are the main causes of biodiversity loss. the loss of biodiversity is particularly harmful and entails losses for nature, for humanity and for the economy: it threatens essential ecosystem services and compromises the earth's natural capacity to respond to new challenges. biodiversity and nature must be at the heart of a smart, sustainable and inclusive europe, and i agree with the call for greater political will to genuinely end biodiversity loss.
in writing. the goal of halting biodiversity loss failed in 2010. the 2011 strategy set a new global goal: to halt the loss of biodiversity and the degradation of "ecosystem services", and to restore them "to the extent possible by 2020". in 2015, it became clear that without significant additional efforts, the eu will once again fail to achieve its 2020 targets. the report calls for better enforcement of the relevant legislation to halt biodiversity loss, in particular the habitats and birds directives (rejecting their revision and weakening them). a major focus is on the agricultural and forestry sectors. these are proposals for additional measures to the commission and the member states to halt biodiversity loss. we have tabled more than 20 amendments to the report. some of them were accepted. but the report lacks a different approach and a background. it is necessary to assume that only by changing the production model, by using natural resources responsibly and by transforming society, which respects all living beings as part of a whole, will we have a strategy that meets the objectives it sets out to achieve. it is not enough to paint capitalism green, to make the world a better and more habitable place for all living things.
‒ the nature directives are important milestones in nature policy, not only at eu level but also at international level. this mid-term review of the biodiversity strategy aims not only to strengthen the measures and programmes implemented, particularly with regard to the birds and habitats directives, but also to extend them to other strategic areas of the environment. i voted yes.
‒ i voted in favour of the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy. it is developed around six specific objectives and assumes biodiversity loss as a political priority. the role of the different national, local and regional actors in this process is crucial to ensure that the proposed targets are met through concrete actions.
in writing. ‒ the loss of biodiversity has become alarming. species are disappearing at a dizzying rate; habitat changes, pollution, over-exploitation, invasive alien species and climate change are the main drivers of biodiversity loss. i argue that biodiversity is paramount to our health and well-being as well as to economic prosperity. i agree with the rapporteur that there is a need for greater political will to genuinely address biodiversity loss as a political priority and for a multilateral approach in which regional and local actors have a special role to play. i am in favour of better enforcement and monitoring of existing legislation to stop the loss of biodiversity, which must be seen as a real european objective. i also agree with the rapporteur that biodiversity and nature must be at the heart of a smart, sustainable and inclusive europe and that we need more political will to put a genuine end to biodiversity loss. i would like to highlight the importance of this issue for eu citizens, as demonstrated by the 'nature alert' campaign, in which half a million citizens called for the observance and better enforcement of nature protection legislation.
‒ the objective of halting biodiversity loss failed in 2010. the 2011 strategy set a new global goal: to halt the loss of biodiversity and the degradation of "ecosystem services", and to restore them "to the extent possible by 2020". in 2015, it became clear that the eu will not be able to achieve its 2020 targets without significant additional efforts. this report calls for better enforcement of the relevant legislation - notably the habitats and birds directives (rejecting their revision, weakening them) - and proposes additional measures to the commission and member states to halt biodiversity loss. a great deal of attention is given to the agricultural and forestry sectors. many amendments were proposed to the report, some of which were considered. however, there remains another approach and a background to the report which assumes that only by changing the production model, by using natural resources responsibly and by transforming society, which respects all living beings as part of a whole, will we have a strategy that meets the objectives it proposes.
‒ biodiversity, the unique variety of ecosystems, habitats, species and genes on earth, of which humanity is also a part, has immeasurable intrinsic value and is under enormous pressure, globally and in europe, as species are becoming extinct at a staggering rate and largely due to human activity. habitat change, pollution, over-exploitation, invasive alien species and climate change are the main causes of biodiversity loss which is particularly harmful and entails losses for nature, for humanity and for the economy. the limits and capacity of the planet are being exceeded and this is necessarily triggering irreversible changes. the european objective of halting biodiversity loss was not met in 2010, and the eu responded by developing a new strategy in 2011. the heads of state and government have set the central objective of ending biodiversity loss and the deterioration of ecosystem services, restoring them as far as possible by 2020 and stepping up eu efforts to prevent the degradation of global biodiversity, and i therefore voted in favour of this mid-term review.
‒ biodiversity has in itself an invaluable intrinsic value and must therefore be protected for the benefit of present and future generations. the progressive trend of biodiversity loss is alarming and urgent political priority needs to be given to environmental issues, while not neglecting the crucial role of regional and local actors in the process, with a view to meeting the eu biodiversity targets. in europe, close to a quarter of wild species are threatened with extinction and many of our ecosystems are severely degraded, causing enormous environmental, territorial, social and economic damage to the eu. i therefore believe that it is essential to promote greater public awareness and to encourage greater investment in these areas, particularly in terms of the preservation and conservation of biodiversity. i have voted in favour of this report because it is a matter which deserves special attention and care and because i agree with the measures put forward by the rapporteur.
the preservation of biodiversity is a concern that must be present in all union policies with a direct or indirect impact on the terrestrial and marine environment. to achieve this, we must ensure an approach that includes all relevant actors and sets clear targets. habitat preservation or genetic conservation are examples of objectives that require strong collaboration between science, industry and citizens, and the ideal conditions for this to occur effectively need to be promoted. the evaluation of the european biodiversity strategy is an opportunity to correct where necessary and to assess what needs to be done. despite some positive developments, the data available also show that more needs to be done and more urgently to avoid losses to nature that may become irreversible. it is necessary to strengthen the means at our disposal for better implementation, to ensure that all sectoral policies incorporate biodiversity objectives and to rethink new areas of action to avoid fragmentation and to enhance the pursuit of these objectives.
‒ the european objective of halting biodiversity loss was not achieved in 2010. so the heads of state or government, by drawing up a new strategy in 2011, set a new global target to halt biodiversity loss and degradation of 'ecosystem services', to restore them 'as far as possible by 2020', and to step up eu efforts to prevent the degradation of global biodiversity. in 2015, it became clear that without significant additional efforts, the eu will once again fail to achieve its agreed biodiversity targets in 2020. the report therefore focuses on the target-by-target biodiversity strategy, calling for better implementation of all relevant legislation to halt biodiversity loss, mainly through the habitat and birds directives. the report opposes any revision of the nature directives as this could jeopardise the implementation of the biodiversity strategy and states that the ongoing refit review of the nature directives should focus on improving their implementation and enforcement, proposing additional measures that the commission and member states should take into account to halt biodiversity loss.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on the mid-term review of the biodiversity strategy because it agrees that biodiversity and nature must be at the heart of a smart, sustainable and inclusive europe, and because it calls for greater political will to genuinely end the loss of biodiversity as an essential measure for nature itself and for the health and well-being of our children and grandchildren. the committee also agrees with the rapporteur that the development of a trans-european network of green infrastructure (ten-t) could create a win-win situation for nature and the economy; advocates a european framework for preventing the loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services; calls for the commission to develop specific criteria for the 'natural capital financing facility' which should ensure that projects produce tangible positive results for biodiversity; by arguing that the decline in bee numbers requires more research and action, in establishing the link between health and biodiversity; and finally by believing that nature-based solutions can make a significant contribution to addressing challenges such as climate change.
madam president, it is the policies of interference and aggression of the usa, nato and the european union that are at the root of the conflicts in the middle east and north africa. policies which do not hesitate to finance and promote extremist forces, to conclude multi-million dollar arms sales contracts with dictatorships such as saudi arabia, with a view to economic and geopolitical domination of those regions. this is the underlying reason for the mass exodus of millions of people who come to the european continent fleeing hunger, poverty, war and death. i would urge this parliament to defend human rights and i would condemn without reservation the response to this reality. the walls, the fascist legislation humiliating refugees, the concept of a fortress europe, the funding of neighbouring states to contain the flow of refugees into genuine concentration camps, are the hallmark of the brutality and inhumanity of the european union. those who manage to survive such solidarity are left with miserable reception conditions that precede a forced repatriation. history will condemn those who now remain silent or support these policies.
madam president, mr president-in-office of the council, mr commissioner, i have said from the beginning of this refugee crisis that the union is required to act on two different levels: one more immediate, the other longer term, one to deal with the emergency, the other to get to the root of the problems. it is not by announcing legislative measures of far-reaching impact that we deal with emergencies. that's how it was with search and rescue operations. the states were initially reluctant to respond and only when confronted with the tragedies in the mediterranean did they grant more support. the same is now true of schengen. the emergency relocation mechanism remains weak, the hot spots in greece and italy still lack the necessary resources, return operations still do not take place and, if that were not enough, there is also a proliferation of isolated and selfish national measures. without an immediate response to the urgency, it is the states, not the refugees, who are putting schengen in danger. of course, reintroducing internal border controls is a possibility for member states, but these are temporary measures, they do not solve any problems. the free movement in the schengen area has always been countered by reinforced common external borders. the new schengen evaluation mechanism, which we approved in 2013 and which was recently used in greece, has shown that the union has the capacity to identify problems, but as this crisis makes clear, the union needs instruments to respond to those problems when member states are unable to do so. frontex should therefore be strengthened.
madam president, commissioner, mr president of the council, i leave you with a very simple recipe for solving the refugee problem, a call: respect the values of the european union, practice the de facto solidarity achieved through concrete actions that robert schuman spoke of in his famous declaration of 9 may 1950. the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force. but solidarity does not mean just receiving, solidarity also means giving, and it is unacceptable that member states which receive billions from the european union budget, hundreds of millions, are not able to resolve this issue after giving a penny. in the face of this problem we have, i leave you with a few questions: is there a member state that refuses to contribute? are the amounts for each member state defined? can this support be extended to jordan and lebanon? who will monitor and follow the execution on the ground? it is important to act with transparency, with credibility and before it is too late, to act without populism, radicalism and national selfishness.
mr president, last thursday i was proud to be portuguese. the national parliament, by a right-left unanimity, rejected the new danish law to confiscate valuables from refugees and delay family reunification. these policies not only remind us of an ominous past, but they play directly into the hands of the terrorists from whom refugees flee. portugal has been ready and waiting for months to receive refugees, but they are not arriving because the relocation system is not working. hotspots in greece and italy are not properly equipped months after they were announced. let us not be fooled, we can only tackle the crisis if we act together at european level. destroying schengen will not bring more control of our borders or fewer refugees, only more confusion and misery and will further benefit the smugglers. european action means not tolerating ministers who shame us by suggesting that others push or drown refugees who arrive on our shores, ministers who draw up laws to criminalise ngos and volunteers who assist refugees, ministers who turn a deaf ear to the alarming news of thousands of refugee children missing at the hands of traffickers. we cannot, finally, allow our governments to continue to fuel the business of smugglers and the clandestine influx of refugees by refusing to open up legal and safe channels to process asylum applications and protect the refugees we can take in.
in writing. the strength of our convictions is tested in the moments of greatest difficulty. unfortunately, the response of some member states to the refugee crisis has revealed the great erosion of humanistic and democratic values that is currently taking place in the european union. a crisis of such global proportions cannot be solved by adopting individually designed national strategies. europe cannot look at the refugee question as a problem that begins and ends at the greek, italian, cypriot or maltese borders. we are facing a crisis which affects europe as a whole and which requires a united, concerted and shared response. nationalist rhetoric, isolation and repression are not the answer. the refugee crisis requires two-dimensional solutions: on the one hand, europe must ensure that people fleeing war and violence are given a decent welcome, without prejudice or fear. the european union must also work towards conflict resolution, working with the countries and regions from which these people come. only a joint solution that simultaneously addresses the causes and protects the consequences will be appropriate, effective and in line with european principles.
the current eu and nato policies do not hesitate to finance and promote extremist forces, to conclude multi-million dollar arms sales contracts with dictatorships such as saudi arabia in order to dominate the economic and geopolitical situation in those regions. the european union has been a major player in the middle east and north africa, and the middle east is a major player in the middle east. this is the underlying reason for the mass exodus of millions of people who come to the european continent, fleeing hunger, poverty, war and death. i would urge this parliament to defend human rights and i would condemn without reservation the response to this reality. the walls, the fascist legislation humiliating refugees, the concept of a strong europe, the funding of neighbouring states to contain the flood of refugees in authentic concentration camps are the hallmark of the brutality and inhumanity of the eu. those who manage to survive such 'solidarity' are left with miserable reception conditions that precede a forced repatriation.

‒ the association agreement with moldova includes a bilateral safeguard clause. the preferences may be temporarily suspended through this instrument if their application results in an unexpected and significant increase in imports causing economic injury. in addition, the agreement also includes the so-called 'anti-circumvention' mechanism, which provides for the possibility of reintroducing the 'most favoured nation' customs duty rate whenever imports of certain agricultural products from moldova exceed a certain threshold without due justification of their exact origin. the agreement we condemned and opposed introduces a system of trade preferences, the comprehensive and deepened free trade area (cfta). the main exports from moldova to the european union are oilseeds, fresh and dried nuts, apple juice, wines and cereals. the main eu exports to moldova are spirits, food preparations, cigarettes, some fruit and vegetables, including citrus fruits, pork and animal feed. this clause and this mechanism do not change the nature of this agreement, which we reject. they can only, under certain circumstances, mitigate some of its most harmful consequences.

in writing. ‒ the association agreement between the european union (eu) and the republic of moldova, signed on 24 june 2014, introduces a trade preference regime - the comprehensive and deep free trade area (cfta). the regulation was recently amended to extend the duty-free regime to moldovan wine and to grant duty-free tariff quotas for apples, plums and table grapes. these amendments are aimed at harmonizing the content of the regulation with that of the eu-moldova association agreement, and i therefore voted in favour. the eu is moldova's main trading partner, accounting for 46.4% of its trade, followed by russia (21.9%) and ukraine (11.8%). trade with moldova represents 0,1% of the union's overall trade. agricultural products represent a significant part of the total imports from moldova into the union. the main exports from moldova to the union are oilseeds, fresh and dried nuts, apple juice, wines and cereals. the main exports from the european union to moldova are spirits, food preparations, cigarettes, some fruit and vegetables, including citrus fruits, pork and animal feed.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement between the european union (eu) and the republic of moldova was signed in june 2014 and has been (provisionally) applied since september 2014. the eu is moldova's main trading partner, accounting for some 46.4% of its trade, so the establishment of a sound and fair regulation for both co-signatories is key to the development of good trade relations between the parties. however, in order to ensure a rapid, fair and effective operation and the proper dissemination of the mutual benefits inherent in this agreement, it is important to introduce a bilateral safeguard clause, which should be applied whenever such trade causes or threatens to cause 'serious injury' to the domestic industry of the union. i voted in favour of this report because i consider that it contains necessary measures to safeguard european commercial interests.

in the case of the eu-georgia association agreement, signed on 27 june 2014 and subject to parliamentary approval on 18 december 2014, the so-called anti-fraud mechanism allows the reintroduction of the mfn rate of customs duty whenever imports of certain agricultural and processed agricultural products from georgia exceed a certain ceiling without proper justification as to their exact origin. the main aim is to prevent countries with free trade agreements with georgia, such as turkey and the europmed countries, from using this agreement to circumvent the 'rules of origin' requirements. the commission proposal for a regulation in this case is precisely intended to define the procedures necessary to ensure the application of this mechanism, ensuring on the one hand compliance by georgia with the obligations arising from the agreement and on the other avoiding potential negative impacts on the eu market. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement between the european union (eu) and georgia, signed on 27 june 2014, provides for an ambitious trade preference regime between the two parties, known as the deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta). it was negotiated following the same approach as was followed in the simultaneous negotiations with other countries in the region, such as moldova and armenia, the latter having abandoned the idea of signing an agreement with the eu in favour of signing a trade agreement with russia. the eu is currently georgia's main trading partner, accounting for 27.2% of its trade. in terms of agricultural products, the main eu imports from georgia are fresh and dried hazelnuts, mineral water and wine. the main eu exports to georgia are processed agricultural products (such as spirits and food preparations) and dairy products. the amendment proposed to the commission text aims to harmonise the wording of the regulation with that of the eu-georgia association agreement and states the obligation of the commission to draw up a more detailed report, so as to expressly mention the application of an anti-circumvention mechanism, which is why i voted in favour.
‒ the eu-georgia association agreement was signed on 27 june 2014 and entered into force on 1 september. it is an agreement establishing a comprehensive and deep free trade area and introducing an ambitious trade preference regime between the two parties. the agreement includes the anti-fraud mechanism, which provides for the possibility of reintroducing the most-favoured-nation tariff rate whenever imports of certain agricultural products from georgia exceed a certain threshold without justification as to their exact origin. as i consider that this is an instrument which will make it possible to strengthen georgia's obligations in relation to the anti-circumvention provisions of the agreement, with the aim also of giving a higher degree of protection to producers in the european union, i have decided to support this report by voting in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament is proud to promote the openness of the institutions and bring citizens closer to the european decision-making centres. following a petition by the european association of the blind, parliament decided to give its opinion on the marrakesh treaty, which aims to facilitate access to published works for blind people, people with visual impairments or people with other print disabilities. this parliament also takes pride in defending the fundamental rights of all across the continent. and here too, it could not ignore the attempt by seven member states to block the ratification of this treaty, signed by the union and its individual member states. access to education and the principle of equality are inalienable values of the european union. it is therefore unacceptable that, despite the political commitment made by signing the treaty, its entry into force is now blocked and the fundamental rights of millions of people are thus disregarded. it is not acceptable that in the so-called "developed world", only 5% of the books published are accessible to the blind and visually impaired.
‒ the world health organisation estimated that in 2010 there were 2 550 000 blind people and 23 800 000 amblyopes in europe, out of a total of 26 350 000 visually impaired people. however, only 5% of books published in developed countries and less than 1% of books published in developing countries are produced in accessible formats. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. member states should speed up this process without making ratification conditional on the review of the eu legal framework or the decision of the court of justice of the european union.
‒ only 5% of books published in developed countries and less than 1% in developing countries are published in accessible formats. the aim of the marrakesh treaty is to facilitate, by means of copyright exceptions, the production of versions of books originally protected by copyright laws that are accessible to people with visual impairments. the eu and most of its member states have signed the marrakesh treaty and have made a political commitment to ratify it. the resolution expresses outrage at the fact that seven member states form a blocking minority which prevents ratification of the treaty. recalls articles 24 and 30 of the un crpd: the right of persons with disabilities to education without discrimination and on the basis of equal opportunities and access to cultural property. we voted in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the ratification of the marrakesh treaty, on the basis of the petitions received, in particular petition no 924/2011. blind and visually impaired persons should have access to published works and other printed matter. it is unfortunate that only five percent of books published in developed countries and less than one percent of books published in developing countries are produced in accessible formats. the eu and the member states are parties to the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the eu should therefore ratify and implement the marrakesh treaty as soon as possible.
in writing. articles 24 and 30 of the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities highlight the right of persons with disabilities to education, without discrimination and on the basis of equal opportunities, while ensuring that legislation protecting intellectual property rights does not constitute an excessive or discriminatory barrier to access by persons with disabilities to cultural materials. according to estimates by the world health organisation, in 2010 there were 2 550 000 blind and 23 800 000 amblyopes in europe, out of a total of 26 350 000 visually impaired people. and only 5 percent of books published in developed countries and less than 1 percent of books published in developing countries are produced in accessible formats. the eu and the member states signed the marrakesh treaty in april 2014 and have therefore made a political commitment to ratify it; however, there is a blockading force of seven member states which impedes the ratification process. i believe that the council and the member states should speed up the ratification process with a view to greater integration and to ensuring that all citizens are treated equally.
‒ the aim of the marrakesh treaty is to facilitate, through copyright exceptions, the production of versions accessible to visually impaired persons of books originally protected by copyright laws, in a context where only a small fraction of books are published in response to this need. the eu and most of its member states have signed the marrakesh treaty and have made a political commitment to ratify it. the resolution expressed outrage at the fact that seven member states form a blocking minority which prevents ratification of the treaty and recalled articles 24 and 30 of the un crpd: the right of persons with disabilities to education without discrimination and on the basis of equal opportunities and access to cultural property.
