in writing. ‒ i am well aware that air pollution causes more than 430 000 premature deaths in the union each year and has an estimated cost of €940 billion due to its effects on health, and that exhaust emissions from diesel vehicles are a major source of nox in urban areas in europe and that, according to the european environment agency, nox emissions are the cause of 75 000 premature deaths in europe. to achieve the eu's air quality objectives, a continuous effort to reduce vehicle emissions is needed, including a considerable reduction in nitrogen oxide emissions from vehicles equipped with diesel engines. i am sensitive to the argument of the committee on the environment that the draft commission implementing decision exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 715/2007 and may be contrary to union law as it is not compatible with the objective and content of that regulation. on the other hand, i admit that postponing the problem and waiting for a new initiative from the commission may represent an excessively long legal vacuum without any clear public health gains. that is why i abstained in the final vote.
‒ the measure proposed by the european commission is part of the second package on real driving emissions testing, which sets emission limits to be respected and dates for their application to new models and vehicles. in the current legal framework, vehicle emissions are determined on the basis of test cycles carried out in laboratories, which do not reflect vehicle emissions under normal driving conditions. the commission has been developing procedures to determine vehicle emissions under real driving conditions, including the use of portable emission measurement systems. the decision will allow the edr procedure to proceed.
in writing. ‒ following a meeting with the technical committee on motor vehicles on 28/10/2015, the european commission presented a proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 692/2008 as regards pollutant emissions from light passenger and commercial vehicles. the euro 6 emission limit for nitrogen oxides (nox) for vehicles equipped with a diesel engine is 80 mg/km in that regulation, applicable to all new vehicles from 1/9/2014 and to all vehicles sold from 1/9/2015. this new proposal introduces a temporary compliance factor of 2,1 resulting in nox emissions of 168 mg/km in the real driving test applicable to all new passenger vehicles from 9/2019 (new types and vehicles 09/2017) and a final compliance factor of 1,5 which would be applicable to all new vehicles from 2021, allowing these vehicles to emit around 120 mg/km of nox in the red test. in practice, therefore, we are faced with a considerable increase in the figures previously forecast. the resolution opposes the adoption of the commission's draft resolution, as the commission's proposal would result in a derogation from the euro 6 nox emission limit values. we voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection under rule 106: emissions from light passenger and commercial vehicles (euro 6) it is important to require manufacturers to ensure, at the time of type-approval and throughout the lifetime of the vehicle, that the emissions produced during an ecr test do not exceed the limit values. the tests shall be real, i.e. road driving tests.
‒ the commission has drawn up a draft decision with the support of the member states. this project is based on an analysis by the joint research centre (jrc) which concluded that the real-life (rather than laboratory) test procedure can introduce a measurement uncertainty margin of up to 30%, i.e. a 'more pessimistic margin' of 25 mg nox/km in the case of the euro 6 limit. i voted against the motion for a resolution because the commission has drawn up a new draft implementing measure with the aim of amending the regulation by adapting the test procedures so that they adequately reflect the emissions generated in real driving conditions on the road. i also regard it as extremely positive that manufacturers are required, at the time of type approval and throughout the life of the vehicle, to ensure that the emissions produced during an ecr test do not exceed certain limit values.
in writing. ‒ following a meeting with the technical committee on motor vehicles on 28/10/2015, the european commission presented a proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 692/2008 as regards pollutant emissions from light passenger and commercial vehicles. the euro 6 emission limit for nitrogen oxides (nox) for vehicles equipped with a diesel engine is 80 mg/km in that regulation, applicable to all new vehicles from 1/9/2014 and to all vehicles sold from 1/9/2015. this new proposal introduces a temporary compliance factor of 2,1 resulting in nox emissions of 168 mg/km in the real driving test applicable to all new passenger vehicles from 9/2019 (new types and vehicles 09/2017) and a final compliance factor of 1,5 which would be applicable to all new vehicles from 2021, allowing these vehicles to emit around 120 mg/km of nox in the red test. in practice, therefore, we are faced with a considerable increase in the figures previously forecast. the resolution opposes the adoption of the commission's draft resolution, as the commission's proposal would result in a derogation from the euro 6 nox emission limit values. we voted in favour.
‒ taking into account regulation (ec) no 715/2007 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 june 2007 on type-approval of motor vehicles with respect to emissions from light passenger and commercial vehicles (euro 5 and euro 6) and on access to vehicle repair and maintenance information, the commission has drawn up a new draft implementing measure with the aim of amending regulation (ec) no 692/2008 by adapting the test procedures so that they adequately reflect emissions generated by real driving conditions on the road. since i consider that the commission does not exceed its implementing powers by presenting its proposal for a regulation in accordance with the objective and content of regulation (ec) no 715/2007 in so far as the emission limits provided for therein are not called into question, i have voted against this resolution which, pursuant to rule 106 of the rules of procedure, calls on the commission to withdraw its draft regulation and to submit a new proposal by 1 april 2016.
‒ air pollution causes more than 430 000 premature deaths in the european union each year and has an estimated cost of around eur 940 billion due to its harmful effects on public health. to meet the reality these figures reflect, and in line with eu air quality objectives, a continued effort to reduce vehicle emissions is needed. to that end, and given the need for brands to ensure, at the time of type-approval and throughout the lifetime of the vehicle, that the emissions produced do not exceed certain limit values, it is necessary to adopt measures to ensure the effectiveness of the emission control systems of vehicles. the european commission has therefore proposed new implementing measures to amend the regulation by adapting the test procedures to reflect emissions generated under real-world conditions. because appropriate regulation is indispensable and urgent in this area, i voted against this motion for an objection because i consider that the commission's proposal to adapt the test procedures allows them to adequately reflect the emissions generated in real driving conditions on the road.
in writing. ‒ following a meeting with the technical committee on motor vehicles on 28/10/2015, the commission has drawn up a proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 692/2008 as regards pollutant emissions from light passenger and commercial vehicles. the resolution opposes the adoption of the committee's draft resolution, as the committee's proposal would result in a derogation from the euro 6 nox emission limit values. it also exceeds the implementing powers provided for in the regulation. the resolution calls for the proposal to be withdrawn and for a new regulation to be submitted without delay, which would provide for real-world emissions testing and be in line with regulation (ec) no 715/2007.
in writing ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution objecting under rule 106 to the draft resolution amending regulation (ec) no 692/2008 as regards emissions from light passenger and commercial vehicles, because i consider that the commission has exceeded its powers in the process and as a sign of disagreement with the recent behaviour of the council in this matter. i would, however, like to stress the evolution of the european commission's position on real driving tests and the application of factor 1 compliance until 2023, and i hope that we can continue to work towards a path that guarantees the confidence and competitiveness of the european automobile industry and safeguards the health of citizens and the preservation of the environment.
‒ the trade in services agreement (tisa) is a trade agreement being negotiated between 23 members of the world trade organisation with the aim of liberalising trade in services between the participants. in the light of the treaties, the european parliament has no negotiating power, but it has the power to express its opinion during the negotiation process with a view to influencing its development, which means that the final agreement cannot enter into force without the approval of the european parliament and the member states. i support mrs reding's report because i believe that tisa is an opportunity for the eu to consolidate its position as the world's largest exporter of services while providing european consumers with more rights and lower prices, more jobs and economic growth in the eu, and reducing a set of non-tariff barriers that exist today in cross-border services and that disproportionately affect small and medium-sized enterprises. i welcome the exclusion of public and audiovisual services from the agreement and stress the importance of the requirements on data protection and respect for private life.
‒ it is necessary to guarantee more opportunities for european companies in foreign markets, the exclusion of public services, the protection of labour rights and the right to legislate in the public interest. if the european parliament's recommendations are followed, tisa will guarantee more rights for citizens on the inside and remove obstacles to businesses on the outside. the european commission therefore needs to ensure that the agreement creates a level playing field in the services sector and opens up new markets for eu service providers in areas such as telecommunications, transport and public procurement.
in writing. ‒ the trade in services agreement (tisa), as well as the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) and the canada-european union comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta), are part of an unprecedented strategy of deregulation and liberalisation of trade worldwide and the commercialisation of essential public services. tisa covers sectors as diverse as telecommunications and e-commerce, financial services and insurance, transport and even health services. apart from any democratic scrutiny and involvement of governments in this process, a complex web of rules and regulations is intended to be imposed, designed to overcome state constraints and to usurp any national parliamentary control. as with other agreements such as ttip, the whole negotiation process has been conducted in the strictest secrecy. in the end, this agreement represents yet another violent attack on national sovereignty, public services and a policy of development and the welfare of the people. this report, negotiated between the right and the social democrats, endorses tisa and the negotiations which have been taking place, even if, as is usually the case, it seeks to deceive the unwary and to ease some bad consciences by proposing measures to mitigate the negative effects which are already in sight. obviously, we voted against it.
‒ the negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa), together with ttip and ceta, are becoming one of the main instruments for enforcing the commission's neoliberal policies which give privileges to large private sector companies while depriving citizens of their rights. this agreement is not intended to protect public services, compliance with the conventions of the international labour organisation, environmental protection, data protection and the right to privacy. for these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report containing the european parliament's recommendations to the commission on the negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa). the european parliament plays a decisive role in eu trade policy. the european parliament has the final say on trade agreements. in this respect, the trade in services agreement (tisa) should reflect parliament's commitment to project a positive image of the negotiations on the agreement. the eu should continue to implement measures to increase transparency in its trade agreements.
‒ this report on the negotiations on the trade and services agreement represents parliament's position on the negotiations now under way between the commission, representing the union, and 23 member countries of the world trade organisation. this document sets out parliament's priorities in an agreement which must above all guarantee more rights for our citizens and at the same time remove barriers to our businesses in markets outside the union. the conditions must therefore be equal in the services sector, from transport to tourism, public procurement and telecommunications. this agreement will open up new markets for service providers in the union. the agreement should also respect the union acquis on data protection and the right to privacy. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the report.
‒ the generalisation of free trade agreements, of which this agreement (tisa) stands out, but also ttip or ceta, are part of a strategy with an unprecedented scope of deregulation and liberalisation of trade worldwide and the commodification of essential public services. the broad spectrum of sectors covered by tisa (telecommunications and electronic commerce, financial and insurance services, transport and even health services) aims to impose itself as a complex network of rules and regulations, designed to overcome state constraints and any national parliamentary control, in a clear attack on countries' sovereignty, public services and a policy of development and the well-being of populations. all outside of any democratic scrutiny. as with other agreements such as those referred to, the whole negotiation process has been conducted in the strictest secrecy. the text clearly demonstrates the agreement between the right and the social democrats to facilitate the progress of the tisa negotiations and to get it approved, by using cunning tricks to try to deceive the most distracted. we voted against it.
‒ i welcome this report, in which the rapporteur aims to assess the first two and a half years and the first thirteen rounds of negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa) and to make clear and sound recommendations to the european commission. i believe that the negotiations on tisa should ensure greater reciprocity in market access, create a level playing field at global level, provide concrete benefits for consumers and also allow interested parties access to the negotiations in order to facilitate future multilateralisation. in this respect, i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european parliament should work constructively and pragmatically to project a positive image of the tisa negotiations and to give them priority so that a good agreement is reached, which is compatible with the interests of both european companies and european citizens.
‒ this report by mrs reding aims to assess the first two and a half years and the first 13 rounds of negotiations on the trade in services agreement, which is being negotiated between 23 wto members with the aim of liberalising trade in services. the commission's objective recommendations include greater reciprocity in market access, fair conditions at global level, a guarantee of concrete benefits for consumers and access to negotiations for all interested parties, as a way of facilitating future multilateralisation. non-negotiable services such as public and cultural services, fundamental rights to data privacy, fair working conditions and the right to legislate should be excluded from the agreement. tisa should be based on the wto general agreement on trade in services and aim at promoting balances in international trade relations. i am sure that this agreement will give european companies more opportunities to provide services to/in third countries without compromising public services, data and consumer protection, as well as high labour and environmental standards, and i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the plurilateral negotiations for a trade in services agreement (tisa) because it contains the european parliament's recommendations and demands to the european commission with a view to a fair and balanced final agreement. these negotiations are important for the european union, which is the world leader in trade in services. the aim is to regulate trade in services in an ambitious way, covering the major issues of the 21st century, including e-commerce. i support the report because it insists on combating social dumping, advocates the exclusion of public services from the agreement, ensures the right to legislate in the public interest, rejects new commitments in the field of financial services that could compromise eu financial regulation, promotes data protection and privacy in the context of a digital economy and advocates the strengthening of the transparency of tisa negotiations. in short, i supported this report in favour of better regulation of trade in services and against social dumping.
‒ another treaty is under discussion which is highly damaging to national states and to the interests of peoples and workers. as the acronym tisa indicates, this is the complete liberalization on an international scale of the so-called services market, which covers highly sensitive sectors of our economies. in addition to financial services, this includes health, education, transport and even audiovisual and cultural services. the negotiations take place in switzerland under the utmost secrecy. in other words, it is the big capitalist countries that are looking for what they have not been able to get in the big international forums where all countries speak on an equal footing. the aim of this agreement, in practice and in summary, is to do the will of the large lobbies of multinational companies by opening up a number of markets which until now have been protected in accordance with the will of national governments. equal treatment in the provision of these services, but also in the collection of public subsidies, as is the case in the audiovisual sector. in other words, the aim of this treaty is to put an end to the notion of public service as it was created, that is, as a political instrument serving the sovereign development and welfare of the people.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report containing the european parliament's recommendations to the commission on the negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa) because it gives a detailed assessment of the first two and a half years and the first thirteen rounds of negotiations on the tisa agreement and makes clear and consistent recommendations to the european commission. i agree with the rapporteur that the negotiations on tisa should ensure greater reciprocity in market access, create a level playing field globally, provide concrete benefits to consumers and allow stakeholders access to the negotiations, so as to facilitate future multilateralisation, and exclude public and cultural services, fundamental rights to data privacy and fair working conditions, as well as the right to legislate, from the scope of the agreement as non-negotiable. the european parliament must continue its work constructively to promote a positive image of the tisa negotiations, to demystify them and to give them priority, so that a good agreement is reached, which is compatible with the interests of both european companies and european citizens. i also therefore argue that tisa must be balanced, otherwise it cannot exist.
‒ gender equality and women's rights remain a priority for the european parliament. unfortunately, despite the immense progress achieved, both the european continent and the world remain unequal. it is therefore necessary to remain uncompromising in the defence of fundamental rights. achieving results in this area is only possible through a joint effort involving each citizen and the various levels of government, from the town hall to the united nations. at european level, therefore, a concerted strategy with clear objectives and well-defined instruments is also warranted. i am, of course, in favour of an active strategy which goes beyond the mere decree of equality. however, i cannot support the exploitation of the union's core values for purely political purposes. i therefore abstained on this resolution.
‒ equality between women and men is a core value of the member states and is crucial as a strategic objective to achieve the overall goals of growth, employment and social inclusion. member states have taken some important steps to strengthen women's rights and gender equality, but there has been a slowdown in policy action and reform over the last decade at eu level. the employment rate in the member states for men (70.1%) remained higher than for women (59.6%), coupled with the fact that almost a third of women (32.2%) worked part-time. i therefore agree that member states should do more to address equality issues, combat violence against women and ensure equal access and opportunities in the areas of employment, health and education, both in the public and private sectors.
‒ the aim of this resolution is to call on the european commission to adopt immediately a communication on a new strategy for gender equality and women's rights 2016-2020, addressing gender equality issues in the areas of violence against women, working time, decision-making, health, education, media and external relations, and in line with the international agenda, namely the 2015 beijing+20 outcome document and the new framework for 'gender equality and women's empowerment: transforming the lives of girls and women through the eu's external relations (2016-2020). it called on the commission to propose legislative initiatives in its work programme with a view to eliminating the remaining inequalities between women and men in the eu. the resolution contains some criticism of the commission work programme for 2016 for not making any specific reference to the eu strategy for gender equality post-2015. it regrets the lack of concrete objectives and a specific budget, without which progress on targets and indicators is neither measurable nor feasible. we voted in favour.
‒ gender equality is a core value of the eu, enshrined in the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights, and is a key step towards achieving the overall goals of the strategy 2020 for growth, jobs and social inclusion. for these reasons, the european commission should not ignore these assumptions, and it is regrettable that in its work programme for 2016 it does not make any specific reference to the eu strategy for gender equality post-2015 and that in the working document strategic commitment for gender equality, 2016-2019 no concrete objectives or a specific budget are presented, which would allow the feasibility and measurability of the targets proposed by the strategy. in this regard, i support the position of the resolution, which calls on the commission to present a communication on a new strategy for gender equality and women's rights 2016-2020, which takes into account gender equality issues in the areas of violence against women, working time, health, education and to adopt further legislative initiatives in this area in its work programme.
‒ i voted against the motion for a resolution on the new strategy for gender equality and women's rights post-2015. i disagree with the text that has been presented which does nothing to promote and strengthen gender equality.

‒ the proximity of local and regional authorities to citizens allows for the maximisation of the impact and efficiency of public spending which, under the auspices of the institutions and administrations of these authorities, is geared to local needs, close to the citizens. in this respect, the role of local and regional authorities in the design and implementation of european union strategies has been covered by article 5 of the common provisions regulation, which lays down the rules for the five european structural and investment funds (esif). in the light of the above, and in order to be able to guarantee the application of community funds, the commission as guardian of the treaties is expected to strive to strengthen the capacities of local and regional authorities, equipping them to play their intended role. this report comes in the context of the question from the committee on regional development, which, in the matter of strengthening the limited resources of local and regional authorities, asks the commission to define clearly what 'concrete support' measures are envisaged. i voted in favour.
‒ this resolution stresses the key role of local and regional authorities in the design and implementation of eu strategies, recognising that the proximity of these authorities to citizens and the diversity of governance at local and regional level is an asset for the eu. i believe it is important to achieve synergies and complementarity between the european structural and investment funds (esif) and other eu programmes, where local and regional authorities can play a useful role in achieving cohesion policy objectives. in this sense, i consider eu cohesion policy to be a good example of multi-level governance, with a bottom-up approach, where local and regional authorities, within the framework of the esi funds, strike a balance between the union's objective of greater economic, social and territorial cohesion and the territorial impact of eu policies. this ensures the fulfilment of the eu's key policy objectives, such as economic growth, social progress and sustainable development. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour of this document.
‒ cohesion policy reform will be the eu's main investment instrument for achieving the europe 2020 objectives. acting at regional level as a mechanism of opportunity for a sustainable growth process, supporting job creation, entrepreneurship, economic innovation, the quality of life of citizens and the sustainable development of regions, the role of local and regional authorities in adapting and implementing eu strategies, cohesion policy is fundamental to an effective response to the unique needs and characteristics of each region. multi-level governance thus exemplifies the democratic dimension of the eu and how the measures outlined can have effective results. economic growth, social progress, territorial cohesion and sustainable development are common objectives of the union which will become more feasible thanks to a plurality of governments at local and regional level, allowing the eu and each region to apply the instruments at their disposal effectively. i agree with the measures presented in this motion for a resolution and consider it of the utmost importance to bring local and regional decisions closer to local authorities and citizens, so i voted in favour of this motion.
in writing. the resolution under consideration advocates a desirable and necessary impetus for the increase and deepening of development partnerships. in this sense, cohesion policy must involve local and regional actors throughout the process of granting and implementing eu strategies. only then will it be possible to work from the bottom up. the importance of a good coordination of technical means at the different levels - local, regional, national and european - should be taken into account in order to ensure the full benefit of participation and funding opportunities.
‒ the role of cities in contemporary development is indisputable. these are areas of high population representation (more than 75% of eu citizens live in an urban context), with growing needs in terms of their political, social, economic and cultural organisation, and also with new demands, both institutional and from various sectors of the population. the creation of two lines of funding specific to cities - community-led local development and integrated territorial investments - through the european structural and investment funds will help to improve access by cities to important funding which can contribute to job creation, infrastructure improvement, optimisation of services, and to their development and that of their populations. however, there is one issue that must be addressed, which is the tendency to overcome the obstacles to a federalist logic (by the member states or in the definition of the treaties themselves) through direct communication between the european commission and 'the cities', without the intermediation of the member states, with their definition of priorities for their regions.
‒ yemen is experiencing an unprecedented humanitarian crisis as a result of the collapse of the regime and the war raging in its territory. the most elementary norms of international law are not being observed, contributing to the impact of this conflict on the civilian population. schools and hospitals attacked, preventing access to education or health care; entire regions without access to food or water. the territory of this failed state is also home to numerous terrorist organisations, including the most active al-qaeda cell. it is urgent that the international community and the parties involved should be able to call for an end to the conflict. but it is even more urgent to ensure that international humanitarian law is respected, thus preventing innocent people, those civilians who have not already been killed by war, from dying as a result of the conflict. even in war, there are limits.
‒ the current crisis in yemen is the result of the failure of successive governments to respond to the legitimate aspirations of the yemeni people for democracy, economic and social development, stability and security. on the other hand, the military intervention in yemen by saudi forces and the use of cluster bombs has led to a dramatic humanitarian situation. since the start of the conflict, at least 5979 people have been killed, about half of them civilians, and 28 208 people have been injured, including hundreds of women and children. i therefore express my concern at the alarming worsening of the humanitarian situation in yemen, characterised by widespread food insecurity and acute malnutrition, indiscriminate attacks on civilians, doctors and members of humanitarian organisations, destruction of civilian and medical infrastructure caused by the existing internal conflict and the intensification of air strikes by the saudi-led coalition.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on yemen. the situation in yemen is worrying and it is important that the eu seeks to find a political solution capable of ensuring peace and stability in yemen.

in writing. the conclusions of the european council are a good illustration of the scale of the crisis, the degree of disintegration, the absence of values and the lack of legitimacy which mark the process of european capitalist integration. the negotiations on the so-called 'brexit' and the 'solution' they have found show that, faced with the worsening crisis and the contradictions between the powers that develop within it, eu leaders have no other answer than to try to 'package' the elements of eu disintegration into a bureaucratic maze and to deepen the reactionary character of their policies. the decisions now announced deny the eu's much-vaunted and much-loved 'freedoms'. the 'freedom of movement' is, after all, as we have always said, the freedom of big capital to carry on its predatory and exploitative activities. when it comes to meeting the interests of big finance capital, resolving contradictions between powers and saving their supranational mechanisms of political and economic domination, the eu's treaties and legislation are subject to change and even subversion. this 'flexibility' now demonstrated in the 'brexit' case contrasts with the unacceptable rigidity and immobility in the face of the very serious social crisis and with the pressures and blackmail that continue to be directed against countries like portugal.

the report on the social and employment aspects of the european semester aims to transform the european union into a modern social europe, taking into account the current potential and challenges, and highlights the concrete measures that need to be implemented to balance the economic and social dimensions and to promote sustainable social development. it emphasises that economic and financial systems are designed to improve the living conditions of citizens, and this is the main reason why we need to continue to consolidate these systems. the commission also proposes that the member states and the european institutions should ensure, in a responsible manner, the long-term stability of their policy and budgetary choices if we are to move towards sustainable growth. in this context, this report focuses on the need to consolidate public finances and tax systems, given the current fragile economic situation in many member states, and stresses the importance of such consolidation in ensuring social stability, not only in the present times, but also in preparing the future of the younger generations. as we have seen in recent years, the resilience of member states to the financial crisis is linked to the strength of their public finances, and those with the most unstable economies and larger deficits perform the worst. this financial consolidation must be accompanied by growth policies, which translate into a set of structural reforms aimed at competitiveness and the defence of the social role of the states in the face of the structural problems we are facing today. the sustainability of social security and social welfare systems and pension schemes is perhaps the most paradigmatic example of this challenge, given the expected trend of an ageing european population in the coming years. education is also seen as a key pillar of development, and we need to ensure that education systems equip young people with the necessary skills, especially in the new areas of employment, such as the digital, green and blue economies. it is also an essential area for meeting the needs of enterprises, which are the prime engine of development. we believe that european policies should still encourage public and private investment at european level, but that investment must be directed towards projects that guarantee economic and/or social returns and must promote growth, and can never be a mechanism for the mere use of public funds. finally, i would like to highlight the entirely new approach proposed in this process, which consists in the unprecedented introduction of social indicators, in particular the activity rate, youth employment and long-term employment, in the analysis of the overall development of the member states. if this report is adopted, parliament will be sending a strong message to the commission and the council that, alongside other existing indicators such as those in the economic and financial field, we must have mechanisms to gauge the extent to which our policies are having an impact on the daily lives of our fellow citizens. this will be a way of ensuring that internal imbalances in the member states are further assessed so that we can redesign their economic and social reforms where necessary. this is a major step which allows us to strengthen the social pillar. in conclusion, madam president, i would like to thank my fellow shadow rapporteurs from the other political groups who have worked very hard with me in our joint effort to reach a common position.
rapporteur.– madam president, we are at an important moment for the european semester because parliament can deliver today three important reports which deal with a situation that is quite unique in the european union. we are dealing with overlapping crises and, if you want to cope with these overlapping crises, it is certain that we need to strengthen the internal cohesion of the european union. this will depend a lot on delivering a much stronger and more balanced recovery. i have the pleasure to present today the report adopted by the committee on economic and monetary affairs. i am very grateful to my colleagues, because i believe that it was possible to reach a very useful compromise with real added value for the situation in the european union. the starting point of our report is to say that the european semester should be used to pursue the rebalancing of our budgets and relevant reforms, but also to implement the europe 2020 strategy for growth and jobs, because we believe that, in the end, the future of europe will depend on this kind of competitiveness geared to the future, based on energy transition, digital solutions and bringing about more and better jobs. but if this is the case, the policy mix should be fully supported for this ambition. this means that in the policy mix to be implemented in the coming year, pushing for investment should be a top priority. this means making the best of the available tools, starting with the european investment plan, but also completing the banking union to make access to credit much easier for small and medium-sized enterprises. we do, of course, also need reforms, but we believe that we need a second generation of reforms pushing for education, innovation and good public administration and ensuring sustainable welfare systems. and, of course, we need to pursue the fiscal rebalancing of our budgets, but in such a way that we do not undermine this pro-growth move and the strategic investment we need to address. we should also take into account the fact that europe is confronted with new challenges, security issues and, in particular, the refugee crisis. i believe that the most important value in our report is the way to manage the euro area, because we recognise that the euro area is an economic entity deserving an appropriate policy mix. that is why we recommend that the investment gap which is there in the euro area should be addressed by sharing the contributions from different countries, particularly those with more fiscal space. the same should happen when it comes to reducing macroeconomic imbalances because, on the one hand, we need more-competitive countries to expand internal demand and, on the other, we need less-competitive countries to increase their competitiveness – not by reducing wages and social conditions but rather by investing in the future. these are important conclusions. we believe that it is crucial to organise upward convergence in the eurozone, assuming that economic and social objectives should be treated in the same way. this can only be delivered if we complete economic and monetary union with a fiscal capacity and the banking union.
i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr dombrovskis, for his report. i would like to begin by thanking the whole team of colleagues who were rapporteurs and in particular maria joão rodrigues for this excellent report. the message from the report is very clear: it says that it is time to change europe's economic agenda. today in the united states, the 2008 crisis belongs in the history books. in the european union, however, we are still "skating" (pardon the plebeianism) on an excessively weak recovery and unemployment. the expectations for german industry today are unfortunately at the level of 2008-2009. banking and insurance have again begun to show signs of strain, because there is no good business without good profitable companies, and there are no profitable companies without domestic demand and without investment, however low the interest rate. in economics, you can't just look at supply, there has to be demand, and the economic policy we've been pursuing has extinguished that demand through excessive austerity. today, any fluctuation in the united states or china's economy is a source of concern for the union. the budgetary policy must be adjusted and there must be symmetry in the adjustment between deficit and surplus countries. we must protect strategic investment and there seems to be a consensus on this. and we must complete the banking union, or the european union will lose control of its own destiny. portugal is a good example of how it is possible to comply with european rules and adopt a policy more conducive to economic growth and employment. but the union and the commission in particular, as well as the council, must be available to support alternatives such as these and also to change the dominant position which has hitherto existed in the general policy of monetary union itself. with so many problems threatening the union, let us have the intelligence to solve the economic component, because that is in our hands. i hope so.

the ep's annual growth survey and european semester 2016 report marks a turning point in the prevailing thinking in the european forum for representing european citizens. the report rejects the austerity model and advocates a coordination of economic and social policies based on the europe 2020 strategy for growth and jobs. it advocates the strengthening of investment and domestic demand. it advocates 'second-generation' structural reforms to boost growth potential, focusing on education and innovation, the sustainability of the social model, the modernisation of public administration and a fair and equitable tax system. it also supports a new model for the management of the euro area which would make it closer to an optimal monetary area by providing it with its own instruments within the framework of economic and monetary union. it is a historic report whose recommendations must be implemented.

‒ the hague convention allows for the recognition of crossborder service of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters. however, in the case of the european union, it is only applicable to documents originating in or destined for third countries, as community rules already exist for the same purpose between member states. since it has exclusive competence in this area and cannot, as a signatory, accede to the convention, the union must authorise individual member states to accede. given the clear european interest in the existence of a common regime, the european parliament is giving its consent to accession.
‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 establishes a system whereby documents may be delivered in another signatory state. of the 28 member states, 26 already apply this convention. austria and malta, the two member states which have not yet applied it, have expressed their wish to join. malta has already deposited its instrument of accession but has made a declaration that its accession will not be effective until this decision is adopted. austria is awaiting this decision in order to complete the accession formalities. since the hague convention has proved useful in the field of crossborder service of documents, and it is in the interest of both the union as a whole and the two member states concerned to have a single system for the service of documents in crossborder relations with third countries, i support the decision allowing austria and malta to accede to that convention.
‒ this convention covers the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters. it also defines the means to be used when a judicial act is to be transmitted from one contracting state to another for service there. it allows for the improvement of the transmission of judicial and extrajudicial documents, facilitates judicial cooperation in transnational judicial proceedings and creates an efficient and reliable system for the citation and service of judicial and extrajudicial documents. the eu cannot be a party to the convention because it does not establish anything about regional economic organisations, only individual states. member states may not conclude the convention without being authorised to do so by the eu in accordance with the tfeu. we reject this reality, which is just another expression of the loss of sovereignty of the states as a result of the deepening of the process of capitalist integration which is the eu. this is the formalization of the procedure for accession to the hague convention for the only two member states which were not members of the convention. by his own free and sovereign decision. we voted in favour.

‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters aims to improve the transmission of judicial and extrajudicial documents to or from third countries. it currently applies to 26 member states, with the remaining two - austria and malta - having expressed an interest in acceding to the convention. while it is true that, in accordance with article 3 (2) tfeu, the union has exclusive external competence in this area, those member states need authorisation to accede to the convention. furthermore, since the union cannot become a contracting party to the convention, it is necessary for the union to exercise its competences through the member states and it is therefore in the union's interest to authorise their accession. in these terms, and considering that it is in the interest of both the union as a whole and the two member states concerned to have a single system for the service of documents in crossborder relations with third countries, i voted in favour of this draft decision authorising the accession of austria and malta to that convention.

‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 regulates the procedure for the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters. of the 28 member states of the european union, only two had not yet applied the convention: austria and malta. since this convention does not allow for the accession of international organisations, the eu should authorise the member states concerned to act on its behalf in order to accede to it. since this convention has proved useful in the field of crossborder service of judicial and extrajudicial documents, it is in the interest of both the union as a whole and the two member states concerned to apply this convention, and i therefore voted in favour of this legislative resolution.
‒ this convention covers the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters. a judicial act is one that is made by a judge or by the parties involved in a judicial proceeding. an extrajudicial act is one that originates outside the judicial area, for example notarial acts. this convention defines the means to be used when a judicial act is to be transmitted from one contracting state to another for service there. the countries shall define the competence of an authority to transmit and to serve the summons and service and that authority shall take the necessary measures to effect such a summons/service. before, this was done through consular or diplomatic channels. it defines alternative means of transmission of documents, for example by post. it is a formal aspect. these two countries are the only two member states not party to this convention.

‒ the free movement of workers is one of the four freedoms which form the basis of the european internal market. the european mobility portal eures is an important tool for such mobility, as it allows a cross-border match between job supply and demand, but also as a reliable source and aggregator of information. however, it should be remembered that labour market policy, including all support measures, remains a matter for national competence. to that extent, the proper functioning of measures such as this depends on national authorities, which justifies, for example, that the public services of each member state should be designated automatically by the member states as members of the network responsible for the application of this regulation. on the other hand, only 3.1% of the european workforce works in another member state and on average only 700 000 people move each year. greater use of this mobility, which allows a greater match between demand and supply, contributes to more employment. faced with unemployment which remains worrying in some countries, notably portugal, improving instruments such as eures is of even greater importance. that is why i support this report.
in writing. the eures network was set up in 1993 with the aim of helping europeans find employment in another member state. however, high unemployment rates in some eu member states coexist with opportunities in other countries, but intra-eu labour mobility remains relatively low. only 3.1% of european workers are economically active in another member state (7.5 million out of 241 million workers). language skills and difficulties in finding a job are cited as the main reasons for this. the proposal for a regulation aims to improve the eures network by broadening the supply of jobs and improving the accessibility of curricula, improving the link between available vacancies and existing curricula, increasing the exchange of information between member states on their shortcomings and including traineeships and other apprenticeship programmes. the network currently has over one million vacancies and 235,000 available cvs.
the report proposes amendments to the european commission's proposal for a regulation on eures a european network of employment services. the original proposal raised some issues which merited our opposition, although in a general, not negative sense. the amendments to it are, on the whole, positive. a warning to the issue of compulsory mobility. the report introduces amendments which give greater prominence to the member states and their (employment and training) structures, ensure the involvement of trade unions, treat mobility as an essentially cross-border issue and guarantee the free provision of all eures services. in this respect, the regulation has been improved. it is understood that a voluntary mobility facilitation network such as that presented in this report is an interesting development, and so, not supporting the original proposal, we voted in favour of this report.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and the development of labour market integration. the european union must use all the instruments necessary to reverse the unemployment situation. in view of the high unemployment rate in some regions of europe, it is necessary to strengthen the mobility of workers within the eu. this regulation will enable the eures network to be an effective tool in the near future for both jobseekers and employers interested in the mobility of workers within the eu. it will be an opportunity to establish a more transparent process so that people looking for a job can get accurate information about working conditions and services at the workplace.
the report proposes amendments to the proposal for a regulation on the eures network (european employment services) and not its development. the commission's original text contains some references which we regard as negative, distorting the relationship between the labour market and school curricula. the extension of the network to include the promotion of traineeships and training is one of the positive elements. we also note a slowdown in the emphasis on mobility, in particular compulsory mobility. the report proposes amendments that reinforce the role of the member states and their structures (employment and training), elements that enhance the sovereignty and decision-making capacity of the states. it values the involvement of the social partners, gives guidance on the perspective of mobility as an essentially cross-border issue and advocates the free provision of all eures services. some considerations and proposals which we believe will improve the regulation. it is understood that mobility should not be coercive, but should result from a voluntary decision, in which case a facilitating network such as that presented in this report can be useful for the workers involved. that is why we voted in favour.
‒ the free choice of workplace within the eu is an integral part of free movement as it constitutes one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union and a crucial element of eu citizenship. the mobility of workers within the eu is relatively low compared to the size of the labour market and the active population in the eu the mobility rate in the eu-27 is only 0.29%. it is therefore necessary to increase the mobility of workers within the eu, to improve employment opportunities and to help employers find better-qualified workers more quickly for the jobs they have available, thus developing the european labour market. the objective of this regulation is to make the eures network (european job mobility portal) an effective tool for both jobseekers and employers interested in the mobility of workers within the eu by providing access, at european level and in a transparent manner, to the widest possible set of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles.
‒ this report concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council which aims to make the eures network a more effective tool for both jobseekers and employers interested in the mobility of workers within the eu by providing access, at european level and in a transparent manner, to a wide range of job vacancies and profiles of jobseekers. however, and although i consider it important to promote labour mobility within the eu, i would point out that this proposal for a regulation provides that priority should be given to nationals of eu member states when filling jobs, without, however, forgetting that labour market policies remain the sphere of competence of the member states. i also believe that, based on the lessons learned from the high unemployment rate in some regions of europe, it is important to enhance the mobility of workers by improving employment opportunities and facilitating the recruitment process for employers. in view of the positive contribution which these measures will certainly make to the development of the european labour market and, consequently, to the increase in employment rates, i voted in favour of this report.

‒ the autonomous emergency trade measures for tunisia are part of a strategy to support the young tunisian democracy, the only successful case of the arab spring. the european union is also concerned about the situation in tunisia, which is suffering from terrorist attacks aimed at destabilising the country, is facing serious problems at its borders, particularly in libya, and is facing a fragile economic and social situation. it is therefore of great importance that europe sends a clear signal of support to the democratic regime in tunisia. the eu countries should not view the opening up to tunisia as a circumstantial threat to specific european economic sectors, but rather as an aid to the maintenance of a still rather fragile democracy. support in a wide range of areas must be seen as essential to preventing a serious problem in that country with unforeseeable consequences on the european territory itself. at a time when the experts on the lucidity of the next day are concentrating on blaming europe for not having acted pre-emptively and are dedicated to holding it fully responsible for the dramatic problems of human rights violations in the north african and middle eastern region, it would be important that they do not oppose a proposal aimed at the democratic stabilisation of a country facing serious problems.
in writing. ‒ i am in solidarity with tunisia as it seeks to consolidate its democracy and recover an economy that was further damaged by the 2015 terrorist attacks in tunis and sousse. i agree that the eu should provide support that will help tunisia's economic development. but this solidarity must be an eu-wide effort and not be mainly a penalty for the countries of southern europe. the proposal aims to facilitate the duty-free entry of 70,000 tonnes of olive oil onto the european market, in addition to the 56,700 tonnes provided for in the association agreement. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of the environment. moreover, the trend in olive oil over the last ten years has been a continuous fall in prices and a decline in crop profitability as a result of a steady increase in production costs. i therefore abstained in the final vote, as the amendments i supported were not adopted.
‒ olive oil is the main agricultural product exported from tunisia to the eu. the olive oil sector is an important part of the economy of the country, as well as of certain regions of certain member states, particularly the south. the proposed regulation of the community executive provides for the granting of an annual tariff quota, duty free, of 35000 tonnes for exports of olive oil from tunisia to the eu in 2016 and 2017 (i.e. 70000 tonnes in total). this quota would be opened after the current 56 700 tonnes, also without tariff, under the eu-tunisia association agreement have been used up. i doubt whether these benefits will compensate for the losses and possible disruptions in the european olive oil sector, particularly in portugal. before this decision was taken, there should have been a study assessing the economic, social and territorial impact of this proposal. for this reason, i abstained on the motion.
in the light of the above, the commission considers that the measures provided for in this decision are in accordance with the opinion of the committee established by article 15 (1) of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council, the quota is available for a period of two years from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017. the philosophy of the measure is the same as that which has explained in the past identical measures, for example, in relation to the import of textiles from pakistan. for portugal, as for other mediterranean member states, olive oil production is of significant economic and social importance and will be adversely affected by this measure. other measures of genuine and more effective solidarity with the tunisian people could have been taken. that is not the purpose of this measure. this measure benefits european importers (and some limited interests in tunisia) but harms the same importers. the truth is that such measures never harm the most powerful countries in the eu (as was the case with textiles in pakistan, as is now the case with olive oil in tunisia). it is always the same people who bear the costs of this false solidarity.
in the report on the introduction of autonomous emergency trade measures for tunisia, my vote was abstention. after the attacks in tunisia, it is important that the european union shows solidarity with that country. however, i have many reservations when i see the european union using trade policy as a bargaining chip in situations of this nature. in that case, the olive oil sector in the southern european countries will be severely damaged. the olive oil sector is extremely important for portugal, which has been promoting domestic production with investment and internationalisation support, having tripled production between 2007 and 2014. i am concerned about the damage that the sector may suffer, and i have therefore abstained.

in writing. ‒ in 2014, the ombudsman opened 325 inquiries based on complaints and 17 own-initiative inquiries. the complaints were mainly from individual citizens (335) and from companies, associations and other legal entities (52). as regards the origin of complaints by country, spain topped the list (309), followed by germany (219), poland (208) and belgium (147). of the 342 inquiries opened by the european ombudsman, 204 (59.6%) concerned the european commission, 47 (13.7%) the eu agencies, 29 (8.5%) other bodies, 32 (9.4%) the european personnel selection office (epso), 12 (3.8%) the european parliament, 13 (3.8%) the european external action service and 11 (3.2%) the european anti-fraud office. in 2014, the ombudsman dealt with 2163 complaints received. in 1217 cases, its services provided advice or transferred the case in 621 cases, the complainant was informed that no further action could be taken and in 325 cases an investigation was opened. the ombudsman's budget is an independent section of the eu budget. the ombudsman's 2014 budget was eur 9 857 002 and the institution's staff included 67 posts. i voted in favour.

‒ despite the european central bank's focus on maintaining favourable financing conditions, private and public investment in the euro area remains considerably below pre-crisis levels. in the context of the complex context of the sovereign debt crisis, falling inflation, credit contraction and stagnating economic growth, the ecb has resorted to unconventional monetary policy instruments. i support the marias report as a whole, as it records the positive effect of some measures, such as the creation of the european fund for strategic investments, as well as the european commission's plan to establish a true capital markets union, which should diversify the sources of finance in the eu economy, boost cross-border investment and increase access to finance for businesses, especially smes. i agree that the supervisory and monetary policy functions of the ecb should be clearly distinguished and should not give rise to conflicts of interest for the ecb, and that the ecb should be subject to democratic control in view of the new responsibilities conferred upon it.
‒ the economic recovery in the euro area is expected to progress, with gdp growth of 1.4% in 2015, 1.7% in 2016 and 1.8% in 2017, but this requires a strong political commitment to implementing sustainable and socially balanced structural reforms that are essential to stimulating economic growth. unemployment in the euro area itself is expected to decline slowly from 11,6% at the end of 2014 to 10,5% at the end of 2016 with large disparities between unemployment rates in different member states, with figures ranging from 6,4% in germany to 26,6% in greece. the average inflation rate in the euro area, after remaining close to zero in the first half of 2015, is expected to increase again, rising to 1,1% in 2016 and 1,7% in 2017, despite the ecb's continued efforts to maintain favourable financing conditions. the truth is that private and public investment in the euro area remains considerably below pre-crisis levels and the european institutions must continue to engage in a permanent dialogue if europe's economic, social and political objectives are to be achieved.

‒ pets make a positive contribution to the lives of millions of eu citizens, and eu legislation already provides for the possibility for owners to travel with their animals safely and in a controlled manner throughout the eu. however, although many member states have implemented mandatory systems for the identification and registration of pet animals, there are discrepancies as regards the type of information held, the animals covered by the identification and registration requirements and the level of governance to which information is provided. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the matter. i support this resolution, which calls for a system of compatible standards for the registration and identification of these animals, thus combating illegal trade and even outbreaks of animal diseases.
in writing. ‒ non-governmental organisations, law enforcement authorities, competent authorities and veterinarians have demonstrated the existence of a growing illicit trade in pet animals, marked by widespread violations of the regime for the movement of pet animals, controls evasion and falsification of documents, and associated with serious and organised crime. i therefore support the existence of a compatible system for the identification and registration of pet animals in the eu which will certainly have benefits beyond simply combating illegal trade, benefits which include tracing the source of disease outbreaks and combating animal abuse and other animal welfare concerns.
the resolution calls on the european commission to facilitate the establishment of a system of mandatory identification and registration of pet animals, allowing access to pet data registered at national level to obtain an eu-wide traceability system, stressing that the personal data of pet owners and sellers must be respected in accordance with eu legal standards on the protection of personal data. it also urged the european commission to explore further measures to combat the illegal trade in pet animals contained in the conclusions of the study on the welfare of dogs and cats involved in commercial practices. the proposal is to harmonise the requirements for the identification and registration of dogs and cats, which could reduce the possibility of falsification of documents and illegal trade, thus improving animal welfare and the protection of public and animal health, and providing for effective traceability in the eu. increasingly, pet owners are traveling with their pets. it is important that they can do so in a safe and controlled manner, given the existence of over 100 zoonotic diseases in these animals and the risks that come with it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the introduction of pet registration systems that are compatible in all member states. since the european commission has funded a study on the welfare of dogs and cats involved in commercial practices and it has been demonstrated by the competent authorities and veterinarians that there is a growing illegal trade in pet animals, with widespread violation of the pet movement regime, evasion of controls and falsification of documents, i think it makes perfect sense to adopt this resolution.
‒ there is an increasing trend towards the movement of pets on the move with their owners. such movement should be possible in a safe and controlled manner, taking into account the existence of more than 100 zoonoses in these animals and the risks arising therefrom. the resolution calls on the european commission to facilitate the establishment of a system of pet registration and compulsory identification which will aggregate data at national level and enable the creation of an eu-wide traceability system. stresses that the personal data of pet owners and sellers should be respected in accordance with eu legal standards on the protection of personal data. it also called for further measures to combat the illegal trade in pet animals to be explored, as contained in the conclusions of the study on the welfare of dogs and cats involved in commercial practices. it is proposed to harmonise the requirements for the identification and registration of dogs and cats, which could reduce the possibility of falsification of documents and illegal trade, thus improving animal welfare and the protection of public and animal health.
‒ the positive contribution of pets to the lives of millions of people and families in the eu is recognised and, as such, it is already provided for in european legislation that pet owners can travel with their pets in a safe and controlled manner throughout the union. however, despite the requirement by some member states to implement systems for the identification and registration of pet animals, there remain numerous differences in the applicability of both the information on animals subject to identification and registration requirements and the way in which that information is managed. because of this somewhat complex reality, the illegal and abusive use of the pet movement regime has been exploited within the eu for illicit purposes and in the pursuit of easy profit. unfortunately, this is a reality that has tended to increase in recent years. i therefore voted in favour of this report, since the aim is to achieve unification of the rules for the registration and identification of these animals in a single system, thus effectively combating illegal trade and, in many cases, outbreaks of animal diseases.
in writing. ‒ although many member states have mandatory systems for the identification and registration of pet animals, most of these databases are not interconnected, preventing full traceability when animals are moved across member states' borders. in addition, where such systems exist, there are discrepancies between the type of information held, the animals covered by the identification and registration requirements and the levels of governance at which the information is held. the resolution therefore proposes that the identification and registration requirements for dogs (canis lupus familiaris) and cats (felis silvestris catus) be harmonised, which would reduce the possibility of falsification of documents and illegal trade, thereby improving animal welfare and the protection of public and animal health, and providing for effective traceability in the union. we voted yes.
‒ the current crisis in yemen is the result of the failure of successive governments to respond to the legitimate aspirations of the yemeni people for democracy, economic and social development, stability and security by creating the conditions for an outbreak of violence. since the start of the conflict, at least 5,979 people have been killed, about half of them civilians, and 28,208 people have been injured. in 2015, the eu allocated €52 million in new humanitarian aid to the crisis in yemen and its impact on the horn of africa and will allocate up to €2 million to the establishment of the united nations verification and inspection mechanism. i express my concern at the alarming worsening of the humanitarian situation in the country, characterised by a situation of widespread food insecurity and acute malnutrition, indiscriminate attacks against civilians, doctors and members of humanitarian organisations, destruction of civilian and medical infrastructure and the intensification of airstrikes by the saudi-led coalition, ground fighting and shelling, despite repeated calls for a new cessation of hostilities.
the serious situation in yemen is inseparable from a process in which foreign powers exploit memories, feelings, tribal and feudal relations, stoking ethnic and religious conflicts, generalising corruption and criminal trafficking, and encouraging and exploiting terrorism, always for their own benefit. imperialism is multiplying conflicts in the middle east which, as in syria, are causing immeasurable human suffering, destroying countries whose wealth transnational capital is trying to seize. this generally positive resolution identifies several problems felt at the present time by the yemeni people, but it is lacking in what is needed. it does not expressly condemn the role of imperialist powers such as the united states and other countries whose actions have contributed to the deaths of thousands of innocent people, as was the case with the bombings of sana and aden. it proposes a political solution to the situation but does not categorically reject future external interventions in yemen. there is no condemnation of the role of the dictatorships of the persian gulf, particularly saudi arabia, in the military aggressions imposed on that country. despite the difficult situation facing the yemeni people, we have full confidence that even in this tangle of contradictions and conflicts fuelled by foreign aggression, the struggle for freedom which the yemeni people are pursuing will triumph.
