‒ animal health is a matter of concern for all european citizens, both because of its relevance to public health, food safety and food security linked to animal health, and because of the economic costs of animal disease outbreaks and the value of animal welfare. i support the selimovic report which approves the council's position at first reading on the regulation on transmissible animal diseases, laying down new rules on the prevention and control of animal diseases which can be transmitted to other animals or to humans, such as avian influenza and swine fever. the regulation replaces some 40 pieces of legislation, placing greater emphasis on preventive measures, disease surveillance and research, and providing for greater cooperation between animal professionals, pet owners, authorities and veterinarians.
in writing. ‒ about 70% of infectious diseases are common to animals and humans. the new eu animal health regulation puts greater emphasis on preventive measures, disease surveillance and research and provides for greater cooperation between animal professionals, pet owners, authorities and veterinarians. the new rules clarify the responsibilities of operators and professionals working with animals, such as farmers, pet owners and veterinarians, to prevent the introduction, development and spread of diseases. for example, farmers, persons selling animals and animal keepers will be responsible for the application of good animal husbandry practices and for the prudent and responsible use of veterinary medicinal products. i voted in favour.
‒ the process of simplifying and updating eu animal health legislation has been ongoing since 2013. this final text, which is still under consideration, is better than the one originally presented by the commission. it is accompanied by an annex containing three statements. a joint action plan to address the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. another concerns the regular reporting of the use of antimicrobial medicinal products in animals. and another on animal welfare, noting that this regulation laying down rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases transmissible to animals and humans does not contain provisions specifically governing animal welfare. of course, the productivism of the current cap and the capitalist production models, which lead to a higher incidence and prevalence of infectious diseases in animals, and the consequent defence of other agricultural policies, must be criticized. there are still a number of doubts about the aquaculture sector, which supplies a large proportion of the fish that reaches the consumer's table. the commission has not yet clarified what it means by 'aquatic health professionals' and what guarantees they offer consumers.
‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on transmissible animal diseases and amending and repealing certain acts in the field of animal health ('animal health act'). the new rules on the prevention and control of animal diseases which can be transmitted to other animals or to humans are essential. the avian flu is a case that demonstrates this danger. that is why animal disease surveillance has never been more important. greater preventive measures, more research and greater cooperation between professionals working with animals, especially authorities and veterinarians, will be needed. for the first time, european legislation recognises a link between animal health, animal welfare and public health.
‒ this proposal concerns european legislation in the field of animal health, which replaces some 40 european legislative acts, some of which date back to 1964. i am voting in favour of this report because i am in favour of the creation of a single, simplified, transparent and clear legal framework which will allow for a clear and balanced distribution of tasks and responsibilities between the competent authorities, the institutions of the european union, the agricultural sector, animal owners and others, in the field of surveillance, prevention and control of different animal diseases. animal welfare is of the utmost importance, including for public health, as approximately 70% of infectious diseases are common to animals and humans. i agree with the importance of establishing rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases which can be transmitted to animals or to humans.
‒ the resolution deals with the process of simplifying and updating eu legislation on animal health, which has been dragging on since 2013. the annex to the final text contains three statements concerning (i) the establishment of an action plan against the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance and the consequent expected reduction in the use of antibiotics in animals; (ii) the regular reporting of the use of antimicrobial medicinal products in animals in the union; and (iii) animal welfare. the latter notes that this regulation does not contain provisions specifically regulating animal welfare, which cannot be dissociated from animal health. the resolution could and should have gone further, criticizing and rejecting the productivism of the current cap and the capitalist production models that lead to a higher incidence and prevalence of infectious diseases in animals, and advocating another agricultural policy. there are still doubts about the aquaculture sector, which is the source of an increasing share of the fish that reaches the consumer's table, in particular as regards the clarification of the category of 'aquatic health professionals' and the guarantee that they can offer to consumers.
‒ this report endorses the council's first reading position on an action plan against the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. it also stressed the preventive role of the regulation on transmissible animal diseases and the expected reduction in the use of antibiotics in animals as a result. i voted in favour of this report because it commits the member states to collecting detailed, comparable and relevant data on the actual use of antimicrobials in animals and to transmitting this data to the commission, in order to ensure a more prudent use of these medicines, thus contributing to reducing the risk of antimicrobial resistance.
‒ the european parliament has adopted new rules on the prevention and control of animal diseases which can be transmitted to other animals or to humans, such as influenza, foot-and-mouth disease or swine fever. greater emphasis is placed on preventive measures, disease surveillance and research, with greater and better collaboration between animal professionals, pet owners, authorities and veterinarians. it is essential that this adherence to the principles of good breeding and to biosecurity measures for the protection of animals and humans is put into practice.
‒ the animal health strategy should contribute to the prevention and control of animal diseases, with particular attention to antimicrobial resistance. this is a public health issue, given the frequency of the same diseases in animals and humans and the hypothetical transmission of antimicrobial resistance between animals and humans, recently corroborated by a study in china. the way in which this issue is approached in practice should take account of the specificities of production in different regions of europe, especially with regard to climatic conditions that favour the occurrence and transmission of diseases. the conditions imposed on european producers in the field of animal health must also be taken into account in trade negotiations with third countries.
‒ we can praise the principle of 'putting legislation together', replacing 50 directives and regulations and more than 400 other legislative acts, using a holistic approach that brings together human and animal health in a single public health concept and also seeks to integrate the issue of animal welfare as a basic element in the health status of our domestic species. however, this is of course a risky aim, since it carries underlying the idea that it is possible and desirable to give more powers to the european institutions in health management and the control and eradication of the main zoonoses. nothing more fake. good sanitary management requires proximity and knowledge of the terrain. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the animal health sector is not affected by the new rules. what the eu could and should do is to radically change the cap, since it generates intensive production, the emergence of new diseases and the intensive use of medicines. this would indeed be a major step towards improving animal health by reducing the impact of zoonotic diseases.
‒ i voted in favour of the selimovic report because i believe that this proposal improves the animal health law by obliging animal operators and keepers to respect the principle of animal welfare in animal husbandry and to adopt biosecurity measures to protect their animals. another obligation is to use veterinary medicinal products responsibly and prudently, in particular to prevent the development of antimicrobial resistance. finally, in the interest of animal welfare, pain and suffering should be avoided when carrying out disease control measures.

‒ the european commission has moved forward with a proposal for a regulation establishing a regulatory framework for access to port services and financial transparency in ports. through this regulation, the european commission intends to make a major contribution to increasing the efficiency and competitiveness of european ports in the trans-european transport network. the development of european legislation governing port activities is of great importance, since it makes a decisive contribution to the standardization of management practices and defines common general rules necessary for healthy competition between european ports. however, improvements were needed to the initial proposal in order to, among other things, provide greater flexibility for port administrations and to strengthen the protection of workers. the rapporteur of the document we have just voted on sought to fill these gaps by introducing amendments which won the support of the s&d, epp, alde and gue political groups. in view of the relevance of the legislation under consideration and the clear improvement which the amendments introduced by the tran committee promote, i have decided to vote in favour of the report under discussion.
‒ the main objectives of the proposal are to modernise port services and operations and to create structural conditions to attract investment in ports. by means of this regulation, the commission aims to counter weak competitive pressure and possible market abuse in order to increase the efficiency of port services. however, the scope of the regulation should only cover port services offered directly to users. moreover, the social provisions governing the labour regime in ports have been virtually excluded from this regulation, but member states must ensure the rights of workers in the event of a transfer of undertakings or establishments.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns the legislative process on ports in the trans-european transport network. the regulation should therefore establish an organisational framework for port services, a set of rules on financial and cost transparency to be applied by management bodies (public or private) or providers of port services. the commission considers that the measure is selective because it does not involve state aid. the amendments tabled by the european parliament in its committee on transport to the commission's initial proposal improve the original text considerably, with direct implications for portugal: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on the free movement of workers are applied in the member states. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it is interesting, for example, to note the concern expressed for the "users" of ports. paradigmatic and funny. at the same time as public transport users become customers, port customers become users. the vote will be taken at the next voting time. we voted in favour of the amendments to the european commission proposal, which make it less bad, and we voted against the original proposal and the amended final document.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a regulatory framework for market access to port services and financial transparency for ports. it is of the utmost importance that the performance of all ports is improved so that they can cope with evolving logistics and transport needs. modernisation of port services and operations is also important to attract investment to ports.
in writing. ‒ i believe we must have a strategy that makes our ports more competitive and efficient not only at european level but also at global level. this regulation allows union ports to maintain their port management models. it is not a total opening up of ports, because this regulation allows access to the market for port services to be limited, for reasons of space limitation, by the need to apply public service obligations. there is a respect for the diversity of them. an example of this is the commitment to exclude ports in the outermost regions, such as madeira, from the scope of this regulation. since these regions are 100% dependent on maritime transport, this single european model for access to the market for port services has a special derogation for them. i hope that this commitment to the outermost regions, reached in the committee on transport, will be maintained in the negotiations with the council and in the final approval.
‒ the report deals with the legislative process for ports in the trans-european transport network. a regulation should establish an organisational framework for port services, a set of rules on financial and cost transparency to be applied by management bodies (public or private) or providers of port services. it excludes market operations, passenger handling and piloting services. the proposals put forward by the european parliament to the initial proposal of the european commission improve the original text very significantly, with direct implications for portugal: they exclude piloting, introduce relevant labour issues and reduce the degree of liberalisation imposed. they do not, however, prevent the final result from being negative, since it is entirely in line with the logic of liberalization. it is interesting, for example, to note the concern expressed for the "users" of ports. at the same time as public transport users become customers, port customers become users. a paradigm that can only be a black humor punchline. we therefore voted in favour of the amendments to the european commission proposal which make it less bad, but we voted against the original proposal and the amended final document.
‒ this report, which i voted for, seeks to contribute to a more efficient, interconnected and sustainable operation of the ten-t by creating a framework that improves the performance of all ports and helps them to cope with changing logistics and transport needs. it should be noted, however, that the scope of the regulation should only include port services offered directly to users. the report recognises that various systems of organisation of port services are currently in place and aims to amend provisions on minimum requirements, limitation of the number of service providers, public service obligations and social safeguards. the amendments emphasise the need for the port administration to be autonomous in order to act in accordance with its economic strategy, while respecting certain fundamental principles. in general, the aim is to create legal certainty for ports and to have a positive impact on the proper functioning of the ten-t network.
‒ the european parliament has approved a proposal for a reform of the union's port services focusing on transparency, ensuring workers' rights and safety and environmental commitments. the proposal also aims to modernise port services and operations and to create structural conditions to attract new investment to ports. the commission aims to counter weak competitive pressure and possible market abuse in order to increase the efficiency of port services. an important condition for competition between ports on a level playing field is the existence of a clear framework on state aid rules. this regulation shall apply to all maritime ports identified in the guidelines for the ten-t (trans-european transport network), with some voluntary exceptions, in particular for ports located in the outermost regions.
‒ about 90% of world trade is carried by sea. in europe alone, its 1200 ports employ three million people. these facts reflect the importance of this issue in the european context and beyond. it is important to liberalise ports so that they operate in a commercially efficient, financially transparent way and that unfair competition is eliminated, but it is essential to ensure that the social rights of their workers are not affected. i believe that the report presented, with the amendments suggested in parliament, adequately responds to the challenge put forward by the european commission. because i consider it crucial that the ports of the outermost regions of the european union be managed in accordance with their specificities, i also voted in favour of amendments nos 4 and 50. we cannot treat what is different in the same way, and as safeguarded in the treaties and in this context, the ops are different.

‒ i voted in favour of the feckenstein report because i believe that it will increase the efficiency and competitiveness of the maritime ports of the transeuropean transport network, without undermining the social and labour rules in force in the member states. i would stress that the report guarantees the right to strike, since collective labour actions taken in accordance with the national legislation of the respective member state and/or the applicable agreements between the social partners are not considered as interruptions of port services for which emergency measures can be taken. the report also provides for financial transparency provisions to ensure fair competition and to avoid price abuse, in particular where port services are not subject to effective competition. finally, i would stress that the report also takes account of the specific situation of ports in the outermost regions.
‒ the proposal for a regulation establishes a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised indices of consumer prices and house prices at union, national and subnational level. hicps provide a measure of inflation which, together with other sources, provide valuable inputs to deflate economic indicators such as wages, incomes, interest rates and therefore serve as a basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. i support the gualtieri report because i think it is crucial that these statistics are objective, unbiased and comparable in all member states and for all product categories, thus allowing a review of the current regulatory framework and maximum comparability for the main users of these indices.
‒ the commission proposal for a regulation establishes a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices at union, national and sub-national level. hicps provide a measure of inflation which, together with other sources, provide valuable inputs to deflate economic indicators such as wages, incomes, interest rates and therefore serve as a basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is therefore crucial that these statistics are objective, impartial and comparable in all member states and for all product categories. i am in favour of the proposal, in particular, because it includes information on the impact of tax changes on inflation.
‒ the commission proposal for a regulation establishes a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of data on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps). the hicp provides a measure of inflation and forms the basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is important that these statistics are objective and comparable between member states, covering all product areas, without forgetting the diversity of consumption structures in the different member states. the current hicp regulation dates back to 1995 and therefore needs to be revised. the current proposal also takes into account the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty, which gives the commission (in this case eurostat) the power to adopt implementing acts or legislative measures that may amend non-essential parts of a regulation delegated acts. in the commission proposal many activities are being defined through delegated acts, as is the definition of the appropriate methodology to produce harmonised indices between countries, or to update the weights of the sub-indices of the hicp. our opposition to this proposal in committee, which we maintain, is based on the possibility that the inclusion in future indexes of illicit goods and activities such as narcotics, gambling, prostitution and others may not be excluded. we consider that unacceptable.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on harmonised indices of consumer prices and repealing regulation (ec) no 2494/95. it is essential to establish a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised indices of consumer prices and house prices at union, national and sub-national level. the statistics shall be objective, impartial and comparable in all member states and for all product categories. the current hicp regulation dates back to 1995, so it is very important that the hicp regulation be updated.
‒ the protection of the european union's financial interests and the efficiency of public spending must be fundamental elements of eu policy, so that citizens' confidence in the correct, efficient and effective use of their money is increasingly strengthened. the multiplicity of legal systems in each member state makes the fight against fraud difficult and the eu should make efforts to intensify the fight against fraud in order to make it effective and with tangible and satisfactory results. i agree with the rapporteur that the commission should address the problem of divergent approaches by member states to detecting irregularities and heterogeneous interpretations in the application of the eu legal framework. i think it is essential that we develop a mechanism for the exchange of information between the competent authorities, so as to allow cross-checks of accounting records between member states, with the aim of preventing transnational fraud. the rapporteur shares the rapporteur's concern about the increase in smuggling, trafficking and other forms of illicit and illegal trade, which have an impact on the collection of customs duties by the member states and, consequently, on the eu budget.
‒ the commission proposal for a regulation establishes a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of data on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps). the hicp provides a measure of inflation and forms the basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is important that these statistics are objective and comparable between member states, covering all product areas, without forgetting the diversity of consumption structures in the different member states. the proposal to revise the current hicp regulation, which dates back to 1995, takes into account the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty, which gives the commission (in this case eurostat) the power to adopt implementing acts or legislative measures that may amend non-essential parts of a regulation delegated acts. in the commission proposal, many activities are being defined through delegated acts, as well as the definition of the appropriate methodology to produce harmonised indices between countries, or to update the weights of the sub-indices of the hicp. we have expressed our opposition to the proposal in committee and in plenary, as it does not exclude the inclusion in future indexes of illicit goods and activities such as narcotics, gambling, prostitution, among others. we consider this unacceptable.
‒ this report establishes a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hpis) at union, national and sub-national level. the report intends to include in the analysis of inflation information on the impact of physical changes on inflation. hicp-ts are an important tool for analysing the causes of inflation and for forecasting the impact of future fiscal changes on inflation, hence this draft report proposes that hicps and hicp-ts be broken down into categories according to the european classification of individual consumption by purpose. the report also calls for euro area member states to provide monthly rapid estimates and for the discrimination of rapid estimates of hicp, opi and hicp to be adopted by means of implementing acts. finally, it was decided that the commission should present to the european parliament and the council every five years a report assessing the main results of pilot studies. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour of this report.
‒ this proposal for a commission regulation updates the existing statistical methodology and establishes a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hpis) at union, national and sub-national level. hicp-ts are an important tool for analysing the causes of inflation and for forecasting the impact of future fiscal changes on inflation and correcting macroeconomic imbalances.

in writing. ‒ the union's financial interests are not only linked to the allocation of funds, but also to the collection of taxes, such as vat. the control is therefore essentially carried out at national level. the real knowledge of this reality is also dependent on the national authorities and therefore, as the report rightly points out, the transmission of information must be exemplary. something that hasn't happened yet, even though it's possible to have a good photograph already. the data available remain worrying at almost all levels, with the most notable being the failure of member states to recover funds after their return has been ordered. in this context, the report also recommends that the institutional and legal framework be strengthened. the importance of completing the legislative process of the so-called financial interests protection directive is underlined. i therefore support this report.
‒ member states and the commission share responsibility for implementing 80% of the union budget and are the main responsible for collecting own resources, in particular in the form of vat and customs duties. efficiency of public spending and the protection of the eu's financial interests must be key elements of eu policy in order to increase citizens' confidence in ensuring that their money is used correctly, efficiently and effectively. according to this report, the reported irregularities involve a total amount of around eur 3,24 billion with an overall financial impact of 36% higher than in 2013, while the number of such irregularities increased by 48%. of the 16 473 irregularities reported to the commission in 2014, 1 649 were fraudulent, involving an amount of eur 538,2 billion. i agree that the commission should take full responsibility for recovering unduly paid funds from the eu budget and for collecting own resources more effectively.
in writing. the committee on budgetary control draws up an annual own-initiative report on the protection of the 'financial interests of the union', which also includes information on irregularities and fraud cases reported by the member states, which has been increasing in percentage and in amount. the report regrets that member states use 'different definitions for similar types of crime and that not all [collect] identical and detailed statistical data according to common criteria, which makes it difficult to collect reliable and comparable statistics at eu level'. it called for the criteria for assessing irregularities and fraud to be harmonised in the member states and for the member states to impose sanctions on those who fail to comply. the commission is also asked to present guidelines to help harmonise fraud assessment. it called on the commission to play a more active role in monitoring the control and supervision systems in the member states and to recover funds unduly paid to the eu budget. the report regrets that the criminal law systems are only partially harmonised, and calls for a regulation to establish the european public prosecutor's office. while accepting and advocating the need to improve the fight against fraud, we do not follow some of the considerations and proposals made in the report.

‒ taking advantage of international women's day, the european parliament adopted a set of reports, which it integrates, highlighting the much that still remains to be done in defence of women and, more than that, for gender equality. discrimination between men and women is unacceptable. but it's not enough to just promote inequality outside the door. parliament, in the exercise of its legislative powers, but also in its functioning, must also take care of gender equality. however, without distorting the independence of its elected representatives, nor the will of the electors they represent, nor an administration that claims to be meritocratic. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. i still support this report but i reiterate the importance of continuing to promote a change of mindsets through equality of opportunity, not of outcome.
‒ gender mainstreaming implies the integration of a gender perspective in the preparation, design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, regulatory measures and expenditure programmes with a view to promoting equality between women and men and combating discrimination. it has a twofold dimension: it requires both the integration of the gender perspective into the content of the different policies and the approach to the issue of the representation of women and men in these policy areas. the report proposes a set of measures to strengthen and make more effective and efficient the current gender mainstreaming structure, including the creation of a strong interinstitutional network, the appointment of a permanent rapporteur on gender mainstreaming and the strengthening of the influence of the committee on women's rights and gender equality on gender-related aspects of the budget.
‒ this report analyses the level of gender mainstreaming in parliamentary committees and other european parliament activities. it advocates the integration of the gender perspective into all aspects of eu policy and points to a number of measures to achieve this. it also argues that such integration must include the rights, perspectives and well-being of lgbtiq people. it recalls that the organisational structure of parliament has different bodies responsible for the development and effective integration of gender, both at policy and professional level. notes that among parliament's staff, women remain in the majority in the group of assistant posts and that, unfortunately, the gender balance objectives at senior, intermediate and senior level, adopted in 2006, were not achieved by the end of the term (2009), or even this year. the report calls for interinstitutional cooperation to promote gender mainstreaming, stressing the need for continuous dialogue with national parliaments to learn about good practice, new techniques and information gathering. we agree with the general concern expressed in the report and with some of the measures advocated, even if we do not follow all of them.
‒ equality between men and women is a fundamental right recognised by the european union, as well as a common value and a necessary condition for the full implementation of the eu's objectives for growth, employment and social cohesion. the european commission has been committed since 1996 to adopting a policy to promote gender equality by involving the gender perspective in the implementation of legislative measures and policies. the resolution aims to continue this process by promoting a greater gender mainstreaming in all measures taken by the european institutions, whether in the drafting of legislative texts, budgetary policies or in promoting the representativeness of women in middle and senior posts within the administration. i voted yes.

‒ i voted in favour of this report which reaffirms the integration of the gender perspective, adopted at international level, as a strategy leading to the achievement of equality between men and women. in practical terms, gender mainstreaming implies the integration of gender into the preparation, design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, regulatory measures and expenditure programmes with a view to promoting equality between women and men and combating discrimination. this report shows that, however, structural inequalities between men and women are still entrenched in society. even where legislation treats women and men equally, women still do not have the same access to or control over resources and assets. the current situation therefore demonstrates that gender sensitive policy content is essential for a good equality strategy.

‒ regarding the issue of refugees and asylum seekers in the eu from the point of view of women, this report contributes to the advancement of this discussion, which is of such importance at this time, and shows particular care when it highlights the problems that a certain 'gender blindness' can mean for women who, fleeing societies that discriminate against them in a sometimes so cruel and inhuman way, deserve special precautions from those who host them so that they are not victims of other forms of discrimination. i will vote in favour of it because it not only draws attention to the specific problems that lead women to seek asylum, in the case of those who flee to avoid being victims of genital mutilation, but also contains recommendations for them to be provided by the host countries with a set of inclusive conditions and to show understanding of the diversity of problems and needs that afflict people who arrive in the eu in this situation. i would like to end by stressing my agreement with the rapporteur when she says that the present humanitarian crisis is exacerbating inequalities in gender relations and that we must do even more to harmonise good practice in the treatment of women asylum seekers and refugees.
‒ on international women's day, the european parliament adopted a set of reports, including this one, highlighting what remains to be done for gender equality. this in particular was intended to highlight a particular reality in this context and for which much work still needs to be done in europe: women asylum seekers and refugees. the report paints a striking portrait of the horrors these women are subjected to and lists a set of recommendations to the member states, which still remain primarily responsible for reception, application analysis and integration. the need to inform these women that their request may be independent of the husband - often the aggressor - is exemplary. however, the report also goes beyond what should be its main objective, including areas where there is no community competence, such as abortion. i can only abstain.
‒ in 2014, half of the world's refugee population were women and girls. there is a historical tendency for international conventions and national asylum policies to ignore the specific situation of women asylum seekers and the gender dimension of refugee situations. given their nature, it is difficult to obtain accurate statistics on the demographic diversity of refugees trying to reach europe. the european union's asylum policy must take account of women's experiences at all stages. i therefore agree that this time of uncertainty and instability is also an opportunity to harmonise good practice in the treatment of women asylum seekers and refugees in europe.

‒ women and children account for about 35% of refugees. this group is in a highly vulnerable situation, fleeing persecution and violence in their home country, and subjecting themselves to dangerous routes to europe in search of safety. unfortunately, when they arrive here, their vulnerability is not given particular attention. this report draws attention to the need for asylum policies and procedures to be sensitive to gender issues, gender-based violence such as rape, forced genital mutilation, forced marriages, domestic violence, among others, which must be valid arguments in asylum applications. however, reception centres for refugees should be prepared to receive them, providing appropriate medical care, sanitary facilities and gender-segregated dormitories where necessary, legal and psychological counselling, as well as promoting measures to facilitate their integration into the host country. i voted yes.

in writing. this report focuses on the measures to be taken in response to the so-called refugee crisis, with particular reference to women and children seeking asylum. the number of women and children arriving in europe has been increasing, accounting for about 55% of the total number of refugees. the report advocates safe and legal pathways to the eu and seeks to frame a broad set of situations that constitute valid grounds for seeking asylum. it is positive, but it does not depart from the logic of creating restrictions on those who, fleeing hunger, poverty and war, seek refuge on european soil, aiming at the distinction between refugees and migrants. the report calls for measures to meet the specific needs of women and children during the asylum application process, around the registration process, psychological support, access to health care, including sexual and reproductive health care, non-detention of children, the creation of adequate facilities for maternal care, labour market integration measures and access to language courses and free, quality public education. despite the absence of any critical position on the causes and the responsibilities of the eu in the origin of this exodus, we voted in favour of the report.
‒ it is difficult to obtain accurate statistics on the demographic diversity of refugees trying to reach europe. however, current studies suggest that more men are coming to the eu seeking international protection than women and children. this is mainly due to the lack of protection women face during the journey. women are often left behind to care for children and elderly relatives and many are not independent enough to leave their home country. those who manage to escape are vulnerable at all stages of the journey - in the countries of origin, transit and destination - and one of the concerns of the report is that eu asylum policy should take into account women's experiences at all these stages. the acts of violence they are victims of are often committed by non-state actors, including family members. persecution occurs when the state cannot or will not grant protection to women. the report therefore states that a new comprehensive package of eu gender guidelines should be adopted in the wider context of reforms to migration and asylum policy, which is why i voted in favour.
‒ in 2014, half of the world's refugee population were women and girls. historically, there has been a tendency for international conventions and national asylum policies to ignore the specific situation of women asylum seekers and the gender dimension in refugee situations. asylum systems have largely been examined on the basis of male experience. although the establishment of the common european asylum system (ceas) has been achieved, laws, policies and practices in the member states continue to vary significantly and there are significant gaps in the protection afforded to women seeking asylum in the eu. this report suggests a series of measures to ensure that the specific needs of women and girls seeking asylum are taken into account by member states.
the report calls for measures to meet the needs of women during the asylum application process, such as individual registration of women, the granting of documents guaranteeing individual safety, independently of their spouse and other family members, specialist trauma counselling and psychosocial assistance, counselling provided by professionals with expertise in all aspects of the different forms of violence against women, etc. the committee also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the rights of children are respected and that the right to education is guaranteed. however, the report makes no critical reference to the real causes of these refugee flows and does not condemn the eu for its involvement in the wars from which refugees flee. in this sense, it does not point to the fundamental solutions that are needed to resolve the fundamental question and that have to do with a policy of peace and cooperation which the eu is not able to put into practice.

‒ simplifying and clarifying european union law is a central objective of the eu. making it more accessible and easier for the ordinary citizen to understand will open up new opportunities for them and enable them to benefit from the specific rights conferred on them. the scattered nature of numerous provisions, which have been amended on several occasions, often substantially (which means that both the original act and the acts amending it must be read), means that, for reasons of legal clarity and transparency, the rules must be codified. i support the ferrara report which codifies council regulation 953/2003 to prevent the diversion of certain medicines essential for the eu and which does not cause substantial changes to the existing texts, so that the new regulation replaces the various acts incorporated in it.
‒ in the light of the interinstitutional agreement of 20 december 1994 on an accelerated working method for the official codification of legislative texts, the consultative group met to examine the proposal referred to above, submitted by the commission. the analysis carried out has thus allowed the consensus to conclude that the proposal in question is in fact a mere codification of the existing texts without any substantive changes.
‒ the report supports a codification of regulation 953/2003/eec of 26 may 2003. the commission simply codifies the existing texts without making any substantive changes to the text as a whole, essentially changing the nomenclature and the link with other documents. this is a highly technical report. as regards substance, the regulation deals with the diversion of essential medicines to the european union and the implementation of the necessary controls. essential medicines are those which are needed for certain serious diseases, such as aids and tuberculosis, and which cannot be procured by countries with the most severe economic difficulties. for this reason, differentiated prices for these medicines are established for the least developed countries. the regulation aims to put in place controls, fines and penalties to prevent countries or the pharmaceutical industry from taking advantage of this price differentiation by reselling them and making a profit on the exchange. among other measures, it allows seized medicines to be used for humanitarian aid to countries in need. it also provides for penalties to be imposed on the importer or any other person responsible for the attempted illegal import. we voted in favour.

‒ given the urgent need for many of the poorest developing countries to have access to essential medicines for the treatment of communicable diseases at affordable prices, these countries are over-dependent on imported medicines. it is crucial to introduce price differentiation between developed countries' markets and the markets of poorer developing countries in order to ensure that these countries have access to essential medicines at very low prices. there are now legislative and regulatory instruments in most developed countries to prevent the importation of pharmaceutical products in certain circumstances. however, there is a risk that these mechanisms will be insufficient in the face of the possible economic interest in diverting these products to higher priced markets. it is essential to establish a mechanism for the identification of the products, countries and diseases covered by this regulation, which aims to prevent the importation into the union of products with differentiated prices. i agree with the rapporteur's position on the fact that manufacturers are using a different presentation of products to make them easily identifiable, and i think it is essential to review the lists of diseases and countries of destination covered by the regulation.

‒ the agreement, on which the european parliament was consulted, updates another concluded between the eu and andorra in 2004, which ensured that the principality would apply measures equivalent to those provided for in the eu directive on taxation of savings income. the aim is to prevent situations where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital corresponding to income or assets for which no tax has been paid. the new agreement will enable the tax administrations of the member states and andorra to correctly identify the taxpayers concerned, to apply and enforce their tax laws in cross-border situations, to assess the likelihood of tax evasion and to dispense with unnecessary additional enquiries.
‒ this agreement follows similar agreements signed earlier, which we also voted in favour of. the signed agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account and interest information, which aims, among other things, to improve international tax cooperation, represents an important step in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. under the new agreement, andorra and the eu will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of each other's residents. the aim is to address situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide the sources of his non-taxed financial income. the agreement aims to ensure that andorra applies measures that are equivalent to the legal framework of the european union and the oecd. we recognise the positive (albeit limited) aspects that can result from this.

‒ the european union and the principality of andorra signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts on 12 february 2016 with a view to improving tax cooperation and compliance with international tax obligations. the agreement marks a major step forward in efforts to combat tax fraud and evasion and updates the 2004 agreement, which ensured that the principality of andorra applies measures equivalent to those provided for in the eu savings directive. the proposed amendment to the agreement provides that eu member states and andorra will, as of 2018, automatically exchange information collected as of 1 january 2017 on financial accounts held in their territories by residents of the other party. the purpose of this exchange is to prevent situations where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital corresponding to income or assets for which taxes have not been paid. i therefore vote in favour of this report.

‒ on 12 february 2016, the european union and the principality of andorra signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, aimed at improving tax cooperation and compliance with international tax obligations an important step forward in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. this report, which i approve, aims to ensure that andorra applies enhanced measures equivalent to the eu legal framework updated in december 2014. the commission notes that the provisions of the 2014 oecd global standard do not allow the member states to impose a tax on the income of residents of andorra. the other provisions of the agreement are intended to ensure that the exchange of information covers not only income, namely interest and dividends, but also account balances and the proceeds of the sale of financial assets. under this new agreement, member states' and andorra's tax administrations will now be able to identify correctly and unequivocally the taxpayers concerned; apply and enforce their tax laws in cross-border situations; assess the likelihood of tax evasion occurring and dispense with unnecessary additional enquiries.
‒ this is an agreement aimed at the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts to combat tax fraud and evasion. it is a document that is in line with the need for greater transparency in eu tax matters in its relations with third countries.
‒ the agreement signed this year on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, aimed at improving international tax cooperation, represents an important step in the ongoing efforts to fight tax fraud and tax evasion. the new agreement will automatically exchange information on financial accounts held in their territory by residents of each country, starting in 2018, for information collected as of 1 january 2017. the aim is to address situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide income-generating capital or assets for which taxes have not been paid. the agreement aims to ensure that andorra applies the recently strengthened measures in the eu legal framework in december 2014 (amending the administrative cooperation directive, 'dac 2') and complies with the 2014 oecd standards for the automatic exchange of information.

in writing. ‒ the term of office of the current executive director of eiopa ends on 31 march 2016. on 28 january 2016, the board of supervisors of eiopa, following a call for tenders, proposed the appointment of fausto parente as executive director for a term of five years. the committee on economic and monetary affairs heard mr fausto parente and parliament approved his appointment.
‒ eiopa is part of the european system of financial supervision (esfs) and aims to support the stability of the financial system and the transparency of financial markets and products. it also seeks to protect policyholders and members and beneficiaries of pension schemes. by creating the illusion that the problems that caused the financial crisis of 2007/2008 are solved, the esfs has not changed the underlying issue of financial speculation, as it has not put a cap on derivatives markets and tax havens and has not instituted the separation of commercial and investment banking. history will show that the creation of these european authorities was not worth it. for these reasons we opposed the institution of this system and its authorities. we therefore abstain on the appointment of the executive director of the authority in question.
‒ the free movement of european citizens, which has its first pillar in schengen, is also translated into an area of freedom, security and justice. among these three dimensions, the case for justice means judicial cooperation and, as this report emphasizes, guaranteeing a common denominator of guarantees and rights for all european citizens. it is for this reason that the procedural rights roadmap has been developed, but also why this directive has now been adopted for the procedural guarantees for minors - normally subject to a special regime in criminal proceedings. the directive applies to all criminal proceedings and ensures the harmonisation of numerous concepts and safeguards which were not consensual in the traditions of the various member states. the definition of a child as anyone under the age of 18, access to a lawyer and legal aid, as well as special safeguards in medical examinations and interrogations, are of particular importance. i cannot therefore fail to welcome and to note that in certain areas it is still quite clear that there can be no security without justice.
‒ the european commission estimates that more than one million minors are subject to criminal proceedings in the eu every year, representing 12% of all persons involved in criminal proceedings in the eu. investigations at european level show that the rights of minors at the various stages of the procedure are not adequately guaranteed within the union and that there are many cases of member states being condemned by the european court of human rights. at present, there are only six member states with specialised juvenile prosecution bodies and nine countries without specialised courts. in some countries, the assistance of a lawyer is not guaranteed; in others, it is possible only in court and not in police stations; in other cases, the decision is taken by the competent court. it is in this context that the proposal for a directive is to be introduced, which aims to define a narrow but organic range of rights for minors who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, with a structured body of 'minimum standards' which are interlinked and adapted to the specific needs of minors throughout the proceedings.
‒ the proposal for a directive on procedural guarantees for minors suspected or accused in criminal proceedings is part of the roadmap for strengthening the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, adopted by the council on 30 november 2009. it is in line with other initiatives, including the guidelines of the committee of ministers of the council of europe on child-friendly justice. it is estimated that more than one million children are subject to criminal proceedings in the eu each year, representing 12% of all persons involved in criminal proceedings. it is in this context that the proposal for a directive is to be introduced, which aims to define a set of rights for minors who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, based on a structured body of 'minimum' rules, which are interlinked and adapted to the specific needs of minors throughout the proceedings. the following are particularly important: the inalienable right to be assisted by a lawyer; the right to individual assessment; the possibility for the child to participate in the proceedings; the inclusion of specific mandatory training for judges, police and prison authorities, lawyers and other individuals working with children; provisions on deprivation of liberty. we voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive on procedural guarantees for minors suspected or accused in criminal proceedings. having regard to article 82 (2) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, this concerns the establishment of specific minimum standards with regard to the procedural guarantees for minors who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, taking into account the specific needs of minors throughout the proceedings, and promoting the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the aim of the directive is to ensure that minors have the capacity to understand and follow the procedure, exercising their right to a fair trial and preventing reoffending.
‒ it is estimated that more than one million minors are subject to criminal proceedings in the eu each year, representing 12% of those involved in criminal proceedings. in addition to these data, there are other alarming factors, such as the disparity between member states in the treatment of minors subject to criminal proceedings. at present, according to studies carried out at european level, the rights of minors at the various stages of criminal proceedings are not adequately guaranteed within the union and there are many cases of member states being condemned by the european court of human rights. i support, as do the conclusions of the stockholm programme, the need to ensure, through common minimum rules, the effective and sufficiently uniform enjoyment of the right to a fair trial at all stages of the proceedings by persons under the age of 18. i would stress as essential, and safeguarded in the proposal, the right to be assisted by a lawyer, the right to individual assessment, the participation of the minor in the proceedings, the inclusion of mandatory specific training for those working with minors and the provisions on deprivation of liberty, on the basis of which the application of preventive detention should be established only as a last resort.
‒ the stockholm programme emphasised the importance and need to ensure, through minimum rules, the effective enjoyment of the right to a fair trial during all stages of the criminal proceedings. this directive is part of a set of measures already adopted which aim to promote the rights of minors. it is estimated that more than one million children are subject to criminal proceedings in the eu each year, corresponding to 12% of all persons involved in criminal proceedings. the commission proposal for a directive aims to define a set of rights for minors who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings in a structured body of 'minimum' standards. among others, these include the inalienable right to free legal aid and to be assisted by a lawyer; the right to an individual assessment; the interrogation procedure; the possibility of the minor's participation in the proceedings; the inclusion of specific training which is mandatory for all those working with minors; provisions on deprivation of liberty and ensuring that minors are detained separately from adults. we voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ at present, there are only six member states (belgium, the czech republic, greece, italy, luxembourg and the slovak republic) with specialised juvenile prosecution bodies, and nine countries do not even have specialised courts. only 12 member states provide for specific mandatory training for judges and lawyers working with minors and in some countries the assistance of a lawyer is not guaranteed; in others, it is possible only in court and not in police stations; in other cases, the decision is taken by the competent court. this is why today a significant number of minors in the eu do not have a basic right to be assisted by a lawyer. it is in this context that the commission's proposal for a directive is to be seen, which aims to define a narrow but organic range of rights for minors who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings (or subject to european arrest warrant proceedings), with a structured body of 'minimum standards', which are interlinked and adapted to the specific needs of minors throughout the proceedings. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour of this report.

‒ the general budget of the european union is a key instrument for dealing with the recent crises and responding to needs that were not foreseen during the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework. i share the view that the eu budget, as an investment budget, brings added value by stimulating growth, competitiveness and job creation and should not be seen as a burden by member states who consider their contribution as an adjustment variable subject to macroeconomic conditions. as in the past, i reiterate the need to reform the eu's own resources system, since it is impossible to demand more europe and more union intervention when the budgetary cake represents less than 1% of european gdp. the 2017 budget will be affected by the challenges of migration and internal and external security and therefore, in its preparation, particular attention should be paid to these emerging phenomena, while not neglecting concerns about unemployment, socio-economic disparities, support for smes and the revitalisation of the internal market.
‒ this report contains the european parliament's position on the guidelines to guide the preparation of the eu budget for 2017. unsurprisingly, it is a report which does not advocate profound differences from what the budgetary priorities have been in previous years. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. as usual, we took an active part in the debate on budgetary priorities, proposing a number of amendments to the report. examples include: advocating substantial budgetary strengthening, especially of the components dedicated to economic and social cohesion, with the creation of an investment plan that mobilises at least 2% of eu gdp annually over the next ten years; advocating cuts in military spending and associated with eu external interventionism; advocating measures to combat poverty, inequalities and social exclusion as well as unemployment; creating specific support programmes for countries, such as portugal, which are affected by the troika and face greater difficulties; creating support programmes for countries opting for a negotiated exit from the euro which, among other aspects, provide for adequate compensation for the damage caused by joining and remaining in the single currency. these are changes that point to an alternative path to the current disaster trajectory. unfortunately, they were rejected.

‒ the institutional architecture of the european union is complex, reflecting to a large extent the sui generis nature of this entity. this is reflected in the relationship between the three institutions of the legislative triangle: the commission, parliament and council. this interinstitutional agreement is part of the 'better regulation' package launched by the commission in 2015 and focuses in particular on the legislative procedure, the relationship between the institutions and legislation. at the legislative level, the agreement aims to make the whole process more transparent and flexible, and to ensure loyal cooperation between the institutions, in particular by guaranteeing parliament's role as co-legislator. it also aims to fulfil an idea championed by the epp and, in particular, by the candidate - now president - juncker: that the union should be big in big things and small in small things. in other words, the level of power should always be as close as possible to the decision-making electorate and, on the other hand, the regulatory impetus should not be an unnecessary burden for citizens and businesses. i therefore support this agreement.
‒ parliament has repeatedly called for the 2003 interinstitutional agreement to be renegotiated to take account of the new legislative framework created by the lisbon treaty, consolidate current good practice and update that agreement in line with the 'better lawmaking' agenda. the conference of presidents approved by a majority the provisional agreement reached by the negotiators on the text of a new interinstitutional agreement on better lawmaking (the 'new iia'). i therefore welcome the agreement reached between the institutions, which is a good basis for establishing and developing a new, more open and transparent relationship between the institutions with the aim of better lawmaking in the interests of the citizens of the union.
‒ the report endorses the interinstitutional agreement between the european parliament, the european commission and the council on better law-making. it's a negative agreement for several orders of reason. we'll highlight three. first, the stated objective conceals the interests it is intended to serve. the so-called 'competitiveness' of firms is now the first and overriding criterion in determining the appropriateness and content of eu legislation. it is not the interests of smes that are being defended. but those of big business, of big economic groups, of big powers. even more than before. social and environmental criteria, if anything (a little) could still contribute to the improvement of the living conditions of workers and peoples, are now relegated to an even more secondary plane. secondly, this agreement represents new and more serious limitations on the democratic nature of the legislative and decision-making process. the door is open to greater concentration of power in the european commission and to limiting the capacity of co-legislators, especially members, to intervene. thirdly, the declarations of good faith on 'transparency' result in a handful of nothing. in the shadows, they command the powers that be. it is for them that we want to "legislate better".
‒ better regulation means legislative simplification, with the aim of promoting legal certainty and security. i voted in favour of the conclusion of the interinstitutional agreement, which is essential for the functioning of a sometimes too complex legislative machinery.

the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. first, the stated objective conceals the interests it purports to serve. the so-called 'competitiveness' of firms is now the first and overriding criterion in determining the appropriateness and content of eu legislation. it is the interests of big capital, of the big economic groups and of the big powers, not the interests of smes, that are being defended. any social and environmental criteria which could have contributed even a little to the improvement of the living conditions of workers and peoples are now being secondary. the second reason concerns the new and more serious limitations on the democratic nature of the legislative and decision-making process which the agreement promotes. the concentration of power in the european commission is foreseen, restricting the capacity of co-legislators, in particular meps, to intervene. thirdly, the declarations of good faith on 'transparency' result in a handful of nothing. we voted against it.

mr president, it is a great pleasure to receive the prime minister here at the european parliament. prime minister, you are coming with a strong pro-european voice, building on the swedish experience. sweden does, of course, have several problems, but it remains one of the best examples to be followed in the european union as a whole. first of all, when it comes to democracy, as you have just mentioned, you have high standards of representative democracy in sweden. secondly, sweden remains one of the best examples of how we can push for sustainable development combining the economic, social and environmental dimensions while delivering a stronger recovery with good jobs. finally, sweden remains a good example of a high degree of engagement with international responsibilities. i know that you are very committed to working for a global new deal. of course, in spite of the problems, sweden remains a very important positive example as to how to integrate the refugees. well let me say that i recently went again to sweden to get some inspiration and i would like to tell the house what i saw. sweden is managing a very big flow of refugees. firstly, i saw refugees being received decently at the border; secondly, i saw them being distributed across the country in many municipalities, where they could find decent housing and access to basic social services. then i saw very well—organised programmes for retraining and integrating refugees into the labour market. so that was the reality which i saw in sweden. what i conclude from this is that these are very simple and nonetheless very humane things to do, and they can be done – as sweden is proving – and should be done throughout europe.

causing microcephaly. in the light of this, the world health organization has rightly declared a public health emergency of international concern and in the european union we have mobilised our structures of cooperation with the member states. the epidemic has arrived in member states’ overseas territories; in continental european union we so far only have cases in travellers returning from the affected areas. so that is why the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) has developed information for travellers and for eu residents in the affected areas, and that i know is one of the points for action mentioned in your resolution. we have also shaped advice to health authorities to help member states increase awareness amongst clinicians, something else that your resolution stresses. it is likely that more infections will occur in europe. we must be prepared for local transmission of zika as temperatures rise, building on our experience in controlling the spread of mosquitoes, which is being brought together by the ecdc. we are already gathering knowledge from countries with experience in mosquito control, as you rightly call for. we are ready to address zika by using tried and tested systems under our legislation on serious cross-border health threats, which gives us the mandate to coordinate the response to a threat together with member states. as regards surveillance of the epidemic, we are on track and we are working with member states to reinforce laboratory capabilities for early detection and diagnosis based on the ecdc risk assessments. it is the health security committee which is the structure we have in place for risk management to cross-border threats. this committee has so far met three times to review the zika situation and we are constantly exchanging information on zika through our early warning and response system. as regards another important point you raised, the disinfection of ships and airplanes, we have developed specific advice to member states on this, again based on ecdc risk assessments. we share your concern at the fact that there are no vaccines or medicines to protect people from the zika virus or to treat them, and that is why we are stepping up our efforts in this area. the european medicines agency has established a task force of experts to advise on scientific and regulatory matters related to the development of medicines against the virus. the agency will also contact companies planning to work on vaccines and offer advice. we are making available an additional eur 10 million of emergency research funding for zika-related research. these are only the first steps in our response. we will continue to support the eu member states and the affected regions in close cooperation with the world health organization and today’s debate and parliament’s motion for a resolution come, i think, at the right moment to focus attention on the urgency of the situation. this is particularly true as in the coming spring and summer mosquitos may pose a danger for the introduction of the virus in europe, so we need effective vector control measures. let me assure you that the commission is ready to address all aspects of the zika virus challenge and is ready to deploy all available instruments and means to this end.

‒ the european commission has presented the proposal for a regulation on veterinary medicinal products which incorporates a complete recast of the legislation on veterinary medicinal products, previously framed by directive 2001/82/ec and regulation (ec) no 726/2004, with the aim of regulating the authorisation, manufacture, placing on the market, distribution and use of veterinary medicinal products throughout their life cycle, as well as the applicable pharmacovigilance process. i support the grossetête report because i believe that a specific regulatory framework, adapted to the specificities of the veterinary sector, is needed, taking into account the problems that have arisen with the application of the existing legal framework, namely the lack of availability of veterinary medicines, the administrative burdens imposed by regulation, the functioning of the internal market and, of course, the increasingly worrying phenomenon of antibiotic resistance.
‒ the proposal aims to improve the availability of veterinary medicines, reduce administrative burdens, stimulate innovation in the sector and fight antibiotic resistance. antimicrobial veterinary medicinal products should under no circumstances be used to improve production levels or to compensate for non-compliance with good animal husbandry practice. the fight against antibiotic resistance must start on farms. the proposal aims in particular to prohibit the purely preventive use of antibiotics, to restrict mass treatment to very specific cases, to prohibit the veterinary use of antibiotics of critical importance to human medicine and to put an end to the sale of antimicrobial medicines via the internet.

madam president, the reform of the common fisheries policy has not helped to solve the serious problems facing small-scale coastal fishing, artisanal fishing and the regions most dependent on them, as was supposed to be the case. on the contrary, many problems have become worse. we want to stress the need for long-standing proposals, which have been confirmed by the development of reality. the development of a specific community programme to support small-scale fishing, the promotion of differentiated treatment with management schemes and models adapted to the specific characteristics and problems of this sector, support for fleet renewal and modernisation, the improvement of the sector's income, if necessary by intervening in its value chain in order to enhance the prices paid for production, the dedication and extension of exclusive access reserve areas in order to better protect fleets and local communities, giving them priority in access to resources. it is not enough to make loud proclamations in defence of small-scale fishing. these declarations must be translated into concrete commitments and concrete measures, far beyond what has been done.
madam president, commissioner, i also welcome the rapporteur. fisheries are a component of marine biodiversity and fisheries are the human activity with the greatest impact on this biodiversity. i therefore consider that an integrated legal and scientific approach is indispensable. i would therefore like to stress in this report the mention of vulnerable marine ecosystems and ecologically and biologically significant areas. the first reflects the recognition of environmental sensitivity by fao, closer to resource maintenance, and the second reflects the recognition of the convention on biological diversity, usually closer to concerns regarding biodiversity and ecosystem functioning. it seems to me that the integration of both approaches in this report could help to provide policy consistency in support of the implementation of a global network of marine protected areas in areas beyond national jurisdiction, in my view fundamental to the conservation of the oceans and their resources.
madam president, the conservation of marine biodiversity, particularly in international waters, unquestionably requires an effort of cooperation and concertation at international level. the united nations is the appropriate forum for establishing and deepening, as required and as evolving circumstances require, such cooperation and concertation with a view to the sound conservation and sustainable exploitation of marine resources, in accordance with criteria of justice and equity. the convention on the law of the sea is, among others, an appropriate instrument to pursue these aims. the measures to be implemented should be based on sound scientific knowledge and a thorough assessment of the impact of the various activities carried out in the marine environment. the european union has a role here which has not always been played with the consistency and the means that were justified. quite the opposite. the example of deep-sea fishing is illustrative. why is it that what is harmful in eu waters is acceptable in international waters?
madam president, commissioner, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs linnéa engström. the formation of a preliminary working document and the constant openness to suggestions from the various shadow rapporteurs seemed to me a particularly appropriate way of drawing up parliament's own-initiative reports. this is an important document, as i have already said, and i agree with what mr gabriel mato has said, but i think it is only a failure to recognise that marine biodiversity is under pressure, with fisheries being among the most immediate threats. i'm sorry this didn't make it into the article. on the positive side, there are many points to be made, and these are the ones which will lead me to vote in favour of this document for which i was the shadow rapporteur for the socialists and democrats. among these, i think it is particularly important to mention a single register for vessels operating in international waters. we must put an end to the constant changing of flags, a practice so widely used by rogue shipowners.
madam president, commissioner, the external dimension of the common fisheries policy is sick with many of the problems, shortcomings, limitations and contradictions of the cfp itself in its various internal dimensions. we have been very critical of this policy and its practical results. under fisheries agreements, so-called partnerships, but with very little real partnership, all or almost all of it is financial transfers, always small, to developing countries in exchange for the right to exploit their fisheries resources. in many cases this has been the case for decades. these countries are continually deprived of the added value they would obtain if they were to exploit their own resources, thus jeopardizing the possibility of creating wealth and employment, their development, sovereignty and independence. the failure of the european union's cooperation policy in this area must be acknowledged and profound changes must be made, involving the countries concerned and linking the external dimension of the cfp more effectively with development cooperation policy, which is intended to be more genuine and effective.
