‒ simplifying and clarifying european union law is a central objective of the eu to make it more accessible and easier for the ordinary citizen to understand, which will allow him/her new opportunities and the possibility to benefit from the specific rights attributed to him/her. the scattered nature of numerous provisions, which have been amended on several occasions, often substantially (which requires reading both the original act and the acts amending it), means that, for reasons of legal clarity and transparency, the rules must be codified. i support the walesa report which authorises the codification of regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 governing imports of products originating in certain acp countries, which has been amended nine times since 2007. the text thus becomes clearer and more readable without any substantive changes to its content.
‒ the report describes the codification and recasting of the market access regulation, which governs imports of products originating in certain acp countries. this temporary instrument provides duty-free and quota-free access to the eu market for products originating in non-ldc acp countries, currently including 27 countries. since the purpose of codification is to ensure the transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation, i voted in favour of the proposal.
the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a regulation on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. this temporary instrument provides for duty-free and quota-free access to the eu market for products originating in acp countries other than least developed countries (ldcs) in the period prior to the conclusion and application of the so-called 'economic partnership agreements' (epas), free trade agreements which follow the logic of the world trade organisation (wto). annex i to the market access regulation currently includes 27 countries. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the acp countries are able to continue their efforts in the immediate future, but they have a limited time horizon, since the proposal falls within the framework of the epas, which it accepts and defends. the epas mean the accentuation of existing inequalities, the serious effects of the deregulation of trade, the free movement of capital and investment, that is to say the deepening of the neoliberal, neo-colonial model which has been imposed, particularly in countries with weaker economies. since this is a codification (of an eminently technical nature), we abstain.

‒ international relations between member states and third countries in the field of aviation have traditionally been regulated by bilateral air services agreements whose designation clauses infringe union law by allowing third countries to reject, withdraw or suspend the licences or authorisations of an air carrier which has been designated by a member state but which is substantially owned by a member state or its nationals and not effectively controlled by them. i support the koch report which is to approve a new agreement which, among other things, is to replace the traditional designation clauses with an eu designation clause allowing all carriers to benefit from the right of establishment.
‒ the eu-macao agreement was signed on 23 november 2013. international relations between member states and third countries in the field of aviation have traditionally been regulated by bilateral air services agreements which have included clauses in breach of union law. it was considered that such clauses discriminate against eu carriers which are established in the territory of one member state but are owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. there are other issues, such as competition, in relation to which compliance with union law should be ensured by amending or supplementing existing provisions in bilateral air service agreements between member states and third countries. however, the commission has therefore negotiated this agreement, which replaces certain provisions of the current 15 bilateral air services agreements by improving the final document. i voted in favour.
‒ relations between member states and third countries in the field of aviation have been regulated by bilateral air services agreements. on the basis of decisions of the ecj, these agreements were found to be in breach of eu law as they provide for discriminatory situations against eu carriers which are established in the territory of one member state but are owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. this (non-amendable) agreement replaces the provisions of the current 15 bilateral air services agreements between the member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. the agreements are part of the ongoing merger monopoly in the eu aviation sector. they serve that purpose, as does all eu legislation for the sector. a sector dominated by five major groups: lufthansa, iberia-british airways and air france-klm, plus the two low-cost airlines ryanair and easyjet. the companies that are still out of this lot, especially if they are flag carriers like tap, and especially if they are still public, are to be dismantled, disappear in time, being absorbed their business, assets and routes by the giants of the sector. a path deeply damaging to national interests, which we reject and fight. we obviously voted against it.

in writing. ‒ the vat directive provides that from 1 january 2011 until 31 december 2015 the standard rate may not be less than 15%. transitional directive introducing a system of minimum rates justified by the fact that vat is still applied at the place of origin, rather than at the place of destination, to cross-border purchases and distance sales up to a certain value. in 2016, the commission will publish an action plan towards a definitive, simple, efficient and fraud-proof system for value added tax, adapted to the single market, which will set out the guidelines for future work and the main features of the definitive vat arrangements applicable to intra-eu trade, as well as the reforms envisaged to adapt the existing vat rules to a definitive system. i voted in favour.
in writing. the intention of setting a minimum threshold for the standard rate was to create a harmonised band up to a single vat rate. however, this option would undermine the fiscal sovereignty of the member states and their options for financing the community budget. directive 92/77/ec provided that from january 1993 until december 1996 the standard rate could not be lower than 15% in any member state. this provision has been extended five times and is now applicable until 31 december 2015. the european parliament now proposes that the extension be extended to the end of 2018 and not to 2017, as the european commission proposes, as it will allow for a more comprehensive debate on vat rates in the framework of the vat action plan. this is the only amendment tabled by the european parliament. the action plan was presented on 7 april and is intended to be the first step towards a single vat area in the eu. all member states now apply a standard rate of more than 15%. the application of a minimum standard rate of 15% gives member states a certain margin of manoeuvre, allowing them to reform vat to reduce the standard rate. we abstained.

in writing. ‒ the vat directive provided that, until 31 december 2015, the standard rate was not lower than 15%. the establishment of a minimum threshold was intended to create a band with a maximum threshold which would be harmonised up to a single vat rate for the whole community area, while respecting the fiscal sovereignty of the member states and their options for financing the community budget. the european parliament now proposes that the extension be extended to the end of 2018 and not to 2017 as the ec proposes, as it will allow, they say, for a more exhaustive debate on vat rates in the framework of the vat action plan. we cannot dissociate this whole framework from the underlying intention to bring european harmonization to fiscal matters as well.
in writing. - i have given my approval to this report, the action plan of which will set out the main features of the definitive vat regime applicable to intra-eu trade which the commission intends to propose, as well as the reforms envisaged to adapt the existing rules on vat rates to a definitive regime characterised by the principle of the country of destination. the minimum vat rates are justified by the fact that they still apply at the place of origin, rather than at the destination, to cross-border purchases and distance sales up to a certain value. therefore, the application of a minimum standard rate in all member states as in the present case constitutes a useful safeguard for the proper functioning of the internal market and avoids situations of unfair tax competition. in these circumstances, and pending decisions on the final form of the definitive regime, the report agreed with the commission's proposal to retain retroactively the principle of a minimum standard vat rate of 15% and to propose the extension of the measures in force for a period of three years (until 31 december 2018) - a timeframe that ensures the necessary legal certainty for stakeholders and allows for a more comprehensive debate on vat rates in the framework of the future action plan.
in writing. ‒ directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of value added tax ('vat directive') provides that from 1 january 2011 until 31 december 2015 the standard rate may not be lower than 15% in any member state. this provision on the minimum standard rate has been extended five times. the committee on economic and monetary affairs now proposes an extension until 31 december 2018 (one year longer than in the commission proposal).
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a legislative resolution on the amendment of directive 2006/112/ec as regards the duration of the obligation to respect a minimum standard rate for the common system of value added tax, which is set at 15% and will be in force for a period of three years (until 31/12/2018). the purpose of the legislation is tax harmonization, which is a useful safeguard for the proper functioning of the internal market and allows member states a certain margin of manoeuvre, in particular as regards the possibility of reforming vat in order to reduce the standard rate and widen the vat base. it will then be important to follow the commission's action plan on the definitive arrangements for intra-eu trade and the reforms towards a new vat rate system, which will apply the principle of taxation at the place of destination.
in writing. the vat directive provides that from 1 january 2011 until 31 december 2015 the standard rate may not be lower than 15%. the initial intention of establishing a minimum rate limit was to create a band with a maximum rate limit which would eventually harmonize to a single vat rate for the whole of the community. however, the establishment of this band for this purpose would undermine the fiscal sovereignty of the member states and their options for financing the community budget. it should also be noted that all member states now apply a standard rate of more than 15%, and the current application of a minimum standard rate of 15% also gives member states a certain margin of manoeuvre, allowing them to reform vat to reduce the standard rate, broadening the vat base and limiting the use of reduced rates. the european parliament now proposes that the extension be extended to the end of 2018 and not to 2017, as the ec proposes, as it will allow for a more comprehensive debate on vat rates in the framework of the vat action plan. this is the only amendment tabled by the ep.

‒ i support the nicolai report because i believe that there is a need to create a legally binding international instrument under the united nations convention on the law of the sea for the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas outside national jurisdiction through modern and sustainable concepts of marine ecosystem management, ocean governance principles and fisheries. this new agreement should include instruments for the accountability of all the actors involved, without which it will not be possible to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves. i believe that an exchange of good practice in this area should continue to exist under eu leadership.
‒ this report follows the recommendations made in 2015 at the united nations general assembly on international cooperation for the protection of ecosystems and the sustainable use of marine resources. it stressed the need to establish a binding instrument under the responsibility of the united nations convention on the law of the sea. the position of the working group which implemented the recommendations and of the united nations general assembly points to the negative impact that the rapid growth and expansion of maritime activities (notably industrial fishing, offshore drilling, transport, etc.) will have and have had on the marine environment. the need to deepen legislation at international level, in a context where 64% of the existing sea area is outside national jurisdictions, is thus considered fundamental. the report does, however, contain some evaluative references to eu policies, in particular the common fisheries policy, which we do not review. nor do we support a centralising approach, supporting the eu's positions and giving power to its institutions, in particular the european commission. this logic has favoured the large fishing industries but has negatively affected small-scale fishing, small-scale industries and fishing communities, with a negative impact on ecosystems.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on fisheries aspects in the framework of the international agreement on marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, the united nations convention on the law of the sea. it is very important to discuss a new international instrument to regulate our seas. a new instrument to include fishing activities. it is not enough to deal with pollution and the growing threats to marine biodiversity. the eu must continue to lead in this area.
‒ it is estimated that 64% of the sea, including the high seas and the deep seabed, are areas outside the national jurisdiction of states regulated by international law. the current legal framework, established more than 30 years ago and based on the principle of freedom of the high seas, needs to be improved in order to successfully promote the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas outside national jurisdiction. it is important to stress the leading role, and frankly positive, played by the european union and the commission, given the preponderance of the eu fishing industry and market and the fact that european fisheries policy is geared towards sustainability. i agree with the rapporteur's position, in particular in recognising the importance of creating a legally binding international instrument which includes fishing activities in that instrument. if we are to achieve an effective and well-coordinated instrument in the field of marine biology, it will have to take account of fishing, since it is one of the most important activities carried out in the waters.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because marine biodiversity is of particular importance in the outermost regions, such as the azores, which give europe an atlantic dimension. illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing threatens marine biodiversity and jeopardises the preservation of ecosystems. this justifies increased cooperation, coordination, transparency and accountability between all the actors involved. the conservation of marine biodiversity and its sustainable use are directly linked to sustainable development in the long term. it is urgent to tackle plastic waste at sea and to fund relevant research in the field of the 'blue economy'. the positive role of eco-labelling in the seafood sector is highlighted, as it allows consumers to contribute to the sustainability of resources and the preservation of biodiversity. it is desirable that the un works with states to implement effectively existing rules and, where necessary, develop additional rules that can indirectly help to protect biodiversity on the high seas and improve social, safety and control conditions, such as the creation of a centralised instrument for the registration of fishing vessels, while avoiding an increase in the bureaucratic burden for fishermen.
‒ blue growth must be a priority. human activities at sea have multiplied in recent decades. the potential for growth and job creation is enormous and must take account of the ecological limits of the sea. fisheries and aquaculture play an important role in the maritime economy and should be developed in a responsible manner, allowing for sustainable development and ecosystem balance.
‒ the un underlined the importance of protecting the world's waters following the 1992 united nations conference on environment and development in brazil - agenda 21. in 2012, in the document published after the un conference on sustainable development, the international community reaffirmed its determination to address environmental problems and the need to promote sustainable development. this shows that while the international community recognises the need for a global approach to managing pollution and the growing threats to marine biodiversity, there is a need to adapt plans and priorities locally to a rapidly and constantly developing world. as i agree with the rapporteur's emphasis on the inclusion of instruments for the accountability of all actors involved in the future agreement, these being important instruments for achieving real efficiency and progress, i voted in favour of this report. taking into account the needs of developing countries, capacity building and information sharing should be a priority in line with good practice and the eu should therefore continue to ensure a leading role in the development of this instrument as well as in its implementation process.

‒ the purpose of this regulation is to lay down zootechnical and genealogical rules for the conservation and reproduction of animals and rules governing the conservation and reproduction of native or endangered breeds. the report improves on the original european commission proposal in several respects (extended scope, clarification of the legal framework, provisions on animal health and welfare). the issues of cloning are not dealt with in this regulation. the aim is to bring together in a single legal framework several important aspects such as the structuring of the livestock breeding sector; to establish rules for the management of stud books, breeding registers, for the breeding of animals and for performance testing and genetic evaluation. it lays down rules for intra-eu trade and imports from third countries, as well as for official controls. one of the negative aspects of this proposal, apart from the assumption that the meat production sector must be more competitive to allow european species and breeds to be exported, is the aspects of animal cloning, which have been left out, even as regards the pedigree register, not being recorded whether the progenitor is a cloned animal or whether the germ products are derived from a cloned animal.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on zootechnical and genealogical conditions governing trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products. eu zootechnical legislation aims to promote free trade within the eu and facilitate the import of breeding animals and their genetic material, ensuring the maintenance of existing breeding programmes and the conservation of genetic resources in europe. however, it is not enough to want to encourage the export of the great european breeds; we must also take into account the local breeds, which are of enormous value to the different countries of the eu. these breeds are part of the genetic biodiversity of europe.
in writing. eu zootechnical legislation aims to promote free trade in breeding animals and their genetic material, taking into account the sustainability of breeding programmes and the conservation of genetic resources. the basic principles of the zootechnical legislation have proved to be appropriate and adapted to technical progress in the field of animal production and are therefore set out in this proposal. however, since the current legislation is organised by species, the almost identical provisions have been simplified and drafted in more precise and coherent language in the form of a regulation in order to avoid barriers to trade resulting from national transposition. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the directive on the protection of animals used for scientific purposes. the commission is therefore aware of the needs of the livestock sector and of the competent supervisory authorities. i support, as does the rapporteur, a harmonised approach to trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products, and to the official controls which need to be carried out on breeding programmes carried out by breeders' associations and animal production centres.
‒ the purpose of this regulation is to lay down zootechnical and genealogical rules for the conservation and reproduction of animals and rules governing the conservation and reproduction of native or endangered breeds. the regulation concentrates in a single legal framework several relevant matters: the structuring of the livestock breeding sector, rules for the management of breeding books or breeding registers for animal breeding and for performance testing and genetic evaluation. it also lays down rules for intra-eu trade and imports from third countries, and lays down rules for official controls and commission controls. as negative elements, the conditioning of competitiveness, as a prerequisite to facilitate the export of european species and breeds, the absence of references to animal cloning.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the vote in favour of this report because the production of bovine, porcine, ovine, caprine and equine animals occupies a strategic place in the union's agriculture in economic and social terms. this regulation should apply to breeding animals of those species and their germinal products where those animals or their offspring are intended to be entered as purebred breeding animals in a breeding book or registered as hybrid breeding pigs in a breeding register, in particular for the purpose of trade within the union internal market. the best way to promote the production of animals of those species is to encourage the use of purebred breeding animals or registered hybrid breeding pigs of high genetic quality. the commission has adopted decisions laying down species-specific criteria and has established a list of third country breeding bodies and the model breeding or zootechnical certificates for the entry into the union of breeding animals and their semen, ova and embryos. however, it should be noted that the demand for competitiveness in the livestock sector should not result in the disappearance of breeds whose characteristics are adapted to specific biophysical contexts.
‒ this legislative resolution of the european parliament concerns a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on zootechnical and genealogical conditions governing trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products. the purpose of that resolution is to ensure a harmonised approach to trade in, importation and control of breeding animals and their germinal products by laying down rules applicable, inter alia, to the performance of official controls by breeders' associations and breeding operations to verify compliance by member states with zootechnical and genealogical rules and other official and administrative assistance activities. given that we are faced with a proposal which offers a regulation with a single legal framework in this area, with clear and well-defined rules, i see no objection to the adoption of this resolution and, in that respect, i voted in favour.
‒ animal husbandry legislation is one of the pillars of animal breeding processes in that it regulates the import of breeding animals and their genetic material. the conservation of genetic resources in europe is a concern that should underpin the regulatory arrangements in this area. the objective of competitiveness, which leads to the export of large european breeds as well as the import of other breeds, should not compromise the survival and reproduction of indigenous breeds, some of which have small populations and are part of the european genetic biodiversity.
‒ the purpose of this regulation is to lay down zootechnical and genealogical rules for the conservation and reproduction of animals and the rules governing the conservation and reproduction of native or endangered breeds. this regulation thus brings together in a single legal framework a number of important aspects, such as the structuring of the livestock breeding sector, the establishment of rules for the management of stud books, breeding registers, animal breeding and performance testing and genetic evaluation. it also lays down rules for intra-eu trade and imports from third countries, and lays down rules for official controls and commission controls. one of the negative aspects of this proposal, apart from the assumption that the meat production sector must be more competitive to allow european species and breeds to be exported, is the aspect of animal cloning being left out, even as regards the pedigree register, not being recorded whether the progenitor is a cloned animal or whether the germ products are derived from a cloned animal.

in writing. ‒ in the face of the huge influx of people that eventually resulted in the so-called 'refugee crisis', the european union has been - late and slow - reacting rather than preventing or anticipating. much has been done, but much remains to be done. i have often said that this crisis has two distinct but complementary levels of action. on the one hand, we have to respond to the emergency, which is essentially humanitarian. on the other hand, we must tackle structural issues, such as the origin of the largest number of displaced persons since the second world war. this report presents a comprehensive vision, which lays out an accurate diagnosis, looks critically at the emergency response, presents a set of structural reforms such as the common european asylum system, or external borders and achieves something that the union desperately needs: solidarity and long-term vision. i support this report. now is the time to act.
‒ the migration crisis is a major political challenge in several eu member states. this report advocates a 'holistic approach' to migration and highlights the need to review the dublin iii regulation, which determines the member state responsible for handling a particular asylum application. the report urges member states to fulfil their obligations regarding the urgent resettlement of refugees and to provide technical and financial assistance to eu frontline countries with the aim of improving the functioning of reception centres. i voted in favour.
‒ the report follows a logic, only apparently paradoxical, of criticism to facilitate acceptance. it certainly contains some positive and critical proposals on aspects which are more widely reported in the media. however, the general sense, the political position it adopts, supports the political choices of the council, the european commission and the european parliament. there is not a single paragraph or line in this report denouncing the eu's responsibility for migration flows or clearly condemning the measures that have been implemented. the main thrust of the eu's migration policy in the face of this very serious humanitarian crisis is to deepen 'strong europe', by criminalising and expelling refugees and migrants, promoting a xenophobic and racist agenda, alongside other discriminatory, intolerant, authoritarian and anti-democratic practices. the decisions of the european council in march confirm an inhuman and cruel policy, in clear violation of international law. they choose to deepen the militarized response to the plight of those fleeing extreme poverty, hunger and military conflicts, locking them into the sinister circle of war that doubly condemns them. the agreement recently concluded is a good illustration of the eu's hypocrisy and the total absence of elementary values of respect for human and democratic rights. these are reasons for our vote against.
‒ the humanitarian emergency the european union has experienced in the context of the refugee crisis requires a coordinated and effective approach to migration. i reiterate that europe has, first of all, the obligation and the responsibility to ensure the security of its peoples. and then, because you're safe, you have an obligation to do good to others and to welcome refugees with humanity. i share the view that any holistic approach to migration must necessarily include measures aimed at dismantling the activities of criminal networks involved in trafficking in human beings and smuggling of persons. i voted in favour.
‒ i express my concern at the incidents at the eu's borders, which are a consequence of this unprecedented migration crisis and which have highlighted the shortcomings of the current system for the reception of refugees and migrants. i argue that the current migrant and refugee crisis is largely due to the conflict in syria and other parts of the middle east, together with instability in the middle east and north africa region, and that the eu will have to play a leading role in putting an end to this situation. i agree with the rapporteurs that the current migrant and refugee crisis in the mediterranean can only be stopped by sustained political will and international cooperation and coordination in all eu institutions and member states, and that an international conference should be organised, on the initiative of the eu, under the auspices of the united nations, in order to respond to the current crisis at the humanitarian level. the vulnerability of women and children, especially unaccompanied children, as they are at risk of becoming victims of trafficking in human beings, and the importance of ensuring that this group receives special care, including psychological support and medical assistance, as well as adequate protection, should be highlighted.
‒ despite some criticism and even positive proposals in this extensive report, its underlying framework accepts and sanctions the criminal european migration policy imposed by the council and the measures that have been implemented, promoting a xenophobic and racist agenda, alongside other discriminatory, authoritarian and anti-democratic practices. the essential pillars of the eu's so-called migration policy in the face of this very serious humanitarian crisis are the deepening of strong europe, the closure of borders, the militarisation of the response to the plight of those fleeing extreme poverty, hunger and war, the criminalisation of refugees and migrants and the implementation of the return policy, in clear violation of international law, in particular since the so-called hotspots, which were transformed into genuine detention and deportation camps after the unthinkable agreement with turkey. throughout the document, there is not a single element denouncing the eu's responsibilities in this humanitarian drama resulting from its interventionist action, in conjunction with the usa and nato, on the african continent and in the middle east. i therefore vote against.
‒ this report stresses that solidarity must be the union's fundamental principle on migration and that a better european response to this scourge remains necessary. it said that great importance should be given to search and rescue operations and that there should be a clear distinction between people who are smuggled into the european union and those who are victims of trafficking. it also considered that resettlement was an important step towards granting safe and legal access to the union and stressed that further measures were needed to ensure that the common european asylum system (ceas) became truly uniform. the report also addresses issues such as the integration and participation of refugees in society, the preservation of family unity, the vulnerability of refugee children, the need for better data and labour exploitation, and considers that the safe return of persons who, following an individual assessment of their asylum application, are not considered eligible for protection in the union should be ensured within the framework of the proper application of the echr. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ this report aims to analyse the results of the specific work carried out by the european union in the mediterranean, in particular in several operations carried out in italy and tunisia, in the fields of security and rescue operations, migration, asylum and border management. the report highlights some of the main highlights of the evaluation, supporting the need for a comprehensive plan with medium- and long-term responses. the rapporteur makes a number of suggestions to help the situation in the mediterranean, such as: a permanent union response in the context of search and rescue operations, the implementation of measures to prevent the trafficking and labour exploitation of irregular migrants, or the introduction of integrated border management with a view to managing migration effectively while also ensuring a high level of internal security. solidarity and the fair and equitable sharing of responsibilities by the different member states should also be an integral part of this package of measures as an eu principle. i voted in favour of this report because i consider that these measures are not only necessary but also urgent.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the metsola/kyenge report which proposes a holistic approach to migration in the eu. the report calls for the maintenance of permanent and effective search and rescue operations to avoid further loss of life in the mediterranean sea. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the report also envisages the creation of humanitarian visas to allow the holder to travel directly to the country where he intends to seek asylum. the refugee crisis has shown that the eu's current approach to migration is not sustainable, and we need a complete overhaul to create a 21st century response system.
‒ the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are of paramount importance for the functioning of the european decision-making process. the first allows decisions to be taken at the level closest to the electorate, the second ensures action appropriate to the aims pursued. subsidiarity in particular has seen its role strengthened by the lisbon treaty. national parliaments can now stop the legislative process for breach of this principle. the years 2012 and 2013 do not seem to have been very active in this area, but on two occasions the so-called 'yellow card' was used, forcing at least a reassessment of the proposal. i do not think it is time to review these procedures, since national parliaments are only now beginning to make use of them, but i welcome the adoption of the report as it shows a clear evolution and growing importance of these two principles.
‒ subsidiarity and proportionality are the eu's fundamental guiding principles and the principles by which the eu should be governed. the commission presented the monti ii proposal on which the national parliaments delivered 12 reasoned opinions, triggering for the first time the yellow card procedure which requires the institution which drafted the legislative act to carry out a review of the draft and to justify its decision to withdraw, amend or maintain the draft in question. the commission withdrew the proposal even though it considered that the principle of subsidiarity was safeguarded. i agree that the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are the starting point for policy-making and i think it is important that, at the beginning of the legislative process, it is assessed whether policy objectives can be achieved more effectively at european level than through national or regional measures.
‒ the tendency in the eu, at the legislative level, has been to strengthen eu action at the expense of national action, with the almost always fallacious argument that certain objectives are better achieved at eu level. what is being done is to subvert and reverse the principle of subsidiarity. national parliaments end up being of little importance and their opinions are disregarded. an example of this is the case of the european public prosecutor, which was given a yellow card by the parliaments, and the european commission nevertheless maintained the proposal. why ask the national parliaments if their opinion does not count? this report is in line with this trend. criticism is directed at the european commission and its actions, but on the other hand, there is talk of the difficulty of having different views at the level of national parliaments, as if everyone had to think the same way - already, the way the eu wants - over and above the differences between member states. the truth is that common policies within the eu always end up benefiting some at the expense of others. national parliaments become mere spectators in the eu legislative process. or just 'notaries' of directives they have to transpose. we voted against it.
‒ in the light of article 5 teu and protocol no 2 to the tfeu, the european institutions must respect the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, which are of a general nature and bind the institutions in the exercise of the union's powers, except in areas of exclusive competence of the union where the principle of subsidiarity is not applicable. subsidiarity and proportionality are key eu guiding principles as essential tools for shaping policies for the benefit of eu citizens, and as tools for assessing the financial impact of legislation. i am pleased to note that the number of reasoned opinions as a percentage of the total number of communications has increased significantly. i agree with the rapporteur's regret that there are no common standards, which makes it more difficult to assess the basis on which the member states' parliaments act. i would stress the importance of impact assessments for decision-making during the legislative process and, in this context, the implementation of rigorous impact assessments, which verify compliance with the principle of subsidiarity, is essential in order to regain the confidence of citizens, for whom subsidiarity is often an essential aspect of the democratic process.
‒ these annual reports monitor the application of article 5 teu. the application of these principles is closely linked to the relationship between the european union and the authorities of the member states, the national parliaments. notwithstanding the wording of that article, practice shows the ongoing trend towards strengthening union action to the detriment of national or regional action, on the grounds that certain objectives are better achieved at union level. national parliaments are not only of little importance but are also disregarded. the european public prosecutor's office, for example, was given a yellow card by the parliaments but the commission eventually kept it. national parliaments cannot become mere spectators in the eu legislative process, which covers key areas of their daily lives and their collective future. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions. the imposition of common policies is aimed not only at the loss of sovereignty of the states but also at the benefit of some states to the detriment of others. we reject the attack on sovereignty and the attempt to empty the role and responsibilities of national parliaments, the structures which represent the citizens. we voted against it.
‒ i voted in favour of this report because i agree that the verification of the principle of subsidiarity is very important for the collaboration between european, national and regional institutions. the principle of subsidiarity allows the union to act beyond its competence only where the objectives of the action in question cannot be attained by the member states, at central, regional or local level, but can rather, by reason of the scale or effects of the action, be better achieved at union level. the principle of proportionality requires that the content and form of union action should not exceed what is necessary to achieve the objectives of the treaties. i therefore agree that policy-making must respect the principle of subsidiarity and have tangible european added value. i believe it is essential that the principle of subsidiarity be respected, taking into account the role of the social partners and ensuring their autonomy in accordance with the customs and traditions of the member states. breaches of the principle of subsidiarity may result in a loss of citizens' trust.
‒ the review of subsidiarity and proportionality by national parliaments analysed in this report is a key part of the application of these principles in the european legislative framework. subsidiarity and proportionality are an integral and guiding element of european policy-making, in order to establish the level of improvement that the political results of european union action can achieve in terms of strengthening dialogue and cooperation with national parliaments. what the 2012-13 reports on subsidiarity and proportionality have shown is a greater participation and involvement of national parliaments in the european legislative process, demonstrating the greater effectiveness of the objectives at a macro level than through mere national or regional measures. like the rapporteur, i believe that it is essential to strengthen the political dialogue between the commission and the national parliaments, and to carry out credible impact assessments to help in the decision-making process during the legislative process, where the issues of subsidiarity and proportionality are most acute. in view of the foregoing, i have decided to support mr karim's report.
in writing. ‒ the subsidiarity principle seems to be a positive one. the problem is that the tendency is to say that the union's action should be strengthened, rather than national or regional action, on the grounds that certain objectives are better achieved at the level of the union. in the end, national parliaments are generally of little importance and their views are not taken into account. the european public prosecutor's office, for example, was given a yellow card by the parliaments but the commission ultimately upheld its proposal. so why ask the national parliaments if their opinion does not count? the emptying of the sovereignty of the representative structures of the citizens closest to them is negative. national parliaments become mere spectators in the eu legislative process (as demonstrated by the experience of the card mechanism, which is concerned with monitoring the principle of subsidiarity), which covers key areas of their daily lives and their collective future.

in writing. ‒ learning about the eu in school can help to develop a sense of european citizenship from an early age, to make european values known and thus to combat the growing euroscepticism that is felt in all member states.
‒ this report, which i voted in favour of, stresses that eu-related topics should be more visible and well integrated into teaching materials and extracurricular activities and believes that the inclusion of explicitly eu-related content can substantially enhance school curricula and pupils' personal development and growth. it also stresses that knowledge and understanding of the history and common values of the eu and its member states are essential for mutual understanding, peaceful coexistence, tolerance and solidarity, as well as for understanding the fundamental principles of the european union, and therefore deserved my positive vote. in this way, these measures will enable pupils to reflect critically on the eu, on governance, on decision-making processes and on how they themselves and their democratic participation influence the member state to which they belong. the document also calls for an intercultural approach to education policies that provides for the genuine integration of immigrant pupils in schools, based on mutual knowledge of different cultures and the development of shared common values.
in writing. ‒ at this historic juncture, the european union is facing unprecedented challenges and has been in the throes of a serious economic and financial crisis in recent years. the social, economic and political effects of this crisis call into question the union's common institutions and values, including the notion of european identity. in this context, intensifying the study and dialogue on the european union in schools, associations or public spaces is crucial to restoring citizens' confidence, their sense of belonging to this union of peoples and states and, consequently, to promoting the process of european construction. it is therefore essential to improve the european dimension in school education, giving citizens better tools to live and work in a union of 28 member states that is embedded in a very complex and globalised world. although the member states have exclusive competence, we note that the situation regarding the inclusion of eu content in national school curricula is unfortunately far from uniform and we therefore consider that specific measures are needed in this area, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
‒ this report assumes that the fact that people have limited knowledge of the eu and how it works is the key factor in making people feel distant and increasingly alienated from the 'european political project' and more eurosceptic and 'perceiving a democratic deficit in eu decision-making processes'. this report does not, of course, condemn but rather calls for education and training to be subordinated to the implementation of the 2020 strategy, advocating the harmonisation of the structure of knowledge and even of content, ignoring the specificities of the education system of each country, in a trend towards vocational training rather than integrated 'education'. for people to believe in the 'european project', it is first and foremost necessary that the project be for the realisation of rights, for cooperation and solidarity between countries; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
‒ i support the report by mr maragall, who calls for the strengthening of mobility mechanisms in the field of vocational education and training (vet). i agree with the emphasis on the need to respond to the training needs of young people who want to enter the labour market earlier or seek training with more vocational characteristics and the need to contribute to reducing school drop-out rates. i also agree that these trainees should have access to european mobility programmes without discrimination, that actions should be developed to reduce cultural barriers and strengthen language skills, and that particular attention should be paid to areas where youth unemployment is most pronounced.
‒ the various pre-existing eu mobility programmes have been merged into one, erasmus+. the effects of this measure are still to be assessed in depth. the overall aim of the report is to call on the european commission and the member states to develop efforts in favour of vocational education and training within all existing mobility tools. the report identifies a number of challenges that eu mobility programmes must address, highlighting the difficulties of access. while erasmus is seen as a successful eu mobility programme, the truth is that mobility rates are low. this is mainly because the grants awarded are few and do not cover tuition, food, housing, study materials, transportation and other expenses. only a restricted social group has access to mobility. the report is not without contradictions. education is defended as a right that should be guaranteed to all people. but 'education for the market' is favoured over 'education for life'. we support many of the criticisms made in the report, in particular the lack of access to education for the most disadvantaged population. we agree to actions aimed at removing barriers and providing greater support for the learning of other languages.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on erasmus+ and other instruments to promote mobility in vet. erasmus as a mobility programme for learning and personal development has shown its important potential for promoting employment, social cohesion and skills development. it is essential that the funding of learning mobility programmes such as erasmus+ is a priority of the european union, within the political agenda for promoting education and youth.
‒ we follow up on several criticisms, notably the elitisation of education, or the inaccessibility of mobility programmes for students in vocational education and training. the integration of several education, training and youth work mobility programmes into erasmus+ has resulted in a reduction in jobs and redundancies in portugal, despite the concentration of competences in one agency. the promotion of student mobility through this programme has not only fallen short of imposing an unacceptable and unavoidable discrimination of access, which is evident with the low rates of mobility. not only has access to the programme been mainly at the higher education level, but it is also clear that it is not accessible to everyone. without the financial backing to cover the entire period outside the country of origin (tickets, accommodation, food), only an elite with greater financial resources benefits from this mobility. the report promotes the view of education and training in a mercantilist logic of market satisfaction and subscribes to the logic that mobility should serve to solve the problems of youth unemployment by linking mobility with employability. we voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the vote in favour of this report as it calls on the eu to remove all socioeconomic constraints that prevent equal access for all to vocational education and training opportunities, including mobility. in addition, the report stresses that the outcomes of education systems can be important in reducing early school leaving and equipping students with transversal skills that will help them match their qualifications with the demands of the labour market. it should also be stressed that learning and training mobility is key to responding to social and cultural challenges, with a view to maximising the opportunities for young people to develop their own plans of action in society. this report states that there is a need to have a flexible, diversified and adapted range of mobility options for training available to cover people from immigration or economically disadvantaged families, participants from the outermost regions, people with disabilities and people with special needs. the report also calls for a review of the multiannual financial framework on the basis of a prior assessment of the effectiveness of measures to combat unemployment and for the funding of the least effective measures to be cut.
‒ all measures aimed at increasing the mobility of education and vocational training in order to contribute to growth and job creation in the eu are positive and welcome.
in writing. the introduction of erasmus+ marked an important step towards greater mobility in european higher education. the remaining differences in the academic/curricular perspective, the organisation and management of educational establishments and the relations between the education system and the business world have been eliminated by the introduction of a system that allows for the standardisation of costs and other operational difficulties. this is a programme for young people which i consider extremely important because it offers the greatest possible range of academic and professional opportunities, while at the same time contributing to the sociological, civic and even personal construction of an effective european identity. continuing to identify the main challenges, promoting a personalised approach to education, reducing school drop-out rates and at the same time ensuring equal access to erasmus mobility actions are some of the factors that led me to support this report. the promotion of language skills, the capacity to act and adapt to new situations, entrepreneurship, self-determination, cultural immersion in a different country, the exchange of experiences and the resulting tolerance are some of the examples that result from the implementation of programmes such as this, and their promotion should therefore be extended.
‒ the report 'erasmus+ and other instruments to promote mobility in vocational education and training a lifelong learning approach' reinforces the european union's commitment to supporting lifelong learning and vocational education and training by providing opportunities to acquire new skills, increase employability, increase cultural awareness and increase foreign language skills. the report highlights the role of society in promoting the visibility of vocational education and training programmes, with a view to breaking down the barriers that hinder access to the programme for people who are discriminated against. the european network of incubators and the exchange of knowledge between schools, universities and businesses should also be given priority. the commission is requested to provide updated statistics on the programme with a view to assessing its impact on youth employability and its mid-term review. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is important to promote youth mobility and to increase access to education and vocational training, especially for disadvantaged groups and people with special needs.
in writing. ‒ we support many of the criticisms made in the report, including the lack of access to education for the most disadvantaged population, that access for students in vocational education and training to mobility programmes should be encouraged and facilitated, in particular through actions aimed at removing cultural barriers, and that there should be greater support for learning other languages. all disadvantaged groups and people with special needs should be effectively included in information and preparation sessions. despite stating that mobility should not become the only solution envisaged for the unacceptable dimensions of youth unemployment in the eu, the link between mobility and employability is still mentioned in one or two paragraphs.
‒ i voted in favour of the maragall report on erasmus+ and other instruments to promote mobility in vocational education and training which proposes a lifelong learning approach with a particular focus on the learning of young people and trainees. erasmus+ aims to build on the previous leonardo mobility programme and invites the european commission and the member states to take concrete measures to improve the social and economic impact of mobility with the aim of achieving a highly skilled workforce through inclusive education policies. i believe that such initiatives, which focus on university mobility and vocational training within the european union, can contribute to growth and job creation in the european area.
in the first place, the commission has not yet taken a decision on the future of the european union. the report points out the insufficient parliamentary scrutiny (both of the european parliament and of the national parliaments) and the lack of transparency and information to citizens of many processes linked to these institutions, especially for civil society, smes, consumer representatives and social partners. i welcome the approach of eu representation in some of these institutions (and not just through the national representation of some of its member states) and i share the view that the under-representation of the least developed countries contributes to the inequalities and funding of the poorest countries not being properly considered.
‒ as a consequence of the free movement of capital, the stability of the financial system depends on the ability to develop and implement, at the supranational level, standards and norms of conduct. the necessary change of scale must not lead to a dilution of responsibilities to the detriment of democracy. in particular, national parliaments and the european parliament cannot be reduced to mere approving assemblies. finally, the eu and the euro area must be able to defend their strategic interests. the eu has the means to meet this challenge. it has created a global internal market for financial services, with recognised financial centres, a systemic risk committee (esrb) and three authorities whose existence has rapidly become more solid. given the strategic importance of the financial sector for growth and jobs, i believe that global multilateral cooperation needs to be re-designed, giving greater importance to the eu and the euro area.
the report proposes a single representation of the european union and the eurozone in international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions, at the expense of the sovereign presence of the member states in these spaces. one voice they proclaim. what voice is this not said nor necessary would be: the european parliament is the voice of big finance capital and the european powers at its service. it is not the latter that should be deprived of their voice in defence of their interests. it would be the peripheral countries, such as portugal, that would be deprived of this voice and subjected even more to dictates and interests contrary to their needs and the will of their people. we have, of course, rejected this report. we have tabled a minority report with a different view. an alternative vision, respectful of national sovereignty, based on cooperation and solidarity between member states, which defends the need for international regulation of the financial system, based on joint efforts of cooperation, which rejects the submission of political power to economic power and the transfer of political power to bodies outside the control and democratic scrutiny of the people.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the role of the eu in the framework of international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies. i share the rapporteur's view that there is a need for greater policy coherence and coordination between the institutions at world level by strengthening the principles of democratic legitimacy, transparency, accountability and integrity.
‒ the increasing interdependence of the world economies makes the adoption of concerted, more globalised strategies imperative. the european union must have a jointly-designed action, with the objectives and values of the eu treaties, so that we can speak with one voice in the international institutions and bodies. i believe that the european parliament, as the democratic body representing the european citizens, and the parliaments of the member states, cannot be limited to giving its consent. they must play a decisive role in the decision-making process, which is to be more active and comprehensive. with the onset of the economic and financial crisis in 2008, it became clear that there is an extraordinary lack of economic and financial governance worldwide and that numerous macroeconomic issues require greater coordination. i agree with the rapporteur that all the parties concerned should have as a common objective the development of a comprehensive framework providing financial stability and ensuring coherence between the global and local levels.
the report is based on the idea of deepening the power of supranational bodies, in a logic of centralisation and of subjugation of political power to economic power, which we strongly oppose. we reject without reservation this eu, which is committed to cooperation and solidarity between member states, attacking national sovereignty. we are strongly opposed to the idea that peer review allows for greater accountability of citizens than the traditional model of formal democratic accountability, and to the establishment of a single eu representation in the international financial institutions, thus taking away the member states' unique capacity to intervene. greater democratic legitimacy and accountability are not achieved by means of concentration and increased supranational taxation. it is up to member states to be represented in international fora and regulatory cooperation at global level should be based on solidarity between countries, not on the defence of major economic and financial interests.
‒ this report aims to contribute to an answer by analysing the eu's action in a dozen political and/or technical organisations and takes as its starting point three findings: transparency, accountability and eu/euro area representation. the report found that, given the global nature of capital flows and financial professions, it is illusory to frame the financial sector without changing the scale of public intervention. the eu has therefore a number of means to meet this challenge: the commission has, for example, created a global internal market in financial services, which the capital markets union will soon be giving new life, and it has recognised financial centres, a committee to prevent systemic risks and three authorities whose existence has become more solid. given the strategic importance of the financial sector for growth and jobs, the report found that there is a need to reframe overall multilateral cooperation, giving greater importance to the eu and the euro area. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of this report.
‒ the national parliaments and the european parliament cannot be reduced to mere approving assemblies. while it is crucial to have an independent assessment of the private and political interests involved, dialogue between experts and elected representatives should be re-launched. the eu and the euro area must be able to defend their strategic interests. in many organizations, europe is represented in a disorderly way, to say the least. this is all the more regrettable when we consider the importance of the challenges not only to financial stability but above all to growth and employment. the european union must make a stronger and more effective contribution to the establishment of a more balanced multilateral cooperation in economic and financial matters. the report also calls for increased international regulatory cooperation, transparency, accountability and democratisation with strong involvement of the european parliament.
in writing. - i support this own-initiative report by mrs goulard on a proposal for a european parliament resolution on the role of the european union in the framework of international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies. this includes answering questions such as 'who decides', 'who sets the rules for the financial sector' and 'what is the role of national parliaments and governments in this context'. i agree with the rapporteur's tripartite approach to the main areas where the european union should act: transparency, accountability and representation of the european union and the euro area. it is essential that the european union plays a more active and prominent role in the process of global economic governance, in particular through membership of international bodies, and it is also really important that fundamental institutional reforms are initiated which will enable the european union to achieve a strong voice and a coherent representation ('enhanced and more effective coordination', to use the rapporteur's words) in the various international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies.
in the light of the above, the commission considers that the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment and the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work should be approved by the council. we reject without reservation this eu, which is committed to cooperation and solidarity between member states as well as to their national sovereignty, the idea that peer review allows for greater accountability of citizens than the traditional model of formal democratic accountability, based on the concept of 'agent and committee', as well as the establishment of a single representation that speaks with one voice for all eu countries in the framework of international financial institutions. we strongly believe that greater democratic legitimacy and accountability will not be achieved by increasing supranational impositions. member states should not be without their own representation in international forums and regulatory cooperation at global level should be based on solidarity between countries, not on the defence of major economic and financial interests.
‒ this report focuses on small fishing communities, small-scale coastal fishing and the factors for their protection and development in a highly industrialised context. the report refers to and advocates the promotion of specific regulation and legislation, financing instruments and technology and know-how transfer, the regionalisation of the common fisheries policy (cfp), a more equitable distribution of quotas, the protection of the environment and the value of socioeconomic diversity, the development of the marine economy with the involvement of stakeholders, the development of gender policies that enhance the economic and social emancipation of women, the strengthening of sustainable aquaculture, the creation of employment and the improvement of working conditions and the respect of rights. in general, the report's approach and proposals are in line with our positions, and we therefore voted in favour. on this occasion, however, we must recall the report adopted in the previous legislature on small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing, for which we were responsible, containing recommendations to improve the situation of this specific segment of the fishing fleet, which is highly prevalent in portugal. for the most part, these recommendations remain valid, but unfortunately they have not been removed from the paper. the new cfp has also degraded an already difficult and precarious situation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on innovation and diversification of small-scale fisheries in fisheries-dependent regions. we must make every effort to protect small-scale fishing, especially in the outermost regions. this report advocates coastal fishing, which guarantees a high level of employment and is a socially and environmentally sustainable form of fishing. it is also important to stress that tourism and fishing should not be separated. both are important to local economies.
in writing. ‒ it is our duty, especially when we know the reality well, to safeguard the interests and defend the specificities of regions which suffer from certain constraints, such as the outermost regions. different treatment is needed to deal with what is different, and in the case of fisheries and fishing or sea-related activities, we need to find different solutions. the adoption of this report defends small-scale coastal fishing and enhances the value of the professions linked to maritime activity, that is, all those who have their source of income in fishing. we have succeeded in ensuring that the outermost regions receive a different treatment in the future of european fisheries. the emphasis is on creating new types of support, within the framework of existing european funding, so that more and new areas can be eligible for funding. as rapporteur for the epp, i am glad to see the report adopted by a large majority.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it has a huge impact on the azores. the document makes recommendations to adapt the definition of small-scale coastal fishing to the characteristics of the regions, as there is no uniformity in this concept, and it also recognises that there are island communities which traditionally depend on fishing for their livelihood, and that greater regionalisation should be pursued in order to have a fisheries policy closer to the sector. aspects such as the progressive increase in the quotas allocated to artisanal fishermen, the strengthening of the role of fishing communities in local development, the priority given to small-scale coastal fishing in the allocation of funding and the simplification of procedures were also reasons for my vote in favour. on the other hand, and since we are witnessing a decline in employment and profitability in this sector, a certain marginalisation of fisheries in developing regions and opportunities to benefit from the new possibilities, i also argue that it is necessary to continue diversification in this sector, deepening the relationship between local communities and universities/technology centres, in order to create new business incubators that will potentially generate business ideas in this sector.
‒ coastal fishing is particularly important in the eu as it provides a high level of employment and is socially and environmentally sustainable. for most coastal and island areas, traditional coastal fishing is a way of life and an important source of livelihood. some coastal and island regions are facing significant economic decline, which is reflected in depopulation and the exodus of their inhabitants, who are seeking opportunities in sectors offering better prospects of employment and education. in addition, some coastal fishing areas are located close to economically developed and tourist areas, but are unable to achieve adequate economic growth. areas dependent on coastal fishing need specific measures and support to grow and develop. the emff may support investments in diversification and contribute positively to fishermen's incomes through the development of complementary activities, namely investments in vessels, restaurants, environmental services in the fisheries sector, cultural and educational activities in the fisheries sector, fisheries tourism, etc.

‒ the common fisheries policy (cfp) includes a chapter on its external dimension, including the establishment of minimum conditions for the establishment of fisheries agreements between the eu and third countries, along with commitments to increase cooperation and consistency of measures implemented within the framework of regional fisheries management organisations; an explicit reference to common standards within and outside eu waters; and the use of scientific information in decision-making. while we do not follow all the considerations made, the report highlights some important issues, which we value: the need to ensure that fisheries agreements provide mutual benefits for the eu and third countries, including their local populations and the fishing sector; the promotion of environmentally, socially and economically sustainable fisheries based on transparency and the participation of non-governmental actors, especially professionals who depend on fishing for their livelihood, in order to ensure a future for coastal communities, the marine environment, the development of local industry, the employment generated by fishing, processing and trade, and the contribution of fishing to food security; measures to promote the transfer of technology and know-how; the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on the external dimension of the cfp, including fisheries agreements. the new eu cfp has evolved significantly. if properly implemented, it will certainly contribute to improving the eu's long-sea fishing standards. the inclusion of a chapter on the external dimension in the recent reform of the cfp regulation, in which sustainable fisheries partnership agreements (sfps) and fisheries under gfcf are formally regulated for the first time, is noteworthy. the eu must ensure transparency, while seeking to promote the protection of ecosystems and the maintenance of fish stocks. this is the only way to generate income for fishermen in different types of fishing. it should be noted that the eu is now the world's largest market for fishery products and has one of the largest fleets in terms of catch capacity.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, as it advocates the inclusion of the outermost regions in the external dimension of the common fisheries policy and also in the framework of bilateral agreements signed with third countries, in order to ensure that local fisheries in these regions benefit. at the same time, this basic cfp regulation includes a chapter devoted to its external dimension, providing for minimum conditions to be respected in the framework of bilateral agreements, which i have always advocated. the eu should promote the harmonisation of fishing conditions with a view to creating favourable conditions for fishermen, promoting sustainable and responsible fishing. only regionalised fisheries management can ensure sustainable and equitable exploitation, and further studies on the state of stocks and habitat and, where necessary, greater protection of deep-sea species and habitats are essential. aspects such as improving the transparency of fisheries agreements and activities, defending sustainability and improving the supply of fish to ensure food security were also reasons for my approval of this report.
‒ this report relates to the external dimension of the common fisheries policy, i.e. the promotion of sustainable fisheries in third countries, while also ensuring that imported fishery products are produced to acceptable labour standards and human rights.
‒ three decades after the start of the implementation of the common fisheries policy (cfp), maritime competition is now more intense. the union therefore needs to promote sustainable fisheries and the best strategy for achieving this objective is to use its influence on the international scene to improve management standards and transparency in the management of fisheries resources. the union, as the world's largest market for fishery products, also has one of the largest fleets for catching them. the marketing of these products is subject to very strict measures in terms of traceability and the verification of the size/hygiene of the catch, as well as in the fight against iuu fishing. these measures aim to ensure competitive advantages, taking into account environmental and social sustainability and the protection of consumer rights, as well as strict application of international regulations. given the significant progress of the new cfp, with notable success in the iuu regulation, which has led to improvements in legislation on fishing activities across the globe, i supported this report, which aims to promote measures for the continuous improvement of fisheries management globally.
