madam president, the panama papers revelations require, first of all, public recognition of the extraordinary work of the international consortium of investigative journalists and also of the whistleblowers who provide them with the data. it is worth recalling that antoine deltour, one of the luxleaks whistleblowers, is to be tried this month for breach of professional and commercial secrecy, and so, by joining and associating myself with the european commission, the commissioner, in this commendation, i would also like to see the european protection statute for legal aid for these citizens, as recommended in taxe, accelerated on its list. a second note on the size of this iceberg of panama papers: it requires the european union to move definitively towards a clear definition of what tax havens are, with objective and transparent criteria and a list of sanctions for those who operate in them. i look to the european commission, not to criticise it, but to praise and encourage it, but i would like to have a commitment from the council, if possible even stronger, that the blockage that the council has made to the tax agenda is now reduced to zero in the face of the scandal of the european union's apathy in tax matters. thank you very much.
the commission is not prepared to accept this. if the panama papers are a drop in the bucket, the commission's proposals are baby steps. i would like to take this opportunity to talk about ourselves and the underlying problem, which is the very existence of tax havens. tax havens are something that nobody likes, but nobody really wants to do anything to stop them, and if you can talk to multinationals and the rich about tax optimization, you can talk to workers and small and mediumsized businesses about tax evasion. there is no political will in the european union, because there are tax havens in the european union, there are countries which are tax havens, the netherlands, luxembourg, belgium and finally madeira itself, and therefore the european union must have political will because it is the world's largest holder of tax havens, and that is really the fundamental problem, mr moscovici. the maintenance of tax havens in the european union sends a very clear message to citizens: those who evade taxes with 100 euros are criminals, those who evade with 100 million euros are entrepreneurs. that is certainly not a matter of fiscal justice.
this tax scandal, one more, is a wake-up call to a reality that is not new. we've had luxleaks before, swissleaks, offshore leaks and now we have the panama papers. this reality cannot be dissociated from the emergence of the neoliberal paradigm and the deregulation of the financial system that has come to dominate since the 1980s. it cannot be dissociated from the wave of privatisations of public financial institutions created in the post-war period. this scandal is not an accident of the road. this is a structural phenomenon which requires fundamental measures, such as the abolition of tax havens, and it also attacks the very heart of the system, which is the sprawling network of banks and financial institutions. we are counting on them to take firm measures to combat tax fraud and evasion, by putting obstacles in the way of the transfer of profits and capital to offshore regions. we impose transparency rules on all processes, including free access to all tax information. they don't count on us to fake what's being done to keep it the same.
the panama papers: another scandal on a global scale which calls on the european union to combat financial crime schemes which facilitate tax evasion, corruption and all types of organised crime, including terrorism. it is imperative and urgent to confiscate the proceeds and punish the politicians, banks, consultants and lawyers who use, and if they do use, offshore secrecy to capture governments, steal from citizens and from democracy. the european commission has proposed that multinational companies should publish country-by-country accounts, but in a general way, they should be published for all the countries in which they operate, not just in europe. it should also require the public register of beneficial owners of companies, foundations and trusts to be made available online to all citizens in the announced revision of the anti-money laundering directive. but make no mistake, without tax harmonization in the european union, tax dumping will continue, with several member states acting as genuine tax havens and ruining others. that is what happens in the netherlands in relation to my country.
the european parliament has been urging the european commission and the european council to strengthen legislative initiatives and coordination on the ground to combat tax evasion and money laundering, which, in addition to being actions against fairness and justice, contribute to increasing asymmetries in competitiveness and growth capacity within the european union and in the world. the taxe committee has recently adopted a robust set of recommendations to deal with phenomena such as those identified in the luxembourg and panama leaks. in may 2015, the european parliament approved the revision of the anti-money laundering directive, which requires that central registers of beneficial ownership of companies, foundations, trusts and other entities be set up and maintained in all member states. recent revelations show that the measures in place are not effective. the adopted directive and taxe recommendations must be implemented as a matter of urgency. new measures will be needed after the investigation of what has happened, but first of all it is important to put into practice the measures already designed, with a great sense of urgency.

in writing. ‒ on 16 february 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for sweden to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in 5 companies manufacturing motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers in the northern region of norrland, sweden. on receipt of the application, the commission concluded that it qualified for a financial contribution from the egf. this is the second application to be examined under the 2016 budget and the 22nd in the area concerned, and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 1 793 710 from the egf for sweden and the redundancies of 500 workers. the swedish authorities state that the reasons for the redundancies are the developments that have affected the european commercial vehicle segment, especially the heavy-duty vehicle industry in recent years, in particular due to the emergence of new truck manufacturers from asia, and the industry's difficulties in adjusting, forcing it to increase efficiency and reduce costs. my vote was in favor.

‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns and may not exceed the annual ceiling of eur 150 million. the proposal concerns the mobilisation of eur 380 000 from the fund to cover the commission's technical assistance expenditure, which aims to finance monitoring and information in order to create a knowledge base/interface for applications and advise member states on the use, monitoring and evaluation of the egf.
‒ technical assistance to the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims at coordinating egf applications and publishing the results obtained: financial monitoring, creating a knowledge interface to advise member states on the use of the egf, monitoring and evaluation of the egf. the budget foreseen for this assistance shall be no more than 0,5% of the annual maximum amount of the egf (eur 150 million). the commission's proposal for this year provides for the mobilisation of eur 380 000 for technical assistance (0.23% of the maximum annual budget available). the report welcomes and appreciates the work being done to standardise the procedures for egf applications, not without pointing out some criticisms such as the relatively high costs. there are positive aspects, such as the requirement to extend support to young people up to the age of 25 who are not in employment, education or training (neets) by amending the current legal framework, as well as requiring that provision be made for a more general use of the derogation from the eligibility thresholds in favour of smes, the extension of the reference periods, and the possibility of including dismissed workers who provide similar services to those of the dismissed workers of the reference companies. it also called for greater monitoring of beneficiaries. we voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ union assistance to workers made redundant should be dynamic and made available as quickly and efficiently as possible, in accordance with the joint statement of the european parliament, the council and the commission adopted at the conciliation meeting of 17 july 2008, taking due account of the provisions of the iia of 2 december 2013 on the adoption of decisions to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). this regulation reflects the agreement reached between parliament and the council to reintroduce the crisis mobilisation criterion, to set the union financial contribution at 60% of the total estimated cost of the proposed measures, to increase the efficiency of the processing of egf applications by the commission, the european parliament and the council by shortening the evaluation and approval deadline, to extend the measures and eligible beneficiaries to include the self-employed and young people, and to finance incentives for the creation of one's own business. these improvements are essential for a more effective egf, which is why i am voting in favour.

‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns. on 22 february 2016, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf, concerning the mobilisation of eur 380 000 from the fund to cover the commission's technical assistance expenditure. the aim was to finance monitoring and information in order to create a knowledge base/interface for applications and to advise member states on the use, monitoring and evaluation of the egf. this is the third transfer proposal for mobilisation of the fund transmitted to the budgetary authority to date in 2016. i voted in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of this resolution of the european parliament on the proposal to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to finance the egf contact group of experts and the networking seminars on the application of the egf, since the fund's own regulation provides that 0.5% of the amount may be made available for technical assistance at the initiative of the commission, precisely for the purpose of financing the preparation, monitoring, data collection, administrative and technical support and information and communication, audit, monitoring and evaluation activities necessary for the implementation of the egf regulation. given, on the one hand, that the amount of the proposed funding eur 380 000 represents approximately 0,23% of the maximum annual budget available for the egf in 2016 and that the other assumptions inherent in the allocation of the fund are met, i considered that there were no reasons, in my view, to oppose its approval.
‒ the commission's proposal for this year, made on 22 february, provides for the mobilisation of eur 380000 from the technical assistance fund (0.23% of the maximum annual budget available). the report contains some positive elements, such as the requirement to extend support to young people up to 25 years of age who are not in employment, education or training (neets), by amending the legal framework of the egf after 2017, and calls for provision to be made for a more widespread use of the derogation from the eligibility thresholds in favour of smes and the extension of the reference periods, as well as the possibility to include dismissed workers providing similar services to those of dismissed workers from reference companies, in cases where these have fewer than 500 employees, the minimum threshold for qualifying for the egf. it called for more data to be collected on the actual employability of the beneficiaries, including in the final reports the individual assessments of these beneficiaries. the commission is also asked to provide a justification for the decision to subcontract an external auditor for the mid-term evaluation.
‒ the large influx of people to the external borders of the union has necessitated emergency responses. the same applies to security issues, which in 2015 and already in 2016 have required increased resources. this first amending budget for 2016 addresses these two dimensions. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting. at the level of the so-called "refugee crisis", the new domestic humanitarian emergency fund. the need and urgency of this new fund is undeniable, but once again we have resorted to an ad hoc instrument which has avoided the normal legislative procedure (where the european parliament is a co-legislator). as this budget that funds it has shown, parliament has always been constructive and prompt in its response to the refugee crisis. the lack of vision and, too often, the lack of cooperation and sense of urgency has come from the member states. the pressure on the asylum and migration fund (amif), which is also a source of funding here, is also underlined and therefore increasingly needs to be reviewed and strengthened.
in writing. ‒ this amending budget proposes eur 100 million for the creation of an instrument for the provision of emergency support in the union. the urgent issue at the moment is the situation of the refugees in greece. there is a humanitarian emergency which requires urgent action, and greece cannot afford to deal with it alone. but this urgency was foreseeable! the eu is still reacting. the commission should also be able to use the appropriations entered in this article to finance the expenditure incurred by the member states in the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance. it should be a fund, based on a regulation, which would be activated whenever a humanitarian emergency situation arose within the eu. its funding should be additional and extraordinary, as is the case with the natural disaster fund and the solidarity fund. the amending budget also includes a eur 2 million increase in the staff of the european counter-terrorism centre at europol. the fight against terrorism requires shared, coordinated and concerted action at eu level.
‒ a budget line is proposed to finance emergency support within the eu more quickly and specifically, whereas there has been only one line for external emergency support. the range of financial instruments available to deal with emergency situations is thus widened. however, the biggest doubts are raised about the new emergency humanitarian assistance mechanism doubts about how the associated funds will be used and for what end, which the committee on freedoms of the european parliament itself has raised. this urgency is clearly due to the lack of a coherent strategy and vision to find a solution to the migration crisis at european level. this draft budget does not provide for new funds, as 100 million will be transferred from the asylum, migration and integration fund to this new emergency fund. the resources of europol and the european counter-terrorism centre are also being strengthened, in a context where the eu insists on policies of aggression and interference which are inseparable from the phenomenon of terrorism, while using it as a pretext to justify a security drift that undermines rights, freedoms and guarantees.
‒ the massive influx of refugees and migrants into europe has created an exceptional situation in which a large number of people are in need of emergency humanitarian assistance in the union, and this emergency situation exceeds the response capacity of the most affected member states. there is no adequate instrument at union level to respond to the humanitarian needs of disaster victims in the union. the commission proposal aims to enable the union budget to provide emergency support within the union in order to cope with the humanitarian consequences of the current refugee crisis. we are now witnessing a deterioration in the situation of migrants and asylum seekers, in particular because of the lack of coordination of the response of european countries, which makes this emergency support all the more necessary and urgent. we must show solidarity with the member states facing this emergency situation on their territory. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the new associated mechanism for emergency humanitarian assistance raises a number of questions as to the procedure for the application and use of the associated funds and the specific objectives they will serve. this new emergency instrument is being set up to respond, belatedly, to a humanitarian tragedy in which the eu has heavy responsibilities and which has worsened over the last year as a result of the various responses it has implemented, such as the criminal agreement signed with turkey. this draft budget is not supported by a financial increase, but by the transfer of eur 100 million from the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif) to this new emergency fund. we note with alarm the concentration and expansion of the powers of europol and its european centre for the fight against terrorism, with the recruitment of 25 additional staff, which will be used as a pretext for the latest events in paris and brussels to strengthen surveillance of citizens, a natural consequence of the measures being adopted in this regard.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because the draft amending budget is intended for emergency humanitarian aid. in view of the deteriorating situation of migrants and asylum seekers, particularly because the response of the european countries is not coordinated, i think this proposal for an amending budget is very timely. it is the creation of a specific budget line, which means that no appropriations are being diverted from the budget for external humanitarian aid, since the commission proposes to finance the first tranche of support under this new instrument by reallocating appropriations from the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif), which were already intended to enable the burden of refugees to be shared between the member states. i therefore voted in favour. i also agree with the proposal to increase the staff of the european counter-terrorism centre at europol, taking into account the current security situation in the european union.
in writing. ‒ this draft amending budget has no net impact on the level of appropriations in the 2016 budget and has essentially a twofold objective: to create a budgetary framework for the proposed new instrument to provide emergency support in the union and for immediate funding needs; to strengthen the staffing levels of the europol counter-terrorism centre.
‒ the migration and refugee crisis that has hit europe has created an exceptional situation for thousands of people who are in dire need of emergency humanitarian aid from the union. in this way, thanks to the inability of the member states most affected to respond and thanks to the lack of an appropriate instrument at european level to respond to this situation, a regulation was created for this purpose and subsequently an amending budget with a view to creating the budgetary structure capable of meeting the immediate financing needs. this is the instrument that this report is concerned with, providing for the provision of eur 100 million in commitment appropriations and eur 80.2 million in payment appropriations to deal, financially and immediately, with the humanitarian consequences of the current refugee crisis. on the basis of the arguments explained and in view of the urgency of the situation, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the creation of a union budget line to fund emergency support within the union more quickly and specifically, when there was until now only one line for support to eu external emergencies, has broadened the range of available financial instruments. however, the new associated mechanism for emergency humanitarian assistance raises many questions about how the associated funds will be used and for what end. furthermore, it is clear that this urgency was/is created by the lack of a coherent strategy and vision to find a solution to the migration crisis at european level. this draft budget does not provide for new funds, as 100 million will be transferred from the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif) to this new emergency fund. more seriously, the power of europol and its european counter-terrorism centre is being strengthened by the recruitment of 25 more staff, on the pretext of the latest events in paris and brussels. as we know, this will not only happen by increasing the number of troops, but also by changing the eu's foreign policy of aggression and occupation.

‒ the court of auditors (the 'court') operates as a collegiate body of 28 members, one from each member state. these members shall be appointed by the council, after consulting the european parliament, for a renewable term of six years. the deadline for 6 of these posts is coming up soon and 6 new candidates have been proposed by the member states. in a joint assessment of the pool of candidates, doubts are raised as to whether they fully meet the criteria of professional competence and experience, as to their political profile and independence, as to their suitability for the specific post and as to the existence of conflicts of interest. some of these reasons led to the rejection of some of the candidates in the specialised committee of the european parliament responsible for examining applications (committee on budgetary control). the report also stresses the need to ensure that the social partners are able to take full advantage of the opportunities offered by the single market. there's not a single woman among the candidates. these are the aspects which have weighed heavily on our group's position in this vote.
‒ the court of auditors is an audit institution, which checks the legality and regularity of the european union's revenue and expenditure and the sound financial management, and exercises its functions with complete independence. in this spirit, the appointment of the individuals who make up the committee must be governed by criteria of competence and independence. the court of auditors has thus been appointed by the council on the initiative of a number of eminent persons from various eu countries. the candidate submitted his cv, answered a written questionnaire and was heard by the committee on budgetary control, and provided sufficient arguments to justify his appointment to the court of auditors in order to perform his duties therein in a competent and independent manner. i therefore voted in favour of the name samo jereb.

‒ this nomination proposal has already been assessed by the committee on budgetary control, in accordance with criteria of rigour and transparency. having received a proposal from the council on 15 march 2016 and having regard to the open and transparent selection process, i agree to the appointment of samo jereb as a member of the court of auditors, as the proposed candidate has demonstrated, at the hearing of the committee on budgetary control, that he has the necessary competence and proven professional experience to perform the duties of a member of the court of auditors.
‒ the selection process was, once again, highly criticized. again, most applicants lack the appropriate professional qualifications and there are strong indications of possible conflicts of interest. none of the candidates has the necessary level of professional expertise for the post and neither of them has been able to ensure that they would be able to perform the functions in question with the necessary degree of independence. in addition, and despite systematic requests by the european parliament in previous reports to the council and the court of auditors, there is a large gender imbalance which is aggravated by the current applications, as all 6 candidates are men. we reject all candidates on the basis of the obvious lack of independence and the likelihood of conflicts of interest, which undermine both the mission and the role of the court of auditors as the eu's independent external auditor, as well as the lack of gender balance.

‒ glyphosate-containing plant protection products are one of the preferred tools of portuguese farmers as systemic herbicides, due to their effectiveness and low cost. they currently represent 70% of the total sales volume of herbicides in portugal, being used in vineyards, fruit orchards, olive groves and cereals. the use of these is part of the farm support programmes under the rdp 2020. i therefore agree with the conclusions of the european food safety authority, which dissociates the carcinogenic potential of glyphosate from that of a co-formulant (taloamine), which should receive special attention from the authorities.
‒ the results of the european food safety authority's toxicity investigation of glyphosate are inconsistent with the conclusion of the world health organisation's agency for research on cancer regarding the classification of the carcinogenic potential of this substance in humans. a high long-term risk has been identified for almost all uses of glyphosate for non-target terrestrial vertebrates, including mammals and birds. the use of this non-selective herbicide not only kills weeds, but all plants, as well as algae, bacteria and fungi, causing a significant negative impact on biodiversity and the ecosystem. nevertheless, the european commission proposes to allow glyphosate to be used until 2031, i.e. for as long as possible, for any use, without any restrictions (except for one of the more than 500 co-formulants), subject only to confirmatory information on endocrine disrupting properties. the european commission's proposal therefore fails to ensure the desirable high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment and does not apply the precautionary principle. we therefore advocate not renewing the approval of glyphosate and establishing a timetable for the establishment of a list of co-formulants not accepted for inclusion in plant protection products.
in writing. ‒ i voted against, because to extend the authorisation of glyphosate for another seven years is to give in to the economic interests of the multinationals. when we talk about glyphosate, we're talking about a chemical that has already been classified by the who as potentially carcinogenic. however, unlike other chemicals with the same who classification, glyphosate is impossible to avoid. every day, we are exposed to glyphosate, without choice or protection, in soil, water, food and even in cotton-based hygiene products. with the decision now adopted, the majority of this parliament sacrifices the rights of all citizens to health and to quality of life, by once again putting environmental and social interests ahead of economic ones.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft commission implementing regulation renewing the approval of the active substance glyphosate, in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1107/2009 of the european parliament and of the council concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market. the european food safety authority (efsa) is the competent body of the european union responsible for independent scientific advice on food safety and potential risks in the food chain. efsa confirmed that glyphosate does not have carcinogenic or mutagenic properties and has no toxic effect on fertility, reproduction or embryonic development. therefore, and taking into account that glyphosate represents a very important tool for the productivity and competitiveness of portuguese agriculture, it is very important that the marketing authorization for glyphosate in the community be renewed for another 7 years.
in writing. the results of the european food safety authority's toxicity investigation of glyphosate as regards the classification of the carcinogenic potential of this substance in humans are contradictory to the conclusion of the world health organisation's agency for research on cancer. there is evidence of a high long-term risk, whatever its use, to non-target terrestrial vertebrates, including mammals and birds. the use of this non-selective herbicide promotes the indiscriminate elimination of plants, as well as algae, bacteria and fungi, which has a significant negative impact on biodiversity and the ecosystem. however, the european commission proposes to allow glyphosate to be used until 2031, the maximum possible period for any use, without any restrictions (except for one of the more than 500 co-formulants), only subject to confirmatory information on endocrine disrupting properties. the european commission's proposal not only fails to ensure, but also ignores the desirable high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment, and opts for not applying the precautionary principle. we therefore advocate not renewing the approval of glyphosate and establishing a timetable for the establishment of a list of co-formulants not accepted for inclusion in plant protection products.
‒ it is a herbicide widely used in portugal (in agriculture and by the chambers in gardens and roads). the opinions of experts are many and contradictory.
in the light of the recent developments in the field of the environment, the commission has decided to extend the existing measures to include the protection of the environment. i did so on the basis of the european food safety authority (efsa) study which states that glyphosate is 'unlikely to be carcinogenic to humans'. however, given the doubts raised by other studies, i strongly support the european parliament's call in this resolution to the european commission to make public, as soon as possible, all the scientific evidence that led to this positive classification of glyphosate by efsa.
‒ i voted in favour of continuing to authorise the use of glyphosate. the scientific evidence regarding carcinogenic effects and as an endocrine disruptor is not consistent. glyphosate has the seal of the european food safety authority. i do think that the arguments of agricultural organizations and of organizations for the conservation of habitats and biodiversity are consistent, particularly with regard to the southern european countries, which are more exposed to invasive species. prohibiting the use of this product would seriously damage our agriculture and the success of conservation actions under the birds and habitats directives. like any product, handling is subject to rules to ensure that there are no risks to people and the environment. precautionary principle, by precautionary principle, i prefer to apply it in favour of the conservation of species and habitats where glyphosate has proven to be a unique and very useful weapon, which has passed the negative impact tests conducted on the basis of monitoring programmes, which i believe to be rigorous. i fear that in addition to the negative impact on agriculture, a ban on the use of glyphosate would mean losing years of good conservation and habitat restoration practices.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the objection to renewal of the approval of the active substance glyphosate, as it now includes an amendment stating that the approval of glyphosate is extended for 7 years, rather than 15 as originally planned, and that the commission may withdraw the approval of an active substance during the period of its authorisation if it no longer meets the criteria for its approval. the amendment also provides for the exclusion of thalamine, a co-formulant that has demonstrated genotoxic potential and cannot be used in plant protection products, and proposes to accelerate the work towards the establishment and consolidation of annex iii to regulation (eu) no 1107/2009 on prohibited co-formulants.
‒ i support the report by mrs kalniete on the challenges for the eu in a more connected and more complex global world. the report reaffirms the eu's founding principles of promoting peace and the well-being of its peoples, with particular emphasis on the ability to anticipate, prevent and respond to challenges and threats, as well as on the security of energy supplies and the effects of climate change. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. i agree with the guidelines that arms export controls are an integral part of the eu's foreign and security policy and that member states are called upon to respect the common position on arms exports. i agree with proposals such as the creation of the format of the council of defence ministers (chaired by the high representative), the enhancement of the neighbourhood policy (and the creation of conditions for the stability and prosperity of neighbouring states), as well as the creation of partnerships with regional actors on specific sectoral issues arising from global threats and challenges.
‒ many of the threats and challenges facing the eu today and in the future are complex and interrelated, stem from state and non-state actors, and originate both within and beyond common borders. these threats are identified in the 2003 european security strategy (terrorism, weapons of mass destruction, regional conflicts, loss of state authority and organised crime) and remain, for the most part, relevant. i therefore believe it is important to strengthen structured and coherent cooperation in defence research and development, industrial-based and cyber defence, through mutualisation and resource sharing and other cooperative projects; to dedicate 2% of defence expenditure to research and to launch an eu-funded defence research and technology programme.
‒ the report presents a comprehensive set of justifications for the need to further strengthen european militarism and eu security policy. it addresses the changes the world has experienced in recent years and the supposed new threats to which the eu is subject. it calls for the overcoming of interinstitutional barriers to overcome the threats, i.e. the deepening of the eu's harmonisation and federalist approach. it advocates increased investment in the various european security-related sectors and greater support for the european military-industrial complex, paving the way for the creation of an eu military force. it advocates an increase in member states' military expenditure. it advocates complementarity and cooperation, read as subordination, with nato, defining it and the us as key strategic partners. it links the military and security posture with the consolidation of the energy union. it leads the eu's migration policy, the frontex action and the creation of the european border and coast guard. it supports the strengthening of schengen, the logic of 'strong europe' and the eu's neighbourhood policy. policies and attitudes which are contrary to the building of policies of solidarity, cooperation and peace, with respect for the sovereignty of states. obviously, we voted against it.
‒ the european union's objective is to promote peace, its values and the well-being of its peoples, while ensuring the security of its citizens and its territory. the eu should therefore ensure its internal and external resilience, its ability to anticipate, prevent and address foreseeable challenges and threats, be prepared to respond swiftly to unforeseeable crises, and ensure its ability to recover from different types of attacks, as well as safeguard the security of energy and raw material supply, while taking into account the effects of climate change, which need to be addressed urgently, and the eu should take a leading role in global climate action and the promotion of sustainable development. in such a volatile and haphazard international environment, the eu must have strategic autonomy to ensure its security and promote its interests and values. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ the international committee on emergency health regulations has declared the zika virus outbreak to be an emergency of international public health concern. experts agree that the causal relationship between zika virus infection during pregnancy and microcephaly is strongly suspected, although not yet scientifically proven. all agreed on the urgent need to coordinate international efforts to improve surveillance, to intensify control of mosquito populations, and to accelerate the development of diagnostic tests and vaccines to protect those at risk, especially during pregnancy. this resolution calls, inter alia, for specific measures to be taken in potentially exposed european regions, for communication plans to be drawn up, for investment in research into the possible causal relationship between microcephaly and pyriproxyfen use, and for other possible and complementary causes of microcephaly. the zika epidemic in the americas continues to evolve and expand geographically, with brazil being the most affected country. there is strong evidence of an association between zika virus infection during pregnancy and congenital malformations of the central nervous system, as well as between zika virus infection and guillain-barré syndrome. all the international solidarity on the part of the eu is due at this time.
‒ on 1 february 2016, the who declared the zika virus outbreak as a public health emergency of international concern. zika virus is an emerging mosquito-borne virus, first identified in 1947 in the zika forest rhesus monkey in uganda by a wild yellow fever monitoring network. zika virus is mainly transmitted to people through the bite of infected mosquitoes of the genus aedes, especially aedes aegypti, in tropical regions, the same mosquito that transmits dengue, chikungunya and yellow fever. it is important to set up communication plans at the most appropriate scale in order to raise public awareness and promote appropriate behaviour to avoid mosquito bites. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ in view of the declaration by the world health organisation of 1 february 2016 classifying the zika virus as an international public health emergency and in view of the fact that some cases of infection have been reported in the member states of the union, it is urgent to establish an action plan to prevent the spread of the virus in europe and to support third countries. zika virus is a serious public health problem, as it mainly affects economically disadvantaged women with less access to health and hygiene care and worse living conditions, and is associated with cases of babies born with microcephaly. in this regard, it is necessary to deepen and support scientific research, improve access to primary health care and prevent the spread of viruses. in this respect, i am voting in favour, because i believe that the union should play an active role in defining strategies to prevent the spread, in supporting research and in providing access to health care.

‒ on 1 february 2016, the who declared the zika virus outbreak as a public health emergency of international concern. this report notes that the zika virus, transmitted by mosquito bites, has been detected in 28 countries and that its consequences can change the lives of victims, in particular young and poor women. the report calls on the commission to present a plan for the prevention of the virus in europe and stresses that research should be articulated in three lines: investigation of the strong suspicions of a link between the virus and congenital brain malformations, development of treatments and vaccines and the creation of tests that allow rapid and effective diagnosis. the commission is also proposing that, where eu public funds are invested in research, the results should be exempt from intellectual property rights and that patients should be guaranteed access to the products developed at affordable prices. the report also welcomes the commission's decision to mobilise eur 10 million for the investigation, recommending that it focus on cases of severe congenital brain malformation in latin america and the suspected link with zika virus infection. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ in 2000, there were about 400 million internet users; today there are over 3 billion. in the last 15 years, the online world has changed dramatically. the european legislative instrument regulating it was more than 20 years old. this new regulation will make up for this mismatch. the main objectives of this regulation are twofold: on the one hand, to give consumers more control over their information and, on the other hand, to stimulate the digital internal market. this regulation will undoubtedly ensure greater respect for the rights of citizens, but it will not do away with the need for continuous awareness-raising and educational work, nor will it completely prevent the misuse of personal data. it will also undoubtedly stimulate economic development by harmonizing the rules in a market of 500 million. but it is not clear that it creates the ideal conditions for the flourishing of small and mediumsized enterprises which have to compete in a global market. in short, i certainly support the adoption of this regulation, which is a very important step, but its implementation will require close monitoring.
‒ the regulation aims to ensure that citizens have greater control over their data, to give greater clarity and legal certainty to businesses and to make transfers to countries outside the eu subject to stricter requirements. european rules on the protection of personal data - dating back to 1995, when less than 1% of europeans used the internet - need to be updated to respond to technological progress, globalisation and new methods of collecting, accessing and using data. the aim of this reform is to strengthen citizens' control over their data.
‒ this report represents a strengthening of the right to the protection of personal data, even if it is guaranteed by a unified legal framework. it proposes that the european commission should have as little interference as possible in its implementation. the new rules provide for the following measures: - improved access to their data people will receive more, clearer and more understandable information about how their data is processed; - the 'right to be forgotten' where a person no longer wants his data to be processed and, if there are no legitimate reasons for keeping it, can complain and have it deleted; - the right to know if your data has been hacked companies should notify the supervisory authority and the data subject of any personal data breaches that put individuals at risk. - the right to data portability will make it easier for individuals to transfer their personal data from one service provider to another. the proposed regulation provides that supervisory authorities may impose fines on companies that breach eu rules of up to 2% of their overall annual turnover.
in writing. ‒ directive 95/46/ec, the main legislative instrument on the protection of personal data in europe, was a milestone in the history of data protection. its objectives are to ensure the functioning of the single market and the effective protection of the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons. however, this directive was adopted 21 years ago, when the internet was just beginning to take its first steps. in the new and challenging digital world we live in today, the rules in place do not ensure the degree of harmonisation and effectiveness necessary to guarantee the right to the protection of personal data. the proposed regulation modernises the principles laid down in the 1995 directive, adapting them to the digital age and harmonising data protection legislation at european level. data protection should be subject to strict standards to restore people's confidence in the way their personal data is used. the aim of this proposal for a regulation is to strengthen individual rights and consolidate the eu's internal market, ensure stricter enforcement, simplify international transfers of personal data and introduce international standards on data protection. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the issue of personal data protection, regulated by directive 95/46/ec, was adopted 21 years ago. in view of the exponential growth and dominance of the digital world, that legal instrument, while the objectives of that directive remain valid, urgently needs updating to ensure the right to the protection of personal data. i believe that individual rights should be strengthened, that the application of the regulation should be subject to stricter enforcement, that there should be simplification of international transfers of personal data and the creation of international standards for data protection. i stress the importance of creating a single pan-european data protection legislation, which harmonises and replaces the 28 different national legislation and which should create an enabling environment for businesses, which does not hinder their economic growth and which fosters innovation.
‒ this report supports the strengthening of the right to the protection of personal data, even if it is guaranteed by a unified legal framework. it proposes that the commission should have as little interference as possible in its application and it is expected that the protection of personal data will be ensured. the new rules provide for the following measures: improving access to relevant data the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on data protection, in particular by ensuring that the data protection rules are applied in a transparent and non-discriminatory manner. the 'right to be forgotten' - when a person no longer wants his or her data to be processed, and if there are no legitimate grounds for keeping it, he or she can obtain the deletion of the data; the right to know if your data has been hacked - companies should notify the supervisory authority and the data subject of any personal data breaches that put individuals at risk. the right to data portability will allow individuals to transfer their personal data more easily from one service provider to another. the proposed regulation provides that supervisory authorities may impose fines on companies that breach eu rules of up to 2% of their overall annual turnover.

in writing. ‒ as recent events have made tragically clear, cooperation between member states in the fight against organised crime, and in particular terrorism, is still lacking. this failure is and has been particularly evident in the sharing of information. without prejudice to the need for new responses, the lack of mutual trust has been clear for a long time. the lack of information that europol frequently faces or the under-utilisation of the schengen information system are prime examples. we will not 'create' more confidence by decree, we can strengthen it through instruments such as this directive, guaranteeing minimum standards in each member state. but this directive is all the more important as new systems are adopted and more and more information from citizens is processed. at the very least, this directive ensures that improper use can be corrected or punished. it should also be noted that this directive is thus in line with the new framework introduced by the lisbon treaty, i.e. without pillars and with parliament as co-legislator.
‒ the directive includes rules on the processing of data in the context of crime prevention. personal data comprise any information concerning a person, whether it concerns his private, professional or public life. this could be a name, a photograph, an e-mail address, banking information, social media posts, medical information, or the ip address of your computer. the reform covers, among other issues, the consent of the data subject, the right to erasure of data ('right to be forgotten'), the right to portability, the right to be informed about personal data breaches, the transfer of data to non-eu countries and the sanctions applicable to companies. companies that break the rules may have to pay fines of up to 4% of their annual turnover.
‒ the directive in question is part of the package of measures proposed by the european commission to reform data protection, which includes a general regulation. for our part, we consider it important to ensure a high and homogeneous level of protection of personal data of natural persons and to facilitate the exchange of such data between the competent authorities of the member states, in order to ensure the effectiveness of judicial cooperation in criminal matters and police cooperation. to that end, the level of protection of the rights, freedoms and guarantees of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by the competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties should be equivalent in all member states. effective protection of personal data across the eu requires not only that the rights of data subjects and the obligations of data controllers be strengthened, but also that equivalent powers be conferred in the different member states to monitor and enforce the rules on the protection of personal data. the directive will enable police and judicial authorities to cooperate more effectively and more quickly, ensuring legal certainty.
‒ the data protection directive for police and judicial authorities is part of the data protection reform package proposed by the commission, which also includes a general data protection regulation. this package of measures aims to create a strong, coherent, comprehensive and modern data protection framework for the european union. it will benefit natural persons by strengthening their fundamental rights and freedoms with regard to the processing of their personal data and their trust in the digital world. it is essential to ensure a high and uniform level of protection of personal data of natural persons and to facilitate the exchange of such data between the competent authorities of the member states in order to ensure the effectiveness of judicial cooperation in criminal matters as well as police cooperation. to that end, the level of protection of the rights and freedoms of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties must be equivalent in all member states. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ the directive on the use of passenger name record (pnr) data requires air carriers to pass on to member states the data of travellers arriving or departing from the eu to help prevent and combat terrorism. provisions have been introduced to clarify the requirements for the retention, analysis, transfer and use of pnr data and to ensure the right to privacy and the protection of personal data. the new rules require air carriers to transfer passenger data from extra-eu flights (from a third country to an eu member state or vice versa) from their reservation systems to a specialised unit in the member state of arrival or departure, with a view to fighting serious crime and terrorism.
in writing. ‒ taking advantage of the legitimate feeling of insecurity caused by the recent attacks on european soil exacerbated by both the media and certain political forces the right and social democrats have made the previously rejected proposal for a pnr, a passenger identification register, be approved in plenary. in the light of recent events, the advocates of this system are using the usual rhetoric and under the pretext of "combating terrorism" to advocate the rapid implementation of the system as a way to prevent and prevent "terrorist attacks". it is to be seen whether any of these acts would have been avoided if the system had been in place. the proposal provides for the creation of passenger profiles to identify potential suspects of possible illegal acts by requiring airline data to be transferred to member states for a period of five years without guarantee of safeguarding. in practice, any citizen, european or foreign, travelling within the eu is considered a suspect from the outset, which justifies the collection and maintenance of data, which will allow, far beyond the fight against terrorism, to identify and create profiles, beyond crime, of trade unionists, political activists, among other social groups and individual citizens, serving a security vision and curtailing rights, freedoms and guarantees. we voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the passenger name record (pnr) directive as i consider it crucial to create a european information sharing system that follows common rules for all eu member states. i have reservations, however, about the final text, which was agreed and approved by the council and the european parliament, but in which many of the latter's demands were blocked by the member states. firstly, the sharing of information between member states is neither mandatory nor automatic, leaving it to the discretion of each member state to define what it considers 'necessary and relevant', which only consolidates mistrust between partners, reluctance to share information, inability to act effectively and in concert, against the very essence of what was intended by this directive. the directive also fails to cover the scope of application, by omitting the possibility for member states to regulate the transfer of pnr data in the case of private flights. we therefore run the risk of ending up with 28 different pnrs, without coordination and without a european action plan to prevent radicalisation and recruitment by terrorist networks.

‒ the nature of criminal and terrorist activity has been constantly evolving in recent years - the european union has become bolder and more sophisticated, showing an increasingly transnational nature. in the face of the high cost of crime, the data show that citizens increasingly want to see stronger action at eu level to fight organised crime and terrorism. i therefore welcome the vote in favour of this report, which has two main objectives: to harmonise the obligation for air carriers operating flights between a third country and the territory of at least one member state to transmit passenger identification data to law enforcement agencies and to define the criteria according to which those same agencies may use the information, in particular for the purposes of preventing, detecting, investigating and prosecuting terrorist offences and serious crime. the proposed system is mandatory, giving each member state two years to set up an operational system. however, member states are allowed to use joint systems for cost-sharing purposes.
‒ passenger name record (pnr) data aggregates information provided by passengers and collected by air carriers during the booking of tickets (name, address, telephone, credit card number, baggage, itinerary). they cover travel from member states to third countries and vice versa. the aim is to combat serious crime and terrorism. in an ideal world, this would be an unnecessary measure. unfortunately, this is not an ideal world. it should be noted that during the negotiations with the council additional safeguards relating to data protection were added.
‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the use of passenger name record data for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and serious crime. the directive, which is due to be transposed into the member states' legal systems within two years, will require air carriers to pass on to member states the data of travellers arriving in or departing from the eu, with the aim of helping to prevent and combat terrorism. the collective security of all of us must take precedence over the protection of personal data and i believe that this is an appropriate means of preventing, detecting, investigating and suppressing potential terrorist threats or serious crime, such as human trafficking, membership of a criminal organisation, child pornography and arms trafficking. the legislative proposal also sought to improve aspects relating to ensuring the confidentiality and anonymity of passenger data and the retention period for personal data (5 years).
‒ the criminal attacks in paris on 7 january and 13 november 2015 and in brussels on 22 march 2016 have fuelled the rhetorical debate on the introduction of the passengers name record (pnr) system. the system's advocates, spurred on by events, are strongly advocating, under the pretext of 'combating terrorism', the rapid implementation of the system as a way of preventing and avoiding 'terrorist attacks' such as those in paris and brussels. the facts make it clear, however, that none of those criminal acts in paris or brussels would have been prevented if this system had been in place. furthermore, there are no studies to date that justify the hypothetical effectiveness of the implementation of the pnr system in the light of reality. it is true that the pnr is a system which infringes the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. i therefore vote against.
‒ i voted in favour of the kirkhope report on the use of passenger identification data, which requires air carriers to pass on to member states the data of travellers arriving or departing from the eu to help prevent and combat terrorism, because it is a compromise between the right to security and the right to privacy of citizens. this data consists of information provided by passengers and collected by air carriers when booking tickets, such as name, address, telephone number, credit card number, luggage, travel itinerary, (there are 19 categories of data listed in an annex to the directive). the new rules require air carriers to transfer passenger data from extra-eu flights (from a third country to an eu member state or vice versa) from their reservation systems to a specialised unit in the member state of arrival or departure, with a view to fighting serious crime and terrorism.
madam president, i find it shameful that, 11 days after the panama scandal, the panama papers, this house has passed a directive that makes life even easier for multinationals and much harder for whistleblowers, journalists and citizens. the reason is that this directive not only protects the specific interests of multinationals, but it also completely changes the burden of proof, placing it on the side of journalists and whistleblowers. it also makes it harder to access information. so after lux leaks, swiss leaks, the panama papers, we may never see any of these scandals again, because those who turn what is public information into public information are now criminalized and fined. i would say, madam president, that intellectual property is already protected. so we didn't have to go into trade secrets, because they're all about information, and in that sense we're a little bit poorer in our democracy.
‒ trade secrets play an important role in protecting the exchange of knowledge between companies, especially smes, and research institutions within the internal market in the context of research and development and innovation. trade secrets are particularly important for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) and start-ups, which often lack the expertise and financial power to obtain, manage, enforce and defend intellectual property rights. i support the le grip report because i believe that it is legitimate to protect trade secrets and that this new instrument will bring legal clarity and a level playing field to all european companies, increasing their interest in developing research and innovation activities and deterring the illegal disclosure of trade secrets. i welcome the fact that a balanced text has been reached which does not prejudice fundamental rights and freedoms, the public interest, in particular public safety, consumer protection, public health, environmental protection, worker mobility and journalistic information/investigation. the whistleblower will also enjoy adequate protection.
‒ protection against the unlawful acquisition, disclosure and use of trade secrets is essential to allowing a fair business environment for businesses. however, companies are more interested in sharing trade secrets than in keeping them confidential. transparency and access to information are also necessary to inform important public policies, such as those on the environment, health and consumer protection. i therefore believe that a fair balance must be struck between not allowing complaints of improper acquisition or misuse of trade secrets and preventing information which is to be shared and exchanged from being kept secret by overly broad protection.
‒ this directive aims to protect knowledge and trade secrets from unlawful use, acquisition and disclosure, in particular by protecting companies and non-commercial research institutions. the proposal states that investment in intellectual capital generates competitiveness and innovative performance in the market and thus enhances financial returns, which is one of the fundamental motives of research. if there is no safety in this process, it is argued, innovation would be impeded. we are talking about protecting small and mediumsized enterprises, when we know that the safeguarding of commercial secrecy and the extension of its scope serve above all the large economic groups. the trade secret is absolute, and everything must be subject to it, even legal proceedings. all in the defense of the supreme interests of capital. the role of this directive in promoting the digital single market is, of course, mentioned. the commission proposal is not improved by the european parliament's amendments, which essentially confirm the logic of subsidizing the economic and financial interests of large companies, while disregarding the rights, freedoms and guarantees of workers, consumers and citizens in general. none of the positions fully guarantees the safeguarding of the rights of workers, whistleblowers, journalists. they do not guarantee the rights of citizens, their health or the environment. we voted against it.
‒ europe has the assets to become a world leader in science and innovation. achieving scientific quality is not only the goal of researchers, it is also a source of important gains for both the public and private sectors. however, business investment in research and development (r & d) is insufficient compared to that in its major trading partners, notably the united states and japan. insufficient investment by enterprises in r&d hampers the introduction of new products, processes, services and know-how. it is therefore desirable to improve the conditions for innovative activities by enterprises. as part of its wider strategy 'europe 2020', the commission has committed to creating an innovation union to protect knowledge-based investments, reduce cost fragmentation and make europe a more rewarding place for innovation. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the protection of know-how and confidential information must be protected, as they provide a competitive advantage for the companies that create or hold the knowledge. companies value this know-how and confidential information in the same way as they value patents and other forms of intellectual property rights, and use confidentiality as a tool for managing business competitiveness and research innovation. i am in favour of the creation of rules aimed at harmonising and standardising national legal systems in order to ensure a sufficient and consistent level of redress in the internal market in the event of the unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure of a trade secret. it should be noted that member states should respect the safeguards laid down in this directive when designing the combination of criminal and civil and commercial measures in order to ensure an appropriate balance between the protection of trade secrets and the freedoms of establishment, expression and information.

in writing. ‒ this directive lays down rules on the protection against the unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure of know-how and confidential business information (trade secrets). businesses and non-commercial research institutions invest in the acquisition, development and application of know-how and information, which are the currency of the knowledge economy and provide a competitive advantage. this investment in the generation and application of intellectual capital determines their competitiveness and innovative performance in the market and, consequently, their return on investment. i welcome the positive vote on this directive because, apart from the above, it will not affect the freedom of movement of workers or the freedom of establishment. it is essential to raise awareness, especially among smes, of the possibility of recourse and redress in the event of the unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure of trade secrets.

‒ i supported the european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of know-how and confidential business information (trade secrets) against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure. in the era of globalisation, with increased exposure of trade secrets to theft, espionage and other techniques of misappropriation, it is important to create conditions for enhanced protection of trade secrets, which are a highly relevant component for small and medium-sized enterprises, as well as for those in their start-up phase and which lack protection of their intellectual property rights. more broadly, this proposal is part of the commitment to create a single market in intellectual property, which is solid, coherent, effective in legal clarity and on equal terms for all european companies, defending their legitimate trade secrets more effectively throughout the european union, without endangering the public interest and security or infringing the rights, fundamental freedoms and protection of consumers.

‒ the revenue and expenditure forecast of the european parliament's budget for 2017 has security and cybersecurity, the phasing out of the irish language derogation, ongoing measures to give meps more means to fulfil their mandate and to make parliament attractive to the public and visitors as its main objectives. the amount proposed for implementation is eur 1 910 073 000, representing an overall increase of 3,9% over the 2016 budget, of which 1,7% is considered as ordinary expenditure. the overall increase is further justified by the additional extraordinary investments of eur 47,6 million to strengthen security and cybersecurity, corresponding to 2,6% of the overall increase.

in the light of the recent events in turkey, the european parliament has adopted a resolution on the situation in turkey. the resolution points to the undeniable backsliding in respect for democracy and the rule of law, deplores the backsliding in the area of freedom of expression and opinion, underlines that turkey is the country with the highest number of journalists in detention, is concerned about the increase in corruption (highlighted by transparency international), condemns the use of anti-terrorism legislation to settle scores and unlawful pressure on the opposition and is alarmed at the high levels of violence against women, among many other aspects. however, the resolution expresses an optimistic view of the possibility of turkey joining the eu, which i cannot follow at the moment, and i shall therefore abstain in the final vote.
‒ accession negotiations with turkey were opened on 3 october 2005, but their outcome remains open. the country has committed itself to respect the copenhagen criteria, to undertake appropriate and effective reforms and to progressively align with the eu acquis. however, the report notes the backsliding in respect for democracy and the rule of law in turkey, the considerable slowdown in the overall pace of reforms in recent years and the backsliding in certain areas such as the independence of the judiciary, freedom of assembly and expression and respect for human rights. i therefore believe that the commission should reassess the way in which the negotiations have been conducted to date and how relations and cooperation between the eu and turkey can be improved and intensified.
‒ we note in this report the more careful and subtle tone with which the accession process is approached. a demonstration of the hypocrisy with which both are treated in terms of their geostrategic and political relevance. the european union is also calling for the immediate release of all political prisoners, including those who have been held in custody for more than two years. this resolution praises and accepts it, whitewashing it with apparent 'concerns'. we recall that progress in these negotiations was the bargaining chip for the conclusion of the agreement. an agreement that is implemented with criminal actions by both the eu and turkey, in clear conflict with international law. the text omits issues such as state terrorism, the conflict with the kurds, or support for the so-called islamic state in syria. the resolution does, however, set out some guidelines for the need to resolve the conflict in cyprus, which still has part of its territory occupied by turkish military forces, a perspective which could contribute to the necessary and hoped for reunification of cyprus, and which we support and value. however, in view of the other provisions of the report, we voted against.
‒ turkey has been the constant target of several terrorist attacks by the self-proclaimed islamic state in recent months. the continuing war in syria has led to a steady influx of refugees into the country, which makes a structured policy towards them necessary. according to unhcr figures, turkey is currently hosting the largest refugee population in the world, some 2.7 million. this solidarity and effort must be shared by all countries and an integration policy appropriate to the vulnerability of refugees must be pursued at multilateral level. despite turkey's important role in trying to achieve a certain stability in the region, i note certain setbacks in respect for democracy and the rule of law, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. i believe that the dialogue between the union and turkey must continue to call for the necessary efforts to ensure the application of a rule of law which respects human dignity and promotes adequate human development.

‒ the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion in the eu has been increasing in recent years, standing at 122.6 million. in 2013, 16,7% of the eu population were at risk of poverty after social transfers, 9,6% were in severe material deprivation and 10,7% of households were in the category 'very low labour intensity'. the report also found that 10% of eu citizens were in arrears on their utility bills, 12% of eu citizens were unable to keep their homes adequately heated and 16% of the eu population lived in homes with leaky roofs and damp walls. i agree that an integrated strategy to combat the various forms of poverty must be adopted, through a holistic approach linking economic, labour, education, energy and transport policies with social policies based on best practice.
‒ the increase of 5 million in the number of people at risk of poverty between 2008 and 2013, to a total of 122.6 million people across the european union, is very significant. the number of people with severe material deprivation has increased to 45 million, as has the number of people who cannot cope with unexpected expenses. the report focuses in this context on the hardships faced by households, unable to cope with the burden of household electricity, gas and water, which have increased significantly in recent years as a result of privatisation, liberalisation and deregulation. this situation has a particular impact on the elderly and children, because of the inability of certain households to pay for heating, with the disastrous consequences that result. the report suggests a range of support measures: reducing energy bills and investing in savings measures; guaranteeing a minimum income for every person; and increasing eu funds for the fight against poverty and social inclusion. it also stresses the importance of access to public services and the inalienable right to water. despite a framework that is not distinct from the eu's macroeconomic policies, the report has essentially positive aspects.
‒ the cost of basic and essential goods and services has risen rapidly in recent years in many eu countries, resulting in an increase in household overheads. there are groups more vulnerable to this increase, such as single-parent families, older women, migrant women and people with disabilities. it is important to note that the number of people at risk of or in poverty or social exclusion has increased, despite the europe 2020 strategy's objective of reducing the number of people in this category by at least 20 million. i believe that the eu, like the member states, should redouble its efforts to combat poverty and social exclusion by creating a uniform, holistic strategy against the various forms of poverty.
