in writing. ‒ between 2008 and 2013, the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion in the eu increased from 117 to 122.6 million people. this report states that one way to contribute to solving the problem is through energy saving and improved efficiency in housing. in 2015, 10% of eu citizens had late payments on their utility bills; in 2014, 12% of eu citizens could not keep their home adequately heated and 16% of the eu population lived in homes with leaky roofs and damp walls. the report invites the commission to carry out an impact assessment of minimum income systems in the eu and to consider further measures taking into account the economic and social circumstances of each member state. it also called for more effective use of the european structural and investment funds by national, regional and local authorities and invited the commission and the member states to hold a summit on poverty reduction, extreme poverty, social exclusion and access to a decent life. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ poverty levels in the eu are unacceptably high. the increase in poverty is directly linked to the financial crisis and the resulting austerity policies. the commission and the member states must now work towards the anti-poverty objectives. a minimum income above 60% of the national average wage in all member states and an energy observatory (for energy poverty) are some of the measures envisaged.
‒ the report focuses on the hardships faced by households in the current context of poverty, unable to cope with housing costs, particularly electricity, gas and water (which have been increasing as a result of privatisation and deregulation). the report calls for a number of support measures: reducing energy expenditure and investing in energy saving measures; guaranteeing a minimum income for each person; and increasing eu funds for the fight against poverty and social inclusion. it also mentions the importance of access to public services and the right to water as something that can be transferred. the report is therefore considered to have essentially positive elements, notwithstanding the framework (europe 2020, european semester), but not valued as such throughout the framework. the group proposes a vote in favour, and it is proposed that we also vote in favour.
‒ micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (msmes) are the backbone of all market economies, but face much heavier regulatory burdens in developing countries than in the european union. the private sector is the engine of wealth creation and economic growth in all market economies, generating 90% of jobs and incomes in developing countries; it also accounts for 84% of gdp in developing countries and has the capacity to create a sustainable basis for domestic resource mobilisation, reducing inequalities. i therefore agree that private investment in developing countries, if properly regulated, can contribute to the achievement of the un sustainable development goals, and the commission should remain engaged in the 2030 agenda discussions, while recognising the diversity of the private sector and the challenges to reducing poverty for the most marginalised and hard-to-reach.
‒ overall, the report shows a greater concern with creating favourable conditions for businesses in developing countries than with supporting sovereign development free from the constraints of 'the outstretched hand'. there is also an unmistakable neocolonialist and neoliberal vision. public-private partnerships (ppps) are emerging as an inevitability, with the need to extend them to more sectors of activity being affirmed. in other words, the idea is to export (impose?) a development model based on the anti-social and neoliberal policies implemented in the european union. although some improvements were made in the course of the debate on the report, it is a bad report. here are some of the ideas it contains: - smes face too heavy a regulatory burden in developing countries (we add: compromising business opportunities for european companies); - ppps have been concentrated in the energy, infrastructure and telecommunications sectors, while the potential of sectors such as agriculture, education, green technologies, research and innovation, healthcare and property rights remains largely untapped; - clear and unjustified privilege of the private sector over the public sector, particularly in relation to eu support,- advocate for the 'modernization' of regulatory frameworks by creating a favourable environment for private initiatives. among other negative aspects.
‒ the main objective of eu development cooperation, under article 208 tfeu, is to eradicate poverty and it should be conducted within the framework of the principles and objectives of the union's external action. article 3 (5) of the treaty on european union provides that the eu's objective in its relations with the outside world is to contribute to sustainable development, solidarity and mutual respect, free and fair trade, poverty eradication and the protection of human rights, and that the private sector has the potential to contribute to sustainable and efficient development in the long term. development is primarily the responsibility of the state, the framework for development aid should be defined by governments and this task is primarily the responsibility of the public sector, but it should be stressed that the fight against poverty requires public policies as well as the involvement of the private sector, since it exerts a major influence on society and development. i am in favour of increased private sector involvement in eu development policy and projects.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european union agency for railways and repealing regulation (ec) no 881/2004. the support which parliament has given to a greater integration of the european railway area is extremely important. this means of transport makes a more sustainable contribution to employment and growth. the fourth railway package therefore aims to improve the technical compatibility of infrastructure, vehicles and signalling.
‒ the european parliament and council regulation on the european union railway agency can increase economies of scale for railway companies and manufacturers across the eu. the reduction of administrative costs and the speed of procedures, while maintaining safety levels, are the added value of the agreement. i am in favour of concerted action between the tea and the national authorities, in close cooperation, sharing knowledge and information, to ensure the proper application of the regulation.
‒ the proposal for a regulation on the european railway agency (era) aims to amend its current regulatory framework in order to define new competences in the field of interoperability and safety. the last three railway packages have brought about substantial changes with a view to making european rail transport more competitive and interoperable, while maintaining a high level of safety. however, the sector still faces numerous barriers to competition, discrimination and the absence of a liberalised, dynamic and business-friendly environment, while at the same time there are too many rules at national level, sometimes with opaque procedures and standards. with a view to improving the performance and competitiveness of the sector and the quality and efficiency of rail transport services, the commission presented the fourth railway package. this proposal for a ten regulation is the technical pillar of the ten and aims to improve the technical compatibility of infrastructure (e.g. track), wagons, signalling and other elements of the railway system and to simplify the approval procedures for wagons intended to operate on the european rail network. having regard to the council's position at first reading of december 2015, i voted in favour of the second reading of this recommendation.
‒ the documents discussed today are based on a clear political-ideological logic, the neoliberal vision of the european union of deepening the single market and its enlargement in the railway sector, eliminating the alleged technical and administrative barriers that limit competitiveness, overriding any national strategy. the european railway agency is an instrument of the federalist vision of this european union, which replaces the national authorities in the railway networks, limiting their role in particular in safety matters, in the name of the so-called competitiveness. a railway package which promotes the destruction of this strategic sector in each member state, privatisations and redundancies, and which advocates direct financing of large multinationals, in a market logic, putting users and member states to facilitate the easy profit of the large financial sectors.
in writing. the overall rail transport market share in the eu has stagnated at 6%, and according to the eurobarometer, 54% of users are not satisfied with rail services. the system provided for in the new directive will therefore bring europe closer to a single european railway area, reduce administrative costs and speed up procedures, while maintaining the current high level of safety. i also hope that it will help to increase the economies of scale of rail transport companies and manufacturers across the eu, which will improve the competitiveness of companies in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of the directive of the european parliament and of the council on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union (recast). the eu rail market has undergone profound changes over the last decade, in a gradual process resulting from the adoption of three legislative 'railway packages'. the fourth railway package therefore aims to improve the technical compatibility of infrastructure, vehicles and signalling. that is to say, to improve the efficiency and quality of rail services by encouraging the creation of a single european railway area.

‒ the european union (eu) rail market has undergone profound transformations over the past decade. the aim of these changes was to open up national markets and make the railway sector more competitive and interoperable at eu level, while ensuring high safety levels. according to the eurobarometer, 54% of rail users are not satisfied with the services provided. the commission therefore presented a new railway package in january 2013 to improve the quality and efficiency of rail services with a view to removing the obstacles to the creation of a single european railway area - which unfortunately still remain on the market. the system envisaged in the new directive will bring europe closer to a single european railway area, reducing administrative costs and speeding up procedures. it is therefore expected to contribute to increasing economies of scale for rail transport companies and manufacturers across the eu. the european railway agency (era) and the national safety authorities shall conclude cooperation agreements. it is also expected that the one-stop shop and the cooperation agreements will ensure a clear distribution of tasks between the tfa and the national authorities. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. in order to create a single market for rail transport services, it is necessary to establish a common regulatory framework in the field of railway safety. member states have developed their safety rules and standards mainly at national level on the basis of national technical and operational concepts. one of the principles is to strengthen the safety culture and incident reporting of railway undertakings and to create an instrument for the exchange of information on safety risks for stakeholders.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of the european parliament and council directive on railway safety (recast). the european railway agency (era) will play a key role in the issuing of safety certificates to railway undertakings. the era shall be competent to issue safety certificates to railway undertakings operating in several member states. any railway undertaking operating in a member state may choose to be certified by era or by a national safety authority.
‒ the single european railway area needs a common regulatory framework in the field of railway safety. directive 2004/49/ec on safety on the community's railways was a major step forward in establishing a common regulatory framework for railway safety. the directive established a framework for the harmonisation of safety standards, safety certification of railway undertakings, the tasks and functions of safety authorities and accident investigation in order to discourage member states from continuing to establish their own safety rules and standards based on national technical and operational concepts. however, the safety certification was left to the individual member states. although it has always been set as a long-term objective, i am in favour of the creation of a single safety certificate at eu level. i think it is essential that the era and the national authorities work closely together, sharing information and knowledge, to ensure that these measures are implemented.

‒ to create a single market for rail transport services, a common regulatory framework in the field of railway safety is necessary. member states have developed their safety rules and standards mainly at national level, based on their own technical and operational concepts. divergent principles, approaches and different cultures have also made it difficult to remove technical obstacles and to create (true) european transport services. the main objective of the commission proposal for the review of directive 2004/49/ec was to propose the transition to a single community safety certificate to replace the previously existing dual certificate system. railway undertakings and infrastructure managers should strengthen safety practices and reporting of incidents - which will have to be carried out in confidential conditions. the european railway agency (era) may establish an instrument for the exchange of information on safety risks for stakeholders, facilitating the cross-border exchange of this information in the event of a safety risk. for the reasons i have explained, i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.

in writing. the manipulation of libor and foreign exchange benchmarks, as well as the alleged manipulation of other indices, has highlighted the importance of benchmarks and their vulnerabilities. i agree with the need to strengthen governance systems and standards; increase transparency through greater availability to users of all benchmarks; and maintain the supply of and access to a wide variety of benchmarks through the application of governance requirements in a proportionate manner.
‒ given the importance of benchmarks in the framework of financial instruments and contracts for the smooth functioning and stability of financial markets, as well as of commodities and the economy in general, i have voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on indices used as benchmarks in the framework of financial instruments and contracts.
‒ the manipulation of libor and foreign exchange benchmarks, as well as the alleged manipulation of other indices, has highlighted the importance of benchmarks and their vulnerabilities. the current legal framework requires a more comprehensive approach, so that it does not simply recognise the illegality of such acts. it should be noted that the stability and efficiency of markets and the general economy also require that legislative action avoid restricting, as far as possible, the number and variety of benchmarks offered and used in the union. i advocate strengthening governance systems and standards, in particular for widely used and systemically important benchmarks, reducing their vulnerability to manipulation and abuse, enhancing transparency by making all benchmarks more widely available to users to enable informed decisions, and maintaining the supply of and access to a wide range of benchmarks through the application of proportionate governance requirements.
in writing. ‒ a benchmark is an index that is used as a reference price in financial instruments or contracts. the most well-known examples are benchmark interest rates such as euribor and libor, which are used in the calculation of interest rates on loans and deposits with an associated remuneration. the manipulation of these benchmark rates, as well as the alleged manipulation of other indices, has highlighted the importance of benchmarks and their vulnerabilities. in response to these revelations, amendments to eu market abuse legislation have been proposed to clarify that such manipulation of benchmarks is illegal and to incorporate this matter into the framework of criminal law. the fact that the production of benchmarks continues to be in the hands of private individuals (and not in the hands of public authorities) means that the problems of manipulation and conflicts of interest persist. the increasing liberalization of the economy and society increases their vulnerability to manipulation. we do not follow the illusion that it is possible to draw up rules to discipline the agents. the problem lies in the intrinsic nature of capitalism and only the subordination of economic power to political power through public control of key sectors can solve the problem.
in writing. this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts introduces a common framework to ensure the accuracy, transparency and comparability of indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts in the union. the political agreement on this new framework was reached in the trilogue in november 2015 and technical work has since been carried out to finalise the corresponding texts. with this agreement, the eu is setting a standard which we hope will become a global benchmark. the new regulation will improve the management of eu-produced and eu-used benchmarks in financial instruments such as bonds, shares, futures and swaps. i voted in favour of this resolution because i agree with the objectives proposed by this legislative resolution of the european parliament.
‒ the recent scandals of manipulation of interest rate benchmarks such as libor and euribor, as well as allegations of manipulation of energy, oil and foreign exchange benchmarks, demonstrate that these can be subject to conflicts of interest. the increasing liberalization of the economy and society increases their vulnerability to manipulation. failures in the accuracy and integrity of, or doubts about, the indices used as benchmarks can undermine market confidence, cause harm to consumers and investors, and distort the real economy. we do not follow the illusion that it is possible to draw up rules to discipline the agents. the problem lies in the intrinsic nature of capitalism and only the subordination of economic power to political power through public control of key sectors can solve the problem.

‒ on the basis of the information contained in this report, i shall vote in favour of giving the european ombudsman discharge in respect of the implementation of his budget for the financial year 2014. i would argue that the comments/suggestions made should be taken into account in the future.
‒ the european ombudsman is a body of the european union which monitors the way in which the european union administration carries out its tasks. it investigates complaints concerning maladministration in the activities of the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the european union, with the exception of the court of justice of the european union, in the exercise of its judicial functions. the ombudsman may consider that there is maladministration if an institution fails to respect fundamental rights, legal rules and principles, or the principles of good administration. this report aims to approve the discharge for the financial year 2014 for this body. the report is accompanied by a resolution which deals with technical and financial questions relating to the rate of implementation of the budget, payment appropriations, and so on. it also comments on the high number of cases to be resolved, including those of polish and spanish nationals, concerns about the very low level of satisfaction among officials, the need to reduce travel costs to strasbourg, the lack of discretion in recruiting staff and the progress to be made on the balance between nationalities and gender. it calls for a report on translation issues.

in writing. ‒ i am pleased to see that the accounts of the european data protection supervisor have been found to be correct and that the rate of implementation of its budget is about 92%, an improvement on the previous year. i would, however, like to stress, as the rapporteur does, the need for greater transparency in recruitment policy and the importance of detailed and specific information on the expenditure of your staff on missions. i also regret to reiterate the need to develop an internal policy on whistleblowing. i therefore support this report.
‒ all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be subject to strict supervision by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, as assessed by the audits known to us, we can say that the institutions concerned are making the right use of the funds made available and are meeting the objectives proposed. it is in this sense that the vote in favour of the report by the data protection authority is appropriate.

‒ the european police college (cepol) is an agency of the european union designed to provide police officers with training and learning opportunities on issues essential to the security of the eu and its citizens. training covers topics ranging from leadership issues to enforcement techniques and eu cooperation to economic crime. its activities aim to facilitate the sharing of knowledge and good practice and to contribute to the development of a common european culture in the field of law enforcement. the european police academy aims to be recognised by law enforcement and education agencies and authorities as a key source of learning and development in the field of education and training with a view to strengthening police cooperation and protection in europe. cepol also collaborates with other related union agencies, including europol, frontex and eurojust, and other international organisations, such as interpol, to ensure a strong collective response against the main threats to our security. on the basis of the basic questions which govern the existence of this agency, we voted against.

in writing. ‒ easa is responsible for the certification of aircraft and pilots at union level. it is a service which should be provided by the aviation authorities of the member states, in respect of the strategic sovereignty of the people, and which is fully integrated into the single european sky strategy. in this report, parliament gives easa discharge for the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2014, which means that the agency has complied with the european regulations on budget implementation and closes its budget. the court of auditors' report finds that there are no significant errors. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the actual implementation of the budget. the report does not raise any issues related to easa and the financial year in question. in view of the above, it is understood that the increase in the budget and the enhancement of the agency take away capacities from the national authorities and are therefore considered to be contrary to the national interests, of the agents and of the users.

‒ the eba aims to ensure consistent and effective prudential regulation and supervision throughout the european banking sector. the commission notes that the bank's capital needs are not limited to the capital needs of the banking sector, but also to the capital needs of the banking sector. by creating the illusion that the problems that caused the financial crisis of 2007/2008 are solved, the esfs has not changed the underlying issue of financial speculation, as it has not put a cap on derivatives markets and tax havens and has not instituted the separation of commercial and investment banking. history will show that the creation of these european authorities was not worth it. for these reasons, we went against the institution of this system and its authorities. we voted against the discharge for the implementation of the budget of this authority.
‒ the three authorities are part of the european system of financial supervision (esfs). the eba aims to ensure consistent and effective prudential regulation and supervision throughout the european banking sector. the commission notes that the bank's capital needs are not limited to the capital needs of the banking sector, but also to the capital needs of the banking sector in general. eiopa aims to support the stability of the financial system and the transparency of financial markets and products. it also seeks to protect policyholders and members and beneficiaries of pension schemes. esma aims to safeguard the stability of the eu financial system by ensuring the integrity, transparency, efficiency and orderly functioning of securities markets and by enhancing investor protection. by creating the illusion that the problems that caused the financial crisis of 2007/2008 are solved, the esfs has not changed the underlying issue of financial speculation, as it has not put a cap on derivatives markets and tax havens and has not instituted the separation of commercial and investment banking. history will show that the creation of these european authorities was not worth it. for these reasons, we have opposed the establishment of this system and its authorities. we voted against the discharge for the implementation of the budget of this authority.

‒ the implementation of control and inspection measures relating to the implementation of the common fisheries policy (cfp) in their respective exclusive economic zones should be a responsibility of the member states, which should be provided with adequate and sufficient means for this purpose, to which the eu should contribute. we do not deny the need for cooperation, coordination and coordination between the various member states in the control and combating of illegal fishing, but we were sceptical about the added value of the creation of this agency, because we believe that some of its powers clash with the competences of the member states. this is a centralisation which, moreover, does not contribute to the necessary effectiveness of control activities. we also expressed our disagreement with the representativeness of the agency's management board, its operating model and the excessive weight the european commission assumes in it, particularly in the voting system. the aecp was allocated a budget of eur 9 217 150 in 2014, which could have been used to support member states in financing control activities.

‒ eurojust's mission is to strengthen the effectiveness of national authorities responsible for investigating and prosecuting serious crossborder and organised crime and to bring criminals to justice swiftly and effectively. the objective that eurojust aims to achieve is to play a leading role and to be the centre of expertise at judicial level with a view to effective action against transnational organised crime in the european union. eurojust's work is based on a close relationship with its partners, which can be national authorities as well as european union bodies such as the european judicial network, europol, olaf (for crimes affecting the financial interests of the european union), frontex, sitcen, cepol and the european judicial training network, in addition to other bodies with competence under the provisions of the treaties. we voted against it.

‒ the report calls for an improvement in the fight against corruption. it calls for internal control of the functioning of the agency. the last audit identified no major problems, only three recommendations considered important. it called for further work to ensure that budgetary executions are efficient and in line with european standards. we are against europol for a number of reasons, including the possibility that 'the processing of special categories of data relating to ethnic or racial origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, party or trade union membership, sexual orientation or health' may not be excluded, the failure to adopt safeguards for the protection of personal data processed in the context of police and judicial cooperation at eu level and in relation to third countries, in particular the us (for example, data on air passengers), the failure to guarantee access by a citizen to data concerning him or her or even to find out whether his or her personal data are being processed by europol, and the failure to clarify the control by national parliaments.

‒ the fundamental rights agency (fra) is a european union agency that provides the eu institutions and member states with 'independent' and reasoned assistance and expertise in the field of fundamental rights. the fra is an 'independent body' of the eu, funded by the union budget. this report aims to approve the discharge for the financial year 2014 for this agency. the report is accompanied by a resolution addressing technical/budgetary aspects. what is important here is the character of this agency, which is not independent in any way, whose view on fundamental rights is the view of the european union, the same institution that constantly violates the fundamental rights of citizens in various countries in the world. it is an instrument which is used to promote eu intervention in third countries. the eu has a role to play in the fight against terrorism, and the eu is committed to the principle of non-refoulement. that is why, in line with our action in favour of the great causes of freedom, the fundamental rights and guarantees of citizens, social progress, peace and solidarity among all peoples, we voted against.

‒ frontex promotes, coordinates and develops the management of the european union's borders in accordance with community legislation. this report aims to approve the discharge for the financial year 2014 for this agency. the report is accompanied by a resolution which deals with the rate of implementation of the budget, payment appropriations and internal audits, among other technical aspects. notes furthermore that according to the court of auditors' report, it is necessary to adjust the calculation of the contributions of the third countries that are parties to the 'schengen agreement' (switzerland, liechtenstein, iceland and norway) and to take measures to align the agency's operating procedure with the proposal for a coast and border guard; we reaffirm that frontex's policy serves to aggravate immigration policy by using more repressive means. it is a fact that the european union's policy in this area, especially in dealing with the refugee crisis, has been shameful, placing various obstacles to the entry of refugees into europe, concealing the fact that, in general, these human beings are either fleeing the wars that the european union itself is fuelling, or are simply seeking better living conditions. because we disagree with the work of this agency, we voted against it.

in writing. the eib's main role as the bank of the european union is to provide financial support for projects of interest to the union which contribute to the balanced development of the internal market and to social, economic and territorial cohesion. in 2014, it financed 285 000 smes, safeguarding 3.6 million jobs, signed contracts for 413 projects in the european union worth eur 69 billion and 92 new projects outside the european union worth eur 7.98 billion. the number of contracts signed by the eib in 2014 is the highest since 2009. i agree with the increase in the capital of the eib by eur 10 billion.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the annual report on the european investment bank. the eib's objective is to support financially projects in the interest of the union that contribute to the balanced development of the internal market and to social, economic and territorial cohesion. the report focuses on the following key areas: prioritising investment to accelerate recovery and improve productivity; promoting youth employment, innovation and smes; enhancing environmental sustainability and climate action; promoting economic and social cohesion and convergence; managing the european fund for strategic investments (efsi); examining the project finance obligation initiative; updating the external dimension of eib interventions; strengthening the eib's governance framework, transparency and control.
‒ the european union is experiencing an unprecedented structural crisis. cohesion policy is no longer a reality. the budgetary treaty and economic governance prevent national states from being able to pursue policies for the development of their economies which serve the best interests of countries and peoples. the eib's results, with some eur 75 billion invested and 400 enterprises supported, represent only a drop in the bucket compared to the levels of investment required. the report is flawed. it does not provide information on the geographical distribution of this investment and the aggregation of smes with medium-cap companies, which may employ up to 3,000 people, and it does not allow us to assess the contribution of this support to social and territorial cohesion. what we see, particularly in the juncker plan, where the eib plays an important role, is that the objectives of cohesion have little weight in a european union which is increasingly serving the interests of the big economic groups, monopoly capital and the great european powers.
in writing. ‒ europe is currently at an impasse. cohesion policy died for lack of means. the budgetary treaty and economic governance prevent national governments from being able to move forward with policies to revive their economies. in short, we are at an impasse and there is no prospect, within the framework of the european institutions, of a relaunch of economic growth on a solid basis. in this context, the eib's results, with some eur 75 billion invested and 400 enterprises supported, represent only a drop in the bucket compared to the investment gap and what needs to be done. we have no information on the geographical distribution of this investment and the aggregation of smes with medium-sized enterprises, which may employ up to 3000 people, and we are unable to assess the contribution of this support to social and territorial cohesion. what we see and read, particularly in the juncker plan, where the eib plays an important role, is that the objectives of cohesion have little weight in an eu increasingly at the service of big business and capital.

‒ transparency in the functioning of the institutions is a fundamental element of democracy, allowing citizens to scrutinise the activities of their representatives. at european level, this transparency is all the more important given the complexity and sometimes remoteness of the union's decision-making process. this does not mean, however, that there is no place for confidentiality, especially when it benefits the union's capacity for action without jeopardizing the right of citizens to vote. this is the case with trilogues, which allow the co-legislators to reach commitments based on the initial positions reached in public debate. this is also the case in the negotiation of international agreements, where there are necessarily conflicting interests between the parties, which force a win-win game. in both cases, the extremes of this equation total transparency or total secrecy are undesirable. a balance is therefore needed. i am in principle in favour of greater transparency, but each case requires consideration. on the other hand, a report assessing the union in this area should be as objective as possible. i believe that this report is not without excesses, nor ideological analyses instead of factual ones, but on the whole it presents a moderate position, which advocates transparency and depicts the state of the union.

in writing. ‒ domestic work is characterised by the absence of a contract of employment and by late pay, by extended working hours without due remuneration, by disregard for the right to holidays and breaks, by non-payment of holidays and vacations, and by the absence of social security payments. it is characterized by the deepening of the precariousness of work, by labour deregulation and by the attack on collective bargaining. we cannot dissociate the plight of these workers from the increase in poverty, which in portugal already reaches 30% of the population, or from the worsening inequalities that have been deepened by the macroeconomic policies and austerity measures imposed by the eu in response to the economic crisis - policies that have promoted privatisation and the destruction of the public network of services and infrastructure for the care of children, the elderly and the sick, forcing many women to give up work in order to provide such care. this is a reality that results from the neo-liberal policies of impoverishment and exploitation that the european union sponsors and imposes on the member states. the aim of this report is to call for legislative measures to regulate the work of domestic workers and carers, defending collective employment, workers' rights, combating precariousness and eliminating discriminatory measures. we voted yes.
‒ the report on domestic workers and carers in the eu aims to ensure common regulation in all member states for those who, in the context of an employment relationship, perform domestic work for one or more households. the aim is therefore to provide workers with a social protection framework similar to the rights enjoyed by workers with legally regulated employment contracts, i.e. a guarantee of a living wage, regulated working hours, paid leave, health and safety at work, retirement pensions, maternity/paternity leave and sick leave, among others. the burden of responsibility for housework falls primarily on women, and it is a low-paying and undervalued job. according to the ilo, 29.9% of domestic workers are not covered by national labour legislation and the fact that domestic work is not considered regular work limits their social protection rights. i voted in favour of this report because i think it is essential that the eu establishes a legal framework for the professionalisation of domestic work and care as genuine work, in order to guarantee better working conditions for women who perform these functions in an unregulated way.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the kuneva report, as i consider it essential that the european union should present a set of instruments in the field of domestic and care work and introduce a general framework for the professionalisation of domestic and care work, leading to the recognition and standardisation of relevant professional skills. i would stress that in many member states, domestic work is carried out in the form of undeclared work in the informal economy, giving rise to abusive and unequal treatment or harassment, as these workers are 'invisible' and live in isolation from other workers performing similar functions and tasks. some 2.5 million people work in the care sector or in the service of a household, 88% of whom are women and immigrants. it is necessary that these workers be protected by the labour law of the member states and that they be granted a status. i therefore support the proposal in this report for the eu-wide recognition of domestic and care work as genuine work, since the recognition of this occupational sector is likely to reduce undeclared work and promote social integration.

the european union's cohesion policy is one of the main factors for the solidarity-based development of its territory. designed to tackle disparities and close the gap in access to opportunities for european citizens, cohesion policy is a key tool in reversing the cycle of stagnation into which the eu has been plunged since the financial crisis that began in 2008. given its importance, the process of implementing cohesion policy should be given particular attention by the european union. the delays in its implementation and the difficulty in combining it with other tools to support development, growth, employment and investment represent missed opportunities at a time when the eu is facing difficulties that require the mobilisation of all available resources. it is essential to speed up the implementation of the cohesion funds, to facilitate their combination with other funds and to reward good governance in the application of resources, by applying the principle of subsidiarity in an intelligent way, favouring local implementation within the framework of broader strategies of aggregation and progress.
madam president, although traceability of fishery products is required by european legislation to ensure that a given product can be identified and its production, handling, processing, packaging and dispatch process can be known, the results of a recent study by an ngo indicated that serious errors in the labelling of fish served in brussels, including in the canteens of the european institutions, were detected in about one third of the samples. if this is happening in the heart of europe, where this legislation comes from, then imagine what is happening in the rest of our union, with serious consequences for consumers, but above all with serious damage to our fishermen, who are seeing their income reduced by illegal and unfair competition, especially by simply replacing them with low-value processed fish, such as fillets, from countries with standards much lower than ours, thus paying for one thing when you end up eating another. it is essential to comply with the legislation and ensure that fishery products are traceable from the boat to the plate, i.e. it must be a continuous process throughout the entire line, because only in this way will we be able to avoid fraud and unfair competition. in addition to food security issues, care must also be taken to ensure the control and sustainability of fisheries resources, as the implementation of traceability systems should ensure the comprehensive monitoring of catches, leading to the consequent sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources. finally, we must also ensure the appropriate value added of high-quality fishery products caught with sustainable and environmentally friendly fishing gear, as is the case in the azores, where, because of this unfair competition, the commercial value of the precious species caught in their waters is not compatible with their high quality and with sustainable fishing methods.
madam president, commissioner, the european union is the world's largest importer of fish and has fleets that operate globally. this in itself requires traceability on the characteristics, origin and type of processing targeted to aquaculture resources. i come from the azores, an outermost region of europe, where the sea has high biodiversity but low biomass, and where it is caught by a small-scale fleet what some of the great chefs call the best fish in the world. i therefore feel particularly sensitive to this problem. it is the responsibility of the european union to monitor the mechanisms used to certify and identify the processing of products and to protect the quality of origin and the quality of our artisanal fleets. i should also like to point out that it was not any administration or authority that alerted us to this matter, but an environmental non-governmental organisation. this reinforces the need to stimulate citizenship in europe.
i would also like to congratulate the two rapporteurs on the agreements under discussion. as the socialist and democrat shadow rapporteur for the fisheries agreement with liberia, i was concerned about aspects relating to the transparency of the relationship, respect for liberia and the values of the european union, including human and workers' rights. i was also concerned about the appropriateness of the funds involved and about compliance with the generally established international environmental standards. the republic of liberia has experienced extreme difficulties in recent years, involving internal conflict and instability of government institutions. after two civil wars and hundreds of thousands of deaths, liberia's economy and politics are slowly recovering. i personally have never had any doubts about supporting this fisheries partnership agreement, the first and only one liberia has. for this country in the process of structuring itself, it is crucial to encourage relations that strengthen ties with the international community. both fisheries agreements under discussion here - liberia and mauritania - allow the european union fleets to expand their fishing opportunities, use only the biologically renewable marine resources not used by each country, open the door to cooperation with local industry and increase food security in europe. so you have my full support.

member of the commission. – madam president, thank you for this interesting debate. i see that there is one point we all agree on. we must not have a lost generation. making sure young people get a foot in the labour market remains therefore one of our highest priorities. this is first and foremost important for the young, to allow them to realise themselves through work, to have a decent wage that allows them to rent or buy accommodation and/or to start a family, that takes care of their professional development, but it is also important for society at large. young people tend to be better educated and computer literate. we need them to support productivity and growth in europe. delivering on the objectives of the youth guarantee requires strategic reforms to achieve more successful transitions from school to the labour market. it is a complex programme that requires time and effort in the member states, but these efforts are starting to pay off. progress has been carefully monitored within the european semester, including those country-specific recommendations where appropriate. in reply to some questions: to marian harkin: the majority of the member states concerned have effectively used advance payment and today more than one million young people have benefited from the scheme directly. however a few member states might not be in a position to have used up to 50% of the advance payment by 23 may. in that case, they will have to pay back the advance but they will not lose the money as that will stay in the youth employment initiative envelope allocated to their regions. in reply to ms pervenche berès: at the end of the budgetary conciliation last year the three institutions agreed to assign to the commission the task of assessing the progress made in the execution of the youth employment initiative this year and, taking into account the available budgetary margins, of considering whether additional funding should be proposed after 2016. this assessment is ongoing and while a few member states might be obliged to pay back the increased advance payments they received one year ago, the results obtained so far deserve to be taken into consideration in the final decisions. on the calls for more growth and programmes, let me remind you that the youth employment initiative is only a part of the solution. there are, for example, specific programmes for small and medium enterprises and there is also the investment plan. moreover, the commission has mobilised a range of instruments to support implementation, for example policy support, mutual learning between member states, outreach campaigns. the commission will report in october on the progress of the youth guarantee and the youth employment initiative.

in writing. ‒ in the context of a people's europe, it is imperative to simplify and clarify union law, making it more accessible and easier for citizens to understand, which allows for new opportunities and possibilities to benefit from the union rights that are recognised to it. this objective cannot be achieved as long as there is a dispersion of numerous provisions, amended on several occasions, often substantially. in this regard, i support this report which codifies regulation (ec) no 597/2009 on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the european community with the aim of simplifying and clarifying union law.
‒ the purpose of this proposal is to codify council regulation (ec) no 597/2009 of 11 june 2009 on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the european community. the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it. the present proposal preserves the content of the consolidated acts in full, limiting itself to bringing them together and only to the formal changes required by the consolidation process itself. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ in accordance with article 103 of the rules of procedure of the european parliament, the existing legal framework for protection against subsidised imports from non-eu countries is codified in a regulation. since the amendments are codified, they cannot constitute a substantive change and must therefore be confined to a mere compilation of the existing texts. i am therefore voting in favour of this resolution, because i think it would be good if the regulation of this matter were not scattered and consisted of a single legislative instrument.
‒ the purpose of this proposal is to codify council regulation (ec) no 597/2009 of 11 june 2009 on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the european union by means of a new regulation which will replace the various acts incorporated therein. regulation aimed at protecting 'eu industries' by establishing a procedure to apply such protection in the legal framework. it sets out measures to take account of situations of tax evasion and the influence this has on the products that are imported. it lays down provisions for the protection of state and commercial secrets. this proposal is a formal amendment to the text, incorporating a number of amendments to the legislation since 2009, and does not make substantive changes that change the substance of the regulation. although this is a codification process, we do not find ourselves in a set of references and expressions that are updated, such as 'eu industries' which point in a direction of eu federalisation, disregarding the diversity, development profile and unique characteristics of industries within each member state, reasons which motivated our abstention.
‒ considering that it is important to simplify and clarify union law so that it can be interpreted more easily and correctly by european citizens, this proposal codifies council regulation (ec) no 597/2009 in the terms considered relevant by the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission. the committee on legal affairs of the european parliament gave a favourable opinion on this subject to the recommendation of the consultative group of the three institutions and, since the proposal is simply a codification of the texts without any substantive changes, i voted in favour.
‒ according to the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, this is merely the codification of existing texts without any substantive changes.

‒ the european union's long-distance fishing fleets have been targeting tropical tuna in the gulf of guinea since the 1950s and currently obtain around 10% of their total tuna catch from the atlantic ocean. these catches consist mainly of bluefin tuna (70%), bigeye tuna (25%) and swordfish (5%). this sustainable fisheries partnership agreement is the first to be signed between the european union and the republic of liberia, which has a 570 km coastline along the atlantic ocean. i voted in favour because the agreement is consistent with the objectives of the common fisheries policy, of the sustainable management of fisheries and aquaculture activities, and is a source of great benefit to both parties.
‒ this sustainable fisheries partnership agreement is the first to be signed between the european union and the republic of liberia, which has a 570 km coastline along the atlantic ocean. the 246 152 km2 eez is home to demersal and pelagic fisheries, including tuna and related species. the main objective of the implementation protocol is to provide fishing opportunities for union vessels in the liberian fishing zone, based on the best available scientific advice, in compliance with the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) and, where possible, within the limits of the available surplus. the protocol provides for fishing opportunities in the following categories: 28 purse seiners and 6 surface longliners. the protocol provides for a financial contribution from the eu of eur 715 000 for the first year, eur 650 000 for the second, third and fourth years and eur 585 000 for the fifth year. that's why i'm in favour.
‒ the eu has signed fisheries partnership agreements (fpas) and protocols with 'third countries', through which it provides financial and technical support in exchange for fishing rights for a wide range of fish stocks in the partner country's exclusive economic zone (eez). this sustainable fisheries partnership agreement is the first to be signed between the european union and the republic of liberia, which has a 570 km coastline along the atlantic ocean, with an eez of 246 152 km2 containing demersal and pelagic fisheries resources, including tuna and tuna-like species. i agree with the rapporteur that the spa with liberia is consistent with the objectives of the common fisheries policy and the sustainable management of fisheries and aquaculture activities, and that the agreement strengthens cooperation between the union and liberia and, in general, west africa, an important tuna fishing area. i am in favour of the adoption of this agreement on the basis of the report.
‒ the report refers to a legislative resolution establishing a new protocol to the eu-republic of liberia fisheries partnership agreement. the app provides for access for eu vessels to the liberian exclusive zone, based on the best available scientific advice and complying with iccat recommendations, where applicable, within the limits of the available surplus. the protocol provides for a financial contribution from the eu of eur 715 000 for the first year, eur 650 000 for the second, third and fourth years and eur 585 000 for the fifth year. this support shall meet the objectives of the national fisheries policy and in particular the needs of the republic of liberia in relation to scientific research, artisanal fishing and monitoring, control and surveillance fisheries and the fight against illegal fishing. it is noted that the capacity development component of liberia's autonomy is higher than that of the previous protocol and deserves support. the establishment of this agreement can be a form of mutually beneficial cooperation and its continuation is therefore supported.
‒ in line with the existing strategic line on sustainable fisheries, and following on from the other partnership agreements concluded in recent years with third countries, the commission has negotiated a new agreement with liberia. liberia already cooperates with the eu through several agreements in the field of marine species conservation, voluntarily applying the standards of good practice in responsible fishing and feeding. in the same way, liberia extends its cooperation with the eu to the fight against illegal fishing and, in particular, this agreement serves to strengthen monitoring, control and surveillance in the liberian exclusive economic zone. the implementation protocol, in addition to quantifying the financial contribution to this third country, guarantees, in return, access rights to eu vessels. this cooperation aims not only at the sustainability of fisheries policy but also at the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the maritime zones of the partner countries. in view of the above, i voted in favour.
‒ this is the first sustainable fisheries partnership agreement with liberia, established for a period of 9 years starting from december 2015. the main objective is to establish fishing opportunities for european union vessels in the liberian exclusive zone, in accordance with the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas. the annual contribution shall be eur 715 000 in the first year, eur 650 000 in the second, third and fourth years and eur 585 000 in the fifth year, on a reference base of 6500 tonnes. in addition, an annual amount is allocated for access and the development of liberia's fisheries policy.
‒ the european union (eu) has recently signed a number of fisheries partnership agreements with third countries through which it provides financial and technical support in exchange for fishing rights targeted at a wide range of fishery resources in the partner country's exclusive economic zone (eez). this sustainable fisheries partnership agreement (spa) is the first to be signed between the eu and the republic of liberia, with a coastline of 570 km and an eez of 246 152 km2. the eu has cooperated with liberia under several multilateral agreements and specifically in the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. the conclusion of an ipa with liberia will clearly support the eu in achieving its objectives in the fight against iuu fishing and in promoting the objective of the common fisheries policy (cfp) which aims at the sustainable management of fisheries and aquaculture activities, which is why i voted in favour of this recommendation.

in writing. the first fisheries agreement with mauritania was concluded in 1989 and since then several agreements have been concluded allowing european vessels to fish in mauritian waters. the fisheries agreement with mauritania is one of the few eu fisheries agreements that allows access to mixed fisheries. the new protocol, which has been provisionally applied since 16 november 2015, provides for fishing opportunities for vessels fishing for crustaceans other than lobster and crab. several countries, including portugal, are authorized to fish in mauritian waters for a period of four years. for portuguese vessels, the protocol provides for fishing opportunities of 250 tonnes for crustaceans, with the exception of lobster and crab. the eu's financial contribution to the african country is €59.125 million per year: €55 million to allow european vessels access to its exclusive fishing zone and €4.125 million to promote the sustainable development of the fisheries sector and the protection of the environment and of mauritania's marine protected areas and coastal areas. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the eu and mauritania have had a fisheries agreement since 1989 and since then several agreements have been concluded which have allowed european vessels to fish in mauritania's waters. the current partnership agreement expired at the end of 2014. following lengthy negotiations, on 10 july 2015 the european union and mauritania initialled a new protocol which will allow eu fishermen to operate in mauritanian waters for a period of four years. i agree with the rapporteur that this new protocol is a major step forward in relation to the previous one and that mauritania has made new commitments on transparency and preferential access to the european fleet. i am in favour of the conclusion of this protocol on the basis of the report.
in writing. ‒ this report refers to a legislative resolution establishing a new protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and the islamic republic of mauritania. the app provides eu vessels with access to a wide variety of fish and other non-fish species in the mauritanian exclusive economic zone. the new protocol provides for an annual eu financial contribution of eur 59.125 million over four years, comprising: - eur 55 million for access to the exclusive economic zone of mauritania; - eur 4.125 million to support policies for the sustainability of the fisheries sector in mauritania. these amounts correspond to a reduction on the amounts transferred under the previous protocol, which were eur 70 million. however, this reduction reflects changes in most quotas and a more realistic forecast of catches. on the other hand, there is an improvement in the value used to strengthen territorial capacity in mauritania, its autonomy and the development of its potential in the fisheries sector. we also welcome the incorporation of 60% of mauritanian workers on european ships, implicitly with the same rights as europeans. the signing of the protocol is supported.
‒ the first agreement between the eu and mauritania on fisheries dates back to 1989 and since then several agreements have been concluded which have enabled european fishing vessels to enter the exclusive economic zone of mauritania. this protocol will allow the activity of eu fishermen in mauritanian waters to be extended for a period of four years. the agreement also negotiated a significant advance on the commitments made by mauritania on transparency and preferential access for european fleets, thus preventing the bitter experience of past years, during which the activity of european fleets was seconded to other foreign fleets. the substantial cost-benefit improvement compared to the previous agreements is also noteworthy, due to a significant decrease of the annual financial contribution of around eur 12 million. the legislator, however, increased the funds allocated to promoting the sustainable development of the fisheries sector and environmental protection in mauritania, in order to promote the environmental sustainability model advocated by the european union also in the field of fisheries policy. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ the current partnership with mauritania dates from 2006, was renewed for two years in 2012 and expired at the end of 2014. the european union and mauritania established a new protocol on 10 july 2015 to allow eu vessels to enter mauritania for a period of 4 years. the protocol has been provisionally applied since november 2015. the annual financial contribution for the authorisation of eu vessels to fish in the mauritanian exclusive zone is 55 million. in addition, eur 4.125 million per year is provided in the form of financial support to promote the sustainable development of the fisheries sector and the environmental protection of marine and coastal areas. it is worth remembering that 42.9% of the population of mauritania is unemployed. it's one of the poorest countries in the world.
‒ after lengthy negotiations, the european union (eu) and mauritania signed a new protocol on 10 july, which allows eu vessels to fish in mauritian waters for a period of four years (which will give some stability to the european fishing fleet moving to mauritania). in return for this agreement, the eu will contribute €55 million. in addition, eur 16.5 million will be paid in the form of financial support to promote sustainable development in the environmental, fisheries and coastal and marine protected areas sectors. in concluding this agreement with the eu, mauritania has made new commitments on transparency and priority access for the european fleet, and this agreement should serve as a model for future agreements signed by the eu with third countries. the balance achieved between the financial contribution and the fishing opportunities is highly positive thanks to the substantial improvements in the cost-benefit ratio. as i said earlier, i voted in favour of this report.
