‒ this type of agreement is very important for the creation of bilateral partnerships that lead to economic development of all parties. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ in 2006, the cooperation agreement on a civil satellite navigation system (gnss) was concluded between the then eec, its member states and the republic of korea. the agreement aims to stimulate, facilitate and strengthen cooperation between the parties in the framework of a global satellite navigation system for civil use. given the importance of this agreement for the parties involved, on the one hand, and taking into account the new framework of competence established by the treaty of lisbon for binding the eu to international agreements, on the other hand, the binding of the union to this agreement is of utmost importance. i am therefore voting in favour of the draft decision, since the union's commitment to this agreement is essential to ensure a stable and healthy global environment.
‒ the objective of this agreement is to encourage, facilitate and enhance cooperation between the european union and the republic of korea on a civil global navigation satellite system (gnss). this agreement, among other aspects, involves activity in fields such as radio spectrum, scientific research and training, industrial cooperation, certification and regulatory measures, trade development and security. the presuppositions of this agreement, which appear harmless, actually conceal what constitutes a step towards destabilisation in that region of the world. if, on the one hand, it is recognized that there are positive aspects in terms of scientific and economic development for both sides, on the other hand, the way is opened to a new chapter of intervention in the permanent conflict with north korea, in which we see new developments every day. in the short term, the agreement may be extended in the fields of encryption and information security (infosec), security architecture systems (space, ground and users), security control capabilities and the exchange of confidential information relating to satellite navigation (galileo). i therefore vote against.
‒ satellite navigation systems establish geospatial positioning by means of artificial satellites. this technique allows receivers on the earth's surface to determine its location by comparing it with signals from satellites. since the global navigation satellite system (gnss) has instrumental utility for the political-military services of the member states as well as various civilian uses (in the fields of transport, fleet management, science and geodesy and cartography), this draft resolution serves to approve the conclusion of a cooperation agreement with the republic of korea. in this context, the report has earned my favourable vote, which approves the maximisation of the coverage capacity of the member states, this time by means of association with korean space technology.
‒ the republic of korea is a country with high technological and space applications capabilities. it is also an active user of satellite navigation services in various sectors, including transport, fleet management, science and geodesy. the european commission, on the basis of the authorisation of the council of 18 july 2005, has negotiated a cooperation agreement on a civil global navigation satellite system (gnss) between its member states, on the one hand, and the republic of korea, on the other. the agreement was signed in september 2006 and the signatory member states and the republic of korea have completed their respective procedures necessary for its entry into force. in accordance with article 218 (6) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the commission is to propose to the council a decision on the conclusion of the agreement on behalf of the european union, after obtaining the consent of the european parliament. we are therefore faced with a draft legislative resolution which is formally largely technical and legislative in nature and, in that respect, i voted in favour of adopting this report.
‒ the apparently harmless assumptions of this agreement actually conceal what constitutes a step towards destabilisation in that region of the world. if, on the one hand, it is recognized that there are positive aspects in terms of scientific and economic development for both sides, on the other hand, the way is opened to a new chapter of intervention in the permanent conflict with north korea, in which we see new developments every day. in the short term, the agreement may be extended in the fields of encryption and information security (infosec), security architecture systems (space, ground and users), security control capabilities and the exchange of confidential information relating to satellite navigation (galileo). i therefore vote against.
‒ territorial cohesion has been recognised as a fundamental objective of the european union and enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. in order to achieve the objective of territorial cohesion, two new tools have been created for the 2014-2020 programming period under the european structural and investment funds: community-based local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti). a bottom-up approach and the involvement of local actors are essential if we are to achieve the objectives of cohesion policy. it is essential to include youth in territorial development instruments, in particular in the clld. i support the ruža tomašić report because if we harness the full potential of cohesion policy, we will be contributing to improving employment opportunities, to promoting sustainable and inclusive growth, to poverty reduction and to social inclusion.
‒ territorial cohesion is a fundamental objective of the european union, enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. the 2014-2020 generation of cohesion policy provides for and encourages the use of integrated and local-based approaches to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion as well as territorial governance. integrated and local approaches are intended to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of public intervention by responding to the specific needs of the territories and promoting their attractiveness. it is therefore necessary to define strategies in the early stages of the implementation process, in collaboration with regional and local actors, in particular at the level of specific and specialised training, technical and financial support, in the context of an effective partnership between the regions, the member states and the eu. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ territorial cohesion is one of the objectives promoted by the union, in line with the provisions of article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the eu cohesion policy framework for 2014-2020 provides for and encourages the use of integrated and local-based approaches to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion as well as territorial governance. in this context, community-local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti) initiatives are innovative cohesion policy tools and can make a significant contribution to achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion, creating quality local employment, sustainable urban development and pursuing the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. i therefore vote in favour of this, as i believe that strengthening regional and local structures is fundamental to the full realisation of cohesion policy.
‒ this report focuses on the role of local and regional authorities as enablers of regional development and, consequently, as promoters of territorial and social cohesion and as potential absorbers of the various eu funds and funding intended to promote such cohesion and development. today, more than 75% of eu citizens live in an urban context, with growing needs in terms of its political, social, economic and cultural organisation. in the european context, there are cities which, on their own, have more population and infrastructure than certain countries or regions of the union. the city context is thus increasingly decisive in the management of public affairs. the response within the eu continues the federalistic logic through direct communication between the european commission and 'the cities', without the intermediation of the member states, ignoring their definition of priorities for their regions, a view we reject. there is a logic to cohesion policies which links the cohesion funds themselves to the whole funding strategy associated with the so-called juncker plan - which aims to directly finance the private sector and subordinate cohesion policy to macroeconomic reforms. even with these fundamental reservations, it is understood that it is important to support policies that are effectively aimed at promoting territorial cohesion.
‒ the new generation of cohesion policy for the 2014-2020 programming period places greater emphasis on the use of integrated and local-based approaches to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion. in this regard, two new tools were created in the 2014-2020 programming period in order to achieve the territorial cohesion objective: community-based local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti). as a member of the regi committee appointed by the group of the european socialists to accompany the report, i managed to get 36 amendments incorporated into the final text put to the vote. i made sure that the regional and local dimension of this funding was not distorted in the document, ensuring: the necessary technical support at the level of specialised training to deal with the difficulties in the application of these instruments; the importance of local and regional authorities not taking a dominant position in the local action groups that would condition initiatives from other social entities; the adaptation of regional and local projects to demographic changes in order to try to reverse the resulting imbalances; the avoidance of duplication of coordination structures; the dissemination of these instruments to local government and an efficient evaluation of the process and results.
‒ territorial cohesion was recognised as a fundamental objective of the european union, enshrined in the treaty of lisbon - a new dimension added to the objectives of social and economic cohesion previously considered (since 1986). in this context, the new generation of cohesion policy for 2014-2020 places greater emphasis on the use of integrated and local-based approaches to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion. the new erdf regulation also establishes a budget limited to specific purposes of 5% of expenditure for sustainable urban development. two new tools have been created under the european structural and investment funds in the 2014-2020 programming period in order to achieve the territorial cohesion objective: community-based local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti). this report aims to assess the implementation of the iti and clld initiatives under the 2014-2020 cohesion policy. i consider this an extremely important exercise in identifying the main challenges encountered and in formulating recommendations to address these challenges, facilitating a more effective implementation of these initiatives on the ground, with the aim of fostering territorial cohesion in particular, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
‒ respect for diversity is one of the values of the european union. to this end, several mechanisms have been defined, one of which, geographically based, is crucial for the autonomous regions of portugal. it is the status of the outermost region. community-based local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti) are innovative cohesion policy tools that some member states will use in this way for the first time and that can significantly contribute to achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion, the creation of quality local employment, sustainable urban development and the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. it seems to me, however, that these tools will have to be equipped with the appropriate legal and financial tools and that their implementation should be carried out in a participatory manner and in harmony and mutual assistance between all the partners, but above all the european union and the member states. for these reasons, and also because some of the recommendations are the result of information and reports from the committee of the regions, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ territorial cohesion has been recognised as a fundamental objective of the european union and enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. in this context, the new generation of cohesion policy for the 2014-2020 programming period places greater emphasis on the use of integrated and local-based approaches to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion. the new erdf regulation establishes a budget earmarked for specific purposes of 5% of expenditure for sustainable urban development. under the european structural and investment funds, two new tools were created in the 2014-2020 programming period in order to achieve the territorial cohesion objective: community-based local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti). we support the promotion of this local development perspective, but we stress the need to avoid any short-circuiting between the european institutions and local government bodies that could undermine the necessary policy coordination with the central and regional governments of the member states.
‒ i voted in favour of the tomasic report on cohesion policy, as i believe that the proposals presented have the potential to generate a development of solidarity in the eu territory. i would like to highlight two tools included in this report: integrated territorial investment and community-based local development, for which some 5% of the cohesion policy budget will be used. i would stress that, because it is designed to combat asymmetries and close the gap in access to opportunities for european citizens, and because of the volume of resources it mobilises (more than eur 350 billion by 2020), cohesion policy is a key tool in reversing the cycle of stagnation into which the eu has been plunged since the financial crisis that began in 2008. i regret that, given its importance, the process of implementing cohesion policy does not merit particular attention from the eu. the delays in its implementation and the difficulty in combining it with other tools to support development, growth, employment and investment represent missed opportunities at a time when the eu is facing difficulties that require the mobilisation of all available resources.
‒ the production of reliable statistics is essential, in particular, to monitor the main economic aspects, such as developments in current accounts and financial flows, within and outside the eu. the existence of reliable statistics is an essential basis for the monitoring process established under the macroeconomic imbalance procedures. i therefore support the revision of the provisions of the regulation to increase the transparency and granularity of statistics relating to balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment.
‒ the aim of this proposal is to amend regulation (ec) no 184/2005 in order to bring it into line with the new institutional context. in particular, it aims to identify the powers conferred on the commission and to establish the appropriate procedure for the adoption of measures based on those powers. it is proposed to empower the commission to adopt delegated acts whenever economic and technical developments require updating of data requirements, including deadlines for submission, reviews, extensions and deletions of the data flows listed in annex i, and whenever it is necessary to update the definitions set out in annex ii. in addition, uniform conditions are necessary for the implementation of regulation (ec) no 184/2005 in terms of quality reports. it is therefore proposed to confer implementing powers on the commission in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in article 5 of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 with a view to adopting common quality standards and harmonising the content and periodicity of quality reports. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment statistics contains references to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny and should be reviewed in the light of the criteria laid down in the treaty. in order to ensure that statistical data are produced in a timely, appropriate, transparent and with the quality and accuracy required in this field, it is important that the commission has the necessary powers in terms of collecting information and ensuring common quality standards, and that member states provide the necessary statistical data. i am voting in favour of this resolution because i believe that access to statistical data is crucial to a clearer and more realistic understanding of economic data.
in writing. the production of reliable statistics allows for consistency and equal treatment in the analysis of economic data from different member states (ms) and is therefore fundamental to the full achievement of the european union's objectives in economic governance frameworks. regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on balance of payments (bop), international trade in services (its) and foreign direct investment (fdi) statistics is a key component of the overall eu framework and is intended to monitor economic developments in each member state and in the union as a whole. however, the increasing intensity and complexity of international capital flows has disturbed their control and tracking. this conjecture makes the fight against tax evasion and aggressive tax planning more difficult and therefore requires a legislative review of the file. in this context, increased transparency and granularity of statistics on gnp, gni and fdi could contribute to an improvement of the statistical indicators available at present. in future, the updating of the regulation, which i support with my vote, will make it possible to have a more reliable instrument for economic policy decision-making.
‒ statistics in these areas help to ensure that the economic policies of the member states are consistent with the general guidelines of the european union and that they comply with the legal requirements resulting from the eu economic governance frameworks. the existence of reliable statistics is an essential basis for the monitoring process established under the macroeconomic imbalance procedures. the revision of regulation (ec) no 184/2005 provides an opportunity to increase the transparency and granularity of statistics relating to balance of payments (bop), international trade in services (its) and foreign direct investment (fdi), as well as to take advantage of the latest legal innovations aimed at making such statistics a more reliable instrument for economic policy decision-making purposes.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. this is the need to produce reliable statistics on the balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment, taking into account developments in the main economic aspects, current accounts and financial flows, both within and outside the eu. in doing so, we are contributing to greater coherence of member states' economic policies within the framework of eu economic governance. i agree with the importance of making these statistics more transparent, detailed and reliable and stress the urgent need to update the regulation in the light of the provisions of the lisbon treaty, in particular as regards the possibility for the commission to adopt delegated acts. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. – the overall objective is to remove all provisions referring to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny from all legislative instruments by the end of parliament’s seventh term (june 2014). in the context of the alignment of regulation (ec) no 184/2005 of the european parliament and of the council of 12 january 2005 on community statistics concerning balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment to the new rules of the tfeu, implementing powers currently conferred upon the commission by that regulation should be provided for by conferring powers on the commission to adopt delegated and/or implementing acts. in addition, the revision of regulation (ec) no 184/2005 represents an occasion for increasing the transparency and the granularity of the bop, its and fdi related statistics as well as for taking advantage of recent legal innovations to make these statistics a more reliable tool for economic policy decisions.
‒ mountain regions represent a significant part (about 30%) of the eu's territory and the whole eu depends on their ecosystem services. these regions are structurally disadvantaged due to their extreme conditions and their ultra-peripheral character, to the extent that many mountain regions face problems of depopulation and ageing populations, which can disrupt the natural generational cycle and lead to a degradation of social standards and quality of life, whereas this situation is often associated with an increase in unemployment, social exclusion and migration to urban centres. mountain regions offer numerous opportunities for achieving the eu's objectives in terms of employment, cohesion and environmental protection through the sustainable use of their natural resources. it is therefore necessary to find appropriate cohesion policies for these less-favoured regions so that they can develop their full potential. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ although mountain regions account for some 28.8% of the territory, they are home to 16.9% of the eu population. these regions face a set of common challenges and at the same time problems specific to each region due to the specificities of their economy, climatic characteristics and the diversity of existing natural resources. while union policies have a major impact on these regions, in particular in the areas of environment and climate change, transport and connectivity, and in the area of entrepreneurship, these policies do not address a specific dimension relating to their condition, just as there is no specific eu policy for mountain regions. i am voting in favour of this because i believe it is essential to create and coordinate specific union policies for mountain regions in order to deal with the disadvantages they face and thus promote their sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ this report focuses on mountain regions, territories with a low demographic rate, ageing, economically lacking dynamism and which require specific approaches to promote their development and cohesion with other eu regions. some of the development strategies that could help to reverse this situation are mentioned: agricultural and craft development, sustainable tourism practices, physical and digital accessibility, development of renewable energy and protection of ecosystems, policies to attract young people, improvement of health and education services, promotion of transnational and cross-border dialogue, considering that mountain regions are not necessarily confined to one member state. these are the right positions, if they are taken in the spirit of public and strategic promotion of territorial cohesion. however, the tendency to link the logic of structural reforms and macroeconomic constraints to eu cohesion policies and funds, under the guise of a stronger link between the juncker plan funds and cohesion and investment funds, the tendency to de-emphasise the member states and their role in strategic territorial management by shifting funding and policy actions to macro-regions, or the response of digitalisation as a means of promoting de-personalized and precarious labour relations, deserve our attention and our full opposition.
in writing. the geographical composition of mountain regions is a challenge for the citizens who inhabit them, due to the difficulties arising from the topology of these territories and the peripheral context in which they are situated. in addition, the treatment given in the field of economic policy and territorial cohesion does not take account of the specific nature of mountain regions, placing them under the exclusive responsibility of the member states. at the same time, and because of these structural disadvantages (see article 174 tfeu), it is necessary to devise a specific 'mountain' agenda that favours the objectives of cohesion policy, in accordance with the principles of solidarity. in this area, i believe that only concerted action by the member states can tackle the scourge of poverty and social exclusion which is currently rampant in mountain regions. also as regards the exploitation of ecosystem services, only the joint efforts of the member states will ensure the use of available resources. i therefore voted in favour of creating a specific agenda for mountain regions and of including a 'mountain' dimension in future programmes. in this respect, i particularly welcome the proposal to increase the appropriations for the esf as the instrument par excellence for unlocking the true potential of the regions.
‒ mountain regions in the european union are seldom the focus of cohesion policy. the difficulty of investment in mountain regions, often linked to the lack of infrastructure and the additional costs of remoteness, means that they are often overlooked. this report shows that the link between mountain regions and the surrounding areas is crucial. it also aims to show how the eu's mountain regions can contribute to its objectives (such as those of europe 2020). natural resources in mountain areas can be used to create jobs and thus reduce unemployment in the eu, especially in the area of green jobs, helping to combat climate change. the variety and abundance of renewable energy sources can contribute to the eu's renewable energy targets. at the same time, poverty and social exclusion in the less developed mountain regions of the eu can be reduced with the help of eu funds. a concrete proposal is needed at the level of the european funds strategy for these regions (a smart, sustainable and inclusive strategy).
‒ the mountain regions of the european union (eu) are rarely the focus of cohesion policy, and issues and challenges related to them are left to the member states. the difficulty of investing in the mountains, due to the lack of infrastructure and the additional costs dictated by their relative extreme remoteness, usually leads to neglect of their needs. this report focuses on how mountain regions can contribute to the achievement of eu objectives, such as the europe 2020 strategy. the endogenous potential of these regions, especially that linked to their natural resources, can generate sustainable and quality jobs. the enormous diversity and abundance of renewable energy sources can also contribute to the achievement of the eu's renewable energy objectives. at the same time, poverty and social exclusion in these regions can be reduced through the use of cohesion policy. the development of many of these regions' endogenous resources can result in an improvement in social, economic and territorial cohesion, stimulating sustainable economic development. i also believe that a coordinated approach is needed to include mountain regions and to ensure that the financial allocations granted by the eu have an appropriate strategic orientation towards sustainable and inclusive growth, which are further reasons why i voted in favour of this report.
‒ unfortunately, the eu's mountain regions are rarely the focus of cohesion policy. while the territorial dimension is a matter of debate, mountains themselves are marginalised and issues and challenges related to them are left to the member states. the difficulty of investing in the mountains, due to the lack of infrastructure and the additional costs of being in the outermost regions, leads to their neglect. we accompany this report on how eu mountains can contribute to sustainable development. the wealth of natural assets and resources in mountain regions can generate jobs and improve the employment situation in the eu, especially in green jobs, which contribute to combating climate change. however, this requires public development policies clearly geared to the establishment of endogenous enterprises which can counteract the spontaneous logic of the market which tends to concentrate economic activity in the cities, promoting the desertification of large parts of the territory.
‒ i voted in favour of the iotova report because i believe that the proposed approach will give greater prominence to the role of these regions in cohesion policy. i would stress that, despite the contribution they can make to european objectives, particularly in relation to strategy 2020, mountain regions have not been an integral part of cohesion policy so far. recalls that, given their structural disadvantages and their ultra-peripheral nature, it is essential to provide additional support to mountain regions with regard to their economic development, the prevention and management of natural disasters and environmental protection, and to contribute to the achievement of the eu's renewable energy targets. i would stress in this respect that mountain regions have the potential to offer numerous opportunities for achieving the eu's objectives of green jobs and environmental protection through the sustainable use of their natural resources. finally, i would like to highlight the proposal in this report to urge the european union to develop a specific policy for these regions through an 'eu mountain agenda', which will form the basis of a european strategy with the aim of ensuring the long-term development of mountain regions and the areas that depend on them.

‒ the regulation in question applies to credit institutions and investment firms, incorporating the legal framework governing access to activity, the supervisory framework and the prudential rules applicable to credit institutions and investment firms. the proposal aims to extend the current exemptions granted to traders in commodities from the requirements relating to large risks and capital requirements. the objectives of this regulation are to prevent and reduce systemic and macroprudential risks, to encourage economically useful banking activities serving the general interest and to discourage unsustainable financial speculation without real added value. the regulation states that 'the liberalisation of gas and electricity markets is an objective of both economic and political importance ... therefore, the capital requirements and other prudential rules to be applied to undertakings operating in these markets should be proportionate and not unduly interfere with the achievement of the objective of liberalisation. we have been very critical of this package, particularly its inadequacy and perversity - the whole content of the regulatory reform carried out by the eu has been determined by the financial capital itself. the regulation determined the lines by which the regulation was to be applied to it. we voted against it.
‒ the purpose of this proposal is to extend the period of validity of the exemption of commodity traders from certain requirements laid down in the crr (capital requirements regulation). no specific implementation plans are required as the extension is directly applicable and allows the continuation of current practices. for the same reasons, there is no need to implement any specific framework for monitoring, evaluation and reporting. on the contrary, those frameworks should be implemented in the context of any changes to the prudential framework applicable to commodity traders resulting from the analysis on investment firms. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ the revision of the legal basis of the european police office had been under negotiation for some years. the guarantees initially requested by parliament, particularly as regards data protection, were broadly welcomed by the council, thus making it possible to approve them. after the terrible events in paris and brussels, this new regulation has become even more important. it is not just now that crime - terrorism in particular - has ceased to know borders. conversely, the police remained domestic and, as has become sadly clear over the past 18 months, did not cooperate or share enough information. mutual trust will not be established by decree, but it will certainly create better conditions for it. it is also noted that the pragmatism of the proposal has enabled the member states, on whom internal security still depends, to support and join. i am not one of those who consider the proposal perfect, but it is certainly reasonable, balanced and, above all, it allows for concrete progress in police cooperation at european level, which is why i support its adoption.
‒ the new regulation determines the structure, operation, scope and tasks of the eu police cooperation agency. the aim is to improve europol's governance and increase its effectiveness in the fight against organised crime and terrorism. europol will be able to more easily set up specialised units and centres to respond to terrorist threats and other forms of serious crime. the regulation, already agreed between the european parliament and national governments, reinforces the need for member states to provide information to europol and establishes a new framework for the processing of personal data.
‒ the joint declaration of the council and the european parliament on article 44 of this report aims to extend europol's powers to 'create a high harmonised level of data protection covering police and judicial activities in the union, as a way of respecting and safeguarding the fundamental rights of union citizens', the document reads. this proposal is a further step in a direction which we have already expressed our disagreement with on several occasions, by extending the scope of europol's powers, placing them above the sovereignty of the states and their competent authorities. we voted against the objectives which we consider to be pursued by europol and which limit individual freedoms and guarantees.
‒ europol's mission is to support national police services and their mutual cooperation in preventing and combating serious crime and terrorism. europol facilitates the exchange of information between the competent authorities of the member states and provides criminal analysis to assist national police forces in their transnational investigations. the proposal improves europol's governance by seeking to achieve efficiency gains, streamlining procedures, in particular with regard to the management board and the executive director, and aligning europol with the principles set out in the common approach on eu decentralised agencies. this proposal for a regulation therefore provides a legal framework for a new europol, which succeeds and replaces europol established by council decision 2009/371/jha of 6 april 2009 establishing the european police office (europol) and cepol established by council decision 2005/681/jha establishing the european police college (cepol). that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the european police office (europol) started as an intergovernmental body governed by a convention concluded between member states and became operational in 1999. by virtue of a council decision adopted in 2009, europol became an eu agency funded from the eu budget. this proposal aims to bring europol into line with the requirements of the lisbon treaty by creating the legislative framework for europol in the form of a regulation and introducing a mechanism for scrutiny of europol's activities by the european parliament and national parliaments, thereby reinforcing europol's democratic form, legitimacy and accountability. i support this proposal to give europol better governance, to make it more effective, to ensure a strong data protection regime for europol and, essentially, in line with the objectives of the stockholm programme, to make europol a vital body for the exchange of information between the police authorities of the member states.
‒ the joint declaration of the council and the european parliament on article 44 of this report aims to extend europol's powers to 'create a high harmonised level of data protection covering police and judicial activities in the union, as a way of respecting and safeguarding the fundamental rights of union citizens', the document reads. this proposal is a further step which highlights the undemocratic nature of this structure, which is increasingly overriding the sovereignty of the states and their competent authorities. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the financial interests of the european union is based on the principle of subsidiarity. the strengthening of the financing of these policies, mechanisms and infrastructures, along with other existing or new ones, and the widening of the scope of their intervention, confirms and continues the european union's security policy, which imposes controls and restrictions on the fundamental freedoms and rights of citizens, which we reject. sufficient reasons to vote in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled.
‒ the report in question is the cornerstone of the european agency europol and, as a result, is also the tool enabling the reinforcement of coordinated action between the police forces of the various member states in the fight against and prevention of serious crime and terrorism. the purpose of this proposal is to promote greater efficiency in the activities of the agency at operational and functional levels and, at the hierarchical level, to promote conditions for democratic scrutiny by democratically elected representatives, thereby ensuring that the accountability obligations laid down by the treaty of lisbon are met. the new rules include the creation of a representative of the commission and the member states within europol's management, the creation of a joint parliamentary group consisting of meps and their national counterparts, and the appointment of an executive director of the agency. the regulation also lays down the mutual obligations of the intervening parties. as regards the efficiency of the agency's activities, the new system for processing information and data protection is noteworthy, as it ensures that data protection standards are raised, without prejudice to the sharing of information, where this is proportionate to the performance of the agency's tasks. i voted in favour.
‒ the new rules and functions of europol will enable it to provide a better response capacity to combat crime and terrorism by intensifying the exchange of information between member states. the new regulation also introduces a mechanism for monitoring europol by the parliament and national parliaments, as well as a more efficient system for data processing and protection.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation underlying this report provides a legal framework for a new europol, which will succeed and replace the former european police office (europol) and the former european police college (cepol). in 2009, europol became an eu agency with the task of providing support to the action of national law enforcement services and their mutual cooperation in preventing and combating serious crime and terrorism. the european police academy, on the other hand, has been an eu agency since 2005 responsible for activities related to the training of police officers, aimed at facilitating cooperation between national police forces. i believe that this merger, in addition to bringing europol into line with the requirements of the lisbon treaty, by enhancing its transparency and accountability, will also create important synergies and efficiency gains in the fight against terrorism and in enhancing the security of european citizens, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. the regulation on the functioning and tasks of the european agency for police cooperation (europol) aims to ensure that the agency is more effective in the fight against organised crime and terrorism. this regulation provides that the fight against crime and terrorism is to be carried out by intensifying the exchange of information between member states, in order to improve europol's response, and introduces new values that facilitate europol's action, making it easier to set up specialised units and centres directed at combating terrorism and other forms of serious crime. this regulation increases direct exchanges of information with private bodies and non-governmental organisations. eurojust and olaf will have access to data stored by europol, which will facilitate the exchange of data between the different agencies. the regulation also ensures the protection of the personal data of european citizens. i voted in favour because the proposal aims at greater european integration through greater cooperation between national governments and their security agents with europol. it also recognised that the agency was essential in the fight against organised crime and that it was now operating in a more transparent framework.

in writing. ‒ the current multipolar world, with its diverse power centres, is also expressed in research and innovation. we are not alone in the world; we need to attract third country nationals. the two directives have therefore been recast and merged, focusing mainly, but not exclusively, on the beneficiaries of the two: students and researchers. on the one hand, it facilitates the entry of researchers, students and their families, and their stay after completion of their studies. the aim is to enable these third-country nationals to develop in europe the skills they have acquired here. the directive also facilitates intra-continental mobility. in other words, since these visas remain territorially limited, even though we live in a space without borders, the procedure for movements within the union is facilitated. for all these reasons, i am voting in favour of this directive.
‒ the directive provides for the possibility for students to stay for at least nine months after completion of research or studies in order to seek employment or to set up a business. the new directive also lays down the conditions for entry and residence in eu member states and the rights of third-country nationals for the purpose of research, studies, training or volunteering in the european voluntary service. the new directive also includes provisions on intra-eu mobility to facilitate the carrying out of part of the research or studies in another member state and on the right of family members to accompany researchers.
‒ this is a second reading report on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purposes of research, studies, training, volunteering, student exchange programmes, educational projects and au pairs. the report does, however, contain some positive aspects. the new provisions improve the current situation. examples are better conditions for job-search, the improvement of the mobility scheme, the creation of a job-search permit which extends the conditions of stay and the entry into the european union of family members of researchers. we support the possibility for residents of third countries to enter, reside and work in the european union, and we support that they can do so under conditions of dignity.
‒ the aim of this proposal is to improve the provisions applicable to third-country nationals who are researchers, higher education students, secondary school students, unpaid trainees and volunteers, and to apply common provisions to two new categories of third-country nationals, namely paid trainees and au pairs. its general objective is to support social, cultural and economic relations between the eu and third countries, to promote the transfer of skills and abilities and to encourage competitiveness, while at the same time providing guarantees to ensure the equal treatment of these categories of third-country nationals. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ this recommendation sets out the position of the european parliament (ep) with a view to adopting the directive on the conditions of entry and residence of foreign nationals, students or au pairs for the purposes of research, studies and exchange. the agreement reached by the various political groups in the ep was reflected in the unanimous adoption of the proposal amending the legislation in force by introducing clear and binding criteria, in particular as regards the definition of visa procedures, (mobility) rights and procedural guarantees. in other respects, and despite the reservations and reservations raised by article 20, the ep and the council reached agreement on the grounds for rejecting an application from a third-country national where this is justified on the basis of evidence or serious and objective reasons. an annex to this legislative resolution is attached to safeguard the application of this provision, in accordance with the interpretation of parliament and the council. in the light of the foregoing, and considering that the directive fulfils the dual objective of recognising and safeguarding the rights of paid trainees and au pairs on the one hand, and promoting the objectives of european action in the field of education on the other, i voted in favour.
‒ this directive concerns the conditions of entry and residence of foreign researchers and students in the european union. one of the objectives is to make europe more attractive in the areas of research and innovation, training or volunteering. we need to attract talent to increase competitiveness. the directive provides for the possibility of staying in the eu country which granted the authorisation for a period of at least 9 months in order to seek employment or to set up businesses. it also provides for greater mobility within the union and family support. let us remember that europe spends only a fraction of its gdp on r & d compared to the us or japan. this is also a good support for legal immigration.
in writing. this proposal for a recommendation refers to the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purpose of research, studies, traineeships or voluntary service, or for the purpose of student exchange projects. this directive redefines certain aspects of the entry and residence of foreign nationals, in line with the principle of simplification concerning the movement of persons into and out of the eu, only in the situations referred to above. enabling third-country nationals to acquire skills and knowledge through a period of traineeship and/or study in europe will not only encourage 'brain drain' but also support and strengthen cooperation with the countries from which these citizens come. the proposal also aims to implement rules to ensure, for example, that the citizens concerned can remain for at least nine months after leaving the job to look for a job or develop a business, which will ensure that the eu benefits from the skills acquired by them. as i said earlier, i voted in favour of this resolution.

member of the commission. mr president, mr rapporteur, ladies and gentlemen, i am very pleased to be here today to continue our debate on tax transparency, which will occupy us throughout this mandate. i promised you that the transparency revolution was underway. a new stage has been reached today, thanks to parliament, whose action i welcome. you know that the commission has been particularly active in recent months on the transparency front. last december, an agreement was reached in record time on the automatic exchange of information on tax returns between tax authorities in the union. since january, the commission and i have been pushing this revolution forward by putting two major proposals on the table: a directive on the publication of country-by-country reports on the activities of multinational companies, the country-by-country report between the tax authorities of the member states of the union. that is what we have to discuss tonight. finally, there is a proposal to amend the accounting directive to make this type of report public, and you know that this has been my firm position from the beginning. we are determined to push the boundaries of transparency further with the strong and consistent support of parliament in this work. our present work is therefore oriented in three directions. the immediate next step for the commission is to examine whether and to what extent the transparency requirements of the anti-money laundering directive could also be used to combat tax fraud. the commission will be presenting a proposal to amend this directive as early as next month. it is also considering how to shed more light on the activities of tax planning schemes - including tax advisers - used by taxpayers to evade tax. finally, we are working intensively on the drawing up of a european blacklist of non-cooperative jurisdictions. there is one, but it is too much the result of a compilation of national lists, which are themselves heterogeneous; this would be a precursor to an oecd list. i had the opportunity to speak on this subject last week with the oecd secretary-general, angel gurría, and our teams are working in full understanding with the oecd. that is the overall picture before we come to the subject of the debate. why is the automatic and mandatory exchange of information between member states' tax authorities so important? simply because it is a fundamental mechanism for the tax authorities to be able to detect harmful tax practices quickly and react to them promptly. clearly, this mechanism, as you have explained, will allow for better tax control and ensure more virtuous practices on the part of multinationals. a word, first, to explain how this proposal articulates with our international work. as you know, this is a proposal to transpose action 13 of the oecd beps action plan into european union law. this has already been agreed at oecd level and endorsed by the g20 in november 2015 in antalya. the commission's intention is therefore not to create a new european union standard but simply to implement the oecd recommendations fully. we must at all costs maintain the course agreed, avoid creating loopholes which could be exploited by the multinationals. the benefits of an initiative at european level are extremely clear to me. this will ensure a coherent, effective and comprehensive approach by the european union and will allow country-by-country information to be published in the internal market. the initiative also provides greater legal certainty for tax authorities and businesses and will contribute to the development of an international standard for the automatic exchange of country-by-country disclosure. i now come to the heart of the proposal itself. on the substance, the proposal requires large multinationals to declare to the tax authorities the tax they pay in each jurisdiction in which they operate and other relevant tax information. as regards its scope, all multinationals resident for tax purposes in the european union or outside but active in the internal market will have to comply with the new rules. as regards the timetable, the directive will enter into force in 2017. the first exchanges of information will therefore cover accounting periods beginning on or after 1 january 2016. i turn to the rapporteur, mr rosati - in fact i have been turning to him repeatedly - to thank him very warmly for his report, and of course i thank all those who contributed to it. i know that parliament would like to go further on several points. i would therefore like to take up some of the points of your work and some of the progress that has been made. first, it is planned to make the information available to the public by country. this is progress, as you know, which i have been very keen on and supporting since i took up my post in the commission. i therefore welcome the fact that the commission has adopted the proposal amending the accounting directive which provides for the disclosure of the activities of multinational companies, the publication of country-by-country information, and in this initiative the commission is working to respond to the urgent demand of citizens and the european parliament for more transparency, with a concern that most of you share, which is to preserve the competitiveness of european companies. so from now on it is a proposal in the hands of the co-legislators. we have taken the first step, it was not an easy decision to make but we have taken it, and we hope that now we will be followed. as regards the role of the commission, it may be desirable that country-by-country information reports should also be shared with the commission. the commission is not a tax authority, having no competence in administering the application of the national tax laws of the member states, and therefore cannot receive or have access to the content of the publication of country-by-country information, which is expressly intended for national tax administrations. the information exchanged should be used mainly by tax administrations to assess risks in the area of transfer pricing and to better target tax controls, areas in which the commission is not competent. the member states and the oecd also consider that sharing the publication of country-by-country information with the commission would not be in line with the confidentiality clause of the oecd agreement. so i would like to agree with you, but you can see that the room for manoeuvre is very small. another point is the content of the reports. some amendments provide for additional information. again, this would not be compatible with the primary objective of this initiative to implement and transpose beps within the union. to depart from this would be to create a new eu standard and thus a new layer of reporting requirements, thus increasing the administrative burden for multinational enterprises. we want to be honest, we want to identify fraudsters, we want to fight tax evasion, we want to limit the erosion of the tax base, we do not want to burden companies. finally, it was proposed that the commission should draw up annual reports to the council and the european parliament assessing the effectiveness of the automatic exchange of information between member states. but the directive on administrative cooperation already exists. member states shall communicate to the commission all information necessary to evaluate the effectiveness of such cooperation and an annual evaluation of the effectiveness including the practical results obtained. in addition, the commission is also to report on the application of the automatic exchange of information by 1 october 2018 and to report on the implementation of the administrative cooperation directive to parliament and the council every five years. we believe that these provisions are sufficient, that they are proportionate and, indeed, that they already meet the legitimate concern you have expressed and which i fully share. in any event, rest assured that the commission will closely monitor the implementation and impact of the directive and will propose, if necessary, relevant amendments. in conclusion, ladies and gentlemen, greater transparency, a stronger fight against fraud and tax evasion are the objectives which are at the top of our political priorities and which are very clearly at the very heart of my mandate in the commission. we have already made remarkable progress with a tight and ambitious timetable. we are helped, it must be said, by a public outcry at the successive revelations: those of last year, those of the panama papers, more recently. we must, of course, build on this revolt to move things forward decisively. i believe that your parliament and the commission are really working in the same spirit and hand in hand. i often come to this house to present the proposals we are drawing up which are the very concrete expression of this commitment. i have an ambition, and i know you share it, that the european union should be the leader and the driving force in the global fight for tax transparency. at the beginning of my speech i said that i would come to you to talk about these issues throughout this mandate. yes, it is certain, our work is far from finished. there are still key proposals to be discussed such as the anti-tax avoidance directive, the anti-tax avoidance package which is on the council table - i hope there will be an agreement on this in a few days' time at the ecofin council - and the proposal on country-by-country public reporting. i have heard complaints before. i think we also have to be aware that by doing so we will really be the first in the world to make such a proposal. it is essential that we continue to work together. i am happy to do so here in the house. i am doing so in the relevant committees, before the taxe committee, before the econ committee, because i know once again that without cooperation between the commission and the european parliament, but also without the conviction of the member states, these proposals would remain an empty shell. that is not my intention, nor yours. i am convinced that together we will really advance this cause that we share and that mr rosati's report illustrates quite clearly and accurately.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal amending the directive on the automatic exchange of compulsory information in the field of taxation. the amendment takes a further step in the fight against tax evasion and in the enhancement of transparency in the tax paid by companies by making automatic exchange of information on multinational companies' country reports between national tax authorities mandatory.
in writing. ‒ this draft directive amends directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation, as last amended by directive (eu) 2015/2376. this draft directive introduces a new article in the existing directive, which establishes the scope and conditions for the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the country-by-country report. i believe that this proposal is already an important step in the fight against crossborder tax evasion, which has been increasing and has become a major cause for concern in the union and worldwide. it is important to note that, following the reports of the econ and taxe committees, the european parliament called for greater transparency of tax information in order to combat aggressive tax planning, in particular by introducing country reports for multinational groups of companies. i agree with the rapporteur that this proposal would improve efficiency with the proposed amendments, which extend the exchange of information to the european commission and ask that on the basis of this information the commission assess the compliance of member states with the european union state aid rules.
in writing. ‒ we are facing an attempt to respond to what has become known as the luxleaks scandal, which directly involved the current president of the european commission when he was still finance minister and later prime minister of luxembourg. the discovery that not only this but also several other eu governments have concluded secret agreements with multinational companies to save them from paying taxes, opening the door to tax evasion and depriving the states of the very valuable revenues that would result from the proper collection of taxes, has generated just and understandable indignation throughout europe.
‒ this proposal makes it mandatory to exchange information between member states' tax authorities in order to identify aggressive tax planning practices by large companies and ensure fair tax competition. companies with revenues of 750 million or more are required to report by country (including the amount of revenues, profit before tax, number of employees, declared capital, retained earnings, etc.). the 750 million ceiling covers only 105 of the multinationals. the s&ds were in favour of reducing this amount to 40 million, allowing some 20 000 firms to be audited. the s&d group has tried to get an amendment to this effect through the plenary, but has not succeeded in getting it passed. however, this is a good principle for tax transparency and fairness.
‒ this report concerns a proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. in the current legal framework of directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation, member states do not yet share country-by-country reports, and therefore in the current cross-border tax avoidance environment, it is essential to promote transparency and to strengthen the tools and mechanisms established by the directive. i am in favour of the commission's proposal which sets out the scope and conditions for the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the country-by-country report and i agree with the more specific details of the reporting obligation for multinational companies, given the volume of revenue in trade transactions. in the interests of greater transparency and a more effective fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and tax avoidance, i voted in favour of this proposal.
‒ as we see the implementation of all these fiscal packages, it is clear that ambitions have been revised downwards, with minimalist measures and far below what is needed. it is ironic that this negotiation is taking place under the dutch presidency of the eu, with the netherlands being one of the most important tax havens in existence, as the starbucks scandals and others have shown. what the european commission is proposing is to follow the oecd rules by proposing a confidential country-by-country report in which multinational companies will provide tax administrations with information about their activities and their taxes. as is recognised, the confidentiality of this information deprives the measure of all its effectiveness and in particular of its deterrent effect. we therefore call on the commission to make the disclosure of this information compulsory, as is the case with banks. we do not understand the limit of eur 750 million, which exempts the vast majority of multinational companies from this measure. in short, we demand that the european union be consistent and take consistent action in the fight against this social inequality, which is inseparable from the capitalist system that promotes the concentration of wealth and social inequalities.
‒ consumers have the right to information communicated in an understandable way, including coastal and geographical information on catch areas, and should be able to have full confidence in the entire supply chain of fishery products to the eu market. however, the results of several studies indicate significant levels of mislabelling of fish products sold on the eu market, which is a violation of eu regulations. member states should therefore strengthen national controls, in particular of unprocessed fish destined for restaurants and the catering sector, in an effort to combat fraud and identify the stage in the supply chain where fish is incorrectly labelled.
in writing. ‒ recent cases of fish not corresponding to the labelling (the fish version of selling cat for rabbit) identified in various restaurants, hotel and commercial establishments justify the development of measures that promote not only a correct identification of the species concerned, but also their origin and processing conditions. in the name of product quality, of improving the conditions of fishermen and producers of fishery products, but also of consumer confidence, we support this measure. certifying the origin and quality of products is a demand of portuguese producers and fishermen, as a means of affirming national products and protecting against adulteration and a kind of commercial dumping. this certification should be carried out by a public body, free of charge, thus avoiding the obligation for producers to pay for this certification to private bodies, which are often not very discriminating. the example of the canning industry deserves special mention. we have asked the european commission on this subject on several occasions. we voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the traceability of fishery and aquaculture products in catering and retail. consumers have the right to comprehensible and non-fraudulent information in compliance with community regulations and standards, so incorrect, fraudulent and intentional labelling of fish species will constitute a breach of eu rules, in particular the common fisheries policy.

‒ several studies show significant levels of mislabelling of fishery products sold in the eu, including restaurants of its institutions. this intentional and fraudulent practice is a breach of european union regulations and may constitute an offence under national laws. minimum standards for informing consumers about the origin of these products in a simple and transparent manner need to be established. the same applies to eco-labelling standards. member states should strengthen controls, including on unprocessed fish for restaurants and catering. a european labelling policy will be a key point to boost the development of coastal communities by recognising best practice and highlighting the quality of their products.
‒ as the world's largest market for fishery (and aquaculture) products, the european union must strive for strict and effective regulation of this sector, from extraction and production to retail/restauration. however, several studies have shown that there is a significant number of cases of incorrect and sometimes even fraudulent labelling of fishery (and aquaculture) products sold on the european market. given this reality, which is a violation of community principles (and regulations), it is imperative to alert member states to the need to strengthen their national controls and to require them and the european commission to take measures to improve the traceability of fishery and aquaculture products. with greater monitoring and traceability of these products, not only consumers but also the operators in the sector benefit from the increased trust placed in the system for the extraction, production and sale of fishery and aquaculture products. i also support the proposal to set up an eco-labelling system for fishery/aquaculture products and welcome the feasibility studies to this end. in the interests of rigour, transparency and confidence in the fisheries sales system, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i am concerned that several studies indicate that there are significant levels of mislabelling of fishery products in europe. i am sure that incorrect, fraudulent and intentional labelling of fish species is a breach of union rules. it seems to me that genetic barcoding techniques, which facilitate the identification of species by dna sequencing, should be effectively sequenced, and i would stress that these techniques were developed with the help of funding from the european union itself. in other words, once again, we need to effectively transfer scientific and technological developments to the world of industry and, in this case, regulation. i believe that it is necessary to ensure that future eu-wide ecolabels and certification and ecolabelling schemes for seafood from european and third countries are consistent with the fao guidelines for the ecolabelling of fish and fishery products caught at sea. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report and i hope that it will have consequences in establishing a method for certifying certificates. in my view, this method can only have its origins in the european union.
