in writing. ‒ the european objective of ensuring gender equality - rectius, as it is a manifestly unfortunate expression, equality of rights, duties and guarantees between the sexes - dates back to the 1975 treaty of rome. since then, the problem of poverty and social exclusion has been the subject of several resolutions adopted in parliament, which still have to deal with the gender gap in the risk of poverty and income inequality. the report stresses that women continue to be more affected than men, especially when they are immigrants, pensioners, disabled or single mothers. the document also identifies the causes of this disparity, considering, in my view, that the union and the member states should strive to ensure that all men and women, without distinction, have equal opportunities in the fields of employment, social security, registration, education and childcare. considering the fight against poverty as a matter of social justice and with a view to reducing inequalities in rights, duties and guarantees between the sexes, i am voting in favour of adopting this report.
‒ the economic crisis from which the union is gradually recovering has led to an increase in the number of men and women at risk of poverty and social exclusion. some 64.6 million women live in poverty compared with 57.6 million men. women work two-thirds of the total world's working hours, produce half the world's food, but earn only 10% of income and own only 1% of property. it was a difficult vote because of the opposition of many right-wing members; however, we have managed to get important messages across, such as: the use of european funds to promote women's entry and retention in the labour market; legislative initiatives towards work-life balance for women and men (maternity, paternity, parenting); guaranteeing access to health care, education and housing for children; inclusion of social indicators in the european semester; assessment by the commission of the impact of the minimum wage policy in the eu or the introduction of a national minimum pension that is never below the poverty line.
‒ the problem of poverty and social exclusion of women has been the subject of particular attention by the european parliament for several years. despite the undeniable differences that persist somewhat across the eu - such as the gender pay gap - these are unfortunately issues that are usually downplayed or forgotten in the political debate. however, poverty and social exclusion know no borders and are not closely linked to gender. that is why i believe that we should have poverty reduction strategies that are more targeted at the most vulnerable age groups, such as children and the elderly, and in social groups or regions with problems of prevailing poverty and where there is a need to break vicious cycles, which unfortunately persist. it is for this reason, as i said in the last paragraph, and because i agree with the absolute need to combat and prevent poverty in the eu, that i abstained in the final vote on this report.
‒ the problem of poverty and social exclusion of women is a reality linked to the gender pay gap, low wages and, consequently, low pensions. in addition, there is precarious work, which has been aggravated over the last four years by the policies imposed by the troika and which has particularly affected women. despite the negative aspects contained in the report, such as the advocacy of the introduction of work regimes such as teleworking, individual and non-transferable parental leave rights or access to credit and financial advisory services to promote female entrepreneurship, we think that, in general, it is a good characterisation of the situation and calls for effective policies that dignify work and the social functions of the state.
‒ i voted in favour of the arena report, as i believe that it contains crucial elements for combating the phenomenon of 'feminization of poverty'. i would stress the call on the member states and the commission to take action to combat all forms of multiple discrimination based on sex, to ensure the application of the principle of non-discrimination and equality in the labour market and in access to employment, and in particular to adopt social protection measures to ensure that women's pay and social benefits, including pensions, are equal to those of men with the same or similar experience doing the same work or work of equal value. these measures are essential to promote the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment between men and women in the occupational field. i also stress the proposal that makes it compulsory for companies to submit equality plans, including actions to eliminate segregation, the design of pay systems and measures to support women's careers.
‒ alongside schengen, the single market is indeed one of the great achievements of the european union that citizens feel in their daily lives, especially through businesses and smes, which are the backbone of the european economy. however, twenty years after the creation of the single market, barriers to this flow remain. one of the main complaints, alongside the vat regulation, is the existence of non-tariff barriers, such as national technical rules and regulatory and non-regulatory requirements, unjustifiably applied to products, service providers and conditions of service provision, which burden companies operating on the market. i support the dalton report because it considers these costs unnecessary and a waste for the real economy of businesses, with the consumer being the most harmed in the end, as he is denied access to the national markets of new entrants, his choice is limited and products become more expensive. i would like to stress the importance of member states respecting existing rules on the single market, not creating rules supplementing the proposed directives, and i welcome the single digital gateway initiative announced by the commission and the improvement of the functioning of the solvit network.
the european union is also committed to the principle of subsidiarity, which is a fundamental principle of the european union. among other things, the report states that: - 'urgent action is needed to put an end to non-tariff barriers'; - 'the abolition of non-tariff barriers shall not imply a limitation of workers' rights, if such rights are not discriminatory, disproportionate or based on a legitimate public policy objective'; - "in cases where the ec repeals unnecessary eu legislation, member states should act swiftly to repeal the corresponding national provisions"; - 'a culture of compliance should be promoted through cooperation between the ec and the member states, as already provided for in the single market strategy'; - 'urgently resolve the issue of non-compliance by member states'; - "persistent national differences in regulation unnecessarily force companies to adapt their products and services to meet multiple standards or repeated testing, thus limiting intra-eu trade, reducing growth and hindering job creation"; - "the low number of crossborder public procurement is a problem"; - "the ec must take a firmer approach to non-compliance with the law". this is unacceptable. we voted against it.
‒ the creation of the single market is a major achievement, made possible by cooperation and a shared objective of eliminating barriers to trade across the european union. tariff barriers were successfully removed almost 50 years ago, but it is the ongoing challenge of eliminating non-tariff barriers that is currently driving our single market initiatives. this situation reflects in many ways the latest innovations in international trade, where tariffs are more easily fought, but the elimination of non-tariff barriers (ntbs) is the ultimate goal. the abolition of gnp will help businesses across the eu, but the main beneficiaries will be consumers. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the creation of the single market has led to the removal of barriers to trade across the eu. although tariff barriers have been removed for almost 50 years, the challenge today is to eliminate non-tariff barriers (ntbs), which are due to the variety of national regulations that a company may encounter when seeking to trade cross-border or provide services in another member state, meaning that the situation on the ground may be identical to the types of barriers they may encounter when trading outside the eu. i agree with the rapporteur that not all gnp should be abolished. the principle of subsidiarity and respect for multi-level governance mean that there will always be a degree of national variation in regulatory practices and public policies. i am voting in favour of this report because, for the proper functioning of the single market, i am in favour of eliminating gnp which is contrary to the principles of proportionality or non-discrimination, or which is not based on a legitimate public policy objective. the abolition of gnp will help businesses across the eu, but especially consumers, as they will benefit from lower prices and greater choice.
‒ this is another report which continues the reflection on the single market and the absolute need to limit any restrictions which may still exist on the free movement of goods and services. it is therefore not surprising that it proposes: the end of non-tariff barriers; the openness and accessibility of member states to their regulatory requirements; deregulation as a means of attracting foreign investment; further harmonisation, particularly in the digital single market, of existing regulation at national level in the member states; further structural reforms in the context of the european semester; the destruction of the social functions of the state, public services and privatisations; in short, the promotion of attacks on workers' rights, exacerbating social inequalities, labour deregulation, the devaluation of wages and the precariousness of work. we therefore voted against.
‒ the removal of barriers to trade and the creation of the european single market are examples of the success of eu action. the single market has boosted the competitiveness of european firms, encouraged joint demand and contributed to an increase in consumer surpluses through a general decline in prices. despite the progressive removal of tariff barriers, the elimination of non-tariff barriers is still an unfinished project. the different national regulations and technical requirements which a company faces when trading cross-border or providing services in another member state constitute barriers to trade which are, in practice, no different from the obstacles imposed outside the european economic area. although it admits a certain degree of discretion in the regulatory practices and public policies pursued by the member states, the report advocates - and rightly so - a change of mindset towards a gradual move away from protectionist measures, often of a sectoral nature. the document also suggests the abolition of non-tariff barriers which are contrary to the principles of proportionality, non-discrimination and the pursuit of the public interest. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ 20 years after the creation of the single market, some non-tariff barriers (national technical rules and requirements for products and service providers) continue to hamper trade between member states. the report analyses the barriers still faced by businesses operating across borders and proposes measures to remove them, arguing that they can constitute an obstacle to the single market and growth. it is not recommended that all of them should be removed, as the principle of subsidiarity and respect for the practice of multi-level governance must be safeguarded, as must the right to legislate in the public interest. however, there are barriers of this kind which are contrary to the principles of proportionality and non-discrimination. these are the ones which must be removed for the sake of the functioning of the single market, especially those with a more protectionist bent. consumers will be the main beneficiaries of greater market opening.
‒ the elimination of tariff barriers, successfully removed in 1968, 18 months earlier than the treaty of rome had provided, is one of the main achievements of the european union (then the eec). the main challenge facing the single market today is the elimination of non-tariff barriers to intra-community trade and their link with the protection of the internal market. this report draws attention to some of the non-tariff barriers, particularly technical barriers, to trade in the internal market. i agree with the rapporteur that some of the measures to avoid the use of non-tariff barriers need to be improved so that the single market can function effectively and fulfil its full potential - as stated in the recently adopted single market strategy. the aim is an increasingly open and competitive single market, and this requires that member states avoid adopting protectionist measures and that some of the current non-tariff barriers be removed in order to bring greater benefits to businesses and, above all, to consumers, who will naturally benefit from a wider choice of goods and services at a lower price. for the reasons stated above, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ we accept as valid the principle that prices cannot be compared without taking into account the specific conditions under which production takes place. what we do not accept is that this principle should serve to undermine social and environmental rights, often won through hard struggles of the people and the workers. we also do not accept that this principle should prevent national governments from setting standards to promote local and regional production. non-tariff barriers are the spearhead of those who want to impose free trade by force and without regard to the specificities of countries and regions and often without regard to their own history. in this sense, we view with great reservations any attempt to set targets for the reduction of these so-called non-tariff barriers, putting everything in the same bag and flattening out local and cultural specificities.
in the light of the recent developments in the field of customs union, the commission has decided to extend the scope of the dalton report to include the following areas: among the various recommendations put forward to reduce the negative impact of non-tariff measures, i would highlight the 'single digital gateway' initiative and the call on the commission to create a one-stop shop for businesses and consumers to deal with single market-related aspects, including the provision of information and assistance, problem-solving and national and european procedures necessary to carry out cross-border transactions in the european union.
in writing. ‒ three decades of the single market have given rise to capitalist concentration and centralisation in favour of monopoly groups, to the dismantling of instruments for the sovereign regulation of economies, to privatisations and liberalisations of strategic sectors and public services. but big monopoly capital wants more: deepening of the market, structural reforms (read: liquidation of the social functions of the state and of social and labour rights). the proposal is to link this with the juncker plan, which serves the interests of high finance and large companies and which favours public-private partnerships by injecting public resources into the financial system. or with ttip, which would liquidate thousands of smes and further attack the labour and social rights of workers. the risk capital and financial products that were at the origin of the 2008 financial crisis are valued. the single market does not serve the interests of workers and peoples. it interferes with the sovereign development of states. it has promoted a lowering of living and working conditions in europe, increasing inequalities, exclusion and poverty. obviously, we voted against it.
‒ this report focuses its strategy on aspects aimed at helping businesses, in particular smes, micro-enterprises and start-ups, to scale up, expand and remain in the single market, thus facilitating innovation and job creation. i am voting in favour of this report, which, in addition to supporting greater integration of businesses into the single market, is also in favour of the obligation to identify the origin of products, thus increasing information for consumers. i also believe that it is essential for the european union to look at the future of the digital single market, in particular how best to create a european ecosystem to support startups, to look at how best companies can operate in the sharing economy and to increase european competitiveness also through trade agreements that will be established.
in writing. ‒ more than 20 years of the single market have meant the acceleration of the process of capitalist concentration and accumulation in favour of monopoly groups, the dismantling of instruments at the service of member states' sovereign regulation of economies, privatisations and the liberalisation of strategic sectors and public services, the harmonisation of legislation. but it's not enough. the big monopoly capitalists want more, and the explicit aim is to deepen the integration of the single market and to contribute to structural reforms, i.e. the liquidation of the social functions of the state and labour rights. the single market has eclipsed such propagandized concepts as convergence, cooperation and solidarity, deepening neoliberalism. in its name and in the name of the famous 'competitiveness', the attack on workers' rights, social inequalities, labour deregulation, wage devaluation and the precariousness of work have been promoted and more redistributive and fairer tax policies have been destroyed or opposed. it serves capitalist aims of further deepening the concentration of wealth in the great powers and economic groups, it makes deregulation, liberalisation and exploitation the norm in the economies of the member states, imposing a single socioeconomic model on the peoples and workers which is contrary to their interests, rights and legitimate aspirations. we voted against it.
‒ the single market is one of the main pillars of european integration, providing a driver for sustainable growth, stimulating job creation, facilitating trade between member states and ensuring a highly competitive economy. the report on the single market strategy states that progress in recent years has opened up possibilities for improvement in a number of areas. in this context, the document is particularly focused on supporting the growth and proliferation of start-ups, micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in a more open, innovative and deeper european single market, in particular through the focus on the digital sector and the promotion of global supply chains. without prejudice to the obligations of economic operators, in particular with regard to product labelling and geographical indication, the report stresses the importance of the european single market for the european project. i therefore vote in favour of this report, considering that, in accordance with article 3 of the tfeu, the union must achieve a genuine single market and regard it as a common good of all european citizens.
‒ the european parliament can make a significant contribution to making the single market strategy more ambitious by deepening it and making it more innovative. the group of the european socialists has succeeded in negotiating the introduction of many measures relating to sustainable growth, job creation, social inclusion, consumer protection, territorial cohesion, environmental concerns, protection and incentives for smes, administrative cost relief; tax justice and the fight against tax evasion and fraud, health and safety at work, the qualification of workers, etc.
‒ the completion of the single market is one of the main objectives of the european integration process. however, in recent years the global economic, financial and business environment has changed dramatically and the challenges are becoming more significant, with a considerable impact on the internal market. significant progress has been made in recent years, but the current situation calls for an even more pragmatic and incisive approach. the report proposes measures such as a vat action plan, a legislative proposal on the insolvency of companies, the creation of a service passport and a legislative initiative to prevent discrimination against consumers on grounds of nationality or country of residence. these are concrete measures which will certainly have a direct impact and a leverage effect on the market and on the strengthening of consumer protection. in order to achieve a more modern, innovative and fair single market, policy priorities should be to strengthen business competitiveness, improve budget implementation, better regulation and strengthen consumer protection. in fact, this work must be continued in a rapid and effective manner, which is why i voted in favour of this report.

it is a fact that enormous progress has been made in the fight against the human immunodeficiency virus, as the commissioner has rightly pointed out. today, nearly 16 million people are on antiretroviral medication, which is equivalent to a reduction of about 35 percent in new infections compared to the year 2000. and the drop in hiv-related deaths since the peak of the epidemic is 42 percent. however, different data show that much more needs to be done if we are to restore dignity and quality of life to all those living with hiv. the data show that some 22 million people still lack access to adequate medication and that half of all virus carriers are unaware of their real situation. ladies and gentlemen, at the beginning of this new millennium, we cannot allow inequities in the response to hiv to persist. ending the aids epidemic by the 20s and 30s is a difficult but achievable goal today. to this end, we must be able to put in place, already in the next five years, a coordinated and comprehensive strategy based on a number of key pillars that give priority to the joint mobilisation of funding and the anticipation of the investments needed in the fight against hiv, with particular attention to the countries with the greatest fragility in their health systems and to the groups most at risk of infection, as well as the assumption that the prevention element is absolutely paradigmatic in the fight against hiv and therefore more resources should be allocated to it. commissioner, only through an integrated and comprehensive approach can we achieve a virtuous cycle of progress in this fight and for this reason i would like to commend the initiative of the united nations, hoping that the european union can also join forces to achieve this millennium development goal.

‒ the stated objective of the protocol is to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. illicit trade in tobacco products is defined in the protocol as any practice or conduct prohibited by law and related to the production, dispatch, receipt, possession, distribution, sale or purchase of tobacco products. in order to address this issue, the protocol targets the tobacco supply chain through the adoption of a series of measures by governments and requires the establishment, within five years of its entry into force, of a tracking and tracing system. this implies the creation of a global information sharing point located in the secretariat of the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control, which will oversee the establishment of national and regional tracking and tracing systems. the protocol will also aim to encourage and strengthen international cooperation, the exchange of valid information, technical and police cooperation and mutual assistance in administrative and legal matters. we voted in favour.
‒ in addition to the loss of important revenues for the eu in terms of unpaid taxes and customs duties, the illicit trade in tobacco is a criminal activity that threatens public health by tearing up public tobacco control policies by increasing easy access to cheaper tobacco products. it is essential to strengthen the international fight against illicit tobacco trade, tax evasion and organised crime. i voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation on the draft council decision.
‒ the world health organisation's protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products aims to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products and targets the tobacco supply chain through the adoption of a series of measures by governments and requires the establishment, within five years of its entry into force, of a tracking and tracing system. the protocol will define the infringements, the issue of liability, the payments resulting from the seizure and the disposal of the seized products, and will encourage and strengthen international cooperation, the sharing of valid information, technical and police cooperation and mutual assistance in administrative and legal matters. in view of the above, i am in favour of the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the protocol.
‒ the stated objective of the protocol is to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. illicit trade in tobacco products is defined in the protocol as any practice or conduct prohibited by law and related to the production, dispatch, receipt, possession, distribution, sale or purchase of tobacco products. in order to address this issue, the protocol targets the tobacco supply chain through the adoption of a series of measures by governments and requires the establishment, within five years of its entry into force, of a tracking and tracing system. this implies the creation of a global information sharing point, located in the secretariat of the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control, which will oversee the establishment of national and regional tracking and tracing systems. the protocol will also aim to encourage and strengthen international cooperation, the exchange of valid information, technical and police cooperation and mutual assistance in administrative and legal matters. we voted in favour.
‒ the world health organisation's framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) is the first global health agreement and aims to respond to the global tobacco epidemic by addressing the root causes, namely illicit trade in tobacco products. the committee also welcomes the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road. i voted in favour.
‒ the objective of the protocol is to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products (any practice or behaviour prohibited by law and related to the production, dispatch, receipt, possession, distribution, sale or purchase of tobacco products). this implies strengthening international cooperation, information sharing, technical and police cooperation and mutual administrative and legal assistance, as well as the supervision of national and regional product tracking and tracing systems. the tobacco industry has a responsibility to act effectively and to combat the illicit trade in its products in an unequivocal manner. the protocol recognises the irreconcilable conflict between the interests of the tobacco industry and the interests of public health and sets out specific obligations with regard to the tobacco industry.
in the light of the above, the commission considers that the proposed amendments to the directive should be adopted by the council in accordance with the procedure provided for in article 189b of the treaty. this protocol addresses the chain of production and sale of tobacco products through the adoption by governments of measures concerning the development of additional provisions to deal with illicit tobacco products. the report, which is aware of the existence of illicit trade in tobacco products, deals with the part of the protocol relating to the fight against this criminal offence, defining offences and addressing the issue of liability and payments arising from seizure and disposal of the seized products. in addition, this protocol will encourage and strengthen international cooperation, the exchange of valid information, technical and police cooperation and mutual assistance in administrative and legal matters. the tobacco industry has a responsibility to act effectively and to combat the illicit trade in its products in an unequivocal manner. as i said earlier, i voted in favour of this report (which relates exclusively to the provisions covered by title v of part iii of the tfeu).

‒ this report concerns the proposal for a directive amending the markets in financial instruments directive, which is aimed only at amending specific dates of the basic directive. the criticisms we have occasionally made of the basic directive and which led us to vote against it remain entirely intact. these amendments do not touch on the essential point, which is the very existence of these markets and their instruments. they keep intact the 'financialisation' of the economy and all productive activity as a central part of the eu's development strategy, always seeking to satisfy the profit rates of the large economic and financial groups, which the production of real goods and services could not and cannot satisfy. this is the strategy of this instrument, which is inseparable from the existence of tax havens, the increasing crushing of public spending and investment, the privatisation and liberalisation of public services and of undertakings essential for economic and social development. for these reasons, i vote against.

‒ this report concerns a draft legislative resolution to amend directive 2014/65/eu on markets in financial instruments by laying down requirements on the authorisation and functioning of investment firms, regulated markets and data reporting services providers. this new framework requires trading venues and systematic internalisers to provide competent authorities with reference data on financial instruments covered by that directive and to describe in a uniform manner the characteristics of each financial instrument. the new data collection structure, which is currently being developed, will allow for an efficient and harmonised collection of data, although its completion is only expected after january 2017, when member states are to apply the measures transposing the directive. given the implications of the lack of a data collection infrastructure for the overall application of the markets in financial instruments directive, it is necessary and justified to extend the period until the full framework is implemented in order to ensure legal certainty and to avoid possible market disruption. i therefore voted in favour of adopting this report.

‒ through policy coherence in a development perspective, the union seeks to take development objectives into account in all policies that may affect developing countries, thereby minimising contradictions and generating synergies between its different policies, so as to benefit those countries and increase the effectiveness of development cooperation. in the context of the eu's fifth biennial report on the cfp, the european parliament is once again proposing a set of concrete recommendations in the areas of trade and finance, food security, climate change and migration, in the light of the recent refugee crisis in europe. i support the dan preda report and the recommendations it makes, and only with a coherent and strong cooperation policy can we achieve the new goals of sustainable development and poverty eradication.
‒ the council conclusions on the commission's fifth biennial report on policy coherence for development (pcd), adopted in october 2015, highlighted that pcd will be an important element of the eu's contribution to achieving the broader objective of policy coherence for sustainable development. while the union has repeatedly reaffirmed its political commitment to the cfp, the challenge remains as to how to deliver this commitment in practice. in addition to taking stock of the progress reported by the european commission and identifying areas for improvement in eu mechanisms for cpd, this report aims to stimulate debate on the future of this concept at union level.
‒ this report analyses the european commission's fifth biennial report on policy coherence for development (pcd). it covers trade and finance, food security, climate change, migration and security, with a focus on eu foreign policy in the context of the refugee crisis. by defending just principles and objectives, such as the fight against poverty and exclusion, it ends up giving an excessive, not innocent or neutral, focus to the private sector in areas such as health and education services, the promotion and protection of children's rights or the promotion of gender equality. the report makes no reference to the instruments which promote the cycle of increasing impoverishment, dependence and subordination of the developing countries, and to the asymmetrical interdependence relations typical of globalised capitalism, which generate unequal development on a global scale. this is the case with the external debt. official development assistance is crucial and should increase, even in line with commitments. but it's not enough. it does not hide the disastrous effects of trade liberalization, deregulation of the financial system, tax havens, etc., nor does it forget the attempt to export and impose models of economic and political organization which do not respect the sovereignty, the needs and the legitimate choices of developing countries.
‒ i have cast my vote in favour of the eu's 2015 report on policy coherence for development. the european union should take the lead in promoting policy coherence for development (pcd), as it is a key element in the implementation of the new sustainable development agenda. we must move towards sustainable development and poverty eradication. the european parliament has a very important role in promoting the dpc, placing it high on its agenda, encouraging the exchange of views with partner countries and promoting dialogue with civil society.
‒ the commission's fifth biennial report on the cpd highlighted that policy coherence for development (pcd) will be an important eu contribution to the wider objective of policy coherence for sustainable development (pcds). the adoption of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development represents a new challenge for the achievement of the sdg, as it sets out a single and universal set of development goals applicable to all. i believe that the eu should take the lead in promoting cpd and that the current european development framework lacks effective mechanisms to prevent and correct inconsistencies resulting from eu policies. it is important to stress that the sustainable development goals concern both developed and developing countries and should be incorporated into the union's decision-making process, both internally and externally. i agree with the rapporteur's recommendation that the union's external policy should be given priority in the face of the refugee crisis and the instability in the union's neighbourhood, which is putting at risk the very foundations of the union itself, such as european solidarity and the schengen system, and making external action a priority area in the context of the cfsp.
in writing. previous european parliament reports have played a central role in promoting the concept of policy coherence for development (pcd), declaring this to be a matter for which parliament is politically responsible (as a co-legislator and democratically elected institution) and putting forward concrete proposals for the practical implementation of the concept at eu level. in addition to taking stock of the progress reported by the european commission and identifying areas for improvement of eu mechanisms on cpd, this report aims to stimulate debate on the future of this concept at union level, with a view to the 2030 agenda for sustainable development. some of the priority areas are migration, trade and finance, food security, health, climate change, gender issues or security. as also expected, there was some controversy over references to sexual and reproductive rights, the approach to the refugee issue, the role of the private sector and the use of military means to implement humanitarian development policies. the socialist group has succeeded in introducing amendments which reflect its values and has also reached balanced agreements. despite the difficulties in implementing the cfp, the eu should strive to achieve more synergies between its policies.
‒ the commission's fifth biennial report on policy coherence for development (dpc) of august 2015 includes the specific objective 'improving policy coherence for sustainable development'. the dpc is an important part of the eu's contribution to achieving the goal of policy coherence for sustainable and inclusive development. although the eu has frequently reaffirmed its political commitment to dpc, the challenge it still faces is how to deliver on this commitment. given that the refugee crisis and instability in the union's neighbourhood are creating serious (internal) political problems for the union itself, external action and, in particular, the edf (european development fund) are indispensable instruments for the proper implementation of the csf and for addressing these new challenges facing the union. this report aims to take stock of progress made, identify areas for improvement and existing mechanisms in the eu on cpd and encourage debate on the future of this concept, and should therefore take the lead in promoting a universal agenda in this area that puts this concept at the service of sustainable development, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ 1.5 billion people still live in poverty and lack access to health, education and living conditions. this requires action, but it must be consistent and coherent. i would argue that the 2030 agenda for sustainable development is a priority. the 17 universal and indivisible sustainable development goals set out in the agenda need to be achieved. as recognised in 15 of these objectives, when addressing the most deprived territories we cannot take a paternalistic position, where we define what models others should follow. it is also essential not to torpedo the creation and emergence of indigenous production capacities and it is important to ensure that developing countries are not left to dump the products overproduced by our economies. on the other hand, i call for firm action by all to implement the recent climate agreement reached at cop21. the so-called developed countries must act and thus prevent the increase of asymmetries and suffering. i think this report sums up the problem well and includes the strategic instruments for implementing many solutions. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.

‒ the new alliance for food and nutrition security in africa (nasan) was launched in 2012 to mobilise private investment in the agricultural sector to improve food and nutrition security in sub-saharan africa. each african country has adopted a country cooperation framework (ccf) which sets out the commitments made by each of the parties involved. however, there are serious doubts about the ability of large-scale ppps such as nasan to contribute to poverty reduction and food security, as it may be the poorest who bear the burden of the social and environmental risks associated with them.
in writing. launched by the g8 summit in 2012, this so-called alliance brings together the g8 countries, the african union and several other african governments with the multinational private sector (represented by more than 150 companies, including syngenta). the alliance consists of public-private partnerships that say they aim to lift more than 50 million people out of poverty and hunger by 2022. from the outset, this alliance has been subject to a number of criticisms and challenges, from the decision-making process to the imposition of inadequate agricultural policies that serve the interests of multinationals. the report contains a number of concerns and criticisms which we share. throughout the process, the main targets, namely the hungry, small farmers, fishermen, indigenous peoples, women and other marginalized groups, were never heard. it is clear that the interests of the private groups and the g8 countries are at the heart of the strategies, not their own. this has meant that in many of the cooperation frameworks, basic human rights are not even guaranteed, such as the right to participate, the right to food and nutrition, the right to land and to produce, to social protection and an income, among others. we have made a number of proposals in the committee on agriculture which were eventually accepted in the final report. we voted in favour.

‒ the new alliance for food and nutrition security in africa (nasan) is a broad public-private partnership aimed at mobilising private investment in the agricultural sector to improve food and nutrition security in sub-saharan africa. nasan's strategy is based on monoculture, mechanization, biotechnology, reliance on fertilisers, long distribution channels and the production of crops for export. the limits of this approach are well known, including the environmental risks involved. the eu and the member states have a key role to play in transforming nasan into a genuine instrument to support family farming and local economies in sub-saharan africa in order to combat poverty and food and nutrition insecurity. the rapporteur believes that the eu should suspend its support for nasan and that donors and national governments should invest in a sustainable farming model for small farmers and women, so as to benefit family farmers and provide consumers with quality food at affordable prices. i voted in favour of continuing support for nasan, as did the socialist group, provided that the shortcomings identified are addressed.
‒ in 2012, the new alliance for food and nutrition security (nasan) was established under the auspices of the g8 to improve food security and nutrition in sub-saharan africa, with the aim of supporting these countries in fighting poverty by 2020. to this end, the participating countries negotiated cooperation frameworks, setting commitments to facilitate private investment in the agricultural sector in africa - unfortunately largely neglected in the last thirty years, which has increased the dependence of these countries on food imports, followed by price fluctuations on international markets. this motion for a resolution, which i generally support, calls for the need for african countries to resume investment in the agricultural sector. however, the model proposed by nasan has some gaps in terms of expropriations, small producers and agricultural practices considered unsustainable. i therefore support the proposals put forward on the need for member states to play an active role in improving the model adopted by nasan so that it can be a real instrument to support family farming and local economies in sub-saharan africa, effectively combating poverty and food and nutritional insecurity.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not distorted. the objectives we set for development policy must be the guiding principle for the other policy areas we undertake in relation to these countries. local communities must continue to have and decide on options for future progress. as regards natural resources, recognising that they can be an economic asset, it is imperative to defend the ownership and preservation of natural heritage for the benefit of the people who depend on it directly. this must be possible within a well-defined regulatory framework, which provides real possibilities for local communities to have recourse to it and under the aegis of the right to food, nutrition, property and participation. these are basic and elementary rights which should not even be the subject of a claim today. because we enjoy progress in europe, both materially and politically, we have an obligation to promote more and better progress in the other parts of the world with which we are developing rapprochement.
‒ this initiative involves the g8, several multinationals and public-private partnerships, through which, we are assured, millions of people in africa are being lifted out of poverty and hunger. the declarations do not hide their purpose: 'to accelerate the flow of private capital', but to do this the so-called charity of the multinationals requires political changes that make it easier for them to do business and create conditions for accumulating millions in profits. this initiative starts from the assumption (to be verified, because wrong) that more production, through investment by large private corporations, will solve the problem of hunger and malnutrition in africa. now these corporations produce for lucrative markets, not for the poor and hungry. this initiative will be a useful way of facilitating access to land and agricultural inputs, while encouraging the change in agricultural practices in the interests of the multinationals themselves, favouring export-oriented intensive production models with a high incorporation of agrochemicals and gmos.
