in writing. ‒ we are in favour of the principle of international cooperation and of helping countries which are experiencing economic difficulties for various reasons. however, this cooperation must be genuine and based on respect for the sovereignty of states and their right to dispose of their resources and to choose their own development model. supporting tunisia to improve its public finances, reform its financial system, improve its regulatory framework for trade and investment, or even correct its budgetary situation is clearly outside the real cooperation we advocate. it is more like imposing reforms to impose a model based on full liberalization of the economy. these are reforms that the eu imposes on its member states and the results of which are in sight. we therefore reject this so-called aid, because it is not without conditions. it imposes on the tunisian people a model which, like here in europe, will generate more inequality and more poverty in the medium term.
‒ the proposal lays down rules against corporate tax avoidance in six specific areas, including the deductibility of interest and a clause on the taxation of income generated abroad. this legislation is aimed at situations where groups of companies take advantage of disparities between national tax systems to reduce their tax obligations. the aim is for companies to pay their taxes where they make their profits. these rules aim to identify all taxpayers liable to corporation tax in a member state, to combat cross-border tax avoidance practices and to provide a common framework for the coordinated implementation of oecd measures against base erosion and profit shifting in the national legislation of eu member states.
in writing. ‒ this is a key directive in the european commission's action plan announced a year ago. it is intended that there will be some degree of harmonisation in the interpretation of the beps guidelines adopted in the oecd. the principle is laudable and we follow the general spirit of the measures, some of which correspond to our proposals in the assembly of the republic. however, there are aspects which distort the proposals and prevent us from voting in favour. the proposal exempts financial firms from the limitation on interest deductions. besides, there's a waiver we're not following. the oecd advocates a limit on the deduction of interest between 10 and 30%. the european commission, in its proposal, not surprisingly, opts for the upper limit. why would you do that? for whose benefit? the criterion for taxation in the country of origin is that the tax rate of the third country is less than 40% of the tax rate of the country of origin. it will therefore not apply to most european cases, such as ireland, the netherlands or even, in some sectors, switzerland or luxembourg. this legislation will conflict with other legislation which is being made on the consolidated taxation matter. in other words, we are talking about isolated, fragmented, and unjoint initiatives. finally, nothing is said about tax havens.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on tax avoidance practices that directly affect the internal market. aggressive tax planning represents a significant loss of revenue for states, which lose their capacity to invest and create jobs. this report represents an important step towards a european union response to the fight against tax evasion and avoidance which cannot be tackled by member states in isolation.
‒ tax avoidance practices can have a negative impact on the full functioning of the internal market and social justice. in this context, it is essential that member states take appropriate measures to discourage tax avoidance practices and to ensure fair and effective taxation, which is carried out in a consistent and coordinated manner. in this regard, this proposal for a directive provides for the adoption of measures to combat tax evasion. it provides, inter alia, for measures to prevent the erosion of tax bases, to promote the transparency of profits earned by companies and their transfer to tax havens, to introduce a mechanism for the resolution of cross-border tax disputes and to implement a european tax number as a vehicle for a more efficient and reliable automatic exchange of information. in order to ensure its full effectiveness, the implementation of that directive should be accompanied by an impact assessment to ensure that tax administrations have the appropriate means. i am voting in favour of this proposal for a directive, since it is essential that the union should define common rules to combat tax avoidance.
‒ according to an oecd study, aggressive tax optimisation by multinationals costs state budgets around the world between usd 100 and 240 billion each year, representing between 4% and 10% of global corporate tax revenues. it is becoming clear that this reality represents a significant loss of income for states and reduces their capacity to invest in promoting employment, combating poverty and developing effective health systems. this report, which i voted for, states that fair and effective corporate taxation should become the cornerstone of the single market and calls for companies to pay their taxes where they earn their profits. to this end, the report decided to establish precise and mandatory definitions of the conditions for proving that a multinational is well established in a country, taking into account that multinational companies are often organized in such a way as to transfer their profits to tax havens without having paid any tax. the document thus states that the ep should be the body responsible for monitoring the effective implementation of this directive in the 28 member states. it should also be able to carry out an independent evaluation to measure its effectiveness.
‒ the main objective of the report is to ensure that companies pay their taxes where they make their profits. the rapporteur has decided to insert a precise and binding definition in the criteria which must be met for a multinational to prove that it is established in a given country. this is the only way to make them pay their taxes fairly. the report also reinforces the role of the european parliament, which should be the body responsible for checking whether this directive is being implemented effectively in the 28 member states. it should also be able to carry out an independent evaluation of its effectiveness.
‒ recent studies by the oecd (organization for economic cooperation and development) show that states lose between usd 100 and 240 million in corporate tax revenues as a result of aggressive tax optimisation by multinational companies. this situation severely undermines the capacity of public investment to promote growth solutions for member states. if we are to achieve an effective single market and a robust and reliable economic and financial union, member states need to agree on european tax harmonisation that is fair and effective for citizens and businesses. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal to establish rules to strengthen the average level of protection against aggressive tax planning in the internal market. the main changes were: the obligation for companies to pay their taxes at the place where they earn their profits, by establishing conditions proving that they are being implemented in a given country; and the clarification and standardization of patent legislation, which no longer allows companies to artificially reduce their profits. both measures are extremely positive and make an essential contribution to the fight against tax evasion and fraud.
‒ the objectives of this directive are laudable. however, as is evident with each passing day, the grand design announced by the commission in 2015, at the height of the tax scandals and the fury of public opinion, is facing reality. in the name of pragmatism, that is to say, in the name of the hypocrisy of the governments of the countries which have created the conditions for exempting the large multinationals from paying taxes, we have today a minimalist proposal from the committee which does not correspond in the least to the legitimate expectations of the citizens. we support the report which called for the adoption of the maximum standards within the framework of the oecd proposals and not the other way around. we don't understand the exemption of the financial system. the commission's criteria for the implementation of the switchover are ineffective. we also do not see how this proposal can be consistent with other proposals that have been promised, such as the consolidation of the common tax base or the list of tax havens. in other words, this directive seems to us more like a propaganda tool, intended to make citizens understand that something is being done to make everything look the same.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the bayet report because i agree with the principle that parliament should use all the means at its disposal to influence the council in the fight against crossborder tax evasion which cannot be effectively carried out by member states alone. this report goes beyond the commission's proposal to achieve a minimum essential level of coordination within the union and calls for greater coordination within the union's legal and fiscal framework. i would stress that this type of measure is crucial, not only to combat tax evasion, particularly by multinationals, but also and above all to restore the confidence of european citizens in their institutions.
‒ the alleged use of european countries by the cia for the transport and illegal detention of prisoners is a matter that was first investigated by the european parliament. very slowly more facts were coming to light, including through a devastating report from the us senate itself. unfortunately, there is still a lot of uncertainty, too much responsibility to be cleared up. even within the european union and in strict compliance with the principle of subsidiarity, several member states have not wanted to cooperate with this parliament. or even each other. unfortunately, too, many of the recommendations that have been made have not been followed up. the concerns of almost ten years ago remain relevant. it is not just a question of finding out the truth, but also of preventing such flagrant violations of fundamental rights from happening again. all the more important as we seek again today a balance between security and individual freedoms. i think that this resolution is sometimes over-exaggerated in its language and even used for ideological propaganda. however, its contents remain true and the european parliament cannot shirk its responsibilities. i therefore support this resolution.
‒ more than a year after the publication of the us senate report on the use of torture by the cia, i regret the lack or slow pace of investigations, the reduced accountability and the excessive reliance on state secrecy. none of the member states has carried out comprehensive and effective investigations aimed at bringing to justice the perpetrators of crimes under international and national law. joint counter-terrorism efforts must respect obligations under international law and the us must continue investigations and cooperate with all requests from european countries concerning the cia programme.
‒ this resolution deals with the us senate report on the use of torture by the cia. the resolution deplores the fact that the investigations have been hampered by various obstacles, that too much time has passed since the start of the investigations, and that there has been no objective clarification of the facts and no convictions. it reiterated its strong condemnation of torture (enhanced interrogation techniques), which is prohibited under international law. expresses its deep concern at the 'apathy' shown by the member states and the eu institutions towards the recognition of the multiple violations of fundamental rights and torture that took place on european soil between 2001 and 2006. but there's a lot that remains to be said. much is left out of the resolution. the united states is an imperialist power which considers itself above any legal obligation, which disrespects international law and which, ironically, has continuously occupied several sovereign countries in the name of defending human rights. the current us president, barack obama, despite all the promises, has not yet closed the guantanamo prison. there is no guarantee that in the present context of murderous wars in which the united states is the main aggressor, similar events or even more perverse and threatening developments to human dignity will not be taking place. the abstention vote is therefore taken.
‒ the european parliament, through multiple resolutions and the creation of the temporary committee, strongly condemned the alleged use of european countries by the cia for the transport and illegal detention of prisoners. given the pillars on which the european project is based, namely the rule of law, i also believe that no reason justifies the violation of human rights. however, i cannot support a report which makes the separation of powers, the cornerstone of the rule of law, unclear and which repeatedly refers to and suggests clear interference by the political system in the judicial system of the member states.
the resolution calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take effective action to combat it. it reiterates its strong condemnation of the use of forced interrogation techniques, which are prohibited by international law and which violate, inter alia, the rights to liberty, security, human treatment, except torture, the presumption of innocence, a fair trial, legal advice and equal protection under the law. it refers to the 'apathy' of the member states and the european institutions in recognising the multiple violations of fundamental rights and torture that have taken place on european soil. more than 50 countries, including portugal, have provided cover for the secret programme of extrajudicial transfer of prisoners suspected of terrorism on cia flights, a demonstration of the us as an imperialist power that acts in defiance of international law and that persists as one of the countries that most promotes the violation of human rights. the military base at guantanamo and its concentration camp where the most barbaric practices have been forced upon detainees, most of whom are innocent and have not even been charged, are examples of this. it is essential to condemn the actions of the united states and not a word is said about this. the abstention vote is therefore taken.
‒ parliament called for thorough investigations into the participation of eu member states in the cia's secret detention and extraordinary rendition programme. one of the studies revealed that a number of member states, their authorities, officials and intelligence and security services were complicit in the cia's programme of harsh detention and extraordinary rendition, sometimes in a corrupt manner, on the basis of the payment of significant amounts by the cia in return for their cooperation. this report strongly condemns the use of enhanced interrogation techniques which violate the rights to liberty, security, humane treatment, the presumption of innocence, fair trials, legal advice and fair production under the law. the report also reiterates that, in the specific situation of guantanamo bay, criminal proceedings under civil jurisdiction are the best way to resolve the situation of the detainees, and urges the us authorities not to apply the death penalty to them. i abstained because i think there are still areas which can be improved and investigated at this level.
in writing. ‒ this was a difficult vote, but we managed to convey the idea that, one year after the publication of the us senate study, we remain concerned about the apathy shown by the member states and the european institutions in recognising the multiple violations of fundamental rights and torture that took place on european soil between 2001 and 2006, in investigating these violations and in taking action to bring the accomplices and those responsible to justice. transatlantic cooperation based on common values such as freedom and security, democracy and fundamental human rights must remain a key priority in the eu's external relations. transatlantic cooperation in the fight against terrorism must respect fundamental rights, freedoms and the protection of privacy as guaranteed by eu law.
in writing. - this resolution was adopted by 329 votes in favour, 299 against and 49 abstentions, including my vote. i decided to abstain because i wanted to make it clear that i strongly condemn the use of enhanced interrogation techniques, and also considering that the european union is based on the principles of democracy, the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity and international law, not only in its internal policies but also in its external dimension, and that this commitment, reinforced by the entry into force of the eu charter of fundamental rights and the process of accession to the european convention on human rights, must be present in all its fields of action, as can be read in the text of the adopted resolution. i also note that the council of europe has decided to close its inquiry and that the inquiry of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs into this matter has not brought to light anything new or relevant, so it seems to me more appropriate that the national parliaments, the national/european judiciary (in particular the european court of human rights) should promote any criminal investigations/actions and/or provide victims with legal remedies.
in writing. the resolution deplores the fact that investigations into the use of torture by the cia have been hampered by the fact that too much time has passed since the inception of the investigations without objective clarification of the facts and the resulting convictions. more than 50 countries, including portugal, have provided cover for the secret cia's extrajudicial transfer of terrorism suspects on flights, launched by the bush administration after the september 11, 2001 attacks. the secret operations consisted of the abduction, transport and torture of terrorism suspects in clandestine detention centres, with the collaboration of several european governments - the united kingdom, germany, sweden - and american allies in africa and the middle east. the united states is an imperialist power which considers itself above any legal obligation, which disrespects international law and which, ironically, has continuously occupied several sovereign countries in the name of defending human rights. justice must be done and those responsible, including the us administration, which unfortunately remains unpunished in this report, must be condemned at national and international level, at the level of the united nations.
‒ space capabilities for european security and defence are important, and in some cases vital, for a variety of situations, from everyday peacetime use to managing crises and more serious security challenges. satellites can be used to more effectively assess and identify illegal immigrant flows, their routes and to identify embarkation zones to initiate procedures more quickly and save more lives. the development and maintenance of space capabilities for the security and defence of europe require effective cooperation and synergies between member states, european and international institutions. national governments and the union should improve access to space capabilities in terms of satellite communications and ensure european non-dependence in critical space technologies and access to space. it is essential to strengthen the coordination of spatial systems used in a fragmented manner by the different member states in order to anticipate as quickly as possible a disruption of the different applications. the eu should continue to seek to ensure the highest degree of spatial and military autonomy. i therefore support this report.
‒ the eu must strengthen its role as a guarantor of security at home and abroad, ensuring stability in neighbouring countries and globally, and contributing to the fight against security challenges, including those arising from terrorism on its territory and beyond, including through support to third countries in the fight against terrorism and its root causes. space capabilities and services play an important role, inter alia, in the context of european security and defence in areas such as external action, border management, maritime security, agriculture, environment, climate change, energy security, disaster management, humanitarian aid and transport.
‒ this report addresses the development of european space capabilities for european security and defence. in short, the aim is to use space capabilities to serve the militaristic and warmongering policy of the european union. space capabilities and services are considered to play an important role in a number of areas, such as external action, border management, maritime security or energy security. it is argued, contradictorily, that space should not be militarized, but it is also considered that space capabilities should not be restricted to civilian activities, but should cover security and defence, i.e. militarization. the security dimension of the copernicus programme is underlined. the space sector is included in a new overall eu strategy on foreign and security policy. the dangers of cyber war and hybrid war are identified - to justify the arms race it is necessary to brandish dangers, create enemies, to which the eu will have to respond. the report also calls for the eu to be able to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. these are more than sufficient reasons for our vote against, which we also justified by our intervention in the plenary.
‒ the increasing proliferation of space technology, with its use for both military and increasingly civilian purposes, such as gps, weather forecasting, fire detection, among others, makes the space sector a strategic area of utmost importance for the european union. given the potential of exploiting space capabilities, the european union should seek to exploit them in an efficient and sustainable manner, both in the context of security and defence policy and in other european union policies in areas such as external action, border management, agriculture, the environment, energy security, disaster management, maritime security, among others. in this context, it would also be important to equate the development of security and defence-related space capabilities to the next generations of the galileo and copernicus systems. i am voting in favour of this because i consider the exploitation of space capability to be a sector of the utmost importance in the framework of the common security and defence policy.
‒ the report continues the militaristic and warmongering policy of the european union, this time through space capabilities as an important instrument for external action, for border management, for internal, maritime and energy security and to improve the development of the european military industrial complex. calls for enhanced eu cooperation (and submission) with the us and nato on future space capabilities/services for the csdp. it supports continued investment in space, security and defence agencies and the use of dual-use space technologies to contribute to the development of the european defence industry. the whole report is imbued with the idea of putting security and defence policies at the centre of the european union's policies, particularly its foreign policy, and it goes further in the aggressive nature of this process of european capitalist integration and the concept of 'strong europe'. we voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the security environment is becoming increasingly dangerous and demanding, inside and outside the union, with terrorist attacks and mass killings affecting all member states. the report calls for a joint strategy by all member states and a coordinated response. the document also considers that space capabilities and services play an important role in this european defence context, helping in areas such as external action, border management, maritime security, agriculture, the environment, climate change, energy security, disaster management, humanitarian aid and transport. the report states that national governments and the union should improve access to space capabilities in terms of satellite communication, space situational awareness, precision navigation and earth observation, and ensure european non-dependence in critical space technologies and access to space. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ space capabilities and services play an important role, among other areas, in the context of european security and defence. current and future space services and capabilities will provide member states and the union with an enhanced operational capacity for the implementation of the common security and defence policy and other eu policies in areas such as external action, border management, maritime security, agriculture, environment, climate change, energy security, disaster management, humanitarian aid and transport.
‒ the development of european space capabilities is of paramount importance to the union and its member states, as technological progress increases the number of innovative applications with everyday applicability and safety. the eu has developed programmes such as galileo and copernicus, which have enabled not only precise positioning, covering the needs of observations made from the ground, but also other plans for acquiring new communication capabilities. the existing programmes require sustained and high investment and are also extremely useful for missions under the common security and defence policy. the security purposes they serve are varied, including border surveillance, migration flows and maritime and air transport. promotion and cooperation within the eu, as well as the exchange of experience and information with external partners, will allow improving detail aspects and maximising the benefits. in recognition of the importance that these programmes can play in the safety of citizens, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ the key message of this report is that space capabilities should also be put to the service of defence and security. space capabilities and services are considered to play an important role including in security and defence issues, covering here several areas where these space capabilities can play an important role: external action, border management, maritime security, energy security, to name a few. the argument of preventing humanitarian disasters is used to conceal the real purpose of strengthening the security and defence capability of space satellites. hence our vehement opposition.
‒ the eu's space activities are of paramount importance for scientific and technical progress, as well as for innovation, economic growth, job creation, enterprise and new opportunities. in this context, the european commission should present a comprehensive and forward-looking strategy to ensure that europe is a leader in space technologies and services in world markets in the short, medium and long term, independent access to space and a level playing field for the european space industry. it should also promote the internationalisation of european space companies, in particular smes, through better access to finance to support the competitiveness of the european space industry, as well as specific actions at eu level enabling europe to access space autonomously. the eu and the member states should, in cooperation with the private sector, step up their efforts to stimulate skills and entrepreneurship and to attract students from technical universities, young scientists and entrepreneurs to the space sector, which will help maintain leadership capacity in space science and prevent brain drain to other parts of the world.
‒ over the next two decades, the economic and social benefits of the action plan on global navigation satellite system applications are expected to amount to around eur 60 to 90 billion, with the potential annual turnover of the downstream earth observation services market by 2030 expected to be approximately eur 2.8 billion, of which more than 90% stemming from the copernicus programme. i agree that autonomous access is of strategic importance for the eu in having highly reliable and accurate positioning and timing information as well as earth observation data.
in writing. ‒ we advocate a space policy based on deepening cooperation between european countries and beyond. but we have always said that this space policy should be exclusively focused on peaceful purposes and should exclude any use of space for military purposes. the criticism of the militarization of space and the abandonment of any arms race in space was a position which the majority of this parliament has never taken. this is the case once again with this resolution, which explicitly takes up and defends militarization alongside the development of the space market. it is revealing how the european union looks at space. it's also dangerous. as we said in the debate, the endless adventure of mankind to discover that great book which is continually open, of which galileo spoke, cannot serve to prolong on earth the wicked, aggressive and oppressive order which some have been imposing. on the contrary, it should help us solve problems, not create problems. an adventure to free, not to oppress. i therefore vote against.
‒ space capabilities play an important role in particular in the framework of response to crisis situations, such as natural disasters, in the efficient management of natural resources, in the provision of services, such as energy and transport, and in the field of security and defence. the activity of the european space industry is characterised by its heavy dependence on institutional initiative and, in comparative terms, by its much lower budgetary availability compared to countries such as the usa, china or russia. the eu space industry market is overly fragmented, facing policy barriers and barriers imposed by various national governments, as well as technical barriers and a lack of skilled labour for the sector. i am voting in favour of this because i believe it is important that the european union should make efforts to adopt a common strategy for space, particularly in the development of the space market.
‒ this report, which i voted in favour of, calls on the commission to present a comprehensive, ambitious and forward-looking strategy to ensure that europe is a leader in space technologies and services, as they guarantee european autonomy, innovation, social cohesion, the creation of skilled jobs, businesses and new opportunities in both upstream and downstream markets. the document also draws attention to the fact that the future development of eu space programmes must be user-oriented and driven by the user needs of the public, private and scientific sectors.
in december 2015, during the world trade organization (wto) ministerial conference in nairobi, 53 members reached agreement on the expansion of the information technology agreement, which includes a timetable to eliminate tariffs on 201 it products. annual trade in these products accounts for approximately 10% of total world trade. under this agreement, some 65% of the tariff lines will be completely eliminated by 1 july this year. in 2019, almost all imports of the products concerned will be duty free. considering that the eu's space activities are of great importance for scientific and technical progress, as well as for innovation, economic growth, industrial competitiveness, social cohesion, the creation of skilled jobs, businesses and new opportunities, and that access to this market by the eu is of particular strategic importance, i voted in favour of this report.

‒ the united nations environment programme (unep) and the world health organisation (who) have identified endocrine disruptors as a threat on a global scale. however, the commission has not respected its legal obligation to publish scientific criteria on endocrine disruptors, chemicals which are the cause of various diseases such as cancer or even increased infertility. in view of this, i agree that the commission should comply without delay with its obligations under the treaty and adopt immediately scientific risk-based criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties.
‒ endocrine disruptors can cause various types of diseases, such as neurobehavioural disorders, various types of cancer, can have negative consequences for pregnancy, genital malformations, obesity or type 2 diabetes. pursuant to regulation (eu) no 528/2012, the european commission should have adopted delegated acts by december 2013 concerning the scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties of active substances and biocidal products with a view to the prohibition of harmful substances. in march 2013, the expert advisory group on endocrine disruptors, set up by the commission and coordinated by the joint research centre (jrc), adopted a report on the main scientific issues relevant for the identification and characterisation of endocrine disrupting substances. the commission has not adopted the abovementioned delegated acts. the commission has been called upon to act at various times and in various ways since then. but even after the court's ruling in december 2015, he did nothing. we therefore consider this resolution to be appropriate. it is worth recalling the allegations of pressure by us officials responsible for trade in the context of the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip), which will justify the commission's attitude. so, all clear as day.

mr president, mr minister, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in 30 years of experience and scientific research at sea, my teams and i have carried out numerous studies on the biology, food ecology, ecotoxicology, migration and population dynamics of various species of atlantic cetaceans. we studied behavior, analyzed outputs, performed biopsies, conducted censuses, put transmitters and sensors on individuals that we monitored through hydrophones and satellites, and produced mathematical models of distribution. we never had to kill any individuals. in addition, we used information from animals we found washed up on the shore. technological developments today give us tools and methods that, while intrusive in some cases, do little to disturb the animals studying, do little to disturb the cetaceans. the study of stable isotopes, genetic analysis and genomics allows us to know about eating habits, migration dynamics and even kinship relations. there is a huge body of nonlethal methods today that are excellent approximations to reality and are fully accepted by the scientific community. for these reasons, i consider it disloyal to argue the need to use lethal methods for scientific purposes. through dna barcoding and other genetically based techniques applied to restoration products, we know that cetaceans from japan's so-called scientific whaling are being traded without proper regulation, leading to unfair and deceptive commercial practices. although its scientific research methodologies have been condemned by the international court of justice and also by the scientific community in general, japan, which i regard and respect as a great historical, cultural, scientific and technological nation, has not yet corrected the essential aspect of its antarctic scientific programme, namely the whaling. on this world oceans day, i want to state, as a scientist and now as a politician, the futility of whaling for scientific purposes.

‒ this report (second reading) aims at the free movement of citizens by simplifying the requirements for the presentation of certain public documents in the eu. this legislation is based on article 21 tfeu and aims to promote the free movement of citizens by simplifying the acceptance of certain public documents in the eu. it is not a question of recognising the content of public documents, especially in order to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in matters of family law. the regulation covers only documents relating to civil status and certain other documents often required of citizens, for example, residence, nationality and criminal records. it is proposed that multilingual forms be created for most of the public documents concerned in order to facilitate the process. the council is criticised for not including diplomas and training certificates, certificates of disability and certain documents relevant to businesses. moreover, multilingual forms cannot circulate independently but must be attached to the national documents concerned, which is an avoidable complication. the aim of this legislation is to facilitate the movement of citizens within the eu area, which is in many respects blocked by unnecessary administrative issues and which could be done more quickly.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the regulation to include the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment. in this connection, some important measures are introduced, including the waiver of two of the formalities normally required for crossborder public documents - legalisation and apostille - greater ease in accepting certified copies and certified translations and the creation of a multilingual form, which relieves citizens of the burden of translation and speeds up procedures. however, it is regrettable that documents such as certificates of incapacity/disability, training certificates and others do not fall within the scope of the regulation. i am therefore voting in favour of this because i consider that the adoption of these legislative measures is a decisive step towards the removal of the existing barriers to the free movement of citizens within the european union.
‒ this is the recommendation with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the promotion of the free movement of citizens by simplifying the requirements for the presentation of certain public documents in the european union. adopts the council's position at first reading. this legislation aims to promote the free movement of citizens by simplifying the acceptance of certain public documents in the european union. the regulation covers only documents relating to civil status and certain other documents often required of citizens, for example, residence, nationality and criminal records. it does not deal with the recognition of the content of public documents, in particular to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in matters of family law. the council is criticised for not including diplomas and training certificates, certificates of disability and certain documents relevant to businesses. moreover, multilingual forms cannot circulate independently but must be attached to the national documents concerned, which is an avoidable complication. the aim of this legislation is to facilitate the movement of citizens within the european union, which is in many respects blocked by unnecessary administrative issues and which could be done more quickly. we voted yes.
in writing. ‒ currently, in the community area, some 12 million european citizens live, study or work in a member state other than the one of which they are nationals. however, citizens and businesses in the union face a number of administrative difficulties when submitting public documents required by the authorities of other member states, which is a prerequisite for exercising the right to free movement and taking advantage of the possibilities of the internal market. in this particular case, we believe that it is the legislator's duty to simplify and improve the formalities relating to administrative procedures, as laid down in regulation (eu) no 1024/2012 (which assesses the requirements for legalisation or apostille, or for certified translations and certified copies). the proposed amendment to the regulation aims to simplify the acceptance of certain public documents in the union: on the one hand, it introduces an innovative electronic mechanism which makes it possible to confirm the authenticity of a document between the issuer and the receiver; on the other hand, it makes it possible to create multilingual forms. in the interests of the citizens of the union and in view of the added value of uniformity and simplification of bureaucratic procedures, i voted in favour.
‒ this document, which i voted in favour of, concerns the legislative resolution of the european parliament of 9 june 2016 on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the promotion of the free movement of citizens by simplifying the presentation requirements for certain public documents in the european union.
in writing. ‒ the mobility of european citizens is a reality: some 12 million people study, work or live in a member state other than their own. currently, if citizens and businesses in the union are to exercise their right to free movement or the freedoms of the internal market, they may face a number of administrative difficulties when presenting the necessary public documents to the authorities of another member state, in particular when crossing a border. following interinstitutional negotiations, the co-legislators and the commission agreed on a compromise text. the regulation covers documents relating to marital status, residence, nationality and criminal records. it also provides for measures to facilitate the acceptance of certified copies and certified translations and the creation of multilingual forms for most of the public documents concerned. parliament would also like to see diplomas, certificates of training and certificates of disability included.
in writing. ‒ we are faced with a proposal for a parliament recommendation to adopt a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the promotion of the free movement of citizens by simplifying the acceptance of certain public documents in the european union, amending regulation (eu) no 1024/2012. the proposal excludes the recognition of the content of public documents, in order to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in matters of family law. given the current situation of constant mobility of european citizens and the consequent right to free movement and the freedoms of the internal market, there are multiple administrative difficulties when submitting public documents required by the authorities of another member state. the agreement reached, which is the result of a commitment made in several interinstitutional negotiations, will make it possible to amend regulation no 1024/2012, by dispensing with the legalisation and apostillation of several documents relating to marital status, as well as others relating to identification, residence, nationality and criminal record. there will also be less formality in accepting certified copies and certified translations. i have always been in favour of administrative simplification and bureaucratization, and as this report is aimed at making life easier for citizens, starting with the creation of multilingual forms for most public documents, i naturally voted in favour.
‒ this legislation is based on article 21 tfeu. this legislation aims to promote the free movement of citizens by simplifying the acceptance of certain public documents in the european union. it is not a question of recognising the content of public documents, especially in order to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in matters of family law. the regulation covers only documents relating to civil status and certain other documents often required of citizens, for example, residence, nationality and criminal records. it is proposed that multilingual forms be created for most of the public documents concerned in order to facilitate the process. the council is criticised for not including diplomas and training certificates, certificates of disability and certain documents relevant to businesses. moreover, multilingual forms cannot circulate independently but must be attached to the national documents concerned, which is an avoidable complication.
in writing. ‒ the court of justice is undergoing a process of reform. among the various aspects of this reform is the reform of the general court of the european union. given the considerable workload of the court, which currently has 40 judges, parliament and the council agreed to increase that number to 56, i.e. two judges per member state. in return, it was also agreed to abolish the seven-judge european union civil service tribunal. the purpose of this regulation is therefore to transfer jurisdiction in disputes between the union and its servants. i therefore support the adoption of the report.
in writing. this is the fourth regulation on the reform of the court of justice. the first regulation introduced a number of changes to the formations and procedure of the court of justice and the general court. the second part of the reform created provisions on the interim judges of the civil service tribunal. the third part was controversial as it concerned an increase in the number of judges of the general court. the initial increase envisaged was from 28 to 40 judges. at the end of the process, the co-legislators, at the instigation of the council, agreed to increase the number of judges at the general court to 56, so that each member state could appoint two judges. this increase was subject to the condition that the civil service tribunal was abolished and civil service litigation transferred back to the general court. we have opposed the abolition of the general civil service tribunal and we do not see the need to increase the number of judges, a situation which could be solved by a system of rotation. that is reason enough not to support this report as well.
‒ article 257 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union constitutes the legal basis for the creation of specialised courts. it was on the basis of this provision that the only specialised court created to date was set up in 2004: the specialised civil service court. however, it has been found that the number of cases brought before that body is relatively small and this proposal for a regulation seeks to remedy this inefficiency of resources by allocating the human resources, in particular the judges, of the specialised court to the general court. although the existence of a basis for this amendment has been questioned, the fact is that the legal basis is the result of an a contrario sensu interpretation of that treaty provision. i therefore vote in favour of this proposal, since i believe that there must be efficient management of resources by the union institutions and that this must be guided by the adequacy of the actual needs.
in writing. ‒ this regulation, which i voted for, is the fourth on the reform of the court of justice. the first regulation introduced a number of changes to the formations and procedure of the court of justice and the general court; the second established provisions on the temporary judges of the civil service tribunal; the third was the most controversial, as it concerned an increase in the number of judges of the general court (from 28 to 56). this regulation is a follow-up to the third regulation. with this report the amendment provisions are made clearer and the section on specialised courts is repealed in its entirety, as it will not be needed until a specialised court is created again. the report also states that not only the rules of procedure of the general court should be amended, but also its internal organisation, with a greater number of cases being assigned to larger formations, where justified by their importance, in order to ensure the consistency and quality of the case-law.
in writing. ‒ we are now looking at the fourth regulation on the reform of the court of justice. after the controversial decision to increase the number of judges, which would have meant the abolition of the civil service tribunal and the transfer of its jurisdiction to the general court, this regulation proposes the repeal of the provisions relating to the civil service tribunal, together with a slight amendment to the transitional provisions and, of course, the repeal of the second regulation. it also contains some amendments of a very technical nature which will better target the legislation, making it clearer and without altering its substance. i agree with the amendments proposed and i agree with the rapporteur's overall views, and i therefore voted in favour.

‒ following up a previous european parliament resolution, it called for the adoption of a regulation on a european administrative procedure law to guarantee the right to good administration through an open, efficient and independent european administration. the regulation adopted today responds to this wish. in a union governed by the rule of law, procedural rights and obligations must always be defined and safeguarded, and citizens should be able to expect a high level of transparency, efficiency, rapid implementation and responsiveness from the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, as well as adequate information on the possibility of bringing proceedings in this area. i support this resolution because i believe that a regulation on the administrative procedure for acts of the union is vital, clearly laying down the rights and obligations of all administrative procedures in the union, based on the principles of good administration and the rule of law and other values which are at the heart of the union.
‒ this resolution calls on the european commission to take action in the field of eu administration. in january 2013, the european parliament called for the adoption of a regulation on an open, efficient and independent eu administration, in accordance with article 298 tfeu. the european commission has taken no action in this respect. the resolution calls on the commission to present a legislative proposal to be included in its work programme for 2017. the resolution opens up a not entirely explicit possibility of codifying administrative law in the eu area, in short, the publication of an eu administrative code. the statement of reasons shall state: the fact that the union does not have a coherent and comprehensive set of codified rules of administrative law makes it difficult for citizens to understand their administrative rights under union law. we do not forget that it is important for administrative regulation to go beyond the application of fundamental rules and principles, always with a view to respecting the principles of transparency, subsidiarity and proportionality. however, it should be ensured that the applicability of such an internal instrument of the european union does not extend to the member states. only in this way will the sovereignty of these states and the national framework of their values be respected.
‒ citizens should be able to expect a high level of transparency, efficiency, rapid implementation and responsiveness from the european institutions. existing rules and principles on good administration are scattered across a variety of sources of law and therefore need to be clarified for reasons of legal certainty and security. i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on an open, efficient and independent administration of the european union.
‒ in accordance with article 298 tfeu, the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the union shall, in the performance of their tasks, support an open, efficient and independent european administration, and the european union shall adopt the necessary provisions to that end. article 41 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union enshrines the right of citizens to good administration. the european union has adopted a number of administrative procedures over the years in a wide variety of sectors without, however, taking account of the overall coherence of the system. in this context, consistency of the union's administrative activities and full respect for the right to good administration and the interpretative conformity of procedural rules should be ensured. the right to good administration implies compliance with the duty of diligence, the principle of proportionality, the duty to act impartially, the duty to state reasons for acts, among others. i am therefore in favour of the adoption of a regulation on this subject, since i consider it essential that the union's administrative activities be governed by an appropriate and coherent structure of administrative procedures, so as to ensure an efficient, open and independent administration.
‒ the purpose of this report is to request the commission to submit a proposal for a regulation on a european law on administrative procedure. the report also calls for the eu to be able to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. this initiative is part of a process of increasingly implementing the federalisation of administrative law, which is continuing, and is also part of a process of strengthening european capitalist integration which aims to harmonise national administrative laws. the report opens the door to the creation of a 'communitarianised' administrative law which would be another step towards the construction of a european federation. we do not overlook the importance of administrative regulation by applying fundamental rules and principles, always with a view to respecting the principles of transparency, subsidiarity and proportionality. however, it must be ensured that the applicability of such an internal instrument of the european union does not extend to the member states, in the context of respect for their sovereignty and the appreciation of their national values, highlighting here the values of state and para-state administration in its broadest sense. we abstained.
‒ in a union governed by the rule of law, it is necessary to ensure that procedural rights and obligations are always properly defined, developed and respected. the rules and principles of good administration currently in place are dispersed over a wide variety of sources such as primary law, secondary law, the case law of the court of justice of the european union, non-binding legal measures and unilateral commitments by the union institutions. this regulation, which i voted for, is intended to guarantee the right to good administration, backed up by an open european administration that can improve the gaps and inconsistencies that the union has developed over the years through sectoral administrative procedures in the form of binding provisions and non-binding measures, without necessarily taking account of the overall coherence of the system. we must provide citizens with a high level of transparency, efficiency, rapid implementation and responsiveness by the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, as well as adequate information on the possibility of initiating proceedings in this area.

mr president, commissioner, international agreements have become a central topic of debate in european societies in recent years. many european citizens have in fact begun to follow and take an interest in the negotiations on these agreements, seeking information and to know the arguments put forward, the advantages and disadvantages that may be involved. this is particularly true of free trade agreements negotiated with third countries. these treaties have polarized the debate among citizens and have fuelled passionate disputes, many of them very much ideologically motivated, which is natural and should even be appreciated positively. this makes the issue of access to information on the negotiating process at its various stages particularly sensitive. it is not by chance that one of the most controversial aspects of international agreements, as we have seen today in this debate, is transparency, which is very much in evidence, for example, in the case of the discussion on the transatlantic treaty, which we are currently negotiating with the united states. in this context, the role of the european parliament in monitoring and scrutinizing such agreements is of great importance. the treaty of lisbon not only strengthened these monitoring and control powers, but also established that, in order to be able to perform this function properly, parliament must be duly informed of the progress of the negotiations on such agreements. moreover, the treaty of lisbon stipulates that the european parliament's right to information on negotiations is not limited to requests for information submitted by parliament itself, but must also result from the initiative of other european institutions. that is why the question of the institutional mechanisms for the transmission of this information is of the utmost importance. and although it was formalised by libe, it also concerns the afet committee, which focuses on international agreements in the more general dimension of european foreign policy, and the human rights committee, which focuses on these agreements in the context of the safeguarding and promotion of human rights. as chairman of the delegation for relations with mercosur, i have been following and keeping in mind the need for a certain degree of confidentiality in the negotiation of trade agreements. however, political action and even some diplomatic action that the european parliament can take is not compatible with sporadic and excessively distant information. it would therefore be very useful for the work of delegations, for example, for relations with third countries, in this case with the mercosur countries, if the negotiators responsible would systematically and in a timely manner provide their members with updated information on the progress of the negotiations on the eu-mercosur agreement, to give this concrete example. that is not the case today. contrary to the provisions of the treaty of lisbon and the framework agreement on relations between the european parliament and the european commission, access to information remains dependent on an initiative by the delegation. i think that the key thing here is to ensure that there is, within the limits of common sense, of course, a regular flow of information between the commission and parliament on this type of agreement, whether this is done by setting up a permanent mechanism or on the basis of institutional loyalty and respect for the provisions of the existing treaties and interinstitutional agreements. in writing. ‒ the european parliament is expected to give its consent to the conclusion of the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement. lebanon is of strategic importance to the eu in the middle east context with regard to security and defence. the report says the eu wants to protect itself from new threats such as terrorism. it also needs another country to act as a buffer to the arrival of more refugees in europe. the agreement consists of a proposal for an association between the european commission and the republic of lebanon to provide technical and financial support to the country, enabling it to participate in certain european programmes such as horizon 2020, cosme, creative europe. the eu is not concerned about the collapse of lebanon. the country has taken in thousands of refugees, there are problems with the syrian border, with israel, with the presence of the self-proclaimed islamic state. the main objective of the euro-mediterranean partnership is economic integration and the privileged relationship of these countries with the eu, and it is inseparable from the objectives of economic domination and market colonization. the agreement opens the door to free trade agreements. it is part of the eu's political and economic agenda for the middle east. these are reasons for our opposition.
‒ the objective of this protocol is to establish the financial and technical rules enabling the republic of lebanon to participate in certain eu programmes. the horizontal framework established by the protocol defines the principles for economic, financial and technical cooperation and allows the republic of lebanon to receive technical assistance, in particular financial assistance, from the european union in accordance with european union programmes. this framework shall apply only to programmes whose constituent legal acts provide for the possibility of participation by the republic of lebanon. therefore, the conclusion of the protocol does not imply the exercise of powers under the various sectoral policies provided for in the programmes, which are exercised when the programmes are established. that's why i'm in favour.

‒ under the european neighbourhood policy (enp), the gradual opening-up of european union (eu) programmes and agencies to partner countries is one of many measures to promote reform, modernisation and transition in these countries. on 18 june 2007, the commission launched negotiations for the signature of framework agreements with the enp partner countries. to date, protocols have been signed with armenia, georgia, israel, jordan, moldova, morocco and ukraine. in december 2013, lebanon expressed its interest in participating in the wide range of programmes open to these partner countries. the protocol includes a framework agreement on the general principles governing the participation of the republic of lebanon in eu programmes and contains standard provisions similar to those applied to all other partner countries concerned. the horizontal framework established by the protocol, whose main objective is to establish financial and technical rules allowing lebanon to participate in certain eu programmes, lays down principles for economic, financial and technical cooperation, allowing lebanon to receive eu assistance, in particular in the financial field, in accordance with the established programmes. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report.

‒ the european union and monaco have negotiated an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information aimed at improving tax cooperation and compliance with international tax obligations, which represents an important step forward in the context of ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. the new agreement will enable the tax administrations of the member states and monaco to correctly and unequivocally identify the taxpayers concerned, to apply and enforce their tax laws in cross-border situations, to assess the likelihood of tax evasion occurring and to avoid unnecessary further investigations.
in writing. the agreement signed this year on the automatic exchange of financial account information, which aims to improve international tax cooperation, is a step forward in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. the new agreement will automatically exchange information on financial accounts held in their territories by residents of each country, starting in 2018, for information collected from january 2017. the aim is to address situations where a taxpayer seeks to conceal income or capital assets for which taxes have not been paid. the agreement aims to ensure that monaco applies measures equivalent to the eu legal framework as updated in december 2014 (with the amendment to the administrative cooperation directive, 'dac2') and is in compliance with the procedures for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts promoted by the oecd at global level. as a result of the new agreement, it is envisaged that the tax administrations of the member states and monaco will be able to:- correctly and unequivocally identify the taxpayers concerned;- administer and apply their tax laws in cross-border situations;- assess the likelihood of tax evasion;- avoid unnecessary further investigations. we voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco, which provides for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec.
‒ in order to improve tax cooperation and compliance with international tax obligations, the european union and monaco have negotiated an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information. the agreement shows significant progress in efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and updates the 2004 agreement, which ensured that monaco would apply measures equivalent to those provided for in the eu directive on taxation of savings income. under the new agreement, as of 2018, eu member states and monaco will automatically exchange information collected from 1 january 2017 onwards about financial accounts held in their territories by residents of the other party. the purpose of this exchange is to prevent situations where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital corresponding to income or assets for which taxes have not been paid. i therefore vote in favour of this report.
