‒ in order to ensure a uniform and effective application throughout the european union of all measures of the recovery plan adopted between 2012 and 2014, this proposal aims to integrate them into a regulation. the proposal contains technical measures, such as those relating to live transfer and caging operations of bluefin tuna, including also measures on the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate bluefin tuna quantities and releases, catch reporting requirements and the implementation of the iccat regional observation programme.
in writing. ‒ this report focuses on the legislative proposal published by the commission to update the previous directive on the conservation of bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean regions, which had been in force since 2009. this multiannual plan is part of the new common fisheries policy (cfp). the multiannual plans have potential, but they suffer from some of the limitations and constraints inherent in the cfp itself. there are positive aspects, which we highlight: - the establishment of quotas takes account of the guidelines of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat); - the regulation is being extended to include a number of amendments that give value to traditional fishing techniques and coastal fishing, which are considered to be sustainable techniques, in particular through the use of objective criteria for the allocation of quotas at national level; - the role of iccat observers is being enhanced. the trend of increasing bluefin tuna stocks has led iccat to increase the quota by 20%. we are in favour of a management of fisheries resources based on scientific knowledge, and the measures adopted under this plan seem appropriate. we voted in favour. we reiterate the need to increase the portuguese bluefin tuna quota, a just aspiration of azorean fishermen.
‒ this proposal aims to transpose into union law the measures of the multiannual bluefin tuna (bft) recovery plan in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) 1 at its annual sessions between 2012 and 2014. this legislative initiative aims to ensure the uniform and effective implementation of the latest measures of the iccat multiannual recovery plan for bft throughout the european union. the relevant conservation and management measures set out in the iccat recommendations are not directly applicable to individual vessels or union nationals. it is therefore necessary to transpose into union law the iccat measures concerning bft adopted in 2012, 2013 and 2014. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) of the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo), responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas, to which the eu is a contracting party, has the authority to adopt decisions (recommendations) for the conservation and management of fisheries in its area of competence. those acts are binding and should be transposed into union law. bluefin tuna is the most important species regulated by iccat. fishermen have made efforts to bring their catches into line with the total allowable catch, from 33 000 tonnes before the recovery plan to the minimum value in 2012 (12 900 tonnes). the stock has evolved positively and the tac has been increasing, reaching 15 821 tonnes in 2015 for the eu of 9 372,9 tonnes. i agree with the rapporteur on three points in particular: firstly, on the importance of the exact transposition of the iccat recommendations and their non-extrapolation; secondly, on the regrettable absence of the ep from the international negotiations; and lastly, on the need to take account of the specificities of the different tuna fishing gear, in particular the artisanal and traditional gear.
‒ the european union is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), which is the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas. bluefin tuna is the most important species regulated by iccat, which in 2006 adopted a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna until 2022. following this plan, it is found that the bluefin tuna biomass has been increasing in recent years. this plan provides for a gradual reduction in the level of the total allowable catch (tac), fishing restrictions in certain zones and periods, a new minimum size for catches, measures related to sport and recreational fishing activities as well as fishing and farming capacities and the strengthening of the iccat joint international inspection programme. following the evaluation of the measures adopted by this recovery plan between 2012 and 2014, this proposal decides to integrate them into a regulation, with a view to ensuring a more effective and simpler application of these measures in the waters of the european union. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the gato report because i agree with the balance achieved in the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. i would like to stress the amendments proposed by the european socialist group to pay particular attention to the preservation and prosperity of small-scale, artisanal and traditional fishermen who use traps and other selective fishing methods and to the encouragement of such methods so that they are not penalized by the criteria for allocating national quotas.
‒ cod, herring and sprat account for more than 94% of the catches in the baltic sea in recent years. the baltic sea is a nearly enclosed body of water in which these three species are omnipresent and interact continuously. it is therefore of the utmost importance to ensure that the rules allow for the interactions between the species covered to be recognised, in particular the influence of cod on herring and sprat stocks and vice versa. given the strong influence of biological interactions and environmental effects on the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea, it is appropriate to be able to adapt the rates and exploitation patterns of these stocks in the light of the evolution of scientific knowledge on those interactions and on the evolution of environmental conditions.
‒ the multiannual plan, one of the instruments underpinning the common fisheries policy (cfp) 2012 reform has as its primary objective to maintain stocks above levels that will allow a maximum sustainable yield. the proposed amendments to this effect have some positive aspects, such as the shortening of the periods between assessments, which could allow for ecologically appropriate catch levels, facilitating a socioeconomic approach to fishing in this region and an equally more appropriate approach to the protection of by-catch species. the report limits the commission's powers to take ancillary acts without consulting parliament and the council. we advocate the practice of consultation and participation not only of the regional advisory councils but also of the member states. there is a trend towards relaxing the limits and time periods to reach the levels needed for the sustainability of stocks, in particular by increasing the target range of mortality rates, and the minimum level of spawning biomass, or by making the proposed limits for 2015 to be met only in 2020. the multiannual plans have potential, but they suffer from some of the limitations and constraints inherent in the cfp itself.
‒ the objective of this proposal is to establish a management plan for the baltic cod, herring and sprat stocks. the plan should ensure the sustainable exploitation of those stocks and the stability of fishing opportunities, while ensuring that management is based on the latest scientific information on interactions within and between stocks, as well as other elements of the ecosystem and the environment. the specific objective of the initiative is to ensure that the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea are exploited in a sustainable manner, in accordance with the principles of maximum sustainable yield and an ecosystem-based approach to fisheries management. to that end, the stocks concerned should be fished at levels capable of producing the maximum sustainable yield. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. the purpose of this proposal is to establish a framework for the management of multiple species of the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, where these three species are the main target of fishing. cod, herring and sprat account for more than 94% of the catches in the baltic sea in recent years. i agree with the rapporteur that the multi-species management plan for the baltic sea is the right choice. the multi-species management approach is much more effective than the single-species management approach. the plan shall provide for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of those stocks and the stability of fishing opportunities and, consequently, of the livelihoods of fishermen. i also share the rapporteur's position on the protection of cod stocks during spawning and on the protection of small-scale artisanal fishing. given the innovative and pioneering nature of the multi-species management plan, i advocate its analysis and consequently revision after the third year of its validity, in order to ensure the desired flexibility of the plan.
‒ given the characteristics of the water body of this sea, these three species are ubiquitous and interact continuously, so it is of the utmost importance to ensure that regulations recognise the interactions between them. cod, herring and sprat are important components of the baltic ecosystem and, given the strong influence of biological interactions and environmental effects on the stocks of these species, it is desirable to be able to adapt exploitation patterns for these stocks in the light of the evolution of the latest scientific knowledge on those interactions and on the evolution of environmental conditions. this report reflects agreement with the commission's proposal on the integration of balanced and sustainable exploitation of these species, which i support and therefore voted in favour of.
‒ i voted in favour of the wałęsa report on the multiannual plan for the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea, as i consider it a crucial step towards the implementation of the reform of the common fisheries policy. this plan is the first multiannual eu management plan under the reform of the common fisheries policy and will serve as a model for other sea basin plans. the objective is to establish a multi-species fisheries plan aimed at restoring, achieving and maintaining the populations of cod, herring and sprat species in the baltic sea above levels that can generate the maximum sustainable yield, while minimising as much as possible the impact on other species such as seabirds and the marine environment in general.
‒ in 2011, the commission presented a proposal on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial matters. this measure is part of a package of instruments designed to make life easier for transnational couples, which are becoming increasingly common in the european union. however, no consensus could be reached in the council, which has exclusive competence in these matters and is bound by unanimity. a group of 18 member states, including portugal, therefore wished to take the measures forward, using the enhanced cooperation mechanism. it is this enhanced cooperation which is adopted today, the text of which welcomes the significant proposals of the european parliament made during the first negotiating procedure between all the member states. in the context of enhanced cooperation, the european parliament has to assess, among other criteria, the respect for national competences, which is the case here. the competences of the member states in the field of family law, in particular as regards the recognition of marriage, shall be fully respected. i therefore support this report.
‒ this regulation will be a very useful tool for international couples in the european union. it covers, in matters of matrimonial property regimes, the applicable jurisdiction and law, and the recognition and enforcement of judgments. however, it excludes from its scope, inter alia, questions relating to the capacity of spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of a marriage, maintenance obligations and the succession of the deceased spouse. the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law is therefore safeguarded. i believe that this proposal for a regulation is clearly in the interest of the union and its international partners. it will help to eliminate many cases of confusion and legal difficulty.
‒ the report approves the european commission's proposal on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regimes. the regulation will be a useful tool for international couples in the eu. today, as a result of the high mobility of people between eu member states, couples face a number of bureaucratic difficulties when dealing with property or division issues, when divorcing or when one of the partners dies. there are problems when property is acquired in different member states, for example. this regulation covers jurisdiction, the applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial matters. however, its scope does not cover issues such as the legal capacity of spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of a marriage, maintenance obligations or the succession of property of a deceased spouse. the regulation also does not affect social security rights or pension rights in the event of divorce. the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law is preserved. nor does the regulation affect the substantive law of the member states on matrimonial property regimes. we supported the opening of the process of cooperation between states on this matter and we voted in favour of this report.
‒ the purpose of this proposal is to create a clear legal framework in the european union for the determination of the competent court and the law applicable to matrimonial property regimes and to facilitate the circulation of decisions and acts in this field between the different member states. the aim of this proposal is to establish a complete set of rules of private international law applicable to matrimonial property regimes. it therefore covers jurisdiction, the applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters. the rules laid down apply exclusively to situations of a transnational nature. the cross-border effect requirement of article 81 (3) is thus fulfilled. this proposal concerns only the matrimonial property regime and does not define the institution of marriage or require the recognition of a marriage in another member state. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the regulation covers, in matters of matrimonial property regimes, jurisdiction and the applicable law, as well as the recognition and enforcement of judgments. however, matters relating to the capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of a marriage, maintenance obligations and the succession of the deceased spouse are excluded from its jurisdiction. it is important to emphasise that the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law is safeguarded. the regulation also clearly defines the court with jurisdiction to rule on applications for marriage licenses. i believe that this proposal is in the interest of the european union, as it provides clarity, legal certainty and legal certainty, particularly for so-called international couples.
‒ this proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial matters was blocked by a lack of unanimity in the negotiations between the member states and was referred to parliament after an enhanced cooperation procedure. since this is a special legislative procedure under article 81 (3) tfeu, the european parliament has been consulted to deliver its opinion. the regulation deals with family law matters with crossborder implications, and lays down a set of measures of significant importance for international couples in the european union as regards jurisdiction, scope, recognition and enforcement of decisions. the autonomy of the member states is safeguarded, taking into account the parliament's request for the maintenance of competence in matters of matrimonial property regimes, the capacity of spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of a marriage, as well as maintenance obligations and the succession of the deceased spouse. as it is a regulation of major interest to the eu and to international couples, in that it removes ambiguities and facilitates the simplification and interpretation of the crossborder matrimonial regime, and as all the proposals put forward by parliament have been taken into account, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in 2011, the commission put forward a proposal on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions on the property consequences of registered partnerships, commonly referred to in our system as 'de facto unions'. this measure is part of a package of instruments designed to make life easier for transnational couples, which are becoming increasingly common in the european union. however, no consensus could be reached in the council, which has exclusive competence in these matters and is bound by unanimity. a group of 18 member states, including portugal, therefore wished to take the measures forward, using the enhanced cooperation mechanism. it is this enhanced cooperation which is adopted today, the text of which welcomes the significant proposals of the european parliament made during the first negotiating procedure between all the member states. in the context of enhanced cooperation, the european parliament has to assess, among other criteria, the respect for national competences, which is the case here. the competences of the member states in the field of family law, in particular as regards the recognition of de facto unions, shall be fully respected. i therefore support this report.
in writing. ‒ there are about 16 million international couples in the eu. the parallel litigation in different countries, the complexity of the proceedings and the resulting high legal costs represent an estimated €1.1 billion per year. i think it is important to clarify which national court has jurisdiction to help international couples - united by marriage or registered partnership - manage their property or divide it in the event of divorce, separation or death (rules of jurisdiction) and which law applies when the laws of different countries are potentially applicable to the proceedings (rules of applicable law). the new rules should also facilitate the recognition and enforcement in one member state of a judgment on a matter of property law given in another member state.
‒ the report approves the european commission's proposal on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions on property regimes in registered partnerships. the regulation will be a useful tool for international couples/partnerships in the eu. today, as a result of the high mobility of people between eu member states, couples face a number of bureaucratic difficulties when dealing with property or division issues, when divorcing or when one of the partners dies. there are problems when property is acquired in different member states, for example. this regulation covers jurisdiction, the applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial matters. however, its scope does not cover issues such as the legal capacity of spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of a marriage, maintenance obligations or the succession of property of a deceased spouse. the regulation also does not affect social security rights or pension rights in the event of divorce. the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law is preserved. nor does the regulation affect the substantive law of the member states in matrimonial/registered partnership systems. we supported the opening of the process of cooperation between states on this matter and we voted in favour of this report.
‒ the purpose of this proposal is to establish a clear legal framework in the european union for the determination of the court having jurisdiction and the law applicable to the property consequences of registered partnerships and to facilitate the circulation of decisions and acts in this field between the different member states. the aim of this proposal is to establish a complete set of rules of private international law applicable to the property effects of registered partnerships. it therefore covers jurisdiction, the applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments on the property consequences of registered partnerships. the rules laid down apply exclusively to situations of a transnational nature. the cross-border effect requirement of article 81 (3) is thus fulfilled. this proposal concerns only the property effects of registered partnerships, and does not define the institution of the registered partnership or require recognition of a registered partnership in another member state. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the regulation covers, in respect of the property consequences of registered partnerships, the applicable jurisdiction and law, as well as the recognition and enforcement of judgments. however, it excludes from its scope, inter alia, questions relating to the capacity of partners, the existence, validity or recognition of a partnership, maintenance obligations and the succession of the deceased partner. it is important to emphasise that the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law is safeguarded. the regulation also clearly defines the court with jurisdiction to rule on applications for the property rights of registered partnerships. i believe that this proposal is in the interest of the european union, as it provides clarity, legal certainty and legal certainty, particularly for so-called international couples.
in writing. this proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships creates a simplified european legal framework, ensuring compliance with the principle of the unity of law, within the legal regime applicable to the property of couples who are nationals of different member states. in fact, these couples are becoming increasingly representative within the european union. following parliament's recommendations, which have now been duly taken up by the commission, and in order to ensure that the principle of subsidiarity is respected, the proposal seems to me to be balanced, since it does not conflict with the member states' powers, particularly as regards registered partnerships and their property effects. moreover, the document enshrines the so-called public policy clause, the provision of which seems to me to be essential, by ensuring that, in this context, the application of a provision of the law of a member state may be refused only if such application is manifestly incompatible with the public policy of the forum (see article 31 of the proposal). i therefore vote in favour.
‒ as in the other proposal on matrimonial property regimes, parliament is consulted on the report in the context of the proposal for a council regulation (also on enhanced cooperation) on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions on the property consequences of registered partnerships. in practice, what this regulation intends to do in this case is to clarify the rules applicable to registered partnerships in cross-border situations, thus covering couples who have assets in another eu country. it is therefore a highly advantageous instrument for international couples in the eu, covering jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions on the property consequences of registered partnerships. the question of the capacity of the partners, the existence, validity or recognition of a partnership, and maintenance obligations and the succession of the deceased partner, in order to ensure the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law, is excluded. given that this legislative proposal will bring more legal certainty and security by clarifying and simplifying a previously dubious matrimonial and partnership regime, i considered it essential to vote in favour of its adoption.
‒ the democratic republic of congo is currently facing a serious humanitarian and security situation, with signs of deterioration in the eastern part of the country, where dozens of armed groups are carrying out massacres and widespread sexual violence and recruitment of children, with an estimated 7.5 million people in need of assistance. i support the present resolution which condemns these acts and calls for an end to belligerent violence with a view to a peaceful and sustainable resolution of the conflict and calls on the international criminal court to investigate these abuses, and that those responsible for war crimes, crimes against humanity, the recruitment of child soldiers and sexual violence against minors and adults be identified and punished in accordance with national and international criminal law. i also condemn the attacks on humanitarian workers and the blocking of access to humanitarian aid.
in writing. ‒ between october 2014 and may 2016, in the territories of beni, lubero and butembo, more than 1160 people were brutally killed, more than 1470 people are missing, many homes, health centers and schools were burned and many women, men and children were victims of sexual violence. humanitarian actors estimate that 7.5 million people are currently in need of assistance and the ongoing conflict and military operations have also led to the internal displacement of 1.5 million people and forced more than 400,000 to flee the country. i therefore express my deep concern at the escalation of violence and the worrying and increasingly serious humanitarian situation in the drc, and i agree with the call for the belligerents to put an immediate end to the violence, lay down their arms, release all children in their ranks and promote dialogue with a view to a peaceful and sustainable resolution of the conflict.
‒ the situation in the democratic republic of congo (drc) is worrying and serious, and the intentions of this resolution are to highlight this concern. this resolution is part of a process of interference and destabilisation in the region, which aims to restore the power and control of the former european colonial powers over the immense natural resources of the country, thus exploiting the conflicts there, using them to their advantage. the resolution conceals the destabilising role of european countries in the drc, for example belgium. there is no call for accountability, no attack on multinationals and their role in financing armed groups. he has not a single word to condemn nato's militarist and interventionist role, nor the strengthening of its military presence through the us military command africom. underlying the criticism of the un mission monusco, whose role and intervention must of course be controlled, is the desire to bring other forces and perhaps nato into the field. it is also intended to contribute to the destabilisation of the political situation in the country as elections approach. we are in favour of non-proliferation of weapons, non-militarisation of the region, support for a political and peaceful solution to conflicts, the sovereignty of peoples and the dismantling of africom.
‒ security in the drc continues to deteriorate in the eastern part of the country, where dozens of armed groups remain active, with many reports of massacres, recruitment and use of children by armed groups, widespread sexual and gender-based violence. the international community as a whole must therefore make efforts to find a peaceful solution to this serious conflict with serious consequences for the population, especially the most vulnerable - women, the elderly and children. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ in 2013, the congolese army brought the designated rebel group m23 under control, raising hopes that the environment of insecurity in eastern congo would evolve towards pacification. however, several armed groups remain active, and the environment of insecurity, ethnic and political divisions, and conflict in the mining sector remains. recently, radical groups have committed a number of human rights violations, including massacres of civilians and abductions of aid workers. the eu is providing humanitarian aid to the democratic republic of congo and in this context should use its influence to promote permanent political dialogue, both with the other international institutions monitoring the situation and with the countries in the region and the congolese authorities, with a view to putting an end to the violations of rights and crimes against humanity and to restoring peace and security in the region. i therefore vote in favour of this report, since i consider it important that the european union should play an active role in respecting human rights and in bringing peace and political stability to the region.
‒ the situation of insecurity in the east of the democratic republic of the congo is today - as it has been for several decades - deeply alarming. in eastern provinces, armed conflicts that have lasted for more than 20 years have escalated, with frequent reports of massacres, recruitment of children, gender discrimination and widespread sexual violence. considered the bloodiest conflict since world war ii, the ongoing humanitarian and military crisis in the democratic republic of congo has already caused the death of some 5 million people. i condemn all those responsible for these conflicts and stress the importance of the procedures aimed at their denunciation and punishment in accordance with the rules of national and international criminal law. i also note that the attacks on the staff of humanitarian organisations, which are primarily concerned with the imperatives of independence, neutrality and impartiality, are truly deplorable. i therefore support this joint resolution and stress the importance of the european union and its member states maintaining assistance to the people of the democratic republic of the congo.
‒ the climate of civil war by armed groups in eastern congo remains extremely worrying, with the recruitment and use of children for war scenarios and systematic sexual violence against vulnerable population groups. it is important that the european parliament expresses its strongest condemnation of these atrocities and expresses its deepest solidarity with the congolese people, giving a clear signal that it is following this catastrophic humanitarian situation closely and with great concern. the international criminal court should conduct investigations to establish whether abuses have occurred and consider the need to investigate the crimes allegedly committed. the eu, for its part, must adopt a coherent policy on arms and raw materials trade, while also ensuring that the negotiations on agreements in this region are consistent with the values of peace, stability, development and human rights. it should also consider the possibility of applying sanctions to those responsible for these massacres in eastern congo. i therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because i consider that we are facing very serious violations of the most basic and essential human rights and because i subscribe to the substance of the measures contained in this motion for a resolution.
‒ the ef2020 strategic framework was taken over by the commission in cooperation with the member states in 2014, and in 2015 the commission and the council published a report on the complex outlook of the framework. i support the krasnodebski report and, in particular, the new generation of working groups under the framework with a greater representation of the different parties by including a greater number of experts, young workers, representatives of civil society, teachers, etc. i also support the creation of an informal coordination body including several high-level commission officials, representatives of civil society, social partners and the ep committee on culture and education, with the aim of ensuring better coordination, policy coherence and follow-up of the ef2020 recommendations. stressing the need to focus more on the quality of education at all levels and the importance of general basic skills in teaching and learning, such as ict, mathematics, critical thinking, foreign languages, mobility, etc., which enable young people to adapt easily to a changing social and economic context.
‒ the joint report published by the commission and the council addresses the problem of the complex picture of the ef 2020 strategic framework, which has not always been clearly understood by some participants or by a part of the community at large. some member states should continue to improve the way they interact with formal and informal structures, ensuring that the right people are sent to the right meetings and that the use of substitutes is minimised. urgent action is therefore needed at national and european level, within the framework of the ef 2020 strategic framework, in the area of education and training for adult asylum seekers newly arrived in europe. given that education is key to integration and employability, failure to address this challenge by national systems could lead to a worsening of social disparities and cultural segregation and thus intensify the existing trend towards the formation of parallel societies.
‒ cooperation and exchange of good practice between member states in the fields of education and training can be positive. however, it is important to examine the content, background of ef 2020 and its priorities. the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training (ef 2020) is part of the eu's neoliberal approach. both the initial and the new priorities seek to harmonise the education and training systems of the member states with the eu's economic and employment policies. the report contains positive aspects, critical of the current state of education and training. but it cannot differentiate itself from the eu's dominant approach. mobility, employability and entrepreneurship are examples. under ef 2020, education and training are placed at the service of market demands. a reductive and erroneous view, which we disagree with. although we agree with some of the points in the report, taken in isolation, they are contradictory to the overall view underlying it. the objectives of reducing early school leaving and increasing the number of young people with a higher education qualification should not be met at the expense of quality in education, the report says. i'll take that. but what are the 'relevant qualifications and competences'? relevant to who? the devil (also) is in the details.
‒ education and training should not only be designed to meet the needs of the labour market, but also be an intrinsic value in themselves, since education plays as important a role in the development of ethics and civic responsibility as it does in respecting the democratic principles on which europe was founded. education should contribute to the personal development, mutual respect and growth of young people, in order to make them self-motivated, responsible and conscious citizens, with civic, social and cross-cultural skills, as well as qualified professionals. inclusive and high-quality training and education are essential for cultural, economic and social development. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the 'education and training 2020' strategy establishes cooperation between the union and its member states in the field of education and training, adopting a lifelong learning perspective in order to ensure coherence between the various measures taken to promote education and training from childhood to adulthood. cooperation in this area is voluntary and actions at union level should therefore support and complement national actions. education and training are important pillars for training as citizens and for acquiring the professional skills needed to enter the labour market. training and education also play a key role in the delivery of union policies, in particular the europe 2020 strategy, the digital single market, the european agenda for security and the investment plan for europe. in this respect, i am voting in favour, as i consider it crucial that the member states should seek to make the most of this cooperation with a view to promoting lifelong learning as a decisive driver of economic and social development in the union.
‒ education and training are essential to enable citizens to acquire the professional skills and knowledge needed to integrate into an increasingly competitive and innovative labour market, fostering a sense of identity and a culture based on respect for common european values. in a context where youth unemployment rates remain at worrying levels and where demographic challenges stemming from, among other factors, the current migration crisis are putting today's education and training systems in the european union to the test, the review of the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training (sef 2020), which has been drawn up by the commission in cooperation with the member states, is, in my view, of extraordinary relevance. in this area, the document emphasises the role of parents and the need to develop positive parenting, as well as the role of educators in integrating migrants and solving problems caused by the harmonisation of european educational practices. education is crucial for integration and employability. we therefore need new measures at national and european level to improve education systems and to take account of the importance of training and education for adult asylum seekers and their children. i vote in favour.
in writing. the evaluation of the strategic framework for education and training 2020 was carried out in 2014 and recommendations were considered to increase the added value of the framework and optimise its effectiveness. although the last decade has seen an increase in the number of people attending formal education, europe is unfortunately experiencing unprecedented levels of youth unemployment, affecting all levels of education, including young graduates. efforts to cultivate the knowledge economy and promote social inclusion were reflected in the europe 2020 strategy's major dual objective of setting a minimum threshold for education and increasing participation in higher education. education and training are important for the acquisition of professional skills and knowledge necessary for the training of motivated and fulfilled workers. i voted in favour of this report because i recognise the importance that these policies play in the formation of an active and responsible citizenry.
‒ the development of renewable energy sources requires a new approach that makes them the fundamental pillar of the european union's energy model. we have a responsibility to fight climate change and reduce our dependence on energy resources from the rest of the world so that we can organise our production model, create quality jobs and be at the forefront of developing technologies for energy transition. the transition to a sustainable energy production model is therefore a social priority that cannot be left to the market alone, we must understand that regulation and democratic participation are necessary to avoid social and environmental externalities. the development of renewable energy will contribute to ensuring energy security and sovereignty, ending energy poverty and fostering the eu's economic development and technological leadership in combating climate change. the future r&d strategy should focus on facilitating the development of smart grids and smart cities. the electrification of transport, intelligent vehicle charging and 'vehicle-to-grid' technologies will contribute to improving energy efficiency and to unlocking the potential of renewable energy sources. i therefore support this report.

the rapporteur's intentions were frustrated in part by a difficult context, arising from the composition and balance of power in this parliament. the amendments to the original version of the report did not improve it. the report nevertheless contains some positive aspects which lead us to support it. the report rightly points out that the transition to a sustainable energy production model is a social priority which cannot be left to the market alone. on the contrary, we must understand that regulation and democratic participation are necessary to avoid serious social and environmental externalities. we must prevent energy oligopolies from being able to define europe's energy future. we would add that a condition for this democratic regulation of the sector is that it be owned and managed democratically by the public. this sector regulation, in which the sovereign choices of each member state must weigh decisively, should solve the many problems hampering the development of renewable energies. public investment, democratic control and a stable framework for investment should be encouraged in order to facilitate collective and democratic energy management and ensure a fully sovereign, efficient and clean energy model by 2050, according to the report. the report advocates an ambitious political push to meet the targets set.
‒ the eu as a whole is on track to meet its 2020 renewable energy targets, although additional, strengthened measures are needed in some member states. we must therefore all continue to work together to achieve the stated objectives, to make the planet more sustainable for future generations. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ directive 2009/28/eu sets the european union as a target of 20% of energy consumption from renewable sources by 2020. in this context, it is essential to ensure that the commission's monitoring is strengthened to ensure that member states not only meet the objectives set out in the directive, but also adapt measures to that end. this includes measures to improve access to funding channels, or even the creation of a financial mechanism at eu level to support the implementation of these measures, as well as improving administrative procedures to take account of cost-benefit schemes. combining renewable energy and energy efficiency policies are key factors that can help reduce the eu's energy dependence, as the eu imports more than half of its energy consumption, representing 20% of total imports. i therefore vote in favour of this report, as i believe it is important that the european union has a long-term strategy to encourage investment in renewable energy.
‒ the european union has done exemplary work on renewable energy. this report, a true statement of science on the relevant social and environmental externalities of today's energy production models, warns of the need to regulate the sector, ensuring its competitiveness and preventing, for example, energy oligopolies. that said, in my view, and in the view of the group of which i am a member, this report has done well in emphasising renewable energy as one of the most effective ways of reducing dependence on fossil fuels and at the same time contributing to the creation of the so-called low-carbon economy. the report also encourages competitiveness and cost-effectiveness in the renewable energy market, without prejudice to the diversity and safeguarding of member states' competences in this field. and, not least, the document favours a sustainable energy system, in which dependence on subsidies is gradually supplied - and abolished - in a self-sufficient internal market regulated by the commission, especially as regards the price of energy. from what has been said, my vote is in favour.
‒ the future of the european union's energy model is fundamentally based on the development of renewable energy sources. to achieve this desired model, it is imperative that we combat climate change and reduce our dependence on external energy (especially fossil fuels), by creating our own production model, which is more environmentally friendly, generating quality jobs and fostering the creation of a new technological (strategic) era in this field. this energy production model must be a social priority, regulated and with broad participation of businesses and citizens, not dependent on the oligopolistic market and not entailing serious social and environmental externalities. directive 2009/28/ec is the anchor legislative instrument underpinning the entire energy transition process to be undertaken by member states by 2020, although more ambitious targets need to be set in the light of what was recently established in the paris agreement. i therefore support the rapporteur's view that this model of energy production must be developed, regulated at european level and made into an engine of economic growth capable of encouraging public investment, generating wealth, creating jobs and ensuring an energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable model in the long term.

in writing. ‒ energy efficiency directive 2012/27/eu establishes a common framework for promotion measures in the european union to ensure the achievement of the union's 20% energy efficiency target by 2020. achieving good levels of energy efficiency is also key to achieving the climate objectives set out at the paris summit in december 2015 and to reducing the european union's energy dependence on imports. although the implementation of the directive has triggered a number of positive changes in the member states, shortcomings in its implementation call into question its full effectiveness and the achievement of the objectives set out in this framework. in this regard, the directive should be revised in some of its aspects in order to promote a transition to a more sustainable and secure energy system and to ensure that consumers have access to information on the conditions and sources of energy supply, including through increased transparency and clarity in billing. in this respect, i vote in favour of this report as i consider the revision and full implementation of the directive to be essential if the energy efficiency objectives are to be achieved.
‒ the european union today has a key role to play in promoting intergenerational responsibility, with a particular responsibility to foster an energy system in which current generations are committed to fighting climate change for the benefit of future generations. in this line of reasoning, this report rightly stresses the importance of energy efficiency in meeting the so-called 'climate targets' and the need for a flexible and unbureaucratized energy system, which monitors and clarifies the definition of smes and state aid. however, i am of the opinion that the report is flawed. on the one hand, it enshrines an unsatisfactory solution to the 40% energy efficiency target for 2030 (also contained in the resolutions of 5 february 2014, 26 november 2014 and 15 october 2015). at the same time, the document is vague on the terms of decarbonisation in 2050, as much more could have been done in this area. finally, and this is not the least, the report does not include the minimum funding targets which, in my view, should be set at member state level. in that sense, my vote is against it.

the decision to leave the eu is a major political event. it represents a fundamental change in the process of european capitalist integration and a new level of struggle for those who are fighting for a europe of the workers and peoples. the british people have sovereignly decided the destinies of their country. this must be respected, all the more so since this referendum took place in the context of gigantic and unacceptable pressure and blackmail, in particular from the large transnational economic groups and the large financial capital, as well as from organisations such as the imf, the oecd and the eu itself. this result is also a victory over fear, inevitability, submission and catastrophism. without ignoring the multiple motivations that were present in the call for this referendum and in a campaign driven by reactionary elements and open political manipulation which we oppose and reject head-on , the results of the referendum unquestionably express a rejection of eu policies. this referendum must be seen as an opportunity to confront and solve the real problems of the peoples, to question the whole process of capitalist integration and to open up a new and different path of cooperation in europe, of social progress and peace.
the british electorate has overwhelmingly decided that the country should no longer be part of the european union. this decision should be implemented safeguarding the interests and the future of the european project. the negotiation of the withdrawal process needs to be transparent and expeditious, following the formal request of the british government, in accordance with the provisions of the treaties. the european union will have to interpret the reasons for what has happened and take action. it was fear, in particular fear of unregulated globalisation, competition in the labour market and the erosion of rights and guarantees, exploited by populists, that led to the decision of the british people. the risk of this situation being exploited in other countries exists and must be combated politically. the eu must therefore act and put in place a strong programme of action to restore citizens' confidence in the european project as a path of peace, tolerance and a response to people's concrete problems. a process that can lead to a convention that consolidates change but that must not begin with it. we need immediate action, to make it happen and to counter fear with smart policies that focus on solutions to people's problems.
in the first place, the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments tabled by the committee on budgets. it is unacceptable and it demonstrates the choices of the majority in this parliament with regard to respect (or lack thereof) for democracy and the sovereignty of the peoples. in the face of a legitimate and sovereign decision, a veiled blackmail is used, a kind of 'revenge' is rehearsed against the british people, on whom stigmas are cast which constitute immense dangers in a context in which the eu's policies - antisocial and disrespectful of the sovereignty of the peoples - are giving way to the growth of the far right. the resolution seeks to trigger a process of so-called 'negotiation' which in reality aims to turn the realisation of the will of a people into a real torture for that people and for a sovereign state, all within the framework of article 50 of the lisbon treaty. this resolution is contrary to reality. it is a leap forward that seeks to ignore the underlying problem that the british referendum expresses: the people of europe are increasingly expressing their opposition to the eu and its policies. another europe is needed. a europe which rejects exploitation and oppression and is based on cooperation, peace, solidarity, mutual respect and the defence of the sovereignty of peoples.

‒ the european union has a visa policy, in particular with regard to the short-stay visa waiver. this exemption is defined at european level, since it is valid for all member states except the united kingdom and ireland. the various conditions for the conclusion of the agreement include reciprocity. in other words, european citizens no longer need a visa either. it is up to the european parliament to give its approval to the agreement for its establishment, which is given. for all these reasons and because this agreement is the culmination of the deepening of relations with the republic of peru, i am voting in favour of its conclusion.
‒ the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and peruvian citizens to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. this agreement will boost tourism and help to intensify trade and investment relations. peru recorded one of the highest economic growth rates in latin america (5% in 2013 and 2.4% in 2014). the country has been growing continuously by more than 80% over the last ten years, placing it among the top ten countries in the world with the highest growth rate over the period under review. moreover, the eu remains the largest investor in peru, accounting for more than 50% of total foreign direct investment in sectors such as the extractive industries, banking and finance.
‒ the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the member states of the european union and for citizens of peru travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days for each 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (common, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders), regardless of the purpose of stay, except for the pursuit of a paid activity. as in the case of other similar agreements recently approved, we are not opposed to this facilitation of the movement of people, and we have voted in favour of this recommendation, in contrast to the rapporteur's instrumental approach (focused on promoting business).
this agreement shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the official journal of the european union. in order to ensure equal treatment of all eu citizens, a provision has been included in the agreement under which peru may only suspend or terminate the agreement in respect of all member states of the european union and, reciprocally, the union may only suspend or terminate the agreement in respect of all its member states. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ this agreement is part of the effort to deepen the european union's relations with the republic of peru. as regards trade relations, the eu was peru's third largest trading partner in terms of imports and the main recipient of its exports. this agreement could have a strong impact on the tourism sector as it will facilitate the entry and exit of citizens, contributing to strengthening economic, investment and cultural relations between the two continents. the agreement concluded between the union and peru provides for the exemption from the visa requirement of citizens of the union and of peru when travelling to the territory of one of the contracting parties for a period not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period. however, member states which do not fully apply the acquis communautaire in the field of the schengen area are excluded from the application of this agreement. i am voting in favour of this agreement because i believe it will strengthen relations between the union and the republic of peru.
‒ the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and peruvian citizens to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in each 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (common, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders), regardless of the purpose of stay, except for the pursuit of a paid activity. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. this agreement was signed on 14 march 2016 and is provisionally applied subject to the approval of the european parliament. it provides not only for the simplification of the procedure for issuing short-stay visas between the contracting parties but also for the exemption of european union citizens and peruvian citizens from the visa requirement for short stays. i consider that the approval of this agreement is the culmination of the deepening of relations between the european union and the republic of peru. this will also be a means of strengthening cultural and economic relations between the parties, the peruvian economy being one of the fastest growing in south america. at the same time, the republic of peru is a stable democracy, because the agreement will also allow for intensified political dialogue on issues such as human rights and fundamental freedoms. on illegal immigration, the agreement contains - and rightly so - a joint declaration of cooperation, in which both parties recall their commitment to the readmission of irregular immigrants. i therefore voted in favour of this recommendation.

in may 2015, the commission opened negotiations for a bilateral agreement between the european union (eu) and the republic of peru on visa waiver, following an overall positive assessment. the agreement was signed in march 2016 and has been applied provisionally, pending approval by the european parliament. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for eu citizens and peruvian citizens to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days for each 180-day period. this agreement is the result of the deepening of relations between the eu and peru following the trade agreement and constitutes an additional means of intensifying political dialogue. peru has one of the highest economic growth rates in south america, with a continuous growth rate of over 80% over the last 10 years. moreover, it is a country that has demonstrated a relatively stable democracy, linked to the values and principles of democracy, good governance, respect for human rights and the rule of law. as an important partner in latin america with whom balanced political dialogue will be established on a regular basis, i voted in favour of this report.

‒ the main objective of this report is to strike a balanced balance between health and environmental concerns and the competitiveness of the eu manufacturing industry and job creation. this is intended to establish stricter standards for most engines already existing under the current directive 97/68/ec, as well as to extend to new engine power ranges, types of combustion and fuels used, as well as new categories of machinery, with the aim of closing legislative gaps. in addition to the environmental and health benefits for citizens, it contributes to the creation of a harmonised internal market for industry and machinery users, which will facilitate trade and competitiveness and strengthen the eu's external trade with other developed industrial economies. with this legislation, we provide industry with certainty for long-term planning and a stable regulatory environment. i therefore support this report.
‒ despite some recent improvements, air pollution in europe remains a concern. in september 2014, the european commission presented a revised proposal for the approval of emission limits for non-road mobile machinery, which covers a wide range of machinery with internal combustion engines that contribute to air pollution. this is one of the sectors which needs to be regulated, even though it is responsible for a minority of emissions. the committee on the environment, public health and food safety has made some changes to the initial version. among other things, the list of exemptions has been extended. the implementation dates for engines used in river vessels have been modified. we agree that member states should be able to prohibit the use of combustion engines for reasons of health and safety at work, particularly in hotspots where the air quality is poor. the rapporteur was keen to include in the amendments her concerns about possible distortion in the internal market. while agreeing with the aim of simplifying administrative procedures and improving the general conditions of application, we do not follow the rapporteur's views on the internal market. concerns should be focused on the protection of the environment and the health of the population. we voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ non-road mobile machinery (nrmm) covers a wide range of combustion engines installed in machines, ranging from small portable equipment, construction machinery and generator sets to automobiles, locomotives and inland waterway vessels. these engines contribute significantly to air pollution and are responsible for around 15% of nitrogen oxides (nox) and 5% of particulate matter emissions in the eu. this proposal aims to protect human health and the environment and to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market for engines installed in nrmm. it also seeks to address aspects related to competitiveness and compliance. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ environmental sustainability is also key to achieving the climate goals outlined at the paris summit in december 2015, as well as to reducing the european union's dependence on imported energy. this proposal for a regulation takes account of environmental objectives set by the union in setting european union emission limits and type-approval procedures for engines intended for non-road mobile machinery. the proposal for a regulation introduces a number of measures which, if properly implemented, can make a decisive contribution to reducing the environmental impact of these equipment, in particular by promoting the use of more efficient equipment and reducing the use of fossil fuels, channelling funding routes to innovative projects that reduce tailpipe emissions, promoting the use of portable emission measurement systems, controlling the type of imported engines entering the eu market, among other measures. in this respect, i am voting in favour of this proposal, as i consider it essential that the eu should define common rules on the type-approval emission limits of engines for non-road mobile machinery.
‒ this report focuses on a proposal covering a wide range of combustion engines that can be installed on a wide range of machinery, from small handheld equipment to locomotives and boats. in the european union, this range of machinery is responsible for about 15% of nox emissions and 5% of particulate matter emissions. i think it is important to note that the proposal in question contains a very satisfactory set of measures to reduce these emissions, such as the extension of the transitional period granted to companies for the replacement of their machinery, the simplification of the implementation phases of projects to introduce new emission levels, the possibility of replacing old engines with new engines with better environmental performance, a new monitoring system which will ensure that the emissions tested in laboratories are in line with those recorded in the real world and, last but not least, the relevant role given to the european parliament in this matter. i believe that the union is thus working to restore european citizens' confidence in the fulfilment of the obligations imposed on companies in the field of the environment. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
‒ non-road mobile machinery emits, according to commission data, 15% of all nox and 5% of all particulate pollutants in the eu. in order to address this problem, the commission should indeed set stricter standards for most engines already existing under the current directive 97/68/ec, as well as extending it to new engine power ranges, types of combustion and fuels used, in order to close loopholes in the legislation. in addition to the obvious and desirable environmental and health effects for our citizens, this has the advantage of creating a harmonized internal market for industry and machine users and of facilitating trade and competitiveness, ultimately making environmental legislation a commercial opportunity as well. we must try to find a balance between health and environmental concerns, as proposed by the commission, the competitiveness of the eu manufacturing industry and job creation.
‒ this report is on a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on emission limitation and type approval requirements for internal combustion engines of non-road mobile machinery. several urban areas in europe do not fully comply with air quality standards and, to some extent, this quality is compromised by the contribution of harmful emissions from the nrmm (non-road mobile machinery) sector, in the form of gases or particles, to the atmosphere, with serious harm to public health. i therefore wholeheartedly support the commission's proposal to establish stricter standards for most existing engines and to extend them to new engine power ranges, types of combustion and fuels used, and new categories of machinery. for the sake of air quality, the environment and the health of citizens, i voted in favour of this report, which will also bring benefits in terms of harmonising the internal market, facilitating trade and enhancing the competitiveness of the manufacturing industry in the european union.
