in writing. - i voted in favour of the gardini report because i agree with the substantive requirements presented with regard to emission limits and approval procedures for engines to be installed in non-road mobile machinery (nrmm). nrmms have a significant, very negative impact on air pollution, accounting for about 15% of nitrogen oxides (nox) and 5% of particulate matter in the calculation of total eu emissions. while the standards governing road vehicle emissions have become stricter, the same has not been the case in the nrmms. a new legislative framework of equivalent measures is therefore indispensable to achieve the air quality objectives the eu has set itself. as a full member of the emis committee of inquiry, i have advocated transparency in the approval process. i therefore welcome the amendments tabled in this connection, in particular the obligation for manufacturers to make publicly available the co2 emissions determined during the type-approval process.
‒ the response to the refugee crisis facing europe needs to be addressed at several levels: on the one hand, the european union must endeavour to contribute to the political stabilisation and social and economic development of the countries of origin; the european union must also implement the relocation agreement and create the conditions for the integration of the thousands of people fleeing war, terror and death. as regards social and employment integration, it is important that the european union and its member states allow refugees access to social protection systems (e.g. housing, health, education, social and employment protection policies) which ensure the conditions for learning the language and culture of their new country and which accompany the processes of social integration in the community. it is also important that awareness-raising activities be promoted among the host communities in order to prevent and condemn any kind of discrimination, xenophobia and racism. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that all these concerns and proposals are reflected in it.
‒ the process of receiving a refugee can be characterised by three stages: receipt of the application, granting of refugee status and finally integration. despite the temporary nature of refugee status, it can extend over a long period of time and even become a more permanent link, which increases the importance of good integration. given the state of conflict in our neighbourhood - and its likely prolongation in time - and the number of refugees and asylum seekers arriving on our territory, the integration component is of even greater importance in the european context. it should be stressed, however, that this is primarily a matter for the member states and that the union can only provide support. the resolution sets out a series of measures to this end. the focus is on the reorientation and reinforcement of funding to member states, the revision of the 'reception conditions' directive or the expedited operation of the relocation mechanism. it also lists a number of good practices, such as the speedy processing of applications for international protection - without neglecting the individual nature of each case - and access to education, particularly in the field of language. i therefore support this resolution.
in writing. ‒ this is a human crisis on a global scale, but more specifically, it is also a political crisis for which the european union was unprepared and which therefore requires urgent and decisive action by policy-makers, as well as long-term measures that respond to the needs of society and the labour market. all humanitarian migrants, as asylum seekers and refugees, leave their countries abruptly and are therefore the most vulnerable group of all migrants, often suffering from serious health problems and psychosocial disturbances and post-traumatic stress or showing some form of disability. secondly, what makes the issue of social inclusion and the integration of refugees into the labour market complex is the current macroeconomic situation in the european union. finally, what makes the adoption of effective social inclusion and integration measures more problematic is linked to their often unpopular nature in the public eye. i therefore voted in favour of the outlines of the report.
‒ the report reflects the need for the inclusion of refugees in the member states, which necessarily involves integration into the labour market. we have tabled amendments to the report focusing on improving working conditions and social protection, rejecting the 'qualifications' criterion as an exclusionary factor, rejecting the existing legislative and institutional frameworks (dublin regulation, blue card directive, eu-turkey agreement), and advocating the extension of support and integration strategies not only to refugees and asylum seekers but also to migrants. unfortunately, these proposals were not accepted. the report thus has some limitations, such as being uncritical of the criteria with which the eu proposes the 'distribution' of refugees (it calls for a review of the dublin regulation, but does not address the reasonableness of this 'distribution'); it calls for a distinction between refugees and migrants, does not mention those responsible for conflicts in the countries of origin, the inhumane conditions in detention camps or the cruelty of repatriation. nevertheless, the overall document contains guidelines which, if implemented, would have positive consequences, particularly in terms of promoting the social inclusion of refugees.
‒ managing the refugee crisis is probably one of the main challenges facing the european union and its society today, given its scale, its pace and the complexity of its social, political and economic implications. this is first and foremost a humanitarian crisis on a global scale, but more specifically it is also a political crisis for which the european union was not prepared and which therefore requires urgent and decisive action by policy-makers, as well as long-term measures that respond to the needs of society and the labour market. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the high number of refugees is a real test of the union's ability to respond to emergency scenarios. in this context, the response to the refugee crisis must be framed in a coherent and coordinated manner by the union and its member states in a spirit of genuine solidarity. in this sense, the strategy for responding to the refugee crisis must cover not only support for arrivals, in particular through food distribution, support for rescuing shipwrecked vessels, support for the provision of health care, among others, but also in terms of integrating migrants into the host communities. the fight against social exclusion and the integration of refugees into the labour market is a challenge for which the union must develop appropriate and timely response tools, otherwise it will contribute to the increasingly prominent movements of social segregation, such as xenophobic and anti-immigration movements. i therefore vote in favour of this report, as i consider it crucial that the european union has a common and coherent strategy for the refugee crisis.
‒ the report reflects the need for the inclusion of refugees in the member states to be linked to integration into the labour market. it presents limitations in the necessary but non-existent criticism of the relocation mechanisms and the dublin regulation, the distinction between refugees and migrants, or the non-responsibility of the eu for conflicts in the countries of origin, the inhumane conditions of the concentration camps, or the criminal return policy. we do, however, follow some of the concerns and proposals in the report, of which we highlight: - increasing synergies between available financial instruments and the proposal to allocate 25% of the european social fund budget to support refugees;- protecting vulnerable groups such as children and women, including from sexual exploitation and violence;- protecting refugees at work by countering undeclared work practices and forms of serious exploitation or discrimination at work;- effectively guaranteeing access to housing, health, education, social security and labour market services;- the key role of free public education, language teaching, culture, intercultural and interreligious dialogue, non-formal and informal education, lifelong learning and youth and sport policies in promoting integration and inclusion. we voted yes.
‒ the current refugee crisis is a global humanitarian crisis, but it is also a political crisis, which calls for urgent and effective action. this report aims at the integration of refugees into the societies, labour market and education systems of their respective member states. i consider it extremely important that the principle of equal treatment be upheld in this area. member states should ensure that refugees have access to public services, as well as to integration courses, language learning modules and other measures in the field of education and training. in my view, the report provides a satisfactory answer in this respect, without prejudice to the fair distribution of responsibility as provided for in article 80 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). i believe that the basis for successful management of the migration crisis is social inclusion and integration which respects equal treatment and equal opportunities. i therefore vote in favour of this report.
‒ it is our duty to intensify efforts to find quick, effective and equitable ways of creating the conditions for the integration of asylum seekers and refugees into our society. this is only possible if the external and internal policies of the union and its member states are synergistic, complementary, fully implemented in a timely manner and based on solidarity, equitable sharing of responsibilities and respect for international law and human rights. a holistic approach to migration requires that eu external policies demonstrate their ability to tackle the root causes of migration, such as conflict, poverty, lack of freedoms, inequalities and extreme environmental conditions. on the other hand, internal policies on employment, education, social protection and health must also be open, harmonious and sufficiently flexible to turn the challenges posed by migratory pressures into a resource for the economic, social and cultural development of our societies. equal treatment and equal opportunities should always be the guiding principles of social inclusion and integration policies. refugee integration is a challenge, but it can also be an opportunity.
‒ managing the refugee crisis is one of the main challenges facing the european union (eu) today, given its scale and the complexity of its social, political and economic implications. this is a humanitarian crisis on a global scale, but also a political crisis, and it requires urgent, firm and permanent measures which also respond to the needs of society and the labour market in the countries, regions and communities of integration. the new european agenda on migration was adopted with the aim of addressing the difficulties resulting from this extraordinary influx of people and creating a european relocation/resettlement regime. it is therefore necessary to intensify the efforts already made, either through the mechanisms already adopted in this regard or by making additional and effective efforts capable of creating the necessary conditions for the integration of asylum seekers and refugees. this report describes the complexity and nature of this situation, and stresses the urgency of finding a solution based on the principles of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibilities, which is necessary to deal with this common problem, which also requires a common response. i voted in favour of the report because i agree with most of the measures proposed by the rapporteur.
‒ the unprecedented phenomenon of the refugee crisis that is sweeping across europe's borders is one of the greatest challenges of our time. the eu has sought to respond to this humanitarian crisis through enhanced intervention in key areas - economic, political and social - as a way of ensuring the proper integration of refugees into the labour market, in order to promote social cohesion and their full integration into european societies. a comprehensive european strategy in this area requires respect for european fundamental rights, providing adequate reception and decent living conditions, and avoiding the creation of fragmented communities. investments are needed in education, including access to language courses, and access to social protection. in addition, migration can provide opportunities for europe's economic growth and development and rejuvenation. the resources of the european social fund need to be increased as a means of facilitating the full integration of refugees into european societies. i voted in favour because this legislation guarantees the implementation of policies for the social inclusion of refugees and their integration into the labour market, thus restoring the dignity of those seeking refuge and safety on the european continent.
‒ this report reflects the need for the inclusion of refugees in the member states, which necessarily involves integration into the labour market. the cfp has tabled eight amendments, focusing on improving working conditions and social protection, rejecting the 'qualifications' criterion as an exclusive factor, rejecting the refugee legislative frameworks (the dublin regulation, the blue card directive, the eu-turkey agreement) and extending support and integration strategies not only to refugees and asylum seekers but also to migrants. these proposals were not accepted by the commission. the report presents some limitations in this respect, such as being uncritical of the criteria with which the eu proposes the 'distribution' of refugees (calls for a review of the dublin regulation but does not address the reasonableness of this 'distribution'), calling for a distinction between refugees and migrants, failing to mention those responsible for conflicts in countries of origin, the inhumane conditions of the concentration camps or the cruelty of repatriation. however, the main body of the document contains information which, if implemented, would have consequences for increasing the inclusion of these people.
‒ i voted in favour of the benifei report because i believe that a common approach is needed to the integration and social inclusion of refugees. i believe that the integration of refugees should be seen as an opportunity for our society, because integrating them into the labour market is not only important for restoring their dignity and self-esteem, but it will also benefit the common good, as it allows them to gain economic independence and become active members of our society. i therefore stress the need for the eu to base its immediate response to the situation on solidarity and equitable sharing of responsibility as set out in article 80 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, as well as a comprehensive approach that takes into account the need to improve safe and legal migration channels and full respect for european fundamental values and rights.
in writing. ‒ in november 2010, the european parliament adopted a set of recommendations on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate social responsibility in two reports focusing on the respect for these dimensions in trade policy and the conclusion of trade agreements. i acknowledge that important steps have been taken in recent years, such as the adoption of the generalised system of preferences (gsp and gsp+) or the consideration of sustainable development objectives and the defence of human rights in the commission's 'trade for all' strategy. i believe that trade policy is an instrument for promoting the values of the european union and must therefore safeguard respect for social and environmental standards and combat human rights violations such as slavery or forced labour. i support the concern to include these issues in the union's multilateral and bilateral international relations, in particular in the negotiations on trade partnerships. i stress the need to fully implement the 2010 recommendations, adapting them to the reality of 2016, in an effort that the commission has been leading. i agree with the value of corporate social responsibility in this context. i therefore support the report.
‒ trade plays an important role in promoting business opportunities, creating prosperity and increasing employment, as well as in boosting economic development, social progress, living standards, quality of life and the long-term improvement of human rights standards. member states should therefore promote binding measures to ensure that companies pay taxes where they carry out their economic activity and create value, encourage mandatory country-by-country reporting by the private sector and promote good governance, including in relation to taxation and tax collection. i also agree with greater transparency and accountability of grassroots organisations in the formulation of international trade rules and national trade policies, while ensuring consistency with respect for workers' rights and human rights, including women's rights.
‒ we appreciate the efforts made by the rapporteur in drawing up this report, particularly when she stresses the absolute need to respect and value labour rights and conditions, as well as the role of the international labour organisation. but beyond the recommendations that may emanate from this plenary session - some positive, some negative and some very negative - it is important not to lose sight of the essential. the social responsibility in question is irrevocably at odds with the interests of the large economic and financial groups, with the promotion of the relocation of companies and of labour and social dumping, with attacks on collective bargaining and trade unions, with the exploitation of resources and workers in third countries, and with the deepening of social and gender discrimination. it will not be eu trade policy that will reverse this reality. on the contrary, it will tend to make it worse. the need to repeal the treaty of lisbon and to reverse its provisions on trade policy is clearly demonstrated. it should be up to each country to define its trade policies and agreements in a sovereign manner and in accordance with its interests and needs.
‒ in the framework of the 'trade for all' strategy, sustainable development is identified as one of the main objectives to be pursued by the european union, as stated in the treaties establishing it. in the logic of an integrated policy approach, eu trade policies should serve not only as a driver for economic development but also for social progress, a good standard of living and respect for human rights. in 2010, the european parliament had the opportunity to address a set of recommendations to the commission on social standards, human rights and corporate social responsibility, which should be taken into account in the framework of trade agreements concluded between the union and third countries. i therefore vote in favour of this report, which calls on the commission to ensure that the recommendations made by the european parliament are implemented in practice in order to promote sustainable and integrated development.
in writing. ‒ in november 2010, the european parliament adopted the following reports: human rights, social and environmental standards in international trade and corporate social responsibility in international trade agreements. the reports point out that by establishing certain regulatory requirements in trade agreements it is possible to promote european values and to raise awareness in third countries of the importance of good social practice. the same can be said of the production of goods without respect for human values, such as slavery, by prohibiting their importation. the report shows that the commission is doing a good job in implementing the 2010 standards. this is without prejudice to the recognition that much remains to be done in this area, especially as many developing countries will be reluctant to include social and environmental responsibility measures. this effort must continue. i therefore vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ the eu is now the richest economy in the world. however, its economic importance is expected to decline: by 2050, the eu28 will account for only 15% of world gdp, compared with 23.7% in 2013. the centre of wealth generation is shifting eastwards to the asia-pacific region and demographic developments will also have negative effects on the eu's position in the world trade landscape. it is therefore essential for the european union to develop an effective, comprehensive and forward-looking trade and investment strategy. in its 'trade for all' strategy, the commission sets a clear objective of rapidly increasing trade liberalisation and further integrating the eu into global value chains, coupled with the modernisation of its trade defence system.

in writing. ‒ the european union (eu) currently accounts for some 23.7% of global gdp and is the world's richest economy. however, by 2050, its share of world gdp is expected to decline to just 15%. the decline may be due to the shift of world wealth eastwards and the negative effects of demographic change. a strategy for efficient trade and investment is therefore imperative, as these are important drivers of growth and job creation. the report warns of the need for a new approach in the areas of responsible supply chain management, the global digital market, trade in digital goods and services, ethical and fair trade, and the social costs of trade liberalisation. the need for a transparent trade policy and a greater voice for citizens is invoked, in the particular case of the ttip negotiations and in the attention given to smes and their specific needs. i voted in favour of this proposal because i consider it essential to develop an effective trade and investment strategy, also at european level.

‒ my vote in favour of this report on the fight against trafficking in human beings in the context of the eu's external relations was due to the good document produced by my fellow rapporteur, especially when she asks the commission to assess the need for a possible review of the mandate of the future european public prosecutor's office, so that the fight against trafficking in human beings is integrated into its competences. i would like to stress the attention that is being called for in relation to trafficking in human beings in the eu's political dialogue with third countries as well as through its cooperation programmes. it also considered it essential that strategies to prevent trafficking in human beings address the factors that facilitate it, as well as the causes and circumstances of the phenomenon, and that they follow an integrated approach, bringing together different national and international actors, mandates and perspectives.
‒ trafficking in human beings is one of the most serious forms of human rights violation and one of the most profitable activities of organised crime, affecting mostly women for the exploitation of sexual services but not only. i support the lochbihler report on the fight against trafficking in human beings in the context of the eu's external relations, which condemns this activity, which cannot be tolerated in the light of european societal values and standards and which unfortunately also takes place within our internal borders. i regret the lack of adequate legislation to combat this scourge and the lack of cooperation between countries, with the number of known victims still high, with no access to adequate protection and support, and with limited or no access to justice. special attention should be paid to illegal migration flows that increase the risk of trafficking due to their vulnerability and irregular situation, in particular unaccompanied minors such as the 10,000 children who have disappeared in europe according to europol. it is urgent that the eu continue its efforts to combat this phenomenon in all its forms (sex, slavery, forced begging, organ trafficking) and in particular in its relations with third countries.
in writing. ‒ around 70% of detected victims are women and girls and make up 79% of detected victims of sexual exploitation. men account for 83% of the detected victims of forced labour. the annual illegal profit generated by forced labour, including through money laundering, is estimated at around $150 billion, with an estimated 90 percent of victims exploited in the private economy and two-thirds of the profits derived from commercial sexual exploitation, making it the most lucrative form of exploitation. i therefore voted in favour of the report which calls for the eu and the member states to take a human rights-based and victim-centred approach and to put victims and vulnerable populations at the centre of all efforts to combat and prevent trafficking in human beings and to protect their victims.
‒ the report provides a comprehensive overview of global trends in human trafficking, the economics of human trafficking, the rights of victims and the issue of compensation, and advocates for cooperation in combating trafficking at regional and international level. finally, it addresses the policy that the eu should pursue on trafficking in human beings in the context of its external relations. unfortunately, the report fails to address some of the root causes of this phenomenon - as evidenced by the rejection of the amendments we have proposed on war, exploitation and inequalities in the distribution of wealth. on the other hand, it is based on the - erroneous - assumption that the phenomenon does not exist within the eu itself, but is confined to other continents. the role and action of nato in triggering such phenomena, for example the war in libya - which has reinforced criminal activities, including human trafficking networks - is ignored. a complacent attitude is adopted towards multinational companies which make use of slave or forced labour resulting from human trafficking. the report contains positive aspects but does not really look at the causes of the phenomenon. for this fundamental reason, it fails in its guidelines for combat.
‒ trafficking in human beings is a serious violation of fundamental rights and an offence against the dignity of the human person, and this criminal activity is one of the most lucrative in the framework of international organised crime. this scourge is of a global magnitude and so the response must also be seen from a global perspective. in this context, efforts should be made to improve the strategy to combat trafficking in human beings, including through cooperation with third countries to combat trafficking in human beings from recruitment to the point of arrival; to better distinguish the concept of trafficking in human beings from the concept of smuggling of migrants; to adopt and implement measures to combat corruption and the flow of profits from the commercial exploitation of this activity into the financial system; and to better implement existing legislation on the protection of victims of organised crime, especially the most vulnerable groups, such as women and children. i am therefore voting in favour of this report because i believe that a coherent approach to eu policies is needed, both at the level of internal and external policy.
‒ this is a report that addresses the issue of combating trafficking in human beings in the context of the eu's external relations. the title immediately denounces the thematic contextualisation on the basis of an assumption we do not recognise: the eu's foreign policy. the report provides an exhaustive overview of global trends in human trafficking, the economics of human trafficking, the rights of victims, including the issue of compensation for victims, the advocacy of cooperation in combating human trafficking at regional and international level, and the eu's policy on human trafficking in the context of external relations. while there are some positive aspects, we cannot ignore the deep hypocrisy which is evident throughout the lengthy report. on the one hand, it follows a line of whitewashing of eu migration policies. it also legitimises the structural policies at the root of this humanitarian crisis and sanctions the return policy, the externalisation of borders and the role of europol and frontex. at the same time, it makes the states less responsible for their role of welcoming and providing solidarity. these unacceptable considerations justify the vote against.
‒ trafficking in human beings (ths), which is part of organised crime and constitutes one of the most serious forms of human rights violation, turns men and women into commodities, violating the dignity, integrity and rights of victims. the different ends of trafficking in human beings - namely, sexual exploitation, organ trafficking and forced labour - are a profitable and growing industry of human suffering, affecting all societies and economies in a profound and permanent way. the current migration crisis increases the risk of trafficking due to the vulnerable and irregular situation of many migrants, and it is therefore incumbent on the european union to promote programmes to support the inclusion of migrants and refugees, with the participation of third countries and also of cultural mediators, which are useful to raise the level of awareness of communities about trafficking and to make them more resilient to the penetration of organised crime. ths is a modern form of slavery and a serious crime that cannot be tolerated in societies firmly founded on respect for human rights and must therefore be severely punished. in view of the above, i vote in favour.
‒ human trafficking is a modern form of slavery and a serious crime that constitutes one of the worst forms of human rights violations, something that cannot be tolerated in societies based on respect for human rights. human trafficking must be understood in a holistic way, focusing not only on sexual exploitation but also on forced labour, organ trafficking, forced begging, forced marriage, child soldiers and baby trafficking. as it is a transnational crime of a global nature, any measures to combat it must take into account the root causes and global trends. hence the importance of a coherent and urgent approach to the internal and external dimensions of eu policies to combat it.
in writing. ‒ this report focuses on trafficking in human beings as a new form of slavery - an extremely serious crime that is highly offensive to human dignity, which has increased significantly in recent years, notably through international criminal networks. the rapporteur clarifies the difference between human trafficking and migrant smuggling, adding that each concept requires legal responses and appropriate practices. given the different forms of exploitation, some may be linked to corruption, and effective measures are urgently needed, starting with the training of competent public officials who are properly prepared to respond to such requests. regional, european and international cooperation against trafficking in human beings is of paramount importance and therefore requires greater coordination and systematic exchange of information to investigate and combat transnational trafficking in human beings, through measures such as enhanced financial and technical assistance, alongside capacity building at governmental and law enforcement level. i voted in favour of the report because i agree with the general content of the proposals in this report.
‒ human trafficking is a form of modern slavery that ravages the lives of many people. trafficking involves various forms of extreme exploitation such as child prostitution, child soldiers, unpaid forced labour and the trade in human organs, and is a highly profitable business for criminal organisations. it is unacceptable that human beings should be treated as commodities, that their dignity, integrity and rights should be constantly violated, and that they should inevitably be relegated to situations of isolation, contempt and misery. the eu has made a notable contribution to the fight against trafficking in human beings. however, the needs of victims, including the provision of assistance, therapy and compensation, must still be taken into account. i voted in favour because it encourages the eu to step up its action in protecting and assisting victims, in strengthening the police against traffickers and in improving cooperation with developing countries. the fight against trafficking in human beings must be a shared responsibility. but unfortunately, many countries in the world still do not have legislation to criminalize and combat trafficking in human beings.

madam president, regardless of the more or less specific aspects which the report rightly points out, the payment deficit, the instruments and the flexibility margins, the plain truth is that this budget is totally incompatible with the proclaimed objectives of social and territorial cohesion set out in the treaties. and this incompatibility arises from two orders of reason: firstly, the amounts are far below what is needed for an effective redistributive policy which would allow the disadvantaged countries and regions to come closer to the richer regions. it is also significant that this multiannual budget has been reduced for the first time in the history of european integration. secondly, this budget is short because a large part of the resources, which are already scarce, are not used to promote cohesion. a significant part of the budget is now being used to finance the repressive and security policies of the european union, thus taking away funds that should be directed towards the objectives of cohesion or support for farmers who are victims of the european union's external policies. we want more money, but we demand that it be put to use in a distribution policy that reduces disparities and reinforces cohesion.
member of the commission. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, let me first of all congratulate the two rapporteurs, mr kofod and mr theurer, the special committee on taxation, its chairman, mr lamassoure, and all those involved in the preparation of the report on their very high quality of work. to achieve this result, the european commission and parliament - i think i can say this - have worked very closely and very positively. i myself have participated on several occasions in the debates of the taxe committee. my colleagues, who have been summoned, commissioners vestager and hill, also appeared before her and our services cooperated closely and, i believe, effectively. we are in a political context which we cannot ignore, with turbulence which invites us to reflect together on how we respond to the most crucial political, social and economic issues facing the peoples of europe. this reflection is just beginning and it deserves to be deepened, it must be open and take account of the demands and needs of all the citizens of the european union in their diversity. a specific issue that comes up again and again in public debate is, of course, the need for greater social justice alongside economic growth, and it is inseparable from the issue of transparency. i do not claim that this is an easy question to solve, but it is a question that we must answer first and we must answer it quickly. it did not win the british vote. it has been a concern of ours for a long time and must remain the guiding principle of our action. in a context where the legitimacy of the european union is being questioned by some, i am convinced that transparency and tax justice are essential to re-establish a pillar of democracy, which is tax consent. that is why the commission has identified fairness, particularly in the area of taxation, as one of its main political priorities for its mandate and, with the full support of this parliament, our work is progressing, i think i can say, considerably towards that objective. let me review some of the main developments in our tax equity strategy in the months since taxe 2 was created; our interaction has already been extremely positive. some of these actions are, in fact, - as the rapporteurs have already said - direct responses to the recommendations of this parliament, which have been directly operational. firstly - and this is still an important point in the report we are discussing today - we have made a great deal of progress towards what i call the transparency revolution. following a commission proposal in january, member states agreed to automatically exchange tax information on the activities of multinationals. this agreement is based on greater openness and better cooperation between tax authorities, to which we already contributed last year with the new legislation on tax resets. the commission also recognised that tax transparency should extend beyond administrations. i repeat here - for those who have not heard - that from the first day i took office i have been in favour of country-by-country public reporting - i say public. in april, we proposed country-by-country disclosure requirements for large multinationals. your report welcomes these proposals very much. mr lamberts, he would like to go further. this proposal is now in the hands of the council and parliament. i am convinced that you will make an ambitious response. and we presented our latest initiative today to combat unfair tax practices with a proposal that aims to give tax administrations access to key beneficial ownership information and other data that allows for enhanced surveillance. these are the concerns you have raised, as have the g20 and the g7. this will enable tax authorities to identify and act against those who hide their income and assets in offshore funds, as was the case with the panama papers. you can see that we have an answer to the problems that are raised right away. we also announced that we would work to expand the cross-border access of tax authorities to beneficial ownership information, and to work towards increased control and accountability of a profession, namely tax advisers, some of whom - but not all - allow or encourage tax fraud. again, these are proposals which i made in this house a long time ago. we have therefore other plans to come to ensure greater transparency, in line with the recommendations of your report, which i would say is entirely in line with our priorities - and mine. secondly - and on this point too we agree - we have put in place new concrete measures to ensure that companies pay their taxes where they make their profits, a fundamental measure in tax justice. there has been a whole debate in the council on minimum taxation, but it is not about that, it is about effective taxation. in january, the commission proposed an ambitious directive on tax evasion to put an end to certain loopholes, certain schemes used by certain companies to avoid paying taxes. i am glad that less than six months later the council has reached political agreement on the bulk of the commission's proposal for a directive. these new rules, once implemented, will deal a blow, a hard blow, to aggressive tax planning in europe and will allow us to take a step further towards fair taxation in the european union. i am not going to pretend here that this directive is sufficient or that it is perfect. i am well aware that the taxe committee and this parliament expect more, and i also know that the commission's proposal was, as is often the case, a little more ambitious than what had been decided by the member states in the end, but again i think we have a good compromise, which the commission has agreed to. i will spare no effort to achieve the results you desire. for example, as requested in your report, we will be strengthening the measures to combat tax evasion during the year, with a proposal to combat hybrid arrangements with third countries. we will, of course, as you ask in your report, relaunch the ccctb, the draft common consolidated corporate tax base, before the end of the year, to make it compulsory for large multinationals. this will create a more favourable and fairer tax environment for all businesses in the european union. this is obviously a fundamental structural measure. i note that the adoption of the tax measures, in so far as it concerns the fight against tax evasion, has nevertheless had a tremendous accelerating effect. it took several years, and more, to get directives on taxation adopted in the council, taking into account the rule of unanimity. with the strong pressure of events, it now takes - you will notice - a few months. i hope that this acceleration will also be seen when measures are proposed which have a structural, long-term effect, as is the case with cfsp. we have failed in the past on this point. we shall now take up the matter in a slightly different way, but i want to tell you how much interest, and even importance, i attach to this proposal. thirdly, we have continued our work to extend good tax governance globally. the commission's objectives are the same as those of parliament on this last point too, or very close to it. our initiatives to combat tax evasion include a new external strategy to encourage good governance in tax matters beyond the single market and to tackle countries that do not play by the rules. a central element of this strategy is to establish a common eu list of non-cooperative third countries - let us say in french, but it is understandable in the other languages - i.e. a pan-european blacklist of tax havens, and also to provide for countermeasures, an idea which, i know, has the backing of the taxe committee. we have already started this process of drawing up lists with the member states and, unlike in the past, a recent past i had proposed a first list, the limits of which were obvious to me, but which had the merit of being in existence a year ago, however things have changed a lot i note that the member states fully support this project and i want to tell you that the first list of the european union should be ready in 2017. this will be a major step forward and will be built in conjunction with the oecd. i think this measure will have a major deterrent effect on third countries who think they are in a position to profit from the erosion of the tax bases of other countries. of course, the need for tax efficiency and fairness does not stop at the borders of the european union. that is why, as part of our external strategy, we place - as your report does - a very strong emphasis on supporting developing countries in their fight against tax evasion and in their integration into the network of international good tax governance. it's not just the g20 countries, it's the whole world. we have committed, in the addis ababa tax initiative, to double our support to low-income countries to help them improve their tax collection. we will honour this commitment and go further, providing full political support to these countries within the oecd and other international organisations. my services have also engaged in discussions with member states and stakeholders on how to prevent the negative impact of community and national tax policies on developing countries. i know that this is a concern shared by all of you. ladies and gentlemen of the european parliament, i have outlined to you today the main lines of the work we are doing to ensure fairer and more efficient taxation in the european union, in line with the expectations of our fellow citizens and with certain recommendations - the main points of your report. i have been able to cover all these recommendations because this report is very comprehensive, but i am of course still prepared to discuss them with you. the strong political pressure exerted by parliament as a whole, through the taxe 1, taxe 2 committees and, i am not forgetting, econ, because there was also very high-quality joint work, has contributed greatly to the progress achieved. our programme, my programme, is continuing and it is addressing many of the other areas that you have mentioned, ranging from improving transfer pricing to strengthening good governance clauses in the case of our international agreements. we have a clear public, political mandate to encourage member states to implement the measures decided upon, through a rapid and ambitious agreement on these initiatives. i think this is very much reflected in the public outrage that has not been dispelled by the publication of the panama papers and other scandals covered by the media, which in this case are allies. there is a real demand from citizens across the european union to strengthen social justice, to improve transparency and to achieve full transparency in economic and fiscal policy. i am therefore happy to continue this work, happy to do so in close partnership with the european parliament to achieve a fairer taxation in europe as our fellow citizens expect and, to that extent, i am also very happy to welcome this report as an important step in our common fight.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud and tax evasion. the two taxe committees 1 and 2 have confirmed this breadth and confirmed that this is a widespread practice throughout europe and in all capitalist economies. the report points out a number of highly relevant aspects, but it does not go to the heart of the problem, because all these arrangements which provide genuine tax breaks do not happen by chance, they happen as a result of a long process of financial deregulation, which has been accentuated since the 1980s and which has been led by governments and parties present in this house today. let the dutch, the united kingdom or the luxembourg governments say so. we do not therefore fully support this report because it condemns the capitalist system which promotes the free movement of capital and financial liberalization and encourages tax evasion. we therefore believe that an effective fight against tax evasion and fraud requires public control of the financial system and restrictions on the movement of capital. relying solely on the regulatory path shows that we have learned nothing from the past. in writing. ‒ the objective of amending budget no 2/2016 is to enter in the 2016 budget the surplus for the financial year 2015 of eur 1 349 million, the surplus being a positive result of eur 980 million in revenue, a non-execution of expenditure of eur 187 million and exchange differences amounting to eur 182 million. the adoption of this amending budget will reduce part of the gni contributions of the member states to the 2016 union budget by eur 1,349 million. i share the view that member states should use the opportunity provided by this reimbursement to honour their commitments in relation to the refugee crisis and increase their contributions to the trust fund for africa and the madad trust fund for the syrian crisis. i therefore support the report by my colleague, mr josé manuel fernandes.
in writing. ‒ in september last year, member states committed to contribute as much as the eu to the two trust funds for the refugee crisis: the trust fund for africa and the madad trust fund for the syrian crisis. the eu contributed €1.8 billion to the former and over €500 million to the latter. by spring, member states' contributions had been reduced to €82 million for the africa fund and €69 million for the syrian crisis response trust fund. an additional €2.1 billion from the member states will therefore be needed to match the eu contribution. if member states use the 2015 surplus of €1.3 billion to strengthen the trust funds, they would be sending a signal that we are united and committed to finding a solution to a crisis that affects us all.
in writing. ‒ this draft amending budget no 2/2016 is devoted exclusively to the budgeting of the 2015 surplus, amounting to eur 1349 million. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance in the context of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe. it is good that this surplus is kept in the budget. but unfortunately, in practice it will no longer be a surplus, as the adoption of this amending budget will reduce the share of member states' contributions to the 2016 eu budget, based on their gni, by eur 1349 million. in other words, the additional effect that this surplus could have is effectively cancelled out. and they mostly save the same ones. the rapporteur without any practical effect argues that, instead of adjusting the contribution based on gni, the eu budget should be able to reuse surpluses from under-utilisation of appropriations or fines imposed on companies in competition matters, in order to meet their financing needs, especially in the context of insufficient payment appropriations, and hopes that this issue will be resolved in the context of the review of the mff.

‒ in the context of the evaluation of the 2015 budgetary year of the european union, a budget surplus of eur 1349 million was found. the correction to the union budget is intended solely to record the budget surplus for 2015, thereby reducing the member states' contribution, in accordance with article 18 of the regulation on the financial provisions applicable to the general budget of the union. in this sense, instead of adjusting the contribution based on gni, the union budget should be able to reuse surpluses from under-utilisation of appropriations or fines imposed on undertakings for breaches of union competition law in order to meet their financing needs. i am therefore voting in favour of this report, as i believe that the union should be given a greater budgetary capacity to ensure that its policies are better implemented, for example by making more investment available for the implementation of projects.

‒ it networks and systems and services play a vital role in society, their reliability and security being essential for the freedom and general security of eu citizens and the well-being of the internal market. i support the schwab report which endorses the council's position at first reading, thus enabling the prevention and response to attacks and disruptions affecting europe's telecommunications systems and providing an effective response to the challenges through a comprehensive eu approach covering common minimum requirements for cybersecurity skills development, information exchange and coordination of actions, including through the establishment of a cooperation mechanism between member states. the processing of personal data is to be carried out in accordance with directives 95/46/ec and 2002/58/ec and in accordance with regulation (ec) no 45/2001, and is to be strictly limited to the minimum data necessary for that purpose. with this new legislation, all eu member states, major internet companies and infrastructure operators such as e-commerce platforms, social networks, transport, banking and healthcare have to ensure a secure and reliable digital environment across the eu.
‒ at least 80% of european companies have had at least one cybersecurity incident over the past year. these incidents know no borders and can cause serious damage to society and the economy. this directive therefore requires operators providing essential services in sectors such as energy, transport, health and banking, and providers of digital services such as online marketplaces, to take a number of measures to resist cyber-attacks. each eu country will have to designate one or more national authorities responsible for this and adopt a national strategy for the security of network and information systems.
in writing. ‒ in 2013, the european commission proposed a directive on network and information security as part of its cybersecurity strategy. the aim of the proposal was to set up a mechanism to create an insight into the breach of security of certain important infrastructures. the proposal called on member states to adopt a national strategy setting out the strategic objectives. member states should also designate/create a national authority to monitor the implementation of the directive and designate a national single point of contact to link member states to the network of it security incident response teams. this report is the outcome of that process. the outcome of the trilogue was weaker than the original proposal in that its scope was somewhat limited and fewer digital service providers were included in the annex and therefore in the european commission proposal.
‒ networks and information systems play a key role as a means of facilitating the crossborder movement of goods, services and people. due to this transnational dimension, a disruption in one member state may also affect another member state and the union as a whole. the flexibility and stability of networks and information systems are therefore essential for the smooth functioning of the internal market. this proposal for a directive recognises the need to harmonise rules on the one hand and to create effective cooperation mechanisms between member states on the other. in this respect, i am voting in favour of this proposal, as i consider it important to harmonise certain aspects of the security of network and information systems within the european union in order to prevent the contagion of possible 'attack' situations in several member states and to encourage a coordinated approach to these situations.

‒ networks, information systems and digital services (nis) play a key role in facilitating the movement of goods, services and people within the european union. however, the dependence of many sectors on such information technologies also carries the risk that security breaches in one member state may spread and create consequences in others, as well as in the union itself - so-called externalities. the proposal covers three areas of action: requiring member states to have a minimum level of national authorities responsible for nis, ensuring their cooperation and coordination with the european network and information security agency (enisa), and requiring economic, public and private actors in strategic sectors such as banking, transport, etc., to report nis incidents and to take measures to ensure nis security. therefore, a resilient and stable network of systems and information is essential to ensure security for both users and operators. having approved the first reading and having seen that the proposed measures provide greater certainty and security in matters of nis, i consider this report to be extremely consistent with these concerns and therefore vote in favour.
‒ it is imperative to improve the security of the internet and of the private computer networks and systems on which the functioning of our societies and economies is based. this will be achieved by requiring member states to increase their level of preparedness and cooperation with each other and by requiring operators of critical infrastructures, such as energy, transport and the main providers of information society services (e-commerce platforms, social networks, etc.), as well as public administrations, to take appropriate measures to manage security risks and to report serious incidents to the competent national authorities.
‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation of the european parliament (ep) at second reading on the adoption of the directive of the european parliament and of the council on measures to ensure a high common level of network and information security across the union. given the increasing importance of networks and information systems and the fragmentation of regulatory frameworks in the member states of the european union (eu), there was a need to introduce obligations ensuring the security of networked information in order to create a level playing field at european level by closing the existing legislative gaps. this proposal requires member states to ensure effective cooperation and coordination between them through an information network to enable the reporting of incidents in information and security systems, and to take appropriate measures immediately to ensure the subsequent viability of these systems. i agree with the importance of the creation of a cooperation group for strategic coordination between member states, with operational capacity and the ability to set up a security incident response team. penalties for non-compliance should also be provided for in the national law of each member state in order to ensure a harmonised approach and a level playing field across the eu with regard to european cybersecurity.

in writing. the energy labelling directive was adopted in 2010 with the stated aim of encouraging consumers to buy more efficient products. the report stresses the need for a new approach to the problem of the market. the creation of a database of products, standards and testing procedures, as well as the consumer information campaign, is also needed. the rescaling relevant concern aims to combine the occupation of energy efficiency classes by the product models available on the market with the technological evolution of the product group, facilitating a correct reading of the information to be transmitted and avoiding a distribution of the models by classes that potentiates misreadings and misinterpretations. the rapporteur believes that the existence of a product database is a central element of this citizen-oriented information and communication system, as it will facilitate access to information, increase the capacity to monitor market developments in real time (and improve legislation accordingly) and enhance the efficiency of 'security mechanisms'. market surveillance, safeguards and conformity assessment are key elements of enforcement. in general, we follow the concerns and recommendations expressed by the rapporteur. we voted in favour.
‒ the european union has been working towards a true energy union, with an energy and climate policy geared to the new challenges of the 21st century. energy efficiency is essential to achieve the climate objectives set out at the paris summit in december 2015. in this context, the energy-efficiency labelling of equipment can contribute positively to achieving the union's 2030 energy efficiency targets. energy labelling allows consumers to make more informed choices about the most energy efficient products/equipment at the energy endpoint. although this has already been regulated by the european union, the transposition of directive 2010/30/eu has led to the adoption of different energy labelling scales and the adoption of this regulation is therefore intended to ensure a uniform application of energy labelling. i therefore vote in favour of this proposal, as i consider it important that consumers have access to clear and accessible information on the energy efficiency of the equipment they purchase, regardless of the member state in which they do so.
‒ directive 2010/30/ec has made it possible to create an energy efficiency label, allowing citizens to have a better understanding of the environmental impact and life cycle of the products they purchase. however, consumer confidence in energy efficiency has been shaken after the so-called 'volkswagen scandal', and it is therefore important to increase the transparency and simplicity of the energy labelling framework. the amendments to the directive in areas such as rescheduling, the information and communication system and union surveillance constitute important developments in the legislation in this area. i therefore vote in favour.
‒ this legislative initiative concerns a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the need to establish a framework for energy efficiency labelling and repealing directive 2010/30/eu. we all know that the introduction of these labels has given citizens a more detailed knowledge of consumption, environmental impact and the life cycle of products. the analysis carried out showed that several aspects of the previous directive needed to be amended and a regulation was chosen as this is the legal instrument capable of avoiding different transpositions in different member states and also allowing greater transparency for consumers and authorities with regard to products related to the energy sector in the eu. i support, in general, the commission's proposals to replace the current energy labelling system and to introduce a mechanism for the re-scaling of energy efficiency classes, as well as the creation of a product database and the imposition of obligations on economic operators. i therefore voted in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes to combine the occupation of energy efficiency classes by the product models available on the market with the technological evolution of the product group. since the post-rescaling distribution of product models by energy efficiency classes a to g will have significant market implications, a flexible 'driving' approach is maintained, proposing three decreasing options of 'rescaling intensity': c-g (with two empty classes at the top), b-g (an empty class) and a-g (no empty classes). these staggering patterns will also be associated with the criteria mentioned above. the objective is to converge to a-g scales within a reasonable timeframe (5 years). information flows and planning tools are also emphasised. together, they should shape a knowledge-driven transition, including solutions adapted to newly labelled product groups and small-sized products. i therefore vote in favour.

‒ the european border and coast guard is one of the flagship measures in the context of the agenda on migration, which lists a number of measures to deal with the migration crisis. this is a good example of how institutions can cooperate and deliver results quickly. the legislative process was completed in record time and the council was ready to reach commitments with the european parliament. this new agency, which is completely reshaping the current frontex, also introduces a number of significant innovations. the agency's own capacity has been strengthened, with its own equipment and a rapid reaction reserve of 1 500 men. however, and despite the very positive step, i cannot help but stress that this is not the solution to all the problems of the so-called refugee crisis. only a holistic approach is capable of tackling the complexity of the problem. moreover, it cannot - for the future - serve to relieve member states of responsibility, who essentially remain the main actors in the management of the union's external borders.
‒ the creation of the european border and coast guard to control migration flows and enhance security involves a european agency and national border management authorities. they will remain responsible for the day-to-day management of the external borders, but will be able to call on a rapid reaction contingent of 1500 border guards, including 47 portuguese, and technical equipment in situations requiring urgent action. this rapid reaction pool shall be a standing corps, which may be deployed from each member state within five working days of the date on which the operational plan has been agreed between the executive director of the agency and the host member state.
‒ the vision of a 'fortress europe', the criminalising, selective and instrumental vision of immigration, embodied in schengen, is more alive today than ever. the much-touted area of free movement of people which, in fact, never was has led to this: eight schengen member states belgium, denmark, germany, hungary, austria, slovenia, sweden and norway have introduced internal border controls in response to the so-called refugee crisis. the walls of the outer borders rise even higher, with barbed wire at the top, duly guarded by guards and weapons. it is in this context that the creation of the european border and coast guard, which is the subject of this report, is being set up. in several areas, the report goes even further than the european commission's initial proposal. the rapporteur considers that 'it is essential that in future the agency has the necessary border guards and equipment at its disposal whenever it requests them and, in particular, that it can use them in a short time when necessary'. we are facing an unprecedented attack on national sovereignty in a field that goes to the heart of that sovereignty: the control of national territorial waters. the attack is part of a security and militaristic drift. obviously, we voted against it.
‒ the recent migration flows have posed a number of problems for member states, particularly in terms of security and border management. the creation of a coast and border guard is an attempt to respond to this problem by ensuring a strict and shared management of the external borders of the european union. the european border and coast guard brings together the european border and coast guard agency established from frontex and the member states' authorities responsible for border management, which are responsible for ensuring the day-to-day management of the external borders. the new european border and coast guard will be equipped with a rapidly deployable reserve of border guards and technical equipment, will have a monitoring and surveillance role, will have the right to intervene, both within the eu and in third countries, by mobilising european border and coast guard teams, the prerogative to launch joint surveillance operations, the competence to carry out analysis and prevention of terrorism, among other competencies. i am voting in favour of this because i consider effective control of the union's external borders to be essential to guarantee the security of citizens and free movement in the schengen area.
in the light of the recent developments in the field of the internal market, the commission proposes to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. they are the expression of a european union closed in on itself, reinforcing the concept of 'fortress europe' and consolidating itself in the externalization of maritime borders to third countries, in restrictions on the free movement of persons, in the creation of genuine concentration camps, in the discrimination and expulsion of refugees. another aspect of the xenophobic and racist agenda that characterizes the criminal migration policy and the response to the serious humanitarian refugee crisis in the european union, and which has as a direct consequence the death of almost three thousand refugees in the mediterranean this year. a crisis for which the european union bears direct and indirect responsibility, with its policies of interference and aggression in the middle east and north africa, coordinated with nato and the united states, favouring authoritarian regimes, promoting the political destabilisation of countries that oppose the interests of imperialism, fuelling conflicts, promoting war. we could only vote against it.
‒ the schengen area, comprising 26 member states, is undoubtedly one of the greatest achievements of the european project. however, due to the current migration crisis, and in response to irregular migration movements, some of the countries have reintroduced border controls. this shows that the instruments and mechanisms developed for the smooth functioning of the schengen area are not sufficient. this report proposes the creation of a new concept of european border and coast guard (ebcg) whose objective is to ensure adequate control of the external borders of the common area as a precondition for the effective management of migratory flows, in order to ensure a high level of security within the common area. the report proposes the creation of a new agency, to replace frontex, which would include the national authorities of the member states responsible for the management of land and sea borders in the field of border control. since i believe that the measures in this report will promote solidarity between member states, strengthen integration in the field of border management and help to prevent crises at the external borders, i am voting in favour.
‒ the schengen area is considered one of the greatest and most visible achievements of european integration. however, the absence of internal border controls is currently facing unprecedented challenges, with too many schengen member states reintroducing internal border controls in response to migration movements. this situation shows that the instruments and mechanisms developed over time for the proper functioning of the schengen area are not sufficient, given the magnitude of the current migration crisis as well as the threats posed by terrorist activities. it therefore makes perfect sense to create a european border and coast guard (ebcg) to ensure adequate control of the external borders of the schengen area as a precondition for the effective, humanitarian and solidarity-based management of migration flows, in order to ensure a high level of security within the area, while preserving the free movement of persons within the union.
‒ the schengen area is one of the greatest and most visible achievements of european integration. however, the absence of internal border controls is currently creating significant challenges, which has led some member states to reintroduce such controls in response to irregular migration movements that may endanger internal security and public order. it is therefore clear that the instruments and mechanisms developed over time for the smooth functioning of the schengen area have proved insufficient, especially in response to the recent challenges posed by the magnitude of the migration crisis and the terrorist threat. this regulation contains a package of measures aimed at ensuring better management and protection of the european union (eu) borders, such as the creation of the european border and coast guard, which will not only ensure the integrated management of the external borders but also contribute to the fight against cross-border crime and to ensuring internal security. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the content of this regulation, which puts the emphasis on the effective management of migration flows, and i particularly agree with the more comprehensive approach to potential external threats, along with the return to an eu without controls in the schengen area.
‒ the regulation creating the new european border and coast guard comes at a time when the eu needs to step up internal and external security at its borders. the multiple challenges facing the eu, including those related to various hybrid threats, call for more coordinated and cooperative action in the area of security. the new agency will be composed of the current frontex with extended functions as well as the national authorities responsible for border management. it is expected to play a key role in organising and coordinating rapid border interventions and deploying european coast guard and border guard teams, based on the rapid intervention contingent, and to be composed of at least 1500 personnel. i voted in favour because i considered it urgent that the new agency should have its own permanent staff and equipment and be able to mobilise them at any time when border intervention is needed. finally, it should be noted that the role of the parliament is strengthened by its involvement in the selection process of the executive director of the agency. the agency will seek to provide a common response to the threats facing member states and to strengthen the eu's resilience in the fight against external threats.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the pabriks report because i believe that a new european border and coast guard agency should be created, with the necessary financial, human and material resources to help member states to ensure more effective management of the eu's external borders. i would stress the shared responsibility nature of this new agency. to that end, it should respond to migratory challenges and potential future threats at the external borders and ensure a high level of internal security within the union in a spirit of solidarity. i would also like to highlight the efforts made by the european socialist group to extend the mandate of the european border and coast guard to include support for search and rescue operations.
‒ the european border and coast guard is one of the flagship measures in the context of the agenda on migration, which sets out a set of measures to tackle the migration crisis. this new agency, which is completely reshaping the current frontex, also introduces a number of significant innovations. the european maritime safety agency is one such innovation, as it will also make its operational resources available for a more integrated management of the union's external borders. however, and despite the very positive step, i cannot help but stress that this is not the solution to all the problems of the so-called refugee crisis. only a holistic approach is capable of tackling the complexity of the problem. moreover, it cannot in the future serve to relieve member states, who essentially remain the main actors in the management of the union's external borders, of responsibility.

‒ this report is part of the 'coast guard package'. it aims to amend and extend the powers of the agencies for maritime security, control and management of operational cooperation at the external borders in terms of border control and coastguard. all eu and member state agencies and bodies which are in any way related to maritime issues should contribute to the objectives of frontex. the european maritime safety agency should assume responsibilities for:- provision of surveillance and communication services based on state-of-the-art technologies, including space and ground infrastructure (including drones) and sensors installed on any type of platform; - capacity building through the development of guidelines and recommendations, support for training and exchange of personnel with a view to improving the exchange of information and cooperation on coast guard functions; - sharing information generated by the merger and analysing data available in ship reporting systems and other information systems hosted or accessible to the agencies, in accordance with their respective legal bases and without prejudice to the ownership rights of the member states over such data. the report and the draft regulation are based on a security logic, on the criminalization of immigration, and constitute an intolerable attack on national sovereignty.
in writing. this proposal to amend regulation no 1406/2002 establishing the european maritime safety agency is part of a strategy to promote cooperation in the field of coastal safety by enabling the development of new forms of cooperation between the agency and the european fisheries control agency and the european coast and border guard. cooperation between these three agencies aims to promote the provision of more efficient support services to national authorities, both in terms of response and costs. in this context, the european maritime safety agency will make an important contribution to improving the surveillance and control capacity of the union's external borders, in particular by sharing information, sharing technical means such as remotely piloted aircraft and developing guides to best practices in coastal safety, among others. i therefore vote in favour of this proposal, as i consider it essential to ensure effective control of the union's external borders, in particular by promoting synergies between the various european agencies in this field, in order to promote the efficient use of existing resources.
‒ more than 300 civil and military authorities are involved in coast guard functions, including security, search and rescue, border control, customs control and policing. these are supported by union agencies, in particular frontex, the european maritime safety agency (emsa) and the european fisheries control agency (efca). emsa was established to ensure a high, uniform and effective level of maritime safety, protection of shipping and prevention and control of pollution caused by ships. the commission concluded that there is a need for better cooperation between national bodies and european agencies carrying out coast guard functions, especially in the areas of operational surveillance and data sharing. the aim of this proposal is to improve cooperation and coordination between the relevant union agencies in order to increase synergies between their services, with a view to greater efficiency in their action, as well as in terms of costs, and my vote could not but be in favour.
in writing. ‒ currently, more than 300 civil and military authorities from the member states carry out coast guard functions, including security, search and rescue, border control, fisheries control, customs control, police and environmental protection. the objective of this legislative proposal, which strengthens european cooperation on coast guard functions, is to improve cooperation and coordination between the relevant eu agencies in order to increase synergies between their respective services, enabling them to provide national authorities performing coast guard functions with more efficient, including cost-effective, multi-purpose services.
