‒ this report is part of the 'coast guard package'. it aims to amend and extend the powers of the agencies for maritime security, fisheries control and the management of operational cooperation at the external borders in terms of border control and coastguard. all eu and member state agencies and bodies which are in any way related to maritime issues should contribute to the objectives of frontex. in this context, the community fisheries control agency should be given responsibilities for:- the exchange of data from control and inspection activities using the copernicus security system;- increased control for the detection of criminal activities and trafficking routes;- supporting the management of the eu's external borders. the report and the draft regulation are based on a security logic, on the criminalization of immigration, and constitute an intolerable attack on national sovereignty. this amendment reinforces the tendency to usurp areas of sovereignty and competence that should be in the national sphere, which led us to oppose the creation of this agency - an inseparable part of the provisions of the lisbon treaty, which considered the management of living marine resources to be an exclusive competence of the eu.
‒ the european fisheries control agency was set up in 2005 with the aim of ensuring the proper and effective application of the rules established under the common fisheries policy, in particular through coordinated inspection actions at sea and on land, as well as training in terms of good practices, among others. the agency shall not seek to replace the member states or the commission in the exercise of their responsibilities or tasks; the commission has also proposed that the member states should be allowed to adopt a common fisheries policy. this proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 768/2005 establishing the european fisheries control agency is part of a wider proposal to give the european maritime safety agency and the european coast and border guard agency, as well as the european maritime safety agency, the competence to coordinate their operations at sea and to share information relevant to their activities. i am therefore voting in favour of this proposal, as i consider cooperation between the various agencies to be important, as it contributes to a more effective response to possible disaster situations and to a more efficient use of resources.
‒ due to the existence of numerous competent authorities in the coastguard, the cooperation system suffers from delays and shortcomings, including lack of information on the tasks of each entity, as well as lack of coordination of operations and planning. the proposal aims to enable the three european agencies - the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european coast and border guard agency - to coordinate their operations at sea and share information relevant to their action. they will support the national authorities and will be able to act jointly and effectively, the means of action being predominantly national, while the coordination of functions will be at european level. in my view, the proposal satisfactorily determines the competences of the european fisheries control agency, which are no longer limited to fishing operations but now cover information sharing, the provision of surveillance and communication services and the sharing of resource capacities. in the face of the challenges facing maritime authorities and in the face of the current migration crisis, this report strengthens the capacity of these bodies to respond, because i voted in favour.
‒ national authorities performing coast guard functions are responsible for a large number of functions in fields as diverse as security, rescue at sea, border control, customs control, environmental protection and police. there are currently 316 such national authorities at eu level. these numerous authorities work together through 70 different structures. perhaps for this reason, the current cooperation system suffers from delays and shortcomings, including lack of information on the competences, powers and capacities of other authorities, limited number of operational resources, lack of interoperability of systems and resources and limitation of joint operations and planning. it is essential that maritime surveillance, prevention and control operations are coordinated at european level in order to improve the knowledge of the maritime situation and to support coherent and cost-effective actions.
in writing. ‒ in the context of maritime surveillance, prevention and control, there are currently 316 national authorities working together across the european union (eu) through 70 different structures and with responsibility for numerous functions in a variety of areas. this is the main reason why the current cooperation system suffers from delays and shortcomings, including lack of information on other authorities, limited number of operational resources, lack of interoperability of systems and resources and limitation of joint operations and planning. the aim of this regulation is to coordinate at european level the monitoring, prevention and control of maritime activities (and not just fisheries), improving common knowledge and supporting coherent and effective action. the three european agencies the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european coast and border guard agency should cooperate with each other, combining capabilities and sharing surveillance information. the joint work of these agencies will facilitate the work of national authorities, allowing for joint and more effective action in control, safety and surveillance operations through the provision of information, equipment, training and the key coordination of multi-purpose operations. i agree with the proposal for a regulation and therefore approve this report.

‒ this report aims to amend regulation (eu, euratom) no 883/2013 as regards the secretariat of the supervisory committee of the european anti-fraud office (olaf). the european parliament has on several occasions called on the commission to take measures to strengthen the independent functioning of the olaf supervisory committee secretariat, as there were concerns about possible conflicts of interest, and called for legal independence to be strengthened. the monitoring committee itself also stressed the importance of its independent and effective functioning and made suggestions in this regard. under the proposed new regulation, the secretariat of the supervisory committee will now be provided by the commission, and no longer by olaf. the budgetary appropriations for the secretariat of the supervisory committee will be transferred from the budget line and staff establishment plan of olaf to those of the commission (article 18), so that the proposed amendment will not have any financial impact on the eu budget. finally, the proposal amends the wording of article 10 (4) and (5) so that the competence of the data protection officer (dpo) of olaf continues to cover the processing of data by the secretariat, and the staff of the secretariat will continue to be subject to the same confidentiality rules as before.

‒ the current multiannual financial framework was adopted in 2013 for the 2014-2020 programming period. i therefore believe that the mandatory 2016 review is important for three reasons: because this mff was the first to be adopted under the special legislative procedure provided for in the lisbon treaty, and it is therefore useful to assess the effectiveness of this procedure; because the mff reflects the eu's priorities in 2013, and therefore needs to be adapted to the challenges we face today; and because a review after the 2014 european elections reinforces the democratic legitimacy of a revised mff endorsed by the current composition of the institutions. the challenges we have faced in recent years, such as the migrant and refugee crisis, the financing of the strategic fund for strategic investments, the fight against unemployment (especially among young people) and the crisis in the agricultural sector, have led us to consider that the ceilings for the mff should be increased under the treaties. i would stress the need to increase funding for union structures which have acquired new powers, such as frontex or easo. i believe that the commitment to compensation under horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility should be respected. i therefore support the report.
‒ the current multiannual financial framework (mff) was the first to be adopted under the new provisions of the lisbon treaty and reflects the priorities of the union at the time of its adoption. however, the eu continues to face challenges that were not foreseen when the mff was adopted, and parliament has called for the inclusion of a post-election review clause. a review of the mff in 2016 should take stock of a number of major crises and new policy initiatives and their budgetary consequences that were not foreseen when they were adopted, including the migrant and refugee crisis, external emergencies, internal security issues, the crisis in agriculture, the financing of the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), the crisis of payments to the eu budget and the persistence of high unemployment, especially among young people, as well as poverty and social exclusion.
‒ this report takes a position on the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework (mff) for 2014-2020. the european commission should submit a proposal for the revision of the mff regulation, initiating the special legislative procedure, which requires unanimity in the council and the consent of parliament by a majority of its members. the report mentions the fact that the mff has already reached its limits. it gives examples of the migration crisis, low investment, youth unemployment, 'internal security' issues, the agricultural crisis, environmental challenges and payment delays. the commission is also proposing to increase the number of member states that have already adopted the euro by a factor of two, i.e. by increasing the number of member states that have already adopted the euro by a factor of two. it is argued that the decision to adopt the mff regulation by the council should be taken by qualified majority. unfortunately, the report misses the essential point: the role of the budget in implementing the much-vaunted principle of economic and social cohesion. there is no real cohesion without a substantial increase in the eu budget, at least doubling it, and without a change in policies.
‒ the current multiannual financial framework, which was established in 2013 reflecting the priorities of the european union at the time of its adoption, has been tested in a number of situations for which no provision existed. given that the eu's financial and political priorities have multiplied and undergone some mutations, this change of circumstances should also be reflected in the mff. in this connection, democratic legitimacy must also be taken into account in the adoption of the mff, which is why a post-election review clause was included, thus giving the new commission and the newly elected parliament the opportunity to reassess the political and budgetary priorities of the european union and make the necessary adjustments. i therefore vote in favour of this report, since i believe it is important to adapt the financial allocations to the new challenges that are emerging.
‒ the current multiannual financial framework was adopted in 2013 for the period 2014-2020 and was the first to be adopted under the new provisions of the lisbon treaty. in this context, the commission should review the functioning of the existing framework by the end of 2016, taking into account the economic context at that time and its future projections. between 2013 and 2016, major crises and new policy initiatives took place in the european space, which were not foreseen when this framework was formulated. the migrant and refugee crisis, worrying levels of unemployment (especially among young people), european fund for strategic investment funding and the agricultural crisis have therefore reinforced the importance of this reassessment. in order to respond to emerging crises, flexibility provisions and special instruments do not have the flexibility and scale to respond to similar situations, thus making it necessary to provide additional appropriations to respond to them in the future. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ regardless of the more or less specific aspects that the report rightly points out the payment deficit, the instruments and the flexibility margins , the simple truth is that this budget is totally incompatible with the proclaimed objectives of social and territorial cohesion set out in the treaties. this incompatibility arises from two orders of reason. firstly, the amounts are far below what is needed for an effective redistributive policy that would allow disadvantaged countries and regions to come closer to richer regions. it is significant that this multiannual budget has been reduced for the first time in the history of european integration. secondly, this budget is short because a large part of these resources, which are already scarce, are not used to promote cohesion. a significant part of the budget is now being used to finance the eu's repressive and security policies, thus taking away funds that should be directed towards cohesion objectives or support for farmers who are victims of the eu's foreign policy. we want more money, but we demand that it be put to use in the service of a redistributive policy which reduces disparities and strengthens cohesion.

in writing. ‒ in principle, we will not be against the need to exploit synergies between horizon 2020 (the research framework programme) and the structural and investment funds which are themselves a fruit of the current multiannual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020 and a (confusion) between structural funds and investment funds. but this resolution hides essential issues. the structural and investment funds are one of the main instruments at the service of cohesion policy. they are not, and have never been, sufficient, even in conjunction with the other instruments, to give effect to the principle of cohesion, far from it. cohesion is nothing but dead letter on the pages of the treaties. as usual, by the way. the research framework programme has always been an instrument which is mainly used by the large countries, which are more powerful economically and have more developed scientific and technological systems. for this reason, portugal, for example, was a net contributor to the previous programmes, i.e. it contributed more money than it had the capacity to collect. the framework programme, including horizon 2020, lacks a cohesion dimension, without which it is nothing but an instrument of divergence. none of these original sins have been corrected in the current mfn. on the contrary, they have been aggravated, a fact which the resolution ignores.
‒ the european structural and investment funds are the main instrument of the european union's investment policy, with a budget of eur 454 billion for the period 2014-2020, and are managed by the eu countries in a decentralised manner under a shared management system. in this framework, coherence and synergy between all eu instruments should be ensured in order to achieve the overall strategic objectives and to avoid overlaps or contradictions between these instruments or between different levels of policy implementation, while complementing national and regional funds and programmes. in this regard, the review of the europe 2020 strategy should identify a more efficient use of available resources and achieve the expected results in terms of overall strategic objectives, given that the quantity, quality and impact of r&d investments should be increased through the coordinated use of the instruments of cohesion policy and horizon 2020. i am voting in favour of this, as i believe it is important to promote synergies in the implementation of the various structural funds in order to ensure a more effective implementation and to contribute to the achievement of the objectives set out in the union's policy framework.
‒ the cohesion policy in the 2014-2020 financial programme aims to increase investment in the real economy and promote solidarity between citizens in all regions, thereby reducing economic, social and territorial disparities between them. cohesion policy should be in sync with the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. however, i believe that efforts should be made to increase synergies with other european policies in the field of competitiveness, information and communication technologies, research and development, support for smes and job creation policies. nevertheless, in the light of all the above, i support this joint resolution.
‒ this report focuses on the importance of synergies for innovation between the european structural and investment funds (esif), the horizon 2020 programme and other union funds in the field of innovation. cohesion policy remains the eu's main instrument for bringing the eu closer to its citizens, bringing together all regions for investment in the real economy and thus constituting the main expression of european solidarity. the esi funds, by virtue of the common provisions, are perfectly aligned with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. in doing so, it should be result-oriented by enhancing synergies with other european policies in terms of enhancing competitiveness, particularly in areas focusing on research and development, information and communication technologies, renewable energy and smes. the involvement of national or regional managing authorities and universities, industry and social partners in smart specialisation strategies in the search for and realisation of these synergies is essential for member states and, above all, for regions wishing to invest erdf resources in these areas of research and innovation. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i consider it very important that there are synergies that catalyse the most appropriate use of all sources of funding, including those from the european union. i find that this report points in that direction, by identifying a number of possibilities and opportunities for improvement. i am concerned that budget cuts have been made in the horizon 2020 programme and so it seems to me that the synergies now identified can help to close this gap. as mentioned, it seems to me important that the commission systematically monitors synergies between the funds and publishes a communication on these synergies, in particular on the synergies between horizon 2020 and ris3, with the aim of disseminating examples of best practices and increasing their impact in the perspective of the review of the europe 2020 strategy. these are the reasons why i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in the same vein, the commission has been working on the implementation of the new eu-portugal association agreement, which will be signed in brussels on 1 january. portugal was a net contributor to the 7th research framework programme, the predecessor of horizon 2020. that is, the same country that for years has been funding the science of the rich, including some who are now calling for sanctions. portugal's structural funds are largely outstripped by capital transfers from portugal to the european union in the form of interest, profits and dividends. it is not just the pressure and blackmail of the european commission that is illegitimate and intolerable. it is also the real extortion to which they continue to subject the portuguese people.
‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the commission should provide more information on the synergies of cohesion policy with the other funds, such as horizon 2020 (h2020), which are currently underestimated. i believe that to close this gap, synergies with other eu competitiveness policies, in particular in the field of research and development, ict, renewable energy and smes, should be strengthened with a view to better exploiting the results of research carried out in the eu, creating new high-quality jobs and maintaining existing ones, as well as promoting the green economy.
‒ the commission work programme for 2017, consistent with the assumptions of the review of the mff 2014-2020 and the eu budget for 2017, should seek to strengthen citizens' confidence in the integration project by tackling the crises we face more effectively. i agree that the eu's migration and asylum policy must be reviewed, but that no reform of the common european asylum system should result in less protection than is currently the case. i stress the need for greater cooperation with the countries of origin and transit of refugees, but i also stress the urgency of committing the member states to a more dignified, committed and effective system of reception and relocation of refugees. i believe that the building of a 'european pillar of social rights' will be successful only if concrete action is taken in the fields of education and work, with a particular focus on combating youth unemployment and promoting decent work. i share the view that the necessary deepening of economic and monetary union must be accompanied by a more active policy in defence of fundamental rights and democracy. i therefore support the joint motion for a resolution.
‒ europe is facing many common and global challenges today, but also growing frustration and concern on the part of many citizens about the uncertainty of life prospects and the lack of opportunities that citizens expect policymakers to address. the eu is our common home and must provide its citizens with a safe space and a stable economic environment. however, europe's economic recovery has been modest and unbalanced, and many regions of the union continue to experience unacceptable levels of unemployment, poverty, inequality and a serious lack of prospects for younger generations. promoting access to and quality of early childhood education, childcare facilities and child health care, closing skills gaps, reducing social inequalities, promoting quality employment and addressing the challenges of work-life balance should be the focus of the commission's thinking in the near future.
the joint motion for a resolution, signed by the right (conservatives, liberals) and the social democrats, thus demonstrating the vitality of the sacred alliance that has underpinned the course of european capitalist integration, is revealing of the nature of these forces and the gravity of the moment we are going through: a deep political, economic and social crisis inherent in the process of european capitalist integration, which highlights the deep contradictions that characterize it, as a result of its class nature. these forces are now dogmatically defending a project which reality shows to be exhausted, and are trying new ways of escaping, deepening the eu's federalist character and the concentration of power in the great powers and the supranational institutions at their service, against the interests and aspirations of the peoples. but the resolution tabled by our group shows that this is not an inevitable path. on the contrary, a different europe, of the workers and the peoples, is possible, one which respects national sovereignty and the equality of rights between states, and which is a champion of social progress, peace and cooperation between peoples. the resolution contains proposals of wide-ranging scope, including the repeal of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and the treaty of lisbon, the creation of a programme to support member states wishing to leave the euro and the renegotiation of debts.
‒ a resolution forged between the right and the social democrats, which has the aftermath of the vote in the uk referendum and a reformist and forward-looking vision that points to the solution of deepening the process of european capitalist integration, more federalism, more austerity and more militarism. it refers to the deepening of the lisbon treaty and the completion of economic and monetary union and banking union. it whitewashes and endorses the current criminal eu migration policy and the militarization of the response to a humanitarian crisis, as well as the xenophobic and racist view of integration based on the qualifications of asylum seekers. the security and militarist vision, the deepening of the european external agenda and the strengthening of cooperation with nato are presented without surprise, using the pretext of the fight against terrorism to defend further integration and external interference obvious efforts to whitewash the deep crisis in which the european union is immersed, the contradictions that result from it and its policies and the oppressive character of this project in the most diverse areas. history is showing how necessary it is to break with this edifice that serves the interests of capital, in order to build a europe of cooperation and relations between states of equal rights. we voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the european project is going through one of its most sensitive phases since the schuman declaration in 1950. the refugee crisis, the successive terrorist attacks, the economic crisis and the result of the referendum in the united kingdom clearly jeopardise the deepening of the union. i therefore believe that the main priority is to strengthen citizens' confidence in the project of integration, cooperation and solidarity that we all aspire to today as we did in the past. this resolution covers several priority areas for action, all of which are important for the development of this joint project. i share the importance of ensuring better working conditions for our citizens, while boosting the european economy and generating wealth for the long term. i also share the idea that we must complete emu, without forgetting the potential of the single market, which must be adapted to the digital age. i believe it is urgent to ensure better levels of security within our borders, while at the same time creating better integration conditions for all those seeking asylum in member states. the present proposal addresses all these concerns and i therefore vote in favour.
‒ europe's economic recovery has been modest and uneven. many regions of the union continue to suffer from unacceptable levels of unemployment, poverty, inequality and a serious lack of prospects for young generations. in this sense, the eu must work towards a dynamic and inclusive labour market that makes a decisive contribution to improving the lives of citizens and enabling their mobility. the commission should therefore take into account in its 2017 programme: improving the working and living conditions of european citizens; strengthening economic recovery and long-term competitiveness with a view to creating jobs, raising living standards and generating prosperity; an adequate response to climate change, ensuring energy security; a consistent response to the increased influx of refugees; citizens' security concerns; the implementation of an ambitious external action agenda; fair fiscal policies; the strengthening of the eu budget and financial instruments and the strengthening of fundamental rights and democracy.

‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the preparation of the commission work programme for 2017, as i agree with the strategic priorities presented for the european commission work programme for 2017. the strategic priorities set are appropriate to the challenges facing the eu: improving the living conditions of europeans, strengthening the economy, responding to the opportunities associated with the energy transition and the digital revolution, integrating refugees, completing economic and monetary union, developing an ambitious foreign policy and fighting tax evasion. i would stress that these strategic priorities must move from the paper to the concrete life of european citizens. the commission must take a constructive and not a punitive attitude. the euro area's shared budget has to be clearly strengthened, approaching 10% of european gdp, to support a functioning monetary area. transparency and democratic control must be strengthened. without these assumptions, the commission will hardly achieve in 2017 what it has not achieved in the previous years of its mandate.
‒ despite an international ban that came into force in 1986, japan continued its whaling activities, killing more than 20 000 whales by 2014 in an activity that causes great suffering to the animals and threatens the conservation status of all whale populations. the court ordered japan to suspend its annual whaling. i am concerned that the decision to resume whaling has allowed the hunting of 333 dwarf whales, including 200 pregnant females, and that japan intends to hunt a total of almost 4 000 whales over the 12-year period, in complete disregard of the court decision.
in writing. in november 2015, the japanese fisheries agency notified the international whaling commission that it would resume whaling under a revised 12-year plan - hunting that, in fact, has hardly ever stopped. this plan would allow the killing of 333 antarctic dwarf whales during the 2015-2016 season and a total of nearly 4,000 whales over the entire 12-year period. the international whaling commission (iwc) banned commercial whaling of all whale species in 1982. however, japan continued whaling under various pretexts, including pretexts of scientific studies, and by 2008/2009 japan had killed over 17000 whales. in 2013, australia and new zealand took japan to the international court of justice, which rejected japan's scientific whaling program. japan is clearly ignoring the court's and the iwc's decision by resuming whaling activities. those activities constitute a violation of international law and undermine the protection of marine biodiversity and ecosystems, in particular because many of the targeted and non-targeted species caught are endangered. the resolution expresses this set of concerns in an overall correct and appropriate way. we voted in favour.
‒ although in 1882 the international whaling commission imposed a moratorium on all commercial whaling activities to limit the killing and commercial exploitation of whales in order to prevent their extinction and promote their recovery, the truth is that this is still a practice in many countries. considering that japan is a strategic partner of the european union and that the bilateral relationship is based on common values, including a firm belief in effective multilateralism and a rules-based international order, the eu should use its weight on the international scene and condemn the resumption of whaling practices in japan, as the protection and promotion of the environment and biodiversity should be a key element of its action. i am voting in favour of this because i believe that whaling is threatening the survival of species and biodiversity in our oceans and that the eu should adopt a common position on this matter.
‒ the international whaling commission is concerned with the judicious conservation of whales and the orderly development of the whaling industry. in 1986 the commission adopted a moratorium on commercial whaling, which is still in force today and aims to protect and enable the recovery of the species. this resolution deplores the fact that japan ignores the decisions prohibiting the continuation of whaling, on the grounds of hunting for scientific purposes, in the period 2015-2016 under a programme called newrep-a. however, the commission investigators concluded that the justification for such a programme did not demonstrate the need for such practices. considering that it is important to protect marine biodiversity and ensure the conservation of species, as well as to respect the international conclusions defined by the international whaling commission, i vote in favour.
in 1982, the international whaling commission (iwc) imposed a moratorium on all commercial whaling activities (which came into force in 1986), which is still in force, in order to protect stocks from extinction and allow their recovery (the moratorium includes special provisions allowing the hunting of limited quantities of animals for strictly scientific purposes). commercial whaling continues to be practiced by several countries and the number of whales killed under special licences for purported scientific research has been increasing (japan has been doing this for decades). since the ban came into force in 1986, japan has continued its whaling activities, killing more than 20,000 whales by 2014. this resolution urges japan to cease its whaling activities and to respect the iwc's conclusions.
in writing. ‒ in 1982, the international whaling commission (iwc) imposed a moratorium on all commercial whaling activities in order to protect whale stocks, combat their extinction and enable their recovery. however, the activity is still practised by some countries. in 2014, the international court of justice (icj) ordered japan to suspend its annual whaling due to 'lack of scientific merit' and the fact that the permits granted were not being used for scientific research as stated. in 2015, the japan fisheries agency notified the cbi that it would resume whaling for scientific purposes. as japan is a strategic partner of the eu, outlining the same common values, this motion for a resolution (proposed by 7 parliamentary groups), which i agree with, is aimed at urging japan to cease these activities, respecting the iwc conclusions. in fact, despite diplomatic efforts and widespread international protest, japan has not yet given in to its position, and the eu institutions and member state governments are called upon to use all available bilateral and multilateral channels to force japan to reverse its decision.
‒ in 30 years of experience in scientific research at sea, my teams and i have conducted numerous studies on the biology, food ecology, ecotoxicology, migration and population dynamics of various species of atlantic cetaceans. in addition, we used information from animals we found washed up on the shore. we studied behavior, analyzed sketches, performed biopsies, conducted censuses, put transmitters and sensors on individuals that we monitored through hydrophones and satellites, and produced mathematical models that we used to understand these fascinating animals. in these studies, we never had to kill any subjects! technological developments now give us tools and methods that, while intrusive in some cases, do little to disturb the animals in their study. the study of stable isotopes, genetic analysis and genomics allows us to know about eating habits, migration dynamics and even kinship relations. there is now a huge body of nonlethal methods that are excellent approximations to reality and are fully accepted by the scientific community. for these reasons, i consider it false to argue the need to use lethal methods for scientific purposes. for all these reasons, and more, i voted in favour of this resolution.

‒ the european banking authority has issued an opinion to the commission expressing its disagreement with some of the proposed amendments to the final draft regulatory technical standards (rtns) on the criteria for determining the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities (mrel). however, the commission should, in a new delegated act, take into account the assessment of the ability of systemic institutions to meet the burden-sharing requirements, the elimination of the downward adjustment test for the recapitalisation amount and the peer-to-peer comparison for systemic institutions and, finally, the maintenance in the delegated regulation of the 48-month deadline for the transition period.
‒ in writing. ‒ in accordance with the second paragraph of article 45 of directive 2014/59/eu (bank recovery and resolution directive), the european commission may adopt, following submission of preliminary standards by the european banking authority, delegated acts specifying valuation criteria relating to the methodology for setting the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities. the resolution is based on the grounds that the political group which proposed it considers that the european commission has weakened the regulatory technical standards of the european banking authority, putting at risk the functioning of the bail-in provisions in the bank recovery and resolution directive. although criticism is directed at the european commission, the criticism in this objection is not limited to the banking union and its real objectives, as well as to this specific banking union directive and its inability to prevent further bailouts of private banks from being carried out with public money. of course, such criticisms are not contained in a resolution with the above-mentioned motivation, nor should they be. our abstention is inseparable from the fundamental disagreement we have on the whole building of the banking union, including this directive, which is an integral part of it.
in writing. ‒ the aim of directive 2014/59/eu on deposit-guarantee schemes is to facilitate access to and the pursuit of the business of credit institutions by removing certain differences between the laws of the member states as regards the rules on deposit-guarantee schemes to which credit institutions are subject. article 45 (2) of directive 2014/59/eu empowers the commission to adopt delegated acts specifying valuation criteria for the methodology for determining the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities. in this context, the commission has submitted this draft delegated regulation, which has been substantially amended. i therefore vote in favour of this report, as i believe that the commission should revise its proposal in order to maintain these criteria, ensure the coherence of the directive and ensure legal certainty.
‒ this motion for a resolution is to some extent opposed to the commission delegated regulation supplementing directive 2014/58/eu of the parliament and of the council with regard to regulatory technical standards specifying the criteria for the methodology for determining the minimum capital requirement and the minimum eligible liabilities (mrel). the relevant delegated regulation of 23 may 2016 specifies the criteria that bank resolution authorities should consider when determining mrel for loss absorption and recapitalisation effects. the objective of mrel is to ensure that banks hold sufficient high quality capital and liabilities eligible for high quality bail-in that can be readily used to absorb losses and for recapitalisation purposes once it has been secured through resolution. these criteria are very important, as they ensure that in times of financial difficulties the banking institution concerned is 'saved' and supported by its shareholders and creditors - and, crucially, not by taxpayers. the recommendations in this report do not make any clear improvements to the commission's delegated regulation, so my vote is against.
in writing. ‒ we believe that, as regards systemic institutions, assessing the possibility of meeting burden-sharing requirements is a requirement that should be explicitly maintained in the delegated regulation, to ensure consistency with the directive and to ensure legal certainty. the commission has deleted two other provisions in the draft rules submitted by eba which are important for the application of the mrel and for the internal recapitalisation. in this respect, the assumptions of the delegated act are lacking.

in writing. the debate on the legal basis in the eu treaties for legislation on the protection of whistleblowers is not a legal issue but a political one, and above all a question of political will. the status quo is intolerable where those with integrity and courage to speak out against corruption, tax fraud and other crimes and to expose information of clear public interest are subjected to retaliation without any legal protection. we need a horizontal framework of protection at eu level. we must protect freedom of expression and those who fight for decency and the rule of law in our societies, such as antoine deltour and raphael halet, the two former pricewaterhousecoopers employees who were at the origin of the luxleaks scandal, and who were perversely sentenced by the luxembourg judiciary to 12 and 9 months in prison respectively, with suspended sentences. the commission is using an excuse about the legal basis for not acting. but this is a political choice, and we have to move now. a society that protects its whistleblowers will certainly be a more transparent, a more just, a more equal and a more democratic society.

‒ this resolution objects to an initiative by the european commission to amend regulation (eu) no 432/2012 establishing a list of permitted health claims made on foods other than those referring to the reduction of disease risk or to children's development and health. by january 2009, the commission should have established the specific nutritional profiles to be met by foods or certain categories of foods in order to be able to make nutrition or health claims, as well as the conditions for the use of nutrition and health claims in relation to nutritional profiles. the commission has submitted a draft regulation which contains claims that caffeine contributes to enhancing vigilance status and to improving concentration. it is therefore considered that the draft commission regulation is not compatible with the purpose and content of regulation (ec) no 1924/2006, which states that 'nutrition and health claims should not [...] encourage or justify the excessive consumption of a given food'. the european food safety authority concluded that there is not enough information to establish a safe level of caffeine consumption for children. the problems are mainly related to the consumption of energy drinks by adolescents. we voted in favour.

madam president, commissioner, even if these summits do not produce the immediate solutions that the world needs, it is important that the great powers should at least be able to agree on a correct diagnosis of the main problems facing the world. at this summit, the g20 leaders realized that the world is facing a return of nationalist and protectionist discourses. seduced by such talk, the populations of various countries are pointing to globalization as the main culprit of the labour and social difficulties affecting them. in their final communiqué, the g20 leaders set out to fight protectionism and remove obstacles to international trade and investment, while recognising, importantly, that globalisation is not a homogeneous phenomenon. in developing countries and emerging economies, globalization has been linked in recent years to progress in poverty reduction, increasing life expectancy and reducing infant mortality, among others. but in developed countries, it has had some adverse effects in terms of, for example, job insecurity and tax evasion. the final communiqué recognises the benefits of globalisation and that these must be widely shared. but a communiqué is no substitute for a plan, and there has been no clear commitment to global regulatory measures that can neutralize the difficulties that globalization has also brought about and restart growth.

‒ research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation (ris3) are a key driver for knowledge-based economic growth, for increasing the eu's innovation capacity and for building a cohesion policy based on the europe 2020 objectives. as such, they are an ex ante condition for member states and regions to benefit from the european structural and investment funds (esif), which leads to the design of an ris3 strategy in each of the regions, which is a positive development. i share the concern about the need to reduce red tape in order to speed up the implementation of the strategies and the need to ensure that they are continuously reviewed, given the constant developments in this area. i stress that the implementation of these strategies should seek to promote interregional cooperation, also promoting synergies between eu research infrastructures, in the context of cohesion policy 2014-2020. the full implementation of the urban agenda, focusing on the creation of smart cities, should be a priority, as should the areas of renewable energy, the digital agenda or public health, as per the swot analysis of each region. i therefore support the report.
‒ ris3 strategies are a valuable tool to bridge the innovation gap and boost jobs and growth in europe. public authorities should try to pay particular attention to the monitoring and review of strategies in order to maximise their results on the one hand and interregional cooperation on the other, with the aim of developing ambitious projects that create added value for the economy. the organisation of a european-wide conference and the development of a policy guidance document incorporating the main lessons learned from experience in this area are very useful tools for continuous improvement.
‒ the european regional development fund (erdf), in support of thematic objective 1, has established that regions should channel their rdi (research, development and innovation) investments through smart specialisation strategies in the 2014-2020 programming period. therefore, ris3 are an ex ante condition for eu member states and regions to benefit from the european structural and investment funds. all european regions have an ris3 strategy in place. these strategies were shaped and started to be implemented during 2014 and 2015. although the report relates to the dimension of meeting eu objectives (in particular through the eu 2020 strategy, which we reject), the logic of centring rdi strategies on member states and regional and local bodies allows for a more realistic definition of needs and more sustained development prospects (not imposed, the logic seems to be that the achievement of the local objective can contribute to the overall objective). the mobilisation of structural and investment funds linked to social and territorial cohesion, in the context of a ris approach, could contribute to investment in economic dynamism, particularly in support of smes, which, especially in the context of the economic depression imposed by austerity and neoliberal asphyxiation policies, seems positive.
‒ in this time of economic, financial and social crisis, the eu must step up its efforts towards smart, sustainable and inclusive economic growth. it is necessary for stakeholders to develop ris3 based on the analysis of the capacities, resources and competences of each region, with the aim of identifying emerging niches or comparative advantages for smart specialisation, avoiding forced and artificial over-specialisation and reinforcing a stronger partnership between the public and private sectors, while avoiding possible conflicts of interest between the public and private sectors. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. ‒ in an era of economic recession and budgetary constraints, as well as increasingly tough global competition, it is crucial for the eu to sustainably improve its innovation capacity in terms of research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation. we will have to pay particular attention to the continuous review of these same strategies; analysing priorities, strengths and potential of each region; developing participation processes; creating synergies between public and private actors; coordinating between all levels of government and departments and identifying alternative funding routes and finally simplifying and reducing administrative procedures.
‒ research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation (ris3) are an ex ante conditionality for the allocation of funding through the european structural and investment funds (esi funds). in fact, ris3 strategies support the thematic concentration objectives and the strategic programming of the esi funds by promoting their 'performance orientation'. this report, which analysed the relationship/inclusion of these strategies within the framework of cohesion policy, reflects parliament's position on them within the framework of the current multiannual financial framework, demonstrating parliament's support for the implementation 'on the ground' of ris3 strategies, calling for their further development and a process of lifelong learning with projects already approved or under implementation, simplification of procedures and greater coordination in the implementation of current programmes. the report, which i voted for, stresses that ris3 strategies are not exclusively aimed at the more developed regions. on the contrary, they are intended to be a smart, innovative and effective means of enhancing the strengths and opportunities of the less developed regions, creating synergies with a view to developing a more knowledge-based economy, creating value and added value for the population.
‒ cohesion policy is the hallmark of the european union, reflecting the practice of solidarity which underpins its construction. cohesion policy serves as a catalyst for national public policies aimed at fostering economic development and growth, employment opportunities, more and better education and social inclusion. this is particularly relevant in regions of europe where there are greater social, economic and territorial disparities and where, inevitably, there is less resilience to economic crisis situations. the outermost regions are part of this context. i therefore call for cohesion policy to remain part of the eu's political priorities and for it to be adequately funded. i oppose any attempt to penalise member states suffering from major macroeconomic imbalances by suspending policy instruments with an impact on cohesion, which are precisely the key to boosting investment, the economy and job creation. the possibility of suspending the structural funds implies a double penalty which follows a logic which departs from the principle of solidarity which is the foundation of the union and which is closer to a strategy of absolute strangulation of economies suffering from additional fragility. this is a logic i can only repudiate.

‒ european territorial cooperation (etc) comprises the crossborder, transnational and interregional cooperation dimensions and is one of the two objectives of cohesion policy. the significant financial dimension of interreg for the period 2014-2020 (eur 10,1 billion), which in addition to these dimensions includes the co-financing of regional development cooperation programmes outside the eu, attests to its importance, but also to the need to de-bureaucratize and streamline processes in order to concentrate resources on priority objectives, strengthen the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy and improve the economic, social and territorial potential of regions by integrating their sectoral policies. i believe that in the 25 years of interreg, best practices in the areas of financial guidance in the areas of connectivity, mobility and accessibility; support for innovation and science; increasing the competitiveness of smes; preventing natural disasters; promoting inclusive growth based on employment, education and training; and sustainable management of environmental and energy resources should be brought together. i support the call for better coordination of the etc's financing mechanisms with the strategic and investment funds, eliminating overlaps and ensuring governance that is more consistent with the objectives of territorial cohesion. i therefore support the report.
in writing. ‒ currently, 28 member states benefit from the etc. the amount allocated to the tec is eur 10.1 billion: 74.1% for crossborder cooperation - 60 programmes, 20.4% for transnational cooperation - 15 programmes and 5.6% for interregional cooperation - 4 programmes. interreg also co-finances regional development cooperation programmes outside the eu: crossborder cooperation programmes under the instrument for pre-accession assistance (242 million specifically for crossborder cooperation) and 16 crossborder cooperation programmes under the european neighbourhood instrument (634 million specifically for crossborder cooperation). i agree, therefore, that cte has a great leverage effect.
in writing. our position on european territorial cooperation (etc) has been critical, based on the understanding that it pursues the objective of overcoming the remaining obstacles to the functioning of the eu's single market, in particular those related to the obstacles to the free movement of goods and the migration of workers between countries, based not on their interests and aspirations (and taking advantage of the hardship of life imposed on them), but on the labour needs of capital. the eec does not correspond to cooperation based on mutual benefit, solidarity and based on the sovereignty and complementary interests of the countries involved, with which we would undoubtedly agree, but rather with the intention of hindering what they consider to be the sovereign and national development models. cooperation and integration are a reality and a necessity enhanced by the development of the productive forces, particularly technological and scientific development. this report, emphasising the issue of financial instruments and giving priority to public-private partnerships, notes that, as in other cases, tax cooperation is being promoted with a view to facilitating the concentration and centralisation of (monopolistic) capital throughout the eu.
‒ the overall objective of the etc is to reduce the influence of national borders in order to reduce disparities between regions, reduce remaining obstacles to investment and cooperation-based work across national borders, strengthen cohesion and promote harmonious economic, social, cultural and territorial development throughout the union. so we have to keep finding the best practices to achieve the goals we set. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ interreg, set up in 1990, was developed as a community initiative with a budget of eur 1 billion, covering exclusively crossborder cooperation and benefiting 11 member states. it was later extended to transnational and interregional cooperation. in 2015, european territorial cooperation (etc) was highlighted as an important cohesion policy instrument, designed to address problems that transcend administrative borders and require common solutions. the etc has numerous examples of the benefits in the following best practices: overcoming border challenges in transport and people movement, supporting smart transport solutions and multimodal transport hubs; simplifying cross-border travel; improving interconnectivity with a focus on road infrastructure; improving maritime accessibility by improving regional ports; specialised services such as healthcare for older people; cross-border health solutions; investment plan for building structures for older people to keep them active in society and to provide them with as healthy and fulfilling lives as possible, among others. i agree with the rapporteur that the management and implementation of the etc programmes should be made less bureaucratic. i support the importance of the etc as a vital instrument for the process of european integration.
‒ i voted in favour because i believe that the etc, through its results orientation, makes a significant contribution to improving the economic, social and territorial potential of the regions by reflecting and integrating various sectoral policies at the territorial level and by transcending national borders, also affecting municipalities and regions on an individual basis. the desire to overcome frontier challenges has enabled smes to participate in concrete innovative activities: networking between companies, knowledge institutes and service providers, access to cutting-edge technologies to test product ideas, use appropriate manufacturing techniques and market their products worldwide, tourism development, among others. the etc has also enabled joint responses to environmental problems such as joint monitoring of watersheds, better use of marine resources and by-products, creating artificial reefs to improve biodiversity, joint cooperation in harmonising activities on flood prevention and water quality improvement and improving spatial planning and risk management in the alpine area, as well as addressing other environmental challenges such as coastal pollution, forest fire risk and improved monitoring of ports, etc.
in writing. ‒ since 1990, interreg - the genesis of european territorial cooperation (etc) - has been developed with the aim of promoting crossborder cooperation, benefiting 11 member states, and has subsequently been extended to transnational and interregional cooperation. in the previous multiannual financial framework (mff), the etc demonstrated its effectiveness in serving the objectives of cohesion policy as a programme designed to solve problems that go beyond administrative borders - but which require common solutions, involving several member states or even third countries. in this mff, the etc has been restructured to become more targeted and efficient. the aim was also to make the use of investments more effective through thematic concentration and result orientation. it is thus seen that the etc contributes significantly to the improvement of the economic, social and territorial potential of the regions by reflecting and integrating diverse sectoral policies at the territorial level and by promoting cross-border/transnational as well as interregional cooperation. recognising the importance of the etc in the strategic areas mentioned and considering that the report shows in a systematic and quite clear way its added value, best practices, support for research and innovation and its contribution to the europe 2020 strategy, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ these new european territorial cooperation practices are essentially designed to strengthen, promote and favour the actions of the territorial space of the member states of the european union in transnational and interregional collaboration. this transnational and interregional cooperation immediately benefits the macro-regions and cross-border areas, immediately increasing their level of integration and economic and social cohesion in the european strategic area. the importance of public-private partnerships should also be stressed in order to harmonise these good cooperation practices, facilitating political and economic issues. clearly, this will have to be accompanied by ensuring transparency and correctness in all planning, approaches and procedures.

in writing. this report deals with a request for the defence of the parliamentary immunity of rosario crocetta, then a member of the european parliament. this member of parliament is facing a criminal case pending before the 3rd criminal section of the court of palermo for allegedly making defamatory statements, which is punishable by article 595 of the italian penal code. meps may not be subject to any search, arrest or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties, as a means of protecting their freedom of expression and political action, article 8 of protocol no 7. the statements made by the member in question in the context of the fight against organised crime were the subject of the criminal proceedings in question. it is considered that the facts of the case, as shown by the documents provided to the competent authorities, such as the committee on legal affairs, indicate that the statements made by rosario crocetta have a direct and obvious link with her parliamentary duties. it can be considered that rosario crocetta was acting in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. we therefore voted in favour of the defence of the immunities and privileges of rosario crocetta.

in writing. in january 2016, the president received a request from rosario crocetta, former member of the european parliament, concerning the defence of his parliamentary immunity in a criminal case pending before the court of palermo. in that case, rosario crocetta is charged with crimes of defamation related to organized crime during a political debate on october 2, 2012. according to the court, a statement made by a member outside the european parliament may constitute an opinion expressed in the course of the performance of his duties within the meaning of article 8 of protocol no 7, the relevance of which depends not on the place where the statement was made but on its nature and content. to be included in the spectrum of immunity, an opinion of a member of the european parliament must have a direct and obvious link with his parliamentary duties. the facts of the case, as evidenced by the documents and the hearing held, show that the statements have an obvious link with the parliamentary activities of rosario crocetta. in the light of the foregoing, and in agreement with the court's premises, i cannot but consider that rosario crocetta, in making the statements in question, acted in the exercise of his duties. i therefore vote in favour of the recommendation of the committee on legal affairs.
‒ at the request of the victims, the public prosecutor's office at the court of palermo has charged rosario crocetta with the crime of defamation, punishable by article 595 of the italian penal code. the committee on legal affairs considers that the facts of the case, as evidenced by the documents provided and the rosario crocetta hearing, show that the statements in question have a direct and obvious link with rosario crocetta's parliamentary activities. given the circumstances of the case and the content of the statements, rosario crocetta's allegations are therefore likely to have a direct and obvious link with her activities as a member of the european parliament. in the light of the foregoing, it can be considered that rosario crocetta, in making the statements in question, acted in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. on the basis of rule 9 (3) of the rules of procedure, after considering the arguments for and against the defence of the immunity of rosario crocetta, the committee on legal affairs recommends that the european parliament uphold the immunity and privileges of rosario crocetta. i therefore voted in favour of this request.

in writing. ‒ with the accession of the republic of croatia, the european union has extended its customs union. it is incumbent upon the european union to enter into negotiations with wto members holding negotiating rights related to the customs tariff of croatia in order to reach agreement on a possible compensatory adjustment. this adjustment is necessary if the adoption of the eu external tariff regime results in an increase in customs duties that exceeds the level to which the acceding country has committed itself in the wto. i believe that the european parliament should approve the agreement because the people's republic of china is entitled to the restoration of its previous trade rights, which were slightly degraded due to the enlargement of the customs union when croatia joined the union.
in writing. ‒ with the accession of the republic of croatia, the european union has extended its customs union. consequently, in accordance with the rules of the world trade organisation (wto) (article xxiv:6 of gatt 1994), the eu was obliged to open negotiations with wto members holding negotiating rights related to the customs tariff of croatia in order to reach agreement on a possible compensatory adjustment. on 15 july 2013, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations under article xxiv:6 of the gatt 1994. the commission has negotiated with wto members holding negotiating rights the withdrawal of specific concessions resulting from the withdrawal of the customs tariff of the republic of croatia in the context of its accession to the eu. although the report is eminently technical, our position is inseparable from the position of principle on the grounds for its necessity, which emphasises the eu's exclusive competence in trade policy conferred on it by the treaty of lisbon. we believe that countries should be able to conclude, as a matter of right, the trade agreements they sovereignly understand.
in writing. ‒ with the accession of the republic of croatia, the european union has extended its customs union. consequently, in accordance with the rules of the world trade organisation (wto) (article xxiv:6 of gatt 1994), the european union was obliged to open negotiations with wto members holding negotiating rights related to the customs tariff of croatia in order to reach an agreement on a possible compensatory adjustment. this adjustment is necessary if the adoption of the eu external tariff regime results in an increase in customs duties that exceeds the level to which the acceding country has committed itself in the wto. the people's republic of china is entitled to the restoration of its previous trade rights, which were slightly degraded due to the enlargement of the customs union upon the accession of croatia to the union. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ with the accession of the republic of croatia, the european union has enlarged its customs union. the people's republic of china is entitled to the restoration of its previous trade rights, which were slightly degraded due to the enlargement of the customs union upon the accession of croatia to the union. in accordance with the rules of the world trade organisation, the eu was obliged to open negotiations with wto members holding negotiating rights related to the customs tariff of croatia. the commission has chosen the increase of the tariff quotas and the decrease of the levels of the duties for the chinese products concerned in order to compensate for losses as compensatory instruments. since the proposed conclusion of the agreement amends the concessions in a proportionate manner and is consistent with previous practice and the wto framework, i am in favour of the conclusion of this agreement.
‒ on 1 july 2013, croatia became the 28th member state of the union, thus extending the number of countries in the current customs union. in accordance with the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the union is obliged to renegotiate the terms of the trade agreements underlying the wto guidelines in the event of an enlargement of its customs union. in this context, the commission negotiated with the people's republic of china the application of certain countervailing measures on certain trade duties. this agreement ensures the proportionality of the concessions of each party and is also consistent with the wto framework. in accordance with article xxiv (4) of gatt, in so far as a customs union or a free trade area must aim to facilitate trade between the constituent territories and not create barriers to trade, and in so far as compensatory adjustments are appropriate, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ this is only a technical document relating to the eu-china agreement, in view of croatia's accession to the eu.

‒ the eu has long been collecting data on natural gas and electricity prices, collected and published by eurostat, and its procedure has been improved, but its basis is voluntary. i support the kappel report, which is moving from a voluntary to a mandatory regime for the collection of data on natural gas and electricity prices, avoiding the problems reported by the states, benefiting the consumer and allowing a wide market coverage with a high level of quality of price data. the new rules set out in this report clarify objectives, simplify procedures and increase transparency.
‒ the collection of data on natural gas and electricity end-user prices was carried out on a voluntary basis with a response rate of 100%. the objective of this regulation is to transform a voluntary regime into a mandatory one, in order to avoid problems in the collection of data. this step is necessary to avoid a significant deterioration in the quality of the data from the electricity and natural gas price survey for the household consumption sector and to continue to achieve a broad market coverage as well as a high level of quality of the price data. the aim of this report is to clarify the objectives, simplify certain provisions for reporting authorities and companies that have to provide data, and avoid misunderstandings that in the worst case would lead to incomparable data sets.
‒ since the 1970s, the european commission has been collecting data on natural gas and electricity prices. in 1990, the council adopted the directive defining the procedure for improving price transparency for industrial end-users of gas and electricity, but not for household consumers. the methodology was changed in 2007 to take account of the liberalisation of energy markets. however, data on natural gas and electricity end-user prices were collected on a voluntary basis with a response rate of 100%. the rapporteur believes that the 'objective of this regulation is to transform a voluntary regime into a mandatory one, in order to avoid problems in the collection of data, as has been reported by several member states'. we are in favour of collecting data on gas and electricity prices, with a view to transparency and the protection of households and final consumers. however, this report is just another chapter in the specifications of the european single market and the so-called energy union, masked here and there with pretended good intentions. we voted against it.
‒ competitiveness, sustainability and energy security are the overarching objectives of a resilient energy union with a visionary climate change policy. high-quality, comparable, up-to-date, reliable and harmonised information on natural gas and electricity prices charged to final customers is necessary to define the energy union policy and monitor member states' energy markets. this regulation aims to make available european statistics to support energy policies, in particular those aimed at the creation of a fully integrated internal energy market for consumers. there should be greater transparency of energy costs and prices, as well as public support, to improve market integration. that is why i am voting in favour.
this regulation aims to make compulsory the collection of data on final consumer prices for natural gas and electricity. this amendment is essential in order to avoid a significant deterioration in the quality of the data of the electricity and natural gas price survey for the household consumption sector and to continue to achieve a broad market coverage as well as a high level of quality of the price data. the report aims to clarify the objectives, simplify certain provisions for reporting authorities and companies that have to provide data, and avoid misunderstandings that in the worst case would lead to incomparable data sets. with regard to price allocation, it is for the national regulatory authority or the government to propose a cost allocation methodology and to provide the information necessary to implement the allocation, subject to prior consultation of stakeholders and verification by eurostat in order to ensure price comparability between countries. i agree with the rapporteur that, in making disclosure compulsory, it is important to protect the confidentiality of sensitive information concerning consumers and suppliers.
‒ the main objective of this proposal is to increase the transparency of natural gas and electricity prices for the household consumer. directive 2008/92/ec of the european parliament and of the council provides in this context for a common binding framework on the production, transmission and dissemination of comparable statistics on electricity and natural gas prices to industrial end-users. however, the collection of data on such prices by domestic consumers shall remain on a voluntary basis. the proposal therefore aims to establish a binding system for the collection of the same data also for domestic consumers, thus avoiding problems in the collection of data and ensuring their accuracy and comparability. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it important that data on the prices actually paid by household consumers should be made public, since this proposal promotes social justice and scrutiny of the energy market.
‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is important that the data collection be done in a top-notch way so as to avoid the quality of data available from surveys on electricity and natural gas prices for the household consumption sector deteriorating significantly and to continue to achieve a broad market coverage as well as a high level of quality of price data. a collection of data by the competent national authorities that is correct and includes any sub-components that have been omitted, in particular excise duties, should be provided for the benefit of the citizen. the national regulatory authority or the government shall, after proposing a cost allocation methodology, provide the information necessary to apply this allocation, subject to prior consultation of interested parties and verification by eurostat, in order to ensure comparability of prices between countries.
‒ this report concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on statistics on natural gas and electricity prices. since 1990 there has been a procedure to promote price transparency for the industrial end consumer in these sectors, but not for the household consumer. for this reason, the purpose of this regulation is precisely to transform the current voluntary regime for the collection of data on final consumer prices into a mandatory regime, as a way of avoiding difficulties in the collection and improving the quality of data on electricity and natural gas prices. i therefore support the amendments proposed by the rapporteur, which seek to clarify and simplify the rules and procedures for both the reporting authorities and the companies when providing data. and of course, because i consider this change in the existing paradigm to be important in the interests of simplifying and making statistical data transparent, without jeopardizing the confidentiality of certain consumer information, i supported this report by voting in favour.

in writing. ‒ recently, as a consequence of the economic and financial crisis, levels of unemployment, poverty, exclusion and social inequality have developed worryingly in many member states. given that the 23 million smes in the union represent around 99% of all enterprises, and that these smes generate two out of every three jobs in the european single market, it is logical to assume that their role is important in the economic and social recovery of the member states. under the 3rd thematic objective of the european structural investment funds (esif), strengthening the competitiveness of smes is of great importance for achieving the objectives of cohesion policy and the europe 2020 goal. among the various suggestions made, this report stresses the importance of increasing the effectiveness of sme support mechanisms by simplifying procedures and improving coordination and consistency between european investment policies. in view of the above and considering that smes are the driving force of the european economy, i agree that the support from the esi funds for smes should be increased and i vote in favour of this report.

‒ the commission's annual report on european smes for 2014/2015 indicates that in 2014 smes accounted for 71,4% of the increase in employment in the non-financial corporate sector and employed around 90 million people i.e. 67% of total employment. small and medium-sized enterprises are therefore essential to the economy of eu regions, both in terms of employment and competitiveness. i believe that if local authorities want to be more involved in the management of the esi funds, central administrations should give them the possibility of receiving more decision-making powers, starting with the selection of projects. technical assistance and early participation in the discussions on investment priorities in future funding phases will contribute to this process. since most countries and regions have only just begun to launch programmes, there is scope for the managing authorities and the commission to apply more systematically the principle of partnership enshrined in the regulation and the code of conduct.
‒ the thematic objective 'strengthening the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) ' is of key importance for achieving the objectives of cohesion policy and the europe 2020 strategy. between 2007 and 2013, €70 billion was allocated under cohesion policy to support businesses that created 263 000 jobs, with a doubling of this target for the period 2014-2020. the introduction of these thematic objectives in the 2014-2020 cohesion policy programming provided an effective tool for designing operational programmes with a stronger focus on investment priorities. the thematic concentration and particularly this objective have led to a better orientation of the operational programmes towards a narrower number of strategic objectives, with the result that growth and the quality of job creation for smes have improved. in this respect, i consider this report to be very important, as it provides, on the one hand, a positive assessment of this thematic objective, and, on the other, a perspective for the financial programming period 2014-2020, measuring the achievement of the results achieved to date and trying to draw conclusions for the remaining mff.

‒ this is the eu's fourth macro-regional strategy and can therefore benefit from the experience of the european union's strategies for the baltic sea region, the danube region and the adriatic and ionian region. macro-regional strategies have so far been based on intergovernmental initiatives aimed at areas of our continent long divided by wars and iron curtains, with the aim of relaunching economic and institutional cooperation between these territories. the eusalp strategy is set in a context characterised by different forms of cooperation in the region, such as the alpine area and the alpine convention, in addition to various crossborder interreg programmes. eusalp covers 48 regions and seven countries represented by five member states (italy, france, austria, germany and slovenia) and two third countries (switzerland and liechtenstein). the region, home to more than 80 million people, has a strong human, natural, economic and cultural attraction. i voted in favour.
