‒ the lisbon treaty, by enshrining a set of rules that point to the design of territorial cohesion, has made it possible to create macro-regional strategies, through intergovernmental initiatives, in order to relaunch economic and institutional cooperation between seemingly distant territories. the union strategy for the alpine region (eusalp) covers 48 regions and 7 countries, represented by five member states. the region is home to some 80 million people and has vast natural, economic and cultural resources. this report identifies the priorities put forward by the constituent parts of the region: improving the competitiveness, prosperity and cohesion of the region, ensuring access and interconnection for all the region's inhabitants, and the sustainability of the alps. it should be noted that the present macro-regional strategy builds on the opportunities of existing cooperation initiatives and synergies between different financial instruments of the union, thus applying the principle of the three 'no's' on legislation, funding and institution building. eusalp offers an opportunity to members of the alpine region, either to invest in joint projects with a european impact, allowing for a joint vision and action on regional problems, or to promote territorial cohesion and good relations between member states. i voted in favour.

‒ balancing work, personal and family life is now an indisputable right in modern societies, contributing to personal well-being and benefiting society at large through a much-desired increase in productivity and birth rates. i support this report, as i believe that further progress is still needed in this area, and i encourage both the european institutions and the member states to integrate these concerns in their policies, with particular attention to gender, age, the status of the family and the new social realities, defending those who are most disadvantaged or even excluded from existing legislation and policies. we need to combat discrimination in the workplace, regulate parental leave fairly, combat stress in managing work and personal life, support women in their empowerment in working life, recognise the work of people who devote their time to caring for others and recognise the role of professionally active grandparents. a just and humanistic society does not tolerate the piecemeal and charitable treatment of a recognized fundamental right to balance work, personal and family life.
in writing. ‒ women are increasingly more qualified, even outperforming men in terms of academic qualifications, although they are still underrepresented on the labour market or working in jobs below their skill level. on the other hand, widespread low wages, greater concentration in part-time work and longer career breaks for caring for others (children and/or dependent family members) contribute to a higher risk of poverty and social exclusion for women, as well as to a large gender gap (40%) in pensions. i therefore agree with the need to modernise the framework for work-life balance at union level.
‒ the increasing deregulation of the organization and of industrial relations, which is an integral part of neoliberal policies and, in particular, of the so-called austerity policies (the latter being a concentrated expression of the former), has a strongly disruptive effect on the balance between professional life and private and family life. this balance is a fundamental right and is linked to a number of issues, such as the aforementioned regulation of work, gender equality, active ageing and parental rights. the report proposes measures which we can support. examples include criticism of the prospect that more and longer working hours are beneficial to the economy in terms of increased productivity, or even criticism of the effects of 'austerity' policies, or even reference to collective bargaining and important positions agreed within the ilo. however, this report is entirely in line with eu policies and its neoliberal orientation. see the reference to the need for flexibility in working relationships and working hours, or the promotion of 'smart jobs' and teleworking as a way of promoting better work-life balance. this is an approach which is not essential and which we do not follow, because it does not contribute to solving the problem, but rather the opposite.
‒ the report highlights important measures on labour market conditions favourable to work-life balance, such as: the importance of a coherent policy framework supported by collective bargaining and collective agreements to allow for a better work-life balance; the importance of 'adequately' paid parental leave which is more balanced for both parents; the importance of having access to affordable, adequate and quality early childhood education and care, dependent care and high quality social services; the recognition that work-life balance policies will not in themselves produce benefits for workers unless accompanied by policies to improve living conditions, alongside policies to promote and promote cultural, recreational and sporting activities, among others. even if i take into account that much work still needs to be done in the field of social inequalities and the living conditions of workers, for the reasons i have outlined above, i voted in favour.

the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling of foodstuffs. mr president, this economic partnership agreement with the six southern african countries of the cadc community has come a long way, but the result is overall positive and deserves the support of this parliament, as the committee on development has concluded in the opinion for which i am rapporteur. firstly, this agreement is necessary to comply with the rules of the world trade organisation. without it, african countries would be less protected in their trade with europe. secondly, it is an agreement which seeks to be fair and is therefore asymmetrical and gradual: the european union is committed to the protection of the most sensitive sectors of the economy of developing countries, including safeguards for industry, agricultural markets and food security. thirdly, this agreement has a sustainable development chapter with clear commitments on labour rights and environmental rights. not everything is perfect, of course, but i think we can say that the end result is, in fact, positive. the challenge now is in good implementation and effective monitoring, and this will only exist with the effective involvement of civil society. we welcome the commitments made here by the commissioner, but this parliament expects more than words and will not fail to monitor this process itself and ensure that this agreement is properly implemented, in the interests of our partner countries in africa but also in the interests of the values of the european union's trade agenda.
mr president, i also greet the commissioner. in a recent report, the iucn said that with an 80 percent decline in the last few generations, four of the six great apes are one step closer to extinction. with the accelerated loss of biodiversity that has been witnessed in recent decades, more rigorous and consequential action is needed. in the heart of europe there are deplorable cases of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, the notorious iuu fishing. the cases of sturgeon and eel, specifically glass eel, are striking. when we distribute yellow and red cards all over the world, we do not prevent, to our embarrassment, iuu fishing from spreading in the european union. the new european wildlife trafficking action plan is important and must be implemented in all its objectives. cites needs to be strengthened and cases of corruption and illegal trafficking must be dealt with.
mr president, europe must remain a means whereby european citizens can keep control of their lives in a globalised world, and for this we need a roadmap with better european solutions. with your speech you have made a remarkable contribution in this direction, and the european parliament supports the adoption of very clear position exactly with this purpose. we would now like the european council to deliver at the upcoming bratislava summit, but let me tell you that, at the heart of this roadmap, we should have a strong social pillar, making sure that all european citizens can count on a common set of social standards on working conditions and social protection. this social pillar should entail powerful instruments to deliver on the social standards. we believe that the european union must become, again, an engine for upward economic and social convergence and, as the law has delivered on cohesion policies, i believe that you should also deliver on completing the economic and monetary union.

in writing. ‒ switzerland, like the eu member states, benefits from the internal market and its enlargements, as highlighted in switzerland's analysis of the consequences of terminating the bilateral agreements. there is no doubt that both croatia and switzerland will benefit from the signing of this protocol iii, which will bring them political, economic and cultural advantages, thanks to a wider internal market with free movement as a fundamental element. i voted yes.
‒ the negotiation of the initial eu-switzerland agreement on the free movement of persons, signed in 2000, was supported by us for several reasons, including the fact that more than 100,000 portuguese migrants work in switzerland, including many thousands of seasonal workers. the inclusion of croatia in this agreement, which provides for a 7-year period during which each country (switzerland and croatia) can mutually restrict the movement of people and goods, is only a consequence of the country's accession to the eu. this does not alter our initial approval of this agreement, which was based on the same arguments of facilitating the fixing of the date, based on questions concerning the rights of workers from other countries and their family members. we voted yes.
‒ this proposal constitutes the legal instrument necessary for the conclusion of a protocol to the agreement on the free movement of persons between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the swiss confederation, of the other part, to take account of the accession of the republic of croatia to the european union. the proposed protocol incorporates the republic of croatia as a contracting party to the agreement and provides that the european union shall provide the authentic version of the agreement in the new official language of the eu. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ switzerland is the eu's most important partner, given its geographical and cultural proximity, and especially its political and economic importance. after switzerland's refusal to accede to the eea agreement, and in mutual recognition of the vital importance of cooperation, a number of bilateral agreements were negotiated, covering the free movement of persons, land and air transport, agriculture and research, as well as technical barriers to trade and public procurement. this protocol to the agreement on the free movement of persons provides that, for a period of seven years from the entry into force of the protocol, switzerland may restrict access to the labour market for croatian citizens (quotas, priority for local workers, control of working conditions and wages). during the last two years of this transitional period, restrictions shall be approved by the eu-switzerland joint committee. i believe that the eu, like switzerland, benefits from the internal market and its enlargements, and that both croatia and switzerland will benefit from the signing of this protocol iii, which will bring them political, economic and cultural advantages thanks to a wider internal market with free movement as a fundamental element.
‒ the european union and switzerland are important partners and have close ties through a large number of agreements. the agreement on the free movement of persons concluded under the first bilateral agreements gave the citizens of the contracting parties the right to enter, reside and take up employment in their respective territories by mutually abolishing most restrictions. the accession of croatia to the eu in 2013 led to the conclusion of protocol iii, with a view to extending the agreement on free movement. however, the process was blocked due to the "anti-mass emigration" referendum in february 2014. on 4 march 2016, protocol iii was finally signed, providing for rules allowing switzerland to set limits on access to the labour market for croatian citizens. i believe that both croatia and switzerland will benefit from the signing of this protocol iii, which will bring them political, economic and cultural advantages, thanks to a wider internal market with free movement as a fundamental element. i therefore vote in favour of this report.
‒ i voted in favour, as i consider this to be another positive step in the process of european integration. this protocol allows, within the time limits set, to deepen the spirit of union and cohesion among the peoples of europe, particularly between croatia and switzerland. switzerland will maintain progressive annual quotas so that it can gradually open its labour market to croatian workers. croatia should be entitled to introduce the same quantitative limits for swiss nationals during the same periods.
‒ simply review the protocol on the free movement of persons with switzerland, taking into account the accession of croatia. it is envisaged that for a period of seven years switzerland may restrict access to the labour market for croatian citizens (quotas, priority for local workers, control of working conditions and wages).
‒ the agreement on the free movement of persons between switzerland and the european union was signed in 2000 and entered into force in 2002. subsequently, in april 2006, this agreement was extended to the 10 new member states in accordance with protocol i to the agreement. following the accession of bulgaria and romania in 2007, the agreement was corrected once again, with the so-called protocol ii coming into force. with the recent accession of croatia in 2013, discussions on what has now been referred to as protocol iii have been initiated. finally, and after some procedural issues were overcome, the two parties signed in march 2016 the now-named protocol iii, thus extending the agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. as this is a very technical procedure following the accession of a new member state to the european union, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ the negotiation of the initial agreement, signed in 2000, was supported by us, because of the particular interest of the fact that more than one hundred thousand portuguese emigrants work in switzerland, including many thousands of seasonal workers. the inclusion of croatia, with a seven-year period during which each country can restrict the movement of people and goods, is only a consequence of its entry into the eu. this does not alter our initial approval of this agreement, on the same grounds of facilitating the fixing of the rights of workers from other countries and their families.
‒ the tripartite social summit for growth and employment (tse), established by council decision 2003/174/ec, has formalised the practice of holding informal high-level meetings since 1997 in the framework of the european employment strategy and subsequently the lisbon strategy. following the institutional changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon, the 2003 council decision establishing the tripartite social summit needed to be revised. the treaty of lisbon has brought about significant institutional changes which justify the revision of the decision, in particular: - institutionalised the european council and created the post of president of the european council; - recognised the role of the cst as an integral part of the eu social dialogue; - repealed article 202 of the ec treaty, which was the legal basis for adopting the 2003 decision (the council's tasks are now defined by article 16 of the eu treaty and the principles on comitology are set out in articles 290 and 291 tfeu). i voted in favour of this recommendation, which adapts the institutional changes introduced by the lisbon treaty and also revises the political framework, replacing the lisbon strategy with the europe 2020 strategy.
‒ the commission does not intend at this stage to use the opportunity provided by this review to carry out a thorough reform of the functioning of the tripartite social summit. the summit has always been regarded by the social partners as a privileged forum for discussing social and employment issues at the highest level. it also provides an opportunity for the representatives of the eu institutions participating in the csf to hear the views and proposals from both sides of the social dialogue spectrum, which enables them to subsequently convey these views to the members of the european council. i agree with a proposal to adapt the existing decision to the institutional changes introduced by the lisbon treaty, while reflecting the positive results of the practical experience recently gained in the context of the cst.
‒ the participation of workers in all decisions affecting them, in the sense of defending their class interests, obviously deserves our support. despite our well-known reservations about the nature and scope of an instrument such as the tripartite social summit (jointly chaired by the european council, the council of the european union, the european commission, 10 representatives of employers and 10 representatives of workers), in the context in which its launch and implementation were considered, it has also merited our positive attention. as a consequence of the treaty of lisbon, the composition of the summit was changed. we are not opposed to the recommendation and we agree with it, provided that there is no change in the level of representation of workers and their relative weight.
‒ the tripartite summit for growth and employment is responsible for ensuring, in accordance with the treaty and with due regard for the powers of the union institutions and bodies, that there is permanent consultation between the council, the commission and the social partners. it will allow the social partners at european level to contribute, in the context of social dialogue, to the different components of the eu's strategy for growth and jobs. to this end, it takes account of the work and discussions between the council, the commission and the social partners, which take place upstream in the various conciliation bodies on economic, social and employment issues. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the tripartite social summit for growth and jobs was set up following the lisbon european council in march 2000 with the aim of promoting high-level consultation with the european social partners. since its establishment under council decision 2003/174/ec, the summit has fulfilled its key role of ensuring high-level consultation. it has contributed positively to the development of social dialogue at union level, in the framework of the lisbon strategy over the period 2000-2010 as well as in the framework of the europe 2020 strategy. the tasks and composition of the summit should be adapted to take account of the institutional changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon, in particular the creation of the office of president of the european council as provided for in article 15 teu.

in writing. ‒ the ep gave its opinion and support on 15 april 2014 at first reading for a uniform application of the common technical requirements for inland waterway vessels in the european union, with the aim of ensuring a high level of safety and efficiency in inland navigation. parliament and the council agreed to provide a harmonised and coherent framework in order to ensure the same level of safety for inland waterway vessels. both institutions agree to streamline the use of resources to develop technical standards and to adapt them to scientific and technical progress, using standards developed by international organisations, in particular cesni. this recommendation concerns the text resulting from the negotiations between parliament and the council and was adopted by the tran committee in april 2016. this recommendation deserves my vote in favour.
‒ the revision of directive 2006/87/ec aims to establish a uniform application of the common technical requirements for inland navigation in the european union, ensuring a high level of efficiency and safety in this area. the current revision also aims at streamlining the use of resources by adapting the directive to technical and scientific progress and by respecting the standards developed by international organisations such as cesni (european committee for the development of inland navigation standards). i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution for two reasons, among others: firstly, because, from the substantive or, if you like, the material point of view, i am in favour of the creation of a harmonized, coherent and up-to-date technical framework on the subject under discussion; i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this matter, but that it should be involved in the matter of the european parliament, which is of great importance to me, and that is no less important because, from a legislative or perhaps adjectival procedural point of view, i consider the involvement of the european parliament in this matter to be of the utmost importance.

‒ the economic partnership agreement between the eu and six southern african development community (sadc) countries, including mozambique, provides for gradual market opening measures, allowing these countries to liberalise 86% of their trade with the eu (74% in the case of mozambique) over a period of 10 years, excluding sensitive agricultural and fishery products. this regional trade agreement currently covers only trade in goods, development cooperation and provisions on trade and sustainable development. it does, however, leave the door open to negotiating new provisions on services, investment, intellectual property rights, public procurement and strengthened provisions on sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ we are facing the culmination for the countries of southern africa of a long process of blackmail. a process in which the european union did everything to impose on the states of the region, against their will and despite their resistance, free trade agreements, which it called 'economic partnership agreements' (epas). the eu's choice is a clear indication of its neo-colonialist intentions and is based on an alleged (false) obligation under the cotonou agreement. the aim of the epas was to go beyond what has been achieved in the wto in terms of trade liberalisation and deregulation. a whole arsenal of pressure was used to this end, including the use of the european development fund, as well as outright blackmail. it is noted that some countries have resisted blackmail (angola). all in the interests of the big european economic and financial groups: opening up markets, selling goods and services, exploiting raw materials and imposing an export-oriented production model, helping to bring down wages, rights and living conditions for workers. we obviously voted against it. this is not a vote against 'trade', but a vote for a different policy, one that promotes effective independence, sovereignty, cooperation, solidarity, development and social justice.
‒ this proposal implements the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, of the one part, and the european community and its member states, of the other part, signed in cotonou on 23 june 2000 ('acp-ec partnership agreement'), which calls for the conclusion of economic partnership agreements compatible with the wto. the agreement contains provisions on cooperation, trade in goods, trade and sustainable development, customs and trade facilitation, technical barriers to trade, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, dispute settlement, geographical indications and rules of origin. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the economic partnership agreements, which establish trade and development partnerships between the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) states, on the one hand, and the european union, on the other, aim to promote trade, regional integration and the progressive integration of the acp states into the world economy, as well as the sustainable development of these states. in 2014, the union concluded negotiations on an epa in the area of trade in goods with six of the 15 countries of the southern african development community (sadc): botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, swaziland and south africa. the sadc-eu economic partnership agreement has the potential to trigger fundamental positive change, contribute to sustainable economic growth and deepen intra-regional trade and integration. i agree with the rapporteur's position on the guarantees and flexibility mechanisms provided for in the agreement, particularly in the area of trade and sustainable development, which can help make the agreement mutually beneficial and development-friendly, ensuring policy coherence for development, provided that it is properly implemented and monitored.
‒ over the past 14 years, the european commission has been negotiating economic partnership agreements (epas) with several african countries, with the aim of moving towards reciprocal trade preferences. one of the fruits of the above-mentioned negotiations is the understanding reached by six countries of the southern african development community (sadc), also referred to as the sadc epa group, in 2014. the agreement led to the conclusion of an epa, which would highlight the objective of eradicating poverty through the establishment of trade partnerships, promoting regional integration, investment and the gradual integration of sadc countries into the global economy. the negotiated agreement presupposes access to markets of asymmetrical size, so as to better respect the interests of each of the countries involved, and makes a reference to respect for human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law. i therefore voted in favour of this regional agreement, which is aimed at promoting good trade relations with africa, a continent which today, more than ever, plays a major role in the world geopolitical and economic context.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, the union concluded negotiations on an epa (economic partnership agreement) on trade in goods with six of the 15 countries of the southern african development community: botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, swaziland and south africa. the rapporteur recommends that the sadc-eu economic partnership agreement be approved. this epa has the potential to trigger fundamental positive change, contribute to sustainable economic growth and deepen intra-regional trade and integration. however, the trade and partnership agreement can only be a small part of a wider strategy. the sadc states should implement trade and development-friendly national policies and carry out structural reforms. another element to consider is a regulatory framework that attracts investment. these countries should also consider the possibility of using the potential of the epa, going beyond trade in goods and including services in the future. the eu should provide support for capacity building and trade assistance, and parliament should monitor implementation and raise issues where necessary. appropriate control structures should be put in place to maximise the impact of the agreement. i voted in favour of this recommendation.
‒ the asymmetric nature of the agreement establishes positive discrimination in favour of sadc epa partners, ensuring duty-free access to the eu market, while at the same time mutually eliminating barriers to almost all trade, ensuring wto compatibility and promoting regional integration, economic cooperation and good governance. this agreement has the potential to trigger fundamental positive change, contribute to sustainable economic growth and deepen intra-regional trade and integration.
in writing. - i am in favour of the proposal for a recommendation on the economic partnership agreement between the european union (eu) and six countries of the southern african development community (sadc): botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, south africa and swaziland. one of the main objectives of the agreement is to liberalise 86% of these countries' trade with the eu over a period of 10 years. this regional agreement will cover trade in goods, development cooperation and certain trade-related matters relating to sustainable development. agricultural products and fisheries products, which are more sensitive, are excluded from the agreement, although the possibility of negotiating a broader scope for the agreement, which could include aspects related to services, investments, intellectual property rights and public procurement, among others, remains open. the union is the largest regional trading partner of these countries, guaranteeing them, under this agreement, access to the european market, free of quotas and customs duties, and i therefore believe that there is every interest in deepening trade relations with these countries, of which mozambique is a member. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of this agreement because i am convinced of its relevance to the economies and populations of the southern african countries which are part of it and which have agreed to it. i understand that's the best deal possible right now. however, it is essential to invest in ways of printing a logic of sustainable social, environmental and economic growth, which has the right follow-up and monitoring measures. in the agricultural sector, it is essential that sanitary control measures are sufficient and effective to prevent the spread of diseases. it is also important to ensure that the agreed quotas do not represent an increased risk of imbalance in the internal market with serious consequences for prices and the outflow of european production.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the economic partnership agreement with six southern african countries, including mozambique, because it is a development-oriented agreement. the trade agreement is reciprocal and therefore compatible with the rules of the world trade organisation, but is asymmetrical and gradual in nature. the southern african countries can protect their sensitive sectors from european competitors and the agreement also includes a number of safeguards for the domestic industries, agricultural markets and food safety of these partner countries. the agreement includes relatively flexible rules of origin and there is also a chapter devoted to sustainable development with commitments in the field of labour and environmental legislation. as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on development, i have advocated effective monitoring of the agreement, with the involvement of civil society, as well as the mobilisation of adequate resources to strengthen technical capacity and cover some of the adaptation costs that an economic transition such as this will entail. in short, provided that the agreement is properly implemented and monitored, the guarantees and flexibility mechanisms provided for in the agreement should contribute to sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ currently, all states that have not concluded an epa benefit from the eu's system of generalised preferences (gsp) or the everything but arms (eat) initiative. however, for countries that concluded an interim epa in 2007, in order to avoid market disruption and to allow sufficient time to sign and ratify the agreement, the eu adopted a market access regulation (mar), council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007, as of 1 january 2008, which allowed for the early application of epas. it was subsequently decided that the ram [free access to the eu] treatment would end on 1 october 2014 for countries that had not concluded a regional agreement or had not taken the necessary measures to implement their provisional epas. the eu is seeking trade liberalisation, from which its major financial and economic groups seek to secure open markets, sell goods and services, exploit raw materials and impose an export-oriented production model in their own interests. we need a different policy that promotes effective independence, sovereignty, cooperation, solidarity, development and social justice. i therefore vote against.
‒ fisheries workers need special protection, taking into account, among other things, the special characteristics of work on board fishing vessels. the high rate of fatal and non-fatal accidents, the risks and incidence of occupational diseases compared to other sectors in a hazardous work environment, the unclear distinction between working, resting and leisure time and the impact on health and safety of fatigue, partly resulting from insufficient rest, as well as the prevalence of informal and atypical employment relationships and pay arrangements, including profit-sharing schemes between crew, are issues taken into account. the agreement, which i voted for, applies to all fishermen employed on board a fishing vessel registered in a member state or flying its flag and engaged in commercial fishing operations.
‒ this resolution concerns ilo convention no 188 on work in the fisheries sector. this convention, adopted in 2007, provides for a set of amendments aimed at contributing to the improvement of the conditions of workers on board, taking into account the very high accident rates in this context. the following measures are particularly important: - responsibility of owners and masters of fishing vessels for the health and safety of workers;- definition of a minimum working age and protection of young workers;- mandatory certified medical examinations;- obligation to have rest periods;- regular payment to fishermen and permission to make transfers for family members;- standards for accommodation and food;- definition of safety and health standards and provision of medical care on board;- discounts for social security;- social protection in case of illness, injury and death. taken together, the provisions of the recommendation, although of limited application, could help to solve long-standing problems in the sector. unfortunately, in the eu context, only france and estonia have signed this convention. the resolution calls for a general support, which is why we voted in favour.
‒ the purpose of this proposal is to implement the agreement on the implementation of the international labour organisation (ilo) fisheries labour convention, 2007, concluded between cogeca, etf and europêche. the commission's proposal aims to improve the living and working conditions of fishermen working on board vessels flying the flag of an eu member state by establishing a consolidated legal framework appropriate to working conditions in the maritime fisheries sector. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ given the high rate of fatal and non-fatal accidents, the risks and incidence of occupational diseases, the hazardous working environment and the impact on health and safety of fatigue resulting from insufficient rest, as well as the existence of informal and atypical employment relationships and pay arrangements, i believe that fisheries workers need special protection, taking into account the special characteristics of work on board fishing vessels. to date, only eight countries have ratified the ilo fisheries labour convention, of which only two eu member states (france and estonia) have done so, despite the council's decision to allow eu member states to ratify the ilo fisheries labour convention. i believe it is important that the eu and its member states ensure a leading role in promoting decent working conditions and pay in the fisheries sector. i am voting in favour of this recommendation, as i am in favour of creating a fair and equitable environment in the fisheries sector, including the fight against exploitation of fishermen, such as forced labour, trafficking and child labour.
‒ today, professional fishermen lack adequate protection in view of the special characteristics of work on board fishing vessels. the high number of fatal and non-fatal accidents and the susceptibility to occupational diseases are factors which give this type of work a considerable degree of risk. the unclear distinction between working, resting and leisure time, informal and atypical pay patterns, and the impact on the health and safety of professional fishermen thus justify a revision of the ilo fisheries labour convention's standards and hermeneutics. the convention sets out guidelines for creating decent conditions for this profession. i believe that incorporating these rules into the legal order of the european union will strengthen the creation of fair and equal conditions in the fisheries sector. in this context too, i would stress the importance of strengthening the provisions on wages, social protection and social security, with the aim of guaranteeing adequate and decent income for workers and their families. i therefore take note of the foregoing and vote in favour.
‒ i voted in favour, considering it imperative that fisheries workers enjoy special protection, taking into account, inter alia, the special characteristics of work on board fishing vessels, the high rate of fatal and non-fatal accidents, the risks and incidence of occupational diseases compared to other sectors in a hazardous working environment, the unclear distinction between working, rest and leisure time and the impact on health and safety of fatigue resulting in part from insufficient rest, as well as the prevalence of informal and atypical employment relationships and wage arrangements, including profit-sharing systems amongst crew.
‒ this proposal for a council directive aims to implement the agreement between the general confederation of agricultural cooperatives of the european union (cogeca), the european transport workers' federation (etf) and the association of national fisheries organisation (europeche) on the implementation of the international labour organisation (ilo) fisheries labour convention, 2007, which was concluded in may 2012 (and amended in may 2013). workers in the fisheries sector need special protection, given the specific characteristics of their work and considering the high risks involved in their professional practice compared to other sectors. unfortunately, this ilo convention had been ratified by only 8 countries (2 member states: france and estonia). in this resolution i would like to stress the need to deepen the provisions on wages and social protection, in particular in the event of injury, accident or death, and the importance of establishing mechanisms for the implementation of this agreement, including the development of appropriate enforcement measures and inspections. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the eu should play a leading role in promoting decent working conditions and pay in the fisheries sector.
‒ this resolution concerns ilo convention no 188 on work in the fisheries sector. this convention, adopted in 2007, provides for a set of amendments aimed at contributing to the improvement of the conditions of workers on board, taking into account the very high accident rates in this context. in the eu context, only france and estonia have signed this convention. we support it.
in writing. ‒ it is essential that all eu member states can share basic principles such as respect for the rule of law and a clear understanding of the separation of powers within each state. when one of the countries that are part of the european union calls these principles into question, it is important that the european union as a whole takes a stand. this resolution seeks to draw the attention of the polish government and, above all, to help resolve a situation which has served to sharpen the positions between the european commission and the polish government. as i consider that respect for the rule of law and the separation of powers are fundamental guarantees of a modern democratic state, and as i consider that this resolution is a clear attempt to protect these values in poland, i shall vote in favour of it. i hope that this sign will make the polish government realize that it is essential to implement the commission's recommendations.
‒ this is not the first time that parliament has spoken out about the situation in poland. since the current government took office, we have seen the degradation of the rule of law in this member state. it is clear that with each new election a change in state policies is possible and even likely. however, what is clearly happening is a change in the very nature of the state, which cannot be tolerated. we cannot tolerate the violation of freedom of the press, we cannot tolerate the violation of the right to privacy and the unprecedented restriction of freedom, we cannot tolerate the independence of the judiciary being called into question and we cannot tolerate the violation of women's rights. all this is at stake in poland. it is clear that we need a constructive approach and the union must promote a productive dialogue with the national authorities. but it is clear that the house of european citizens, including the polish people, cannot remain indifferent and has a duty to exercise its powers in defence of our common values.
‒ the polish government should cooperate with the european commission and reach a compromise with the other polish parties to resolve the constitutional crisis that is endangering democracy, fundamental rights and the rule of law in the country. recent events in poland, such as the paralysis of the constitutional tribunal (tc), threaten democracy, fundamental rights and the rule of law in the country. issues relating to women's rights are also a cause for concern. i welcome the european commission's determination to pursue a constructive and productive dialogue with the polish government with a view to finding rapid and concrete solutions to the systemic threats to the rule of law.

in writing. - this report on the european union's relations with tunisia deserves my vote in favour, because, as i have argued in this parliament, this was the country where the arab spring began and is so far the only successful example of this historic event. the consolidation of tunisian democracy is fundamental to the stabilization of the whole region and this report is careful to emphasize the need for strong support from the european union. i consider it extremely important to consolidate democracy in tunisia, taking into account respect for human rights and also taking care to involve civil society organisations, and its inclusion in this report also contributed to my vote in favour.
‒ tunisia is a key partner of the european union in the european neighbourhood policy, but also in the fight against terrorism, in resolving the refugee crisis and in stabilising the region, especially with regard to libya. i would remind you that there are over a million displaced libyans in tunisia who are without access to basic infrastructure, because they are mostly in former refugee camps. i am also concerned about the fragile state of the tunisian economy, which is heavily dependent on tourism and foreign investment, as the high level of unemployment is exploited by radical organisations such as the islamic state to recruit young people. any approach to eu-tunisia relations must take this reality into account. i agree with the priorities set out in the report, but i particularly follow the recommendations to abolish the death penalty, to eradicate the practice of torture of detained citizens, to decriminalise homosexuality, to respect freedom of expression and the press, to conclude a free trade agreement with a programme of macro-financial assistance, to promote public administration reforms and to combat corruption, to strengthen cooperation in the field of security and to give priority to programmes to support youth and youth employment. i therefore support the report.

‒ europe was defined by its founders as a democratic space with good economic performance and a high level of social protection. priority was given to building and strengthening the internal market, but no such harmonisation exists as regards social rights. there is in fact an asymmetry between the reality of an internal market which is practically complete and very heterogeneous social rights. this paradox calls into question the very principle of fair competition between undertakings and the promotion of a social market economy by the union. this situation of unfair economic and social competition also represents an obstacle to the maintenance of a high level of social protection in europe. i support this report, which argues for the need to increase controls and inspections, both at national and european level, in application of existing legislation. i am in favour of creating a single digital document containing the social rights of all european workers. i would stress the need to revise the posting of workers directive in order to make way for the amendment of its current legal basis, as well as the regulations on the coordination of social security systems.
in writing. ‒ social rights in the eu have not been harmonised and, with the exception of certain principles enshrined in the treaty and in some directives, it was agreed that member states would remain competent in social matters. there is in fact an asymmetry between the reality of an internal market which is practically complete and very heterogeneous social rights. these situations of unfair economic and social competition also represent an obstacle to the maintenance of a high level of social protection in europe. i therefore support the proposals contained in this report.
‒ this report addresses the problem of 'social dumping' in the eu, in a logic of combating the phenomenon, the relevance of which is unquestionable, in particular in the light of the so-called austerity policies, which have promoted precarious employment, unemployment, the increase of poverty and exclusion and the reduction of labour and civil rights. the report emphasises the need to strengthen inspection, including cross-border cooperation, as a way of combating 'social dumping'. it advocates strengthening resources and manpower, alongside strengthening collective hiring and negotiation, the recovery of social rights and incomes, the promotion of work with rights, and the limitation of the posting of workers, among other measures. the report contains positive aspects, contrary to the existence of 'dumping'. but it also has negative aspects: concerns about the single market for people and goods, its promotion and defence. provisions which go against what was required in this context. there is no good in the single market is at the heart of the policies that have led to the dumping of companies in the eu and the disfigurement of work as a structuring factor in the development of states. these inconsistencies of principle and contradictions justify our abstention. it would be desirable for the report to make a clear break with the causes of social dumping in the eu.
‒ this report, although there is still a long way to go, is presented as a first step in the fight against social dumping. the report contains very positive aspects, such as the need to strengthen inspection, also at the level of crossborder cooperation, as a way of combating 'social dumping', and also the promotion of working conditions, measures to support women affected by social dumping and urgent measures in the transport sector, which are often real areas of social non-justice. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
‒ undeclared work and false self-employment can cause distortions of competition, resulting in long-term damage to social security systems, in the increase of precarious work and in the deterioration of levels of protection of workers and the quality of employment in general, and must therefore be combated. it is crucial to ensure fair and fair conditions of competition throughout the eu and to eliminate social dumping. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the question of social dumping is too often raised without a legal basis, leading to inconsistencies in the achievement of the internal market. as far as transport is concerned, we need legal clarity for carriers and a simplification of the existing regulatory framework. the fault lies not in cabotage operations but in the lack of effective control by the competent authorities and in the differences in the application of certain provisions, such as the prohibition of regular weekly rest on board vehicles in belgium and france. to do this, we need to review the establishment requirements, avoiding the transfer of activity to other member states for the purpose of deliberately avoiding taxation and labour taxation. we need more clarity in the application of existing provisions, in particular in the regulations on cabotage and access to the profession.
‒ although it is one of the most ambitious sets of legislation on social rights, the european legal order does not exhaust the range of competences in this area and should, moreover, be supported by the legal systems of the member states. the discrepancy in the exercise of the member states' powers in the area of the establishment and protection of social rights leads, however, to an asymmetry in the european project, which, despite having an internal market which is practically complete, presents a heterogeneous catalogue of social rights. it is well known that this distinction contributes to the distortion of the principle of competition between undertakings and to the promotion of a social market economy, by creating incentives to reduce labour costs and thus weakening the social standards in force in the union. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of hiv/aids, and for the eu to support the fight against aids. i am therefore voting in favour of this report, which seeks to correct the asymmetry between economic freedoms and social rights.
‒ given that europe has been defined as a democratic area with good economic performance and a high level of social protection, this report stresses that greater priority has been given to building and strengthening the internal market. the rapporteur stresses that social rights have not been subject to such harmonisation and that it was agreed that the member states would remain competent in social matters. it also notes a paradox which encourages competition between firms, even though european workers do not have the same social rights and obligations, and stresses the political repercussions of this asymmetry between economic freedoms and social rights. the report also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the european parliament is given the opportunity to express its views on the proposals for directives and to make proposals for the adoption of the relevant directives. the report also calls for the creation of a social protocol guaranteeing the primacy of social rights over economic freedoms and recommends setting minimum wage limits. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ in the eu, social rights have not yet been harmonised and it has been agreed that member states would remain competent in social matters. there is an asymmetry between the reality of an almost completed internal market and very heterogeneous social rights. this paradox encourages competition between companies, even though european workers do not have the same social rights and obligations. several measures can close the legislative and regulatory gaps that favour 'social dumping': increased controls and inspections, both at national and european level, in application of existing legislation (human and financial means must be strengthened); the creation of a single digital document containing the social rights of all european workers; the fight against 'shell companies', in particular by imposing new obligations on official addresses; the creation of a european list of companies that have committed serious infringements, such as the use of undeclared work; the adoption of urgent measures in the transport sector, which are often true zones of social non-law; the creation of a social protocol guaranteeing the primacy of social rights over economic freedoms and the setting of minimum wage limits.
‒ this report draws attention to the dichotomy between what is meant by 'economic freedoms' and what is meant by 'social rights', and warns that this often leads to abusive practices, unfair social competition and the subversion of the social market economy, with the consequent encouragement of protectionism by member states and unilateral decision-making in the social field. however, it is certain that there is already a greater awareness and concern on the part of the european authorities regarding this problem, namely the fight against so-called 'social dumping'. in this respect, i am in favour of the need to close down some legislative and regulatory loopholes that may lead to the promotion of unfair competition within the internal market, as well as the revision of the directive on the posting of workers and the regulations on the coordination of social security systems. despite the controversy surrounding some of the proposals for the harmonization of social policies at european level and the introduction of stabilizing mechanisms, compromise solutions were found between the various political groups to achieve a balanced report, which i voted in favour of.
‒ this report aims to combat 'social dumping' in the eu. this phenomenon is relevant, particularly in the face of austerity policies, which have promoted job insecurity, unemployment, increased poverty and exclusion, which facilitates the reduction of labour and civil rights. the report emphasises the need to strengthen inspection, including cross-border cooperation, as a way of combating 'social dumping'. combining this increase in resources and staff with the reference to the strengthening of recruitment and collective bargaining, the recovery of social rights (including income security) and the promotion of work with rights and the limitation of the posting of workers, it is understood that the report has many positive points, contrary to the existence of dumping. concerns about the 'truth' of the single market for people and goods, in the interests of defending and promoting it, go, however, in the opposite direction to what was required in this context. there is no goodness in the single market. this inconsistency of principles justifies abstention in this document, which would be desirable if it affirmed a break with the causes of social dumping in the eu context.
‒ i voted in favour of the balas report because i think it is essential that the european parliament has a stronger voice in building a fairer europe so that all european workers can be covered by the same levels of social protection. despite some attempts to undermine this report, i would stress the action of the european socialist group which has managed to include the need to ensure fair and fair conditions of competition throughout the eu in order to eliminate social dumping. in this context, i would highlight the definition of social dumping in the report which, while acknowledging the lack of a legally recognised and universally accepted definition of social dumping, notes that the concept covers a wide range of intentional abusive practices which allow the development of unfair competition by illegally minimising labour and operating costs and generate violations of workers' rights and exploitation. i would also stress the call on the european commission to make a recommendation to the 28 member states that have ratified ilo convention 81 on labour inspection to ensure that labour standards are respected and workers are protected, including provisions on working time, safety and health.
in writing. ‒ it is essential that consumer information on investment products is comparable, so as to promote a level playing field in the market, irrespective of the type of financial intermediary designing or marketing them. the treatment of products offering multiple options itself still needs to be clarified. the lack of detailed guidance in the delegated regulation on the 'understanding warning' creates a serious risk of inconsistent application of this element in the key information document across the single market. i therefore have some doubts about the regulation that has been produced.
in the case of retail investment products, the retail investor protection scheme (rpp) is a specific type of protection scheme that is intended to protect the interests of retail investors. the european commission's proposal to impose more regulation on the priip sector emerged, albeit belatedly, as a response to the financial crisis. the proposed reforms are designed to protect retail investors in the financial sector who sell inappropriate and high-risk products without providing appropriate information beforehand. the key information document (kid) is a standardised information document that should inform potential investors about the potential risks, costs and future performance scenarios of the associated products. the objection arises from the fact that the delegated act adopted by the european commission contains errors in the method of calculating the future performance scenarios. in particular, it does not show, for some packages of retail investment products and insurance-based investment products, that investors may lose money. furthermore, there is a lack of detailed guidance in the delegated regulation on the 'understanding warning'. we voted for the objection.
in writing. ‒ it is essential that consumer information on investment products is comparable, so as to promote a level playing field in the market, irrespective of the type of financial intermediary designing or marketing them. the delegated act adopted by the commission contains errors in the method of calculating future performance scenarios and therefore does not meet the requirement, laid down in regulation (eu) no 1286/2014, to provide information that is 'accurate, correct, clear and not misleading' and, in particular, does not show, for some priips, even in an adverse scenario, and even for products that have regularly caused losses during the recommended minimum holding period, that investors could lose money. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ today, in the course of their business, retail investors are increasingly confronted with the offer of a wide range of packages of retail investment products and insurance-based investment products (priips). some of these products offer specific investment solutions tailored to the needs of retail investors and are often combined with insurance contracts, and can therefore be highly complex and therefore difficult to understand. in addition, information on priips is often provided to retail investors in a disorganised manner. consequently, retail investors often make investments without understanding the risks and costs associated with them, sometimes suffering unforeseen losses. it is necessary that consumer information on investment products is comparable in order to promote fair competition. the document in question is precisely in that direction. therefore, with the aim of strengthening the protection of retail investors and increasing their confidence in priips, i voted in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of the opinion that it is essential that consumer information on investment products is comparable, in order to promote a level playing field in the market, irrespective of the type of financial intermediary designing or marketing them. whereas furthermore the fact that the elimination of credit risk from the calculation of the risk classification of insurance products could mislead investors, such as the treatment of products offering multiple options still needs to be clarified, in particular with regard to the explicit exemption granted to ucits funds under regulation (eu) no 1286/2014;
‒ the single market legislation states that it is essential to provide consumers with the most complete and accurate information possible on packages of retail and insurance-based investment products, allowing for appropriate comparison and healthy and balanced competition in the market, irrespective of the type of financial intermediary that develops or markets them. however, the delegated regulation adopted by the european commission is not fully reliable as regards the method of calculating the future performance scenarios of these products, casting doubt on the accuracy, correctness and clarity of the information provided by it. in this context, and in view of the fact that the delegated regulation may contain unreliable and poorly detailed guidance which jeopardises the consistent application of the key information document and the fact that the rules laid down in the regulation may themselves be contrary to the spirit and purpose of the legislation in this area - which is intended to provide small investors with information on this type of investment products in a clear, rigorous and objective manner - i consider that the conditions for its application are not in place and therefore i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which objects to the entry into force of the delegated regulation.
in writing. ‒ we agree that it is of the utmost importance for investors to have reliable and accurate information and a high degree of transparency. we do not want the notion of transparency to be used to distort the very nature of the crisis. transparency helps and is welcome. but it's not believed that lack of transparency caused the financial crisis. the crisis was caused by the greed of the big institutional investors who had all the information possible, but who still didn't want to give up their profits. the problem was the speculative spiral that was going on with the banks and the other financial institutions, who knew they could take risks, because they knew and they know now that they can always rely on governments and central banks to solve this problem. no matter how much regulation they invent, nothing can erase the need for public oversight of the financial system today.

mr president, commissioner, welcome back to this house for this working session. one of the common mistakes in the construction of policies on a given subject is the tendency to isolate that subject. in the specific case of employment, we have further reasons to deal with the issue in a global way, as it is closely linked to economic development, people's skills, the potential of firms and market needs, among others. for the european guidelines for the employment policies of the member states to be effective, they must be adapted to the realities and common objectives of the union, but also to the specificities of each member state. that is why i believe that they should be linked in a balanced way with the country-specific recommendations arising from the european semester process. i would like to draw attention to the fact that in this year's report on the social and employment aspects of the european semester, for which i was rapporteur, we have introduced a major innovation by increasing its social dimension. we included three employment indicators in the macroeconomic imbalance procedure, namely the activity rate, youth employment and long-term unemployment, and called for in-depth analyses to be carried out on the basis of these indicators, taking into account the proposal and implementation of further reforms in the economic, social and labour market fields. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. if we do not make this link, employment policies are hollow, because they are out of touch with reality.
madam president, we do not deny the need to improve access to finance for smes. we also think that this is a key issue for our economic growth. however, we cannot approach this question without a proper diagnosis. the attempt to solve the lack of sme financing through the capital markets union or the banking union shows that we have learned nothing from the past. all the rhetoric about market fragmentation is only meant to further increase capital mobility and the integration of financial markets, and to further strengthen the institutions that are said to be 'too big to fail'. those who know the reality of smes know that their financing is dependent on a banking sector with a strong national presence and clearly targeted at local and regional investment, and only public control of the financial system can guarantee banking for development.
we do not deny the importance of greater transparency in the securities markets and greater consumer protection. we must not be under the illusion that this document will solve the serious problems of the financial system, in particular its opacity and complexity, and we must not believe that this is the fundamental step towards a capital markets union, which will only strengthen the large financial groups which continue to speculate, always relying on public aid when necessary. to expect that these kits can solve information asymmetry seems to us, to say the least, overly optimistic, when we know that every day new financial products are born with increasing complexity. therefore, aware that the genesis of all these problems stems from the private nature of the financial sector and the principles of maximising shareholder profits that underlie it, we continue to advocate public control of the financial system, thus aligning the priorities of its institutions with the needs of the economies of each country.
mr president, the concept of a minimum income, in the context of a profound economic and social crisis, requires a deeper reflection on its objectives and its implementation, which takes account of the reality of each country. only in this way will it be possible to define a value which will in fact guarantee a minimum of dignity to those who are victims of poverty and long-term unemployment. today it is questionable whether the 60% of median income, thanks to the crushing of workers' wages, fulfills that goal. this concept will not in itself provide an answer to very serious social problems, which cannot be solved by palliatives but by reversing the economic and social policies of the european union and which will be aggravated if its objective is perverted, serving rather to accentuate exploitation by means of the assignment of work conditional on the provision of work, an explicit way of creating cheap labour. the fight against inequalities and poverty will only be possible through economic and social development policies that value wages, work with rights and a balanced distribution of wealth.
mr president, the question of the minimum income cannot be treated lightly. we are debating people's lives, their dignity, and we can do it in a small way or with ambition. to solve the problems of poverty, i advocate for much more than a minimum income. in my country, portugal, we have a social income of insertion, but do not be fooled by the altruism of the expression, because in portugal we have only made a change in the definition, because we have simply allocated a subsidy to people. i am in favour of a much more than an income, i am in favour of a social inclusion programme which, in addition to a minimum income, guarantees the poorest that they can have social aspirations. children from poor families can also be doctors, teachers and lawyers, whatever they want. genuine social mobility requires the articulation of an income with parental support, lifelong learning and child education programmes. we need a mechanism of independence and social accountability.

‒ the creation of a standardised european travel document is essential for the management of migration flows, thus aiming to increase the recognition of the document by third countries, to ensure greater acceptance of returnees by these countries and to reduce red tape and waiting periods in member states. increasing the rate of return of irregular migrants is vital for the integrity of the eu asylum system, for cooperation between eu member states and third countries and for maintaining the trust of eu citizens. a long-term solution is needed to stabilise the current migrant crisis, relieve pressure on member states and eu agencies and strengthen the capacity and resources available in the eu.
‒ the objective of this proposal is to establish a specific european travel document for the return of third-country nationals who are the subject of a return decision, providing for a standard form and enhanced technical and security features that ensure wider acceptance by third countries and increased use of this document for readmission purposes. their use should be promoted in bilateral and eu readmission agreements or other agreements. this proposal follows the announcement of the eu action plan on return to explore ways to improve the recognition of eu free-transit passports by third countries. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ as one of the central actors in the current migration crisis, the european union cannot be satisfied with the current rate of return of illegally staying third-country nationals to their respective states in cases of unsuccessful asylum applications. in order to ensure the integrity of the new union asylum system, as well as cooperation between member states, it is essential to address the difficulties faced by irregular migrants at an early stage. one of these difficulties is that some third countries do not accept return documents issued by member states. this report proposes to harmonize the format and technical specifications of this document - that is, it proposes a european document tout court - always on the assumption of guaranteeing the highest safety standards and safeguarding the risk of counterfeiting and falsification. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that by harmonising the format of the travel document, member states will be able to reduce the bureaucracy, variation, costs and waiting times associated with the return of irregular migrants to their own countries, as well as the recognition of this travel document by third countries.

‒ following the unprecedented wave of migration that has hit the eu in recent years and which is now one of the main priorities on the european agenda, many migrants are not covered by the eu's international protection regime and need to leave the european area. this report concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a european travel document for the return of third-country nationals who are in the eu illegally. the aim is not only to try to stabilise the current migration crisis, but also to relieve the pressure on member states and european agencies, whose capacity and resources are, as we know, limited. it is not a question of trying to respond to a merely temporary situation, since this is a drama that affects the very structure of european migration policy; the aim is rather to promote a harmonisation and substantial reformulation of the format and application of this european travel document, enhancing its recognition by third countries. this regulation will enable the eu to ensure a higher degree of security and reliability of technical standards, in particular in relation to counterfeiting and falsification of these documents. i agree with the rapporteur's suggestions in general and have therefore voted in favour of this report.
