‒ the europe 2020 strategy proposed by the commission should enable the union to steer its economy towards smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, accompanied by a high level of employment, productivity and social cohesion. the eu needs holistic policies and public investment that tackle unemployment and poverty. in this context, the evolution to date of the employment and social indicators of the europe 2020 strategy is of great concern, given that the number of people at risk of poverty and exclusion has increased by 5 million instead of decreasing, the employment rate in some countries has not yet reached the pre-crisis levels and in some member states the proportion of young people not in employment, education or training (neets) is above 20% and the early school leaving rate is as high as 23%. the european employment strategy has a key role to play in delivering the objectives of the new strategy on employment, social inclusion and the labour market. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the problem of unemployment is, of course, one of the european union's main priorities. this report presents a set of guidelines in this area, which aim to highlight the importance of filling gaps which are acknowledged to exist , to raise awareness of social factors related to unemployment, and to promote a fairer labour market. the rapporteur stresses the importance of facilitating and investing in the creation of quality and sustainable jobs, promoting young entrepreneurship and pursuing and promoting policies that guarantee fair wages for all workers. i voted in favour because i believe that by boosting labour demand, increasing the skills of workers, improving the functioning of the labour market and promoting equal opportunities, we will be on the right track towards a europe in which the social market economy contributes to the dignification of the labour market and the eradication of unemployment.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal because i consider it essential that the member states and the union should work towards developing a coordinated strategy on employment and, in particular, to promote a skilled, trained and adaptable workforce and labour markets that respond quickly to economic change. member states, in cooperation with regional and local authorities, should effectively and rapidly address the serious problem of unemployment, facilitate and invest in the creation of quality and sustainable jobs, address the issue of accessibility for groups at risk, reduce the obstacles to companies hiring people at different skill levels and sectors of the labour market, including by reducing red tape while respecting labour and social standards, promote young entrepreneurship and, in particular, foster the creation and growth of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in order to increase the employment rate of men and women. member states should actively promote, inter alia, jobs in the green, white and blue sectors as well as the social economy and foster social innovation.
‒ this report aims to confirm for 2016 the validity of the guidelines for the employment policies of the member states, which were launched in october 2015. unfortunately, many of the concepts used such as 'adaptability' and 'flexibility' involve changes in working relationships and conditions, leading to deterioration of workers' rights. on the other hand, the main solution advocated, entrepreneurship, is encouraged in multiple ways, including as a curricular component in the public education system. there is also the reference to "necessary flexibility in education systems and a practical orientation", revealing an essentially vocational education paradigm and the concept of subordinating educational policies to the needs of enterprises. this report was also based on the logic of the europe 2020 strategy, the european semester and other policies based on supranational interference and the imposition of austerity. our vote was against. the motion for a resolution now before us contains positive considerations as regards the defence of the rights of workers, regardless of their gender or sexual orientation, the strengthening of collective bargaining and the fight against poverty. however, it does not depart from what we voted against in the original document.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the agea report, as i believe that parliament should state its guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. i believe that the eu, in implementing its employment policies, must ensure the creation of an integrated and inclusive labour market that is able to combat the impact of unemployment, to ensure a high level of employment, to ensure decent working conditions throughout the union, including adequate remuneration and adequate levels of social protection, and to combat discrimination on grounds of sex, racial or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. in addition, the eu needs holistic policies and public investments that tackle unemployment and poverty. in this context, the evolution to date of the employment and social indicators of the europe 2020 strategy is of great concern, given that the number of people at risk of poverty and exclusion has increased by 5 million instead of decreasing and the employment rate in some countries has not yet reached the levels recorded before the crisis.
in writing. ‒ cites, with 181 parties, including the eu and its 28 member states, is the largest existing wildlife conservation agreement in the world and according to the red list of threatened species drawn up by the international union for the conservation of nature and natural resources (iucn), more than 23 000 species, representing about 30% of the 79 837 species assessed by the iucn, are at risk of extinction. eu member states declared the import of almost 117 000 specimens of wild species as hunting trophies, these being species listed in the cites annexes for a period of ten years. i support the eu's accession to cites because it is a key step in ensuring that the eu can achieve the wider objectives of its environmental policies as well as the regulation of international trade in endangered species of wild flora and fauna.
‒ cites, with 181 parties, including the eu and its 28 member states, is the largest existing global agreement on wildlife conservation. cites aims to ensure that international trade in wild animals and plants does not threaten the survival of these species in the wild. the eu's accession to cites is a key step towards ensuring that the eu can achieve the broader objectives of its environmental policies, as well as the regulation of international trade in endangered species of wild flora and fauna, and promote the sustainable development policies of the united nations 2030 agenda. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the imperative to ensure that international trade in wild animals and plants does not threaten the survival of these species in the wild. wildlife trafficking is now a transnational organised crime that has major negative impacts on biodiversity and on the livelihoods of local populations, as it denies a legal income, creating insecurity and instability. increasingly, illegally traded exotic species are being treated as pets in europe and the rest of the world, and the escape of these animals could lead to uncontrolled spread with consequences for the environment and for public health and safety.
‒ the european union's (eu) accession to cites was a key step in ensuring that the eu and its member states achieve the broader objectives of their environmental policies, improving the regulation of international trade in endangered species of wild flora and fauna and promoting the sustainable development policies of the united nations 2030 agenda. this is the first time that the eu has become a party to the convention, making relevant proposals, in particular on the fight against corruption and the regulation of the hunting trophy regime. i would point out the recent adoption of the eu action plan against wildlife trafficking, which aims to combat organised wildlife crime more effectively, and which should also be implemented by the member states, as a way of demonstrating the importance of fighting this type of crime. finally, i would also like to mention the importance of encouraging the eu and the member states to promote initiatives that increase protection against the impact of international trade in species for which the eu is an important transit or destination market, by creating legislation to that end aimed at reducing their illegal trade.
‒ this report points to ways of significantly improving cites. among many, i would highlight the proposal to strengthen controls on certificates of origin for ivory, to strengthen sanctions for trafficking in protected species (including elephants, rhinos, tigers, primates and tropical timber varieties) and the challenge to develop new guidelines and support the development of additional techniques and methodologies to distinguish species from captive production facilities from wild species. i hope that all these suggestions will be taken into account at cites cop 17 and that this will help to fight corruption and protect biodiversity. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in view of the 17th meeting of the conference of the parties (cop17) to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), in johannesburg, south africa, from 24 september to 5 october 2016, and given that the eu is participating for the first time as a party to cites, the envi coordinators decided to submit an oral question to the council and the commission, together with a proposal for a resolution. the resolution addresses the main topics of the next cop17 and makes several recommendations, including on transparency in decision-making and reporting, wildlife trafficking and corruption, enforcement and financing. the text supports the proposals put forward by the eu and its member states, in particular the proposed resolutions on corruption and hunting trophies, the extension of cites to protect a number of species that are imported into the eu, such as pets, and proposals for changes in the control of trade in personal and household goods.
‒ i voted in favour of the resolution setting out the main objectives of the 17th session of the conference of the parties to the cites convention, as i agree with the european parliament's position on this, the largest existing agreement on wildlife conservation in the world. unfortunately, the union is now an important destination and transit market for illegal trade in wildlife, in particular birds, turtles, reptiles and flora. in this context, i particularly welcome the eu's accession to cites, especially as the eu is participating for the first time as a party, making the eu's legal status in cites more transparent and confirming the eu's role in multilateralism. this accession will allow the eu to express a coherent position on cites matters and to participate substantially in the negotiations of the conferences of the parties.
‒ since the liberalisation of postal services in 2008, there has been a paradigm shift in the sector, with the reduction of paper-based communications, the application of new technologies and an exponential increase in packaging and orders thanks to online shopping. i support the ferber report, which responds to these new challenges by setting out a set of observations for the national regulatory authorities, whose main task is to give practical application to the provisions of the postal services directive. i agree with the need to strengthen cooperation and coordination between regulatory authorities with a view to increasing the efficiency and interoperability of the cross-border delivery service, as well as improving geographical coverage and accessibility to universal services for parcel delivery to citizens with disabilities or reduced mobility or living in remote areas. i believe that it must be ensured that market liberalisation benefits all users, in particular consumers and smes, while promoting the strategy on e-commerce and crossborder parcel delivery. these rights should be accompanied by a simple and effective cross-border complaint and dispute resolution system.
‒ in 2009, at european level, postal services accounted for an annual turnover of eur 72 billion, corresponding to 0.62% of gdp in the eu. as regards universal services, more than 85 billion postal items and almost 2 billion parcels were dispatched by universal service providers in the eu in 2013. the european postal sector accounted for an annual turnover of eur 91 billion in 2011, equivalent to 0,72% of eu gdp. however, parcel delivery is a competitive, innovative and fast-growing sector. some 1.2 million people work for universal postal service providers, together with people working for other letter and parcel delivery operators. i agree with the need to promote and safeguard effective competition in the postal services sector.
‒ the postal market is still an area of the economy with strong growth prospects and increased competition, although between 2012 and 2013 the general mail service decreased on average by 4.85% in the eu, according to the european commission's database on postal statistics, which is consistent with the decrease in the volume of mail over the last ten years, largely due to the process of substitution by electronic means. the postal services directive provides member states with the flexibility to address local specificities and ensure the long-term sustainability of the provision of universal services, while responding to user needs and adapting to changes in the technical, economic and social context. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the adoption of directive 2008/6/ec was crucial to achieving the fundamental objectives of the liberalisation of european postal services. indeed, postal services comprise a wide variety of services, from the delivery of letters and parcels to homes and offices to the promotion of value-added services (e-commerce, insurance, banking, advertising). the sector is an important part of communication in the internal market of the european union, playing a key role in european social, territorial and economic cohesion. however, postal services have now changed the way in which their services are sought, with many of these services now being provided by digital means, which is already being accentuated by the increase in online purchases and parcel deliveries. this report concludes that promoting competition in this sector is important to achieve the objectives set out in strategy 2020. therefore, by identifying the european postal services sector as a vital part of communication in the internal market and by sharing the view that strategy 2020 is fundamental in this area, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. the 2008 review of postal services has achieved key objectives in terms of its liberalisation. however, they have undergone enormous changes since the market was fully opened. paper communications have seen a sharp decline and the number of letters has decreased across the eu. on the other hand, new technologies make online shopping more convenient and therefore increase the number of packages and orders processed by postal operators. over the past five years, the business-to-consumer segment has grown rapidly in the parcel and packaging markets. good postal services are an essential part of communication in the eu's internal market. however, the main trend is in parcel delivery services, due to the development of e-commerce. however, parcel delivery is a competitive, innovative and fast-growing sector. the european express delivery services sector employed an estimated 272 000 workers in 2010 and this number is expected to increase to 300 000 by 2020. finally, one of the commission's main tasks is to promote and safeguard effective competition in the postal services sector. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of this directive.
‒ this own-initiative report deals with the implementation of the 2008 postal services directive and analyses in a very detailed and exhaustive way the significant changes that postal services have undergone over the last few years, proposing some measures to improve them. i agree with the overall characterisation, and i am sure that postal services must adapt to the current reality by promoting greater competition in this sector, taking into account the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy with regard to more sustainable growth and a more competitive and resource-efficient economy. as regards the proposals in the report, i would stress two: the need to strengthen the independence of the national regulatory authorities and to ensure fair competition. a final word on the importance of member states' administrations also adapting to this new reality - more technological in nature - in order to promote more actively the economic, social and territorial cohesion of their territories, and the need to ensure that all users of this market, with particular emphasis on end consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises, benefit equally from the liberalisation of this market.
‒ the implementation of the postal services directive, especially since its revision in 2008, has achieved its fundamental objectives of liberalising european postal services. this liberalization has resulted in a reduction in geographical coverage and distribution frequency; in higher prices and the shutdown of unprofitable services; in social and labour dumping, through the replacement of permanent jobs by temporary, precarious workers, with wages often below the national minimum wage. the report, in a context markedly more diverse in terms of communications (in view of the increasing digitalisation), which has taken away the scope of the objectives of liberalisation (maximising profits for financial capital), calls for more competition, more value-added services and a reduction (or no obligation to provide) in the provision of mandatory universal services. this whole process deserves our complete disapproval. the evolution of this sector has been a regression for the populations and the users.
‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are a key pillar of the european union's economy: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used to support the development of the community's economy. i believe that the eu should seek to overcome the difficulties of the heterogeneity of types of smes and of the different national circumstances of economic environment or legal framework. in this context, considering that bank credit is the main source of financing for smes and that its decline, driven by the crisis, has had a significant impact on the european business fabric, i argue that the capital markets union in prospect should take smes as a priority vector of its affirmation. i share the concern about the balance between the stability of the banking sector and support for smes, and i therefore believe that the new rules for the banking sector should take account of the financing needs of smes. i also share the view that financial literacy for entrepreneurs and investors must be promoted: in the case of the former, to raise awareness of non-bank forms of financing on the capital markets; in the case of the latter, to increase confidence in investment. i therefore support the report.
‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) and midcaps represent a substantial part of the eu economy. access to finance for smes is therefore a longstanding issue on the political agenda. the variety of smes in the eu is considerable. different member states have different types of smes, depending on their business model, size, stage of development, financial structure and legal form. it is important to support smes' access to finance throughout their life cycle and to increase smes' awareness of complementary market-based sources of finance.
‒ micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, as well as midcaps, play an important role in terms of employment and growth for the european economy, with smes contributing in 2014 to 67% of total employment, 71.4% of employment growth and 58% of value added in the non-financial business sector in the eu. the creation of incentives to improve access to finance and the diversification of sources of finance for smes is therefore necessary. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (msmes) and midcaps play an important role in the european economy in terms of employment and growth, with smes contributing in 2014 to 67% of total employment, 71.4% of employment growth and 58% of value added in the non-financial business sector in the eu. i am voting in favour of this report which encourages institutions to create new ways of financing smes, different from those which have traditionally been available. i therefore believe that the capital markets union should actively contribute to the existence of other ways of providing financial support for companies, as can and should happen with venture capital.
‒ it is now clear that access to bank financing for smes has been severely restricted in recent years, mainly as a result of the financial crisis in the european economic area. this is all the more serious when it is a well-known fact that bank loans are the main source of finance for european smes. despite this heterogeneity in the genesis of these smes and their financing methods, this report identifies the importance of support for the transfer of enterprises, the encouragement of financial literacy, the creation of complementary non-bank sources and the simplification and harmonization of the tax systems of the member states. i am voting in favour of this report because smes are a substantial part of the european business fabric, with a tremendous socioeconomic impact, and it is imperative to ensure that these companies can obtain the appropriate support and financing, especially in times of increased instability in the european and global economic and financial systems.
‒ i voted in favour of the fact that i believe it is important to support smes financially, understanding that there are different types of smes depending on their business model, size, stage of development, financial structure and legal form. country-specific factors such as the economic environment, structural factors such as the legal framework and cultural issues have a strong influence on financing needs and the availability of financing options. all these sme and country specific factors have an impact on the productivity, profitability and risk profile of smes. given the multiplicity of factors, it is difficult to assess the influence of each. this has to be taken into account when designing appropriate policy measures with a view to diversifying cost-effective financing options for smes. the public availability of financial information on smes is essential for their successful access to the capital market. investors, whether banks, institutional investors or small investors, should be able to assess the profitability and the degree of risk of their investment.
‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) represent a substantial part of the eu economy. access to finance for smes is essential. during the crisis, smes had more limited access to finance than larger companies. the high dependence of smes on bank credit and the 'disadvantage' of banks triggered by the crisis have contributed to this situation. an initiative to diversify funding options for smes as one of its priorities, with special attention to those run by women and minorities, is therefore urgently needed.
‒ a very significant part of the european economy is made up of smes and midcaps, with a geometry that varies in different member states according to business model, size, legal form and financial structure, plus country-specific structural factors. this heterogeneity has repercussions on productivity, profitability, job creation and the complexity of sme financing itself. therefore, each of these specific factors should be taken into account when designing policy measures to diversify investment throughout the business life cycle. i therefore support the rapporteur's proposals to support access to finance for smes, whether through tax incentives, bank loans, improving the level of support through existing or newly created credit channels, and through complementary non-bank sources of finance such as those listed in the capital markets union action plan. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour of this own-initiative report.
‒ the diversification of sources of finance for smes in the capital markets union is a bright spot. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. the report masks the real objectives of this initiative and does not condemn the negative impact that austerity and neoliberal policies have had on smes. instead of making the case for the banking union and the capital markets union, it would be preferable to read the real causes of the crisis which, at the very least, should make us aware of the need for effective public control over the financial system.
in the light of the above, the commission considers that the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment against the adverse effects of certain substances and mixtures from the production of certain products is appropriate. i note that on the one hand, european smes are very heterogeneous and include a large number of microenterprises, 'start-ups' and fast-growing innovative companies, which, because of their different business models, face different problems with different financing needs. i therefore stress the need for smes to have improved and more diversified public and private financing options, not just for the start-up phase but for the whole life cycle of the sme. to this end, the commission and the member states should support smes in this process, not only in terms of funding but also in terms of regulation and the initiatives to be supported. as there is no one-size-fits-all financing model, it is necessary for the commission to support the development of a wide range of tailor-made programmes, instruments and initiatives to support enterprises in their start-up and growth phases, taking into account their size, turnover and specific financing needs.
‒ unemployment and migration are the biggest challenges facing europe today and have multiple implications for the future. the number of unemployed in the eu remains at historically high levels and the recent arrival of hundreds of thousands of migrants is another huge social challenge, with more and more jobs needed to integrate people settling in europe. the european economic structure is based on small and medium-sized enterprises as a source of new jobs and the engine of the eu economy. i agree with the need to ensure a level playing field for smes in relation to their competitive position compared to large companies. i support the need for a stable regulatory environment and better quality of regulation and enforcement as the right way to reduce burdens on smes, including wage costs. i would stress the need for specific measures for smes, with the aim of reducing market failures, enabling their internationalisation and boosting their job creation potential. i therefore support this report.
‒ the number of unemployed in the eu remains at historically high levels, reaching 23 million people in 2015, with 4.5 million young people under 25 years of age and both sexes outside the labour market and education system. in 2015, small enterprises contributed up to 71% of the growth in employment in the non-financial market economy. the report stresses that in order to achieve a sound environment for business development and boost its job-creation potential, national and european policies must, as a priority, address issues related to skills (shortages, gaps, 'brain drain'), regulatory uncertainty and administrative burdens, as well as the problem of undeclared work and the de facto privileged position of multinational enterprises.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, smes contributed a large share to employment growth, with up to 71% in the non-financial market economy. job creation in smes is influenced by a number of internal and external factors, and among the latter, key assumptions are controllable competition (including from multinational companies and the shadow economy), controllable administrative burdens and overall production costs, and access to finance and skilled labour. we must create mechanisms to make the best use of the potential of smes in job creation and economic development. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ it is important to remember that almost 99% of european enterprises are smes, thus forming the backbone of the eu economy and are strategically important in terms of job creation. i am voting in favour of this report, on the understanding that smes must actively contribute to sustainable growth and the creation of quality jobs. at the same time, new and updated teaching methods and the development of skills and competences must be promoted in order to meet the needs of smes, thus increasing the employability of thousands of european citizens.
‒ high unemployment rates and migration flows have been putting increasing pressure on the european labour market. while europe is not the continent with the highest birth rates, youth unemployment is certainly a further threat to demographic prospects and exposes the risks of social security systems and pension schemes. the recent arrival of hundreds of thousands of migrants in the european area is now forcing a rethink of the union's social integration model, which is to be made more robust and, at the same time, needs employment solutions that alleviate potential social tensions in the host member states, as exemplified by the united kingdom. this report identifies the importance of smes in the current scenario, stressing the need to address issues such as regulatory uncertainty, undeclared work, multinational privileges and other issues of scale, such as the so-called 'brain drain'. for the above reasons, and because i consider it essential to create new and sustainable jobs in all the member states of the union, i voted in favour of adopting this report.
‒ high levels of unemployment threaten demographic prospects, as many young people without work are delaying the start of a family. the recent arrival of hundreds of thousands of migrants is another huge social challenge, with more and more jobs needed. in the face of these challenges, strengthening the conditions for job creation in all eu member states has become essential. smes must be a central point in the definition of enterprise policy and the necessary measures must be taken to enhance the job creation potential of this sector. the report stresses that issues related to skills (shortages, training gaps, 'brain drain'), regulatory uncertainty and administrative burdens, as well as the problem of undeclared work and the de facto privileged position of multinational enterprises, must be addressed. the importance of reducing the burden on smes, the further development of vocational training, the need to ensure a level playing field for smes and the 'paradox of the labour market' are highlighted, as many jobs cannot be filled easily due to the labour gap in europe. i voted in favour.
‒ the european economic structure is based mainly on small and medium-sized enterprises as a source of new jobs and the engine of europe's economy. over the last decade, smes have created 85% of european jobs. in 2015, small enterprises contributed up to 71% of the growth in employment in the non-financial market economy. smes must therefore be at the heart of the definition of enterprise policy in the european union and all necessary measures must be taken to enhance the job creation potential of this sector. national and european policies should, as a priority, address issues related to regulatory uncertainty and administrative burdens, as well as the problem of undeclared work and the privileged position of multinational enterprises. we must not forget the aspects of social protection, social enterprises and cooperatives, the creation of quality employment, the problem of precarious employment, unfair competition, gender inequalities in employment and income, the fight against tax evasion and the shadow economy, the impact of trade agreements on workers' rights, wages and jobs, and also the impact of the digital single market.

‒ smes are the sector of the economy that leverages society, contributing to 71% of employment growth in the non-financial economy in 2015. this report recognises the importance of smes and their relationship to the development of societies and the quality of employment. it contains some points which are considered positive, such as the reduction of burdens, the fight against fake selfemployment, the consequences of the trade agreements ttip and ceta or the need for funding opportunities to boost organisations. however, it takes on assumptions which are completely contrary to the conditions necessary to guarantee the development of enterprises that promote employment with rights and the overall development of societies. these assumptions are based on the reduction of wages and labour deregulation to promote competitiveness; the promotion of dual education systems, 'less academic' and with entrepreneurship disciplines; the encouragement of teleworking and so-called 'smartworking' and deregulated forms of labour organisation, mainly through the defence of temporary work.

‒ article 10 of the treaty on the functioning of the eu states that in defining and implementing its policies and actions, the union shall aim to combat discrimination on grounds of sex, racial or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. fifteen years after the adoption of the directive on equal treatment in employment and occupation, this is the guiding principle we must continue to follow in its application, and the values must be impervious to the current sentiment or political winds of the member states. i support the weber report, which is intended to strengthen the fight against discrimination, pointing out the still low level of awareness of the issue and the existence of real phenomena of discrimination in specific groups and the urgency of unblocking the horizontal anti-discrimination directive. i refer to the extensive case law of the european court of human rights on this matter and welcome the commission's initiative to reconcile privacy with privacy, which is inseparable from this directive.
‒ according to the fourth eurobarometer survey, compared with the previous survey, more europeans are tolerant of groups at risk of discrimination and europeans are also better informed about their rights in the event of discrimination. according to data from the european union agency for fundamental rights (fra), 40% of roma seeking employment are victims of discrimination, 75% of homosexual couples do not shake hands in public, 38% of jews surveyed admit they do not wear symbolic clothing in public, 37% of muslims surveyed said they have been victims of discrimination and 11% that they have been victims of hate crimes. overall, the situation has a negative impact on social cohesion as well as on respect for fundamental rights. efforts are needed to strengthen dialogue between governments, civil society and social partners in all areas and to raise awareness among the general public.
in writing. ‒ the european union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights and must combat social exclusion and discrimination. it is necessary for all member states to remove the natural, social and economic obstacles which prevent the principle of equality from finding material expression and which limit the freedom of european citizens. only then will the proposed objectives be achieved. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the employment equality directive is based on one of the union's basic principles. article 10 tfeu provides that the union's policies and actions are to be based on non-discrimination on grounds of sex, race or ethnic origin, religion or belief, age or sexual orientation. however, according to the commission report, the existence of legislation is not sufficient to achieve full equality. therefore, awareness of existing protection, the use of eu funds and the strengthening of national equality bodies should be strengthened. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the report.

‒ established by regulation no 1927/2006, the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to support and express solidarity with workers who have lost their jobs as a result of large-scale redundancies due to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, where such redundancies have a significant negative impact on the regional or local economy. since 2006, the egf has been subject to numerous reforms: the intervention criterion was reduced from 1000 to 500 redundant workers, making the egf more accessible to the regions and member states; the period of intervention was extended from 12 to 24 months, enabling many beneficiaries to have access to more advanced training or education programmes; self-employed workers can now access the egf, which allows them to have the same social protection and safety net as other workers. the reforms of the regulation have helped to improve its functioning and simplified the procedures for member states to access the egf. i therefore support mrs harkin's report.
in writing. ‒ since its inception, member states have had the possibility to use the egf in exceptional circumstances or in small labour markets, where the intervention criterion was not met, if the redundancies concerned had a considerable impact on employment and the local economy. the scope of the egf was extended between 2009 and 2001 and from 2013 to include workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. in addition, as of 2013, self-employed persons were included in the scope, and the same was true in regions eligible under the youth employment initiative with a number of neets equal to the number of targeted beneficiaries. i agree with the conclusions of the report.

‒ the objective of this report is to analyse the activities, impact and added value of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in the period 2007-2014, and to identify the importance and effectiveness of the reforms implemented in that period. the egf is an emergency instrument and is not covered by the multiannual financial framework. it was set up to provide solidarity for workers who have lost their jobs as a result of large-scale redundancies due to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation. between 2007 and 2014, the functioning of the egf underwent some changes, notably the reduction in the number of staff required to benefit from the fund (currently 500 staff) and the increase in the budget of this mechanism. the use of support from the egf requires the submission by the member states of a final report on the implementation of the egf, including statistics on the reintegration of assisted workers. i support this report because i value the increase in the capacity and the action of the egf, identifying this solidarity fund as an indispensable tool for the protection of european workers, in a social context where unemployment is one of the problems to which it is urgent to give a european response, for europeans.

in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund, which was initially set up to enable solidarity with workers made redundant as a result of structural changes in world trade patterns, was subsequently extended to include workers made redundant as a result of the financial and global crisis, including self-employed workers. also in terms of eligible actions, funding and beneficiaries, the scope of application was broadened in the period 2007-2014 to include the most disadvantaged people, the elderly and unemployed young people, with a longer period of use of funding - 24 months - and consequently increasing the number of beneficiaries reintegrated into the labour market. as the report shows - and i voted in favour of it - i would also point out that the intervention criterion for recourse to the fund has been reduced from 1 000 to 500 redundant workers, which has made it easier for smaller regions and member states to apply, thus contributing to achieving greater economic, social and territorial cohesion. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

madam president, relations between the european union and the acp countries must be based, from the outset, on the recognition of a historical debt to be repaid for hundreds of years of colonialism, plunder, oppression and exploitation; on the recognition and combating of the deeply asymmetrical nature of north-south interdependencies which have not been mitigated in recent years. the objective of the progressive integration of the acp countries into the world economy cannot ignore the fact that this integration must not be, but is, a subordinate, dependent and peripheral integration based on unfair relations between unequal parties. the liberalization and deregulation of trade, which the so-called economic partnership agreements are an instrument for, serves the interests of the northern powers and economic groups, but not the needs of sustainable development of the southern countries and communities, quite the contrary. the relationship with the acp countries must respect their sovereignty, their legitimate choices and aspirations, not a biome to impose on them models of political and economic organization or geostrategic alignment with the priorities and choices of the european union.
mr president, the persistence of hunger, the persistence of millions of cases of chronic malnutrition in the world, at a time when scientific and technological development is reaching levels which could easily allow this phenomenon to be eradicated, is one of the most vivid libels against the capitalist system which is largely dominant on a world scale. the reasons for the famine are political, first and foremost. it is no coincidence that we are seeing a resurgence of the phenomenon even in countries normally included in the group of countries called 'developed'. look, for example, at the devastating effects of the european union and imf programmes. free trade that ruins small-scale farming, family farming and the food sovereignty of entire nations, land grabbing, the monopoly of transnational agribusiness on seeds and other production factors, the dismantling of public infrastructure and services and the attack on the social functions of states are among the inevitable causes of hunger, and a genuine effort to combat hunger must necessarily take into account the need to combat its causes.

‒ the paris agreement represents a milestone of enormous historical significance in the fight against climate change. it is an ambitious, balanced, equitable and legally binding agreement. it is crucial for comprehensive and collective action at global level with the aim of transitioning to a climate resilient global economy. it shows solidarity with future generations. we must live well within the limits of our planet. this agreement shall enter into force on the 30th day after the date on which at least 55 parties to the convention, representing together at least about 55% of total greenhouse gas emissions, have deposited their instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession. so far, 62 countries responsible for 51.89% of global greenhouse gas emissions have deposited their instruments of ratification. the eu accounts for about 12% of global emissions. with eu ratification, the second criterion of 55% of emissions is met.
‒ despite the immense publicity, the paris agreement does not fully meet the objectives of reducing greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions. no concrete limits have been agreed on ghg emissions and the package of measures already announced by the overwhelming majority of the 195 countries that have approved the text are insufficient to meet the proposed warming target. the agreement maintains and legitimises a market-based approach to climate change, of which carbon trading is the main (but not the only) instrument. an approach based on the commodification and financialization of nature and its resources, which has created tradable pollution rights and fixed their price at ridiculous levels. an approach which has revealed to satiety all its inefficiency and perversity but which is insisted upon, even though alternatives exist. the agreement abandons the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibility' between developing and industrialised countries, opting for a single system that could deepen inequalities between the countries that have contributed most to the accumulation of carbon in the atmosphere and developing countries. finally, the agreement also includes a dimension of financing projects by large transnational groups in developing countries, thus strengthening the imperialist domination of the resources of these countries.

in writing. the request concerns a total of 2 161 workers made redundant at microsoft and eight suppliers and downstream producers (1 889 workers) between september 2015 and january 2016, with 3 finnish regions affected (helsinki-uusimaa, south finland, west finland). initially, microsoft re-employed some nokia workers who had received support from the globalisation adjustment fund (gef). nokia moved production lines to the far east, then closed some of the more specialized production areas, finally selling to microsoft in 2013 the production of mobile phones, and now until it is being closed. another example of relocation, another procession of destruction and unemployment, another few thousand victims of the reigning neoliberalism. the resolution makes the usual recommendations. but it makes no reference to the fact that the workers resulting from the nokia redundancies had already received 'help' from the egf, and there was therefore a breach of the egf's presumption at least as regards the provision of secure long-term contracts to the workers, which reduces the weight of those recommendations. the need to support the workers made redundant is still felt, but the way in which this instrument has been used is deplorable.

‒ the proposal for a directive on legal aid is also part of the roadmap for strengthening the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, adopted in 2009 and which has been followed up over the years. compromise has been particularly difficult in this area, given the diversity of legal cultures and also the sensitivity of the criminal procedure - a cornerstone of the essential core of sovereignty of states. for this reason, and despite the long process, the harmonization achieved is of the utmost importance and must be valued. in particular, the outcome could have been better in the area of legal aid. parliament's position was to ensure support for economically deprived suspects and accused persons, irrespective of deprivation of liberty. however, the council was intransigent and had been blocking the adoption of this instrument since 2014. however, parliament has managed to extend the scope of the directive, ensuring that it protects not only provisionally but permanently as well. parliament has therefore decided to accept this compromise, which, although not the best, will certainly ensure the effective exercise of the right of defence by many europeans.
‒ judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the union is based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions. the council approved the roadmap for strengthening the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings which identifies as the right to legal aid and legal aid. the commission proposal is an important step towards ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states. however, i consider that defendants, suspects or wanted persons may feel inhibited from seeking legal aid if member states can require them to pay the costs relating to provisional legal aid because they do not meet the eligibility criteria. it is therefore fair to limit the recovery of costs to cases where defendants, suspects or wanted persons intentionally provide false information.
‒ the right to legal aid is intrinsically linked to the right of access to a lawyer. the european commission's proposal aims to ensure a minimum level of legal aid in all member states. however, it is limited to the right to provisional legal aid of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings who are deprived of liberty, as well as to the right to provisional legal aid and to legal aid of persons wanted in the context of proceedings for the execution of european arrest warrants. the commission has presented, in a separate recommendation, additional aspects of the right to legal aid. the rapporteur believes that this fragmented approach may reflect the sensitivity of the matter, but does not increase legal certainty or make clear to suspects or accused persons to what extent they will actually be entitled to legal aid or what the quality of legal aid will be. the scope of the directive should include the right to provisional and ordinary legal aid in all circumstances. in general, this report is moving in a positive direction, which we support. for several member states this is a clear step forward. but it is still short of the concrete measures and resources which guarantee universal access, free of charge, to legal aid for defendants, as one of the most basic rights to defence and dignity.
‒ this proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council aims to establish a set of common minimum standards on the right of suspects or accused persons to provisional legal aid in criminal proceedings if they are deprived of liberty and on the right of persons subject to proceedings under framework decision 2002/584/jha on the european arrest warrant (the 'wanted persons') to provisional legal aid, whether provisional or not. the directive aims to ensure that suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings who are deprived of their liberty and persons subject to european arrest warrant proceedings have access to legal aid to exercise their right of access to a lawyer, as provided for in the directive on this matter. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ this proposal concerns interim judicial support for suspects or accused persons deprived of their liberty and judicial support in proceedings for the execution of european arrest warrants. legal aid can ensure the effective exercise of the right of access to a lawyer for those who do not have the necessary financial means. i agree with the rapporteur that defendants, suspects or wanted persons may feel inhibited from seeking legal aid if member states can require them to pay the costs of interim legal aid because they do not meet the eligibility criteria. it therefore seems fair to limit the recovery of costs to cases where defendants, suspects or wanted persons intentionally provide false information. i believe that the scope of the directive should cover the right to provisional and ordinary legal aid in all circumstances. therefore, the directive should have the same scope as directive 2013/48/eu on the right of access to a lawyer.
‒ the general approach set out in the commission proposal is limited in its content, despite improving the existing legal protection framework. we point out as less positive technical elements of making this guarantee conditional on the financial situation of the person concerned, together with an assessment of the merits, that is, an assessment of the interests of justice, situations which are included in the commission's proposal and which stand out more assertively in the proposal presented by the european parliament, thus demonstrating the presence of some mechanisms which place limitations on the guarantee of universality in access to justice. the presence of a non-refoulement clause ensures that rights and guarantees established in any member state providing for a higher level of protection, such as in the case of portugal, cannot be derogated from or limited. a proposal which falls far short of what is enshrined in article 20 (1) of the crp: 'everyone shall be guaranteed access to the law and to the courts for the protection of his rights and legally protected interests, and justice shall not be denied on the grounds of insufficient economic means'. we also note that no reference is made to the political choices that in many countries, such as portugal, have deepened structural problems in the justice system.
‒ the implementation of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions presupposes that each member state has confidence in the criminal justice systems of the other member states, including in the way the rights of suspects or accused persons are safeguarded. differences in the interpretation of the right to a fair trial constitute an obstacle to justice and to the effectiveness of cooperation in criminal matters. the commission proposal is thus an important step towards ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states. the rapporteur believes that the current approach may reflect the sensitivity of the matter, but does not increase legal certainty or make clear to suspects or accused persons to what extent they will actually be entitled to legal aid or what the quality of legal aid will be. it also considers that defendants, suspects or wanted persons may feel inhibited from seeking legal aid if member states can require them to pay the costs of interim legal aid because they do not meet the eligibility criteria. the rapporteur also believes that member states have difficulty in collecting data on the implementation of the directive in each individual case. in this context, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ we must continue to work towards strengthening the rights of suspects and accused persons by establishing common minimum standards on the right to a fair trial. the existence of common minimum standards governing these rights will contribute to increasing mutual trust between judicial authorities, thus facilitating the application of the principle of mutual recognition. a degree of compatibility between the laws of the member states is essential to improve judicial cooperation in the union. those minimum rules should also take into account the differences between the legal traditions and systems of the member states.
‒ it is at the initial stage of the proceedings, especially when deprived of liberty, that suspects or accused persons are in a most vulnerable situation and in greatest need of legal assistance. this proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council aims to strengthen the rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings by establishing common minimum standards governing those rights, thereby contributing to increasing mutual trust between judicial authorities. compatibility between the laws of the member states is therefore essential to improve judicial cooperation in the union. however, the approach initially proposed did not increase legal certainty or make clear to suspects or accused persons to what extent they would be entitled to legal aid or what the quality of legal aid would be, and therefore the right to legal aid in all circumstances should be included in the scope of application. it was considered relevant to also include in the directive the provision that the preference/will of suspects or accused persons should be taken into account as far as possible in the choice of a lawyer and that provision should be made for the replacement of a lawyer in the event of loss of confidence. i agree with the proposal put forward by the rapporteur, and i therefore voted in favour of it.
‒ the right to legal aid is intrinsically linked to the right of access to a lawyer, in respect of which the european parliament and the council adopted directive 2013/48/eu of 22 october 2013. for those who do not have the necessary financial means, only legal aid can ensure the effective exercise of the right of access to a lawyer. the costs of providing legal aid should be borne by the defendant or by the person seeking legal aid. it seems fair to limit the recovery of costs to cases where the accused, suspect or wanted person intentionally provides false information. the report is moving in a generally positive direction, which we support. but it still lacks the recognition, the concrete measures and remedies that guarantee universal access, free of charge, to legal aid for defendants, as one of the most basic rights to defence and dignity. we voted yes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the de jong report for agreeing to the application of minimum rules on legal aid throughout the european union. i would particularly like to stress that the european socialist group has succeeded in extending the scope of the directive to cover all cases of legal aid and not just cases of provisional legal aid as envisaged in the original proposal of the european commission. at a time when the number of legal instruments in criminal and penal matters to combat terrorism is increasing, it is essential to remember that the european union is based on the rule of law and that this means harmonising the fundamental principles and procedural defence which must be guaranteed to suspects or accused persons accused of committing a crime.
‒ in june 2005, the council of the european union adopted regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 on trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment or for the purpose of torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, which allows, by means of a delegated act, for the revision of the control lists (set out in its annexes). these eu control mechanisms are not just trade control mechanisms but cover policy guidelines, in particular preventing and prohibiting the production, trade and use of goods which are intended for torture or which could be used for lethal or inhuman purposes. i therefore support the schaake report on the revision of regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 which strengthens controls on instruments of torture by adding a new specific annex to prevent medicines from being used to apply the death penalty by lethal injection, by prohibiting brokering services for prohibited goods, by creating a union general export authorisation and by providing for a new emergency procedure which will allow a rapid response to the circulation of new products which may appear on the market and which are likely to be used in acts of torture.
‒ the aim of this regulation is to prevent eu exports from contributing to human rights violations in third countries. it therefore reviews eu controls on trade in instruments of torture. this legislation aims to close the loopholes in the current eu regime, including new clauses restricting and prohibiting advisory services, transport, brokering, advertising and promotion of risky or prohibited products, such as at trade fairs, exhibitions and on the internet. the regulation also provides for a new urgency procedure, which will allow a rapid response to the circulation of new products which may appear on the market and which are likely to be used in acts of torture. i voted in favour.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 1236/2005, which aims to combat torture, is an instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights by controlling products and activities that are, or may be, used improperly to apply the death penalty or to inflict torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the regulation establishes a prohibition on trade in 'single-use' products intended for torture and executions and related technical assistance (annex ii) and a system of authorisation for versatile products that could be misused for torture and executions by lethal injection (annex iii). it is now proposed to strengthen controls on instruments of torture. the lists of specific items provide clarity for exporters and importers and help to ensure compliance with the rules. in a context of increasingly complex external trade operations, the key role of effective implementation of controls, checks, sanctions, guidelines and awareness raising actions by national authorities is emphasised. a system of periodic reporting and review, consistent with other export control regimes, would appear to be appropriate. the objectives of the regulation appear to be fair and the means it defines proportionate.
in writing. ‒ in june 2005, the council of the european union adopted regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 on trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment or for the purpose of torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the regulation entered into force on 30 july 2006. i agree with this proposal and with the ban on trade in these substances. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the anti-torture regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 is a unique instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights by controlling products and activities that are or may be used improperly to apply the death penalty or to inflict torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the 'anti-torture regulation' contributes to the eu's long-standing policy to eliminate the death penalty worldwide and to prevent torture. it contributes to these objectives by combining prohibitions with licensing requirements for trade in the listed products. i support the need to review the rules on eu controls on trade in instruments of torture and to update the control lists. it is essential to ensure an appropriate combination of eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures in order to prevent and prohibit the production, trade and use of products intended for torture and to effectively control products liable to lethal and inhumane uses.

‒ the european union has for many years taken a firm stand against the use of the death penalty, torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the adoption by the council of regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 reiterates the intention to eliminate such practices. thus, by establishing export control mechanisms at union level, it becomes possible to prohibit the export of goods whose destination may be related to acts of torture or used for lethal purposes. the revision of the regulation aims to strengthen and update the checklists in the annexes to the diploma, to extend the ban on brokering and technical assistance services to controlled products, to introduce a union general export authorisation and to create urgent procedures to allow for rapid amendment of its annexes. as it is essential to ensure an appropriate combination of legislative, administrative and judicial measures against the trade in products which are liable to be lethal or inhuman, i am voting in favour of this report.
‒ i voted in favour, as i consider it imperative to ensure an appropriate combination of eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures in order to prevent and prohibit the production, trade and use of goods intended for torture and to effectively control products which could be used for lethal or inhuman purposes. the absence of multilateral export control regimes for goods intended for torture, unlike the 'dual use' regime, inevitably makes this difficult. however, the eu cannot limit its action to eradicate torture to reducing the availability of abusive equipment, to putting an end to circumvention practices and to promoting appropriate controls beyond its borders. trade instruments are part of a comprehensive approach that draws on all eu instruments for external action. it is essential to ensure consistency of eu export controls, including controls on lists of military equipment, dual-use items, firearms and goods for torture, without subjecting goods to duplicate and/or unnecessary controls that may create unnecessary burdens and restrict trade that has a legitimate purpose.
‒ the european union must take up its role in the control of products and activities that are, or may be, used in abusive ways to apply the death penalty or to inflict torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. these proposals follow the eu's longstanding policy of eliminating the death penalty worldwide and preventing torture. it contributes to these objectives by combining prohibitions with licensing requirements for trade in the listed products. this regulation establishes a prohibition on trade in 'single-use' products intended for torture and execution and their technical assistance, as well as a system of authorisation for versatile products that could be misused for torture and execution by lethal injection. the review of eu controls on trade in instruments of torture is long overdue and the updating of the control lists is another step in the right direction.
‒ export control mechanisms at eu level are trade policy instruments serving a set of broader policy objectives. regulation (ec) no 1236/2005, which aims to combat the use of torture, is an instrument that promotes the protection of human rights through the control of products and activities that are, or may be, abused for the purpose of capital punishment, torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the anti-torture regulation aims to contribute to the eu's long-standing political objective of eliminating the death penalty worldwide and combating the use of torture. the review of community controls on trade in instruments of torture has been long awaited. it is therefore important to ensure an appropriate combination of eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures in order to prevent and prohibit the production, trade and use of goods intended for torture and to effectively control products that could be used for lethal or inhuman purposes. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with its content.

‒ this proposal concerns the approval of a strategic cooperation agreement between europol and china. the information exchanged may include specific expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analysis, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods, training activities and the provision of advice and support in individual criminal investigations. like other european union agencies, europol is a structure created to enforce the implementation of a path of progressive federalisation, and moreover in particularly sensitive areas which touch the heart of the sovereignty of states, because they interfere with rights, freedoms and guarantees. since its creation, it has been given powers which undermine the sovereignty of states, and its activities have been carried out without any democratic control. we believe that europol should not override national police forces and their activities and we support cooperation between the internal and external security structures of the various countries. our vote against this report is therefore inseparable from our position of principle on europol.

‒ the current eu-acp partnership agreement, signed on 23 june 2000, has since formed the framework for the eu's relations with 78 countries in sub-saharan africa, the caribbean and the pacific. that agreement, revised in 2005 and 2010, as provided for in its provisions, was concluded for a period of 20 years and expires on 29 february 2020. it is a legally binding instrument which creates common institutions and defines a framework for dialogue with each of its members, including a major political, economic and trade cooperation dimension, as well as a development finance cooperation dimension (linked to the european development fund). i support the neuser report as i consider it important that in relations after 2020 this multi-faceted dimension of the acp-eu partnership based on respect for the human rights acquis, good governance and democracy (included also in the economic partnership agreements) is emphasised and that a new agreement includes the sustainable development goals and the 2030 agenda and from the institutional point of view a strong parliamentary dimension and the inclusion of regional infrastructures.
‒ more than 80% of the world's least developed countries are located in acp regions and together account for less than 5% of world trade and approximately 2% of world gdp. some eur 900 million is earmarked for the african peace facility and some eur 1.4 billion from the edf reserve will be used for the eu trust fund for africa. acp-eu cooperation is a unique and valuable achievement, which has strengthened the ties between the peoples and countries of the acp and the eu member states and their national parliaments over the past 40 years. however, in order to improve the effectiveness of cooperation and to adapt it to new challenges, it is necessary to adopt a new structure that maintains the parts of the acp-eu acquis that are universal in character, such as the commitment to human rights and gender equality, human development, good governance and democracy, the objective of the rule of law and the exchange of best practices under a common framework.
in writing. ‒ as we have said, there is a need for a change in the relationship between the eu and the acp countries, which is now governed by the cotonou agreement. that is not the view underlying this report, quite the contrary. the report calls for a more in-depth and critical approach to the relations of dependence and subordination to which the acp countries have been subjected and the role of eu policies in establishing these relations, but in essence it endorses the course taken in recent years. when the so-called economic partnership agreements (epas) imposed by the eu and the consequences of their implementation were called for criticism, the epas were not criticised or scrutinized, but were seen as the instrument that should frame relations between the eu and the acp countries, because they were supposedly promoting growth and development. when a new framework for cooperation was called for, genuinely capable of promoting the sovereign development of the acp countries, the report ignores this need, does not address hot-button problems such as the illegal exploitation and expropriation of natural resources by foreign interests in the acp countries, ignores the will, opinion and participation of the acp countries, giving greater importance to the affirmation (explicit or implicit) of the eu's geo-strategic interests. we voted against it.

‒ the current relations with the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries and the european union have not produced much for the parties to the agreement. after the cotonou agreement, it is vital to prepare a more effective and efficient framework and, more importantly, one that is adapted to new and emerging global challenges. this new framework should be defined in close cooperation with the acp countries, including civil society, and in coordination with regional organisations, and should build on the lessons learned from the cotonou partnership agreement, in order to avoid duplication of efforts and structures. i believe that in the post-cotonou framework there should be mechanisms to facilitate trade and that growth and development should be its main objectives. i agree with the rapporteur that it is important to have a renewed acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly and to have it involved at all stages of the discussions on the post-cotonou framework, and that there should be strict parliamentary control of the future framework.

in writing. legitimised by the cotonou agreement, initially signed in 2003, the partnership between the 79-nation african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of countries and the 28-member european union (eu) is a binding document with an unprecedentedly large number of members. the cotonou agreement has as its main pillar the reduction and eradication of poverty, in line with the objectives of sustainable development and the progressive integration of the acp states into the world economy. the agreement is based on a set of values such as respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, democracy and the rule of law. but it will be exhausted before december 2016. the overall picture is that, despite political rapprochement between the parties and progress in the development of poverty eradication, the results have proved to be insufficient and unequal. this report identifies priority areas for future acp-eu cooperation action, of which i highlight, on the one hand, the need to give binding character to the common frameworks and regional agreements, and, on the other hand, the importance of placing the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals at the heart of the new agreement, and thus the continuation of the priority objective of poverty eradication. i therefore vote in favour.
‒ the european parliament, taking into account the partnership agreement between the african, caribbean and pacific states and the european community and its member states, calls for the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals to be placed at the heart of a new agreement, as well as the establishment of robust follow-up mechanisms, to ensure that the implementation of the agreement promotes and contributes to the sustainable development goals. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action against terrorism. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu, including the member states, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions, was adopted by the council on 14 june. in view of the above, i voted in favour.
‒ cooperation between the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) states and the european union is a unique and valuable achievement that has strengthened the ties between the acp countries and the eu member states and their national parliaments over the past 40 years. in order to improve the effectiveness of cooperation and adapt to new challenges, it is necessary to continue investing in human rights and gender equality, human development, good governance and democracy, the rule of law and the exchange of best practices under a common framework, while taking into account specific regional needs.
‒ the cotonou agreement has helped to strengthen political ties between the european union and the acp countries (africa, caribbean and pacific). however, the results of this partnership are not yet visible and acp-eu relations need to adapt to the political, structural and demographic changes that have taken place in the meantime. i therefore consider it of the utmost importance to establish a new framework that implements the 2030 agenda and meets the sustainable development goals (sdgs). the future partnership should still meet mutual ambitions, so it is important that there is great clarity from the outset on the priorities identified. the eradication of poverty will have to remain one of the primary objectives of acp-eu cooperation. i also believe that political dialogue must be more effective and better exploited both at the level of governments and at the level of the states themselves as a whole, and that it must be carried out proactively and not just as a crisis management tool. as vice-president of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly, i tabled 23 amendments, and this report therefore contains some of my proposals, particularly on the involvement of local authorities, regional authorities and civil society organisations, and on the maintenance of poverty eradication as one of the primary objectives of the future partnership.

madam president, commissioner georgieva prepared her candidacy for the united nations while she was on salary from the european commission. duro barroso has formalized his old bond with goldman sachs and moved from a de facto union to a marriage. commissioner cañete, yes, he left the oil lobby to come to the climate and energy portfolio. and this list is far from exhaustive. there is a problem of registration and there is a problem of conflicts of interest, but none of these examples would be solved by the new proposals from the european commission. we need an intertemporal register with absolute incompatibilities over the periods of break and not just relating to the periods in which they hold office, otherwise we will continue to have commissioners who come from industry and to industry they will return. the bottom line is that no one can serve two masters: it cannot serve the financial interests and serve the interests of the citizens at the same time, and so if there are revolving doors, it's because the rooms in these institutions are contiguous. as long as the commission is at the service of the financial interests and not at the service of the interests of the people, we will continue to have these types of commissioners, but the day it is at the service of the people, i guarantee that these commissioners will not even want to go to the commission.
madam president, there is a first fundamental and structural conflict of interest in the european union. the conflict between the interests which the european union defends, the interests of the great powers, the great economic groups, the great financial capital, and the interests of the workers and peoples of europe. everything else we discuss here are expressions, revelations, if you will, of this fundamental reality. it is now known, not surprisingly, that duro barroso already worked for goldman sachs when he was president of the european commission, just as it is known that draghi continues to work for goldman sachs as president of the european central bank, but the problem goes far beyond the so-called revolving door. all the legislation adopted in recent years by the european union in the financial field, to give just one example, has been determined by the interests and direct intervention of the big banks and insurance companies. there is no code of conduct that can alter the matrix, the class nature of this integration process. it will be the struggle of the workers and the peoples to defeat it and to oppose it with the necessary alternative in defence of their own class interests.
