mr president, in july i led a delegation from the libé committee to calais. we found two very different realities. in grande-synthe, by the action of a mayor with a humanist sensibility; in calais, by the inaction of a president with a speech hostile to refugees and immigrants. the approach makes all the difference in finding worthy solutions to manage the influx that puts so much pressure on this border region. although the french authorities are accepting asylum applications, the people we spoke to in the jungle do not lose hope of crossing to the uk where they have family, fellow countrymen, and they think they have a future, because they know that the trafficking networks are still active and crossing is just a matter of being able to pay, including hundreds of unaccompanied minors who the uk is slow to reunite with their families. ethiopians i spoke to in the jungle said that hundreds of their countrymen had arrived there weeks earlier, two to three months after leaving their villages, on dangerous journeys, risking their lives. mr president, building walls and refusing to open legal and safe pathways for immigrant refugees is to continue to give business to smuggling networks. it is not only immoral and a violation of human rights, it is ineffective and only aggravates the security of europe. calais could be on any beach in europe.

the european union's asymmetrical nature is revealed in small as well as in big things. ending roaming in mobile communications is a long-held objective. apparently consensual, it even served as an election propaganda tool. but behind the goodness of the proposal lies the flip side: roaming calls have higher costs than those associated with domestic calls. who will pay these costs? in addition, net tourism receiving areas will experience seasonal increases in pressure on their networks, which may require investment in their strengthening. who pays for them? the operators in these countries have already warned: if it is not possible to reflect these and other costs in the roaming tariffs, they shall be reflected in the national tariffs. so, just to be clear: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the european union. this is the single market in telecommunications. in this as in other sectors, liberalisation and the miracle of free competition serve the aims of monopolistic concentration at european level, and serve neither consumers, nor households, nor firms, nor the national interest.

in writing. this structured dialogue is an integral part of an unspeakable process of blackmail and conditioning designed to prevent any deviation of national governments from the neoliberal agenda of the european union. we are naturally against the suspension of the structural funds and we follow a lot of what was said today in this meeting. but this dialogue, this possibility of suspending the structural funds, the sanctions and the fines did not fall from the sky. they are the application of concrete rules which have been adopted by this parliament and by many members who are now faced with the consequences of directives and regulations adopted earlier. they are therefore an integral part of an economic and monetary union which, with its rules and its mechanisms, represents a real obstacle to the development of the economically weaker countries and regions. in this sense, rather than recommending that the suspension of the structural funds should not be applied, we must demand a thorough reflection on the euro, on economic and monetary union and, ultimately, on this process of neoliberal integration which has ceased to be part of the solution and has become part of the problem.
‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a fundamental instrument in the context of judicial cooperation between contracting states in resolving cases of international child abduction. the convention aims to harmonize the different legal systems of the states which normally both declare themselves competent to adjudicate the action and declare the custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent, by adopting the criterion of the state of residence of the child. since this matter is currently the exclusive external competence of the union, a council decision calling for the acceptance by member states of the accession of third countries to the hague convention is necessary. i support the dzhambazki report in this respect and congratulate the state of peru on its accession to the convention.
‒ the convention in question establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states aimed at finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. this type of situation occurs very often when a couple separates. there are quite frequent cases of international child abductions reported in the press that occur as a result of separations and divorces. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children. the accession of peru to the convention deserves my praise and approval.
‒ the report agrees with a council decision authorising peru's accession to the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. this convention establishes a system of cooperation between states to find a solution to cases of international child abduction. its purpose is to ensure the return of children unlawfully transferred to or wrongfully retained in any contracting state and to ensure that rights of custody and access existing in a contracting state are effectively respected in other contracting states. child abduction sometimes occurs when a couple separates, with the parents from different states. it is common for the courts of the respective countries to declare that they both have jurisdiction and for the courts to grant custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. the importance of the system ensuring the immediate return of abducted children is underlined. we voted in favour of the agreement, since its justified purpose is to protect the interests of minors.
‒ the objective of the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction (hereinafter referred to as the '1980 convention'), which has so far been ratified by 93 countries, including all eu member states, is to restore the status quo by the immediate return of children who have been unlawfully transferred or retained through a system of cooperation between central authorities designated by the contracting parties. in 2015, peru informed the commission of its interest in the entry into force of the convention also for austria and romania, which should therefore be authorised by the european union to accept the accession of peru to the 1980 convention. the acceptance of austria and romania will make the 1980 convention applicable between peru and all eu member states except denmark. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction of 25 october 1980 is a vitally important instrument and has been ratified by all eu member states. this convention establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states with the aim of finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. with the accession of peru to the convention, a council decision is required to authorise the two member states which have not yet accepted peru's accession, namely austria and romania, to do so. the convention will thus enter into force between peru and the whole of the european union. i support the adoption of this proposal in order to ensure the protection of the minors concerned throughout the european union.
‒ this convention establishes a system of cooperation among contracting states aimed at finding a solution to cases of international child abduction, seeking to ensure the immediate return of children unlawfully transferred to or wrongfully retained in any state. the situation of child abduction occurs very frequently when a couple separates and when the parents are from different states. the convention thus aims to ensure that the rights of custody and access existing in a contracting state are effectively respected and to mitigate nationalist responses from the legal systems of each state. it is common for the courts of their respective countries to both declare that they have jurisdiction and for courts to grant custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent, decisions based on reasons that do not necessarily respond to the best interests of the child. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. peru has deposited its instrument of accession and we have voted in favour of it, since this agreement is designed to respond better to the protection of the best interests of minors.
‒ i support this report on peru's accession to the hague convention, as the hague convention system becomes more effective if more countries join it. in divorce situations where the parents are from different states, there is a temptation to take advantage of the lack of international cooperation to obtain custody of the children. custody is often granted to the parent who is a national of the state in which the courts are seated, and there are thus nationalist tendencies in the legal systems of each state. by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence, the convention allows for cooperation between the parties, as it tends to settle such disputes at international level. it should be noted that the commission, together with experts in the field of social justice, assessed and approved the functioning of the judicial system of peru and its willingness to cooperate. for all these reasons, i vote in favour.
‒ i voted in favour, as the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a vitally important instrument that has been ratified by all eu member states and which establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states aimed at finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. in the case of children whose parents are divorced, each from a different state, it is common for the courts of the two countries concerned to declare themselves competent and for the courts to grant custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent. there are quite frequent cases of international child abductions reported in the press that occur as a result of separations and divorces. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children. the accession of peru to the convention should therefore be welcomed, as the hague convention system becomes more effective if more countries join it.
‒ following the accession of peru to the hague convention, a council decision is needed to authorise the two member states (austria and romania) which have not yet accepted accession to do so. this will allow the convention to enter into force between peru and the whole of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation on the proposal for a council decision authorising the republic of austria and romania to accept, in the interest of the european union (eu), the accession of peru to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. this is a procedure which falls within the exclusive external competence of the eu (according to an opinion of the court of justice on the declaration of acceptance of accession to this convention), and is intended to ensure the full protection of minors in the european territory in the event of international child abduction. unfortunately, these situations are recurrent, especially when parents of different nationalities divorce. it is customary for each legal system to choose to declare the state of origin of each parent as competent, and the convention therefore plays a key role in resolving these transnational conflicts, providing for the jurisdiction of the court according to the place of residence of the child and a system that ensures the immediate return of abducted children. as austria and romania have not yet accepted the accession of peru to the convention, a council decision (after consultation of the european parliament) is required for the convention to enter into force between peru and the eu.
in writing. ‒ this is a proposal for a council decision on the authorization of the accession of this country, there is another, as we all know, to the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. this convention gives priority to international cooperation, for example in a divorce case where a parent of different nationalities flees with his or her child to another country. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children. in this case, the accession of peru is recommended to the other member states, since ireland, the czech republic and lithuania have already endorsed such accession. denmark is excluded from this cooperation. we support it.

‒ i voted in favour, as the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a vitally important instrument that has been ratified by all eu member states and which establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states aimed at finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. in the case of children whose parents are divorced, each from a different state, it is common for the courts of the two countries concerned to declare themselves competent and for the courts to grant custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent. there are quite frequent cases of international child abductions reported in the press that occur as a result of separations and divorces. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. it also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children. the accession of the republic of korea to the convention should therefore be welcomed, as the hague convention system becomes more effective if more countries join it.
‒ following the accession of south korea to the hague convention, a council decision is needed to authorise the two member states (austria and romania) which have not yet accepted accession to do so. this will allow the convention to enter into force between korea and the whole of the european union.
‒ as in the reports on kazakhstan and peru on the same convention, i also voted in favour of the proposal for a council decision authorising certain member states to accept, in the interest of the european union (eu) and with a view to its entry into force for the whole of the eu, the accession of the republic of korea to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. this is a highly administrative procedure, since it involves a council decision authorising the member states to accept the accession of this country to the convention, so that it can be applied fully and effectively throughout the territory of the european union, guaranteeing stronger protection for minors who are, unfortunately, increasingly the targets of international abductions. this accession of south korea to the convention is all the more important given the korean community residing in europe, which may be covered by the rules laid down in it, which is why i considered it logical, appropriate and relevant to vote in favour of its approval, as mentioned earlier.

in writing. the process of establishing a european public prosecutor's office started with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which only allows parliament to give its consent. the commission's most recent proposal dates from 2013. more than three years later, doubts about the establishment of the office of the prosecutor, as well as its contours, remain. parliament has repeatedly called for a change in this status quo. parliament made clear early on what it was not abandoning: that the office should take account of the so-called 'pif directive' on crimes against the interests of the union; that it should coordinate its action with eurojust, which should be independent, respect national constitutions and the highest international standards. in this last parameter, the office can draw inspiration from the portuguese model, whose institutional architecture is considered to be one of the best in the world. in short, a set of clear guidelines, to which the council has not yet been able to respond. i therefore support this resolution which asks the council for clarification, calls for the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office and rightly points out that the cost of not having a european public prosecutor's office is increasing every year.
‒ the eu collected €159.5 billion in value added tax (vat) revenues in 2014, but it is important that the eu and all its member states detect and punish fraud affecting the eu's financial interests in an effective and dissuasive manner in order to protect the taxpayers of all member states who contribute to the union budget. i consider it essential that a clear and unambiguous set of competences and procedures for the european public prosecutor's office be established, based on the proposal for a directive on combating fraud to the detriment of financial interests through criminal law, and that efforts be intensified to reach an agreement on the pif directive so that vat is included in its scope.
‒ this resolution addresses a controversial issue. the european parliament has long been concerned about the need to make a leap forward in the area of the federalisation of justice, which would involve, among other things, the creation of a european public prosecutor's office. the resolution calls on the council to establish 'a set of competences and procedures for the european public prosecutor's office' and to 're-open negotiations with the european parliament with a view to its establishment'. it defends the 'importance of the role of eurojust in improving judicial cooperation and coordination between the competent judicial authorities of the member states'. it states that 'in order to ensure effective cooperation and exchange of information between the eppo and eurojust, the two bodies should operate on the same premises'. we are facing another attempt to make progress in areas which go to the heart of state sovereignty, in this case justice. the vision expressed here is to centralise, structure and strengthen bodies such as eurojust, which escape democratic and judicial control, going beyond the guarantees of rights and freedoms provided for in national legislative and constitutional frameworks. the free and sovereign cooperation between the national states is thus being overtaken by the creation of supranational control mechanisms, which are inseparable from a security drift that increasingly puts fundamental rights, freedoms and guarantees at risk.

‒ in accordance with article 86 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the council may establish a european public prosecutor's office after obtaining the consent of the european parliament. this motion for a resolution is in line with this, by proposing the creation of an effective and independent european public prosecutor's office with a clear and unambiguous set of powers and procedures to combat economic crime, tax fraud and tax evasion. the proposal therefore calls on the council to abandon the rule which deprives the public prosecutor's office of the possibility of intervening in certain cases where pif infringements are committed. the proposal calls for a clear distinction between the competences of the court of justice and those of the national courts, avoiding conflicts of jurisdiction, which is a negative effect of the so-called 'national link'. at the same time, the document focuses on the protection of the rights, freedoms and guarantees of the subjects of proceedings investigated by the office of the prosecutor, as well as on the delimitation of the spheres of competence of the office of the prosecutor and eurojust. i think it is important that the union and its member states detect and punish fraud against financial interests in an effective and dissuasive way - because, as margaret thatcher rightly said, there is no such thing as public money; there is only taxpayers' money. i therefore support the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office as proposed in the report.

‒ the global financial crisis has put on the g20 and eu agenda the role of international financial reporting standards (ifrs) in financial stability and growth, in particular the standards for recognising losses in the banking system. the issuance of ifrs 9 financial instruments emerged as a key response to some aspects of the financial crisis and its impact on the banking sector. this financial instrument moves from an impairment model based on 'losses incurred' to one based on 'estimated losses' by addressing the problem of 'too little, too late' in the process of recognising losses by granting loans. however, the european supervisory authorities, in cooperation with the commission and efrag, should define guidelines in this regard in order to avoid any abuse of management discretion.
‒ in 2014, the international accounting standards board adopted ifrs 9 as the international accounting standard for financial instruments. ifrs 9 replaces the existing ias 39. ifrs 9 represents a fundamental change in the process for measuring impairment losses for institutions and arises as a response from the international accounting standards board to the late recognition of losses in the ias 39 model of losses. ifrs 9 is based on a forward-looking approach through an expected loss model, which enables institutions to recognise losses before they occur. the change in approach requires financial institutions to model future market trends, which will require a large set of macroeconomic data that historically were not required for accounting purposes. the resolution, while containing some concerns, does not call into question the standard-setting process. in addition, the new ifrs 9 has not been fully effective in addressing the pro-cyclicality problem and may even have some negative implications, especially for smaller financial institutions (e.g. cooperative banks) that use the standard method to assess credit risk.
in writing. ‒ ifrs 9 will enter into force on 1 january 2018 and replaces ias 39. ifrs 9 is an improvement over ias 39 in that the change from an impairment model based on 'losses incurred' to one based on 'estimated losses' is an answer to the problem in the process of recognising losses on loans. this regulation will be very important to prevent future crises in the financial sector. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ international financial reporting standards have played a key role since the global financial crisis as a guarantee of financial stability and growth, especially when it comes to standards for recognising losses in the banking system. the international accounting standards board issued ifrs 9 - financial instruments, as a key response to some aspects of the crisis and its impact on the banking sector - which will replace ias 39 as of 1 january 2018. this is an equally complex standard, but already an improvement on ias 39, adopting a model based on 'estimated losses' as opposed to 'unrealised losses' and will lack an assessment of the impact on the banking, insurance and financial markets in general in macroeconomic terms. i am in favour of the measures suggested in this motion for a resolution, which aim to identify and assess the effects and implications of the application of this ifrs 9 standard in the eu, particularly in relation to long-term investment, and i therefore voted in favour of it.

‒ materials and articles in contact with food are widely used in everyday life (e.g. food packaging, kitchen utensils). when placed in contact with food and depending on their composition and properties, materials behave differently, passing on parts of their constituents. however, the chemicals emitted by these objects can alter the composition of foodstuffs and endanger human health. although these products are subject to community rules (to which they are legally bound), the existing regulation sets out only the general safety requirements and also provides for the possibility of adopting specific measures in accordance with the legislation of each member state. so far, only four specific measures common to the eu have been adopted for materials/objects. however, the specific measures adopted by one member state may differ from those taken into account by another, so the absence of common european measures not only impedes the internal market, but also leads to increased compliance costs (often passed on to consumers) and a loss of competitiveness and innovation/development capacity. i think that this is a very important aspect of food safety and i therefore voted in favour of this own-initiative report.

‒ the european union's leadership in the fight against climate change gives dignity to the union and its member states. the ratification of the paris agreement, which will allow its early entry into force, and the commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030 are generational contributions of which we should be proud. i believe that the eu must maintain its leading role at cop22 in marrakesh, accompanying the moroccan presidency in making renewable energy a priority. i share the concern about the deepening of the market for emission allowances, and i reiterate the need to harmonize the principles of the paris agreement and even the kyoto protocol with the other international legal instruments in this field. only in this way will the 2020 and 2030 objectives be met. i share the view that conditions must be created for industrial adaptations to environmental objectives to promote employment, competitiveness and economic growth. in this respect, it is essential to coordinate environmental policy with energy policy, to promote scientific research and technological innovation and to integrate the objectives in external action, with environmental diplomacy, especially in relation to development support. i therefore support the motion for a resolution.
‒ the eu and its member states have presented their planned nationally determined contributions which commit to the binding target of at least a 40% domestic reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030. efforts to mitigate global warming should not be seen as an obstacle to the fight for economic growth, but should rather be seen as a driving force for the creation of new sustainable jobs and the achievement of sustainable economic growth. the eu must drastically reduce its greenhouse gas emissions beyond current commitments in order to avoid as far as possible large-scale negative emissions, as technologies have not yet been proven to be successful, socially acceptable, cost-effective and safe.
‒ this resolution addresses the preparation of the 22nd un conference of the parties on climate change, to be held later this year in marrakech. the conference will inevitably be held under the auspices of the paris conference and the agreement reached there. this resolution also reflects that. we are not following the laudatory tone with regard to the paris agreement. there are several problems with this agreement. in addition to the lack of agreed limits on ghg emissions, the agreement maintains and legitimises a market approach to climate change, of which carbon trading is the main (but not the only) instrument. the agreement abandoned the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibility' between developing and industrialized countries, opting for a single system that could deepen inequalities between the countries that contributed most to the accumulation of carbon in the atmosphere and developing countries. the agreement also includes a dimension of financing projects by large transnational groups in developing countries, enhancing the imperialist domination of the resources of these countries. these are views and options which are also expressed and defended in this resolution, and to which we are obviously opposed and which we counter with an alternative view, based on a normative approach and a common but necessarily differentiated responsibility.

‒ the paris agreement on climate change is a historic achievement of unparalleled importance in the fight against climate change and in favour of multilateralism. this is an ambitious, balanced, equitable and legally binding agreement and its adoption marks a decisive turning point towards a more comprehensive and collective global action to combat climate change. despite the positive commitment by all countries to limiting average global warming, this alone does not guarantee that significant negative impacts on climate can be avoided and it is therefore necessary to understand the concrete policy implications of limiting global warming to 1.5 °c. the eu has actively promoted the implementation of this agreement and should therefore demonstrate its commitment to it, including by reviewing its own long-term policy objectives and instruments - and by starting this process as soon as possible. the eu's relentless commitment to 'climate diplomacy' is essential to improve the perception of the importance of this fight, especially among global public opinion and in third countries where such perception is low or non-existent. i also believe that a sound architecture for the implementation of this agreement is fundamental - ideas also expressed in this report which i voted in favour of.
‒ the paris agreement has been called a landmark. the big problem is that cop-21 did not set targets or define the means to achieve the objectives presented. and he pushed the problem to 2030. the marrakesh conference (cop 22) is not expected to bring any new developments in this respect. the rich countries will continue to beat their breasts, hoping that this alone will reduce emissions and meet the pious promises and agreements that have been made. they will continue to propose market solutions to a problem whose root lies precisely in the market economy and capitalism with its logic of profit accumulation. for us communists, the resolution of this environmental emergency is inseparable from the struggle to overcome capitalism and the emergence of a new society and a new model of social production in which the state has control of the fundamental levers of the economy. everything else is more palliative.
‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the 2016 united nations climate change conference in marrakech, morocco, for advocating the need to tackle the global challenge of climate change through international cooperation. i would stress the introduction of several amendments to the text of the resolution, among which i would highlight the call for concerted action by the eu and other major global emitters to bring the 'predicted nationally determined contributions' closer to the 2°c target. it is now up to the parties to the agreement to demonstrate their commitment to decarbonisation through concrete actions at the next summit in morocco. in this context, i recall the historic ratification of the paris agreement by the european parliament on 4 october, which will allow it to enter into force as early as 4 november 2016, launching the first conference of the parties in marrakesh under the new agreement.
‒ the regulation of materials intended to come into contact with food contributes to the defence of public health and the protection of consumers. the adoption of legally binding standards for four of the 17 materials listed in annex i to regulation (ec) no 1935/2004 (plastics, ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials), the framework regulation on this subject, has resulted in legislative harmonisation that defends competitiveness and innovation in the internal market by subjecting all operators to the same rules. i therefore advocate harmonizing the regulation of the other 13 materials intended to come into contact with food, especially those which pose the greatest risk to the health of consumers and which are in greater demand on the market, namely paper and cardboard, metals and alloys, glass, silicones and rubber. the absence of common rules undermines the internal market and often transfers compliance costs to consumers. i share the concern about the implementation and enforcement of the current legislation, in particular in the areas of risk assessment, traceability, enforcement and compliance monitoring. to this end, i believe that the european food safety authority (efsa) should receive increased support (including financial support). i therefore support this report.
‒ food contact materials are widely used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, cooking utensils, tableware, etc. when brought into contact with food, different materials may, depending on their composition and properties, behave differently by transferring their constituents to food. further harmonisation in the area of food contact materials (including non-harmonised materials) is one way forward because it would be a step in the right direction, giving priority to materials that pose a specific risk to human health and that are in greater demand on the eu market. action at eu level is needed to address the absence of specific measures and gaps in risk assessment, traceability, compliance and control.
‒ this report addresses the need for a review of the regulation on food contact materials (fcms), widely used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, kitchen utensils, cutlery, etc. when brought into contact with food, these different materials may behave differently, transferring some of their constituents to food - a phenomenon known as migration - and some may endanger human health by contaminating or adversely altering the composition of food. to date, specific measures have been adopted at eu level for only four fcms: plastics (including recycled plastics), ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. for other fcms, member states may adopt specific measures at national level. these measures may differ from one member state to another, with different standards for product safety depending on where the product is used and marketed. current eu legislation on fcms allows chemicals that are banned to be used for other purposes. on the other hand, it ignores the effect of endocrine disruption, carcinogenic, mutagenic or reproductive toxic effects, bioaccumulation effects or other harmful properties. it is therefore relevant to address the lack of specific measures and gaps in the risk assessment, implementation, traceability, compliance and control of fcms.
‒ food contact materials are widely used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, cooking utensils, tableware, etc. when brought into contact with food, different materials may, depending on their composition and properties, behave differently by transferring their constituents to food. in such cases, chemicals emanating from food contact materials may endanger human life or adversely affect the composition of the food. this legislation aims to safeguard a high level of consumer protection while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market for materials intended to come into contact with food. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ this report addresses the need for a review of the regulation on food contact materials (fcms), widely used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, kitchen utensils, cutlery, etc. when brought into contact with food, these different materials may behave differently, transferring some of their constituents to food - a phenomenon known as migration - and some may endanger human health by contaminating or adversely altering the composition of food. to date, specific measures have been adopted at eu level for only four fcms: plastics (including recycled plastics), ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. for other fcms, member states may adopt specific measures at national level. these measures may differ from one member state to another, with different standards for product safety depending on where the product is used and marketed. current eu legislation on fcms allows chemicals that are banned to be used for other purposes. on the other hand, it ignores the effect of endocrine disruption, carcinogenic, mutagenic or reproductive toxic effects, bioaccumulation effects or other harmful properties. it is therefore relevant to address the lack of specific measures and gaps in the risk assessment, implementation, traceability, compliance and control of fcms.
‒ food contact materials are widely used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, utensils, etc. the regulation lays down safety requirements for all possible materials intended to come into contact with food, providing for the possibility of adopting specific measures for 17 materials. specific measures adopted by one member state at national level may differ from those in another member state, creating different standards for product safety. in addition, it leads to barriers in the internal market, with an increase in compliance costs and a loss of competitiveness and innovation. according to the ep study, a major challenge is that several substances in food contact materials are not currently under assessment. this is the case of so-called 'non-intentionally added substances' (nia) which are impurities of intentionally added substances or substances resulting from chemical reactions, which are present in the finished material. action at eu level is needed to address the absence of specific measures in the eu and gaps in risk assessment, traceability, compliance and control. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
‒ food contact materials are widely used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, cooking utensils, tableware, etc. when brought into contact with food, different materials may, depending on their composition and properties, behave differently by transferring their constituents to food. in such cases, the chemicals emanating from these materials may endanger human life or adversely alter the composition of the foodstuffs. the legislation aims to safeguard a high level of consumer protection while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market for these materials. specific measures have so far been adopted at eu level for only four materials intended to come into contact with food: plastics, ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. for other materials intended to come into contact with food, member states may adopt specific measures at national level. this creates a situation where specific measures adopted by one member state at national level may differ from those in another member state, creating different standards for product safety and barriers to the internal market. greater harmonisation at eu level is a step in the right direction.
‒ materials and articles in contact with food are widely used in everyday life (e.g. food packaging, kitchen utensils). when placed in contact with food and depending on their composition and properties, materials behave differently, passing on parts of their constituents. however, the chemicals emitted by these objects can alter the composition of foodstuffs and endanger human health. although these products are subject to community rules (to which they are legally bound), the existing regulation sets out only the general safety requirements and also provides for the possibility of adopting specific measures in accordance with the legislation of each member state. so far, only four specific measures common to the eu have been adopted for materials/objects. however, the specific measures adopted by one member state may differ from those taken into account by another, so the absence of common european measures not only impedes the internal market, but also leads to increased compliance costs (often passed on to consumers) and a loss of competitiveness and innovation/development capacity. i think that this is a very important aspect of food safety and i therefore voted in favour of this own-initiative report.
the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body. this report says it gives voice to the call of various stakeholders, including ngos and universities, stating that there is an urgent and clear need for action at eu level to address the lack of specific measures and gaps in risk assessment, implementation, traceability, compliance and control of fcms. greater harmonisation at eu level is called for for non-harmonised materials, through specific measures based on scientific evidence, giving priority to materials that pose a particular risk to human health.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the schaldemose report because i consider it necessary to adopt minimum harmonization rules for materials and articles intended to come into contact with food. the eu already has common standards for plastics, ceramics and pulp, but there are still 13 types of materials for which member states can still adopt national provisions, such as paper, cardboard, certain metals, glass, silicone and some paints. i would like to point out that within these materials, bisphenol is a particularly controversial endocrine disruptor. portugal has already gone ahead of the european union in banning the use of bisphenol in baby bottles. i believe that in situations where substances with potentially harmful effects on health are involved, the precautionary principle should prevail. at the same time i support the need for scientific research with solid results on the safety of materials and articles intended to come into contact with foodstuffs, for the benefit of consumers, the environment and manufacturers.
in writing. ‒ parliament looks annually at the state of implementation of community legislation. a key exercise for the legislator, but one which is particularly important given the institutional architecture of the union: for example, directives depend on action by member states to enter into force. once again, this report makes a good diagnosis, identifying the areas where member states are most likely to fail to comply. it also notes a decrease in infringement actions, as a result of increased dialogue between the commission and the member states in the 'pre-litigation' phase. although desirable, this dialogue - called the 'eu pilot' - is not very transparent, limiting public scrutiny and scrutiny by the institutions, in particular this parliament. i therefore support this report, stressing the need to improve the implementation of community legislation and the scrutiny of parliament.
‒ the report shows that environment, transport, internal market and services are the areas where most infringement cases remained pending in 2014 but the number of formal infringement cases has decreased over the last five years. one conclusion that can be drawn from the report is therefore that the application of community law remains insufficiently transparent. it is therefore agreed that parliament could and should play a more structured role in analysing the way in which the candidate countries and the countries which have concluded association agreements with the european union comply with eu law and in developing appropriate support in this area for these countries.
‒ this annual report monitors the application of eu law by the eu institutions. the general sense is no different from previous years. they highlight some curiosities. for example, it states in the recitals that there were 3715 complaints, with a significant number concerning spain (553), italy (475) and germany (276). but when we move from complaints to cases (initiated by the european commission) the figures change, with the following countries in the lead, totalling 893: greece (89), italy (89) and spain (86). the obvious question is: what happened to germany? what about greece? it's very clear. we oppose the supervisory approach, advocated in the report and embedded in the treaties, which gives the european commission the power to initiate infringement proceedings 'in order to ensure compliance with union law' and supports the court of justice being able to impose sanctions on member states for late transposition of eu law. and not just because of the discriminatory nature of the assessments, which are always political assessments, as is clear. we also reject outright the possibility of financial sanctions, as advocated in the report, which is the situation portugal is now facing. we obviously voted against it.
‒ the 32nd annual report of the commission on monitoring the application of eu law contains, once again, interesting information on the effective transposition and practical application of eu law. the report thus shows that the environment, transport, the internal market and services are the areas where most infringement cases remained pending in 2014. the annual report also points out that the number of formal infringement proceedings has decreased over the past five years. we must therefore continue to work to minimise the existing impacts. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. this commission report concerns the monitoring of the application of eu law and contains data on the effective transposition and practical application of eu law. according to the commission, the number of formal infringement procedures has decreased over the last five years, and this decrease reflects the effectiveness of the dialogue with the member states in the context of the eu pilot procedure. however, it is regrettable that the european parliament has little access to information on this procedure and on the cases pending. i am in favour of extending the time limits for implementing the legislation to ensure that member states are able to comply with them. to this end, more appropriate timetables for the application of the regulations and directives should be established, taking due account of the necessary monitoring and consultation periods. the new interinstitutional agreement on better law-making contains provisions aimed at improving the implementation and enforcement of eu law. improving the transposition process and the need for member states to identify and notify national measures that complement european directives is vital.
the document reflects the usual evaluation of the application of eu law by the european institutions. a hymn to interference, which nevertheless reveals the duality in the respect of the 'rules' by country. the great powers will benefit from the so-called closer cooperation and more structured dialogue with the commission, which the report highlights, but which in practice will be nothing more than a procedure by which they escape the rules they impose and use to ensure the centralization of power and control of small and medium-sized countries, coerced under the cunning and unacceptable process of blackmail and the threat of sanctions, such as those to which portugal has been subjected. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used effectively. a view of control and punishment which constitutes an attack on the sovereignty of the member states and which we reject outright. the pressure and interference on member states in defining their priorities and legislative framework is further increased by the 'better regulation' institutional agreement, an instrument for the harmonisation of the legal and legislative framework, or the proposal to create a european administrative law. reasons that could only justify a vote against.
‒ the annual report shows that the environment, transport, the internal market and services are the areas where most infringement proceedings remain pending in 2014. given that the european parliament still has relatively limited access to information on the eu pilot procedure dialogue with member states and on ongoing proceedings, it is difficult to assess to what extent the reduction of formal infringement proceedings better reflects in practice the compliance of member states with eu law than solutions agreed between the commission and the member states. as can be seen, the application of community law is still not sufficiently transparent. the rapporteur therefore believes that a regulation on the administrative procedure of the union administration could be useful and easily enacted. it also considered that parliament could and should play a more structured role in analysing the way in which the applicant countries and the countries which have concluded association agreements with the european union comply with eu law and in developing appropriate support in this area for these countries. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ this report shows that the environment, transport, the internal market and services are the areas where most infringement cases remained pending in 2014. it also stresses that the number of formal infringement proceedings has decreased over the past five years. according to the commission, this decrease reflects the effectiveness of the dialogue with the member states in the context of the eu pilot procedure. however, the european parliament still has relatively limited access to information on this procedure and on ongoing proceedings. one conclusion that can be drawn from the report is that the application of community law is still not sufficiently transparent. parliament could and should play a more structured role in examining how the applicant countries and the countries which have concluded association agreements with the eu comply with eu law and in developing appropriate support in this area for these countries.
‒ this is the 32nd annual report produced by the commission on monitoring the application of european union law. the report finds that sectors such as the environment, transport, the internal market and services are those with the highest number of infringement cases pending, although the volume of cases has decreased over the past five years. this may be due to the effectiveness of the eu pilot informal pre-litigation phase procedure, although there is some difficulty in confirming whether its use has an effective reflection in a greater and better compliance with eu law by member states. this means that there is still a lack of transparency in the application of community law and in this respect i support the solution proposed within the juri committee to create a regulation on the administrative procedure of the union's administration as a way of promoting a better and more effective transposition and practical application of european law. i voted in favour of the report because i agree with its content.
‒ this annual report monitors the application of european union law by the european institutions. it is the responsibility of the commission, as guardian of the treaties, article 17 teu, to monitor whether or not states apply the treaties and union law. we do not recognise financial sanctions against states. look at what is happening now with portugal. we are against the commission's monitoring role and the discriminatory nature of its assessments of whether or not community law is being applied correctly. that is never more than political appraisals, as you can see.
in writing. ‒ the draft commission implementing decision exceeds the implementing powers provided for in directive 2001/18/ec and the risk assessment of the crop carried out by efsa is incomplete and the risk management recommendations proposed by the commission are inadequate. the draft commission implementing decision is not in accordance with union law on the protection of human health and the environment when deliberate releases of genetically modified organisms into the environment are made for any purpose other than placing on the market. i agree to withdraw the draft implementing decision.
‒ once again, the exception has become the rule as regards the procedures of this authorisation decision. the genetically modified event bt11 maize expresses the cry1ab protein, which is a protein (derived from bacillus thuringiensis subsp. kurstaki) that confers resistance to european maize pitch (ostrinia nubilalis) and mediterranean maize pitch (sesamia nonagrioides), and the pat protein, which confers tolerance to the glufosinate-ammonium herbicide. there was no consensus among the member states, so, according to the perverse legislative framework in place, the decision falls in the hands of the european commission which invariably takes a pro-gmo stance, even in the absence of long-term food toxicity studies and in the face of insufficient risk assessment. reasons which have been the basis for the refusal (or abstention) of several member states. this resolution objects to the authorization of this genetically modified organism (gmo). we voted in favour. it is necessary and urgent to amend the current legislative framework in order to respect the right of each member state not to want gmos on its territory for food and/or cultivation, for reasons of food sovereignty, the environment, biodiversity and public health.

in writing. - i voted against this report, following the indication of my group, which advocated opposition to the commission's decision concerning the placing on the market for cultivation of genetically modified maize seeds designated bt11 (syn btø11-1) (d046173/01). in the scientific opinion adopted in may 2015, the european food safety authority (efsa) stated that the existing data are insufficient to place the larval mortality linked to bt maize in the context of the overall mortality. however, in july 2016, the commission requested efsa to assess by the end of september 2016 whether, on the basis of existing scientific literature and other relevant information, new data have emerged that could change the conclusions and recommendations set out in the scientific opinions on the planting of the genetically modified maize varieties. since no comments were received from easa in the light of what had been previously reported, i do not see any reason to reject the commission's decision, subject, in the light of the principle of prudence, to appropriate amendments if new elements arise which justify this.

madam president, the nuclear agreement with iran is decisive, as we all hope, for regional and global security and non-proliferation, the result of historic negotiations in which european and american diplomacy have been engaged. a new page has thus been opened in eu-iran relations which cannot be overridden by the need for dialogue in an area where the european and iranian authorities maintain substantial differences on respect for human rights, including women's rights, the use and abuse of the death penalty and other degrading treatment. this dialogue is not useless, it must be frank, vigorous and creative: it must not fall apart in the face of a government which is under pressure from within by a young, educated society eager to reintegrate into the international community. economic and trade opportunities are also enabling greater exchange between the european and iranian peoples. the lifting of sanctions against iran opens the iranian market to european companies and investment. however, iran still needs to commit and invest in complying with the recommendations of the international financial action task force to create a transparent and accountable economic environment. but let us be clear: to restrict the euro-iranian relationship to economic and commercial objectives is to fail strategically. iran is a regional power that should be encouraged to play a role in resolving conflicts and not in aggravating them. iran can help end the war in neighboring syria, but today it fights alongside russia to preserve the tyrant assad at the expense of the slaughtered syrian people. the european union should use a new relationship with iran and other regional actors to deter the sunni-shiite sectarian confrontation fuelled by saudi arabia, qatar and erdogan's turkey. a solution that gives peace and a future to the syrians and all the peoples in the region is the only way for europe and iran to protect their own security.
mr president, commissioner, about a year ago a historic agreement was reached with iran which represented a milestone in the fight against nuclear proliferation and an important step towards making the world a safer place. with the lifting of economic and financial sanctions related to iran's nuclear programme, europe has sought to seize the opportunities of a market of 80 million people, even if it has to turn a blind eye to the constant human rights violations of the dictatorial regime of the ayatollahs. but if it is true that europe is doing everything it can to take advantage of these opportunities, it is equally true that the expansion of institutional and trade relations must be strictly conditional on the progress made by iran in the field of human rights. i therefore believe that the motion for a resolution on iran which was voted this month by the committee on foreign affairs of the european parliament does not reflect this conditionality and maintains an unacceptable business-as-usual stance against an oppressive regime which systematically manipulates the democratic process, has a dismal record of human rights violations, is the world leader in executions per capita and of persons under the age of 18 and is a repressor of women and religious minorities. for all this, mr howitt, i feel it is our duty to ensure that this resolution does not become a mere political propaganda tool for the theocratic regime in tehran, which, being a regime which needs this level of violence to repress its own citizens, shows great weaknesses in order to become a true, credible and reliable diplomatic and economic partner for the european union. ladies and gentlemen, human rights are not negotiable, they are part of our collective responsibility as human beings and europeans!

in writing. this report, on which i worked as a shadow rapporteur on behalf of the s&d group, is a clearly progressive report, which seeks to respond to the challenges posed in the field of human rights by the transnationalisation of business activity, including european companies, for which we obviously have an increased responsibility. it called for human rights clauses to be systematically included in trade agreements between the eu and third countries. it calls for the worldwide implementation of the un guiding principles on business and human rights. the eu is also calling for a stronger commitment to the binding international treaty being negotiated at the un. it stressed that multinationals should be held legally accountable whenever their operations in third countries result in human rights abuses and that they have a duty to compensate the victims of such abuses. it includes highly relevant recommendations, such as the creation of an eu certificate for products whose production has not involved human rights abuses. at my suggestion, the report states that such a certificate discriminates positively against companies, enabling them to benefit. in short, this excellent report presents very valid ideas and proposals to counter some of the negative effects of globalisation and deserves, in my view, the support of this house.
mr president, commissioner, i would like to thank mr gyürk for his work on this very important strategy and, as rapporteur for the opinion in the committee on transport, i obviously could not miss this opportunity to mention the importance of liquefied natural gas for maritime transport and for heavy vehicles as an alternative fuel. it is essential to create a network of supply and storage infrastructure, but not excluding the maritime ports of the islands, as referred to in the alternative fuels directive. the solution also involves the construction of small-scale infrastructure and the use of regular cabotage vessels. that is why, as also mentioned in this report, i proposed the creation of a joint project for blue lng corridors to the islands, the outermost regions of the atlantic, in particular madeira and the azores, and to make it possible to adapt ports, work on sea links and the conversion of ships. i therefore ask the commissioner to pay particular attention to this project, which is of interest to portugal but also to the european union, and to commit himself to supporting and providing funds for its implementation.
mr president, mr commissioner, liquefied natural gas is a very important component in ensuring energy diversification and security and in supporting a sustainable transition to a model based on renewable and clean energy. i was a rapporteur in the envi committee and the opinion stresses the optimisation of existing networks, the importance of supporting the energy transition and, in particular, decarbonising heavy transport and maritime transport. this strategy must be in line with the paris agreement and it is very important to use lng for this transport, maritime and heavy transport issue. i would therefore like to stress the recommendation in this report that the azores archipelago, because of its geographical location, should have a fuelling station for transatlantic shipping routes and it is also very important that the european commission should provide for the financing of such projects in its various financing instruments.

madam president, mr timmermans, ladies and gentlemen, respect for the rule of law is a basic principle of the european union, we demand it as a condition for joining the union, it is one of the copenhagen criteria. but we are less effective in ensuring this once a member state becomes a member state of the european union and we know that in many states this principle is going through difficult times. it is true that we have article 7 of the treaty on european union, but this is a limiting situation and we have a set of mechanisms in parliament, the european commission and the council which are of little consequence and have no coherence. the initiative we are discussing today is therefore a good step in the right direction, calling for integrated action by the three institutions. but we are still taking the first steps in what will certainly be a long process. i congratulate rapporteur sophia in t veld and the epp shadow rapporteur frank engel, among others, for their commitment and work, but let us be clear from the outset that this is not an exercise in bureaucracy, it is not an attack on the sovereignty of the member states, it is certainly not against any people. protecting the rule of law means defending each and every european citizen, each and every one of the nationalities that make up this union. it is to reaffirm that the union is not just an economic construct but that it has values and knows how to preserve and defend them.

‒ decision 2008/615/jha on the strengthening of crossborder cooperation substantially incorporates the prüm treaty into the community legal order, while maintaining the objective of encouraging greater cooperation between the security forces of the member states, in particular through greater exchange of information. as i have said on several occasions, this exchange of information is essential in the field of security, as is the requirement for a result of greater mutual trust. certain requirements must therefore be met, in particular the principles of necessity and proportionality and respect for fundamental rights. therefore, in order for the automated exchange of dna data to take place, each member state should ensure that data protection standards are implemented. this council decision rightly authorizes the start of the automated exchange, since denmark has successfully implemented it.
‒ following the entry into force of the treaty (signed between belgium, germany, spain, france, luxembourg, the netherlands and austria) on the deepening of crossborder cooperation, in particular in the field of combating terrorism, crossborder crime and illegal migration the so-called prum treaty, a decision (2008/615/jha) was adopted by the council in 2008 with the aim of incorporating the content of the prum treaty into the eu legal framework. the report on the automated exchange of dna data in denmark fits into this framework and the serious security measures that have been implemented under the cover of the so-called 'fight against terrorism', involving serious risks to the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. the framework for police cooperation, joint operations, mutual assistance and even the possibility of police services from one member state operating in the territory of another member state, as well as the exchange of a very large amount of information, including personal data, are at stake. we proposed amendments - rejected by the majority - which aimed to prohibit the processing of personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, party or trade union affiliation, or relating to health or sex life. we voted against it.

‒ to cross the external border of the european union, third-country nationals need to be in possession of a visa, in this case for a short stay. however, many countries are already exempt from this obligation, as they meet a set of criteria approved in 2001 and 2014 by the european parliament and the council, including respect for fundamental rights, the security of the visa system or the risk of illegal immigration. the visa exemption in this case, however, only applies to holders of diplomatic passports. it is up to the european parliament to give its approval to the agreement, which is given. i am voting in favour of concluding this agreement with the people's republic of china.
‒ china is one of the countries whose nationals must be visa-holders when travelling to the schengen area. eu citizens also need a visa to enter china. the council adopted a decision authorising the commission to open negotiations and to address the negotiating directives for the conclusion of an agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union holding valid eu diplomatic or free-transit passports and for chinese nationals holding diplomatic passports travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the abolition of visas will reduce the waiting time in front of consulates and the costs associated with travel. it will facilitate people-to-people contact - an essential condition for the stable development of economic, cultural and scientific links, as well as other links, as it intensifies people-to-people contact.
‒ in accordance with council regulation (ec) no 539/2001, china is one of the countries whose nationals must be visa-holders when travelling to the schengen area. citizens of eu member states also need a visa to enter china. in addition, the visa information system (vis) officially became operational on 12 october 2015 in china. since then, all applicants from china must provide their biometric data when applying for a schengen visa. in this context, on 14 september 2015, the council adopted a decision authorising the european commission to open negotiations and to address negotiating directives for the conclusion of an agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the member states of the european union holding valid eu diplomatic or free-transit passports and for chinese nationals holding diplomatic passports travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. we voted in favour.

‒ the economic and financial crisis has put a heavy strain on national economies and member states have adopted adjustment measures to balance their budgets. with the pressure on national budgets, it may be difficult for countries in budgetary difficulties to have sufficient resources for national co-financing of regional policy projects. in this regard, the amendments to regulation no 1303/2013 provide for the granting of aid to member states experiencing temporary budgetary difficulties. the objective is to increase payments to a member state under an adjustment programme by applying a 10 percentage point top-up to the co-financing rates applicable to the priorities of the programmes. it is also proposed to change the period during which the country receives financial assistance and is eligible for additional payments. for the period 2014-2020, the commission proposed that the eligibility of a member state should continue until 30 june of the year following the calendar year in which the member state ceases to receive financial assistance. the increase in co-financing will have a positive effect on the economies of the member states concerned, which will be able to mobilise more resources to complement investment efforts. i therefore support this report.
‒ the economic and financial crisis has put pressure on national economies and member states to adopt austerity measures to balance their budgets. in this context, it is important to ensure the proper implementation of the eu's main funding instrument, the european structural and investment funds (esif). with national budgets under pressure, it may be difficult for countries in budgetary difficulties to find sufficient resources for national co-financing of regional policy projects. the legislation clearly indicates that the commission would carry out a review before 30 june 2016 and that if the economic situation of the countries concerned so requires, the deadline for providing additional support would be extendable. the commission has put forward a legislative proposal to the european parliament and the council on this extension, which i agree with as a precise and budget-neutral solution to the temporary liquidity problems facing two member states.
‒ the economic and financial crisis, as a result of the implementation of eu policies, has put in question the ability of states to meet the requirements for co-financing of the structural and investment funds, which are, moreover, the only (insufficient) driver of economic and social investment in most of these countries. in this context, at the request of a member state, interim payments may be increased by 10 percentage points above the co-financing rate applicable to each priority for the european regional development fund (erdf), the european social fund (esf), the cohesion fund, the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) and the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff). the measure is identical to that already adopted for the countries receiving troika assistance. it now applies exclusively to greece and cyprus. we voted in favour, although we think that this measure could be extended to other countries. of course, this is a mere palliative measure which does not resolve the fundamental question of the constraints which prevent adequate investment flows into these countries. these constraints - which it is increasingly necessary to remove - are linked to the policies and instruments of subjugation of states by the eu, of which the euro and the economic and monetary union are the most striking examples.
‒ this report supports the commission's proposal to amend the regulation on the financial management of member states in serious difficulties with regard to their financial stability as a budgetary neutral solution to the temporary liquidity problems faced by the two member states, greece and cyprus. to the extent that national budgets are under strain, it becomes difficult, if not impossible, for countries with budgetary difficulties to find sufficient funds for national co-financing of regional policy projects. for these reasons and with the proposed regulations, the commission will be allowed to increase payments under esif programmes to countries which are in economic difficulties. i voted yes.
‒ the prolonged financial and economic crisis has put pressure on national financial resources as member states adopt the necessary fiscal consolidation policies. in this context, ensuring the good implementation of programmes supported by the european structural and investment funds (esif) is of particular importance for investment in growth and jobs. this proposal will allow the commission to continue to make higher payments to member states benefiting from financial assistance after 30 june 2016 for as long as they benefit from this support mechanism, without changing the overall allocation of the esi funds in 2014-2020. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ the defence of the independence of the mandate of a member of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and that independence cannot be called into question. in the present case, during a radio programme, mr mario borghezio was asked to comment on the appointment and competence of a new member of the italian government, namely the new minister for integration. the statements allegedly made exceed the tone generally used in a political debate and, moreover, are of a nature profoundly contrary to the parliamentary character. the statements are contrary to article 21 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and therefore cannot be considered to have been made in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. i therefore vote in favour of the waiver of mario borghezio's immunity.

‒ mario borghezio has requested the defence of his parliamentary immunity in the criminal case pending before the court of milan. during the radio programme in question, mario borghezio was asked to comment on the appointment and powers of a new member of the italian government, namely the new minister for integration. opinions were expressed regarding the national political situation, which included the advocacy of ideas of racial superiority, the advocacy of racial or ethnic hatred, the conscious and free dissemination of racist and xenophobic views, and the promotion of discrimination. these statements have no direct and obvious connection with your parliamentary activities. they are also statements contrary to article 21 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the committee's assessment, which we are following, does not support the immunity, because it concludes that the statements made cannot be considered to have been made in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. we do not agree with the criticism in the report to the milan court that, under community law, the case should have been suspended, because we believe that it is a sovereign body which should not be subject to any decision of the european court of justice, a supranational body which we do not recognise. we voted in favour.
‒ the italian public prosecutor's office has requested the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mario borghezio, member of the european parliament, in the context of the opening of an investigation procedure concerning an alleged offence. the action is brought on the basis of a speech he gave on a radio programme in which he defended ideas based on racial hatred and racial superiority. given that the judicial procedure does not concern opinions or votes cast in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament and that there is no reason to believe that the intention underlying the judicial action is to prejudice the political activity of the member, this request, which i voted in favour of, decides to waive the immunity of mario borghezio.
