‒ this report concerns the request for defence of parliamentary immunity requested by mario borghezio mep following a criminal action brought against him before the court of milan for advocating ideas based on superiority and racial hatred during a radio programme, which is likely to constitute a crime, punishable under italian law. in view of the content of the report, the statements made by the mep concern allegedly discriminatory opinions, contrary to what should constitute the parliamentary spirit and to what is enshrined in article 21 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and cannot be considered to have been made in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. in view of the foregoing, i do not think that the maintenance of his parliamentary immunity is justifiable in this particular case, although i should regret the failure of the milan court to suspend the proceedings against the member, contrary to the established case law of the court of justice on this matter, hoping that this is an isolated case and will not be repeated in the future.
‒ parliamentary immunity is intended to guarantee the right to freedom of expression enjoyed in principle by members of the european parliament. however, this right does not mean that they may defame, slander, incite hatred or make defamatory allegations. the complaint in question relates to the fact that mr borghezio defended ideas based on racial or ethnic superiority and hatred during a radio programme. since statements made by members of the european parliament outside the premises of the european parliament cannot be considered as being made in the exercise of their duties, we support the decision not to uphold the privileges and immunities of mr borghezio.
‒ the objective of this report is to amend regulation no 91/2003 with a view to updating, simplifying and optimising the existing regulatory framework for european rail transport statistics. i support this recommendation for second reading because the creation of a genuine european internal market in transport is fundamental to the revitalization of the railway sector which will help to make rail freight and passenger services more competitive and attractive and to increase its annual transport share. to develop and monitor the common transport policy, the european commission needs detailed statistical data on rail freight and passenger transport. two memoranda of understanding were signed to this end: one between eurostat and the european commission and the other between eurostat and the european railway agency. these two memoranda are important for optimising the use of existing information and reducing the administrative burden, and also meet the requirements of the co-legislators as regards the better use of rail transport statistics. these statistics will enable all categories of users to have easy and reliable access to data on the progress of european policies in the rail sector.
‒ the european parliament decided that the scope of the regulation on rail transport statistics should be extended to include data on infrastructure, in particular on the deployment of the european rail traffic management system (ertms), because it considered it imperative to have a clear vision of the development of this system in the european union, given that the european union has spent millions of euros in financing this type of infrastructure without any concrete result, so far, in terms of the operability of the system across europe, due to irregular deployment and delays. parliament also decided that eurostat should provide statistical data on barrier-free stations accessible to people with reduced mobility and to people with disabilities, and on the use of crossborder railway infrastructure. parliament believes it is of the utmost importance that eu citizens have easy access - as a one-stop shop - to data relating to the implementation of eu policies. i voted in favour.
‒ this is an essentially technical text (although it cannot be isolated from a given context and policy options) on the communication of information on rail transport by member states to the commission, as regards goods, passengers and accidents, allowing a supranational analysis of the sector also in comparison with other means of transport and making the european rail system operational, following the 4th railway package. recognising that the exchange of statistical information could help the development of rail systems and that, when issues such as privacy are assured, it is an acceptable (or even desirable) issue, the context in which it is proposed here deserves our repudiation, with successive railway packages being the main instrument of eu policy that has promoted the privatisation and total disorganisation of the companies responsible for rail transport; that has promoted the deregulation of labour and increased labour exploitation in the sector; that has resulted in the increase of user charges and the degradation of infrastructure and reduced rail safety. the document contains references which are in line with this policy and the centralising options underlying it, such as the strengthening of the role and action of the european railway agency in the field of safety.
‒ the main objective of the european union's transport policy is to create an internal market by promoting common policies that encourage a high level of competitiveness and the harmonious, balanced and sustainable development of economic activities. the creation of a genuine internal market is essential for the revitalisation of the railway sector and will contribute to making rail freight and passenger services more competitive and attractive and increasing their modal share of transport. the objective of this proposal is therefore to amend regulation (ec) no 91/2003 in order to update, simplify and optimise the existing regulatory framework for european rail transport statistics and to bring that regulation into line with the new institutional context. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. ‒ although customs legislation is fully harmonised and is the exclusive competence of the union, the imposition of penalties for infringements is within the framework of the national law of the member states, with 28 different sets of legal rules and different administrative traditions, i.e. member states may impose the penalties they deem appropriate for infringements of certain obligations arising from the union's harmonised customs legislation. the new directive aims to harmonise this implementation framework so that there is an integrated approach to the enforcement of customs rules, which is also a consequence of the external obligations to which the eu is bound under the general agreement on customs tariffs. i support the kallas report, which i believe has achieved a balanced approach in this matter, respecting the principle of subsidiarity, pursuing a logic of proportionality of sanctions, avoiding the criterion based on the value of goods. this will ensure greater legal certainty and transparency for operators, reduce the risk of market distortion and ensure greater convergence in the member states' sanctioning systems.
‒ although the customs union is regarded as one of the foundations of the european union and the backbone of the single market, there is still no integrated approach to the enforcement of customs legislation, including sanctions. this means that the rules are the same but, when these rules are broken, the penalties applied vary considerably. if differences between member states' sanctioning systems persist, this could potentially mean that an undertaking may lose the status of authorised economic operator in a particular country while another undertaking operating in another member state will not lose that status for the same infringement. this report therefore clarifies the scope of the directive to ensure that only infringements committed by negligence or intentionally constitute infringements, thus removing the element of strict liability that does not require a degree of fault.
the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. at present, there is still no integrated approach to the enforcement of customs legislation, including sanctions. this means that although the rules are the same, the penalties applied as a result of infringement of the rules vary between member states. this may mean that an undertaking may lose its status as an authorised economic operator in a particular country while another undertaking operating in another member state will not lose its status for the same infringement. our position is inseparable from the position we took earlier in the assembly of the republic in the process of scrutiny and verification of the principle of subsidiarity by the national parliaments. we consider that the proposal violates the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, which is why we voted against it.

in the light of the commission's proposal for a directive published on 13 december, the amendment of the union legal framework on infringements of customs legislation and the penalties for those infringements is under discussion. although the customs union is considered to be a major pillar of the single market and one of the foundations of the european union (eu), there is still no integrated approach to the enforcement of customs legislation, including sanctions. since the customs union and trade policy are exclusive competences of the eu, only the eu can develop a common approach to the application of customs legislation. the differences in the level of sanctions create a lack of mutual trust between administrations and compromise the level playing field for eu economic operators. they have been regarded by the court of justice as measures having an effect equivalent to equitable restrictions. for the reasons i have mentioned, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the idea that it is imperative that in identical cases of infringement of customs rules the penalties should also be identical. the differences between the sanctioning systems of the member states create a lack of mutual trust between administrations, whereas trust and cooperation between customs authorities is central to the good management of the customs union and to the protection of the eu's financial interests. they also compromise the level playing field for economic operators in the european union. in order to ensure that penalties are effective, proportionate and dissuasive, it is appropriate to leave sufficient scope for the customs authorities to assess the relevant circumstances and, on that basis, to decide on the most appropriate penalty, as this has proven to be an effective means of reducing non-compliance.

‒ the fight against organised crime has been a priority for the european union from the very beginning. it is a necessary part of judicial and police cooperation in criminal matters, which has its origins in the schengen agreement and in free movement. it is also clear that, particularly in the last 15 years, organised crime has taken on a new dimension, among other things, it has become more cross-border, it makes greater use of new technologies. this resolution, which i support and vote in favour of, is the result of the work that parliament has been doing in this area since 2011. new problems are being identified, for example in the area of misuse of funds, but also new avenues, particularly in the area of environmental crime.
‒ the adoption of a european action plan to eradicate organised crime, corruption and money laundering must be a priority for the eu, which, to be effective, must have adequate financial resources and qualified staff. the fight against fraud, corruption and money laundering should be a political priority of the union institutions and, for this reason, police and judicial cooperation between member states is essential. i voted in favour.
‒ this is a report on the fight against fraud, corruption and money laundering, covering sectors such as counterfeiting, drug trafficking, gambling and addiction to sports results, tax havens, environmental crimes, cybercrime, organised crime and terrorism, and trafficking in human beings and migrants. in general terms, this report considers that police and judicial cooperation between member states should be a political priority for the eu. while we agree that it is imperative to combat the types of crime mentioned above, we disagree in substance with the approach adopted in the report and the solutions proposed, without prejudice to specific specific measures which may be appropriate. the report omits something that would be unexpected - the intimate relationship between the capitalist system, the policies that support it and the whole of the crime phenomena mentioned. the alternative is to further integrate the judiciary and police, areas that are at the heart of the sovereignty and independence of states, with further steps to cut off parts of that sovereignty, in order to concentrate power in the supranational structures of the eu, controlled by the great powers and serving reactionary and backward agendas that restrict rights, freedoms and guarantees.
‒ this report follows the resolution adopted in october 2013 on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the report provides recommendations on measures and initiatives to be taken in the areas of transparency, environmental aspects of corruption, better communication between judicial authorities, the need to address the exploitation of migrant labour, enhanced protection of witnesses and whistleblowers, as well as other relevant issues in this context. however, the establishment of mandatory rules so that people accused of a crime or public offence cannot run for public office after serving their sentence is a pernicious argument. in that case, people like nelson mandela could never come to power. i abstained.
in writing. ‒ a stronger eu commitment is required to achieve better results in the fight against corruption. the development of a genuine priority prevention strategy to combat corruption requires the intensification of police and judicial cooperation through the exchange of information between national authorities, greater attention to public procurement and public-private partnerships, whether by combating corruption in sport, criminalising the manipulation of sporting events and strengthening the fight against illegal betting in the field of sporting competitions; regulation of lobbying and its relationship with official bodies; awareness of the availability of new tools for organised crime; the emergence of new phenomena of organised crime, particularly of an economic nature, using cross-border associations, which requires the provision of the technological, logistical, technical and financial means necessary to combat them in an articulated manner between member states. it is now up to the european commission to develop a legislative proposal in line with the european parliament's strong call to fight corruption and organised crime. i voted in favour.
‒ organized crime has a transnational dimension and covers various types of criminal activity, such as drug trafficking, smuggling of migrants, money laundering and trafficking in counterfeit goods, firearms, wildlife and cultural goods. the 2030 agenda for sustainable development recognises the need to combat corruption in all its forms and calls on member states to eliminate illicit financial flows, bribery and corruption, and to establish effective, accountable and transparent institutions. i believe that the eu must impose strong political will in the fight against tax evasion and tax planning, in accordance with the principle of policy coherence for development, enshrined in article 208 tfeu. it is essential that developing countries strengthen transparency and accountability in resource contracts, audits and financial reporting of companies, as well as in the collection and allocation of revenues, as part of their anti-corruption agenda. the eu should step up its assistance to resource-rich countries in implementing the principles of the extractive industries transparency initiative.
in writing. ‒ the report is based on fair values such as the fight against fraud, corruption and money laundering, covering sectors such as counterfeiting, drug trafficking, gambling and addiction to sports results, tax havens, environmental crimes, cybercrime, organised crime and terrorism, and organised crime and trafficking in human beings and migrants. however, it transforms police and judicial cooperation between member states into a deepening of a federalist and security vision, pursuing the policies of the european union in this field. the call for increased specialisation of europol and greater use of agencies such as eurojust, cepol and the european judicial training network is therefore justified. the pnr register, which we rejected and voted against, is valid, as is the enhancement and increased capacity of the european public prosecutor's office, another supranational instrument which we do not follow, in that it contributes to the loss of the sovereignty of the member states in the field of justice. i therefore vote against.
in writing. on 25 october 2011, the european parliament (ep) adopted a report on organised crime, following which a special committee was set up to analyse organised crime in europe. the outcome of that special committee was a report which was adopted by the ep in october 2013 and which is followed up by this report. organised crime is a global threat and therefore requires a joint and coordinated response by the eu and its member states. it is therefore necessary for all member states to ensure the proper transposition of the provisions in force, to monitor their application and to assess their effectiveness. the rapporteur notes that the phenomena of organised crime, corruption and money laundering often have a cross-border dimension, and that more effective police and judicial cooperation is therefore needed at european level. corruption, in particular in the field of public procurement and public-private partnerships, provides privileged channels for organised crime to infiltrate the legal economy. i am voting in favour because i believe that the current political cycle must include among its priorities the fight against money laundering, corruption and human trafficking.
‒ i voted in favour, as there is still no full awareness of the complexity of the phenomenon of organised crime and the danger of criminal organisations infiltrating the social, economic, business, political and institutional fabric of the member states. organised criminal groups have shown a tendency and a great facility to diversify their activities, adapting to different territorial, economic and social contexts, and taking advantage of their weaknesses and vulnerabilities, operating simultaneously in different markets and exploiting the disparity between the legislative provisions of the legal systems of the member states to flourish their activities and maximise profits. organised crime, corruption and money laundering pose serious threats to the eu economy, significantly reducing tax revenues for member states and the eu as a whole, as well as to the reliability of eu-funded projects, as criminal organisations operate in a number of sectors, many of which are subject to government control.
‒ this resolution reiterates the ideas and recommendations set out in its resolution of 23 october 2013 on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. it reiterated its call for the adoption of a european action plan to eradicate organised crime, corruption and money laundering, which, in order to be effective, must have adequate financial resources and qualified staff. expresses its wish to focus its attention on specific areas requiring priority action in the current context: - ensuring the proper transposition of the existing provisions, monitoring their application and evaluating their effectiveness; - priorities and operational framework for the fight against organised crime and corruption; - a more robust legislative framework; - more effective police and judicial cooperation at european level; - to seize the assets of criminal organisations and to encourage their reuse for social purposes; - preventing the infiltration of organised crime and corruption into the legal economy; - the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office; - specific areas of intervention (counterfeiting, drug trafficking, tax havens, crimes against the environment, cybercrime, organised crime and terrorism).
‒ this own-initiative report by mrs laura ferrara concerns the fight against corruption and the follow-up to the resolution of the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. we all know that corruption and organised crime are universal and constitute a global threat to the security of citizens, territories and the social, economic, political and institutional fabric of different countries, requiring a concerted response by the eu and the member states. it is against this backdrop of fragility that i strongly support the proposals in this report on what should be the eu's priorities and the operational framework for the fight against organised crime and corruption, as well as for the implementation of a more robust and effective legislative framework and more competent and effective police and judicial cooperation at european level. a word of appreciation for the idea of seizing the assets of criminal organisations and encouraging their reuse for social purposes, as well as for the idea of creating a european public prosecutor's office independent of national governments and european institutions.
‒ this is a report on the fight against fraud, corruption and money laundering, covering sectors such as counterfeiting, drug trafficking, gambling and addiction to sports results, tax havens, environmental crimes, cybercrime, organised crime and terrorism, and organised crime and trafficking in human beings and migrants. in general terms, this report considers that police and judicial cooperation between member states should be a political priority for the european union. we agree with the principle that greater cooperation between states is needed to combat these phenomena, but we do not share the trend which, on the one hand, centralises the fight against them in supranational structures and, on the other, does not call into question the effects of the policies of liberalization in progress, particularly at the level of the financial system and the capital market.
‒ the european union is committed to solidarity with all those who are forced to leave their country by armed conflict, political persecution, human rights violations and extreme poverty. the rights of migrants, whether in transit or in destination, must be respected. i share the concern about the situation of stateless people and the need for greater efficiency in their identification and protection. i believe that the mechanisms for granting asylum should be more rapid, more effective and more concerted. in this respect, i am in favour of sharing good practice between national administrations, training of officials and a balanced system of information exchange. member states should comply with international law obligations and european commitments in this area. i share the concern for specific segments such as women and children. the fight against all forms of violence (especially sexual violence) must be a priority, as must the fight against human trafficking and slavery. i believe that the issue of migration should be taken into account in the eu's external policy, in particular in its neighbourhood policy, in eu-acp relations and in development aid. i therefore support this report.
‒ migration is a global and multidimensional phenomenon, which has its origins in a variety of causes, such as economic conditions, social and political conditions, working conditions, situations of violence, the security situation, the gradual degradation of the environment and the worsening of natural disasters. today, some 244 million people are considered international migrants. i therefore support taking measures to combat networks of smuggling of migrants, creating legal and safe pathways, including through humanitarian corridors, for people seeking international protection, establishing permanent and mandatory resettlement programmes and granting humanitarian visas to people fleeing conflict zones, improving the functioning of 'registration centres' and entry points at the union's external borders and creating effective tools for coordination, aligning information flows, data collection, cross-checking and analysis.

in writing. ‒ according to the united nations, some 244 million people are currently considered international migrants. migration should be seen as a global and multidimensional phenomenon, with a variety of causes at its origin, such as economic conditions (including changes in the distribution of wealth and regional and global economic integration), social and political conditions, working conditions, situations of violence and, of course, the security situation. i believe that this phenomenon must be dealt with in a coherent and balanced way, in accordance with a global perspective which takes account of its human dimension. i express my solidarity with people who are forced to leave their country because of conflict, persecution, human rights violations and situations of extreme poverty. i also express my deep concern at the serious human rights violations to which many migrants are subject in the countries of transit or destination. however, i do not think that this report contains the most appropriate provisions to deal with this phenomenon. i therefore do not vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the protection of the fundamental rights of workers or of all those who are involved in the production chain in any way is an obligation of the union and all its member states, whether in the eu or outside it. at the international level, i welcome the adoption of the un guiding principles, but i stress the importance of work towards the conclusion of a binding un treaty on business and human rights. the eu has a key role to play in this context, such as in including concerns on this matter in its trade agreements. i see the instruments based on corporate social responsibility (csr) as a way of defending human rights in third countries, and i therefore advocate that they be strengthened and that they take account of the specific nature of small and medium-sized enterprises. we must look for greater efficiency and not an overload of bureaucratic rules. i believe that responsibility is not only legal but also moral, and i therefore support the existence of effective remedies for human rights violations in third countries by european companies. i am pleased to note the concern about the labelling of 'conflict minerals'. i therefore support this report.
‒ an identification label indicating respect for human rights throughout the production chain of a product is one of the proposals in the european parliament's own-initiative report on corporate responsibility for serious human rights violations in third countries. the european union is a champion of human rights, and legislation that would oblige european companies to respect human rights abroad would send a strong message to the world. the report builds on the un guiding principles on business and human rights, focusing on respect for human rights in all chains of production, distribution and exploitation of natural resources in third countries, especially in developing countries. i voted in favour.
‒ the report addresses one of the problems that currently marks the crisis of capitalism and the crisis in and of the european union: the humanitarian crisis and the gross violations of rights on european soil. the report has a number of positive points, but it also reveals shortcomings and is compromised by a set of negative references which the right and social democrats would impose, although not to the extent they would like. the result of the vote is that. the causes of the problems and the direct and indirect responsibilities at their origin are omitted. the eu, with the us and nato, is responsible for destabilising the whole of the middle east and north africa, fuelling the extremist groups, which now, in the name of the fight against 'terrorism', claim to be fighting. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. it welcomes the euronavfor med mission and its role in combating the smuggling of migrants and calls for these missions to be stepped up. we strongly disagree with this analysis because of the criminal reality it portrays, which is imbued with the eu's security vision. the positive elements contained in it and its origin justify abstention.
in writing. ‒ the eu is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities, and its action on the international stage (including trade policy) is based on these principles. businesses are a key player in economic globalisation, financial services and international trade, and are required to respect all applicable legislation and international treaties in force, and to respect human rights. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ addressing a pertinent and fair question, the report starts from the mistaken premise that capitalism can be humanized. it is the nature of the capitalist system, its predatory and exploitative aspect, that is the root of the problem. the big companies and multinationals exploit, directly or indirectly, in the name of profit and greedily, the natural resources of the peoples of third countries, without any qualms about committing the most heinous environmental crimes against the population or inhumanely exploiting workers. it is not surprising that references to the need for greater workers' rights, the regulation of work, a better distribution of wealth, or the sovereign role of the states in protecting workers, peoples and resources from the exploitation of big monopoly capital have been overlooked or are nonexistent. the need for trade policies which are not new neo-colonial instruments, but which respect the sovereignty of states and are based on genuine mutual benefit between equal parties, is also absent. we value the references and the call for the application of the un guiding principles on business and human rights and the un global compact, principles which the practice of eu policies escapes, because their class nature is contrary to it. i therefore abstain.
in writing. ‒ i am concerned about the human rights violations committed by companies worldwide, as they are a major player in economic globalisation, financial services and international trade and must be required to respect all applicable legislation and international treaties in force. the business community must not only respect human rights but also have an important role in providing incentives to promote them, as well as democracy, environmental standards and social responsibility. because the eu is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and human rights, and because companies must follow the same values, i support this motion for a resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the view that human rights violations by companies are a matter of concern worldwide and that all companies in the world have a duty to respect human rights, while the european institutions have a primary duty to regulate the liability of companies with an eu link. unfortunately, corporate human rights violations are ongoing and there remains a lack of a comprehensive holistic approach to corporate responsibility for human rights violations. the eu has in turn played a leading role in negotiating and implementing a number of global responsibility initiatives, which are linked to the promotion and respect of international standards.
‒there is still no comprehensive holistic approach to corporate responsibility for human rights violations. companies should adopt, support and implement a set of core values in human rights, labour standards, the environment and the fight against corruption, committing to these values and integrating them into their business activities on a voluntary basis. businesses are the main agents of economic globalisation and are required to respect all applicable legislation and treaties in force. trade and human rights can be mutually reinforcing. european companies operating within the eu and in third countries must set an example in respecting human rights.
‒ the increasing globalisation and internationalisation of business activities and supply chains, in addition to making the role of labour rights more important, brings with it increased responsibilities in respecting human rights, and the creation of standards, rules and cooperation at international level is absolutely crucial to this end. this report proposes measures to ensure respect for human rights and to prevent their violation in third countries as a result of any management decisions by companies, individuals, non-state actors or governmental entities in the european union, recalling the responsibilities these entities have in carrying out their operations. two of the proposals listed, with which i agree, state that: trade agreements are fundamental to strengthening the world trading system, based on values that are above all respect for human dignity; and that trade must evolve alongside values, as recently stated by the commission in its new trade strategy entitled 'trade for all'. i am therefore very pleased that the commission has taken the initiative to present this report to the council and parliament.
‒ the council of the united nations human rights council (hrc) approved on 26 june 2014 the launch of the process of developing new binding international standards on multinational enterprises and human rights. the initiative aims to end impunity for human rights violations by multinational companies, directly or indirectly caused by their activities, and to ensure access to justice for victims. we have doubts about the importance attached to smes and the definition of a good behaviour label given by the european commission, to whom we do not recognize political and moral legitimacy in the field of human rights and multinational companies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the corrao report because i believe it is fundamental that multinationals with global operations respect human rights rules wherever they operate, regardless of where they are based. i would stress the great importance of corporate social responsibility, especially the practice of integrating the responsibility to respect human rights into contractual requirements binding on companies and their customers and suppliers, whether these are companies or individuals. in this context, i would also like to highlight the work that has been initiated to draw up a binding un treaty on business and human rights, in which i hope the eu and the member states will play a constructive role.
‒ the azores archipelago, due to its geographical location, can act as an important fuelling station for the transatlantic liquefied natural gas routes. the commission should therefore make available funds to support european projects to this end and create a joint project of 'blue lng corridors to islands' in the maritime sector. the report highlights the importance of finding cost-effective and environmentally sustainable energy supply options to increase long-term security of supply in the iberian peninsula and elsewhere in europe, which are not sufficiently connected or integrated into the internal energy market and deserve the eu's full support in the name of the principle of solidarity.
in writing. ‒ this report on the eu lng and gas storage strategy is perfectly in line with the so-called single energy market and the objectives that inspire it. it advocates strengthening the role of the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer). it explains the eu's geostrategic interests in terms of dominance of supply routes and energy production points. it advocates the removal of barriers to market integration, i.e. the creation of the single energy market, i.e. opening the door to monopolistic concentration on a european scale in the sector. it advocates the convergence of world gas markets, a position that is inseparable from the efforts being made in the trade field through free trade and investment agreements, in particular with the usa and canada (ttip and ceta). these are paths and options that we fundamentally disagree with and oppose. without prejudice to the recognition of the role of lng in a future energy mix and to any guidelines which may be pursued at national level in this respect, which is why we voted in favour of the amendments concerning the role of portugal (and particularly its autonomous regions, in the case of the azores), we voted against the report.
‒ this report aims to outline an eu strategy for liquefied natural gas (lng) and gas storage, which is mainly structured in the energy security package presented on 16 february 2016 by the commission. this package consists of proposals to prepare the eu for possible disruptions in energy supply, with the aim of making the eu an attractive market for gas suppliers. this report does not fully address important issues such as access to energy, the affordability of energy, energy as a social public good, the need to combat energy poverty. i voted against it.
‒ gas can play an important role in the eu energy system in the coming decades in the industrial production sector as a source of heating in buildings and in support of renewable energy as the eu meets its greenhouse gas emissions, energy efficiency and renewable energy targets and makes the transition to a low-carbon economy, in which the role of gas will gradually decrease in favour of clean energy. the eu lng and gas storage strategy is one element of the energy union which aims to translate into concrete terms the eu's ambition to move rapidly towards a sustainable, secure and competitive energy system, and which also aims to end dependence on external gas suppliers. it should be noted that one of the objectives of the energy union is to make the eu the world leader in renewable energy. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ this report is on the eu's liquefied natural gas and gas storage strategy and reflects the most negative aspects of the union's energy market. in other words, it favours the domination of private monopolies, always with generous public support, and does not have as its fundamental matrix the public control of these key sectors as a way of ensuring a sustainable management of resources and equitable access to this fundamental good. on the other hand, it insists on confronting the russian federation, rather than understanding the need for political dialogue and respect for the sovereignty of states.
‒ this report on the european union strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage is in line with the european commission's communication of february 2016 under the winter energy package. the rapporteur believes that in order to ensure the achievement of the objective of a resilient energy union, a single energy market should integrate liquefied natural gas and gas storage. the priority should be to create market-based solutions and to use existing regional lng infrastructure. i believe that the most effective way of ensuring energy security is through better coordination of national energy policies, the establishment of a genuine energy union with a genuine single energy market and a common energy policy, and cooperation between member states in this area, in accordance with the principles of solidarity and trust. i support this report.
‒ i voted in favour of the view that liquefied natural gas (lng) offers an opportunity for europe both in terms of increasing competitiveness by exerting downward pressure on natural gas prices and increasing security of supply, and also as a flexible reserve in relation to renewable energies in the context of electricity production. current developments in international lng markets demonstrate that excess supply has led to a reduction in prices, providing an opportunity to offer energy at lower costs to eu consumers through cheaper gas supplies. the report also advocates an lng refuelling station in the azores, which reinforces my vote in favour. the most effective way to ensure energy security is through better coordination of national energy policies and the establishment of a genuine energy union with a genuine single energy market and a common energy policy, as well as cooperation between member states in this area, in accordance with the principles of solidarity and trust.
‒ this report concerns the european union's strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage. the azores, in particular, because of their geostrategic position and importance, could prove to be an important location for the implementation of a fuel station for the transatlantic liquefied natural gas routes. this is precisely the purpose of this report, in which the european parliament is asking the commission to provide funds to support european projects capable of creating a common blue lng corridor project for the islands. in terms of a european strategy in this area, the importance of adopting cost-effective and environmentally sustainable alternatives to current energy supply is highlighted. it is also important to stress that these solutions will ensure long-term supply throughout the european continent and in particular on the iberian peninsula, and thus reduce the current energy isolation. i therefore believe that lng can be a good alternative fuel solution, both at sea and on the road, and also help to reduce the emission of harmful gases into the atmosphere, which is why i voted in favour of this report.

‒ i voted in favour of the gyürk report, for which i tabled several proposals approved as rapporteur for the eu lng and gas storage strategy in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, to ensure energy diversification and security and support a sustainable transition to an energy model based on renewable and clean energy. in this connection, i would like to stress the recommendation i made for the report that the azores archipelago, because of its geographical location, should be able to act as an important fuel station for transatlantic shipping routes and that the commission should provide funds to support european projects such as the one mentioned and create a common blue lng corridor project for the islands. i would also like to stress the amendments tabled by the socialist group to bring the report into line with the targets set in paris and the progressive phasing out of natural gas to achieve these targets, without prejudice to the continued focus on biogas, which is expected to play a decisive role in the future energy mix of the eu. i regret that the wording of the amendments was not more explicit in this respect.
in writing. ‒ fishermen in the various eu countries should be treated equally with uniform inspections. harmonising inspections so that there is a level playing field between all fishing activities, extending controls to the whole production chain and creating a 'basic curriculum' for training inspectors are some of the measures i argue should be adopted. i also agree with the creation of funding mechanisms to increase the use of low-cost technologies to enable voluntary control and to increase the monitoring and safety of fishermen, especially in small-scale artisanal fishing.
‒ eu fisheries controls aim at biological sustainability by fighting illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. the revision of the cfp has decontextualised some issues related to controls, which have become outdated. indeed, there are specific needs to make controlled fishing more uniform, in that this sector is more controlled than any other sector or profession; and that the rules are not applied uniformly between different types of fishing or even between different member states, creating a number of contradictions among fishermen, as regards the regularity, frequency, duration, severity, rigor, effectiveness and methods of controlling fishing in europe. the report highlights a number of issues that can contribute to non-discriminatory treatment in the sector, the effectiveness of controls and the sustainability of marine resources. however, the report has several aspects that raise concerns and ambiguous interpretations, such as those related to the use of new technologies for monitoring; the introduction of a points-based penalty system with implications for fishing licences. at the same time, the report reflects a high degree of centralisation and eu-level definition of technical and policy measures relating to controls, rather than cooperation between member states, and therefore cannot be supported globally.
‒ this report aims to further harmonise fisheries controls in europe, as the rules are not applied uniformly across fisheries or even across member states, and highlights a number of issues that can contribute to more effective and non-discriminatory treatment in the sector, to the effectiveness of controls and to the sustainability of marine resources. however, the report has several aspects that raise concerns and ambiguous interpretations, such as those related to the use of new technologies for monitoring, the introduction of a points-based sanctions system with implications for fishing licences, reflecting a high level of centralisation in the eu in the definition of technical and political measures related to controls, rather than cooperation between member states. i abstained.

in writing. - i voted in favour, as the uniformity of the application of the regulation and its effectiveness are fundamental for the fisheries sector. if it is possible to suspect that the rules are not applied with the same rigor, it is to be feared that we will reach a situation where the rules are no longer respected because they are not the same for everyone. the modernisation of fleets would add value to the success of this measure by equipping the operators with useful capabilities for the control of irregularities. at the same time, it is urgent to defend the fishermen of the outermost regions, who are greatly disadvantaged by their large eezs and by the limitations of the member states in controlling them. the control and monitoring measures in the eezs of the ors must therefore be increased, as i have advocated in an amendment to this report which was approved by the european parliament. in this regard, the budgetary means available, in particular through the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff), should be consistent with the objectives of control and allow for the promotion of research and innovation. it is through these instruments that the control policy as a whole can be modernised. unfortunately, the emff is clearly insufficient to meet the needs of the sector.
‒ the harmonisation of fisheries control legislation in europe and control procedures must be transparent and uniform. the different control bodies should seek to coordinate their activities. the penalties should be the same for everyone. the first step is to create a function of judges specialised in maritime matters in each member state. in order to make controls more effective, it is also necessary to make the means of financing, in particular the emff, more consistent with the objectives of control.
‒ this report has been drawn up in the light of the preparation of the next fisheries control regulation. the rapporteur stresses the importance of ensuring effective control of fishing activities in order to ensure the sustainable exploitation of marine resources, while maintaining a level playing field between fleets. to this end, member states are urged to ensure the effective application of the control regulation. i welcome the significant improvement in the control system thanks to the current regulation combined with the iuu regulation, while not forgetting the disparity between the different inspection sites and the discriminatory nature sometimes resulting from the control of fisheries. the text of this report reiterates the importance of strengthening the mandate of the european fisheries control agency (efca) in order to create joint fisheries control operations that will allow for efficient coordinated action by (many) local, regional and national authorities, as well as eu agencies carrying out similar functions. the lack of interoperability between data collected at member state level has to be considered as a key element for this desired further harmonisation, so it is important to share data in real time. i have voted in favour of this report because i agree with the proposals made.

‒ prompt access to well-connected transport networks covering the local, regional, national and cross-border dimensions of passenger and freight transport is at the heart of promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion in the eu member states and amongst themselves. member states and the eu will have to pool their resources and cooperate closely in the design and implementation of projects with a view to completing the strategic core network by 2030 and the comprehensive network by 2050. member states and the commission should first focus on bridging the gaps, removing bottlenecks and ensuring seamless connections for both passenger and freight transport, thus fulfilling the objectives of the ten-t. however, these efforts to complete the core corridors should also stimulate the development of the overall network by providing a link to neighbouring regions, in particular in cross-border regions, and thus achieve the consolidation of the network corridors.
‒ the existence of quality transport infrastructure and systems is a guarantee for the development of countries and for the improvement of the quality of life of the population. the linkage and interoperability of transport systems within a country or between countries is also a facilitating element in the development and establishment of commercial relations and socio-cultural communication. the countries of central and eastern europe have every right to develop fully and to use the instruments available to ensure greater cohesion. this report, however, emphasises strategies and instruments which represent interests which are contrary to those of the peoples of the various member states and not just those of the targeted countries. the report's main objective is to deepen the single market. more than improving the operability of transport in central and eastern europe, it is important to extend the market of european monopolies to this macro-region. at the same time, it seeks to anticipate future enlargements (western balkans, ukraine) by expanding the transport system so that entry into the single market can be smooth. it also called for the form of infrastructure to be provided by the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) and for the possibilities offered by hybrid projects in the framework of public-private partnerships. we voted against it.

in writing. - the opportunity of this proposal could not be greater. it is clear to everyone that there is a contradiction between the level of demands we place on the applicant countries and the fact that certain member states are calling into question the core elements of the rule of law. but what model to adopt? on the one hand, there are advantages to an institutional agreement: it would not require changes to the treaties, it could bring greater coherence and effectiveness to the work of parliament, the council and the commission (which today each have their own mechanism). on the other hand, there are issues relating to its operation which will need to be fine-tuned, starting with the composition of the panel of experts. but it also points to solutions that could bring immediate improvement: restarting the process of accession of the union to the council of europe convention on human rights or giving more resources to the court of justice of the european union, thus increasing its capacity to respond. this is undoubtedly a good initiative, which is for good causes and which is now taking the first steps in what will be, given its sensitivity and complexity, a long process. i therefore vote in favour of this report.
‒ the commission should present, by september 2017, a proposal for the creation of a union pact for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights including a preventive and corrective dimension, a cycle similar to the european semester of fiscal policy coordination and country-specific reports. the new european mechanism, which would complement and supplement existing mechanisms, must be based on concrete elements, evaluated on a fair basis and not be subject to external influence, in particular from a political point of view. it should apply to both the member states and the european institutions and be based on a step-by-step approach, including a preventive and a corrective approach. the assessment of the state of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in the member states and the drafting of the country-specific recommendations should be carried out by a panel of independent experts.
‒ this report proposes the creation of an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in the form of an interinstitutional agreement providing for measures between the eu institutions and the member states, under article 7 of the eu treaty, which is proposed to be revised in order to make sanctions against any member state relevant and enforceable. the proposal to revise article 7 is intended to go beyond the current planned measure of suspension of voting rights in the council, so that 'financial sanctions or suspension of union funding' can also be applied. it would be funny if it wasn't too serious. the eu is both a reference and an arbiter of democracy, the rule of law and human rights. that's too bad. we are looking at a monument to cynicism and hypocrisy. obviously, we voted against it. it is not surprising that the ps and psd voted in favour of this report, while the cds and be abstained. in the vote on the proposal to revise article 7 teu, which includes the possibility of imposing financial sanctions, ps, psd, cds and be voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities, enshrined in its core principles and objectives in the first articles of the teu, as well as in the criteria for accession to the european union. i welcome the creation of a comprehensive union mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights that includes all relevant stakeholders. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ we are facing an unacceptable assault on the sovereignty of states, from which we firmly distance ourselves. it aims to deepen the mechanisms of federalisation of the european union and provides for the creation of a political cycle for democracy and the rule of law (as understood), similar to the european semester; to make the teu and the tfeu the legal basis for legislative measures and to revise article 7 of the teu by introducing relevant and applicable sanctions against any member state; to abolish the principle of subsidiarity of the tfeu; to revise the requirement for unanimity in the council for decisions involving fundamental rights. these points legitimize the sanctions and the unacceptable blackmail and pressure that are being applied to portugal. the eu institutions are not exemplary when it comes to democracy and fundamental rights. the harmonization of these constitutes, for countries like portugal, an unacceptable negative pressure, levelling down the standards of social and labour rights. the complexity of european treaties and legislation is, in fact, an obstacle to the legitimate sovereign decision of each people to decide its own destiny, an obstacle to the implementation of the portuguese constitution and the achievements of the revolution which the portuguese people will sooner or later be able to take up and impose, freeing themselves from the constraints of the treaties. we voted against it.
in writing. ‒ we can proudly say that europe has a long tradition of democracy, the rule of law and citizens' rights. building on its roots in athenian democracy, the magna carta of 1215, the declaration of the rights of man and of the citizen of 1789, the european convention on human rights and the charter of fundamental rights, the european union has enshrined democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights (def) in its main principles and objectives as enshrined in the first articles of the treaties, as well as in the eu accession criteria. in its external policies too, the eu stresses the importance of human rights and democratic governance, thus promoting them in partnerships such as the acp-eu. however, while the eu has various instruments to enforce its laws and treaties on material issues such as budgets, public health programmes or tax rulings, the same is no longer true for the fulfilment of its treaty obligations in the areas of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. it is important to adopt a structure that enables the eu to combat both breaches of specific eu legislation and serious threats to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. i vote in favour.
‒ i voted in favour, considering it imperative that democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights be enshrined in the main principles and objectives enshrined in the first articles of the treaties and in the eu accession criteria. attempts to include in the treaties a reference to europe's judeo-christian roots have failed, but they demonstrate that the european union is seen as a community of values. in its external policies, the eu stresses the importance of human rights and democratic governance and expects immigrants living in europe to respect and embrace our common values. although the eu has a number of instruments to ensure respect for the principles of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, substantial gaps remain and in practice these instruments show limited scope, are inadequate and inefficient or are unlikely to be implemented. it is therefore essential to adopt a structure that enables the eu to combat both breaches of specific eu legislation and serious threats (and risks of threats) to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights.
‒ the eu has a wide range of instruments to enforce its laws and treaties on substantive issues. in such cases, member states do not question their obligation to comply with eu law. the same is no longer true when it comes to the fulfilment of the obligations laid down in the field of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. although the eu has several instruments to ensure compliance with these principles, substantial gaps remain and in practice these instruments show limited scope. there is no integrated mechanism for systematic, impartial and comprehensive monitoring of all member states and their institutions. it is imperative to adopt a structure that enables the eu to combat both breaches of specific eu legislation and serious threats to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the eu's failures to uphold its own standards and the perception that there are no common european values are also undermining mutual trust and the establishment of a stable and reliable legal framework, which is essential for the eu's smooth functioning in all areas of intervention.
in writing. ‒ the eu is, by definition, a union governed by the principles of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, which are expressly enshrined in its treaties and constitute criteria for accession. it is the body of instruments at its disposal for the enforcement of laws and treaties on a wide range of substantive issues relating to the various areas of union competence, including taxation, budgetary matters, public health and employment. however, it is clear that the same is not the case in the area of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, where member states and the european institutions sometimes have difficulty in respecting the founding treaties and principles, with substantial gaps in their adequacy, efficiency, exemption, fairness and applicability. as the rapporteur points out, it is important to create an integrated mechanism for systematic, integrated, impartial and comprehensive monitoring of all member states and their institutions, capable of combating breaches of european legislation and threats to these key principles and values. in the light of the above, i was in favour of adopting this report with a view to adopting an eu pact for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in the form of an interinstitutional agreement, in the form proposed.
in writing. ‒ this is yet another unacceptable assault on the sovereignty of states. we do not recognize the european union's legitimacy to give lessons in democracy to anyone. the eu's concept of democracy is that of sanctions, which the report defends and deepens, and of blackmail and pressure. in the case of portugal, with our legislation, this would constitute an unacceptable negative pressure, levelling down the standards of social and labour rights. this is indeed the aim of the eu, creating a standard of minimum rights that excludes other fundamental rights such as the right to health, education or decent work.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the veld report because i agree with the considerations concerning the implementation of the european values enshrined in the treaties. i would particularly stress the call for the creation of a democratic evaluation mechanism. this mechanism aims to monitor member states' respect for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, in the same way as the countries applying for eu membership are assessed.

‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns and may not exceed the annual ceiling of eur 150 million. estonia has submitted a proposal to reintegrate workers made redundant in the manufacture of chemicals and man-made fibres. the application concerns the dismissal of 800 workers and provides for the mobilisation of eur 1 131 358.
‒ 1,550 workers were laid off from 3 different companies in estonia, two from shale gas production, including the main energy company in the baltic states, and one from chemical production. only 800 of the workers made redundant are expected to participate in the european globalisation adjustment fund measures. some of those workers have been employed since this application. this application will mobilise eur 1 131 358, 60% of the total estimated cost of the proposed measures. the report proposes specific measures which will include, for example, psychological counselling and a study grant of eur 260 per month. it proposes an active consultation of the unions. it also proposes an estonian language course for the russian minority (although this is a good measure to enable these workers to speak estonian, it also relates to a government option which considers that 63.3% of the workers laid off are 'non-eu citizens'). since estonia does not grant citizenship to its russian minority, this high number actually includes russian speakers. it is expected that the planned measures will include training for all (and covered transport to enable participation). a fundamental change is needed, which involves a break with the neoliberal policies which have made it necessary to mobilise this fund.
