‒ this directive aims to approximate the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to the accessibility requirements of public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications, thereby making those websites and mobile applications more accessible to users, in particular to persons with disabilities. i support the charanzowa report which approves the council's position at first reading, thus allowing the obstacles within the internal market resulting from the lack of harmonisation of national approaches to web accessibility to be removed. it is inconceivable that the internet should not be a reality for everyone today, with segregation in access to information and the full exercise of rights for millions of european citizens. i welcome the fact that this new directive will facilitate access to information and public services on the internet for these people, contributing to an inclusive society and the completion of the digital single market, by making websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies such as administrative, judicial and police services, as well as hospitals, universities and libraries, subject to common european accessibility standards.
in writing. ‒ public administrations are increasingly making online services available to citizens. however, there are currently around 80 million people in the eu with some form of disability for whom access to these types of services is not easy. the new directive, already agreed between negotiators from the european parliament and national governments, aims to ensure that public sector bodies take the necessary steps to make their websites and mobile applications more accessible by making them discernible, operable, understandable and robust. public bodies will have to develop tools, such as magnifiers or screen readers, to help older people and people with disabilities use their websites and applications. i voted in favour.
‒ we consider the proposal to introduce mandatory accessibility for certain types of public bodies' (state, regional, local and public law bodies) websites in essential government e-services such as network services, banking, education, social security, health services, social inclusion services and cultural activities to be generally positive. this directive aims to improve the lives of citizens, especially people with disabilities and the elderly, in terms of accessibility to these public bodies' websites, given that much of the information available is online. however, we consider that it should be safeguarded that member states that have already developed their national accessibility policies and standards on the basis of wcag 2 should be exempted from the application of this directive. this avoids additional costs for national, regional, local and other public authorities. furthermore, the provision of these services on a digital platform cannot in any case mean the removal or limitation of access to the same services through traditional infrastructures. the absence of access to the internet or the inability to use this resource and functional illiteracy are a reality that cannot be overlooked and affect a significant part of the population.
‒ this directive will help member states to meet their national commitments on web accessibility, as well as their commitment under the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities to public sector bodies. the commission is proposing to harmonise national public sector measures at eu level as a necessary condition to end this fragmentation and lack of confidence in the web accessibility market. this directive concerns the websites of public sector bodies because those bodies provide essential information and services to citizens and because public procurement alone can already create a secure and reasonably sized market for website creators. harmonisation will lead to better market conditions, more jobs, lower costs of web accessibility and more accessible websites - a triple win for governments, businesses and citizens. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the evolution towards a digital society offers users new ways of accessing information and services. information and service providers, as well as public sector bodies, increasingly rely on the internet to produce, collect and make available a wide range of information and services electronically that are essential for the public. for the purposes of this directive, the term 'accessibility' should be understood as the principles and techniques to be observed in the design, construction, maintenance and updating of websites and mobile applications in order to make their content more accessible to users, in particular to persons with disabilities. i advocate a close relationship to help member states meet their national commitments on web accessibility, as well as their commitment under the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities to public sector bodies.
‒ we consider the proposal to introduce mandatory accessibility for certain types of public bodies' (state, regional, local and public law bodies) websites in essential government e-services such as network services, banking, education, social security, health services, social inclusion services and cultural activities to be generally positive. this directive aims to improve the lives of citizens, especially people with disabilities and the elderly, in terms of accessibility to these public bodies' websites, given that much of the information available is online. however, we consider that it should be safeguarded that member states that have already developed their national accessibility policies and standards on the basis of wcag 2 should be exempted from the application of this directive. this avoids additional costs for national, regional, local and other public authorities. furthermore, the provision of these services on a digital platform cannot in any case mean the removal or limitation of access to the same services through traditional infrastructures. the absence of access to the internet or the inability to use this resource and functional illiteracy are a reality that cannot be overlooked and affect a significant part of the population.
in writing. ‒ in 2012, the commission presented a proposal for a directive relating to the standardisation of accessibility requirements for websites and mobile applications of public bodies. after the european parliament's approval at first reading, and following agreement in the negotiations with the council, a second reading is now put to the vote. the proposal aims to facilitate access to content on public bodies' platforms for all users, with particular attention to those with special needs. the directive provides for the introduction of minimum accessibility conditions, as required by the monitoring and regular reporting of the websites and mobile applications of public bodies in the member states. because the public information and services available on the internet must meet the standards of an inclusive society, i support this text and in that sense i am voting in favour.
‒ this directive aims to improve the accessibility of public sector websites and their content for citizens with disabilities, but also for the elderly. we live in a digital age and all citizens should be treated equally in terms of access to information. this directive is an important step towards an inclusive digital society by ensuring that public sector institutions make their websites and applications accessible to everyone.
in writing. in 2012, the european commission presented its proposal for a directive on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites. in addition to the objective of introducing standardised accessibility features within the eu, the process of accessing such content is also intended to be easy and accessible for all users. this directive aims to establish minimum conditions for the accessibility of websites on an equal basis, requiring regular monitoring of the functioning assessment by the member states. in addition, mobile applications have also been included in the directive, following a proposal from the european parliament. public bodies must also prepare an 'accessibility statement' - in line with the directive in question - thus allowing citizens to request more specific information if the content is or is not accessible, and to report any shortcomings of the website or application. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that this directive will bring substantial improvements to the present system once it is implemented.
‒ the proposal for a directive on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites (com (2012) 721) submitted by the ec lays down specific technical provisions whereby member states are required to make accessible the content of certain types of public sector bodies' websites (which provide information and services essential for citizens' participation in the economy and society). the directive aims to approximate the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites by laying down harmonised requirements.
‒ plant health is an essential factor for sustainable and competitive agriculture, horticulture and forestry. healthy seeds and propagating material are needed to produce profitable crops and to ensure jobs, crop innovation and food security. pests from other continents are particularly dangerous. in general, european plants and trees do not have adequate genetic resistance to allotment pests, which, moreover, do not usually have natural enemies here. when introduced into europe, allotonic pests cause serious economic damage. economic losses, sometimes severe, are affecting the profitability and competitiveness of agriculture and forestry. i therefore agree with the protection measures proposed in the report.
‒ the purpose of this regulation is to prevent the entry and spread of two types of plant pests, quarantine pests and non-regulated quarantine pests which are allowed up to a limit. one of the main concerns raised by the legislative proposal was the registration and certification of producers, which posed a risk of potential impact on small producers with low risk products, selling only small volumes of low or no risk plants (including seeds), who would have to pay to register and face prohibitive fines, when they should not be the target of these measures. there was also another group that was unintentionally affected, seed-supply organisations that take action to conserve rare varieties and species and ensure genetic biodiversity. these concerns were duly safeguarded in the final version of the regulation. during the negotiations it was also possible to ensure (thanks to pressure from the southern countries) that this regulation imposes strict controls on the import of plant material into the eu, hoping to prevent future outbreaks of plant diseases (such as the recent attack of xylella fastidiosa on olive trees). even though not all concerns have been removed, but the main ones have been removed, the text has been improved throughout the process of its discussion.
‒ plant health is an essential factor for sustainable and competitive agriculture, horticulture and forestry. healthy seeds and propagating material are needed to produce profitable crops and to ensure jobs, crop innovation and food security. in the case of trees and shrubs, plant health protection is essential for the preservation of forests, landscapes and public and private green spaces across the union. plant health is also important for the protection of biodiversity and ecosystem services. the proposal is part of a package of revisions relating to plant health, the quality of plant reproductive material, animal health, official controls on plants, animals and foodstuffs for human and animal consumption and union expenditure on these policies. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the current eu regulatory framework on plant health aims to protect european agriculture and forestry by preventing the entry and spread of allotment pests. in recent times, this framework has been criticised for its inability to stop the increase in new dangerous pests entering the eu territory due to the increase in international trade. this legal framework needs to be amended to be able to fully address the growing risks and to modernise. the main problems identified are insufficient concern for prevention in high-risk goods, the need to prioritise pests at eu level and in the 28 member states, the need for better tools to control the presence and spread of pests and the need to improve tools for movement within the eu. i agree with the rapporteur that professional operators must be covered by the system of protection measures against plant pests, just as it is essential to combat pests also in public or private green areas. however, it is essential that this process is as transparent and predictable as possible.
‒ the dominant agricultural models, based on intensive export-oriented monocultures, reduce the resilience of agricultural systems to pests and enhance their devastating effects, which is why it is necessary, first of all, to question and abandon these models, along with the rejection of any form of privatisation of genetic resources, in particular through the patenting of seeds. the intention, under the pretext of pest control, to impose registration and certification measures which in practice make small farmers' activities, traditional agriculture and traditional plant propagation methods unviable is unacceptable. on the contrary, it would compromise a sustainable response to the pest problem in the long term. as regards the import of plant material from third countries, strict phytosanitary controls are entirely justified, which eliminate the risk of future outbreaks of plant diseases with potentially devastating agronomic and ecological consequences.
‒ the new legislation must ensure a high level of security for the european union in relation to the import of plants and plant products. the new system will make it much more difficult to introduce pests such as xyllela fastidiosa in southern italy or the asian longhorned beetle in the uk. the new quarantine measures envisaged will also take account of the specificity of each case and farmers will be supported in eradication procedures and will receive compensation for losses. the introduction of the plant passport is also an innovation brought about by this regulation, with the aim of ensuring a high degree of traceability.
‒ plant health is an essential factor for sustainable and competitive agriculture, horticulture and forestry, enabling profitable crops and acting as a guarantee for job preservation, innovation, food security and biodiversity protection. pests from other continents are particularly dangerous, given that european agriculture is not genetically resistant to allotment pests which are already causing serious economic damage, compromising the profitability and competitiveness of european agriculture and forestry. the current eu regulatory framework for plant health has been the subject of several criticisms. the shortcomings identified include the insufficiency of preventive measures with regard to the increase in imports of high-risk goods, the need to prioritise pests at eu level for member states, the lack of tools to control the presence and natural spread of pests should they reach the union territory, the lack of modernisation and updating of tools for intra-eu movement, and the need to provide for additional resources. the aim of this revision is to fill the gaps identified and to establish a robust, transparent and sustainable regulatory framework, adapted to its objectives, which is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
‒ the dominant agricultural models, based on intensive export-oriented monocultures, reduce the resilience of agricultural systems to pests and enhance their devastating effects, which is why it is necessary, first of all, to question and abandon these models, along with the rejection of any form of privatisation of genetic resources, in particular through the patenting of seeds. the intention, under the pretext of pest control, to impose registration and certification measures which in practice make small farmers' activities, traditional agriculture and traditional plant propagation methods unviable is unacceptable. on the contrary, it would compromise a sustainable response to the pest problem in the long term. as regards the import of plant material from third countries, strict phytosanitary controls are entirely justified, which eliminate the risk of future outbreaks of plant diseases with potentially devastating agronomic and ecological consequences.

in writing. ‒ transesterified fatty acids (tafas) are unsaturated fats that can be found in foodstuffs obtained from ruminants or in the production of industrially produced partially hydrogenated vegetable oils. they are cheap and easily obtainable raw materials. consumption of these oils has been linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, obesity, and some cancers. the products that currently have the most unsaturated fats are fast food and snacks (salty or sweet) and foods classified as highly processed. according to the relevant agencies who, efsa and fda these fatty acids are not considered safe for human consumption and their consumption should be kept to a minimum. we are in favour of limiting the use and consumption of this type of trans fatty acids as much as possible in order to prevent disease and promote healthy eating habits. we generally agree with the wording and content of this resolution. but we must point out that the issues of promoting healthy eating and the consumption of fresh, low-processed products cannot be solved simply by legislation on labelling or by limiting the use of agts in processed foods. the reasons for economic inadequacy are, in this context, inescapable.
‒ trans fatty acids (tfa) are a specific type of unsaturated fat. the question of agt is a priority for parliament, which reiterates its concern about the risks that agt poses to human health. the food industry should give priority to alternative solutions that respect health and environmental standards, such as the use of improved oils, new fat modification processes or the combination of ingredients to replace agt (fibres, pulp, starches, protein blends, etc.). we should work for healthier food. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ trans fatty acids (tfas) are a specific type of unsaturated fat that can be found naturally in foods derived from ruminants, such as dairy products and meat, as well as in some plants and plant products. they are mainly present in industrially produced partially hydrogenated vegetable oils (vegetable oils that are modified by the addition of hydrogen atoms and used for frying and cooking and in processed foods to extend shelf life). this resolution concerns only industrially produced fatty acids. the issue of agt is a concern with regard to the risks it may pose to human health. i agree that the proposal should be accompanied by an impact assessment to calculate the costs of industrial reformulation that may result from the imposition of mandatory limits and to assess the risk of those costs being borne by consumers. i believe that the commission should work with the member states to increase knowledge in the field of nutrition, encouraging consumers and enabling them to make healthier food choices.
‒ consumption of these fats has been linked to the risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, obesity and some cancers. agencies such as who, efsa and fda warn of the dangers of this consumption and recommend that it be as low as possible. we are therefore in favour of limiting the use and consumption of trans fats. but promoting healthy eating and fresh, low-processed products is not just done by legislating to improve labelling. it should be borne in mind that many of these products are distinguished by their low price. in other words, the consumption of processed foods is now associated with situations of economic insufficiency, which impedes access to quality and healthy products. no strategy for promoting healthy eating should ignore this fact. moreover, you must actively fight it.

‒ although trans fatty acids (tfas) are naturally present in ruminant-derived foods such as dairy products and meat, as well as in some plants and plant products (garlic, peas, lettuce, rapeseed oil), they are mainly present in production partially hydrogenated vegetable oils. this resolution concerns only industrially produced fatty acids. many restaurants and fast food establishments use agt to fry food, as these fats are cheap and can be reused several times in industrial frying machines. frequent consumption of these has been associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease (more than any other factor), infertility, endometriosis, gallstones, alzheimer's disease, diabetes, obesity, and some cancers. the consumption of agt should be as low as possible in the context of a nutritionally adequate diet (less than 1% of the daily energy intake). the european commission needs to set as soon as possible a legal limit for industrial agts (both as an ingredient and as a final product) in all food products in order to reduce their consumption by all groups of the population.

madam president, we value volunteering, and in particular the social role it can play in promoting effective solidarity and mutual aid between citizens, by fostering feelings of altruism and genuine generosity, which are contrary to the culture of individualism that the neoliberal policies of the european union help to promote. the report mentions concepts that we do not follow, such as the concept of european citizenship, the european civic service or the european solidarity corps. the relevant role of volunteers in supporting the humanitarian refugee crisis is mentioned. in appreciating this participation, we cannot but denounce that these concepts and entities will contribute to legitimizing and deepening a dynamic that has been used to discredit the role that states and the european union should and should not assume in responding to the very serious humanitarian crisis. finally, it should be noted that volunteering cannot replace jobs, a practice which is unfortunately becoming increasingly common, which justifies the need to strengthen its legal framework and the defence of its social rights.
in writing. ‒ for the eighth time in a row, parliament has given the council discharge for 2014 by a large majority. for the eighth time, the council has disregarded parliament's budgetary powers. it ignored requests for further information, in particular on the council's real estate assets, which were being refurbished and newly built. it ignored the request for greater transparency by continuing to fail to submit the accounts. it has ignored the call for administrative modernisation and for the separation of accounts between the council of ministers and the european council. this approach does not dignify the council and casts a stain of irresponsibility on all the european institutions. once again, the european parliament - and rightly so - reiterates that it will not accept this approach, refusing to grant discharge to this institution and thus postponing the completion of the discharge procedure.
‒ the union institutions must be transparent and fully accountable to the citizens of the union for the funds entrusted to them as union institutions and both the european council and the council must be subject to democratic accountability to the citizens of the union as beneficiaries of the general budget of the european union. i regret that the european council and the council do not provide parliament with their annual activity reports, which i consider unacceptable and damaging to the reputation of the eu institutions, and that the budget of the european council and the council have not yet been separated, as recommended by parliament in recent discharge resolutions.
the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action against terrorism. we voted in favour, as we have done on previous occasions. the council has not yet taken a position on the observations made by parliament in its discharge resolution of april 2016 on the trend of the previous years towards an increase in the under-utilisation of appropriations and the transfer of commitments. the european council and the council do not provide parliament with their annual activity reports. the report reiterates the call for reports on the progress of the building projects and a detailed breakdown of the expenditure incurred to date. it considers that information should be provided on the costs of delaying completion of the europa building. the report reiterates the request to the council to provide information on the process of administrative modernisation, in particular on the expected impact on the council's budget. calls on the council to adopt a code of conduct as a matter of urgency in order to ensure the integrity of the institution; reiterates its request for the application of rules on whistleblowing; calls on the council to join the eu transparency register in order to ensure the transparency and accountability of the institution.
‒ all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be subject to strict supervision by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, the institutions in question are using the funds appropriately and are meeting the objectives set. it is in this spirit that i vote against the discharge to be given to the secretary-general of the council in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european council and of the council for the financial year 2014
‒ the institutions of the european union must be transparent and fully accountable to the citizens of the union for the funds entrusted to them as union institutions. the european council and the council, as institutions of the union, must be democratically accountable to the citizens of the union, since they are beneficiaries of the general budget of the european union. i agree with the rapporteur that it is regrettable that the european council and the council do not provide parliament with their annual activity reports, considering that this is unacceptable and damaging to the reputation of the eu institutions. since it is the competence of parliament to grant discharge in accordance with articles 316, 317 and 319 tfeu, in line with current practice and interpretation, in particular to grant discharge for the implementation of each budget line in order to maintain transparency and ensure democratic accountability to union taxpayers, and since the council has not submitted to parliament the requested documents, it undermines the right of citizens of the union to information and transparency.
in writing. ‒ since the council has not yet taken a position on the observations made by parliament in its discharge resolution of 28 april 2016 on the trend of the previous financial years towards an increase in the under-utilisation of appropriations and the transition of commitments, and has not provided the ep with its annual activity report, we follow the proposal not to grant discharge.
‒ the discharge procedure is the final approval by the european parliament of how the eu budget is implemented for a given year. parliament shall examine the reports of the parliamentary committee on budgetary control and, taking into account the recommendation of the council, shall decide whether to grant, postpone or refuse discharge. the discharge for the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2014 is not yet finalised, as a number of issues relating to section ii - european council and council - remain unresolved. in the documents provided by the council, only three of the 27 questions put by parliament have been given a clear answer. requests for information on real estate assets, the accounts report, among others, were ignored. it is totally regrettable that the european council and the council do not provide parliament with their annual activity reports, which is unacceptable and damaging to the reputation of the institutions of the european union, especially in the current conjecture. finally, i remind the council of the commission's view, expressed in 2014, that all institutions should be involved in the follow-up to the observations made by parliament in the context of the discharge exercise and that all institutions should cooperate to ensure the smooth running of the discharge procedure. i therefore support this report.
‒ i voted in favour, considering that the failure of the council to submit the requested documents to parliament is above all a breach of the right of citizens of the union to information and transparency and is becoming a cause for concern, reflecting a certain democratic deficit within the union's institutions. i believe that this situation constitutes a serious breach of the obligations arising from the treaties and that the parties concerned must take the necessary measures to resolve this problem without delay. a review of the treaties and financial regulations may therefore be necessary to clarify the objectives and procedures of the discharge procedure and to define penalties for non-compliance with the rules laid down in the treaties.
in writing. ‒ all european institutions must be governed by criteria of rigour, transparency and accountability with regard to the funds entrusted to them. both the european council and the council, as european institutions, are beneficiaries of the eu's general budget and, in this sense, they must answer to the citizens, which is why it is not understandable that the council has not so far commented on the european parliament's observations on the tendency of previous years to involve an increase in the under-utilisation of appropriations and the transition of commitments. in parallel, there is another set of outstanding issues, related to the failure to provide the annual activity report of both institutions - which tarnishes and destroys the reputation and credibility of all european institutions. in addition, the failure to follow the recommendation for the separation of the european council and the council, as has been proposed in recent discharge resolutions, and the lack of information on the costs of buildings and real estate projects under way, amongst others, are also worrisome facts. in the light of the foregoing and the content of the other observations in the report, i voted to refuse discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014 of these two institutions.

in writing. eniac was established in december 2007 for a period of 10 years with the aim of defining and implementing a 'research agenda' for the development of core competencies in nanoelectronics across different application areas. eniac is a public-private partnership. the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of eniac for the financial year 2014, published a qualified opinion for the fourth consecutive year on the regularity and legality of the underlying transactions, on the grounds that the administrative agreements signed with the national funding bodies with regard to the audit of the payment applications related to the projects do not include the practical provisions for ex post audits. according to the court of auditors' report, eniac did not assess the quality of the audit reports submitted by the national funding bodies on the costs of the completed projects. after the evaluation of the audit strategies of three national funding bodies, it was not possible to conclude whether the ex post audits work effectively, as the different methodologies used by the national funding bodies did not allow eniac to calculate a weighted error rate or a residual error rate.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the marinescu report for agreeing to the discharge for iter and the development of fusion energy. i would stress my support for the formula of joint ventures that combine private institutes and public partnerships in support of research through synergies that can accelerate the introduction of new technologies on the market, provided they bring clear added value for european citizens. the iter joint undertaking in particular seeks to cover the areas of air traffic control, low-carbon energy, nanotechnology, aviation technologies and nuclear fusion. i would point out that the iter project is currently facing challenges that affect its development and that it is therefore necessary to implement the measures set out in the iter organisation action plan in order to successfully complete all the project phases.
‒ iraq, along with syria, has been one of the countries most affected by the incursions of the so-called islamic state. the terror and slaughter that has been sown in this region is the cause of the largest number of displaced people since the second world war. this offensive against daesh is, however, of particular importance because it is attacking its last major stronghold in iraq. not only is mosul the second most important city in iraq, but because of the ethnic and religious diversity of this region, it is the paradigmatic example of the destruction wrought by the occupation. the effort made by the us-led coalition, in this case with the support of the iraqi army and the peshmerga forces of the kurdish regional government, is commendable. however, it is crucial to safeguard the future of this region now by guaranteeing humanitarian aid, a state which can guarantee the security of the territory and which respects the numerous minorities. only then can stability be restored to the region. the european union must play a key role here. i think it's clear the moral duty is beyond the geostrategic importance.
‒ according to the united nations high commissioner for refugees (unhcr), more than 1.5 million people are at imminent risk of displacement in mosul as a direct consequence of the operation to retake the area. the eu has so far provided €134 million in humanitarian aid to iraq, including €50 million for mosul. i think it is important to redouble our efforts to stabilize the liberated areas. i strongly condemn the violence and mass executions that continue to be perpetrated by is in iraq and the 'draconian regime' it has imposed in mosul, and call for full respect for the rights of the different ethnic and religious minorities in the country, in particular the yazidis, the chaldeans/syrians/assyrians and the turkmens.
‒ this resolution does not put into context the instability that iraq has been experiencing since the invasion of the country in 2003, in violation of international law, nor the responsibilities that the us and the eu have in the destruction and destabilisation of the country. the alleged fight against the islamic state has violated iraq's territorial integrity and sovereignty, and the crisis in the country, with its conflict between different ethnic groups and foreign interference and interference in the country, is in fact jeopardising its independence and sovereignty. turkey's role in iraq in defending its political, economic and geostrategic interests should also be mentioned. we also note that when mosul has been under occupation for two years now, without any initiative to liberate it, it is at this very moment that it is moving forward against a city which also plays a role in the syrian conflict. which could make you link an alleged humanitarian intervention with military objectives related to the syrian conflict.
‒ the iraqi army, with the support of the international coalition against isil/daesh and the kurdish regional government (krg) peshmerga forces and the popular mobilization forces, launched an operation to liberate mosul, iraq's second largest city, and many towns and villages in the isil/daesh 'mosul corridor'. 0020. i support the operation launched by iraq to liberate mosul from isil/daesh, this operation is a decisive element of an ongoing global effort to inflict a lasting defeat on the islamic state. that is why i am voting in favour.

madam president, commissioner dombrovskis, mr president mario draghi, the first thing we must acknowledge in this debate is that the monetary policy of the european central bank has made not only an important but a decisive contribution to defending the euro, stabilising sovereign debt markets, giving a chance to the european economy and countering deflationary pressures. we must value that clearly. we all know that there can be collateral damage from a too long negative interest policy. but it is dangerously unwise to call for a precipitous retreat from monetary policy at this time, which is still a time of uncertainty and turbulence, and which may become, after brexit and the new trump administration, a time of uncontrolled financial speculation in sovereign debt markets. what we expect from the european central bank is a message of stabilizing the markets, a message of decisive intervention to ensure the integrity of the euro area. i ask mr draghi whether this is still the fundamental mission of the ecb at this historic moment in the european economy, when the euro is still under threat. this is very important for the whole euro zone, but also for the countries most threatened by speculation, such as portugal. i would also like to ask you whether, after the results achieved on the economic and budgetary fronts with the assessment of the ratings, portugal is still eligible for the european central bank's asset purchase programme.
mr president, it is now clear that the banking union, which was created to give the financial system stability and to deal with the systemic banks, which are known as 'too big to fail', is nothing but a manoeuvre designed to remove from the national public sphere any possibility of intervention and to impose a series of merger operations between financial institutions, thus aggravating the problem it is supposed to solve. in the case of portugal, the situation is glaring. with the centralisation of all supervisory and resolution functions in the ecb, the largest portuguese banks were eventually sold to foreign groups at the balance price, with the loss being borne by taxpayers, since the resolution fund has only been financed by the portuguese state. it is clear that this banking union does not help to solve any of the problems of economies, with or without a deposit guarantee system, because this banking union is the expression of the domination of the financial system over the political power of the european union, which has long since renounced the defence of the interests of the citizen in order to devote itself to serving the interests of those who actually rule in europe.
mr president, we are facing a further deepening of the single market, extending it to retail financial services. like other initiatives, it is based on concepts which, while apparently aimed at improving the conditions of users, in practice represent another element of harmonization, of federalist deepening, which will serve the big financial interests, facilitating the concentration of wealth and the centralization of economic power. some of the most perverse aspects of this initiative are: liquidation of smaller companies and promotion of pan-european banking oligopoly; increase of profits of large banks, in particular by reduction of operating costs, which include the layoffs of workers, processes facilitated by the digital side and reduction of the physical location of companies; degradation of conditions of direct service to the public and job insecurity; deregulation of the economy and intensification of the free movement of capital; further suppression of the autonomy and sovereignty of the member states; and facilitation of capital flight, making it difficult to combat money laundering by states. these are goals and consequences that deserve our utter repudiation and condemnation.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, mr president, after the neo-conservative wave of the 1980s and the neo-liberal fury that deregulated the financial sector, it was soon realised that private banking needed some rules or else the whole system would be called into question. the rules created from basel 1 to 3 aim to impose minimum levels of equity capital. however, the rules for their accounting have become increasingly complex and opaque as always suits the interest groups that profit from the lack of transparency. today, the citizen learns that the risk assessment models for assets are the responsibility of the so-called systemic banks, unlike the others which are subject to a standardised model, i.e. we have, as was shown by a standard & poor's study, assets with different weights from bank to bank, i.e. we have a system in which solvency ratios and stress tests are completely manipulated by the big banks, thus removing any credibility from the supervisory system. the solution is very simple for us. credit is too important to be left to the free initiative of the private sector. public control of banking and the financial system is now more than a matter of course, it is a necessity.
mr president, mr vice-president dombrovskis, the new rules for banking supervision under basle iii, in particular the methodology for assessing credit risk, raise two particularly important questions. the first is whether or not these new regulatory requirements risk further limiting the flow of credit available to households and businesses and what safeguards the commission will adopt to protect an economy that needs credit to grow. the second issue is proportionality, so how will these rules fit into the different size, risk level and business model of the various financial institutions? what assurances can the commission give us that what is the same will be treated as the same and what is different will be treated as proportionately different?

on behalf of the gue/ngl group, mr president, we naturally support all measures aimed at improving access to information and cooperation between the tax administrations of the member states. in this respect, the inclusion of the entire body of classified information in the framework of the fight against money laundering at the level of administrative cooperation represents a positive step. we stress, however, that it seems to us essential that this information be exchanged automatically if this change is to have any practical effect. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is not left in the lurch. we believe that it is not possible to combat this phenomenon by relying solely on the due diligence of private companies and the financial system. as has been criticised by many organisations, the results of the fight against money laundering have been residual over the last few decades. this is due to the conflicts of interest of the entities with the responsibility to report suspicious movements; this is because of money laundering and the legal instruments that have been built by the developed countries in the name of economic liberalisation; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. in other words, money laundering, as well as tax fraud and evasion, is one of the visible faces of the liberal economy and the capitalist system. in this sense, the restoration of public control over banking and the financial system is also an indispensable condition for a more effective fight against these phenomena and for a better functioning of the economy.
finally, after the panama papers, bahamas leaks and other scandals, the council and the commission recognise that there is a link between the fight against tax fraud and evasion and the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing. against the onshore and offshore secrecy of crime, transparency in the financial and business sectors, more synergies and more exchange of information between law enforcement agencies, including tax authorities, are needed, as this commission proposal sets out. unfortunately, the member states reached agreement in the council without consulting parliament, but they will have to face up to what we recommend in this report by emmanuel maurel. attention should be paid to its proposals to extend the scope of subjects and the amount of data on which there should be automatic and mandatory exchange of information, including on beneficial owners of companies and other legal entities to be recorded in a publicly accessible register. to this end, we are working on the revision of the fourth anti-money laundering directive. the information in question should also be made available to the commission, by virtue of its powers to apply the state aid rules. it is essential to break down the boundaries of financial crime investigation in the european union. tax and other authorities should cooperate in carrying out cross-border investigations.

‒ this proposal for a regulation has been pending since the previous legislature, following its referral to the court of justice of the eu, following a disagreement between the european parliament and the council on the competence of the multiannual plans. the original proposal of the european commission provided for the introduction of delegated acts in the following areas: adaptation of fishing mortality rates and associated levels of biomass of the stock to scientific findings; adjustment of fishing effort in case of exclusion or re-inclusion of a group of vessels in the effort regime; specification of the rules on the method of calculating fishing capacity and adjustment of maximum capacity levels; and establishment of the rules on the method of calculation allowing member states to adapt the maximum allowable fishing effort in relation to quota management and following transfers of effort between effort groups. the report, broadly in line with the commission proposal, does however propose a stricter definition of the circumstances in which the commission may adopt delegated acts, which is considered positive. however, it is noted that this document will be replaced by a multi-species plan for the region where it is applied, which will require further and more in-depth consideration.
‒ this report aims to regulate a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, which supports, in general, the application of the principles of the new common fisheries policy and its implementation, providing eu countries with greater control at national and regional level. this policy aims to ensure that fisheries are environmentally, economically and socially sustainable and that they provide a source of healthy food for european citizens. its aim is to promote a dynamic fisheries sector and to ensure a fair standard of living for fishing communities. i voted yes.

‒ we support all measures to improve access to information and cooperation between the tax administrations of the member states. in this respect, the inclusion of the entire body of information required in the framework of the fight against money laundering at the level of administrative cooperation is a positive step. we stress, however, that only if this information is exchanged automatically can practical results be achieved. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right of initiative. it will not be possible to combat this phenomenon by relying solely on the due diligence of private companies and the financial system. as has been criticised by many organisations, the results of the fight against money laundering have been residual over the last few decades. in other words, money laundering, as well as tax fraud and evasion, is one of the faces of the liberal economy and the capitalist system. in this sense, the restoration of public control over banking and the financial system is a necessary condition for a more effective fight against these phenomena and for a better functioning of the economy.
‒ this report is about the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu, reinforcing the idea that tackling tax evasion and tax avoidance is (or should be) an eu priority. the luxleaks, panama papers and other scandals confirm the need for greater tax transparency and cooperation between jurisdictions. it is thus established that the tax authorities of the member states will automatically exchange, within three months of receipt, the documents and information communicated with any other member state if the beneficial owner of an undertaking or any other account holder is a taxpayer in that member state. furthermore, it was also decided that access should be granted to the commission for the performance of its tasks on a confidential basis. i voted yes.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the maurel report because i agree with the need to combat tax evasion in the european union effectively. the report therefore states the need to ensure that tax authorities have quick and complete access to anti-money laundering information and the need to have sufficient qualified staff to carry out this task in order to have the capacity to exchange this information. the rapporteur himself, on behalf of the european socialist group, has proposed that this exchange of information be automatic and compulsory between member states, which should include this data in a 'public centralised register' of companies, trust funds and other structures, which would be a new, more proactive approach to combating tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ the real objectives of the banking union are now clearer to more people. created under the false pretext of giving the financial system stability and taking care of the systemic banks, considered 'too big to fail', it was nothing more than a manoeuvre designed to remove from the public sphere, from the national states and their governments, under public, democratic control and scrutiny, any possibility of intervening in the system. its real objectives are to impose banking concentration on a european scale, thus aggravating the problem it is supposed to solve. in the portuguese case, the situation is glaring. with the centralisation of all supervisory and resolution functions in the ecb, the largest banks were eventually sold to foreign groups at the balance price, with the loss being borne by the taxpayers, since the resolution fund has only been financed by the portuguese state. the banking union will obviously not solve any of the problems of the economies, with or without the deposit guarantee system. because this banking union is an expression of the dominance of the financial system over the political power of the eu.
‒ this annual report on the ecb's activities for 2015 once again supports the idea that monetary policy can only achieve its full potential if it is complemented by sound fiscal policies and ambitious structural reform programmes. moreover, the loan programme at almost negative interest rates, without any conditionality, served mostly to consolidate the balance sheets of the banks, with little or no effect on the real economy. now this view is once again wrong. until we adopt a truly expansionary and distributive monetary policy, which supports sme investment and job creation by providing low-interest bank loans to peripheral member states that face the greatest difficulties in accessing credit, the objectives of sustainable economic recovery will not be achieved. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the euro area continues to experience high unemployment, excessively low inflation and large macroeconomic imbalances, including in the current account, and that the euro area is also faced with a very low level of productivity growth, which results from a lack of investment 10 percentage points below the pre-crisis level and from the absence of structural reforms as well as from a shortage of domestic demand. the high level of government debt, in particular the high volume of non-performing loans and the persistence of an undercapitalised banking sector in some member states, continue to cause fragmentation of the euro area financial market, thus reducing the room for manoeuvre that would support the weakest economies. sound fiscal policies and socially balanced structural reforms geared to increasing productivity are the only way to bring about sustainable economic improvements in these member states. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. ‒ today, it is clear that banking union, created to give the financial system stability and deal with systemic banks, dubbed too big to fail, is nothing more than a manoeuvre designed to remove from the sphere of national governments any possibility of intervening and to impose a set of merger operations between financial institutions, thus aggravating the problem it was supposed to solve. in the case of portugal, the situation is glaring. with the centralisation of all supervisory and resolution functions in the ecb, the largest banks were eventually sold to foreign groups at the balance price, with the loss being borne by the taxpayers, since the resolution fund has only been financed by the portuguese state. the banking union will obviously not solve any of the problems of the economies, with or without the deposit guarantee system. because this banking union is an expression of the domination of the financial system over the political power of the eu, which has long since given up defending the interests of the citizen to devote itself to serving the interests of those who actually rule in europe.
mr president, the financial crisis has shown two things: firstly, that financial concentration is a very dangerous thing, and secondly, that only strong regulation can protect the interests of consumers. this report seems to have forgotten both lessons. i am a strong supporter of product standardisation, but the report is very vague on this. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. it's important, but it's naive, that we think we can eliminate risk while banks sell products that consumers can't decipher. let us be honest, this report does not prevent further bank losses and so many people in europe have already lost their life savings. on the contrary, this report, for example, by eliminating restrictions on competition in retail services, will result in the formation of huge financial conglomerates and the creation of more institutions that are too big to fail. i voted against all of that. we should have learned and we didn't.
in the case of the european union, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are not undermined by the failure of the member states to implement the acquis communautaire. this initiative will lead to the liquidation of smaller companies and the promotion of pan-european banking oligopolies, with increased profits for large eu banks, notably through reduction in operational costs, including staff redundancies, digitally facilitated processes and reduction in the physical presence of companies. we will have less transparency, more fraud and tax evasion and a sharpening of the problem of 'too big to fail' companies. we cannot but reject this course.
‒ the dynamics of retail financial services, characterised by a combination of relatively high concentration and insufficient competition, can result in limited choice and low cost-effectiveness, as well as significant disparities between member states. a european market for retail financial services is only viable if it represents real added value for the consumer, ensuring effective competition, accessibility and consumer protection, in particular for products that are actually necessary for participation in economic life. the green paper initiative is timely, taking into account the need to work proactively at all stages of the decision-making process in order to respond effectively and appropriately to developments in such an innovative and rapidly changing market. that is why i am voting in favour.
in the case of the european union, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are not harmed by the introduction of the euro. an initiative that will lead to the liquidation of smaller companies and the promotion of pan-european banking oligopolies, with increased profits for large eu banks, in particular through reduction in operational costs, including the layoff of workers, processes facilitated by the digital side and reduction of the physical location of companies. we will have less transparency, more fraud and tax evasion and a sharpening of the problem of 'too big to fail' companies. we cannot but reject this path.
‒ the union retail financial services market is still lacking in strong development, particularly in the face of the low number of cross-border transactions, and measures are therefore needed to fully exploit the potential of the single market and to facilitate innovation for the benefit of end-users. a european market for retail financial services must represent a real added value for the consumer in terms of accessibility and protection of the legal sphere of retail financial services, while ensuring effective competition between the various players. in this regard, it is important to foster a competitive environment and to maintain a level playing field for all actors, in particular established and new operators. to that end, the applicable rules should be based on a model that is as neutral as possible both at technological and business level. in short, the approach set out in the green paper is important for encouraging the development of start-ups and new and innovative smes. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
‒ this green paper provides an opportunity to reflect on the possibility of further opening up the european market for retail financial services including insurance, loans, payment accounts, current and savings accounts and other retail investments producing better outcomes for consumers and businesses, while maintaining an adequate level of protection for both the consumer and the investor. it seeks to identify the specific obstacles faced by consumers and businesses in making full use of the single market and possible ways of overcoming these obstacles, including by taking better advantage of new technologies, provided that appropriate safeguards are in place. it makes perfect sense, in a cohesive union, to allow: firms based in one eu member state (em) to have greater ease in offering retail financial services in other ems; consumers to be able to buy retail financial services offered in other ems; citizens to be able to continue to enjoy their financial services products if they move from one em to another, whether for the purpose of study, work or retirement (called 'portability').
in the case of the european union, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are not harmed by the introduction of the euro. this initiative will lead to the liquidation of smaller companies and the promotion of pan-european banking oligopolies, with the increase of profits of large eu banks, in particular through the reduction of operating costs, including the layoffs of workers, processes facilitated by the digital side and the reduction of the physical location of companies. we will have less transparency, more fraud and tax evasion and a sharpening of the problem of 'too big to fail' companies. we cannot but reject this course.
‒ the establishment of a european defence union as a means of further integration is important and timely. the international challenges facing the union require a fully realised and operational common security and defence policy (csdp). i believe that the eu should exploit all the potential of the lisbon treaty, such as permanent structured cooperation or the petersberg missions, this requires financial commitment in the mff and in the annual budgets to eliminate the cost of non-europe in this area (eur 26.4 billion/year). i welcome the initiative to draw up a white paper on defence and the current consensus on further integration. i hope that this diligence and political will will be translated into concrete instruments. to this end, i believe it is urgent to implement the action plan of the eu global strategy in this area. i highlight priorities such as cybersecurity, maritime security or hybrid warfare as current challenges for european defence. in this context, i would stress the importance of scientific research for an effective approach. i believe that an edu should be an opportunity for young entrepreneurs, for european smes and for european public procurement in this area. i therefore support this report.
‒ this report reflects the ongoing process in the eu of strengthening the security perspective internally and a militarist perspective externally. the report argues that the eu must develop its military capabilities so that it can be prepared to intervene in any situation inside or outside its borders. the report considers that the european defence union will contribute to the strengthening of nato itself and to further cooperation with this organization. the report proposes cooperation and development in the industrial and military research sectors. the aim is to increase funding and support for this sector. it promotes the definition of a common arms policy. it proposes the drawing up of a white paper on defence matters. he's advocating increased spending on defense budgets. it advocates the establishment of a european armed forces. it calls for the common security and defence policy to be deepened. it advocates autonomous eu action and the development of eu military capabilities to act where nato cannot. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament. finally, the report challenges a whole dark military menu which we must vote against.
‒ this report promotes the strengthening of a security perspective at the internal level and a militarist perspective at the external level of the eu, i.e. a common arms policy. it proposes, in particular, to increase military spending by using 2% of gdp for this purpose and 20% of its defence budgets identified as necessary, in breach of article 41 (2) teu. what this report advocates is the (re) militarization of europe, based on a vision of security and a fortress europe. i voted against it.
‒ to ensure its long-term security, europe needs political will and determination backed by a broad set of relevant policy instruments, including strong and modern military capabilities. the establishment of the union's common defence policy is a step forward in the implementation of the common security and defence policy of the lisbon treaty, which is subject to international law and is effectively indispensable to enable the eu to promote the rule of law, peace and security worldwide. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ inland waterway passenger transport plays a key role in building a more sustainable and efficient european transport sector. the eu's maritime transport objective is to become a world leader in maritime research and innovation and shipbuilding, with a view to improving the efficiency and energy intelligence of ships, reducing environmental impact, minimising the risk of accidents and improving the quality of life at sea. it is necessary to eliminate bottlenecks in the links between the extended inland waterway system of western europe and the current system of eastern europe, whose degradation is marked and in some places total. the commission should develop a harmonised system for the collection of statistical data on accidents and incidents for inland waterway vessels, including cross-border traffic. member states should promote and support local initiatives to activate inland waterway transport and as a means of meeting the needs of urban agglomerations. i therefore support this report.
‒ the development of waterway transport sea and river is a very important issue for the mobility of passengers and goods, with enormous environmental and economic benefits. the operation of this transport system requires the adequacy of natural conditions and infrastructure. in recent years, the divestment of equipment and infrastructure, as well as the precariousness of work in this system, have put many services at risk. this report is based on a good principle, namely the development of inland waterway transport as a factor of territorial, social and economic cohesion; as a factor in meeting the objectives of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and increasing the environmental sustainability of transport; as a safer and more controllable means of transport. however, the way of achieving the development objectives of the sector is the same as that which has led to privatisation, deregulation, loss of quality of service and, in some cases, abandonment of the provisions of the white paper on transport, the connecting europe facility, the trans-european transport network and, as a major source of funding, the esi funds. in recognition of the importance of the sector, we cannot support this report.

‒ strengthening aid and development effectiveness has been one of the eu's main concerns over the years. with the second high level meeting of the global partnership for effective development cooperation approaching, it is necessary to take stock of the implementation of the global commitments on aid effectiveness and development. i believe that the eu should continue to play an important leadership role in these issues and be a strong contributor to the thinking and implementation of development standards. we must not forget the key role of official development assistance, recalling that most providers have not fulfilled their commitment to allocate 0.7% of gross national income; we must strive for greater coordination and transparency, demand improved public financial management and absorption capacity in the beneficiary countries and greater cooperation with the national parliaments of third countries. i would point out that only by ensuring peace, respect for human rights and the rule of law, as well as independent judicial systems and the protection of minorities, can we achieve these development goals and the achievement of the sustainable development goals.
‒ the debate in the european parliament on the effectiveness of development aid is a recurring one. the reports which deal with this issue rarely go into the depths of the matter, but rather use it to try, often in a cynical and hypocritical manner, to condition the developing countries by imposing on them models of political organization of the state, particularly as regards the ways of economic and social organization. that is what is happening once again with this report. the saving power of the market economy, the private sector, the opening up of the economies of these countries to world competition are defended. finally, the typical neoliberal recipe which has caused the economic and social disasters that are in sight (in particular as a result of the interventions of the imf and the world bank). while we agree with a number of fair observations in the report, notably the need to increase official development assistance, criticism of the failure to meet the targets set, among other aspects, what prevails is a certain neo-colonial vision evident in the references to corruption, circumscribed to references to the countries receiving aid and discrediting the eu and its policies. not a word about the harmful effects of deregulation and trade liberalization, for example.

‒ on 27 april 2009, the council authorised the commission to negotiate an economic integration agreement with canada on behalf of the european union and its member states. the negotiation and ratification of the canada comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta) took about six years. in addition, not only european and canadian experts, but also various european institutions and other supranational bodies were involved in this procedure. the agreement was approved in the european council and signed at the canada summit on 30 october 2016. i believe that ceta is in accordance with all the rules of the european legal order. in view of the foregoing and in recognition of the crucial importance of the agreement in question, i am voting against this report.

‒ in 2013, the european commission adopted a package of proposals to improve air quality in europe, called the 'air quality package'. the main part of the package is a proposal to revise the national emission ceilings directive (nec). the current european commission considered withdrawing the proposal in 2014, but due to strong resistance from the european parliament and several ngos the proposal was maintained. the revised nec directive provides for controls on different types of pollutants in the member states. it will aim to halve the number of premature deaths estimated at 400 000 per year in the eu caused by air pollution by 2030. this proposal for revision sets new national emission reduction commitments, applicable from 2020 and 2030, for sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), non-methane volatile organic compounds (nvocs) and ammonia (nh3), and for fine particulate matter (pm2,5) and methane (ch4) as well. as a result of the vote in the environment committee, among other things, mercury (hg) was added to the list of pollutants, the 2025 average targets were added to the legislation, methane targets were postponed until 2030 (to give the agricultural sector time to adapt) and the european commission's flexibility proposal was dropped.
‒ this report concerns the emission of certain air pollutants with a view to their reduction and the improvement of air quality conditions. initially, the measures proposed by the european parliament and the commission were much stronger. however, these measures suffered several limitations and cuts during the negotiations with the council, supported by several eu countries. based on a recent who report, air pollution is the greatest environmental health hazard, with an estimated three million air pollution-related deaths occurring each year. this report, among other weaknesses, does not include some air pollutants whose emission seriously threatens the environment and health. i voted against it.
‒ policy-making based on hard data should be the cornerstone of eu legislation. laws should be based on robust and comprehensive impact assessments, which explain why the legislation addresses the fundamental questions of whether a proposal is necessary and proportionate and evaluates the best action at eu level. in the case of air quality, the answer is clear: it is a significant cross-border human health and environmental issue, which deeply affects all eu citizens and requires immediate action. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ in 2013, the european commission adopted the 'air quality package' of proposals to improve air quality in europe. the main part of the package is a proposal to revise the national emission ceilings directive (nec). the current european commission considered withdrawing the proposal in 2014, but due to strong resistance from the european parliament and several ngos the proposal was maintained. the revised nec directive provides for controls on different types of pollutants in the member states. it will aim to halve the number of premature deaths estimated at 400 000 per year in the eu caused by air pollution by 2030. this proposal for revision sets new national emission reduction commitments, applicable from 2020 and 2030, for sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), non-methane volatile organic compounds (nvocs) and ammonia (nh3), and for fine particulate matter (pm2,5) and methane (ch4) as well. as a result of the vote in the environment committee, among other things, mercury (hg) was added to the list of pollutants, the 2025 average targets were added to the legislation, methane targets were postponed until 2030 (to give the agricultural sector time to adapt) and the european commission's flexibility proposal was dropped.
in writing. this proposal on the reduction of national emissions of certain air pollutants is part of the clean air for europe programme announced by the commission on 18 december 2013. after years of political neglect, air pollution has emerged on the international agenda as a major public health problem. there is no doubt that poor air quality contributes to premature death, sickness absence from work, lost productivity, lost crop yields and damage to buildings. significant health costs are another consequence of poor air quality, with the total external health-related costs to society from air pollution in europe estimated at between eur 330 and 940 billion per year. the commission proposal repeals and replaces the existing directive on national emission limit values for certain air pollutants, setting new emission limit values for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, ammonia and non-metallic volatile organic compounds for 2020 and 2030. since these values reflect the limits that have been agreed internationally under the gothenburg protocol and since only compliance with these limits by the member states will enable them to meet their emission reduction targets, i voted in favour.
‒ poor air quality is responsible for about 400 000 deaths a year. added to this is the enormous financial effort in medical care. the commission has adopted a proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs. it's a more ambitious proposal. different limits are defined for each member state and for each pollutant. the proposal is the result of difficult negotiations with the council. there were several controversial issues between the groups, mainly those related to the inclusion of methane and the demand for less ambitious targets for ammonia. it was agreed to support the full inclusion of ammonia and to exempt enteric methane emissions from ruminant cattle. the s&ds wanted more ambitious targets, but we support the agreement as it is the best that can be achieved without risking the directive being retained indefinitely in the council.
‒ this report concerns the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the reduction of national emissions of certain atmospheric pollutants and amending directive 2003/35/ec. i would remind you that air pollution is responsible for more than 400 000 premature deaths per year throughout the european union. with the adoption of this report, parliament approved new national emission reduction targets, setting national emission limit values for certain air pollutants such as sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and fine particulate matter. new targets are also set to reduce the health impacts of air pollution by around 50% by 2030, with different limits for each member state and each pollutant. i therefore voted in favour of the amendments contained in this proposal for a directive, as they contribute to improving air quality and combating environmental and public health problems.
in writing. the report finds that after years of political neglect, air pollution has emerged on the political agenda as a major public health problem. poor air quality contributes to premature death, sickness absence from work, significant health costs, lost productivity, lost crop yields and damage to buildings. thus, according to the report, in europe, the total external costs to society related to health and caused by air pollution are estimated at between eur 330 and 940 billion per year. in addition, there is a growing body of evidence that atmospheric nitrogen deposition is leading to changes in the natural environment with impacts on biodiversity. unfortunately, the real causes of this inertia are not addressed, and the appeal is to ever more complex and ineffective regulation. for our part, pollution and the inability to deal with this problem stem from the policies of privatisation of vast sectors of the economy, including transport and energy, condemning the states to be mere passive spectators of the progressive destruction of the planet.
in the first place, the commission has not yet taken a decision on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. i would stress that poor air quality is responsible for more than 400 000 premature deaths every year and has an estimated health impact of between 300 and 900 billion euros each year. i therefore welcome the proposals in this report to set more ambitious air quality targets, which will reduce the number of premature deaths from toxic air by almost half by 2030. i would also stress the role of clean electric mobility as an option that can make a very significant contribution to the fight against the reduction of emissions harmful to health. finally, i would also like to stress the global call made in marrakesh to maintain the trajectory of combating global warming, and this directive, now amended, will make an important contribution to this by the european union.
‒ in the face of the neo-liberal offensive of the 1980s and the deregulatory and liberalising fury that deregulated the financial sector, it was soon realised that private banking needed some rules or else the whole system would be called into question. the rules created from basel i to iii aim to impose minimum levels of equity capital. however, the rules for their accounting have become increasingly complex and opaque, as befits interest groups that always take advantage of the lack of transparency. today, asset risk assessment models are the responsibility of the so-called systemic banks, unlike others which are subject to a standardised model. so we have in practice assets with different weights from bank to bank. so we have a system where the solvency ratios and the stress tests are completely manipulated by the big banks, thus taking away any credibility from the entire supervisory system. the solution is simple for us. credit is too important to be left to the free initiative of the private sector. public control of the banking and financial system is now more than ever a necessity.
‒ banks need to be well capitalised to support the real economy, reduce systemic risk and avoid a repeat of the massive bailouts seen during the crisis. adequate regulation of the shadow banking sector is necessary to ensure fair competition and financial stability. a resilient and well-capitalised banking system is a prerequisite for preserving financial stability, ensuring adequate credit supply to the real economy over the cycle and enhancing economic growth. that is why i am voting in favour.
