‒ the european union faces a set of threats, both conventional and hybrid, created by states and non-state actors from the south and the east. this complex framework requires an operational and effective common security and defence policy (csdp). this is recognised by two thirds of european citizens, who favour greater european commitment to security and defence (eurobarometer). to this end, i advocate a revision of the csdp to establish the permanent structured cooperation provided for in the treaties. i believe that the increase in defence investment (ideally to 2% of gdp) should be complemented by better defence procurement processes and include greater support for research. we need a more capable and competitive defence industry. i support the desire to establish a permanent eu headquarters for civil and military operations, but i am alert to the need to coordinate action with nato as a pillar of europe's collective defence. in this respect, the eu-nato relationship should be strengthened and include cooperation with other partners such as the african union or the osce. i share the concern about cybersecurity as the most urgent vector in greater defence cooperation. i therefore support this report.
‒ this report pursues essentially the same objectives as the report on the so-called european defence union, adopted at the same session. increased defence budgets of the member states, financing and development of military industry and research, creation of european military forces, specialisation of military forces by member state, increased cooperation with nato and the eu's ambition to become a military bloc. all in the name of fighting terrorism, radicalisation and reinforcing the confrontation and the siege of russia, obliterating any analysis of eu responsibilities in military conflicts in neighbouring regions. the report is part of the militaristic escalation that is taking place in the eu and that the eu is actively promoting, with the european parliament playing its part. this attitude is fuelling the arms race, not forgetting nuclear, is increasing world tensions, is contrary to commitments made under the non-proliferation and disarmament treaty, and is increasing the risks of a large-scale military conflict with unforeseen consequences. a policy which is opposed to and compromises peace, and which is not detached from the policies of exploitation and impoverishment of the workers and peoples. the eu reveals its true face as an enemy of peace. we could only vote against it, of course.

in writing. ‒ in europe alone, there are about one million sign language users and more than 50 million people with a hearing disability. these figures are sufficient to understand the impact of any measure in this area. however, there is no holistic approach at european level to this issue, which must take into account the increasing mobility of citizens, with the resulting language barriers, as well as the specificities of the online world, in particular in access to public services. this resolution identifies these challenges in detail and presents a set of solutions and best practices, intended to be a first step towards their implementation. in this connection, parliament - as this resolution proposes - must implement a set of measures to combat unjustified discrimination within the home. i therefore support this resolution.
‒ the issues of sign language and interpreting are of paramount importance. this resolution comes a few days after the national day of portuguese sign language, an event that should be valued in respect for the inclusion of its users. the cfp has taken some measures in this direction through its intervention in the assembly of the republic. here are some measures to consider: - the need to provide technical support for deaf pupils, including interpretation (so that it is not paid for by the families); - considering that few companies have the resources to include deaf people, it is important to promote services that promote an inclusive policy (availability of interpreters); - to promote the recognition of sign languages as official languages; - to involve associations of deaf people in policy-making; - improve the professional status of interpreters and teachers of sign language by placing them on an equal footing with equivalent professionals (other language interpreters and teachers); - allow bilingual people/children to enter schools which use sign language; - develop technologies that enable access to emergency or other services (such as the recently announced measure '112'). this resolution, which is of an eminently technical nature, emphasizes the needs of deaf people. many of the issues that are part of our proposals in this area are included. we voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ as full citizens, all persons with disabilities, including deaf and hard of hearing persons, including those who use and those who do not use sign language, enjoy the same rights and have the inalienable right to dignity, equal treatment, independent living, autonomy and full participation in society. the eu institutions should be an example of good practice to eu citizens in adopting reasonable accommodation measures and accessibility measures, including the provision of sign language interpretation. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the issues of sign language and interpreting are of extreme relevance in the face of the continued disregard for the rights of deaf people and their families. the resolution incorporates many of the issues on which we have been speaking with concrete proposals, including: - the need to provide technical support for deaf pupils, including interpretation; - the need to promote services that promote an inclusive policy, seeking to counteract the exclusion factors, including access to employment, to which deaf people are subject; - the need to recognise sign languages as official languages; - the need to involve associations of deaf people in policy-making; - the need to improve the professional status of interpreters and sign language teachers by equipping them with equivalent professionals; - the need to allow bilingual people and children to enter schools that use sign language; - the need to develop technologies that allow access to emergency or other services. the resolution, which is eminently technical, rightly emphasizes the needs of deaf people, which is why it was voted in favour.
‒ all european citizens deserve equal treatment and equal opportunities, regardless of their differences. in this sense, in view of the provisions of the tfeu, the european union must combat potential inequalities in the definition and implementation of its policies and activities. in this context, citizens with special needs, such as deaf and other hearing impaired persons, including those who communicate through sign language, should enjoy the same status as the rest of society. thus, the human dignity inherent in their existence and inalienable, as well as the right to equal treatment, autonomy and full and active participation in society, must be guaranteed to these citizens. today, there are about one million deaf people in the european union, as well as 51 million citizens with severe hearing impairments who communicate using sign language. the recognition of sign language as an official language in the member states and their organisations is therefore crucial. consequently, my vote is in favour.

‒ all citizens, and in particular citizens with disabilities, are entitled to equal rights, including the right to dignity, equal treatment, independent living, autonomy and full participation in society. there are currently around one million sign language users in the european union (eu) and 51 million citizens with a hearing impairment, many of whom are sign language users. the tfeu states that the eu aims to combat discrimination on the grounds of disability in the definition and implementation of its policies and actions, and therefore gives the eu mechanisms to adopt legislation to combat such discrimination. the proposal lists measures for the eu to strengthen the promotion of the qualifications of interpreters and sign language professionals, the inclusion of sign language in the various public services, the political and democratic process and digital services. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i consider the provision of sign language interpretation to be a fundamental measure which helps to combat discrimination and facilitates the inclusion of millions of people with hearing impairments.

in writing. ‒ in accordance with the time-limit laid down in regulation (eu) no 1141/2010, an application was submitted for the renewal of the authorisation of the active substance benthazone, as the authorisation initially expired on 30 june 2016. this resolution opposes the draft implementing measure of the european commission approving the renewal of the substance for another 15 years. there are legitimate concerns regarding the effects of this active substance on the environment, which justify the further development and improvement of the available knowledge with a view to taking the measures necessary for the protection of the environment and public health. it should be borne in mind that the substance is highly dependent on certain crops, such as rice, and that there are currently no restrictions on the use of bentazone, whereas in the past the substance was only authorised for use as a herbicide. in view of the problem of the lack of alternative, which is cited by several producers, it would be appropriate to consider immediately the compulsory reduction of the doses of application and the concentration of this active substance, while taking into account the role of the adjuvants, the necessary inhibition of harmful parallel actions and thus the facilitation of decomposition.
‒ the active substance bentazone acts as a selective post-emergence herbicide against broadleaf weed infestants on a wide range of crops and is commonly used in agriculture. the active substance bentazone, due to its intrinsic properties, has a high potential for leaching into groundwater. in view of the foregoing and the terms in which this proposal was put forward, i voted against.

in writing. - i voted against this motion for a resolution which objects to the renewal of the approval of the active substance bentazone, which in portugal is registered in maize, rice and peas, the two main staple crops of national agriculture. this type of herbicide has proven to be an important tool for farmers as it contributes to the maintenance of sustainable pest control of the crops for which it is authorised. for this reason, and because both the report and efsa stress that this substance does not represent an increased risk to human health or the environment, i considered that there would be insufficient reasons to object to its renewal, especially in view of the impact that such a measure would have on european farmers in general and portuguese farmers in particular.

‒ the report states that the directive should ensure that institutions have an appropriate level of freedom to invest, with institutions that run occupational pension schemes being able to invest in shares, multilateral trading facilities, organised trading facilities. the limitation of risk management by quantitative requirements is also assumed and it is therefore essential to ensure an effective governance system. this solution implies that pensions are at the mercy of the suitability of the manager and the performance of the products in which the pension money is invested. in a scenario where the number of defined contribution occupational pension schemes is increasing, this becomes potentially problematic and dangerous. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. we do not regard pension funds as a commonplace financial product. we are against the creation of a single pension market and against the creation of pension schemes at european level.

‒ this own-initiative report is a response by the european parliament to the action plan on vat published by the european commission in april this year. it provides for the harmonization of rates and more rigid lists of products subject to reduced rates, a position with which we disagree. it also provides for a new system of collection in international transactions with tax payable at the place of purchase. the report considers that the goods and services to which reduced rates may be applied should be reduced. it considers that for some of the goods and services for which reduced rates may be applied, this should be fixed jointly at eu level. for our part, we believe that the minimum and reduced rates of vat play a positive, redistributive role in a tax which is highly regressive and, for that reason, we do not accept that the way in which the minimum and reduced rates of vat are defined should be changed for the worse in the name of reducing complexity and the consequent obstacles to competition and the single market.
the report proposes to change the current transitional vat regime in the european union to a definitive regime based on the principle of taxation in the country of origin of the supply of goods and services. in 2014, vat revenue reached almost eur 1 trillion, corresponding to 7% of eu gdp, constituting an important financial source of own resources for the eu. unfortunately, the current vat system has been subject to tax fraud and evasion from the outset. the commission estimates that the vat gap due to fraud amounts to eur 170 billion annually, of which eur 50 billion is due to crossborder fraud. in this connection, there is an urgent need for reform of this system, simplification of bureaucratic and administrative systems and consequent reduction of regulatory costs, as well as greater coordination between member states in the application and monitoring of the system. despite some shortcomings, such as the assessment of the social impact of these measures, this report presents some important steps towards the implementation of the vat reform and the fight against fraud. i abstained.
‒ the commission communication of 7 april 2016 on a vat action plan put an end to the long delay in moving towards a single vat area in the eu, pointing out that the time to decide has come. the commission has announced that it will present a legislative proposal on a definitive vat system, which will be based on the principle that goods and services are taxed in the country of destination. with this proposal the commission is definitively departing from the principle of taxation in the country of origin origin originally requested, which is apparently not feasible due to a number of problems and distortions of competition. in concrete terms, this means that the tax provision under which the supplier of goods charges vat to the customer will extend to cross-border trade, thus significantly reducing the opportunities for vat fraud. i agree with the future amendments proposed by the commission, hence my vote in favour.
‒ this own-initiative report is a response by the european parliament to the action plan on vat published by the commission in april this year. it provides for the harmonization of rates and more rigid listing of products subject to reduced rates. it also provides for a new system of collection in international transactions with tax payable at the place of purchase. it also called for the commission to be given the power to adopt legislative acts to ensure that the rules on the free movement of goods and services are respected. we believe that the minimum and reduced rates of vat play a redistributive role in a tax which is highly regressive and therefore we do not accept that the way in which the minimum and reduced rates of vat are defined should be changed for the worse in the name of reducing complexity and the consequent obstacles to competition and the single market.
in writing. the commission's communication on a vat action plan, published in april this year, suggests new proposals and guidelines towards a single vat area in the eu. this tax is an important source of revenue for the union as a whole, corresponding to 7% of gdp. however, the current system is unreliable and highly susceptible to fraud. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that this proposal is insufficient and does not represent a fundamental reform, since this would require the introduction of a system of self-assessment throughout europe and in all trade between companies. it is a simpler, more unified and more durable system with less revenue loss and less fraud. since this is already the case in other member states, it is hard to understand why the commission should not be more demanding and make a bolder proposal to apply this system uniformly to all the member states. in view of the above and in agreement with the rapporteur's views, i voted in favour of adopting this report.

‒ wildlife trafficking is an international organised crime worth an estimated €20 billion a year, making it one of the most lucrative forms of organised cross-border crime in the world. wildlife trafficking has major negative impacts on biodiversity, existing ecosystems, the natural heritage of the countries of origin, natural resources and species conservation. i welcome the action plan against wildlife trafficking, which stresses the need for coordinated action to address the causes of wildlife trafficking, to effectively implement and enforce the rules in force, and for the implementation of the plan, adequate human and financial resources in the community budget and in national budgets are needed. it is also necessary to provide assistance, guidance and training to the authorities in the countries of origin, transit and destination with regard to investigation, enforcement and judicial proceedings at local, regional and national level. i therefore support this report.
‒ wildlife crime, such as poaching, illegal trade in species or illegal transit of wildlife products and derivatives, has become a multi-billion euro criminal industry dominated by organised crime groups. the risk of detection is low and the financial impact is high, attracting criminal gangs to exploit illegally captured, moved and traded wildlife to fund their criminal activity. the eu is a major destination for illegal wildlife products, as well as a transit point and often source for wildlife trafficking, especially between africa, asia and latin america, and therefore has responsibilities in combating this phenomenon. the eu action plan presented by the commission lists a number of measures to be taken by the eu institutions or by the member states. the main aim of the measures is to improve cooperation between all actors, to make more effective use of existing instruments and policies and to strengthen synergies between them, so that the fight against wildlife trafficking can be tackled more effectively across the eu and globally. we voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ all companies play a crucial role in the transport of passengers and goods. thanks to a more specific knowledge of the local market, greater proximity to the customer and innovation capacity, small businesses improve individual passenger transport. small transport companies are therefore inherent in european mobility. new technologies are driving the modernisation of the mobility economy. these platforms, particularly those linked to the sharing economy, are introducing a radical change in the transport landscape by optimising the impact of supply and demand at the same time. in the face of the arrival of new operators, legal uncertainty regarding the definition of transport service providers prevents the creation of fair competition and hampers many ambitions of small companies. i support the need to accelerate efforts to complete the single european transport area by ending disparities in the application of the law. we should encourage convergence between the traditional and the platform economies and their collaborative economy models in order to foster innovation, consumer protection and fair competition. i therefore support this report, which will help to improve urban mobility in the future, which will be totally low-carbon.
‒ this report aims to focus on the need to boost the transport market at the level of small and medium-sized enterprises, with a special focus on companies in the so-called collaborative economy. in fact, it is intended to whitewash the ongoing process of deregulation of the sector and to pave the way for the multinationals that aspire to dominate it. the report diagnoses the reality of the sector, with references to the existence of monopolies (which would not be good for its development), the great flexibility brought by digitisation, in contrast to the over-regulation, protectionism and corporatism that put the internal market in question. the report welcomes the emergence of new models of the collaborative economy, which the eu should support (considering the opportunities opened up by the efsi and taking into account that the majority of those operating in the internal market are american), criticizing the fragmented response of the member states to the growth of these models, which would be inconsistent with the potential and benefits of the sector and contrary to consumer expectations. the report also advocates flexible working patterns, which would be beneficial for workers. the report conceals the lack of support for public transport policies and public mobility strategies. their purpose is different: to promote the ubers of this life. we voted against it.
‒ in the absence of relevant statistical data, the reality of small transport enterprises in europe is difficult to assess. while their importance varies from one mode to another (road, inland waterway and maritime transport are heavily targeted, rail and air transport somewhat less), there is no precise way of knowing their number, their share of employment or their share of the wealth created within the union. small transport companies play a key role in the smooth functioning of mobility in europe, but often face difficulties in accessing or remaining in the market, in particular due to the existence of monopolies in this market. it is time we did something to change this situation and help these companies to develop more appropriately and more effectively. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ it is important that we look at the challenges and opportunities facing small businesses in the transport sector, particularly in the context of a collaborative economy and new business models, especially in the context of smes, micro-enterprises and start-ups. we also need to be mindful of the digital economy and its influence on changing the way small transport companies operate.
‒ this initiative report focuses on new opportunities for small and medium-sized transport enterprises, including collaborative business models. stresses that small transport companies are indeed essential for a strong, dynamic and economically viable digital economy, and that there must be collaborative business models that create new business opportunities for such companies, which are often confronted with legal and bureaucratic complexity as well as unfair competition created by protectionist national mechanisms, which generate legal uncertainty; the new collaborative business models should therefore be geared towards technological innovation, based on greater legislative and procedural de-bureaucratization, which provides more fairness, greater balance and is capable of generating greater competitiveness and efficiency for small transport companies, so that they too can promote greater interconnection between consumers and producers and thus help the process of economic, social and territorial cohesion of the regions. as regards the digital platforms that have revolutionised the transport sector, i agree that the logic should be to open up to innovation and fair competition, in a spirit of cooperation and harmonisation of the regulation of these innovative segments with the traditional sectors.
‒ digitalisation and the services of the so-called collaborative economy have interesting benefits from the user's point of view that cannot be ignored. what the report omits, however, is the policy of privatisation of transport services and the depletion of public transport services, which reduces the quality of service to users, deregulates labour relations and removes responsibility from policy makers for mobility strategies - increasingly linked to the market and to an on-demand, individualised logic. because this report conceals the lack of support for public transport policies and public mobility strategies and because it focuses on direct competition between so-called collaborative companies outside the eu and those that may be set up in the eu (forgetting the contradictions that, for example, uber promotes from the point of view of taxation or the application of labour legislation), not in its regulation, we cannot support it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the riquet report for agreeing to a coherent european approach to supporting the emergence of new business models for small transport companies. i would stress the call on the commission to take into account the difficulty of penetration of new collaborative business models in rural and non-urban environments when drawing up guidelines on this matter. i also stress that the opportunities arising from the development of connected and self-piloted vehicles (cars, ships, drones, platooning) should lead the commission to present a roadmap on connected and automated vehicles and to analyse the potential effects that this technology may have on the european transport sector, especially in small and medium-sized enterprises.
‒ the eu has an important role to play in the democratization effort of belarus, a country of key geostrategic importance. i am against the death penalty under any circumstances, and i cannot accept that it has been carried out four times this year alone. i support the call for belarus to join the international moratorium, but i am in principle in favour of its abolition. i share the concern about the transparency of electoral acts, considering the difficulties of the 2015 presidential and 2016 parliamentary elections. i believe that a thorough electoral reform must be undertaken to facilitate the formation of political parties and to promote citizen participation. the eu cannot accept political imprisonment. i am in favour of the immediate restoration of all civil rights to released political prisoners and a comprehensive reform of the administrative and criminal codes which preserves freedom of expression and of the press. i am concerned about the construction of a nuclear power station in ostrovets, near lithuania and poland. i believe that any decision on visa facilitation must take account of the respect for fundamental rights by the belarusian authorities. i support the motion for a resolution because it takes all these aspects into account.
in writing. - this resolution continues a line of external interference and interference with the political and social situation in belarus, which we consider unacceptable. the resolution addresses the 'approach' of belarus to the eu, which led to the lifting of some of the previously applied sanctions, in a process that imposed changes, which the resolution says were made 'reluctantly'. the electoral process in belarus is criticized, while other electoral processes, such as georgia's, are praised, all depending on the interests that the winners are (or are not) available to serve. two weights, two measures. the resolution develops the eu's view of the situation in ukraine. it takes into account what the belarusian people want or desire. it defends interference in the internal situation in belarus by supporting 'civil society organisations'. it criticises belarus' options in the field of energy policy. whatever our opinion or position on the belarusian government, whether it be for reservations or for reasons of distance, the line of interference which this resolution develops is unacceptable. it is up to each people to define the political, economic and social system that best meets their interests and aspirations. it is not for the eu to make these decisions. we voted against it.

in writing. - this resolution continues a policy of external interference and interference with the political and social situation in belarus with a view to its internal change, in line with the interests of the european union. despite identifying what they identify as belarus's rapprochement with the eu, the resolution proceeds with a barrage of considerations, recommendations and demands that are absolutely unacceptable in the logic of institutional relations with a sovereign state and that violate international law. he calls for reforms to the belarusian electoral system and talks about democratization of the country. it considers the judicial system and the principles of the rule of law in that country. it promotes external support for so-called independent organizations and information sources, which of course are in direct confrontation with the belarusian government. it presents criticisms of the country's development model aimed at its conditioning. regardless of the economic, social and political development model of that country, we consider it unacceptable that the eu should always be in the lead in relation to third countries, daring to lecture and directly interfere where it should not, and thus destabilising states. it is up to each people, within the framework of its supreme sovereignty, to decide on the directions and paths of development of its country. we voted against it.

participatory model of internet governance. the 2016 global forum, to be held in guadalajara, mexico, from 6 to 8 december, under the banner of inclusion and sustainable growth, will now consolidate the model of governance with evidence, founded on democratic values and based on networks of user forums structured at national, regional and global levels. it is essential to ensure that, with the in writing. ‒ this report aims at amending article 136 of the union customs code, which entered into force on 1 may 2016. the possibility of requiring the presentation of goods which have temporarily left the customs territory of the eu by sea or air is not currently enshrined. the customs authorities thus face difficulties in carrying out their supervisory activity in respect of these goods, since they cannot control them. in order to ensure equal treatment of goods and the effective application of the union customs code, it is necessary to amend the wording of that article. i voted yes.
in the absence of a clear legal basis for requiring the presentation of goods to customs authorities, customs authorities find their customs supervision difficult in practice, as they will not be able to: ensure the correct application of import duties and other charges, ensure the correct application of non-tax measures such as health checks and identify the risks of goods arriving at their ports or airports. the proposal to amend article 136 is intended to fill this gap and thus ensure equal treatment for goods and restore the legal basis previously established by the old customs code, hence my favourable opinion.
in writing. the entry into force on 1 may 2016 of the provisions of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the european parliament and of the council of 9 october 2013 laying down the union customs code has exposed certain clear loopholes in its drafting. the current article 136 of the treaty does not provide the competent authorities of the member states with a legal basis for the application of the lodging of the entry summary declaration, the notification of the arrival of a seagoing vessel or aircraft, the forwarding and presentation of goods to customs after unloading or transhipment, the waiting period for authorisation before unloading or transhipment of goods and the provisions governing temporary storage. the provisions of this article shall apply to goods which have temporarily left the customs territory of the union, travelling between two points in that territory by sea or air, and if the transport has been carried out by a direct route without a stop outside the customs territory of the union. the proposal to amend article 136 aims to fill this gap and ensure equal treatment for goods and to restore the legal basis previously established by the old customs code.
‒ article 136 of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 on intra-union air and sea services has been amended, which provides that a set of articles is not applicable to non-eu goods or to eu goods if they have temporarily left the customs territory of the eu, travelling between two points in that territory by sea or air, and if the transport has been made by a direct route, without a stop outside the customs territory of the eu. the current article 136 does not provide the competent authorities of the member states with a legal basis for applying a set of provisions, and there is no clear legal basis for requiring the presentation of goods to customs authorities. the problem is that the customs authorities are limited in their supervisory powers. the proposal to amend the existing regulation aims to ensure equal treatment for goods and to restore the legal basis previously established in the old customs code.
‒ this report concerns the need to amend article 136 of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the european parliament and of the council establishing the union customs code, given the existence of content gaps which demonstrate the absence of a clear legal basis for requiring the presentation of goods to customs authorities. this makes it difficult for customs to supervise, in particular, the correct application of import duties, non-tax measures such as health checks and the identification of risks of goods arriving at their ports or airports. as this is a change in the legal basis of the regulatory framework, which will give greater legal certainty and security to the competent authorities of the member states in the application and enforcement of the regulations in customs matters, i voted in favour of adopting this report.
‒ the issue is the amendment of article 136 of regulation (eu) no 952/2013, which concerns intra-union air and maritime services and provides that a number of articles do not apply to non-eu goods or to eu goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the eu, if they have temporarily left the customs territory of the union, moving between two points in that territory by sea or air, and if the transport has been made by a direct route, without a stop outside the customs territory of the eu. the absence of a (clear) legal basis for requiring the presentation of goods to customs authorities raises the problem that the authorities may be limited in their supervisory powers. the aim of this proposal for a regulation is to ensure equal treatment for goods and to replace the legal basis previously established by the old customs code.
‒ this report is based on regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 of the european parliament and of the council, which introduces a series of measures to strengthen investor and consumer protection and restore investor and consumer confidence in financial services. the date set for its entry into force was 31 december 2016. however, on the grounds of increased transparency in the financial investment market and the need for time for the parties concerned to comply with the new requirements, a delay of 12 months is proposed for the entry into force of the regulation. the delay is excessive because the regulation is urgently needed and there is a risk that during this period certain demands from the financial services industry will be met and that the provisions of the regulation on consumer protection will be distorted. i abstained.
in writing. regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 was adopted on 26 november 2014 with the aim of strengthening the protection of retail investors in packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (priips). in addition, it aims to restore consumer confidence in the financial services sector in the wake of the financial crisis. in order to meet those objectives, regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 requires priip manufacturers to comply with a uniform set of product disclosure requirements and retail investors to receive the key information document on the proposed priips. the information disclosed should enable retail investors to better understand the economic nature and risks of a specific product and to compare different products offered. that's why i'm in favour.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 of the european parliament and of the council introduced measures to strengthen investor protection and restore consumer confidence in the financial services sector by increasing transparency in the retail investment market. it requires manufacturers of packaged retail investment products and insurance-based investment products to draw up a key information document. on 30 june 2016, the commission adopted a delegated regulation supplementing the regulation by specifying the presentation, content of the key information document, its standardised format, the methodology underlying the risk and reward presentation, the cost calculation, the conditions and the minimum frequency of review of the information in the document. on 14 september 2016, the ep objected to the regulation and called, together with the vast majority of member states, for a postponement of the date of application of the regulation to give everyone more time to comply with the new requirements. it is therefore relevant and appropriate to amend regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 accordingly.
‒ the ec's proposal to impose more regulation on the priip sector emerged, albeit belatedly, as a response to the financial crisis. the proposed reforms are designed to protect retail investors from the financial sector selling inappropriate and high-risk products without providing appropriate information beforehand. the report, adopted in econ by a simplified procedure, aims to postpone by one year the date of adoption of regulation 1286/2014 (on priips tier one), i.e. the requirements to provide priips key information documents to retail investors will only come into effect on 1 january 2018. it would be desirable that the requirements for the key information document be implemented as soon as possible. however, it should be avoided that the regulation enters into force until the regulatory technical names have been defined. however, this does not justify a one-year delay in the obligation to submit the sid. the 'delay' may rather be related to the fact that the european parliament and the ec have agreed to revise the regulatory technical standards in line with the interests of the sector. this is yet another act designed to benefit big finance and monopoly capital to the detriment of workers and peoples.
‒ i supported this report which concerns a proposal to amend regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 on key information documents for insurance-based investment products and retail investment product packages. the regulation in question provides for a set of measures aimed at strengthening and restoring consumer confidence in the financial services sector with a view to greater transparency in the retail investment market by enabling various regulatory and supervisory authorities to draw up technical standards specifying the elements to be included in the documentary information drawn up by the entities which carry out these packages of retail investment products and insurance-based investment products. however, the amendments to the regulation in the meantime, concerning the format, methodology, cost calculation, revision and other formalities to be included in the documentary information, require a longer period of time for interested parties to comply with these new requirements. in this respect, i endorsed the proposal to postpone the entry into force of the regulation by 12 months, so that the amendments to the regulation apply from 1 january 2018.

‒ the european union has a visa policy, in particular with regard to the short-stay visa waiver. this exemption is defined at european level, since it is valid for all member states except the united kingdom and ireland. the various conditions for the conclusion of the agreement include reciprocity. in other words, european citizens no longer need a visa either. it is up to the european parliament to give its approval to the agreement for its establishment, which is given. for all these reasons, and because this agreement is the culmination of the deepening of relations with the republic of kiribati, i am voting in favour of its conclusion.
in writing. relations between the european union and the republic of kiribati are governed by the partnership agreement between the african, caribbean and pacific states, of the one part, and the european union and its member states, of the other part, referred to as the cotonou agreement. the agreement provides for a visa-free regime for citizens of the european union and the republic of kiribati travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (common, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders), regardless of the purpose of stay, except for the pursuit of a paid activity. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ with the amendment of regulation (ec) no 539/2001 by regulation (eu) no 509/2014 of the european parliament and of the council, the republic of kiribati was transferred to annex ii, which establishes the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement to cross the external borders of the member states. regulation (ec) no 539/2001 as amended shall apply to all member states with the exception of ireland and the united kingdom. following the adoption of that regulation, on 20 may 2014 the council adopted a decision authorising the commission to open negotiations for the conclusion of a bilateral agreement between the eu and the republic of kiribati. the agreement provides for a visa-free regime for eu citizens and nationals of the republic of kiribati travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (common, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders), regardless of the purpose of stay, except for the pursuit of a paid activity. i am therefore in favour of concluding the agreement.

‒ this decision is intended to grant visa exemption to citizens of the european union and reciprocally to citizens of the republic of kiribati travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in each 180-day period. the agreement is the culmination of the deepening of relations between the two parties, and is of political importance within the framework of the cotonou agreement, promoting the strengthening of economic and cultural relations. quiribati is a democratic republic that respects human rights constitutionally. however, it is expected that the political dialogue on this matter will be intensified. the agreement will not only make travel more viable for businessmen but also facilitate travel for european citizens, thus investment and the dynamisation of the economy and tourism. i agree with the position taken in this report on the importance of visa-free travel as a means of bringing the peoples of europe and the pacific closer together, and of fully benefiting from the acp-eu partnership.

‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to provide the union with an instrument to respond to major natural disasters, such as the 2002 floods in central europe, which prompted the creation of the fund. over the years, some €3.8 billion has been mobilised to respond to more than 70 disasters, making it a real symbol of solidarity within the eu. i share the concern about the delays in the eusf procedures. i would stress the need to ensure greater speed and less red tape in the processing of applications, the mobilisation of funds and the preparation of implementation and closure reports. i believe that the use of the eusf must respect the strictest principles of sound financial management and that independence and transparency in the award, management and implementation of the eusf must be guaranteed. the resulting sharing of good practice is essential to progressively improve this instrument. i believe that sustainable reconstruction and other post-disaster activities should be part of the structural funds, but that the evaluation of the implementation of the eusf should result in recommendations for reconstruction to be in line with the purpose of prevention and adaptation of infrastructure. i therefore support the report.
in writing. following the tragic floods of 2002, the european union established the european union solidarity fund (regulation (ec) no 2012/2002) as an immediate expression of the union's solidarity with countries affected by major natural disasters. the eusf has been put to good use and has helped many countries. however, improvements are always possible, which is why this report was drawn up in order to find better solutions for the future. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the report, making a positive assessment of the implementation of this fund and the acuteness of the reform, suggests that member states optimise synergies with the strategic investment funds - in terms of developing natural disaster prevention, adaptation and mitigation instruments - and that reconstruction and these natural disaster prevention, adaptation and mitigation instruments always take into account the sustainability of reconstruction and resources, increasing resilience to the randomness of disasters. the report also makes a number of positive suggestions to the commission, including: increasing the threshold for advances from 10% to 15%; reducing the time taken to process applications from six to four weeks; fixing the eligibility threshold for regional natural disaster losses at 1% of regional gdp and taking into account the level of socioeconomic development of the affected regions in the assessment of applications; weighting indicators other than gdp, such as hdi or gni, for the assessment of eligibility. the report is considered positive, we vote in favour.
‒ the initiative report in question relates to the evaluation process of the european union solidarity fund (eusf), set up in 2002 to deal with situations of severe natural disasters affecting the member states of the union, which is extended to the candidate countries. this own-initiative report, which i voted in favour of, follows the report presented by the european commission in october 2015 on the use of the eusf in the previous year. the analysis carried out shows that although it is impossible to predict disaster and emergency situations, it is desirable to improve the management of the consequences of disasters at their various stages, especially in terms of sustainable damage repair and risk management. i agree with the rapporteur that there is a need for faster activation of the eusf, greater transparency in its use and greater cooperation between the different levels of decision-making. i also support the adoption of a prevention policy that promotes complementarity between the use of the eusf and other european instruments, with particular emphasis on the cohesion funds, particularly when we are dealing with infrastructure projects (which should take into account aspects linked to risk prevention and potentially reduce the costs of natural disasters).
‒ the report, making a positive assessment of the implementation of this fund and the acuteness of the reform, suggests that member states optimise synergies with the strategic investment funds - in terms of developing natural disaster prevention, adaptation and mitigation instruments - and that reconstruction and these natural disaster prevention, adaptation and mitigation instruments always take into account the sustainability of reconstruction and resources, increasing resilience to the randomness of disasters. the report also makes a number of positive suggestions to the commission, including: increasing the threshold for advances from 10% to 15%; reducing the time taken to process applications from six to four weeks; fixing the eligibility threshold for regional natural disaster losses at 1% of regional gdp and taking into account the level of socioeconomic development of the affected regions in the assessment of applications; weighting indicators other than gdp, such as hdi or gni, for the assessment of eligibility. we consider the report to be positive and we vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ on 3 december 2010, the council adopted a decision authorising the commission to open negotiations for an agreement between the european union and the united states of america on the protection of personal data transferred and processed for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorism, in the context of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters (hereinafter referred to as the 'framework agreement'). this agreement has raised doubts about its compatibility with the charter and eu secondary data protection legislation, in particular as regards the right to judicial redress, access by law enforcement agencies, limitation of access by the data subject and data retention periods. the resolution seeks to request the court of justice to give an opinion on the compatibility of the proposed agreement with the treaties. we do not recognize the legitimacy of this court, which is shaped by the interests of this process of capitalist integration of the eu.
‒ the so-called framework agreement on the protection of personal data with the united states has been under discussion for the past 5 years. the european parliament has always taken the position that european citizens should have their rights respected. i am aware that cooperation and the exchange of information with the united states in the fight against crime are fundamental for the european union. however, as i have argued in many other areas, we cannot sacrifice everything for the sake of security. that is why i welcome the fact that clear limits have been set on the use of the data transmitted and on the retention period. the us administration also agreed to set up a provider and to recognise the fundamental right of european citizens to judicial protection. it is in recognition of this new framework, and in stressing that this agreement does not authorize the transfer of data but only creates the legal framework, that i am in favour of its adoption.
‒ this recommendation is based on a draft eu-us agreement on the protection of personal data. the draft agreement proposes a legal basis to ensure a high level of protection of personal data for the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences in the context of police and judicial cooperation between the parties. however, there are serious doubts as to its compatibility with community legislation, as it does not provide the legal certainty and security needed to safeguard the fundamental right to personal data. i voted against it.
in writing. the framework agreement establishes (for the first time) a comprehensive agreement on data protection principles and safeguards when personal data are transferred for the purposes of criminal law enforcement between the us on the one hand and the european union and its member states on the other. the two-fold objective is to ensure a high level of data protection and thereby to enhance cooperation between the parties. while not constituting the legal basis for the transfer of personal data to the usa, the framework agreement complements, where necessary, the data protection safeguards provided for in existing or future data transfer agreements or national provisions authorising such transfers. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ this recommendation approves the conclusion of the eu-us agreement on the protection of personal data in the context of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorism. the agreement provides for a supposed guarantee of high data protection and the strengthening of police and judicial cooperation between the two sides of the atlantic, and announces that 'european citizens' will have the same rights as their us counterparts, including in bringing an action before us courts. however, the ambiguity of the terms in which the agreement is drawn up, and the premise that this is an international agreement which overrides national and european data protection standards and makes them a blank slate, makes us believe that we are dealing with an agreement which, in fact, calls into question and compromises rights, freedoms and guarantees. on the other hand, it is an agreement which further undermines the sovereignty of the member states, in clear conflict with the rights and interests of the peoples. we voted against it.
‒ this proposal for a recommendation concerns the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of an agreement with the united states of america on the protection of personal data transferred and processed for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorism, in the framework of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. the main objective is therefore to ensure a high level of protection of fundamental rights and individual freedoms, in particular privacy, when transferring personal data between the authorities with coercive powers in the eu and its member states and the us counterpart. the provisions of the agreement set out the fundamental principles of data protection and establish the rights of natural persons and the rights of administrative and judicial redress. i believe that overall we are facing an agreement which will be a step forward for the protection of personal data transferred between the eu and the us, without restricting or violating any rights of data subjects, and for that reason i voted in favour of the adoption of this report.
‒ this agreement between the european union and the united states of america concerns the protection of personal data transferred and processed for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of crime, including terrorism, in the context of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. personal data comprise any information concerning a person, whether it concerns his private, professional or public life. this could be a name, a photograph, an e-mail address, banking information, social media posts, medical information, or the ip address of your computer. the agreement is clearly a dangerous attack on freedoms and guarantees and opens the door to all kinds of abuses in terms of invading the private sphere of citizens. the idea is, under the heading of combating terrorism, to legitimize a security framework with all kinds of abuses, opening the way to the persecution of any and all troublesome personalities who question established institutions and values.
in writing. this proposal constitutes the legal instrument necessary for the conclusion of a stepping stone economic partnership agreement (epa) between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and ghana, of the other part. the agreement provides a contractual safety net, guaranteeing duty-free access to the union market until the entry into force of the regional agreement. the stepping stone agreement will be applied provisionally and will be replaced by the epa concluded at regional level on the day it enters into force. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ this report on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the stepping stone economic partnership agreement between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and ghana, of the other part, recommends that the european parliament give its consent to the conclusion of this agreement, paving the way for its provisional application. ghana and the eu are partners in different areas, including the promotion of regional economic integration and investment. in 2015, the total value of bilateral trade between ghana and the union amounted to eur 5,4 billion, representing more than 20% of ghana's external trade. the country is one of the main agri-food exporters in the economic community of west african states (ecowas) region, exporting cocoa, fruit, nuts and fish, and importing rice, sugar and meat. nothing is said about the harmful effects of free trade, the appropriation by multinational companies of natural resources and biodiversity, the increase in unemployment and the threat to sovereignty. while rejecting this recommendation, we express our full solidarity with the people of ghana and with the other peoples of west africa for their right to development, sovereignty and independence. we voted against it.
‒ this proposal for a recommendation concerns the draft council decision on the conclusion of the economic partnership agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and ghana, of the other part, in view of the delay in the signature of the eu-west africa economic partnership agreement. the ratification of this agreement will provide ghana with a contractual guarantee of duty-free access to the union market until the entry into force of the regional framework agreement. it is therefore a step-by-step agreement which will be applied provisionally until the entry into force of the regional agreement, in strict compliance with wto rules. although not the ideal solution, given the absence of a regional dimension, rules of origin and a comprehensive institutional framework, ghana is implementing a set of reforms and is making efforts to combat corruption and eliminate child labour, this step-by-step agreement provides a stronger legal basis than the market access regulation and is a precursor to what will be the regional framework agreement. i voted in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of the eu-ghana economic partnership agreement because it is an agreement that guarantees continued 'duty-free and quota-free' access to the union's internal market, thereby protecting thousands of jobs and strengthening ghana's exports. this agreement, which has been negotiated for some years, is provisional and will only be in force until the regional agreement (already concluded) between the eu and the west african states (ecowas) is ratified. i would point out that the ghanaian parliament, which is responsible for deciding on the national interest, unanimously approved the agreement. this is not a perfect agreement, but it is compatible with wto rules and offers stability. neither the acp market access regulation (mar) nor the eu's generalised system of preferences (gsp+) incentive scheme are satisfactory alternatives. finally, the bilateral agreement contains safeguard measures for local industry and excludes from liberalisation the most sensitive products for the ghanaian economy. my vote respects the national choice of ghana.
‒ this epa grants ghana, a low/middle income country, full market access, which will allegedly provide the stability needed for new investment and job creation. some 35% of union exports to ghana are already fully or almost fully liberalised and the further reduction of customs duties will allow this proportion to be gradually increased to 80%. the cfp has serious doubts about these partnership agreements, which are based on free trade and the principle of the free functioning of markets. time will tell whether this agreement has benefited the people of ghana or has contributed to disrupting the economy, undermining food security or compromising its nascent industry.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the fjellner report because, although i consider the ec-ghana steppingstone economic partnership agreement to be incomplete and outdated, i believe that a steppingstone agreement will fulfil its objective of helping to avoid trade disruptions in ghana and, at the same time, will prepare the ground for a future relationship based on a regional partnership agreement. i would also stress that this landmark economic partnership agreement offers opportunities for promoting regional economic integration and investment. the commission notes that the union has not provided any evidence that the exporting producers concerned have been able to obtain sufficient quantities of the product concerned from the union producers.
in writing. article 13 of council regulation (eu) no 1311/2013 defined a contingency margin of up to 0,03% of the gross national income of the union. in accordance with article 6 of that regulation, the commission calculated the absolute amount of the contingency margin for 2016. having mobilised the flexibility instrument in the amount of eur 1 530 million available for 2016, it appears necessary to mobilise the contingency margin in order to respond to the needs arising from the refugee, migration and security crisis by increasing the commitment appropriations in the general budget of the union for the financial year 2016 above the ceiling for category 3 (security and citizenship) commitments. in the framework of the general budget of the union for 2016, this report mobilises the contingency margin with the aim of making available an amount of eur 240,1 million in commitment appropriations over and above the ceiling for commitments in category 3 of the multiannual financial framework. i therefore support this report.
in writing. article 13 (1) of the mff regulation defines the contingency margin as an instrument of last resort to respond to unforeseen circumstances. having examined all other financial possibilities to respond to unforeseen circumstances, within the ceiling for expenditure in category 3 (security and citizenship) for 2016, and having proposed to mobilise the flexibility instrument for categories 3 and 4 for a total amount of eur 1 530 million available in 2016, the mobilisation of the contingency margin is necessary to respond to the needs arising from the refugee, migration and security crisis in order to increase the commitment appropriations in category 3 in the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016 above the ceiling for that category. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed, together with draft amending budget no 4/2016, to mobilise the contingency margin in the amount of eur 240,1 million in 2016 to supplement the commitment appropriations for security and citizenship expenditure (category 3) of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2016. given the need to respond to the challenges arising from the refugee, migration and security crises, it is essential to mobilise the contingency margin by increasing the commitment appropriations in the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016 above the ceiling for category 3 commitments. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report.
‒ the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument is related to the need to complement the financing of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016 with a view to financing the appropriations for commitments under category 3 (security and citizenship), in order to allow for the exceeding of the ceiling of this heading for the year 2016 in accordance with the current multiannual financial framework. in addition to not being 'new' money, it adds insufficient value to cope with and help take action against the ongoing migrant and refugee crisis. it is once again clear that the amounts provided for in the mff (within its limits) are once again below what is needed to deal with the repeated crises in the eu, not to mention what is needed for an effective redistributive policy that allows disadvantaged countries and regions to come closer to the richer regions.
in writing. article 13 of council regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 has defined a contingency margin of up to 0,03 % of the gross national income of the union. the european commission has calculated the absolute amount of this margin for the period in question after having examined all other financial possibilities to react to unforeseen circumstances, within the ceiling of the category 3 (security and citizenship) commitments and after having mobilised the flexibility instrument. the total amount of eur 240,1 million was allocated to deal with unforeseen events during 2016. the need to mobilise this contingency margin arose from the urgency of responding to the needs arising from the refugee, migration and security crisis. given that this is a very specific situation, i voted in favour of this report, as the commission has proposed that this extra funding should supplement the commitment appropriations for category 3 (security and citizenship) of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016.

‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to enable the union to respond to emergency situations caused by large-scale natural disasters and to show european solidarity to the disaster-stricken regions of europe. the fund may provide financial assistance to member states and countries negotiating their accession in the event of a major natural disaster. i support the šulin report which aims to put in the general budget of the union for 2017 the amount of 50 million for the payment of advances, in an efficient and timely manner, in the event of a disaster in the next year. this is the direct result of the new provision in the 2014 amending regulation (article 4a), strongly advocated by the european parliament, which aims to accelerate the disbursement of aid to affected countries by paying an advance before the final decision on aid is taken, thus enhancing the effectiveness of the fund.

in writing. ‒ we are faced with a budget which cannot, no matter how much rice powder is thrown at it, disguise the deep crisis in which the european union finds itself. the european parliament and the commission's proposal, based on a short multiannual framework, did not correspond from the outset to the real needs of a european union which was severely depressed and increasingly asymmetric from a social and economic point of view. yet the council soon made it clear that this minimalist proposal would not merit their agreement. the agreement announced, with a small increase in funds to deal with the refugee crisis and a slight increase in funds to support the mobility of young people under the erasmus+ programme, falls far short of the possibilities and needs and even goes in the wrong direction, reducing the weight of cohesion and support for productive activities and increasing the dimension of foreign and security policy, emphasising the repressive character of the eu, particularly in relation to refugees. it is also a budget that is becoming less and less transparent, with trust funds and other financial instruments taking up an increasingly large share, making the parliament's monitoring role even more difficult. all the more reason for us to vote against.

‒ the european parliament has a duty to assess the capacity and suitability of european commissioners at all times, but especially at the time of their appointment. i believe that this assessment is above all political and to some extent technical, but that it must also include a dimension of monitoring possible conflicts of interest. i therefore believe that the concept of conflict of interest should not be vague and that its verification should be based on objective and verifiable criteria. i generally support the recommendations on the code of conduct for members of the commission, because once implemented, they bring greater transparency to declarations of financial interests. i would stress the need to balance these transparency requirements with the need to respect the privacy of commissioners, in particular their family members. i would remind you that parliament should be given a structural role in the examination of the financial statements at the beginning of the commissioners' term of office and whenever there is a substantial change in circumstances, whether it be a change of portfolio or a change in the financial interests of each one. however, this evaluation should be substantive and not investigative, resulting in recommendations that promote and advocate transparency. i therefore support this report.

in writing. the report deals with the follow-up to the application of the european order for payment procedure and allows creditors to obtain an order for payment more easily for the recovery of uncontested claims in civil and commercial matters. this is an optional procedure that can be used in cross-border cases as an alternative to equivalent national procedures. late payment is one of the main causes of insolvency, which is particularly threatening to small and medium-sized enterprises, often resulting in job losses. the procedure was designed to enable the rapid recovery of amounts arising from debts which are certain, net and due and not disputed by the defendant. although operating in a generally satisfactory manner, this procedure is far from having exhausted its full potential, since it is mainly used in member states whose legislation provides for a similar procedure. despite the considerations set out in the report on the improvement of the functioning of the single market, which is also responsible for the difficulties faced by many micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, this is a technical procedure for judicial cooperation at european and civil level, which aims to combat one of the main causes of insolvency.
in writing. this own-initiative report, which i voted in favour of, concerns the european order for payment procedure, which is characterized by enabling creditors to recover their uncontested claims in civil and commercial matters in cross-border cases more easily, quickly and effectively. this is an optional procedure, which does not require the intervention of a lawyer and can be carried out electronically in any member state without any additional formalities. although this procedure is more widely used in countries with similar systems, it is important to make efforts to disseminate this instrument to companies and professionals in the field, making them aware of the advantages and benefits of its application. i agree with the suggestions made by the rapporteur on the elements necessary for the efficient use of the european injunction procedure, in particular as regards the time limit for issuing the injunctions, the submission of online forms and the acceptance of applications in other official languages of the member states. i welcome the legal clarifications that have been made to the regulation, especially those relating to consumer protection, although some aspects need to be further harmonised in the legislation of each member state.
‒ the report deals with the follow-up to the application of the european order for payment procedure, which results from regulation (ec) no 1896/2006. the procedure allows creditors to easily obtain an order for payment for the recovery of uncontested claims in civil and commercial matters. the application may be submitted by post or, often, by electronic means, does not require the intervention of a lawyer and is applicable in other member states without further formalities. the european order for payment is issued automatically, solely on the basis of the application, but the debtor may lodge a statement of opposition within 30 days. in the event of opposition, the order for payment procedure shall be terminated and counter-claim proceedings may be instituted. this is an optional procedure that can be used in cross-border cases as an alternative to equivalent national procedures.

the distribution of marine species knows no borders. in the case of deep-sea species, the problem is even more complex. scientific research has long shown that deep-sea habitats and species are inherently more vulnerable because they generally have high longevity, late maturation, low reproduction and few natural enemies. in some deep-sea fisheries, such as those in the north-east atlantic, the azores and madeira, restrictions on industrial trawls and gillnets have been in place for many years. the habitats and ecosystems of this region are of the same nature as those of the international waters of the north-east atlantic. this regulation, which is being discussed here today, extends some of the rules that were implemented for macaronesia 11 years ago through european commission regulation no 1568 of 2005, but falls far short of this. it was perhaps the consensus document possible and as such i commend the rapporteur for her effort. it is already some progress to stop fishing below 800 metres and in vulnerable marine ecosystems below 400 metres. by reducing the damage that drift does to cold coral reefs and deep-sea sponges, we are preserving a legacy that goes back thousands of years, and at the same time, we are helping to protect the reproduction and sustainability of fisheries resources. but we could have gone further and i fear that if we have not done so, it will continue to affect, for example, small-scale fishing in archipelagic regions, given the connectivity of the oceans.
i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in the negotiations, but that it should be involved in the negotiations. the compromise that has now finally been reached is reasonable in terms of the objectives pursued and the solutions suggested, which, in our view, was not the case with the european commission's initial proposal. freezing the fishing footprint by restricting the action of highly impactful gear to areas where this impact can no longer be avoided, while taking specific measures to protect vulnerable seabed ecosystems, seemed to us from the outset to be sensible and appropriate. we also value measures to improve scientific knowledge, making it more robust to better support policy decision-making and impact assessment processes. we would, however, have liked to have gone further in the field of international waters, where fishing activities are now carried out which would have required stricter regulation, thus benefiting, for example, the resources in the waters of the autonomous regions of the azores and madeira.
