winner of the sakharov prize (the following is a transcription of the interpretation of the original speech from kurdish into english). – mr president, president of the european parliament, distinguished guests, members of the european parliament, i would like to thank all of you for this very valuable prize and i feel that this prize is a prize for every woman and girl that has been sexually enslaved by daesh and for every yazidi woman that has been a victim of daesh and for everybody around the world that has been a victim of terrorism, everybody, all and every one of them, each and every one of them deserves this prize. i am a yazidi girl. my real age is 18 years old. i loved school very, very much when i was little and my father decided to increase my age by a year so that i would be able to go to school. and when daesh attacked my village i was 15 years old. they killed all the men in the village, including my brother, my father, relatives, young and old. and then they took us to another place and they separated us between older and younger women. they killed the older women and then they divided the younger girls up and we were then traded on the slave trade market. i myself was sold four times by daesh and every single time i was sold i tried to escape. they tortured me, they beat me and they insulted me and captured me again. and one of the individuals made explosive devices and bombs and forced me to help him, forced me to make these bombs. the last person who bought me was an iraqi doctor called doctor eslam. he was the director of the houwaja hospital. he used to torture me. he used to torture all the yazidi women and he would even rape girls who were only nine or ten years old. together with a friend of mine called kathrin and a nine year old girl, all of us were raped by dr eslam. the three of us did actually manage to escape but before we actually managed to arrive to safety kathrin accidentally walked over a landmine and it exploded and the last thing i heard was her death screams and this was awful, absolutely awful and it was the worst thing that i have ever heard. when i managed to pick myself up i knew that i would not be able to ever see again because the whole of my body was burnt, my body was burning and i did not think that i would actually be able to open my eyes ever again. and then i was taken to germany and i was helped to travel from iraq to germany and i was helped, i was treated and i am now able to see through one eye. i can see now again and i would like to thank god for the possibility that i can see now, that i can be a voice to the victims. and the sakharov prize gives me great strength. and this is why i have taken a decision to become a voice for the voiceless. the yazidis have been victims of extremism, of violence and terrorism, they have lost their lives but i very much ask you and urge you to promise me, to promise us, that never again, never again will you allow these kinds of things to happen. that you will listen to us and see that justice will be done so that the criminals can be brought to justice and held accountable. it has been two-and-a half-years now since the tragedy that affected the yazidi people and there are still more than 3 500 children and women held by daesh as slaves and every day they die a thousand times over again. the bones in the yazidi mass graves that remain untouched in the area of singhar, and the yazidi people, have no value in iraq, whether dead or alive. our village, ladies and gentlemen, has been a neighbour to arab cities for hundreds of years and when people visited us, when an arab or a muslim visited us, they would not eat meat in our homes because this was prohibited under their religion. they were not allowed to eat this meat. and my father would tell our muslim guests that they should slaughter the animal themselves so that they would then be able to eat halal meat when they visited us. when islamic state arrived and attacked us then it was our neighbours who actually attacked us first of all, before them. and they killed our men and they enslaved our women. as a result of this we have lost the social order in our own society and we have lost trust with these countries because they do not treat us as yazidis as equal to other citizens. so today we need europe so that we can go back to our country, so that we can build up our country again and so that we can experience peace again in our society. these criminals must be brought to justice, they must be held to account. the yazidis and the christians need international protection and they, both children and women that have been victims of daesh, need some kind of psychological rehabilitation. we need programmes for that and they need to be resettled. and ladies and gentlemen i would like to thank you very much for this prize. i stand here before you and i would like to accept this prize on behalf of all the women and all the girls who are still in the camps in kurdistan, who are living in those camps where the conditions are absolutely appalling and i very much hope that you will all help us. thank you very much. (the house accorded the speaker a heartfelt standing ovation)
winner of the sakharov prize (the following is a transcription of the interpretation of the original speech from arabic into english). – mr president, esteemed members of parliament, as i stand before you today, my heart is full of happiness, because you decided to stand by a yazidi woman and the yazidi community in the midst of a genocide. i am happy because not only did you stand by us as a community but you stood by millions of women and children in iraq, syria and in conflict zones where they face blind terrorism. receiving the sakharov prize today is a great honour for us. daesh wanted, by enslaving us, to take our honour, but they lost their honour, and here you have given us this honour. daesh and the extremists came on 3 august to erase the yazidis from existence and they gave us one option: death or islam. there is no doubt daesh committed mass genocide. this genocide did not only consist of killings, but it also sought to enslave women in a systematic manner and to take the children away. daesh wanted to break our will to live. they started by killing the disabled and the elders and the women that they did not desire for themselves. then they destroyed places of worship and infrastructure so that we wouldn’t return. daesh and other global radical groups do not want anyone to have a life. they target all those who stand against their ideology, including millions of muslims. terrorism and radicalism are the enemies of mankind. i was a girl in a big family. i was the closest to my mother among my sisters. i learned from my mother the meaning of goodness and mercy, and what it means to challenge poverty. i learned from my small community that when we pray every evening we pray for all the peoples of the world before we pray for ourselves. i learned from my religion that god is tolerant and noble and that the difference between religions and cultures is a difference chosen by the creation, and it ought to be respected as such. daesh took my mother, who believed in the essence of humanity, along with 86 yazidi women in soulagh. they killed them all because they did not hold any value in the human sex trade. today, my community has disintegrated under the weight of genocide. half a million people do not know where their future is leading them. will we return to our lands? how will we return to our lands under the same conditions that led to the genocide? should we emigrate? this is what some 75 000 yazidis did. they mostly emigrated to germany, and i thank germany with all my heart for taking in my community, and i also thank germany also for taking in 1 000 yazidi women to provide them with medical and psychological care. half a million yazidis remain in iraq and they are the last members of this community present in the middle east. they are the few who remain after thousands, or perhaps millions, of yazidis were exterminated throughout history. the harsh conditions forced them to emigrate from turkey and syria, especially under the ottoman empire. we look up to europe as a symbol of humanity, and europe is indeed confirming today that it is such a symbol. europe should remain a model for the world and a model for the coexistence of peoples and cultures. the world today faces two of its biggest threats – the danger of terrorism as well as the dangers of reactions to terrorism. we must fight terrorism and we must dry its source. we must also work with the islamic community around the world so that they can change the teachings of islam and make the mosques a place for mercy, love and peace, free of extremism. we must prevent radicalism and racism everywhere. radicalism and extremism have become such dangers today. we must respect the individual, regardless of religion, creed, colour, sex or place of residence. the religious communities in iraq must be protected, and amongst them my community after this genocide. they can be protected through the establishment of a protected zone or zones under the aegis and protection of the international community in coordination with the iraqi government and the regional government of kurdistan. if the world is unable to protect us in our lands, i invite europe to open its doors to us to provide refuge to half a million yazidis from iraq, through an organised mass migration similar to what happened following the holocaust. for we cannot afford to remain the fuel of genocide and slavery. there must also be an accountability system to hold those who committed these crimes accountable both at [local] level and in the international community. there are still thousands of terrorists in iraq and syria and they must be brought to justice. thank you again for giving us this great award. from here, i would like to say to daesh, and all terrorists in the world, if you have chosen for yourself the path of no dignity, then europe has chosen for itself the path of humanity and honour. (the house accorded the speaker a loud and sustained standing ovation)

‒ the draft euro-mediterranean agreement aims to create an association between the european community and its member states, on the one hand, and algeria, on the other. the objectives of this framework agreement are: to provide an appropriate framework for political dialogue between the parties in order to allow the strengthening of their relations and cooperation in all areas they consider relevant; to develop trade and ensure the development of balanced economic and social relations between the parties and to define the conditions for a progressive liberalisation of trade in goods, services and capital; facilitate human contacts, in particular in the context of administrative procedures; to encourage the integration of the maghreb by promoting exchanges and cooperation in the region and between the maghreb and the european communities and their member states; promote cooperation in the economic, social, cultural and financial fields. respect for democratic principles and fundamental human rights as enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights is an essential element of this agreement. for these reasons, i support this recommendation on the conclusion of a protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement.
‒ this recommendation aims to approve the conclusion of a protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing a set of general principles governing the participation of algeria in eu programmes. algeria has been a member of the euro-mediterranean agreement since 2005 and has now applied to join eu programmes. the programmes set out in the protocol concern economic, financial and technical cooperation, which will enable algeria to obtain assistance, in particular financial assistance. algeria may participate in the programmes open to its participation and should contribute to the eu budget in those specific programmes. the specific terms of the protocol will be determined in a memorandum of understanding between the european commission and the algerian authorities. we have known reservations about the contents of the euro-mediterranean agreement, which opens the door to free trade agreements. but that is not what we are taking a position on in this report, which is nevertheless related to it. we have not blocked algeria's request, which is an expression of its sovereign will to join eu programmes. we reiterate, however, certain doubts and reservations about the financial assistance issues as referred to in the council decision.
‒ this recommendation aims to approve the conclusion of a protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing a set of general principles governing the participation of algeria in union programmes. the programmes set out in the protocol concern economic, financial and technical cooperation, which will enable algeria to access assistance provided by the union through its programmes. algeria may participate in union programmes open to its participation and should contribute to the budget of the union in the specific programmes in which it participates. although it is part of the euro-mediterranean agreement which opens the way to free trade agreements, it is not an agreement of this nature which is involved in the conclusion of this framework agreement, but rather an instrument from which algeria can benefit in its development.
‒ the european neighbourhood policy aims to share the benefits of the european union with neighbouring countries, thereby contributing to the enhancement of stability, security and well-being within and outside the union. in this context, this text refers to the protocol negotiated between algeria and the eu, which aims at algeria's participation in certain community programmes. because the european union cannot close itself off from the world around it, and because algeria's geographical proximity to the european area justifies the creation of synergies with this state, i approve this report.
‒ as part of the european neighbourhood policy (enp), the gradual opening of certain union programmes and agencies to the participation of enp partner countries is one of many measures to promote reform, modernisation and democratic transition in the european union's neighbourhood. this agreement with algeria is an example of this.
‒ the gradual opening of some european union (eu) programmes and agencies to the participation of countries in the european neighbourhood policy (enp) is one of the many measures promoted by the eu in support of reform, modernisation and democratic transition processes in its neighbouring regions. in 2007, the european council instructed the european commission to negotiate agreements with the eu's neighbouring countries, of which algeria was a part. the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement between the eu and its member states, of the one part, and the people's democratic republic of algeria, of the other part, contains general principles for the participation of algeria in eu programmes, which require the adoption of financial and technical rules for its integration. these programmes will establish economic, financial and technical cooperation measures with a view to facilitating assistance, particularly financial assistance, to algeria. i voted in favour of this report approving the protocol between the eu and algeria, taking into account that all the legal and regulatory criteria inherent in this decision are met.
‒ this recommendation sets out a set of general principles for the participation of algeria in union programmes. algeria has been a member of the eu mediterranean agreement since 2005 and has now asked the european union to join eu programmes. the programmes set out in the protocol concern economic, financial and technical cooperation, which will enable algeria to access assistance and in particular financial assistance to be provided by the union through its programmes. algeria may participate in union programmes open to its participation and should contribute to the budget of the union in the specific programmes in which algeria will participate. the specific terms of the protocol will be determined in a memorandum of understanding between the european commission and the algerian authorities. it is a request from algeria. while there are still doubts about the nature and implications of these agreements, the sovereign will of algeria and its government prevails above all.
the proposal provides for new rules for deep-sea fishing in the north-east atlantic, including a general ban on trawl fishing below 800 metres and a system for protecting vulnerable marine ecosystems in areas where fishing is still permitted under certain conditions. the regulation also provides for special protection measures for vulnerable marine ecosystems applicable to operations with bottom fishing gear below 400 metres depth; the limitation of directed deep-sea fishing to the area where this activity took place in 2009-2011 (the so-called 'fishing footprint'); the introduction of two types of fishing authorisation, one for vessels landing more than 8% of deep-sea species in each fishing trip and at least 10 tonnes in the calendar year concerned, and the other for vessels catching these species as by-catch.
‒ this is a complex dossier, the discussion of which has been going on for more than three years. the compromise finally reached is reasonable in terms of the objectives pursued and the solutions suggested, which was not the case with the european commission's initial proposal. the regulation provides for the eu to freeze its 'fishing' footprint. the fishing depth limit is 800 metres in order to safeguard deep-sea ecosystems. vessels fishing in vulnerable marine ecosystems at a depth of more than 400 metres will have to stop their operations and move at least five nautical miles from the fishing zone concerned. the regulation provides for improvements in transparency, information provision and the collection of scientific data - aspects which we value. we argued that more should have been done in the area of international waters (ices zones), where fishing activities are carried out and which should have been subject to stricter regulation, thereby benefiting the resources in the waters of the azores and madeira - regions where specific measures have long been adopted to protect vulnerable marine ecosystems, but which end up being affected by fishing activities carried out by european fleets in more northerly areas.
‒ this recommendation for second reading is aimed at the adoption of a report on the regulation of fisheries in eu waters in the north-east atlantic. one of the measures envisaged is the definition of the zone where deep-sea fishing activities will be authorised, with concrete sanctions being proposed for vessels that violate the provisions of the regulation. the proposed measures show a strong concern for the protection of vulnerable marine ecosystems and biologically sensitive areas, while ensuring the sustainability of the ecosystem. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ this report aims to freeze the european union's fishing footprint by defining the zone where deep-sea fishing activities will be allowed. parliament also secured specific sanctions for vessels infringing the deep-sea fisheries regulation by introducing new, stricter transparency rules, including the obligation to provide information to the public on european vessels targeting deep-sea species and to record all catches (vulnerable fish and ecosystems).
‒ following the various trilogues which took place to reach a negotiating agreement on the adoption of a regulation laying down specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea species in the north-east atlantic and provisions applicable to fishing in international waters in this region, it was possible to adopt your position at first reading. the main measures included in the compromise are the freezing of fishing effort by defining the zone where deep-sea fishing activities will be allowed, the application of specific sanctions to vessels that violate the regulation and the establishment of a 800m limit to protect vulnerable ecosystems on the seabed. the adoption of these and other measures set out in the regulation will improve scientific knowledge of deep-sea species and their habitats, implement technical fisheries management measures and thus ensure a more sustainable exploitation of deep-sea species, while minimising the impact of deep-sea fishing activities on the marine environment. in view of the above, i voted in favour of adopting this report.

mr president, one of the founding principles of the european union is equality between all citizens. this means that all the votes of all citizens are equal, they are worth exactly the same and, consequently, the members elected by them have the same rights and are also equal within this house. i repeat, they should all have the same rights. that, mr president, is democracy. however, this report is a total disregard for democracy in the sense i have just described: it is the shameless legalization of the worst kind of backstage politics, in all the worst ways of this backstage politics. i never thought that the european parliament was the only european institution directly elected by the citizens of europe to help to close the democratic gap. don't talk about a democratic deficit, they just legitimized it. i voted against it because i'm not an accomplice.
‒ the european parliament has regularly revised its rules of procedure, often following the adoption of new treaties which have strengthened the institution's powers. the proposal provides parliament with a better 'modus operandi', clarifies the rules of procedure, increases transparency and protects the ep from disruption by political elements intent on sabotaging its work.
‒ in the face of the deep and persistent crisis in which the eu finds itself, the reaction of the main forces that have determined its course - the right and social democracy - is to strengthen instruments of an undemocratic nature. this is another example. these amendments, taken together, severely limit the power of intervention of members and smaller political groups, further increasing the power of the larger groups. the introduction of amendments to reports and opinions, written questions to other institutions, resolutions, explanations of vote, participation in specialised committees - all this is severely limited. written declarations - an instrument which has allowed important struggles to be expressed (two recent examples: the renegotiation of debts or the re-establishment of milk quotas) - are abolished. instruments of democratic control over the work of parliament and members are weakened or eliminated, in particular by imposing accelerated procedures and reducing the possibilities of requesting 'nominal votes'. it is worth saying that some are afraid or ashamed to take the positions they take here. the ps, psd and cds voted in favour. the cpp voted against and put forward many dozens of proposals that would strengthen democracy, pluralism and transparency in the european parliament's workings.

‒ the revision of the european parliament's rules of procedure is an ongoing work. the group of the european socialists is generally satisfied with the measures proposed in this agreement, which are aimed at greater efficiency and transparency.
‒ over time, there have been several revisions to the rules of procedure, often linked to the adoption of new treaties. this review is mainly for internal reasons, with the aim of bringing greater operationality, clarity and transparency to the internal rules of operation, with the exception of the cases of the amendments resulting from the 2016 interinstitutional agreement on the better regulation programme and the creation of new bodies in the area of the banking union. the working party set up in this context was able to reach agreement on a number of issues, mainly technical, legal and linguistic. as regards the substantive amendments, i would stress the new rules for maintaining agreements at first and second readings, the introduction of topical and urgent debate on topical and urgent subjects and the introduction of new rules/procedures on transparency. on the question of the efficiency and effectiveness of parliament's work, i would like to highlight as positive the measures concerning voting, the motions for resolutions and the amendments i have endorsed for the introduction of two new types of written questions to the commission/council, in order to give them greater political weight and thus obtain better-informed answers and consequently an improvement in the quality of parliament's work and debate.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the corbett report because i agree with the proposals put forward to improve the european parliament's rules of procedure. i would stress that the report seeks to align the ep's rules of procedure with the 'better regulation' work programme and to strengthen the links of institutional cooperation between the three institutions of the union: parliament, the council and the commission. i believe that the package of rules presented will serve to make the european parliament an even more transparent, efficient, open and responsive institution to its citizens.
‒ this annual report is a crucial exercise for the european parliament, especially at a time - i would say - of crisis. the year 2015 was particularly difficult with regard to fundamental rights: threats to the rule of law, terrorist attacks on security and freedom of expression, as well as difficulties in respecting the right to asylum. this report provides an overall assessment of the human rights situation in the union and identifies the impact of the measures taken. unlike in previous years, the diagnosis is based on reality, the proposals are consistent with the position of this parliament and the fundamental rights have not been used for political purposes. the picture presented is not new, but it reinforces the feeling of apprehension. but above all it must reinforce the urgency of union action.
‒ the european union is a community based on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy and equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. rule of law which is the backbone of european liberal democracy and one of the founding principles of the eu, deriving from the common constitutional traditions of the member states. at least 3,771 people died or were reported missing in 2015 while trying to reach safety in europe, bringing the total number of dead and missing to more than 30 000 in the last two decades, and terrorist acts represent one of the most serious violations of fundamental rights and freedoms. i would remind you that human dignity is the inviolable basis of all fundamental rights, that it must not be subject to any kind of exploitation and that it must be respected and protected in all eu initiatives, condemning all forms of discrimination and violence in the eu against all human beings, as they constitute a direct violation of human dignity.
‒ we welcome the recommendations in the field of freedoms, the rights of refugees and migrants, freedom of movement, the right to privacy, the right to information, non-discrimination, equality between men and women, the rights of the child, the rights of persons with disabilities and the defence of social rights, among others, which we support and call for. but well-meaning recommendations are not enough. concrete political measures must be taken to create the real and material conditions for their effective implementation. the strengthening and expansion of public services; the right to health, education and culture; the right to employment and employment with rights; respect for the sovereignty of peoples, non-interference, international law and the un charter are some of the urgent and necessary measures which have no place in this report. on the contrary, beyond the empty evocation of the infamous 'fundamental rights in the european union', the path indicated, explicitly or implicitly, is that of strengthening restrictive and limiting measures of freedoms, it is the narrow, repressive and protective vision of the ideal of democracy. the usual narrow and instrumental conception of human rights prevails.
‒ this report is about fundamental rights in the eu, which should be understood as rights inherent in all human beings, valid for all peoples and at all times. they are therefore inviolable, timeless and universal rights, which must always be protected and respected. although this report does not cover all the situations that should be taken into account, it proposes a number of positive measures to protect and safeguard fundamental rights in the eu, in particular in migration/asylum situations, gender equality and violence against women, corruption, discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation, etc. i voted yes.
‒ we welcome the recommendations in the field of freedoms, the rights of refugees and migrants, freedom of movement, the right to privacy, the right to information, non-discrimination, equality between men and women, the rights of the child, the rights of persons with disabilities and the defence of social rights, among others, which we support. recommendations which, however, omit the real causes of the problems mentioned, on the one hand, and, on the other, as in the case of the humanitarian refugee crisis, suppress the degrading reality that the european union has imposed on tens of thousands of human beings. the strengthening and extension of public services, such as access to health care, access to education, access to information, the creation and enjoyment of universal and quality culture, the right to employment and employment with rights, are some of the urgent and necessary measures which have no place in this report. on the other hand, it continues to defend the 'rule of law' as a tool for interfering with sovereign states, imposing the model outlined in the treaties on each country, leaving no room for the implementation of its own development models, in a demonstration that this is not possible in the vest of strength that is the eu. we voted against it.
‒ the union is a community based on respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and human rights, including the rights of minorities. in particular, the rule of law is the backbone of european liberal democracy and one of the founding principles of the union, stemming from the constitutional traditions of the member states. at the same time, human dignity - man as a value in himself - is the inviolable basis of all fundamental rights, which must not be subject to any kind of exploitation and which must be respected and protected in all eu initiatives. the report puts the right emphasis on the degree of compliance with the catalogue of fundamental rights enshrined in the european union, and provides an accurate and satisfactory picture of the situation regarding respect for fundamental rights in the current year and in the european universe. i therefore support this report.
in writing. ‒ mr president, in recent years we have seen a resurgence of fundamental rights in some countries of the union. this is why this diagnosis is important, but only if it implies effective measures in the attempt to counteract this state of affairs, especially as it relates to the rule of law, women's rights, lgbti people and migration.
‒ the charter of fundamental rights is an integral part of the european treaties and the legislation of the member states (with the exception of the derogations granted to poland, the united kingdom and the czech republic). however, breaches of its principles continued in 2015, as stated in this report, which i voted in favour of. the rule of law is the backbone of european democracy and a prerequisite for the protection of fundamental rights, and the union's 'pact' on these matters should therefore include country-specific recommendations to facilitate the process of its implementation. freedom of expression, the social inclusion of migrants and refugees, human trafficking, child poverty and exclusion, discrimination against minorities or gender inequalities are some of the violations identified in the report for which the eu needs to adopt effective solutions in order to welcome joint solutions in their prevention and combating. member states need to ensure that their legal systems comply with established european and international standards in order to ensure integration policies and effective measures against incitement to fear, hatred, radicalisation and extremism. the promotion of european values and the exchange of good practice are also essential.
‒ this annual report on human rights and democracy in the world (2015) and the eu's policy on the matter takes stock of the european union's work in defending and promoting human rights by the european union. the european union has used human rights in particular this year, as in other years, to justify external interference and interventions in sovereign countries which have subsequently caused problems of respect for and violation of human rights. although it is causing instability in the world, it does not engage in self-criticism. what moral value does the european union have when it does not make a self-criticism of the human rights that are constantly violated within the borders of its member states in this report? it speaks of the plight of refugees but says nothing about the causes of the plight and the disastrous balance sheet of european refugee policy. of course there are positive aspects in the report, for example the reference to the demand for the closure of guantanamo and some issues relating to the rights of women, disabled people, children, issues relating to the death penalty. however, this cannot make us accept the hypocrisy of the eu and its subjective and superficial approach to human rights.
‒ i voted in favour of the nagy report for agreeing with the assessment of the situation of fundamental rights in the eu and for sharing the proposals to improve the situation of these rights in the future. i stress that fundamental rights are universal, indivisible and always complementary, and a fair balance must be struck between the rights of everyone in a diverse society. in this context, i would remind you that in its relations with the rest of the world, the union must contribute to the protection of fundamental rights. finally, i would stress the condemnation of any and all forms of discrimination or violence on grounds of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or disability.
in writing. ‒ the cultural and creative industries (ccis) are characterised by their dual intrinsic value: they play a key role in preserving and promoting europe's cultural and linguistic diversity, reinforce a sense of belonging to european and regional identity, contribute to the transmission of knowledge and values and preserve europe's cultural and intangible heritage for present and future generations. it is therefore strategically important to support innovative and research-oriented kics. to realise the full potential of the sector, concerted action is needed at national, regional and local level, but also at eu level, and this requires: gathering reliable statistics and data on the sector; stimulating innovation and entrepreneurship in the cultural and creative sector; improving access to finance and developing skills, including entrepreneurial skills. the ccis play a key role in the reindustrialisation of europe, are a growth engine and are strategically positioned to unleash positive innovation effects in other sectors such as tourism, retail and digital technologies. the eu should take a leading role in promoting the important positive impact of the creative sectors across europe by promoting their culture. i therefore support this report.
‒ cultural and creative industries are industries based on cultural values, individual creativity, skills and talent with the potential to generate wealth and employment through the creation of value from intellectual property. to realise the full potential of the sector, therefore, concerted action is needed at national, regional and local level, but also at eu level. gathering reliable statistics and data on the basis of a comprehensive definition in order to raise awareness of the characteristics and needs of the sector, monitoring the evolution of the sector in order to create solutions for purpose-appropriate ccis, stimulating innovation and entrepreneurship in the cultural and creative sector by facilitating cooperation with other sectors and policies (crossings), and improving access to finance by supporting new business models are some of the measures advocated, which i agree with.
‒ the main thrust of this report is based on views that we do not share. there are aspects which we do not disagree with, although they must be put into perspective in the overall context of the report. the report proposes a definition of the cultural and creative industries (ccis) as being based on cultural, creative, individual values, skills and talent, capable of creating wealth and employment through the exploitation of intellectual property. architecture, archives and libraries, handicrafts, audiovisual (including cinema, television, video games and multimedia), cultural heritage, design, creative-oriented luxury industries and fashion industry, festivals, music, performing arts, books and publishing, radio and visual arts. in essence, all areas of cultural activity that have been commodified, and areas of commodity production that are now being considered for "cultural" status. it is enough to look at our country and imagine the consequences that would have, in an already degraded cultural framework, the classification of heritage, archives and libraries, and the arts in general, in the universe of the cultural industries, alongside fashion, jewellery, festivals and video games, competing with them in the creation of wealth and employment through the valorization of intellectual property. it would be the consecration of a commercialised conception of culture which is in itself a reason for rejecting this report.

‒ the cultural and creative industries (ccis) are at the heart of a dual system, made up of large groups of internationally competitive innovative smes and startups, whose benefits for the economy and for job creation are today undeniable. however, they often have more difficulty in accessing markets and financing. it is important to note that in the european area, ccis are responsible for the creation of more than 12 million full-time jobs, representing 7.5% of the union's workforce. it should also be noted that almost 39% of the union's gdp is generated by them. this report calls on the member states to improve the investment environment and to expand the range of financial instruments available to micro-enterprises and smes in the cultural and creative sectors through new and innovative financing schemes such as microcredit, repayable contributions, crowdfunding, venture capital financing, start-up capital and venture capital. i therefore support this report.
‒ this report recognises the cultural and creative industries (ccis), traditionally based on cultural values and creativity, as a strategic sector for job creation and sustainable growth, supporting cultural heritage and promoting innovation. the report focuses on a number of measures to realise the full potential of the sector through a concrete definition of ccis. it highlights the importance of education and training, its ability to generate value from intellectual property and proposes solutions to facilitate access to eu funding and funds. the s&ds introduced a new chapter on the status of workers in the cultural and creative sectors, calling on the member states to develop or implement a legal and institutional framework for artistic and creative activity in the areas of contracts, social security, health insurance, direct and indirect taxation and european compliance with standards. as regards financing, emphasis is placed on new forms of financing such as micro-credit or crowdfunding and the role of the commission and the member states in promoting and improving the regulatory framework.
‒ cultural and creative industries (ccis) are based on cultural values, individual creativity, skills and talent with the potential to generate wealth and employment through the creation of value from intellectual property. this report summarises the cultural and economic potential of the sector and indicates the pillars on which the european industrial policy for ccis should be based. the rapporteurs considered that concerted action at european, national, regional and local level was needed to realise the potential of the sector. identifying the characteristics and needs of the sector, monitoring its development, stimulating innovation and entrepreneurship, facilitating cooperation and synergies with other sectors and policies, improving access to finance, supporting new business models, using existing financial instruments at european level, developing skills and addressing skills shortages are some of the measures listed by the rapporteurs, with which i agree. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that ccis are essential in the 'reindustrialisation' of europe, as a strategic growth engine to boost innovation in other sectors. the eu must therefore promote the impact of this sector through policies that defend europe's most unique asset: its culture.
‒ the development of the so-called cultural and creative industries, with the usual commercial logic, points to the fact that they are not a factor in promoting cultural and linguistic diversity, but, on the contrary, a factor in cultural homogenization, in the reduction and dilution of cultural and linguistic particularities and specificities. this 'european identity' will at best be the identity of a certain conception of 'europe', which has nothing to do with the diversity and the broad dialogue that the best european cultural tradition has established with other cultures. it is significant that we are talking here about 'european' and 'regional' identity, but not about national identities, which are an inescapable factor of european identity. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the views expressed here about the place of culture in society and of cultural industries in culture are reductive and unacceptable. in some cases, they seem to be tailored to the interests of the big companies in the audiovisual and fashion industries.
in the first place, the commission has to be able to take account of the fact that the european parliament has a right to be consulted on the draft budget. i would like to stress as a starting point the proposal for a definition of the cultural and creative industries put forward by the european parliament, which should serve as a basis for future policies in this field. among other calls, i would highlight the request to the commission to address the precarious contractual situation of the cultural and creative industries by ensuring that fundamental social and labour standards are respected. the commission is also invited to take appropriate measures to reduce disparities and ensure that authors, creators, performers and rightholders receive fair remuneration for their works.
‒ the eastern partnership, launched by the prague declaration (2009), is one of the main instruments of the european neighbourhood policy and pursues objectives of respect for international law and the values of democracy, the rule of law and human rights. in this context, the area of cooperation for gender equality and the defence of women's rights is promising, in line with the riga declaration (2015). i welcome the fact that the principle of gender equality is enshrined in the constitutions and legal systems of the six partner countries of eastern europe and the south caucasus, but i would remind you of the way ahead in terms of women's participation in politics (only 14% of ministers and 16% of members), in business (10% in employers' organisations and 15% in trade unions) and in pay justice (disparities between 24% and 50%). i share the concern about the regrettable phenomenon of violence against women, in particular domestic violence. its eradication is a civilization imperative. i stress the urgency of cooperation in combating trafficking in human beings (mostly women), given that these countries are used as a source or transit point for this crime. i therefore support this report.
‒ women continue to be extremely absent from political power structures, both at the executive and parliamentary levels, mainly due to discriminatory practices. women represent on average 14% of ministers and 16% of members. in the economic field, despite the fact that women are generally more qualified than men, they represent 10% of the members of the social bodies of employers' organizations and 15% of the members of trade unions. the gender pay gap is generally considerable, but there are significant discrepancies between the eastern partnership countries (between 24% and 50%), while horizontal and vertical segregation of the labour market is very marked. combating violence against women is a challenge shared by the eu and its eastern neighbours. statistics on reported cases show that between 7% and 25% of women have been victims of domestic violence, but most cases remain unreported. the report highlights the obstacles to women's empowerment and how greater equality between men and women can contribute to the achievement of the eastern partnership and enp objectives.
in writing. the report states that equality between men and women is enshrined in the constitutions of the countries that make up the so-called eastern partnership (eu member states, armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, georgia and the republic of moldova) and in their legal systems. all these countries have ratified most of the relevant international conventions in this field. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of information and consultation services. the report calls for the fight against discrimination to be stepped up and for existing legislation to be enforced. advocates the role of education - nursery, pre-school, primary, secondary and university education - accessible to all; stresses the need to set targets for the elimination of child labour; stresses the need to combat gender-based domestic violence - sexual harassment, forced surrogacy, trafficking in human beings for sexual exploitation, prostitution; the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of women and girls seeking asylum. among other things, we support and value it. but the report also contains less positive aspects, some omissions and aspects with which we disagree. it is noted that nothing is said about the situation in ukraine, the coup that the eu supported and the forces of an avowedly fascist character that have taken over the government of that country and have caused it to regress for decades, also in this area.
‒ we support many of the concerns raised in the report, particularly the urgent need to overcome inequalities between men and women. we believe, however, that the report falls far short of analysing the causes of these inequalities and the ways in which they can be overcome, particularly as regards the need to break with right-wing and exploitative policies. among other things, compulsory quota mechanisms are being proposed to overcome the gap in women's political participation, a mechanism which we reject. the situation in ukraine is mentioned, without mentioning the eu's responsibilities in the establishment of a fascist regime. the report does not escape the usual interventionist approach which so well characterizes the european parliament. this justifies the exacerbation of the european neighbourhood policy and its role in supporting and financing initiatives which naturally aim to contribute to political change, of course, under the ideological matrix of the eu, but also the use of enp for reforms in the public administration and the principles and policies of the states.
‒ stabilising the neighbourhood is one of the main objectives of the european union's external policy and, in particular, of the european neighbourhood policy (enp). women play a key role in this. in view of the principle of differentiation of the enp, it is important to emphasise that women's rights, as well as equality between persons of different sexes, are enshrined in the constitutions and legal systems of the various eastern partnership countries. unfortunately, there is still a great deal of social discrimination in this area. these stereotypes not only prevent women from being more involved in the labour market and in political life, but also maintain the social acceptance of the phenomenon of undeclared domestic violence. statistics on reported cases show that between 7% and 25% of women (depending on the country) have been victims of domestic violence, but most cases remain unreported. i have to say that i voted in favour of this report because it reflects the issues raised above.

mr president, commissioner, the trade agreement, the negotiations of which were concluded in 2010, has been in force between the european union and its member states, on the one hand, and peru and colombia, on the other, since march and august 2013 respectively, and has proved mutually beneficial for both parties. it is now intended that ecuador, as a member country of the same andean community, should also be an integral part of this agreement, which bolivia may also join. however, adding to its economic and social vulnerability, the country was hit by an earthquake last april. i am, however, in favour of the accession of this country to the trade agreement between the european union and the andean community, not for reasons of circumstance or as a response to natural disasters, but because this agreement will enable the country to continue its path of economic, social, labour and environmental growth and development in a more sustained way and geared to the real interests of its citizens, while at the same time intensifying its relations with our continent, which thus has the possibility of strengthening its political, economic and financial weight in this part of the world with which we have strong historical, cultural and diplomatic relations. however, it should be borne in mind that ecuador is the world's largest exporter of bananas and that its accession to the agreement could have a significant impact on community producers in the outermost regions of europe. i therefore consider it essential that, in parallel, the amendments to regulations 19 and 20/2013 on the application to ecuador of the safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for the import of bananas into the european territory, agreed today, be adopted swiftly.

‒ poland has notified the commission of a substantial reform of its national restructuring legislation and has requested that the lists be amended accordingly. the commission has examined whether the request of poland complies with the requirements of the regulation and has submitted a proposal to the european parliament and to the council to ensure that the scope of the recast regulation is adapted to the legal framework of the polish insolvency law at the time of its application. i agree with the aim of the proposal and its content in general terms. however, i think it is important to make three technical amendments to the proposal. the first two reflect the position of the united kingdom and ireland. the third amendment aligns the date of entry into force of the amending regulation with that of the main regulation.
‒ this report seeks to introduce minor technical amendments to regulation (eu) 2015/848 on insolvency proceedings. the amendments are intended to take account of a restructuring reform carried out by poland, which has requested that the lists in annexes a and b to this regulation be amended accordingly. the annexes to the regulation may be amended only by a regulation adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure. as such, the european commission has submitted a proposal to the european parliament with a view to ensuring the scope of the recast regulation, taking into account as such the legal framework of the polish insolvency legislation at the time of its application. the proposal from the european commission and the three amendments tabled are purely technical in nature and do not substantially alter the regulation. as regards the content of the regulation, we have expressed our concerns in due course about negative elements, such as the issue of workers' credit, because they are not granted credit privileges.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal, which is purely technical in nature, in that it seeks to adapt the reform of national legislation carried out in poland to the regulatory framework for insolvency proceedings. in legal terms, the procedure for amending legislation in poland is only qualified as 'insolvency proceedings' if it is covered by the respective annex a of the regulation in question, and the respective annexes can only be amended by a regulation, in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure and the legal basis on which the original regulation was adopted. in view of this, the request of poland was analysed in the light of the legal and regulatory requirements, with the aim of ensuring that the scope of the recast regulation is adapted to the legal framework of the polish insolvency law, and that there is no substantial change to the regulation.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to introduce minor technical amendments to regulation (eu) 2015/848 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 may 2015 on insolvency proceedings. the amendments are intended to take account of a restructuring reform carried out by poland, which has therefore requested the amendment of the lists in annexes a and b to this regulation accordingly. the commission proposal and the other three proposals are purely technical in nature and do not substantially alter the regulation. as regards the content of the regulation, we have expressed our concern about negative elements, such as the issue of workers' credit, basically because they are not granted credit privileges. the rules of procedure are not the subject of this vote, so we voted in favour.
the report approves the conclusion of the protocol amending the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of uzbekistan, of the other part, in order to extend the provisions of the agreement to bilateral trade in textile products. the report of the last ilo monitoring mission noted that child labour had been almost completely eradicated during the cotton harvest. public authorities have taken various measures to eliminate child labor. the same conclusion was not reached with regard to forced labour. the efforts of the uzbek authorities should also be encouraged. i agree to the conclusion of the textile protocol with uzbekistan.
‒ this recommendation is aimed at the conclusion of a protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of uzbekistan, of the other part. the nature and objectives of this agreement do not differ substantially from the free trade matrix which usually characterises agreements of this type. perhaps it is particularly noteworthy that the european parliament itself, which endorses the agreement, recognizes the existence of cases of forced labour in the country with which it is signing the agreement. it doesn't matter. the constraints arising from the low diversification of uzbekistan's economy, from the high dependence on, for example, 'cotton monoculture', are recognised. it doesn't matter. free trade will accentuate this trend, with the intensification of the exporting nature of production and the underestimation of the internal market. this is putting further pressure on european countries which still have a textile industry, such as portugal. this is nothing new: the big importers in central europe benefit, while the producers on the periphery suffer. we obviously voted against it.

in writing. the purpose of this recommendation is to approve the conclusion of the protocol amending the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of uzbekistan, of the other part, in order to extend the provisions of that agreement to bilateral trade in textile products. the ratification of the protocol on textile products resulted in the inclusion of these products in the partnership and cooperation agreement concluded between uzbekistan and the european union in 1999. the provisions of the title 'trade in goods' of that agreement are therefore also applicable to textile products. one of parliament's concerns about this agreement was the respect for human rights in uzbekistan, in particular in relation to child labour and forced labour in the context of the annual cotton harvest. i welcome this report and welcome the cooperation established between uzbekistan and the international labour organisation to assess and conclude that the measures taken to eradicate child labour in the context of the annual cotton harvest in uzbekistan have had results.
‒ textile products are included in the partnership and cooperation agreement concluded between uzbekistan and the union in 1999. in december 2011, an interim report had already been adopted, conditional on the agreement being approved on the improvement of the human rights situation, in particular in relation to child labour and forced labour in the context of the cotton harvest. following the adoption of this report, a dialogue was established with uzbekistan, in the framework of which annual hearings were held, involving a number of stakeholders, including civil society, the uzbek authorities and european and international institutions. close cooperation has also been established between uzbekistan and the international labour organisation. parliament considered that, in the current context of dialogue and cooperation, the efforts of the uzbek authorities should be encouraged. however, if the uzbek authorities suspend the implementation of measures to abolish forced labour, parliament reserves the right to ask the european commission and the council to activate articles 2 and 95 of the partnership and cooperation agreement, which allow for general or specific measures for breaches of human rights.
in writing. - we are faced with a report concerning a proposal to amend the partnership and cooperation agreement with the republic of uzbekistan concluded in 1999 to include the area of bilateral trade in textile products. this inclusion of textile products in the chapter 'trade in goods' provides, inter alia, for the reciprocal granting of most-favoured-nation status, freedom of transit and restrictions on imports, exports and goods in transit on grounds of public morality, public policy and public security. the european parliament has made this amendment to the agreement conditional on an improvement in the human rights situation in the country, particularly in relation to child labour and forced labour. according to a recent report by the international labour organisation (ilo), there have been clear improvements in this area, especially in the area of child labour, although there are still gaps in the area of forced labour. given that this worrying situation is still being closely monitored by the ilo and that uzbekistan has made considerable efforts to comply with and enforce labour standards and respect for human rights, i was in favour of adopting this report in order to approve the conclusion of the textile protocol with this country.
in writing. ‒ the report accompanying the recommendation, which proposes the conclusion of the agreement, contains, under the pretext of alleged aid, unacceptable and unequivocal considerations of the instruments which the european union uses to intervene on sovereign states, seeking to condition its social and economic policies, with the superb vanity of those who think they can teach lessons. we voted against it.
‒ the uzbek government authorised the ilo to monitor the cotton harvest and the ilo carried out a number of checks, initially focusing on child labour and later extending to forced labour and recruitment conditions. the latest monitoring campaign carried out by the ilo during the 2015 cotton harvest shows that the use of child labour for the cotton harvest has become rare, sporadic and socially unacceptable, but that there is a need to maintain continuous surveillance. the uzbek government has been working towards the eradication of forced labour in collaboration with the ilo, and some progress has been made. the eu should therefore take full advantage of the enlargement of the apc to ensure that the uzbek authorities engage in a transition process leading to better governance, strengthening the rule of law, democratic reforms and substantial improvement in the human rights situation.

‒ this new agreement maintains the exclusive access granted to each other by the vessels of denmark, norway and sweden to the waters of each of the three countries outside the four-nautical-mile limit measured from the baselines. traditionally, fishermen do not operate in certain waters. kattegat and skagerrak are typical examples of this. swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together for the same fish stocks in these waters since at least the middle ages. the fact that two of these countries have become member states does not alter the principle that the fishermen of these three countries should enjoy the historical rights to fish in the skagerrak and kattegat. the eu's common fisheries policy establishes a system for managing fish stocks in the waters it covers, thereby supporting the historical rights of fishermen.
‒ this recommendation aims to update the agreement on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat between denmark, norway and sweden. this agreement dates from 1966, before denmark and sweden became members of the eu. the update proposed by norway aims to bring the old agreement into line with the 1982 united nations convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 united nations fish stocks agreement, in particular in terms of control arrangements, or on maritime conservation and management issues. this agreement, with its updates, contributes to strengthening the historical rights of fishermen in the region, regardless of their nationality, considering that fishing grounds do not know administrative jurisdictions and that fishing activity depends on access to resources. involving two eu member states and a third country, this agreement would not have to be the subject of any decision by the eu (european parliament and council) if, under the institutional framework provided by the lisbon treaty, the management of living marine resources had not become an exclusive competence of the eu. we voted in favour. we reiterate, however, our disagreement with the institutional framework mentioned above.

in writing. the agreement between denmark, norway and sweden on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat entered into force on 7 august 1967. this agreement allowed the three countries reciprocal access to fishing activities up to four nautical miles calculated from their baselines in the skagerrak and kattegat. the 1966 agreement remained in force for an initial period of 35 years, until 2002, and was subsequently extended for two five-year periods, until 2012. in view of the evolution of international fisheries law, norway considered that the existing agreement was not in line with the current provisions of the law of the sea and called into question the control mechanism. following formal negotiations between norway and the commission, an understanding was reached in 2013 with the aim of establishing a replacement agreement on reciprocal access to fishing activities in those areas. i voted in favour of this report because the new agreement safeguards the historical fishing rights of fishermen from denmark, norway and sweden in the kattegat and skagerrak, without prejudice to the rights of fishermen from other states, while ensuring that appropriate fisheries management and conservation measures are taken in these waters.
‒ this new agreement maintains the exclusive access granted to each other by the vessels of denmark, norway and sweden to the waters of each of the three countries outside the four-nautical-mile limit measured from the baselines. it guarantees the two member states and norway continued reciprocal access to their respective waters in the skagerrak and kattegat, while ensuring appropriate conservation and fisheries management measures in this area. it also allows for control measures in line with the principles of normal jurisdiction of a coastal state, as is already the case for fisheries in the north sea. fishing in these waters predates the creation of states and the recognition of territorial waters and, subsequently, the exclusive economic zone. swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together for the same fish stocks in these waters since at least the middle ages. the fact that two of these countries have become member states does not alter the principle that the fishermen of these three countries should enjoy the historical rights to fish in the skagerrak and kattegat.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which concerns the conclusion of a new agreement on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat, which is to replace the old agreement between denmark, norway and sweden on this subject. the new agreement, like the previous one, maintains the exclusive access granted to each other by the vessels of denmark, norway and sweden to the waters of each of the three countries, beyond the four-nautical-mile limit. it also ensures continued reciprocal access to the waters of the three countries and appropriate conservation and management measures for fisheries in this area, and also allows for control measures in line with the principles of normal jurisdiction of a coastal state, as is already the case with fisheries in the north sea. it is basically a matter of common sense and balance, since the fishermen of these three countries fish in the same waters for certain fish stocks, in what is a procedure prior to the creation of the states, the recognition of territorial waters and the exclusive economic zone. the fact that two of them later became member states should not alter this tradition or the historical principle underlying it.
‒ the update proposed by norway aims to bring the old agreement into line with the 1982 united nations convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 united nations fish stocks agreement, in particular in terms of control arrangements, or on maritime conservation and management issues. this agreement, with its updates, contributes to strengthening the historical rights of fishermen in the region, regardless of their nationality, considering that fish stocks do not respect administrative jurisdictions and that fishing activity depends on access to resources.

‒ this resolution is accompanied by the recommendation to update the agreement on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat between denmark, norway and sweden. this agreement dates from 1966, before denmark and sweden became members of the eu. the update proposed by norway aims to bring the old agreement into line with the 1982 united nations convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 united nations fish stocks agreement, in particular in terms of control arrangements, or on maritime conservation and management issues. this agreement, with its updates, contributes to strengthening the historical rights of fishermen in the region, regardless of their nationality, considering that fishing grounds do not know administrative jurisdictions and that fishing activity depends on access to resources. involving two eu member states and a third country, this agreement would not have to be the subject of any decision by the eu (european parliament and council) if, under the institutional framework provided by the lisbon treaty, the management of living marine resources had not become an exclusive competence of the eu. we voted in favour. we reiterate, however, our disagreement with the institutional framework mentioned above.

‒ this new agreement maintains the exclusive access granted to each other by the vessels of denmark, norway and sweden to the waters of each of the three countries outside the four-nautical-mile limit measured from the baselines. it guarantees the two member states and norway continued reciprocal access to their respective waters in the skagerrak and kattegat, while ensuring appropriate conservation and fisheries management measures in this area. it also allows for control measures in line with the principles of normal jurisdiction of a coastal state, as is already the case for fisheries in the north sea. fishing in these waters predates the creation of states and the recognition of territorial waters and, subsequently, the exclusive economic zone. swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together for the same fish stocks in these waters since at least the middle ages. the fact that two of these countries have become member states does not alter the principle that the fishermen of these three countries should enjoy the historical rights to fish in the skagerrak and kattegat.
‒ like the motion for a recommendation on this subject, i also support this non-legislative motion for a resolution, as it contains a set of suggestions concerning the historical rights of fishermen in these three countries, which must be preserved in order to allow them to continue fishing together in the kattegat and skagerrak fishing areas. to that end, it is essential to ensure that appropriate fisheries management and conservation measures are taken in those waters, keeping stocks above levels that can achieve maximum sustainable yield. i also agree with the importance of the presentation of an evaluation report on the implementation of the agreement by the commission, which should also be responsible for ensuring that the fixing of customs duties on food and fishery products from the eu is not contrary to the principle of free trade.

‒ this report concerns the proposed approval of an operational and strategic cooperation agreement between europol and georgia, which provides for the exchange of information, including personal data. such information may include expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation processes as well as on crime prevention methods, as well as support in certain criminal investigations. there also appears to be a clear need for europol to deepen its cooperation with georgia, as it plays an increasingly important role in the fight against organised crime, especially as a transit country for so-called foreign fighters and a key partner in the fight against organised crime groups.

‒ i support the report by mr esteban gonzález pons which will allow the mobilisation of eur 856 800 from the globalisation adjustment fund for the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in the manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers in the community of valencia, spain, and eligible for egf contributions. the redundancies were caused by the decline in car production in spain, which led to a reduction in both the number of firms and the number of jobs, and by the closure of 62 out of a total of 187 firms in the automobile sector in the valencian community. through the use of this fund, which was set up to provide complementary support to workers due to major structural changes in world trade, it will be possible to support these workers through measures ranging from guidance/interpretation and facilitation of job search to support for business creation or personalised vocational retraining.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns and may not exceed the annual ceiling of eur 150 million. spain submitted a proposal to reintegrate into the market the workers made redundant by bosal s.a., which is active in the manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers. the application concerns the dismissal of 250 workers and provides for the transfer of eur 856 000.
‒ this application concerns 250 workers made redundant in 29 companies in the economic sectors classified as 'manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers' in spain. the justification is the same as always: spain has lost market share over the last decade thanks to the trend of 'geographical transition of consumption associated with globalisation'. in addition, 'european industry was also affected by the decline in domestic demand due to the economic and financial crisis'. since 2008, due to the combined effect of these two factors in the automotive industry, many companies have closed down or severely reduced their activity, resulting in redundancies or reductions in working hours. spain has already approved 9 applications to the european globalisation adjustment fund to support workers made redundant in the comunidad valenciana region since 2009. this is yet another vivid libel against capitalism, against european capitalist integration and the neoliberal policies it promotes. we support the mobilisation of support for the workers made redundant, but we continue to say that only a break with the policies currently being pursued by the eu will be able to stop this path of social and economic disaster.

‒ this proposal is part of the fourth eu railway package and aims to repeal regulation (ec) no 1192/69. this regulation concerns common rules for the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. it allows member states to compensate railway undertakings for charges that undertakings in other modes of transport do not have to bear, such as special payments in the event of accidents at work. this regulation was adopted before the process of liberalisation of the railway market and at a time when rail transport in europe was developing within a national framework and integrated undertakings were simultaneously providing transport services and managing the railway infrastructure. the process of destruction, deregulation and privatization of companies has been a disaster for the railway system. the aim: monopolistic concentration at eu level, without regard for passengers and the development strategy of each state. we have been in breach of regulation (ec) no 1192/69. we also recognise that this may be out of context and that it currently allows for the shifting of public funds to the privatised companies managing the railway system. but one thing is clear: the proposed repeal is not to stop liberalisation but to deepen it. we're against it.
