‒ this report is part of a set of three legislative proposals relating to the fourth railway package. in this case, the aim is to repeal regulation no 1192/69 on common rules for the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings, the purpose of which was to promote a better balance between railway undertakings and other undertakings in other modes of transport as regards the payment of social and external costs. after the liberalisation of the railway market and after several railway packages, the regulation lost its original purpose, being at odds with the current legal context, which is to establish a discrimination between railway companies on the list of companies owned by the states and companies outside this list, which do not receive any kind of compensation. after six rounds of trilogues, an interinstitutional agreement was reached, proposing the repeal of the regulation, with the exception of the provisions on the standardisation of accounts relating to compensation paid for level crossings, which need a longer period of validity until the member states adapt their national legislation in this field. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. regulation (eec) no 1192/69 was adopted before the liberalisation of the railway market and at a time when rail transport in europe was mainly developed within a national framework and integrated undertakings were simultaneously providing transport services and managing the railway infrastructure. the purpose of the regulation was therefore to put railway undertakings on an equal footing with undertakings in other modes of transport as regards the payment of social costs or externalities. moreover, the relationship between governments and mainly state-owned railway companies was not yet regulated by contractual agreements and there was a much more direct ownership link between the two parties. due to its original purpose, the regulation contains a list listing the formerly state-owned railway companies. this list has been adapted several times to take account of the accession of the new member states and currently contains 40 companies. the repeal of this regulation can only be interpreted as another way of liberalising the sector and further reducing the ability of the public authorities to intervene in this sector vital to the economy and society.
‒ the aim of the commission proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 is to improve the quality of rail passenger services and to increase their operational efficiency. the commission proposal relates to the proposed amendments to directive 2012/34/eu establishing a single european railway area. after six rounds of trilogues, parliament reached an agreement with the council presidency on 19 april 2016. the agreement reached includes, inter alia:the obligation for the competent authorities to define the specifications of public service obligations (psos) for public passenger transport;the setting of compensation will have to be done at a level that ensures the financial sustainability of the provision of the public passenger transport service;the compliance by public service operators with the applicable obligations in the field of social and labour law as defined in union legislation, national legislation or collective agreements in the exercise of psos;the obligation for public service operators and infrastructure managers to provide the competent authority with information that is essential for the award of future public service contracts (psos). i therefore support this recommendation.
‒ the new legislation, already agreed with national governments, provides for public tenders to become the rule for the award of public service contracts, with some exceptions. direct adjustment will continue to be possible where it leads to better quality of service or cost-effectiveness. the performance requirements will include the punctuality and frequency of the trains. the reform of the railway sector will facilitate the entry of new operators into the market and the provision of their services. member states may, however, limit the right of access of a new operator if the proposed service would compromise the economic equilibrium of an existing public service contract. the competent authorities will have to clearly define the specifications of public service obligations for public passenger transport and the scope of their application, including the geographical areas concerned.
‒ this proposal is part of the fourth eu railway package and focuses on amending regulation (ec) no 1370/2007. the stated objective is to improve the quality of rail passenger services and increase their operational efficiency, so as to improve the competitiveness and attractiveness of rail transport in relation to other modes of transport and develop the single european railway area. i speak well known. to achieve this objective, the commission proposed to introduce compulsory tendering for public service contracts in order to intensify competitive pressure on national railway markets. in other words, in conjunction with the proposal for a european railway area, it opens up national rail systems, which are already completely deregulated, to international competition. another step in the growing monopoly concentration in the sector. it is no less paradoxical that we talk about 'improving the competitiveness and attractiveness of rail transport compared to other modes of transport' by using more liberalisation, when the statistics show that liberalisation has only contributed to the loss of attractiveness. in this respect it should be noted that since 1988 portugal has lost 43% of passengers per km (pk); in the same period, germany gained 24% and france 35%. we obviously voted against it.

in writing. ‒ the commission proposal to amend directive 2012/34/eu, also known as the governance directive, aims at:-opening up the market for national rail passenger services, with the aim of intensifying competitive pressure on national rail markets;-strengthening the governance of the infrastructure manager, with the aim of ensuring equal access to infrastructure. these amendments are intended to help increase the level of competition, ensure financial transparency and fair financing conditions. the european parliament played a key role in reaching the overall agreement with the council, and succeeded in introducing the following improvements to the commission proposal: - the creation of safeguards to ensure the impartiality and independence of infrastructure managers;- the creation by the member states of a national framework for the assessment of conflicts of interest;- the creation of mechanisms for mandatory coordination between infrastructure managers and railway undertakings;- the strengthening of the powers of regulatory bodies. i therefore support this recommendation.

‒ the new rules cover more than 300 seaports in europe, including 13 in portugal. the legislation adopted aims, among other objectives, to increase transparency in the fees for port services and the use of port infrastructure, as well as the use made of public funding. these rules do not impose a specific model for the management of seaports and do not affect the competence of member states to provide non-economic services of general interest. different models of port management are possible, provided that the regime for the provision of port services and the common rules on financial transparency laid down in the regulation are respected. the port services covered by the regulation are refuelling, mooring, towing and the collection of waste generated on board ships and cargo waste. freight handling, passenger services and piloting are subject to financial transparency rules but exempt from the rules on the organisation of services.

‒ the european parliament has approved new rules on the provision of port services and financial transparency for ports covering six maritime infrastructures in mainland portugal (aveiro, lisbon, portimão, porto/leixões, setúbal and sines), with lisbon deciding on the ports of the azores and madeira. the legislation adopted today aims, among other things, to increase transparency in the charging of port services and the use of port infrastructure, as well as the use made of public funding. the port services covered by the regulation are refuelling, mooring, towing and the collection of waste generated on board ships and cargo waste. freight handling, passenger services and piloting are subject to financial transparency rules but exempt from the rules on the organisation of services. the agreed text provides that social and labour rules are not affected by the regulation and that port workers receive appropriate training on their working conditions. the report also guarantees the right to strike. the regulation also adopted financial transparency provisions to ensure fair competition and prevent price abuse, in particular where services are not subject to effective competition.
‒ this report is on a proposal for a regulation establishing a regulatory framework for access to port services and financial transparency in ports, in order to contribute to a more transparent, efficient, interconnected and sustainable operation of the trans-european transport network (ten-t). the main objectives are to modernise port services and operations and to create conditions for attracting investment in order to counteract the reduced competitive pressure and possible market abuse in this segment. overall, i find this proposal very positive and i very much agree with the rapporteur's suggestions to contribute to more efficient, transparent and participatory port management and thus to provide greater legal certainty for the proper functioning of the ten-t network.
‒ under the guise of modernising services and operations, the liberalisation and privatisation of another strategic sector of the economy, the port sector, is being pursued. we have already seen the promise in other sectors: attracting investment, greater efficiency, better quality. we know what they mean, but they are denied by reality, without appeal or aggravation. this proposal falls far short of the european commission's initial ambitions. a retreat forced by the struggle, by the resistance of the workers. however, the proposal does point the way. a negative path and one that must be fought.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors (coa) operates as a collegiate body of 28 members, one from each member state. its members are appointed by the council, after consulting the european parliament, for a renewable term of six years. the estonian auditor's post will soon expire, so a candidate has been proposed by the estonian government and then by the council. the proposed candidate is presented as having a long political experience. he was deputy chancellor at the ministry of justice; member of the board of the estonian privatization agency; later became prime minister of estonia; was minister of economy and communications until 2014 and is currently a member of the estonian parliament. during the interview, the candidate took a politically biased view of the functions he proposes to assume. at the end of the hearing, a number of serious doubts remained about what his position would be if he were to be confronted with situations that challenge his political positions and convictions. the appointment of the estonian candidate was adopted with the gue/ngl, some greens and efdd voting against. the candidate has shown himself to be an enthusiastic supporter of the privatisation of all public assets, which certainly calls into question his ability to be an objective taxpayer in analysing the expenditure of public funds on public or public/private projects.

‒ the court of auditors (the 'court') functions as a collegiate body of 28 members, one from each member state. its members are appointed by the council, after consulting the european parliament, for a renewable term of six years. the post of estonian auditor will soon expire, a candidate was proposed by the estonian government and then by the council. the appointment of the estonian candidate was adopted with the gue/ngl, some greens and efdd voting against. we voted against because there is a gender imbalance in the ect that needs to be addressed. furthermore, the candidate is drawn from the ranks of the conservative political parties in power, further skewing the political vision of this body. this candidate has shown himself to be an enthusiastic supporter of the privatisation of all public assets, which certainly calls into question his ability to be an objective taxpayer in analysing the spending of public funds on public or public/private projects.
‒ the research fund for coal and steel (rfcs), financed by the remaining assets of the former european coal and steel community (ecsc, whose founding treaty - 1951 - expired in 2002), supports research and development in the steel (72.8%) and coal (27.2%) sectors at an annual rate of around eur 50 million. i therefore believe that this financial flow should promote innovation in the exploitation of these resources (production, use and conservation), in ensuring environmental sustainability and in the safety of workers. i share the concern about the harmonisation of rules, processes and terminology with horizon 2020. the policy of supporting research in the european union must be coherent and initiatives must be complementary. i share the intention to clarify the rules on expert groups in order to ensure the greatest possible transparency in the commission's management of the rfcs. i would remind you that the commission has already decided on the establishment and functioning of expert groups (decision of 30 may 2016) and that the european parliament is preparing its position on this matter, so the regulation must be consistent. i therefore support this report.
‒ the eu has supported coal and steel research for more than 50 years. the research fund for coal and steel (rfcs) is complementary to horizon 2020 and is managed independently of it. it provides annual funding of approximately eur 50 million for r&d and innovation in both the coal and steel sectors (with a distribution of 72,8% for steel and 27,2% for coal). it brings together industrial partners, smes, universities and leading research centres across the european union to develop knowledge and promote innovation in the sector. the research funded covers production processes, resource use and conservation, environmental improvements and occupational safety in the relevant sectors.
‒ the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community (ecsc) was signed in 1951. when the treaty expired in 2002, it was decided to make ecsc assets available to a research fund for coal and steel (rfcs). the programme is financed by the revenues generated by the remaining assets of the former ecsc and is managed by the european commission. the rfcs is complementary to horizon 2020 and is managed independently of it. in any event, the main beneficiaries are known. it provides annual funding of approximately eur 50 million for r&d and innovation in both the coal and steel sectors (with a distribution of 72,8% for steel and 27,2% for coal). it brings together industrial partners, smes, universities and leading research centres (mainly from the major eu powers) to develop knowledge and promote innovation in the sector. the research funded covers production processes, resource use and conservation, environmental improvements and occupational safety in the relevant sectors. the report proposes simplifying some rules and improving the transparency of the management of the rfcs. guidelines to which we are generally not opposed.

‒ coal and steel have been high on the european union's agenda for more than six decades, dating back to 1951, when the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community (ecsc) was signed. when the treaty ceased to be in force in 2002, it was decided to make ecsc assets available to a research fund for coal and steel (rfcs). the programme is financed by the revenue generated by the remaining assets of the former ecsc and is managed by the commission. the commission now proposes amendments to clarify the characteristics of the experts appointed to participate in the advisory groups and technical groups established in accordance with the legal basis of the rfcs programme, in order to avoid any conflicts of interest. this is a significant step. i support this report.
‒ the eu has supported coal and steel research for more than 50 years, since the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community (ecsc) was signed in 1951. when the treaty expired in 2002, it was decided to make the ecsc assets available to a research fund for coal and steel, which was to be financed by the revenues generated by the remaining assets of the former ecsc and managed by the european commission (ec). the research fund is complementary to horizon 2020 and provides funding of approximately eur 50 million annually for innovation in the coal and steel sectors. the objective of this proposal is to amend the legal basis of the programme following the periodic evaluation of its management rules with a view to facilitating access to funding, through simplified rules and a harmonisation with the rules of the general research programme horizon 2020 (with which stakeholders in the sectors are familiar), ensuring that the programme is managed by the ec with due transparency. i voted in favour of this resolution because i agree with it and i recognise the importance of harmonizing and simplifying the rules governing this programme.
‒ the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community (ecsc) was signed 50 years ago, in 1951. when the treaty expired in 2002, it was decided to make ecsc assets available to a research fund for coal and steel (rfcs). the programme is financed by the revenue generated by the remaining assets of the former ecsc and is managed by the commission. the rfcs is complementary to horizon 2020 and is managed independently of it. the proposed amendments are designed to facilitate access to funding through simplified rules and proportionate harmonisation with the rules of the overall horizon 2020 research programme and to ensure that the programme is managed by the commission with due transparency and in accordance with the commission's rules on expert groups. we voted yes.

‒ the challenges facing the european union in the field of defence (terrorism, hybrid threats, cybersecurity, organised crime or energy security) require an operational and effective common security and defence policy (csdp). i note the presentation of the annual report on the cfsp and the progressive increase in the political will for greater integration in defence, reflected in documents such as the global strategy for the cfsp. i share the view that external action should be based on three pillars: diplomacy, development and defence. i am in favour of using all the instruments of the lisbon treaty, in particular permanent structured cooperation, as a dynamic force for greater integration. i believe that member states should invest more in defence, both politically (by creating a permanent civilian and military headquarters) and financially (by increasing defence investment in line with the 2% of gdp target under nato). the implementation of a 'defence' training in the council of ministers or the creation of a defence semester should correspond to concrete actions and avoid the complexity of decision-making processes. i share a comprehensive approach to csdp, in line with the neighbourhood policy, cooperation or development support. i therefore support this report.

‒ agricultural activity depends on biological processes and is therefore strongly dependent on climatic conditions and plant and animal diseases. these natural factors are beyond the farmer's control. the development of the performance of agricultural holdings is more uncertain than that of enterprises in other economic sectors. income uncertainty is particularly detrimental to investment and innovation and can affect the economic viability of farms. market uncertainty, as well as economic and climate risks, are likely to increase in the coming years. i agree that the volatility of agricultural product prices is one of the main factors in the dramatic situation currently faced by many european farmers and it is part of the european union's role to find solutions to this phenomenon, particularly through the cap.
‒ the instability of prices in agriculture is inseparable from the capitalist globalisation of trade in agricultural products. it is due to market factors (supply and demand), political decisions (trade agreements in the global market), financial investments and speculation (financial investments in agricultural products) and climate factors. the report sets out objectives to strengthen the organisation of the different agricultural sectors and contractual systems; addresses inequality in the food chain between large retailers and primary producers; and solutions to protect farmers' incomes more effectively through the use of risk management tools, income stabilisation instruments, individual provision mechanisms and mutual funds. the report also stresses that the current cap lacks effective response tools. however, it does not give clear answers, looking for solutions in the wrong places, failing to identify the real cause of the volatility problem. on the contrary, it supports a market-oriented and competitive model of agriculture. price volatility is a structural problem, to which the liberalisation of trade in agricultural products contributes. the risk management instruments proposed, in particular the various types of insurance and mutual funds, as well as the experiences with public-private partnerships in the framework of the cap crisis management tools, do not represent a solution.

‒ agricultural activity is exposed to various risks, as it depends on biological processes and is thus heavily dependent on climatic conditions and plant and animal diseases, factors which are to some extent beyond the control of farmers. agriculture is thus confronted with higher levels of volatility than other economic sectors. income uncertainty is particularly detrimental to investment and innovation and can affect the economic viability of farms. the report argues that the cap does not currently have sufficient risk management tools to meet the needs of the sector, in the context of increasing volatility in the markets. i support this report because i believe that one of the main objectives of the cap must be to combat price volatility in order to guarantee fair incomes for farmers, to stabilise agricultural markets and to ensure the viability of food production.
‒ we need effective measures in the european union to protect farmers as well as consumers against unfair trading practices. farmers are the weakest link in the food chain, although they are one of the most important. the future common agricultural policy (cap) must seek new ways of combating price volatility and stabilising farmer incomes. the current system is either not working or is too slow to react to market imbalances such as the russian embargo or low international demand for agricultural products. the report also states that the ability to create and maintain rural jobs is the first step towards the next cap.
‒ agricultural activity obviously depends on biological processes and is therefore subject to natural factors outside the farmer's control (exogenous factors), thus making the performance of agricultural holdings uncertain and calling into question their economic viability. the common agricultural policy (cap) was initially characterised by strong regulation of agricultural markets through guaranteed prices, which ensured farmers a minimum value for their products in the event of a crisis. with successive reforms, its functioning has been altered. the last reform in 2013, which defined the cap for the period 2014-2020, was based on two pillars and the direct payments system was re-designed (more targeted, more equitable and greener). however, the risk management instruments provided for in the second pillar of the cap are insufficient to circumvent price volatility in farmers' incomes - one of the main factors of the instability currently experienced by many european farmers. strengthening the organization of the sectors and contractual arrangements, improving the protection of farmers' incomes through risk management instruments adapted to price volatility and increasing the transparency of the markets are some of the measures proposed by the rapporteur, which i support and for which i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ as has been well said, volatility is a complex process with many causes. however, we must not mix these causes because otherwise we are not applying the appropriate instruments to this volatility. fever can be caused by a virus or a bacterium. treatment, to be effective, always implies a correct diagnosis. in this particular case, i fear that the randomness of the climate is being deliberately mixed with financial speculation and price manipulation by the big multinationals and the big retailers. to try to blame climate change as the main cause of increasing price volatility is to try to impose or accentuate an increasingly market-oriented reform of the cap and further aggravate the consequences of this instability. the stability of farmers is not at stake here. what is at stake here is the definitive abandonment of a logic of direct income support, which is stable, by a logic of income insurance, following the american model. price volatility is tackled with public regulatory instruments rather than financial instruments.
mr president, i also congratulate my colleague, mr díaz de mera, on his excellent work, as is customary. the european visa policy, in particular the visa exemption, is an essential element of the union's external relations, allowing for better cooperation with third states. cooperation with neighbouring countries is particularly important. the visa liberalization with georgia and ukraine - which this parliament has already approved - is a prime example. the approval of this suspension mechanism will contribute to greater security by allowing the exemption to be suspended in the event of a substantial increase in irregular stays. it will also be possible in the event of human rights violations in the third country. equally important is the increased flexibility of the mechanism, giving it a greater and faster reaction capacity. finally, thanks to the determined position of mr dias de mera, parliament has been able to be involved in more serious situations involving a longer suspension. the council has already reached the stage where it is time to unblock visa liberalization with georgia and ukraine. not only are the requirements met, but the importance of the matter for foreign policy is also clear.
mr president, i congratulate the rapporteur of parliament, agustín díaz de mera, on his ability to reach a consensus on an important issue for the construction of a genuine visa policy for the european union. the new rules allow for flexibility and a rapid activation of the suspension mechanism in the event of a substantial increase in the number of nationals of the country concerned, or irregular entries into the territory of the european union, a substantial increase in unfounded asylum applications, a lack of cooperation in readmission and in the event of threats to public policy or internal security related to third-country nationals. this agreement with the council will, we hope, calm some of the member states and, consequently, allow the adoption of the visa liberalisation agreements with georgia and ukraine to be completed quickly. it remains to be hoped that these rules will not be used for perverse political games. parliament will be watching.

‒ the 'thalidomide generation' began to appear in the late 1950s, but it was not until 1961 that the first alert was made about cases of congenital malformations associated with the use of thalidomide. it was withdrawn from the market in germany and england in 1961. it is estimated that between 10,000 and 20,000 people worldwide are affected by thalidomide, with varying degrees of disability. in 2012, the chief executive of chemie gruenhental, responsible for the product, for the first time in half a century, made a formal apology which was considered inappropriate, pathetic and offensive by victim advocacy organisations, considering that his apology was too light, too late and full of hypocrisy, since for 50 years, grunenthal was involved in a corporate strategy calculated to shield itself from any moral, legal and financial consequences. this resolution follows on from the qo and the debate which took place in the plenary in march this year. the urgency of putting it on the plenary agenda is that in january 2017, the german parliament is expected to amend the law on the rules for financial support to survivors and, by using this resolution, to press and ask that this support be given to all victims in eu member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on support for the victims of thalidomide because i believe that survivors should be formally recognised in all member states and receive fair compensation from the german fund specially set up for this purpose. i would remind you that the drug thalidomide was marketed by the german pharmaceutical company grünenthal in the late 1950s and early 1960s as a safe medicine for the treatment of nausea, headache, cough, insomnia and constipation during pregnancy and that it has caused the death or malformation of thousands of newborns after being administered to pregnant women in many european countries.
‒ the paediatric medicines regulation has had a considerable impact on the development of paediatric medicines, helping to improve the overall situation and giving rise to concrete benefits in relation to a number of childhood diseases. despite the existence of more paediatric research projects, more high-quality information, sufficient progress has not been made in several areas, particularly in oncology and neonatology. i support this resolution, which calls on the commission to submit the report provided for in article 50 in due time so as to provide a full identification and in-depth analysis of the obstacles currently impeding innovation in medicinal products for the paediatric population and to consider introducing changes, including through a legislative review of the regulation. i believe that priority should be given to paediatric needs and medicines, based on scientific data, in order to match the best available therapies to the therapeutic needs of children, especially those affected by cancer, and to optimise the resources used in research.
‒ the paediatric medicines regulation has had a considerable impact on paediatric medicines development, as pharmaceutical companies consider paediatric development as an integral part of overall drug development. childhood cancer remains the leading cause of death by disease in children aged one year and over, and 6000 young people die of cancer every year in europe; two thirds of patients who survive suffer from side effects due to existing treatments. in this context, i agree that the commission may be able to introduce amendments, including through a legislative revision of the paediatric medicines regulation, which take due account of the need for paediatric development plans based on the mechanism of action and not just on the type of disease, models for disease and medicines prioritization, earlier and more viable pips, and incentives that stimulate more research and respond more effectively to the needs of the paediatric population.
‒ children have often been referred to as 'therapeutically orphaned' as they are often denied treatment appropriate to their specific characteristics as well as to the diseases and conditions that specifically affect them. in 2006, regulation (ec) no 1901/2006 on medicinal products for paediatric use entered into force. while it has resulted in an improvement in the overall situation and concrete benefits in a number of childhood diseases, sufficient progress has not been made in several areas, in particular in paediatric oncology and neonatology. the legislation in force in the eu also has several shortcomings. for example, there are considerable delays in starting paediatric clinical trials of cancer medicines. the current legislative approach is not satisfactory for specific and exclusive diseases of children, as well as for rare diseases. there are no paediatric investigation plans (pips) for specific childhood fatal diseases such as high-risk neuroblastoma. this is not financially attractive to pharmaceutical companies. the resolution fails to recognise the right of children to access appropriate treatment and innovative medicines tailored to their specific conditions and rare diseases. instead of recognising the market's flaws and perversities, it does not envisage solutions beyond its narrow limits.

‒ the existing legislation in the eu on medicines for paediatric use still has several gaps that it has not been able to close. there are no paediatric investigation plans (pips) for specific childhood fatal diseases such as high-risk neuroblastoma, however some pips exist for extremely rare cancers in children and adolescents. this is because the approval of an imp is encouraged by research done by adult pharmaceutical companies, thus saving money on part of the study. the resolution fails to recognise as a right of children access to appropriate treatment and innovative medicines specific to their specific conditions and rare diseases, it is based on the principle of market being stimulated to respond to a problem of lack of resources to respond to a very specific population. in addition, the concern to find suitable cancer drugs alone leaves a whole host of childhood conditions and diseases outside the remit of the pharmaceutical companies, which only research and market what suits their interests, rather than the interests of children and adolescents.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the oral question with resolution on paediatric medicines because i agree with an early position by the european parliament before the review of the paediatric medicines regulation which the european commission is due to present early next year. i regret that many children suffering from rare paediatric diseases do not have access to specific paediatric medicines. i would remind you that the existing paediatric regulation has had a positive effect on the development of paediatric medicines and has led to tangible benefits for a number of childhood diseases, but insufficient progress has been made in several areas. it is therefore urgent to promote innovation in paediatric medicines to ensure that in the future all children can have access to appropriate paediatric medicines. in this context, i would also stress the need to develop tests for primary immunodeficiency in the member states to detect diseases that can be treated if they are diagnosed in good time.
‒ the 2015 annual report is intended to provide a summary of the work of the committee on petitions. statistics show that most citizens turn to parliament for help on issues relating to the environment, justice, the internal market and fundamental rights. most of the petitions declared inadmissible are because the petitioners continue to confuse european and national competences and the competences of the european institutions with those of the council of europe and the court of human rights. i support the vallina report, which argues for the need to redouble efforts to better inform citizens about the right to petition and what they can get by petitioning the european parliament. i agree with the need to develop the solvit network and the importance of access to it for all those who need it. the committee on petitions has the opportunity to maintain a dialogue with citizens, since by listening to and resolving the problems which concern them, it can help to link the institutions and citizens of the union.
in writing. according to statistics, in 2015 the european parliament received 1431 petitions, which represents a decrease of 47% compared to the 2714 petitions submitted in 2014. in 2015, 943 petitions were considered admissible (65,9% of a total of 1431) and 483 were declared inadmissible (33,8%). in 2015, 63,4% of the petitions received, i.e. 907 petitions, were dealt with quickly, either because they were considered inadmissible (33,8%) or because, although admissible, they were closed immediately after transmission of information to the petitioners or after their referral to another parliamentary committee competent for the matter (29,6%). it should be noted that the percentage of petitions considered inadmissible decreased compared to 2014 (6,1% in 2015), and that the percentage of petitions considered admissible increased (5,9%). for 2015, there were several changes in the list of countries of origin of petitions, with spain remaining at the top, followed by italy, germany, romania and poland. however, there was a significant increase in the proportion of italian petitions, from 7.9% to 12.3%. i voted in favour.
‒ this report describes the activities and work of the committee on petitions of the european parliament. it gives details of the number of petitions received, closed or dealt with by this commission or on the countries or issues concerned, and is an important quantitative tool in evaluating its work. during 2015 1431 petitions were received (down 47% from 2014), 943 were considered admissible, of which 424 had a rapid examination. the analysis shows that most citizens who use this procedure to turn to the european parliament seek assistance on matters relating to the environment, fundamental rights, justice and the internal market. other petitioners seek to make their proposals for the implementation of eu policies heard and others still address the european parliament to challenge decisions taken by national authorities and to appeal against judgments of national courts. the majority of them complain of weaknesses in the application of european legislation, either because of faulty transposition of legislation, or because of non-application of community rules, or because of violations of them. this confirms the discontent and growing alienation of citizens from the process of european integration. we stress that the final version of this report has been considerably weakened, as the right wing has dropped references to so-called austerity policies and their effects.
